There are many interesting sights on your stops so a good excuse to catch your breath. Plenty of Guides / Assistants will offer to take you to the top. A fair price is US$20. Beware that assistants will start helping you on the steps and despite us repeatedly saying "No" three of them continued all the way to the top and back telling us they were locals and only want to help to make us happy. At the end they asked for US$75 but after reminding them we did not agree and were constantly saying no, we paid them something because they did help my wife on some of the steeper sections. Anyone younger and fitter can do this climb without the use of a guide / assistant. If you need the help on the 1200 steps up and 1200 steps down then I would advice to engage a strong assistant as they will take your arm or push you up the steep parts. There are plenty of signs in multiple languages explaining everything you are looking at. Despite the warning signs about being quiet so as not to disturb the hornets there was many people making lots of noise. There is a treatment tent half way up is someone gets stung but never saw anyone bitten so I think as long as you do the correct thing all will be okay. Also seal you bags and keep food hidden as the monkeys will steal things as they are after food. We saw one lady grabbing her shoulder bag that a monkey was trying to steal because it was open and had food in it.

WOW, WOW, WOW ! This place is a must for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. An ancient world heritage site that is on par with Ankor Wat, Borobodur, and the Pyramids at Giza, a site not to be missed. Start off in the remains of the landscaped gardens then slowly meander up the 200 + meters on stable steps past the lions feet entrance up to the business end of the fortress. It is hot and relatively steep but take a steady hike with lots of rest stops and most people of most ages and ability should be able to get to the top. Once at the top the views are amazing as is the remaining structure that must have been an incredible feat of engineering way back in the 5th century. This really is a must do activity when in Sri Lanka and is sensibly priced and wasn't particularly crowded when we visited in mid November.

A must do! The climb is worth it but it's worth it. The views are incredible! We can only regret the large number of tourists... choose to go up not too late in the morning because at 10 a.m.... it's Disneyland
Sigiriya or Sinhagiri (Lion Rock Sinhala: සීගිරිය, Tamil: சிகிரியா/சிங்ககிரி, pronounced see-gi-ri-yə) is an ancient roc
Worth the climb, iron steps not for the faint hearted but place one foot in front of the other and you'll get there and you won't be disappointed with your efforts...

Sigiriya Rock has between 1210 and 1300  steps to get to the top and thee ladies on our tour did not make it to the top and one man did not even make it to the start!. I made it and was the oldest man in our tour! The view was worth it at the top

A must- visit place together with visitors from around the world, including many Sri Lankans. Take a tour guide, officially registered at the museum (also ticket office)  to understand the history and importance. Beautiful view on clear days.
Sigitiya is valuable travel destination in the sri lanka. Absolutely greate view. Best experience for life

This truly is a magnificent site, particularly for those, like us, who set off early to watch the sunrise. The climb is taxing in places and not great for those with mobility restrictions but the view from the top makes the ascent worthwhile.

This was a truly worthwhile hiking experience.  Please note it is extremely expensive for foreigners ($50AUD) and it is quite challenging especially going up with the heat.  That being said it is well worth it and you can take constant breaks in the shade.  The views all the way up were breathtaking and the top is very interesting.  We added Dambulla on our itinerary just for this and we were so glad we did.

The Sigiriya in Sri Langka is famous for it's palace ruins on top of a massive 200 meter high rock. It is surrounded by the remains of an extensive network of gardens, reservoirs and other structures. The rock itself is a lava plug left over from an ancient long extinct volcano.

Sigiriya is a one of its kind experience of a fort on a rock. To think that a ~490 AD site could have such planned architecture is a wonder in itself. Word of caution, it is quite a steep climb with lots of steps, so one needs to be prepared for that, and carry minimum baggage on them.  Also, though entry is allowed till 1730 hrs (mandatory exit by 1830 hrs) , it makes sense to get there in broad daylight as it will difficult to climb all the steps in the dark. The entry was USD 30 for foreigners (non SAARC) and USD 15 for foreigners from a SAARC nation.

Visited the place in Aug 2018. The cave paintings were awesome and the place oozes history! The climb to the top was quiet strainfull and not easy for aged people - took about 2 hours to climb to the top. But once you're on top, the view is just amazing! There are guides who explain the history of this place and take you to a few spots that most unguided tourists are likely to miss. Do visit the museum as well - It is included in the ticket price. Tip: Buy water before climbing and carry them with you - you'll definitely need it!

Start the climbing early in the morning and it was one of my best experience in sri Lanka, lovely walk through the gardens, steps and spiral staircase. Also our guide was superb, knowledgeable. Views and the architectural designs are amazing. Must visit place in sigiriya

What a great experience and great views from the top of the rock.  But beware there are a lot of steps from the entrance to the top.  And the steel staircase might be a bit of a challenge for people who have issues with with heights or mobility.  If it's the latter the "Rock Boys" will happily drag you up for a fee.  Agree the fee before you start.  And beware of the wasps when you get to the top.  They can be dangerous if riled. When we were there a couple of people ventured into a roped off area and set off a swarm which meant everyone had to get back down that staircase PDQ.  So it was pretty hectic and tense.  All in all a must see destination

The climb up was hot and tiring but worth it. There are guides who explain all about the history of the place as you rest at intervals during the climb. The view from the area near the lions paws is amazing. While you don't need a guide, it makes the experience much more interesting. There is no set fee, they rely on donations from tourists for their services.

I'll start by saying that I don't know the amount of the tickets, but taking into account where we are, that tourists are bled with super outrageous prices, I'm not surprised at all that the amount is extremely exaggerated,,, a local can be charged 1 E, and they can charge the tourist 30,,, they are authentic chorizos. This way no more tourists will come.... The place is very beautiful, a huge area with spectacular ruins and ponds with water, and at the end a small rock mountain with archaeological remains on the top,, A short walk along the side of the rock by some stairs, it is reached in just 5 minutes, to contemplate some beautiful ruins and beautiful views....E
It was amazing to be on the top... the panoramic view was breathtaking. Morning time is much advised for climbing as it can get quite hot. Plus, avoid rainly day as stairs can get a bit slippery.
The view at the top is amazing. The journey is tiring with so many steps. But the top is worth it. Could increase the quality of facilities tho.

Seeing the rock and then hiking up were more amazing than I had anticipated.  Although I have acrophobia, I attempted to do it thinking I wouldn't be able to make it to the top.  But while being guided by the handrails and not looking down until I got to the top, I happily climbed up to the most amazing views and history.  It is strenuous and - as I said - not for the faint of heart with heights but well worth doing.  Go early when the crowds are less and the temperatures are lower.

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to Sigiriya, a world heritage site. It is expensive for foreign visitors at  9.900 rps, but the experience was very good. This is not for the feint hearted, those who are unfit or a bad medical condition as there are many steep steps to climb up on the outer face of the rock, however those who do are treated to a very ancient and historic place together with amazing views for many miles. The ancient frescos were in good condition for being 1600 years old. The museum included in the price was also interesting with ancient displays and information. This is well worth a visit.

The first thing you notice is that there tons are restaurants and hotels all over - too many for my taste. The second thing is ‘foreigner discrimination’ for paying money but then everyone is equal again for the rest. There are ‘guides’ everywhere, this place is really too commercial  and all about money, money, money

Main attraction and iconic image of Sri Lanka. We started the climb around 9.30 in the morning, the climb is challenging but doable, among other things in the morning it is largely in the shadow of the rock itself. The entrance fee is 25 dollars, you can also pay in rupees and with a debit card. The view from the top of the rock is worth the effort, it spans 360° over the valley, impressive! Absolutely worth doing

Sigiriya rock fortress was such a beautiful and breathtaking site. It helped that I had an extremely knowledgeable guide from Lanka Tours & Excursion named Kaan that made experience one to remember. To this day, I'm in awe with the foresight and preservation of this UNESCO site, the climb can be challenging for some but if you're able to take your time and pace yourself, you'll be rewarded with the breathless view and exploration up top, especially with the mirror wall and sacred paintings we saw as part of the tour. Highly recommended!

An absolutely stunning area.The lakes and small rivers around the bottom of the Rock Temple are just beautiful.The climb up to the roco is not to difficult,there are places to rest.At the top the view is just amazing.This is one of the better places to visit and well worth the trip out to Sigiriya.

It takes a few steps before you can really enjoy the view and the murals. The view is the toughest part, but if you are trained a little, it is very doable. First walk to the large plateau and then the last steps to the top. There is a beautiful view of the surroundings. If you walk from that plateau to the exit, you will automatically pass the beautiful wall paintings. Then just climb a small spiral staircase. Unfortunately you are not allowed to take photos there. So you don't have to climb everything if you come mainly for the paintings. And near the exit are a number of other small sights including a kind of water tank and an altar.

Another amazing trip with Tony's Tours Sri Lanka. What a fabulos day and sight. We Met another guide at Sigiriya who explianed the history of the rock and palace, grounds and the king livining there. To learn about how they built the palace, gardens swimming pools and how they protected the palace. The paintings and bees waxed walls to look like a mirror. We managed to climb to the top (no mean feet) and we were so pleased that we did what a view !! a must for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. We then drove to the cave temple. again another amazing site another must.

Unfit 65 year old and managed to get to the top of Sigiriya, you need to start early before it gets hot, I am afraid of heights but I was determined to get to the top. Had alot of help from our fabulous tour guide Viraj from Jetwing.

It's one of the top attractions in that area . The entrance for foreigners is higher than locals . At the top, you will have an awesome 360 view . Else, you can go to a viewpoint to get a nice photos with the rock .

Beautiful view over the jungle. Climb the stairs that are built into the rocks, it's an advantage if you're not afraid of heights. Walk through the park beforehand. It's worth it early in the morning, afterwards it's very hot and there are lots of people
Great experience, must do. Take a guide so that you learn about all of the history and see the hidden parts. Not too difficult a climb, take a hat for shade and water.

Visited on the 28th August 2023. People say that Sigiriya is a must-visit place, and it's the number one attraction in Sri Lanka. However, I'm not sure if that's the case. Yes, the view from the top is beautiful, but that's all you get. Tickets for locals cost 100 rupees (0.25p), while for foreigners, it's 9000 rupees (£25.00). I understand that there should be some price variation between foreigners and locals, but charging foreigners 90 times more than locals is outrageous. Additionally, the climb to the top is dangerous, with no staff present in case of an emergency. You wouldn't know who to contact. Overall, I wouldn't recommend visiting this place. If you're passing through Sigiriya, you can take some beautiful pictures at the entrance without paying the exorbitant admission fees. However, if you do decide to go and climb the rock, take plenty of water bottles with you, as there are no shops once you pass the admission entrance. The climb takes about 60 to 180 minutes, and with the blazing hot sun and 1200 uneven steps, it can be quite challenging.
Super view inbthe top. We went top of sigiriya in the evening. We recommend when you go sigiriya try to go in evening.
The view is mesmerising!! It was windy but absolutely amazing place. The hike is a bit long, not too hard, but you can enjoy small breaks on the way and enjoy the view.
Beautiful climb with a scary final view. We did it at sunset with children aged 11,7 and 2. Very doable!

The incredible Sigiriya, and I must say, it exceeded all my expectations. The ancient rock fortress, surrounded by lush greenery, offers a mesmerizing glimpse. The architecture and engineering marvels showcased here are truly awe-inspiring. The ascent to the summit might seem daunting at first, but fear not—it’s not as tough as it appears. The breathtaking views from the top are absolutely worth every step. All in all, Sigiriya is a must-visit destination for history enthusiasts, nature lovers, and anyone seeking a blend of cultural exploration and stunning vistas. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable experience!

Overall a hard climbing but worth spending 30$ for entrance to see how the ancient king has lived inside the rock with the beautiful arts inside and the upper part, be aware of the monkeys which will steal your stuffs

We arrived at Sigiriya Rock at 7am. Tickets were 30 USD. A tour guide met us at the start which we assumed was included in the ticket price - very knowledgeable, friendly snd worth having a guide to learn about the history of the rock - however at the end of the trip he asked us for 10 USD each which we had not expected and later found out was not correct and should have been 10 USD in total not per person! Go careful and ask for the price before. The climb itself was tiring but manageable and felt safe with steps and guard rails. View from the top made the climb worth it. Be prepared to be hot and out of breath! (We are 4 reasonably fit people in our 20s)

It is a space that is worth visiting despite the $30 they charge per entrance (compared to the €20 in Pompeii, for example, it seemed a bit abusive to us). In any case, you have to visit it. I would advise going first thing in the morning to avoid the queues that form later to get on.

The views from the top are amazing. Recommended to go in the morning as there are little to no shades at the top. Make sure to have a hat and water. Nice experience. Tickets are a bit overpriced I think.
I think sigiriya is the best world heritage site in Sri Lanka. Best time to visit is morning. better have a comfortable shoes & cloths.

I’ve said this before about other attraction sites in Sri Lanka: the high entrance fees do not go towards the site itself which is very sad. On Lions Rock, a lot of signs on the site were damaged and could not be read. The app did not work either, garbage in the ponds… The museum is quite good compared to that in Polonnaruva. Although the building is already run down. For that reason, many other tourists we met in Sigiriya did not actually visit Lions Rock and only went up Pidurangala which costs merely a fraction of the fee. Still we thought it was worth a visit but 30USD is really the pain limit money wise. Definitively go as early as possible (they open at 5:30 am not 6:30 as many locals confirmed and was the case when we visited).

A magnificent place An isolated bank in the countryside is home to a very ancient royal palace The cave with frescoes with still very vivid colors is absolutely worth seeing It requires physical fitness because you have to climb 1200 steps Happy adventure
Fairly simple but impressive climb Enough at the park for $25/person Last admission at 5:00 p.m., great for seeing the sunset

This is the most beautiful and impressive place we saw on our trip to Sri Lanka. The history of the place is fascinating as is its shape. Better to make the climb in the morning with the mountain providing shade. Truly unique place!!!

Came here with a tour group, suggest come earlier in the day where the weather isn’t as hot. It’s such a beautiful view to the top (after many steps). Definitely check out the cave frescos although no photography is permitted. It’s amazing to imagine how this was built back then with no cranes or heavy machinery. The lion paws at the halfway mark are beautiful and majestic. Stairs are steep for the last portion. Unfortunately this activity would not suit anyone with mobility issues at all to climb. Great way to start the day with some cardio exercise. View is captivating

The climb up the most famous and publicized rock in Sri Lanka is absolutely worth it. I chose to go up in the evening to admire a splendid sunset from above. From a physical point of view, the climb is absolutely doable. For those who, like me, suffer from vertigo, there are some parts that are a little more complicated, especially the second and last part of the climb (when you reach the famous lion's paws). Once you arrive at the esplanade the view is simply crazy! I didn't take any guides, they are insistent it's true, but all you have to do is be determined and they'll let you lose. My advice is to go up for sunset and see the sunrise from Pidirangula rock, this is because the latter is more difficult to do after sunset. (You have to climb some rocks and it's a path while the climb to Lion Rock is 90% steps). ABSOLUTELY a must do!

it was fantastic, It's true that I really like historical parks but this is very spécial like crazy place built so quickly and so magnificient for a fairly short lifespan as a capital. an engineering treasure. I rode with a young baby on my shoulders, it's quite physical

Sigiriya is a must do!!! Highly recommended to go there early if you want to avoid the harsh afternoon heat. We left there in the morning like 5am and reached abouts 6am. It was perfect, wasn’t crowded. The architecture was very interesting. Can’t imagine a king lived right up there. My biggest highlight was Saman who is a local that has lovely souvenir’s. I was just inquiring, I had no interest to buy but he wasn’t pushy, he was so humble and explained to me on the meanings of the masked devils, the Buddha statues and other arts. Thank you so much saman, May you be blessed!
Interesting experience, fascinating history but hard work in hot sun with very little shade at top. Go early to avoid queues and heat.

The climb can be challenging at some parts where the steps are made of metal rods. Watch out for the several dogs that hang out at different parts of the rock and could even be found sleeping, blocking an entire step on the way. Don’t be disheartened when you see small kids and old people ascending faster than you. View from the top is nice, on a clear day. There is no shaded place at any point up from the lion’s paw segment of the rock. Would be advisable to bring sun shades and hat, and water bottle, and wet tissues to wipe your hands after you have descended.

A 'do not miss place'. the view from the top is nothing but magical....even go as far as on of the most beautiful sights. as for the climb, not easy but doable...pace yourself and take plenty of water, hot as the day we went. My personal opinion, you pay $35 US but you really don't need a guide, pretty self explanatory. the biggest issue was the 'un official helpers along the way. men who try and help you up the stairs if you are older. they were relentless and despite many attempt to politely ask them to stop trying to help, I had to be firm and insist, hated doing so but it was ruining the experience. aside from that, be firm but polite and enjoy the trip x Australia

The view is beautiful, the climb is quite difficult. Unfortunately, hardly any fountains work because it is the dry season. That makes sense and we knew that, but it does make the experience a lot less fun. The climb is tough, you may also be able to take beautiful photos from a nice terrace. Then you have the feeling that you are there, but not completely done yourself. This may be a much better option for people with reduced mobility or visual impairment.

Has been on my bucket list for years and it did not disappoint. Early start and started climbing at 5.30 making it to the top for sunrise. Although dark to climb was not as tough as I thought it would be and avoided the crowds and bottlenecks on the stairs that can happen later in the day. Stunning sunrise and amazing frescoes. Walked through the gardens on way down as many more people walking in for the climb Would advise an early start. Wish I had had some dog biscuits for the 2 dogs that followed me up to the top
This was amazing experience. The scenery was mind-blowing.our tour guide tOOk care of us untill end of the jouney

When we are able to visit Sigiriya, it is like stepping back in time and experiencing the greatness of a past civilization. The combination of historical significance, stunning architecture and natural beauty makes it a must-see destination for history buffs.

Absolutely the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. It is 1200 steps climb to the top of the rock fortress. We started earlier in the day as in July it can get very hot and humid during the latter part of the day. You do not need a great fitness level to be able to climb it. Anyone can climb it. If you are not used to climbing then you can take breaks at different intervals of the climb, where you have sitting areas and view points, when you take the breaks. I think it took me about 45 minutes to do the climb with the photographs in between and I am not in any great shape. Even if you have a fear of heights, it is not at all difficult to do the climb. Though looking at the steps clinging to the rock may seem challenging, it really is not, once you start climbing it. To see the frescos, you need to walk a very small path hugging the rock, which again looks like a vertigo inducing one, but once you walk, it is easily doable. The spiral staircase to the frescos also has barriers on all sides, so just take it step by step and you will be fine. Just make sure that you have water with you and a hat or a cap against the sun. You can do the climb to the top and back in less than 3 hours but it is nice to take the time to do the climb and stop at each section of the climb, which has interesting things while going up and down ( different paths if you go to the frescos ). You can easily spend an hour at the top, admiring the sweeping views and taking loads of pictures and giving your legs a rest for the climb down. You do not need a guide to take you to the top. Going up or down or to the frescos is pretty straight forward and you will not be rushed if you do it on your own.
It was a rainy day but finally we did it ,😍 we were there for 2 hours and our guide the local guy samatha took care of us untill the end of our journey

A must do for your Trip to Sri Lanka, the buxom celestial nymph frescos are  wonderfully preserved. There are lots of steps ,even before you get to the Lions feet- so take it easy and you will reach the top, lots of families of monkeys along your way and I have no idea how there was a dog at the top. The views are amazing, the ancient city was much smaller than It looks on the photos.I took around 15 minutes to walk around and I was expecting it it to take much longer.

On the 3rd day of our Tour of Srilanka, in the early morning at 06.30 am we proceeded for the visit of Ancient City of Sigiriya which is a  Rock Fortress. Sigiriya or Sinhagiri (Lion Rock) is also a UNESCO World Heritage site of historical and archaeological significance that is dominated by a massive column of granite rock approximately 180 m.

I wasn't expecting much before I went, but it ended up as one of the highlights in our trip. The rock is on top of a hill, so there are two parts in climbing up. Tips: - Try yout best to go earlier in the afternoon, as at the top it could be rather windy. I reached the rock level at 3pm - that was already a bit late in my opinion in July. - The second part looks a bit scary, but 10-year-old kids can make it. If you hire car, and the driver likely wait at the car park. Even if you have good sense of orientation, I suggest you ask him to mark it on the map how to get there, because there are many paths to get there, when on the way down..... you have too many choices to make ;-)
Definitely go here if you are staying in the area The paintings are incredible. It’s expensive but we think it worth the cost.

Sigiriya is such a beautiful and wonderful place. The hike is not bad at all, just many steps that are deffinitely worth to climb. For foreigners the entrace fee is quite high (10000LRK per person). We went wround 4.30 pm to see the sunset later on. This is a place you should not miss. So much of history, amazing views and peace in one spot.

1200 steps! It's mind blowing with the windy weather. I dare not turn my head to look left and right upon climbing (ACROPHOBIA).Reaching the summit, I feel like being in MACHU PICHU!All I could say is that the visit is to SRI LANKA is incomplete without a climb to SIGIRIYA! And a special thanks to our AMAZING, KNOWLEDGEABLE guide friend, DONALD KALUGAMAGE for his excellent service! He's worthy of praise! I'll be visiting again!

Once you reach the top of the rock, there's no turning back. You are a Royal. You feel indescribably powerful. The pool, the ruins, the view points and everything makes you feel Royal. You suddenly start wondering how King Kashyapa was looking out from the top, how the services were taken up the rock, how the bricks and other supplies were transported and many more things. You run of feelings at the top. Don't forget to feed the little pups guarding the top and who are following you to make sure your journey is safe and smooth. But, never leave any biscuit covers or plastic bottles at the top. It's a heritage site and when we take care of it only it will last.

Amazing climb and views, well-worth the fame! We went in the evening around 4pm and we’re so glad we did - very few people around, and the sun was less direct and intense, making the climb a bit easier. There are stairs all the way, feels a little precarious coming down at the top so make sure you start coming down before it gets dark. Worth a quick look around the museum beforehand - only 10-20 mins worth but gives you good context. Entrance is $30 (approx 9,250 LKR at time of writing).

Go while you can as I'm sure the 'Health & Safety' elves will close it 1 day 🙈. An amazing climb, quite a feat when I look back. It's hundreds and hundreds of steps either carved into the rock face centuries ago or using an iron staircase (in some parts spiral) in others what feels more like a ladder so not for the faint hearted. But oh the view when you finally get to the top is so worth it. 👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼 Would I do it again, definately....would i recommend it, definately...would I be as scared on the way up, definately....🤞🏻

The rock fortress was in nice grounds. The climb to the top was hard. My wife almost collapsed when we were near the top. We went early to avoid crods, so go before 10am. when we came down, there were about 10 times more people. The views at the top were stunning. HOWEVER, once inside you will be harrassed constanly and relentlessly to the point you get annoyed with the. I understand the hawkers are poor and struggle to survive but it was painful. Much worse were the employee 'helpers' paid by the tourism board. They will only target Westerners and will not take no for an answer. They tell you what you already know, try to 'help' when you don't need it and point out the obvious. They follow you all the way to the top and down again. When you leave, they DEMAND money and when you give them, they demand more saying it's not enough, even if you argue you told them no and to go away and you didn't want them to come. If you go, you need to just ignore them. As I said, the hawkers, you can understand but these guys are like vermin and spoilt our experience there.
Great location. Most historical place in the world. View is amazing. Everyone visith the sigiriya when you visit in sri lanka

It’s a tough climb but worth it just for the views. There are different stages as you ascend so plenty of time to catch your breath and take on water. We got up and down in around 2 hours but did it tough, my advice is to go early and take all the time you want as you will unlikely never do this again. Enjoy…….

Spectacular!!!!    I didn't go right to the top but got to 3/4 way up.  Tough climbing but now wish I'd done the last part as apparently it was easier going.  Loved the trip to Sri Lanka and plan to go back and see more.
Not a climb if you are unfit. The steps are steep and until you reach the top there are no hand rails. The guide, Bandara, was very helpful and knowledgeable about the area and surrounds.

Loved it at Sigiriya it is a really fascinating experience but just be aware that the climb can be quite daunting when it is hot and humid and that a good level of fitness is required to reach the top.

Loved our trip here, we went in the morning arriving by 9am and it wasn't too busy at all. The museum part at the start is a bit rubbish of the old photos but it was nice to see the jewellery and things uncovered from the site. The walk along the flat to the rock just brings home the scale of the place its just incredible. The climb up is all even steps and in different sections, the first part is steady wide stone steps with places to stop on the way. Once at the top of that you can see the stone lions feet as the entrance of the fortress itself. There are some dogs/ monkeys about so be careful of having food and drink out here but they were very calm and I never saw them trying to get anything from people. From here its tight metal steps and no places to stop but not as bad as it looks from the bottom. Once at the top of the fortress there is beautiful views over Sri Lanka. Easy to spend and hour or so wandering around and some places to sit and enjoy the views too. Definitely worth the money. Not sure how anyone can moan about the difference for tourists and locals - is their country of course they should enjoy it cheaper and tourists who can afford to travel should pay more to upkeep this beautiful place.

What can I say, this is one of the highlights of my 13 day trip to sri lanka! There are govt approved guides at base if you want to have a little history lesson and guide all the way to the top. I declined because I wanted to experience without alot of talk. Obviously  I went when  tourism was down in sri lanka so there were only about maybe 25 people or so I got to enjoy to myself. I took over a 100 photos and had all developed. There is photo opportunities at every step. The hike up and down took me about 3 hrs but I took my time, its steep but I'm used to hiking uphill. I can say it's safe but I would recommend being fit. The cost as I saw some complaining is NOT expensive of what you get to see. This is on the same scale as Machu picchu or chichennitza in cancun. So ignore those posts. $30is nothing to someone who comes from the west and travels that far!!. On a historical note this fortress dates 500 yrs before Christ. There's only one place at the top which you cannot take photos and a man sits there so you don't and thats ancient Buddhist frescos which very colorful. Once again, this fortress is an incredible place

One of the highlights of our holiday in Sri Lanka. This is an amazing experience. This must have looked fantastic when it was first completed. You can still see some of the Lion’s claws and there are still some of the original fresco paintings.you need to visit this place definitly.
Amazing view and one if the must visit places in Sri Lanka, but it's so hot during the day time, avoid weekend crowded and difficult to climb.

We went as part of our Walkers tour so included in our paid for itinerary. Our guide suggested going early so we started the climb at around 6 am and was at the top in 30-40 minutes. It is exhausting if like me you are not as fit as you though you were but the views on the way up and at the top are worth the effort. To see the sunrise and the forest jungle landscape below is literally breath taking. We sat for a while taking in the panoramic view then explored the fortress. Marvelled at how they would have built it in 400ad and then took the descent past the cave fresco and mirror wall. It’s a must do experience if you come to Sri Lanka.

Going up is a bit exhausting but coming down is scary…at the end you don’t feel disappointed as the journey is both rewarding and exciting View from the top is amazing it’s a protected site so lot of history is available avoid taking a guide as you don’t need one and you will be a lot happier doing this on your own instead of being heckled by a guide
Locals paying 100 rupees, foreigners paying 10.000 rupees, its like 30 cents for locals, 30 dollars for foreigners 🤣🤣 most shocking thing i have ever seen in my whole life.

This is a mind blowing experience, almost an 8th wonder of the world but I just can’t help but feel taken advantage of by the astronomical expense of entry - where does this money go? The upkeep of the site? Paying of guides to help you (no it can’t be as you have to pay extra for them)? It just feels like a bit of a low blow to be ripped off like this. Pidurangula was much cheaper and tbh more mind blowing of a view though with less historical importance

I and my boyfriend are a living proof that this place is manageable even on a rainy day. Actually, the experience is amazing! There were almost no people, shorter or none queues. Just bring a raincoat or an umbrella, and open sandals, and you will be fine. The complex consists from the rock that you will climb using the famous stairs. In the second half of this journey, there is something called Mirror Wall and then frescoes, which is a small cave with very old pictures with still vivid colors. The place is full of self-employed tour guides - locals that will follow you around, saying that they are tour guides and that you definitely need one. Then they will walk with you, talk with you, and expect money at the end. We were warned that there is no need for a tour guide and that the place is mostly about walking the stairs and the view afterwards. Lion's Paws is the stairway where are normally those long lines of people that are trying to get to the top of the rock. At t the base of the stairs, there are statues in a form of lion's paws, so hence the name. This place is what you want to experience when someone talks about Sigiriya Rock. And form my experience, it's the biggest fun! The Mirror Wall itself is not that wow, I would say. It's not shiny anymore, you can't touch it, it's just therein its not shiny form. Frescoes that are waiting for you at the end of the line are much more interesting, since it's something to look at. The line leading to the frescoes is heading among the Mirror Wall. It's not possible to take pictures of frescoes, thought, there is a lot of staff watching everyone so nobody does it. I didn't see any toilets on the way, just those at the ticket office. So count with that, if you want to spend few hours of wondering at the place, or if the queues on the particular day are too long.

It’s a well known rock on the tourist trail of Sri Lanka , but don’t let the crowds put you off, but go early to catch the morning light. This is a strenuous climb of stairs, metal staircases, and clambering of the ruins on the top, and anyone with vertigo might be advised not to do this, or those with weak stamina. That said it’s a fabulous view, and a great ruin with a nice history to it. You will be pestered by ‘guides’ offering to take you up there, but really they’re not necessary, and they want a tip of rupees for it. Basically you climb up the stairs ( over 1000!).

Dont go on a Full Moon holiday as crowds are huge!  But other than that expect to climb lots and lots of steps but well worth it for the view and to learn about the despot king who was carried around there and had 500 concubines too!

Beautiful ancient rock fortress! Easy climb. We really enjoyed the views. Only reason I’m giving it a 2 starts is because of our guide. We actually had a great time once he left us alone. Be careful with tour guides and “helpers” We had a man following us from the start and he was talking about the Sigiriya Rock. After approximately 5 minutes he stated that he was a freelance guide and offered to accompany us to the top while telling us about the history of this rock fortress. He stated that he didn’t have a price and we could decide at the end what to pay him depending on how we liked his services. We agreed. About 5 minutes after that he brought us to a man selling “magic boxes” and insisted we try to open them. We were not interested in buying any boxes. A few minutes after that his friend arrived and started “helping” me up the stairs. I did not ask for help nor was it needed.  He insisted on holding onto my hand however it was very awkward and opposite of helpful. It quickly became hazardous as none of the steps are the same size and walking with a stranger like that out of the blue was weird. This helping up the steps became annoying and I tried numerous times to stop it but he kept holding his hand out. My husband was actually walking behind us and thought it was the funniest thing.  It’s funny now looking back at it. He even snapped some photos. After a few more sets of steps I had to tell my husband that I am not climbing 1200 steps and up the rock like this. Luckily we were still in the beginning. My husband told our guide who translated to the helper that his assistance was not needed. We were then told he doesn’t work for free! Our guide then told us that his services were $40-$50! We paid less for a taxi drive with all our luggage from the airport to our hotel! Be careful! We told both of them to have a nice day however the guide still wanted money for his services “thus far”   Ruins the experience!

Well worth a visit.  Recommend that you take one of the numerous guides who are at the entrance waiting for tourists to roll up.  They all wear a uniform polo shirt so you know that they are offical guides, however as like anywhere you need to be prepared to negotiate a price.  We paid $20 US for a guide for 3 hours, our guide was excellent giving you a lot of background to the fortress which you would not get from reading the information pamphlet you get given with your ticket.  There are toilets located just by the ticket office, very clean but no toilet paper so make sure you take tissues.  There is also a water station before you enter with purified drinking water where you can fill up your water bottle.  Be prepared to climb up narrow stairs to get to the top, the view is amazing and worth the climb.  When we went in Feb there were no hornets which we had read about however we were told that it was the wrong season.  Beware of monkeys everywhere which is all part of the Sri Lankan experience.  When you exit the fortress there are numerous toilet blocks which were all clean and well maintained, again take your tissues.  Make sure you wear comfortable walking clothes, shoes, hat and take water, there is nowhere to purchase water along the way until the exit.  We arrived about 9.30ish which we found to be fine, the heat was bearable, the timing of your visit will all be dependent on the time of year you go.

About 1200+2 steps on the top most point of the summit. This hill was developed by King Ravana and later occupied by Buddhists monks. These monks were then relocated by King Kashyapa and the hill was developed into a full fledged fort. This fort had a robust defence system containing concentric circles of water, quick sand, crocodiles and barracks of soldiers guarding the palaces. One gets to see remains of water fountains and swimming pools used by the kings of the past. Right next to the swimming pool is a huge elephant shaped stone. On the way up are soldiers barracks, a huge stone resting on a hill, paws of the lion and steps leading to the summit. Do note that the original lion head is no longer in place and only the paws can be seen. Once you reach the summit there is a series of ruins of walls, beautiful scenic view of the forests and a buddha statue in the distance which is the second largest standing statue in the world. (note: not on same this hill). On the way down, there is a cave with a few paintings and a mirror wall(a plastered wall) and resting rooms of the king. Followed by a cobra head shaped rock, an open conference area and another rock pass leading to the outward area where you can buy souvenirs. All in all, I would the say the place is worth visiting since it is a UNESCO heritage site and has a rich past. However things to keep in mind are: 1. Guides are optional since every major check point has a bar code readable display and a placard of information. 2. It can get extremely hot if you start after 8am. So plan to be there early and do not underestimate the number of steps. 3. Steps are not even, damaged in some areas and extremely steep as well. Without proper posture one will definitely slip and injure themselves. 4. After a tough climb do remember that all you will see there are ruins that do not speak anything about the history as such for a layman. Limited objects to see but the climb is definitely worth the view. 5. Sellers need a bit of haggling and are very polite to tourists. 6. Carry a bottle of water since it isn't sold until you reach the exit. Can be difficult on a humid day. 7. Keep an eye on kids while you walk through the initial garden patches, since insects are not rare. But nothing to worry for a regular tourist.

My Husband and I were here 4 weeks ago and decided to go early in the morning at 7am as the heat and humidity was just horrid anyway and thought it would be less then, but it really wasn't. Anyway we went shortly after opening time which is at 7am. Now, we are both nearly 60 years old and totally unfit fatties and both of us have bad hearts, bad knees and ankles, plus me with an already sprained ankle from a collapsing bridge a week earlier, but hey, I wasn't going to come all this way from Australia and not climb this Sigiriya Rock right?. Anyway we climbed to the very top in 50 minutes from the very start to the very top, including a few stops in between to catch our breath and trying to stop out hearts from exploding, but just quietly were were so very proud of ourselves, so kudos to us. Now just a word of warning, for those of you who have really bad knees or ankles this climb is not for you, and if you have even the slightest fear of heights, this climb is definitely not for you. I'd say go as far as the Lions feet and that's it as it is really frightening after that especially if people are trying to get past you and your clinging to the edge of the rock for grim death while letting them pass. For those of you who are not scared of heights then go on up to the very top, the 360 degree view you will love and you get to see all the ruins also. I must say watch out for the scammers too who will approach you along the way up at different points, they will make conversation with you and try and help you get up rocks etc and they will start to tell you all about the rock and the history and then they will become your guide without you even knowing about it and it will cost you money, but if you want to use them then go ahead, these locals are desperate for money. Also when you get there, there is no signage, well in English anyway, to where you buy the entry tickets from, we found it a bit confusing where to go to get the tickets, and that's a walk in itself too. There are plenty of Tuk Tuks at the bottom when you come back down that will take you back to your Hotels at a reasonable price. Just be aware that where the Tuk Tuks will drop you off at the start where you buy your tickets from is not the same place where you finish up when you come back down from the rock, you seem to get rail roaded out a different exit to an other side of the rock so you end up having to go past all the souvenir stalls. Our rooky mistake was telling our Tuk Tuk driver to pick us up here where he dropped us off, and he failed to tell us this was not the spot you finish up at when you come down from the rock, so once we came down and realised this was not where we started from, we then had to figure out how to get back around to the other side of the rock where the entrance was to meet our tuk tuk driver who was waiting so patiently for us, it was a long walk in the heat. All in all, we were both glad we did it and didn't drop dead from heat exposure and blown heart valves. We never want to see another step again as long as we live, our knees and ankles were aching for days afterwards. But done it now and so a big TICK off our bucket list.

DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME, EFFORT AND MONEY This is a over hyped place most probably by locals to attract tourists and extort money. There is nothing special about this place, other than steep climbing of a huge rock using steel staircase. Ticket for foreigners USD30 per person, USD15 for people from SAARC countries, for locals it is Sri Lankan Rupee 50/-. The steel staircase is very narrow and most of the part climbing up and down use the same narrow path, so it slow down the movement of the people. With so many people climbing up and down on the narrow staircase, there is a chance of stampede like situation.  NOT AT ALL SAFE. I had been to many UNESCO sites, this one is a BIG disappointment. CLIMB PIDURANGALLA ROCK INSTEAD. BETTER VIEWS, MORE FUN AND MUCH CHEAPER.

This was spectacular, and a must-do for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. We managed it in a day-trip from Kandy, but were up at 6.30am to make it work. We’d recommend staying nearby and combining it with Pidurangala (another absolute must), Kaludiya Pokuna, and perhaps Polonnaruwa. The view at the top is spectacular – make sure you leave plenty of time to explore Royal Gardens at the bottom, Boulder Gardens at the end, and the archaeological remains at the top. We had a wonderful time.
