This place is not for the unfit as there are a lot of stairs but the views and the whole experience is amazing. We were lucky because it was overcast for our climb. Definitely bring water and wear sunscreen and a hat.
This the kingdom built by king Kashapa. This place world famous and beautiful place.we can see paintings, Mirror wall,ruins & water parks.This is 8th wonder of the world.

Firstly it's a ruin. So you don't get to see walls or actual structure. It's left to your imagination. It's for people who love to trek, climb, walk in the hot sun. I would suggest you to not go by the Ariel view or drone shots. You won't find the place like that unless you are flying. So once you reach the top after walking, climbing, sweating it's entirely left to your imagination. Price is high. Do it if you like sweating it out. The view is nice from the top. You can just feel WOW and think how someone would have built a palace on this huge rock. That's about it.

I LOVE LOVE Sigiriya! One of the best places I have visited. Lion's Rock (ancient rock fortress) mesmerising to see and can't wait to visit again. Note: I am writing this review is after completing 15 days holiday in Sri Lanka; therefore, I have considered all pro and cons.

We had a great experience around this rock fortress. The Tickets for SAARC nations are at a discounted rate of 15USD. you need to provide your actual passport to avail the discount. For non saarc nations the tickets are 30 USD. We hired a local guide who asked for 5K LKR but we bargained and got him to agree for 3K. He explained all relevant details right from the start. Great site to visit.. The climb is a little strenuous and become overcrowded sometimes. Overall we completed the climb and descend in around 2 to 2.5 hours (along with my kid - 7 year old). View from the top is great . you can see a huge buddha statue a little far away and also the pidirangula rock. Overall i recommend a visit to this heritage site.
While a tour guide is not included, the driver did his best to show me the places I wanted to see and customized the trip based on my list.

Amazing destination for those who like to explore heritage sites. Climb to the lion rock top is a bit strenuous. Best time to start the climbing is in the morning, avoid climbing in hot sun. The museum has some splendidly preserved artefacts dating back to 2 century A.C. This also houses 5000 (claims) year old human remains. Tools and Furnaces dating back to 2nd to 5th Century A.C. Amazingly preserved earring.

Had a lovely time wondering around with hardly anyone else there! People were working on the gardens and doing maintenance ready to welcome people back. The frescos were incredible, luckily our guide knew a lot about them as there wasn't any information around.

We had a great tour of Sigiriya! It was an excellent experience with a very knowledgeable guide! We highly recommend this tour! It was really nice to hear so much about the history of the Sigiriya, the extensive engineering feats, and the wildlife.
Overrated and over priced. I understand this is to protect the ruins, but the opposite hike of pidurangala is much more challenging and beautiful, and you get the view of the sigiriya rock.

We were thinking of doing this at 8 am but kids did not wake up so decided to reschedule it to 3 30 pm. we started the climb around 3 45 to 4pm after buying tickets and I felt it was much easier to do than we expected as as it was not as hot and had a good breeze on the top. I felt morning would have been more hotter. overall not much structure on top just a nice gorgeous view. there is no water or food being sold on top so carry your own snack and water. just treat it like a nice trek with steps and enjoy the view on the top.

You can see the rock for miles around and it does look a little daunting when it comes to climbing up to the top.  In fact, although it is 1200 steps up and the same down, taking a steady pace, it wasn't too bad.  If you don't like heights - just keep going and don't look down.  The metal walkway takes you up the last few metres and it's worth it when you get up for the view (and sense of achievement).  Don't miss the side walk across the front of the rock and the spiral staircase to visit the caves.
The view from the top is amazing really good view Although to clam to the top must go through stairs more than 1000 one but it definitely the BEAUTIFUL view ever

A must visit in Sri Lanka, a hidden jewel. A must see for people who like history and culture. A special mention to Priyanthe who was our guide for the tour. He was very helpful and had deep knowledge of the Rock Fortress. Note - if you are from SAARC countries, carry your passport, you will get a 50%discount. And would definitely recommend a guide. It takes approx. 2 hrs to complete the climb and come down. The view from the top is just breathtaking.

This must be part of your Sri Lanka tour. This is a fort ruin and to imagine this was constructed before the advent of modern technology is breathtaking. Few things to note when you plan this tour: 1. It's a steep climb of 1200 steps. If you are not used to climbing, it can be daunting. 2. Definitely get a guide to learn some amazing details about this fort. 3. The overall time, going up, staying for pics, and coming down will take about 3-4 hours. Depending on how many selfies you may want to take the duration will change. 4. Check out the frescos dating back 100 of years that are still preserved. You can see this on your way back. 5. Since it's just the opening of tourism, do not expect food stalls. Carry your own water bottles. The situation as on end-of-nov 21. 6. There are no restrooms once you begin the ascent. 7. You can wear your shoes all the way up, and also wear comfortable clothes. 8. Keep an umbrella or a poncho, incase it rains. 9. For citizens from SAARC countries, there is a price discount. You must show your passport for tickets.

If you're in the area, a visit to this ancient rock fortress (a.k.a Sigiriya) is a definite must visit! Although the climb to the top isn't easy, the view from the top combined with the history surrounding it makes the climb well worth it. Tip: Plan your climb so that you aren't at the top at midday when the sun is scorching hot. Also you might want to apply sun screen.
An ancient rock fortress which was shaped like a lion back in the head. It's not an easy climb but the view from the top as well as what you see along the way makes it well worth it!
this is my favorite trip. Amazing 360 view. Like to climb again and again. Specialty i like to the Bees and breeze on the top.

If you are looking to break a sweat and get some steps in.. I definitely recommend this historic site. You will be rewarded with a nice view! I would recommend bringing a water bottle and wear comfortable shoes.

The ticket price is high, anyway it is worth. You can see large archeological complex in the bottom and on the top of the rock and historical paintings too. Visit Lion's rock before sunset and enjoy spectacular view!

Offers lovely views of the region. There are about 600 steps to climb, the first few are steps in rock and later on steel steps bolted on rocks. The climb is steep but doable. Contrary to earlier reviews, all the steps now are in perfect condition and it is safe to climb. There are railings throughout so you have something for support. There is a lush green garden before you begin the climb and a small musuem. While on top, you can see the remains of the foundation of the erstwhile palace, and the pond (/swimming pool). There are only about a few trees so make sure you carry sun protection and plenty water and some snacks. There are no shops / shacks en route or on top. On the way down, you can climb up a few stairs again for paintings in the cave. PS: if you're from SAARC countries, do NOT forget your passport. The ticket prices are significantly lower for SAARC citizens but you'll get that rate only if you're carrying the passport, soft copy is not accepted.

Worthwhile visit but maybe not quite matching the hype, especially in considering the views offered by neighbouring Pidurangala were better and the weather was a little sub-prime. The admission price of $30 felt a little steep. The museum bit was very good and informative but felt a little short. The ponds and gardens are beautiful and interesting. The walk up felt crowded at times. The temple ruins at the top did not have enough information around them to help you picture the magnificence of this place as it was centuries ago. A trip to Sigiriya is definitely worthwhile and helps put into perspective how ancient the Sri Lanka culture is, but maybe did not match up to our unfairly high expectations going by what we had seen from neighbouring viewpoints.

Do not visit Sri Lanka without visiting here. The views once on top are breath taking, you can see for miles and it’s beautiful. Also you get the benefit of learning all about the history during the stop, the grounds surrounding the rock are just as beautiful. Just be aware there are a lot of steps to get up! But you do have a break about half way up.

We saw the tripadvisor review and after we planned to go to visit the Sigiriya. It is the good decision we got. It was fantastic experience for me and my family. My kids were overenjoied. It was wonderful journey .i highly recommended to all this place to visit.

The rock fortress is a must to visit in Sri Lanka. When we where there in the beginning of november 2021, we was almost the only visitors, due to covid. But it is clear they are used to many many visits every day. We bought a guide at the gate to show is around, it was worth all the money. We spend 9 days in total travelleling around to turists sites, but this one is a clear no 1.

It is an impressive natural feature which we enjoyed exploring. However, there are many good aspects to the area but it could be executed slightly better. If you want to find out more about the history, it would be better to do research before coming to the attraction. We would have expected a lot more pomp, but it seems to be more low-key. It was relatively expensive to get in, but worth it overall. It took around 30 minutes to get to top, but overall spent around two hours in the area.
We, Sri Lankans, believe it as the 8th World wonder.The palace complex was built in the 6th century AD.before that it was a Buddhist monastery complex.

From walking through the water gardens and seeing the spectacular rock to actually walking around on top of it this is a wonderful experience. I would go as far to say one of my top 3 archaeological experiences. We took it nice and steady and took between 3-4 hours to complete the site. Wonderful photo opportunities at every point. You can't take pictures of the frescos, but there are copies in the museum where you can. One day later still in awe of the place and should be on everyone's 'bucket list' in my opinion. Cost at the current time LKR6000, but worth every Rupee.
Awesome experience just how old and sophisticated everything is - but get here early in the day

Sigiriya is situated in middle of Sri lanka. That kingdom built by king kashyapa. Sigiriya fresco is second to Indian ajantha fresco. Garden and rock surrounded by water cannels. that is famous place among local and foreign traveller's.

Located in the Matale District, Sigiriya dates back to the 4th century. With its tourist attractions, this is known as the 8th wonder of the new world. This is one of the must visit destinations in Sri Lanka.

If you intend to visit Sigiriya, prepare to arrive early in the morning. Climb Sigiriya in the morning. The surroundings are breathtaking. When the wind blows with a little dew, it's a little chilly. But it was a fantastic experience for me and my family. The youngsters were overjoyed. Kids are fascinated by the historical narrative of Sigiriya. On the same day, we learned about the ruins near Sigiriya and their history. It was a wonderfully enjoyable and instructive vacation.

We visited here. This time with much knowledge of the fortress and the surrounding area. We had ample time to visit the area. It was somewhat warm you must have have enough water. It took us about 3 hours to cover the area.

My third climb this time with a 9 year old in tow. Left the hotel a bit behind schedule which meant were were at the car park around 9am. While driving I spotted a board mentioning local car park. So I drove towards that. Car park to entrance ticket counter is about 01 +KM walk. I didn't measure, alternatively you can take a tuk for a few hundred rupees. Due to the pandemic the crowds were less and it was nice to have space and less crowd to e joy the climb up. It was a lot g climb. Walk past the garden to the base and then comes the first set of steps to reach the lions paw area. Onwards are the rest of the steps via a iron staircase and a narrow one to the top. The last bit of stairs and you are at the top. Exhausted! Amazing views all around and my son enjoyed exploring the area while I caught my breath! It took as about two hours from car park to the summit. With plenty of breaks in between. Coming back down was a far more pleasant experience, we didn't walk up to see the frescoes as my son had enough and wanted to get back to the hotel. It took about 45 mins coming down. Like another reviewer has suggested I do recommend purchasing drinks or other items from the vendors below on your way down as they are most impacted by the decline of tourism in that area. entrance tickets for locals are 100 rupees.

Breathtaking scenery, recommended time to visit Sigiriya is early morning or evening. But if you visit Sigiriya in the morning, you could see around and visit places like Aligala Cave, Kaludiya Pokuna (The Black Pond).

It was sad to see how empty this place because of the COVID-19 pandemic. But I’ve enjoyed this time as I’ve spend few extra hours just to relax myself as not many people around. If you are planning to visit Sigiriya make sure you are on your walking and outdoor gears. Approximately 8000 steps . I would suggest that you would buy something from the street sellers just help for the local communities as they have suffered heavily in this pandemic time
Third visit and this place blew my mind as always with it's amazing views. The climb is worth it whether you are young or old - you can make it to the top!

The rock is very impressive, standing quite alone in the middle of the forest. At the beginning, you will cross the former gardens with some water basins; one of them is in form of octagon. Then you begin to climb the stair, about 1.600 steps! However, you will find several terraces and belvedere where you can stop and take advantage of the view. I stopped at the platform where the ruins of the Lion Gate are because I had crutches for walking and it was impossible for me to go ahead. Pay attention you must not have vertigos to climb the last part, the stairs are actually in the void! More or less at mi-walk you will find wonderful paintings, unfortunately, there is not a lot of place and you cannot stay long time. Pictures are strictly forbidden. It is suggested to visit the rock in the morning or in the late afternoon, you will find less tourists and less humidity. Take some water with you there are no kiosks inside the site.

It took us several hours to reach there. A long, tiring climb, surrounded by a huge crowd. Of course, you’re treated with an amazingly beautiful view from the top. Just be prepared to be jostled a bit by the locals during the climb. The frescos themselves took just a few minutes to see - suddenly you feel ‘hey, did I trek so long to see these few meters of frescos?’. Of course, they are beautiful and of historic significance. Maybe a good idea to start in the early morning to avoid the midday heat.
We started in the morning and that is the best time before the sun makes it warmer. Make sure you have a good guide with you to give an insight into the place. Not for the faint-hearted though.

Sumitting Sigiriya has been a lifelong dream.. it took three decades, a pandemic and a few adventurous friends to make it come true. When I told people it was my first time, they were in shock..I now understand why. It transcends time and space, and is worth every step you take and the aches after. Take your time to savor the sumitt. There's quite a few things to see and relish

One of the must visit place in Sri Lanka & great wonders of the world. This is a UNESCO heritage site protected for its history. Sigiriya rock fortress is a classic example for Sri Lankan ancient architecture & talent of the people. Weekends are generally busy & suggests to visit on week day.

This 5th century AD rock fortress is a must visit for any local visitor or foreigner. starting the journey very early (gates open at 06.30am) will be great as you can escape from the scorching midday sun and large number of visitors at late hours.it takes about 45min to get to the top of the rock normally.there is a vast number of places to see around the rock but most visitors tend to get to the top and also see the frescoes. the view from the top is breathtaking and the wind is very strong. Follow the instructions given along the way to prevent damage to the historic remnants and escape the attacks of giant honeybees nesting around the rock(this is a very rare incident).carry a bottle of water with you and don't dispose any polythene or plastic items on the way. Make sure to visit the museum at the entrance of the fortress.

No visit to the central province is complete until you have experienced the wonder that is Sigiriya.  Given the pandemic, we feel very fortunate to have explored the rock with minimal tourists.  Stunning and a must see.

Amazing experience. One should start the climb as early as possible. A fitting cap as the wind is strong and the sun is hot,  also would recommend to wear a light cotton long sleeved shirt/ blouse when climbing. You need to carry a bottle of drinking water On your person whilst keeping both your hands free to hold the rails. It took us approximately 1 hour 45 minutes to climb to the top and return. Currently due to COVID the Public car park is closed so one can park near the entrance and take a Tuk to the start of the climb. Tuk cost approx Rs 150 per one way. Advisable to do this as the walk to the start is 3 kilometers of scorching sun.

Different experience for both of us.This is our first hiking together. We talk about the kings fully facilitated castle. And how much safety that place to him. And why lots of song writers written about this kingdom and the king with beautiful womans .The paintings talks about kings artistic feelings. We sang songs about this lovely kingdom. All of those things felt us this hike is how romantic...
Tough but can be done! super signage to guide you and the people around are very helpful. Friendliest doggies around to keep you company

Its known as the 8th world wonder It's better to stay in a hotel at Sigiriya and start climing the rock early in the morning as its its too warm during the noon. No cloting restrictions and since there is steps to the top climbing isn't hard as well. It's a fortress and not a kingdom owned by king Kashyapa. But early historical stories go back to Rawana era.......

My Sigiriya tours provided the best service for us :) Chandu helped us a lot and he showed a little bit of his village beauty. He cares about us all the time. Like our fathers. But he is a young father. He recommended us a place to stay for a month. It was the perfect place. We really had fun there. We followed the Chandu. He made our plans. They are really good plans. The best thing was to spend the night camping in the jungle. We had a lot of experiences that we had never experienced before. At once we felt like fish living in the water. That's because we're camping in the most beautiful lake in Sigiriya. We climbed the Pidurangala rock, we climbed the Sigiriya rock and went swimming in the Thalkote lake. Chandu took us to see the hidden beauty of Sigiriya.  " Mapagala Fortress, Galkanda Temple, Kaludiya Pokuna, Ritigala, and jungle safari ". If you want, you can help Chandu get a guide to study history or the past in depth. There is a lot to write but I will stop here. Chandu's service is excellent and I highly recommend him to you.

It is better that you visit the place early in the morning. to avoid the heat. The ticket counters open at 6 a.m. If you are not the person who like to walk to the site (approx 1.5 km) it is best that you take a Tuk up to the entrance which will cost you around LKR 300/-. Just call the place and see whether the frescoes  are open for public view. Otherwise you will be disappointed when the frescoes are closed due to wasp attacks. There are plenty of other things to view apart from the frescoes however they are the center of attraction. The view from top of the rock is overwhelming. So is the ruins of the palace of king Kashyap
Really Enjoyed with My Sigiriya Tours Team.  They showed us many hidden places around Sigiriya and they teach us about history. Thank you & sure we'll come back to sigiriya.

Panoramic views of the lush green forest is worth the trek up. Get there early to avoid the crowds and the heat and do take enough water with you, It's nice trek up to the top, but plenty of places on the way to catch your breath and enjoy the views. If you are afraid of heights, be aware that part of the trek up are narrow stairways, but everything is fairly safe. You can explore the area around the temple after you get down. The view of the rock from the bottom is just as pretty as the view of the forest from the top.

this place is great for people interested in history. It is safe though it is a long hike to the top. People scared of height should not climb as well as those with physical ailments as there are a lot of steps. has caves with beautiful paintings right in the middle of the climb. The place is very crowded and need to be careful as there is only some room to climb. this place is associated richly with sri lanka's history. The climb is steady. The best part of it is the view from the top though there are incredible views throughout the climb. it is enchanting and fills one with amazement. it is covered with forests on all sides.A must see when in sigiriya.

Before you climb the rock there are lots of structures and courtyards at the base which is worth spending a bit of time exploring. There are lots of steps to climb up to the top with picturesque views on the the way up. At the top there are more structures and incredible views which are wonderful at sunset. It is very busy and touristy and much more expensive than visiting the nearby rock at Pidurangala (highly recommend as you can see Lion Rock from there). If you're in Sigiriya then this is a must see (but we prefer Pidurangala).
Two trips to Sri Lanka in a year and two visits to the rock fortress! Definitely a highlight of the area, a great experience!

Beautiful place full of history - we had our driver with us who told us all about it which was fascinating! There are a lot of steps but lots of places to catch your breath if you need to. Take your time - absolutely worth it to the top! Railings all the way and a comfrtable walk (compared to Pidurangala!). We went mid afternoon - very hot but not many people at all which was great. Would absolutely recommend to anyone visiting the area.

As my experience Sigiriya is the most popular tourist spot in Srilanka having the written history back to 1600 years. not just climb the rock. but there are so many things to see from the ground in each step. so many ruin areas in the each step at the ground level water garden another mid-level of the rock the with ancient frescos, mirror wall, flight up to step through the line paw entrance and at the summit in palace. and some techniques of architectural and building the kingdoms the world history. of course this is a one of world wonder. Recommend to receive this early morning or in the afternoon and avoid the noon because of hot.

The approach is through ancient landscapes gardens, the Lion Rock has  thousands of steps but well hewn, with safe handrails & passing places. However it's well worth the climb, as the carving of the colossal lion, and the steps between his paws to climb up to the temple is an extraordinary feat of skill.  Plus the views are far reaching and themselves, worth the climb

The climb up Sigiriya is well worth it! Take your time and you will get there :) It's best to start the climb early if possible around 6.30-7.00am. It is also worth getting a guide as they can explain the history of the  rock as you go. If you go early there  are far less people and it is much cooler for climbing. It can get very hot from about 9.30am on, and those 1,200 steps can become challenging. It will take about 2-3 hours to climb up and back down, but the view from the top is well worth the effort.

We had limited time so we focused on climbing to the top.  However, our tour guide showed us the amazing water/irrigation system that could only be seen during rainy season.  It was quite amazing given it was built so long ago.  So if you have time, don't miss exploring the grounds. Also, if it is an option, go on a cloudy day.  We lucked out - we went on a cloudy day and the climb was so much easier.

If u climbing the sigiriya rock , best time to visit in early morning .i was start to climb the rock at 6.30 am. Becos the weather s too hot due to the summer. U hv to buy tickets from ticket counter .it s located in between Sigiriya & Habarana town, turn right from Inamaluwa-Sigiriya junction. It s hight from 660 ft from ground  . This palace built in 473 - 495 reign by king kashyapa. have to climb 1200 steps to reach top of sigiriya rock fortresses . It will take 1.5 to 3 hrs to climb up & get back to down . There s several platform s that u can take break .. if ur tired. When u getting to top of the rock ,there s a brick structure of the king kashyapa palace .It s a best hiking experience u can have in Sri lanka. & Also be the eye witness of the Sri Lanka s proud heritage.

My vertigo has got worse with age. It was put to the test getting up the stairs to the top of the rock, but thankfully one of the local guides put his hands on my waist and guided me up. It gave me a little bit of security that I needed to finish the trek. The fact there was one of Sri Lanka's many cute stray dogs at the top of the rock just rubbed salt into the wound and made me realise I should have been a little more robust. Sigiriya is one of Sri Lanka's best-known sites to see and it easy to understand. It is an incredible archaeological site, and the mind boggles when you reach the top passing the ancient steps people clambered up, and you realise a whole civilisation lived here. The views from the top are truly breathtaking and well worth the wobbly legs on the way up. Monkeys and butterflies and fortunately no hornets were enough distraction from the rocky drop below. The walk-up is a workout, and I was dripping with sweat when I reached the top but having said that it was over 30 degrees, so dripping with sweat was just the norm. If you go to Sigiriya and don't think you will make it to the top, then I would recommend not going. Getting to the top is what this excursion is about, and once there, the sense of achievement is tremendous but more significant is the experience of what you see all around. There are plenty off guides around if you want one. I would have got one personally, but my partner is a little more frugal and not as free-tipping as I. But when a man is willing to hold the waist of another grown man with wobbly legs to get him to the top - he deserves a tip. Sigiriya is the kind of place that now lives in my dreams, and for that, I am grateful.

A fabulous experience as only 4 of our group made it to the top. As a fairly fit 60+ I thought it was pretty tough in places. Maybe i had too many Lion Beers ?? Either way, this 5th Century marvel was created by King Kassapa 1 and was used up till the 12th C. The moats & ramparts and the steep climb kept the invaders at bay. The frescoes paintings are worth the effort and the ladies are nice !  The terraced gardens & the water movements were all before their time ! A wonderful trip & glad we decided to do it. Anyone can get to the top if they just pace themselves, it is worth it !

This is a must-see for any traveller to Sri Lanka.  We were lucky that because of the coronavirus outbreak, there were very few people there, so we were able to rest at frequent intervals on the the climb: there are plateaus on the way up.  I think it would be very hard if crowded, but the views are spectacular and the Lion's Gate is amazing: I stopped there but it's well over halfway up.  You just have to see it to believe it!  Take lots of water and sensible shoes, and arrange a reputable guide before you get there (there is a lot of history to be explained) - there are lots of men at the entrance who offer to take you up but expect a lot of money.

This rock is doable, provided you go in the morning. Luckily when we went, there weren't  many people climbing, so we could take our time climbing up, and coming down. There are resting areas, so you could have a breather. Carry water and wear comfortable shoes though.

We arrived on a wet morning and started to climb with some trepidation, wondering if we would be able to see anything.  The climb was not as bad as we feared as there were plenty of places to have a break and when we arrived at the top, the rain had stopped and views were magnificent.  Well worth the early start and the many steps to the top.

We climbed the rock very early in the morning to avoid the worst of the heat but it still gets very hot, take lots of water with you. Lovely walk through the gardens and moat to the bottom of the rock. Lots of steps and even a spiral staircase, some parts one way. Our guide was very informative about the history of the rock. Amazing views from the top, there are remains of the swimming pool and throne area. Quicker coming down with a few stalls and water/ice cream at the bottom. Highly recommended, tough climb but worth it, take your time!
A climb up to the ruins on top of this amazing rock is a bit strenuous, but for reasonably fit people very gratifying because of the fantastic view from top

Sigiriya Rock is beautiful and the history behind it is incredible, but it is not a place for people who are scared of heights. I went with my spouse and she had a hard time getting up the narrow stairs. The structures are safe and well reinforced, but simply  put, if you are afraid of metal stairs on ledges, don't climb all the way to the top.
Worth the effort but definitely should be undertaken in the morning and not the afternoon
A unique fortress with surrounding gardens. Everything built in and used for only some 10 years. They did it without modern technology. Shame on us

WOW. Awsome sight driving up to the site. 1222 steps to summit, not a trip for the faint hearted, but well worth the strenuous effort needed.300 meters above sea level. Wall paintings in excellent condition considering the age of them. Be careful of the monkeys trying to steal anything.

Fascinating insight into Sri Lankan history so well preserved and presented! The museum and grounds are extremely interesting but do be aware the walk to the top is not suitable for those of us with mobility issues!
Definitely worth the climb, but I would recommend going there early in the morning as it gets very hot and crowded.
Magnificent views from the top and an amazing climb with 100's of others, Best to start around 7 AM while its cooler. Great history and a must do in Sri Lanka. Coming down is very easy.

This is a great historic site. It is well worth the effort of climbing up to see the various points of interest but the bit is the actual views when you get to the top of the rock. This is a must visit site when you are in Sri Lanka. Make it a full day trip to get the best out of your visit.

We went to Sigiriya March 2020.It is a fantastic place and well worth a visit.Many guides came and offered us help,we said no thankyou.A man suddenly came ,said he was a helper,started to take my hand in the stairs.We said no thankyou but he went all way up and down with us.After that he wanted money,said he usually get 30-40$ !(that is for one hour) Bewere of them,they just want a lot of money!
This place is very interesting and the views are incredible! Get there early to avoid long queues. It's a bit pricey but worth it as this place is something else.

Took me some time to decide scaling Sigiriya due to one bad knee but am glad I attempted it upon hearing the story behind it and reached the top after much huffing and puffing.  Having done it, I must say the stairs are manageable if you pace yourself and keep hydrated as the temperatures can go up as the day progresses. There are also many locals who would offer to help for a fee, but I found that saying no thanks decisively holds them at bay. After reaching the Lion's Staircase, the climb u the metal stairs are a little more steep with less resting platforms but once you reach the top, one can appreciate the ruins of this architectural monument. Hard to imagine how one can build a palace on the rock until you see the remnants of ancient urban planning for yourself.

This was an amazing place. First things first, there are over 1,200 steps to climb, 370 metres high. Take it slowly you will get there. Once you reach the top, the views and the sights is incredible. I probably spent an hour or more up there, just walking around, imagining what was there. It was certainly an experience not to be missed.

This is one of the impressive UNESCO World Heritage Sites we have visited. Steep entrance fee LKR5,460 per person, but it is well worth it! Since 5th century, this place was built by the King Kashyapa who killed his father, King Dhatusena, usurping the throne of his father. He eventually fled to Sigiriya from Anuradhapura to avoid the retaliation of his half-brother, Moggallana who was the rightful heir of the throne. Kashyapa ordered to build fortress and palace on top of Sigiriya Rock. Eventually, Moggallana came to Sigiriya for revenge and war was declared between the brothers. Kashyapa lost the battle and committed suicide, and Moggallana returned to Anuradhapura after winning the battle, and Sigiriya Rock was converted to a monastery. Four parts to appreciate this site: First, the fortress at the foot of the rock with viewing site of Sirigiya Rock from far after passing by the main entrance surrounded by moat. Some of the highlights are the Summer Palace, Cobra Hood Cave, etc. Second, the decoration of the authentic fresco half way up to the rock, reachable by spiral staircase. Third, the small plateau half way up the rock with massive gateway of Lion Rock with gigantic rock carvings of Lion Paw as entrance to the palace to the top of the rock. Fourth, where is the last part at top of rock where the ruins of the palace is located. The idea of building a Palace on top of a massive rock is already very incredible! 360 degree panoramic views from the top is amazing with sunset view in the evening. In summary, this heritage consists of intriguing historical background, plus the incredible architecture back then in 5th century. It is one of the highlights of our Sri Lanka trip!

This is an absoleutly gorgeous place! It is worth noting that it is not an easy climb and I wish I knew that before going. The steps to go all the way to the top don't feel stable (although for sure they are) but because they are wide opened, you can see how high up you are on both sides and for people with fear of heights, that is really difficult! I was very shocked to get there and realize that it was too scary for me to do. There were other people who were scared too but ended up doing it - good for them! But me, despite several tries with my spouse helping me, I was too scared. It's worth knowing that because it was hard emotionally to finally get there and be excited about it but then realize that you can't get yourself to do it. My spouse went and says it was absolutely incredible!

It was absolutely beautiful but it's worth noting that the steps up are open on the sides meaning that if you are afraid of heights this might be a difficult climb for you. I wish I knew that ahead of time/ I wish someone warned me because I was shocked once I made it there and felt like I couldn't go any further. I was really scared as were many other people. My spouse went all the way up to the top with no problems but I honestly couldn't despite several tries so I waited for my spouse to come back from the very top. A lot of people around me who were also scared ended up going all the way up so it is very do-able but I just want to give heads up about what type of climb it is!
I have being to the lions rock 4-5 time as a teenager and now with my kids.. It's very interesting tell them the true story about the lions rock, dating back to king Ravans age
This is my 2nd trip to Sigiriya and I had to climb it this time, lovely experience, easy steps and any one can do it, around 1200 steps, great views from the top.

We climbed Sigiriya Rock in the late afternoon when it was cooler.We went to the museum first which was very interesting.We then started our climb at about 4.30pm.We went up to see the frescoes which involves going up a spiral staircase.It is worth it as the frescoes are fantastic.If you don’t like heights you don’t have to go up.The last steps to the top aren’t too bad but just take your time. Think of the reward at the top which is spectacular. Well worth the climb.We came half way down and then stayed for the sunset which was lovely.
You have to start your trip at 5am to beat the heat, 32 degrees when I visited, but worth it. Stunning views from the top

Took us by surprise how magnificent it is. I can hardly imagine what a wonder it was when everything worked and people lived in it. Definitely worth to go late afternoon for the sunset, or early in the morning for the sunrise and to avoid the hottest hours. The whole site is well maintained
Definitely worth the climb but go early in the morning before it gets too hot and crowded.

A must do in Sri Lanka. The climb is tough work but we recommend going early in the morning or in the evening. The final climb feels a little hairy but the views and the experience is worth it. Make sure you do the extra walk to see the ancient paintings about half way up. It was a great experience

An amazing place that you must visit, if you're in Sri Lanka. Most package or guided tours will take you here (or get a taxi/tuk-tuk), and if they have any sense, you'll arrive early in the morning, That way you not only miss the queues at the entrance, but you can be up, down, and gone before the hot sun makes it even more difficult! There are a lot of steps (1200), and some of them are steep/high, and some of them are a little bit scary - especially if you have a poor head for heights. There are no facilities for wheelchairs. In fact, you probably need be pretty able bodied to do this one. We had a guide who took us slowly from the top to the bottom, stopping to show us the small details we might otherwise have missed, and also to give us a breather! There are plenty of things to see before you reach the upper staircase. But once you are at the top, it provides a spectacular view (though early morning mist can limit this), and there are some extensive ruins. You'll be scratching your head trying to figure out how they got all the bricks up there. Get there early to beat the queues (the stairs are very narrow), or get there later for a clear view. Take your pick. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip to Sri Lanka. There's nowhere else like it. Tips - wear sensible shoes, carry water, and although a hat is useful, it can get pretty windy up the top, so hang on to it.

The walk up to the foot of the rock, looking at the restored pools, birdlife and rocks was interesting. I was a bit wary as I do not like heights, but I made it to the top. Well worthwhile the effort. The paintings on the way up were fascinating, the view from the top was great. Be wary of being “offered” help to climb the steps (at an exorbitant price !), also some of the sellers of souvenirs, we could have bought them cheaper elsewhere! We had a guide who was good.

Was on a tour with G Adventures and this climb was one of the activities. So glad that I climbed it but it was hard going! Some 1300 steps! Steep stairs. The view from up top was spectacular! A must do!

A stunning location, immaculately maintained and clean.  The climb up looked daunting but we took our time and paced ourselves, enjoying the views as we ascended.  My own personal highlight of a wonderful trip to Sri Lanka.
A very popular place to visit so advice would be to get there as early as possible to miss the crowds and the heat. Very tranquil and fascinating.

This is an exhausted trip with two small kids, specially one carrying in hand since stroller cannot make up there. It worth the visit to see those but avoid noon and use always early morning or evening to climb, glad I read reviews before I climbed.
Nice place to see it, amazing view how building this rock ......? Riyal place to srilanka dont miss it
Been there, done that, avoid if scared of heights, otherwise it is well controlled area, little can go wrong. Frank tip, start the ascent early, the earliest the better, i.e. 8AM
Well worth a visit if you go to this part of Sri Lanka. It’s a lot of steps up but worth it for the view from the top.

Well worth the designation of a UNESCO world heritage site. The hike is not too long, but you gain quite a bit of elevation and the staircases can get rather steep. Bring plenty of water and try to go earlier before it gets too hot. Well worth the trip and entrance fee!!

What a fascinating place this is. We went on Independence Day so it was quite busy.  It really is worth the climb and having a guide to tell you all the relevant history. Go early before it gets too hot.

Quick review to say that this site is not to be missed. But I found no reviews on how vertiginous the climb up might be.  Clearly it wld be steep climb but for those    who have a slight fear of heights the issue is whether you felt ‘safe’ making the climb. We asked a few of our fellow hotel guests the night before and had a mixed response.  So we gave it a try. However I only got one third of the way up via means of a broad staircase which reached a platform with some terrific views over the countryside. But then onwards it became more challenging as I saw a steel caged spiral staircase built into the rock face. I knew straight away I wld freeze half way up and not be able to come down!  So I agreed that my partner would carry on up and I would meet him an hour later down in the visitors’ car park. I had an enjoyable hour watching everyone come and go for an hour and the wonderful vistas knowing I had made the right decision. This was confirmed by my partner when he got back to say it only got worse going up and he witnessed a number of people being vertiginously challenged on the way down. Phew! But it sounds worth the challenge if you know you can get back down. I was happy with my own 1/3 way up kind of achievement! Later found out that the steel spiral walkway (to see some cave paintings)is not obligatory and can be bypassed as you make your way further up. But you still faced further open and steep staircases built into the rock face.  But not me!
1200 steps to the top is a a small challenge but we met people from 3 to 80 on our way up. Start early before it get to hot, bring Lots of water

When we got there the queue was huge. We decided not to take the central spiral stairs, we used the ones on the lest, where there are the Lions. We were able to climb in less than 1h, despite the crowd.

There is a rich history in this rock and decently climb if you are in good physical shape. It is not an easy climb we stopped at many places to take a rest and must bring water since the sun can dehydrate you very fast.

Firstly it is worth it... but... If your legs are not on the tall size you may find the many largish steps a challenge. We used hiking sticks and they helped a lot. Take plenty of water. It's hot! Go early to avoid worst of the great if you can.

Definitely a must do! Amazing views at the top. Not too tough a climb really, as do in stages and can take your time. Tips: Wear good shoes and bring water and hats as it’s pretty exposed up top. Watch out for the ‘guides’ who’ll charge you if they accompany you. Go early to avoid being busy. Recommend as early as 7am! Cost: about roughly $30 per person for international visitors.

Even though I didn't claimed the rock I regret that for not going when the kids returned with dad after climbing the rock. They had taken bunch of pictures and they looked amazing. During the day time sun is too much so use a sun screen otherwise you'll get sun burn.

My trip to Sri Lanka had only one item which was to get to the top of Sigiriya and I succeeded. The site is very well maintained with it very well set up to show the site and its history. Getting to the top was hard due to the temperature but the crowds are the only problem. The site is very important to Buddhists who wanted to see the painting but I didn't and there was no easy way to bypass it. It was well worth the climb
This is a beautiful place and definitely worth the climb. Take a guide with you it was worth it. The climb was difficult for my mom but she made it with breaks.
This is a must visit place. Views from the top are stunning. Climbing the Lion's rock is not easy, but worth it.

We never managed to climb to the top as it was far too busy. We got some lovely camera shots but really wanted to climb it. Make sure you don't go on Buddhist day. Schools etc come out. There is a museum which was interesting. Beware of the guys offering help. Don't offer any money. They are like vultures preying on the weak. I had to be stern and tell them to go away. They did cos I am quite fit and strong. The weaker are not so lucky.

I am in my early sixties, with a lung condition. Was very hesitant to climb the zillion or so steps, so climbing this was , for me, a trial of resolve. I managed it, but took my time. Sri Lanka, right now, is sparsely touristed-but not at Sigiriya. I would dread to think what it is like when the overseas visitors arrive back en masse, once the memory of the 2019 bombings and Coronavirus are ancient history. This place gets crowded and people taking it slow like me tend to get in the way of the more fit individuals. Mind you, I was not the slowest by far. Unfortunately, however, being slow attracts the attention of ‘helper’s’. Fit young Sri Lankan’s standing like hungry carrion, scanning for prey and constantly picking at the perceived weak ones and “assisting” up each flight of stairs, whether that attention was requested , required or not. Their keen eye for a sucker is uncanny and they latch onto a potential monetary catch like seagulls on a chip, regardless of whether you are struggling or not. If you are not quick with a kind hearted rebuke, then they claim their prize and the hassling for large tips starts. They have a hide like an elephant and nothing short of an angry expletive will shake them off.  Be aware. These guys get aggressive and persistent  if you don’t make it absolutely clear that you do not wish their assistance. However, you are not out of the woods, as a couple more of these vultures wanting an easy kill will be at the next flight and the process starts again. I hated that and my patience and initial good natured banter was retired in short order. This spoiled things for me, but that is just my personality. Being honest, Sri Lankans are a good natured and, largely, well mannered bunch, but I set my standards for other people’s behaviours at, possibly, unrealistic levels. This is a dirt poor country trying to provide for its’ peoples and the population have grown to act in a certain way to feed their families. Their behaviours are borne from a need to earn money and, as a result, they can be a bit pushy bordering on exasperation at times. Did I enjoy the Sigiriya experience? Well, besides the huffing , puffing and wanting to turn back at every step, I guess I did. Was that enjoyment because I was using the      climb as a yardstick for my failing fitness and a small mental personal victory was my just reward? Probably. Would I do it again? - Not a chance!

A must do in Sri Lanka. The climb is tough work but we recommend going early - we arrived at 6.45am to make the most of the cool weather. The final climb feels a little hairy but the views and the experience and worth every leg wobble!! Make sure you do the extra walk to see the ancient paintings about half way up.

We arrived at Sigiriya at around 7:15am and there were already people ahead of us. Buy your ticket in the museum near the car park. Because this is not a sacred area, you do not need to cover your shoulders or knees. I recommend sneakers and dressing for a hot sweaty walk up many stairs. It took us approximately 35 minutes to walk up with very little in the way of crowds. We looked at the murals and mirror wall quickly on the way up and then went straight to the top and explored for about an hour. On the way back down, we went more slowly and looked at the lion paws, octagonal pool, caves, and gardens. This is an incredible place and is famous and a major tourist destination for a reason. Highly recommend going and getting there as early as possible to avoid heat and lines. I would say you’d want to be in reasonably good shape to make it up without too much suffering. Bring water and a hat too!

It is amazing to hear how ancient Sri Lanka was so advanced to provide water up to the hill and draw those beautiful faces in the rock wall. So many people climbed all the way to the top and must go after the sun down.
Thought it might be too challenging but in the end it was fine. A series of steep steps but you can go at your own pace and it took under an hour to get to the top.

Myself and my husband are in our 50's and managed the climb up this in around 50 minutes.  There were a few points where we stopped and took a break and some water.  We did not find any of the steps too steep and the views at the top were breathtaking.  It's maybe close to being as good as Ayers Rock but then we are biased!

This was our second time of climbing the rock having done it two years ago. Amazing place and every step is worth the effort. This attraction is vastly improved from our last visit however there was a few things that could of been clearer. Guides now are registered and have to be engaged before you enter the ticket site. They should cost no more than 2000 rupees but some folks where charged 5000. The car parks are different than before and you are dropped off outside the ticket office however your car or Tuk Tuk then collects you after your climb in the foreigner car park in a different area. No issues as such but this means you must do the museum before you climb. Some guides just want you to commence your climb and don’t give you this choice. Also it is not clear when you buy your ticket. The friends of Sigiriya are still at the bottom to assist you up if you require and this can cost 2000 rupees or more. The ticket price is $30 each and when you now exit there is a little market selling what you would expect at variously different prices depending on which one you would chose. The toilets in the Foreigner Car Park are extremely good. This attraction is worth a 5 star review but the lack of information regarding the museum and the car parking arrangements just made it a four.

Visiting and climbing the Sigiriya Rock is a must.  We arrived around 7:45am and our tour guide had arranged a local guide to take us up the rock - I would definitely recommend having a guide as it really brought the rock to life.  He explained what we were looking at and gave us some history to help set the scene, from the gardens right up to the fortress at the top. The guide also took us up at a steady pace, stopping along the way to give us information but to also allowing us to rest - it is not easy but if you pace yourself it is doable. We are two unfit forty-somethings, along with my mum who is 75 and we all managed to get to the top! Highlights of the climb was of course the view - you can see for miles even on a hazy day like we had - the frescos which are unbelievable seeing as how old they are, and also seeing the two huge lion paws. It felt like a great achievement getting to the top - we think it took us approx 3 hours from leaving the car park to getting back to the car.  We were happy to pay the entry fee as it allows the site to be properly maintained.

It is built in the 5th century by King Kashyapa. It was a Kingdom built at the top of a massive rock. It consists of many bathing pools, gardens, ponds and fountains in addition to the other standard structures of a kingdom. It is famous for it’s engineering marvel of how water supply has been done to the ponds at the top and how they maintained the consistency of supply of water. The main objective of this kingdom built at height of this nature is to protect it from any enemies and to get a view of any obstructions from a distance. Price for entrance is 50USD per person. It also uncludes entrance to the Museum located at the bottom. All food and water needs to be purchased from the vendors at the bottom if needed as there are no such food or water will be available on the go. Climb is easy with the steps and stairs. It is strictly prohibited to touch the old paintings in the walls and its surroundings. Climb is usually easier in the evenings as there is no sun. But it gets windy and colder at around 6pm at the top. Entrance to the premises closes by 5pm. But make sure you descend before its too dark. There'nt any lights at night.

What a climb but well worth it! The views from the top are amazing although when we were there it was cloudy and a bit misty. Queues can be quite long so get there early if you can. Amazing cave art to be seen on the way up.

First of all, I cannot believe that someone would rate this as over-priced.  It takes a full half-day and even before you get to the top the scenery is amazing as you go through the boulder garden and water areas.  I saw the rock paintings that remain on the western wall and - in my opinion - they were magnificent.  They stretched over several metres and had such vibrant detail and colour, depicting several young maidens.  I found it fascinating that you could see the mistakes such as an arm being moved position or lady with 3 nipples as you couldn't correct once the ink was on the plaster.  And the view on the top?  Magnificent again.  All the foundations remain so you can clearly make out the rooms and gardens of what must have been a vast citadel.  Not unlike Machu Picchu in its look.  It was also one of the easier climbs with tourist friendly steps!  I wonder if some reviewers have even been to the place... And if you love Duran Duran and the Save A Prayer video then you will be in absolute heaven - although I didn't have a helicopter of white linen suit to recreate the look!

The story of Sigiriya is fascinating and to say that you’ve climbed to the top is one of the must-dos in Sri Lanka. The views are amazing and the remains at the top are interesting. However, it was a chaotic ascent with no staff, no decent signage and a complete free for all with ignorant, impatient people pushing in and ignoring the queues that the rest of us were patiently observing. One of the few places we visited that didn’t reflect well on the people of this wonderful country. A shame and therefore not recommended.
Amazing ancient kingdom with nice sunset and green view around. Wall paintings and nice garden with monkeys. Must visit place !

Sigiriya shows us how developed technology could be used in a fortress built 1600 years ago...After defeating 1200 steps you can admire a wonderful view. There are a lot of tourists there but not so many to spoil the joy of visiting the place. You can meet a lot of monkeys there.
This was a one of the greatest adventures for your life. If your plan to go Sri Lanka for your next tour, definitely add Sigiriya to the list. The view is magnificent! Definitely worth the climb!

Like all sites in Sri Lanka, this is very, very overpriced. The best part of the sight is the view, so I recommend climbing the neighbouring rock for the view at a fraction on the cost. The rock paintings are sparse and just tiny segments. There is a pair of carved lion claws at the base of some stairs. That is it for things to see on the rock. Does not come close to justifying $30 US or $40 Canadian a person. I felt rather ripped off.
Worth the climb to the top. Start as early as possible. We went at 7.30am. We would not have wanted to start much later.

Imagine an amusement park without the fast track. Well, apparently there actually is a (mini) fast track which we realized after about our first hour of waiting. It’s not really a hike to the top - more like a queue to the top. And a crowded one. If you are going to hand over the money for the steep entrance fee and hike to the top then do it as early as possible. Otherwise, the experience is one that you might want to skip.

This giant, ancient rock fortress has an impressive view of the surrounding area.  A 30 minute to hour vertical climb to the top, but it's sure footed with stone steps and some metal stairs.  Bring water and a camera!  It's UNESCO too.

we had heard about this place and had always wanted to visit. there is a beautiful garden as you approach the fortress.the climb is around 1000+ steps.so be sure you are properly hydrated and ready with spring in your step. on the way there are painting on the wall which we can see. from there on, we have to keep climbing till we reach the base where we could take a break and chill for some time.the last part of the climb is absolutely bonkers. but it is well worth it. Once you reach the top,the view from the top is simply brilliant. and we spent time just feeling the cool breeze and the picturesque view from the rock fortress. it is a must visit  attraction,if you are in sri lanka. highly recommend to others.

We took a special taxi to visit this place about 3 hours drive north of Kandy, where we were staying, as friends at home had all said it was a must place to visit. They were right. Arriving there early morning, having left home at 6am, it was a coolish time to make the climb.   There were many older people struggling but on the whole it’s not a difficult path and it’s all got hand rails and decent metal steps and stone steps too.   The views from the top are wonderful.   The fact that this place had been constructed centuries ago is just breathtaking. The site is huge and has gardens all beautifully kept tidy by armies of staff. Definitely make the journey early in the cooler part of the day.

Begin at the Persian-style gardens, then walk up the face of the rock-- on the way see the beautiful paintings on the rock (this rock was once all plastered and painted)-- then arrive at the lion's paws where you continue to climb until you reach the very top. The most spectacular view!

It was a great experience, view from top was amazing. Try to avoid visit on weekends, you may find much of crowd. There is another rock nearby, you can go in that too. You will get the good view of Sigiriya rock.

While I was on a trip of Sri Lanka with G Adventures, I hired a driver to take me out to see the Sigiriya Rock as it is #191 on the Lonely Planet's ultimate travelist. Since the entrance fee into the area of the rock is $30 USD, I did not climb the rock as it has 1200 steps to get to the top.  There are also many tuk tuk drivers that try to get you to pay $30 USD to take a tuk tuk around the base of the rock.  I did not take them up on their offer as you can walk around the base of the rock and see the moats without their services, and you do not need to pay anything to do this. I think that $30 USD is way overpriced as the locals pay only a fraction of this cost. Sri Lanka is not the only country that charges too much for foreigners.  I found that this was true in India and Nepal as well.

A must see if travelling to Sri Lanka. Our guide took us to the rock about 6.30-7am which was the best decision...barely any other tourists there and before the heat. The climb up, which is a combination of flat areas, stairs and sights, took about an hour going easy. Views and ruins at the top are amazing and worth it.

Prepare for the day. We first climbed a mountain to get the view of sigiriya rock and then climbed the sigiriya rock. The first treck was hard but the view was breathtaking and totally worth it. Then we climbed sigiriya rock. It’s better to take a guide outside. They help you to climb and tell you stories which makes the experience better. The guide costed us 2000lkr.

I was looking forward to Sigiriya and also dreading the climb up as im unfit. We got there around 9am and it was quite busy but not crowded. It was hot but we walked up in about 45 mins with a few stops. Beware of the 'helpers'. One helper grabbed my arm and pulled me up about 10 steps while i was saying not to help and that i was fine, at the top of the 10 steps he made some conversation then asked for the equivalent of £3. We said no as he had been told that I didn't want help, he then came out with a story about his child being in hospital and he needed money, i suspect this isn't true. We loved the views from the top and also on the way up. Beware of the cheeky monkeys.
Stunning place and must see. There are over 1000 steps to get to the top, but all ages are able to enjoy and we’ll worth the views from the top. Highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka

Well worth the climb, not going to lie was dreading it a little, it was hard at times, but so glad that I made the effort and got to the top. Get there early to avoid the crowds and the heat. Take a camera for the fantastic views.

A very beautiful place to visit when in Sri Lanka. A UNESCO Word Heritage site.  Definitely a must visit location.  Large rock with a castle carved into it with natural water pools and frescos that have lasted 100s of years.  Everything there was built by human hands and has amazing architecture.  The best view is all the way on the top.
The work involved in build the fortress on an impenetrable rock is amazing. Well worth the climb. Just be wary of the thieving monkeys

This is an extremely large and impressive area. It is quite a climb to the top but very doable as long as you have a bit of patience with the crowds. The views from the top are spectacular. You need to be wary of the resident monkeys who are very keen to steal thing out of back packs even if they are closed. Also hornets apparently can be an issue.

This is a complete must to do experience. I am a not very fit 54 yr old and even in the heat at 8am managed to get to the top with no  problems. And it was worth every step of the climb. The view is jaw droppingly beautiful and the remains of the palace incredible. We didn't have enough time to really explore everything and next time would put aside a whole morning,

Set off at 4pm, a short drive from my villa. When reaching there, we had a site guide. He explained as we move along towards the Lion Rock. The excavation, moats, lower compounds, caves, even the steps has its reason why it was coated. 1200 stairs up. 1/2 of the journey to the frescoes and wall mirror (no photos & videos allowed). 3/4 to the base of the lion 's paw entrance to the Palace up on top of the rock. By now, my legs almost gave way. I stayed at the lion's paws. But my hubby & site guide went all the way up to the top. He explained that the highest is not 1200 stairs but 1202. There are 2 steps of stone right in the centre of the Palace! Worth participating in this UNESCO site. Entrance fee USD30 each. They accept USD.

When you’re climbing the 1000 steps (like a 60 storey building) to the top, where the fortress and palace were (after walking 2km from the car park to get to those very uneven steps) you will marvel at the engineering and sheer audacity behind such a place. Millions of bricks. A massive swimming pool. (How did the water get there?) And on and on. Greater views, including that of a nearby mountaintop Buddhist temple. Bring water and be sure to stop at the toilet before your ascent. Wow.

My wife and I are 72 and have each had major surgery on a leg. We climbed up in less than an hour, starting about 8 AM. So the climb up is really no big deal. And the view from the top is also not that exciting. What make this site so amazing is the sheer (no pun intended) wonder that an ancient people were able to build this fortress. They were clearly geniuses at engineering. The same is true for all the massive man-made lakes throughout the country, especially at Anuradhapura, where the lake is easy to see.
A lot of irregular steps make this climb a bit difficult and exhausting, but it is nonetheless worthy when you reach the top.
Absolutely nice and wonderful world heritage place in Sri Lanka. Ancient technology is amazing here. Its very hard to identified how they bring water to the top of the rock.

Nothing prepared me for this and I was glad I was wearing sturdy trainers.  The climb is quite steep for the uninitiated!  It's a combination of stone steps, some rickety and on occasions nothing to hold onto and metal open stairs, with railings.  You really have to look where you're going!  There are various stopping points on the way so you don't have to do it in one go. A good tip - our guide took us up early, as it opened - about 7.30 I think.  We were at the top by 9.  It's quite a steep climb in parts and not for the fainthearted, but I didn't see anyone turning back.  When you get to the top it's a stunning 360 degree vista and well worth the climb.  How they ever built a palace up there several hundred years ago, I can't imagine.  There are various interesting features on the way up and down, one being the wall paintings, hundreds of years old.  You have to climb up a metal spiral staircase on the side of the rock, but you are caged in.  As with many things in Sri Lanka, its very ad hoc!  What an amazing morning!

Not all guides created equal! Beware! You really don’t need a guide! Buy the ticket pick up a brochure before bargaining for a guide. Go to the museum first and read the brochure. I ended up with a guide that was clearly drunk and kept talking about naked women pictures and swimming naked for the king to watch. He pointed to things and said their name that was clearly on the sign. Knowledge was abysmal. Then said the court was a night club. Seriously an idiot. I said it wasn’t and he said same thing. I fired him on the spot. Ugh. Felt safer as a single female and more relaxed once he was gone

Trip advisor Sigiriya I am writing this mainly for people who, like me, have a fear of heights. Most reviews focus on the effort of getting up the rock. I am moderately fit and found it hardly taxing at all. My Apple Watch said I had climbed 48 flights of stairs but it did not feel anywhere near that much. More of a challenge for me was the height and especially the two separate  flights of iron stairs. I had debated whether to do the climb at all and was pretty apprehensive. Having done it, my advice would be to do it if you have a mild fear of heights or a moderate fear that is under control ie not subject to serious panic attacks. It also helps to have a supportive companion. I would suggest not doing it if your fear is more severe. Most stairs are stone with balustrades but there are two iron sections:- One that leads up from the mirror wall via a caged-in iron spiral staircase to the cave paintings. (You go up to the paintings but then have to come down again to continue.) The steps are solid so one cannot see the drop below but of course you can look out as you go round. I managed this by focussing on the central post of the staircase and talking encouragingly to myself! if you are anxious about this you can probably bypass the cave paintings and head straight for the Lions Claw platform, although the paintings are interesting. Another section leads up from the Lions Claws level to the top. This has iron sections crossing the rock, again with solid steps, but is more exposed. Going up was easier as one faces the rock. I was more anxious about coming down but my husband went in front of me so I could hold on to his back with one hand and the railing with the other. The walkway gets quite crowded which slows the descent but means you are surrounded by people. This made me feel less exposed. I was nervous but it was very manageable. I have found other places more challenging like going up a tower in San Giminiano and inside the dome of St Paul’s. I would make two other points:- There are guides along the way who look out for people who look anxious and are quite insistent about holding your hand. Kind but probably better declined. The remains at the top and the views are very impressive - well worth the effort - and if you get there with your fear of heights, a real achievement. I hope this is helpful - it would have helped me if I had been able to read this before I went.

We were counting on the climb to the Sigiriya ancient rock fortress to be one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka.  And it certainly was!  The best piece of advice we can give you is to go early.  This will help with the heat and with the crowds.  The rock opens at 6:30 am, which is when we arrived.  However, it appears that the ticket office opens earlier, so I suggest arriving around 6:15 and being among the first to go through the gate. Be warned that the price is hefty: around $30.  At the gate, a guard will take any label off your water bottle, so you can save time by doing this in advance.  Then, you will proceed on a straight path for about 10 minutes just to reach the beginning of the stairs to climb.  We were pleasantly surprised that the climb, while strenuous and very sweaty, was not as difficult as we expected.  We were not hurrying, and made it to the top in about 20 minutes.  I do feel this is primarily because there was no one else in our way on the stairs.  I can see how this would easily become a bottleneck and slow down your progress. Once at the top, you will be rewarded with beautiful views of the surrounding area.  The ruins are peaceful to explore when crowds are light.  On our way down at 7:30 am, the crowds were now rolling in, so even 8 am is too late to embark. Do go early, do take water, and enjoy the experience!

Sigiriya is ancient rock citadel located in Sri Lanka’s cultural triangle. The enormous rock towers above the surrounding jungle offering extensive views. I will suggest to stay nearby and start the hike as early as 06:30AM as the temperatures rises to 100 degrees Fahrenheit and humidity around 80%. You have to climb about 1200 steep steps with elevation gain of about 650 feet. My advice is to start early, drink water regularly, wear hat, use sunscreen and go slow. If you are from SAARC countries then carry your passport to get 50% discount on admission ticket. Sigiriya is a world heritage site declared by UNESCO in 1982. It is a unique combination of 5th century urban planning, architecture, engineering, hydraulics, garden design, painting and poetry. The city is designed in a square module 2750 meter east to west and 925 north to south. 1. Royal Gardens- This is massive water gardens. 2. Three water gardens. 3. Boulder Garden- It begins at slope of hill at base of the rock. 4. Cistern Rock- Huge stone that has been split. 5. Audience Hall Rock 6. Preaching Rock 7. Painted maidens- These frescos  are preserved in a cave pocket about 40 feet above walkway. 8. Mirror Wall- Highly polished surface is original stucco. Most poetic verses had been written in praise of maidens on cliff face. 9. Lion Terrace. 10. Palace- It is located on summit but none of superstructure remains.

An absolute must do for anyone who is able to make the ascent, Sigiriya Rock is stunning! Seen from below, the massive granite outcrop looks daunting. We made it to the top in 30 minutes, with two young kids, and two adults with bad knees! We arrived around 800 and were glad we had because it was incredibly crowded as we descended. The water gardens viewable on the approach are impressive. Incredible feats of ancient ingenuity and engineering prowess. The climb is well organized and with the $30 US for adults (kids 6-12 are half price). Most of the way you go up metal stairs the are secured to the rock face. These are narrow, and a bit unnerving when the wind gusts, but we saw people of all ages and fitness levels work their way up. It is worth the sweat and sore legs when you reach the top! The palace ruins are incredible, but it is the 360 degree vistas that are the real payoff. We spent close to an hour roaming around and snapping breathtaking pics. The descent retraces the final section of the climb, at first, before reaching a much easier exit pathway. Again, it took roughly half an hour. One of the coolest, and most singular, experiences I’ve ever had!

My wife an I climbed to the summit in approximately 40 minutes with a few small rests along the way. The spectacular view from the summit is worth the effort, as well as the beautiful grounds and fort below. This site is a must see in Sri Lanka !

In addition the staircases felt a bit unsafe when considering there were hundreds of climbers on them at the same time and they were only bolted on to the rock.
