Our way up took us about an hour even though it should take about 10 - 15 minutes. Our way down was also super crowded and took us 40 minutes.. The views on top are nice but nothing special especially after visiting Ella first. On top of all, this day of fun cost 27,50 euros which is a ripoff compared to everything else in Sri Lanka. Definitely a nightmare for anyone who is scared of bees, heights or claustrophobic.

We visited sigirya during our trip to Sri Lanka. I was already knackered from waking up at 7 am to get there early (trust me - don't do this later than 10 am) Having said that climbing Sigirya is 100% the most fun activity my wife and I did during our trip to Sri Lanka. It costs $20 or $30 to enter (expensive compared to the $2 entrance fee at Pidurangala). It's a steep climb easier than Pidurangala and there are stairs for most of the way up but everyone can do it. I saw people with babies doing it with one hand and old people with sticks getting pushed up the hill. Apart from the fun way up you get 360 views of Pidurangala, Dambulla and the nearby parks. I left with major aches in my legs but I can't stop thinking about that day . I would do it again on a heartbeat. If someone asks to help just refuse politely. I was scammed again and some "helpful" employee extracted 3000 rupees from me for grabbing my wife's hand to "help her up" . He wouldn't let go. For this behavior alone I am not willing to give 5/5

We went really early in the morning to avoid the crowds and so glad we did. The climb we easy to access with nonstop views and photo opportunities. It can be a challenge for some, but well worth the effort. The top is breathtaking and so peaceful (without all the people). This is a MUST see! Highlight of our trip so far... When we got down there were thousands of people, so get up there first to appreciate it more!

This is the best sight we visited in sri  lanka.filled with old history and  challenging to the summit to complete.we felt difficulty at half way,but manged to the top some how.a must and must visit when you are in sri lanka.

We hired a local guide and hiked up the rock.  It was crowded, especially because we went on a local full moon holiday, but it didn't detract from the experience and we loved seeing the grounds and ruins.

Sigiriya rock looks imposing. At first, we were scared we might be too unfit to climb it. Such fears proved to be baseless, however. The climb is very easy. Anyone in good health should be able to make it, and they should! This castle is something out of a medieval fairy tale. It's absolutely stunning. Its history is fascinating, too! Go and see it!

Too crowded that you don't enjoy. And very expensive around 30$ and for locals only 5Rupis. The place is amazing to see but to be hours of waiting lines for achieve the highest points is really disappointing.

Had a fun day at Lion Rock! This is a serious rock with a fascinating history but the climb is not for the faint-hearted or the unfit. As a 65yr old in decent condition it was still a reasonable challenge. There seemed to be some doing the climbing who may have under-estimated it. It’s 1-way up and 1-way down so turning back might be an issue. There are places to take a breather along the way. You should have good non-slip footwear, enough water, camera and as little to carry as possible. You will get hot and sweaty! Having said all that....go for it! The view is spectacular! For others who don’t feel up to the climb there is a museum and interesting parklands to walk thru. Be warned of spruikers claiming to be “official” guides and who won’t take no for an answer but I suppose can be helpful to assist the less agile.

2000 years old and with a history going back before that, the climb up to the top of the rock fortress Sigiriya is a must do. Take time to check out the museum - it has some basic information but is helpful in understanding the history of this place. There is so much yet to uncover. 2400ish steps will get you to the top but the half way mark at the lion’s paws offers great views too. Wall frescos are a little detour on the way. As a foreigner, if you have a guide you’ll learn a lot more about the place.

This was an amazing fortress set upon a massive rock that towers over the forest. The climb is a little scary if you are not good with heights. But the view is amazing. The crowds do make the climb up and down are little long as you have to wait in a line.  Remember to bring ID

Though, many Indians don't write a review and hence, we didn't took our passports which can save 50% fee to the fort. The fee which is $30 per person is reduced to $15 person if you carry your passport. This is applicable for all SAARC countries.

Firstly, this point should be covered either early morning or later afternoon unless the weather is good. If it is hot, then you might not enjoy this place that much. Coming to the place now. Entry Fee is 15 USD for SAARC nations and 30 USD for others. I paid 2760 LKR per person. You have to walk for about 10 minutes to reach the point from where the climb begins. However, the place is extremely well managed and surpassed my expectations. It is a world heritage site and known as the eighth wonder. There are gardens and mini water bodies on both the sides. There is a very small bridge with water on both the sides just after the ticket checkpoint and one can have nice clicks standing on that. Please DO NOT THROW away your tickets after this point since it is again checked midway into the ascent. Coming to the climb, there are about 1200 steps. The difficulty is moderate. It surely tests your stamina. But if the weather is good, it is all worth it. As you keep on climbing, the view of entire surrounding just keeps on getting better. I doubt if you can get better views from any other place. It took us about 30-40 minutes to complete the climb. Do not recollect noticing any restrooms on the way so be mindful of that. Once you reach the top, you truly appreciate the work that has been done at such a height. It is a refreshing feeling at the top. You can easily spend an hour at the top, just sitting and roaming around. While climbing down, check with someone the way to Tourist Car Parking area since that is different from the original place where your driver might have dropped you. It is must visit place. If the weather is on your side, then you will have an Unforgettable time. This was the best sightseeing point for us on our entire Sri Lanka trip.

I took a foreign friend to visit Sigiriya, on a overcast weekday. The flock of Tour Guides at the entrance was quite daunting. They charge anything between Rs. 2000 - 3500. I asked for an English speaking guide from the staff at the entrance to the ticket counter, and they called up someone trustworthy, and Lal was recommended. He was not a pushy guy, and showed us around well. It is not essential to have a guide, if you have time to follow the map in the sequence given and read all the plaques that are placed everywhere. But a guide does give a good overview and life to the ancient fortress. He also provided help when a naughty monkey jumped on my friends back pack to steal a face tissue! Tip - do not carry any edibles on you, as you becomes a target of the very confident monkeys. And please be quiet, as wasps can get agitated at certain locations. We started climbing at 9am, and was down by 11am. My entrance ticket as a local was Rs. 50 but my foreign friend had to pay Rs. 5640! It seems exorbitant when not even a water bottle was provided complimentary! I would expect the tour guide to be provided FOC, for this price....but that was not so. This is my 4th visit, and this place never ceases to amaze me!

The price entrance ticket perhaps makes it up for the restoration work but barring it, the experience of such marvellous engineering genius for 5-6th centuries is commendable. It’s suggested to visit during early hours to avoid the hot rock. Definitely carry water with you and avoid locals selling anything.

Sigiriya is one of the eight World Heritage Sites of Sri Lanka. It is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning worldwide. There are remains of an extensive network of gardens and reservoirs. Some structures like fountains are still intact today. The monolithic rock itself is a lava plug left over from an ancient long extinct volcano. It rises 200 m from the green scrub jungle surrounding it. Today on top the visitor finds the ruins of what was once a king´s fortress in the sky. While climbing up the steps there was a lady before us who got in the middle of a fight between a monkey and a dog. She got bitten by the dog and needed to go down to get treated by the red cross at the lion’s gate. This is nothing that you would like to happen to you. So be aware of stray dogs and over-curious monkeys. If they approach you too boldly you might want to try out a self defense technique Marcell has discovered to be effective. He has successfully kept monkeys distant by using insect repellent.

Is a must see thing here. The rock is so amazing. Have to walk a short distance to reach the bottom then climb the stairs up. Can be scary for those weak hearts as the stairs are along the rock. After the lions paw the stairs are much steeper and narrow so walk with caution. On top is flat, able to view the surroundings and capture nice pictures. Beware of the monkeys too as they are everywhere.

World heritage venue worth the effort and surrounding views. Lots of history albeit this should have been presented in a better way. Museum is ordinary. Steep climbing recommended only for super-fit genre. $30 entry fee is relatively expensive.

Excellent trip to lion rock! This place is so beautiful to see the kings former palace! We bought a book on this in advance a d read up in the history but it was still worth having a tour guide. The guide was able to take great pics for us and added history value! This is payable in addition to the cost of entry. But worth it, we bartered with the guide, guides range from 1500-5000 rupees depending how much your willing to pay. It took us 1 hour roughly to walk up and down. We were quoted 2 hours 30. Bear this in mind when paying the tour guide. But really enjoyed it. You will get very wet if it rains so bring waterproof kit.
This is a must see! Make sure you get here early to beat the crowds. When we came it was raining so there wasn’t many people which made it great

This sightseeing was always in mu bucket list. When i visited i felt amazed by the view of the rock fortress, by the area and the views and remains on the top. I can write for hours for this marvellous world herittage. Everyone must visit it at least once. It makes you wonder who made this at those ages and how a single rock can be there in the middle of the jungle. We strongly recommend it to visit it around 11 in the morning when there are not so many crowds and wear trainers which will help you climp up all those stairs. The dissadvantages and the points that should be mentioned is the high entrance fee especially when you have to spend hundreds of dollars till you reach that point, some locals were to noisy and annoying,not respecting their own sightseing moreover other people that tried to enjoy it and take photos by pushing them or standing in front of them. Local people are so nice and kind but there are some among them that ruin everything, this need to change...we saw even one of them spitting inside the monument. The activity is not recommended for elder,young kids and disabled although we see many of these categories which you can guess...causing problems. Sad for such a place.

Did this hike 7am - the ideal time. Just before the crowds and the temperature increased. Loved it! It’s about 30USD to get in. They offer you a tour guide for extra fee, we didn’t bother. The views at the top are fab! Lots of steps, but nothing too drastic. Some people were wearing flip flops, we wore trainers and I’d definitely advise that!

We visited Sigirya on a day when it rained and rained. All this added to the wonder of the rock. The rock paintings are fantastic , the remains at the top are a fantastic act of construction. Seeing that they built the kings swimming pool at the top is a real how did they do that moment. The climb is relatively easy as most of it is on metal steps with handrail. If you suffer from vertigo though its probably not advisable. If the weather had been better we would have loved to explore the gardens in more detail. Stunning

Beautiful ancient site, well worth the visit. Cost is $30 USD or 5460 rupees at todays exchange rate. Stairs are an easy climb and there are many "rest" areas (straight stretches). Wonderful to be a part of a this history, and to see the ryins of the ancient fortress

For me it was an achievement as I had had surgery a couple of weeks prior and was nervous about the climb especially as our driver mentioned that we would be 4 hours or so. It was a challenge but doable and a great feeling when you reach the top. We only took one bottle of water each (contrary to others advise, which Im glad I didn't take) and only had a drink when we got to the top (or it will weigh you down). Also visit the washroom before you start. We arrived at 830 after breakfast and had a very comfortable climb without to many people, however on our way down, there were heaps of people crawling single file up the stairs.... you can go for sunrise if you choose and its quiet but dark. Spectacular views 360 degrees

I climbed the other rock the day before, and was told by many that sigirya wasn't worth the money, same view, same experience. This is not the case the view from the top is so different and the rock is full of history. Steep stairs, but a quick climb for the height of the rock. Don't be overwhelmed, I was concerned about my fear of heights, just don't over think it, 1 step at a time and look into the rock.

The mood at the top is not bad, even though there are many tourists, if you wait a while and walk to other areas, you are able to find a silent spot. There are handlebars to accompany you all the way, I think this is a good thing, but made the area less ''authentic". Not sure about the museum, maybe I can go again.

Awe inspiring and it never ceases to impress.  I hope that the US$30 entry fee for tourists really goes back into the conservation of such an important archaeological titan.  Interesting visiting the museum to see the reconstructed superstructure of palace buildings on top of the rock.
Historical yet also a beautiful natural feature. Stunning views in every direction. Well worth climbing up all the steps!

Sigiriya is surely a wonderful place to visit, with its title as the most vital place of the Cultural Triangle in Sri Lanka. We had a nice stroll in the location with some of my family members. this is one of the wonders of the ancient world. I would recommend to visit early morning or evening to skip the strong sunlight.

Just amazing. So many steps (more then 2300) by fantastic view and spirit there . Spectacular view from the top of all valley. In the top is like Machu Picchu .Get strong rain in the top and same time in the valley was sunny . Really recommend, but take good shoes and have enough power to go top

Meander through narrow rock passageway and steep stairs to the summit of Sigiriya's Ancient Fortress, also known as the Lion's Rock. This charming site was once the palace ground for the ancient king and his 500 wives. Do check out the oldwall paintings and climb the 1200 steps to the summit for the breathtaking views of the surrounding atmosphere.

As the most popular attraction in the area it wasn't ridiculous the amount of people there, not helped by arriving at the same time as 3 coaches of tourists. I strongly suggest to wear decent footwear and avoid sandals or flip-flops as the steps can be wet and dusty from the dirt around. The walk up is a bit steep but all steps and once you reach the main part of the rock you get a lovely breeze. The stairs are the busy bit, once you're at the top it fans out over the ruins and there is plenty of exploring to do. Head for the far corner with the royal pool and see the balcony for a great pano shot. I'm sure if your visiting Sigiriya you wouldn't miss this but just to say it's a must do. If you're feeling a bit fit and energetic head to the other rock that over looks Sigiriya for some amazing photos (be warned it's a bit of rock climbing(

Suffering very strong vertigo I took it upon myself to climb the rock The circular metal stairs do not take you to the rock but to the place where you can see the paintings of the damsels ( forbidden photos ) The ascent takes place on metal steps in straight stairs , which follow the ancient steps carved in the rock At the top a masterpiece of architecture for the time, a swimming pool and a splendid view The descent is even worse than the climb for people suffering from vertigo Monkeys everywhere. 1500 rupees ( 7.5 € ) access per person but worth it Take 15 minutes to walk through the gardens to get to the bottom of the steps , then 20 to 30 minutes to climb ) idem downhill .

We stayed in Sigiriya for a few days and this was a must for us. It certainly didn’t disappoint. At over 200m high the views over Sigiriya are spectacular. We were told to visit early in the morning before it gets to hot and busy, this certainly pays off.
This fort is really amazing and one of the best places we visited in Sri Lanka. The views from top are amazing.

This place is stunning, Take it slow and you'll get to the top. Carry as little as possible but make sure you have water. Make sure you have a good pair of trainers. Oh and dont forget your camera, the views are amazing.

There is really no need for a guide, with the good information plaques throughout and the free pamphlet with a map you will be will equipped information wise. Take as little to carry as possible, it is a tough climb but there are plenty of places you can rest. I hate heights but took it slowly and did not look until I was right at the top,  there is plenty of space there so felt safe. Go as early in the day as possible.

It was a great experience.there were two entrance for the sigiriya rock, one for locals and the other for foreign tourists. should buy a tickets and no one allowed to take polythene in to the fortress premises. tickets are not issuing after 5.30pm. after 7pm it is highly prohibited to stay in the premises. top of the fortress we can see a astonishing view of a massive area.

A very interesting attraction, I got to the murals only as it was hot and very humid, I was amazed at the views across the land and how flat it was. I loved seeing all the gardens, cave shrines and the workmanship of the stonework. Definitley a place to visit.

A visit to this UN World Heritage Site is a must. It's an exhilarating climb and amazing remnants of the ancient civilization that built this fortress city centuries ago.  We recommend staying at one of the great hotels just walking distance from the site, so you can get an early start before the crowds and the heat increase. We were fortunate to have a break in the rain for the morning, and were treated to fantastic views from the top. It's a steep climb but all stairs with handrails, so even those with aversion to heights should be able to stomach this. Carry as little as possible other than camera and plenty of drinking water. No need to hire a guide as there is signage throughout, and if you read up even a little in advance you will have a good understanding of what you are seeing.

The way up is a bit difficult if you are not fit. But it's worth it! The view of the valley through and from the top is beautiful. You are standing on a rock, on the ruins of a former city surrounded by jungle! Fantastically!

It will well worth the journey up to the very top if you can.  The views from up there see unforgettable.  You can see everything.  It is tough to imagine from the bottom how many buildings could have been up there during it time, however,  when you reach the summit, you can see how vast an area it really is.  If would have been a truly magnificent site when all the buildings are temples were standing! The walk is quite tough, especially on a hot day.  There are lots of different heights steps so.e of which are steep.  You must also take a metal staircase up to the top via the side of the rock, which could be scary fot those afraid of heights. On the way up, the frecos on the ceilings are worth looking at. Remember no pictures, but it is amazing to see how vivid and detailed the paintings are still, and unbelievable to think the whole area would have been covered in such figures. The gardens at the bottom are equally majestic.  They are vast and very well preserved. you could easily walk around these and not do anything else.  There is also an ebony tree in the gardens which is worth looking out for. A must if staying in Sigiriya.  It is a once in a lifetime experience

This sacred city was established around a cutting from the 'tree of enlightenment', the Buddha's fig tree, brought there in the 3rd century B.C. by Sanghamitta, the founder of an order of Buddhist nuns. Anuradhapura, a Ceylonese political and religious capital that flourished for 1,300 years, was abandoned after an invasion in 993. Hidden away in dense jungle for many years, the splendid site, with its palaces, monasteries and monuments, is now accessible once again.

I realise it's a main attraction, but 30 USD pp is pretty ridiculous. Especially when locals pay about 50 cents!. Its a hard climb up thousands of steps and can get really crowded. View is nice and good to say have done it. Sri Lanka tourism/government really need to rethink how much they gouge tourists.

Entrance ticket for SAARC country citizens is at 50%discount,so comes upto 15 dollars per person. Make sure u carry ur passport with u. Right at the entrance is the Museum,do visit it before starting ur climb,itll put in perspective a lot of things. Make sure ur carrying water,wearing comfortable clothes and shoes. Its not that its a hard climb, even then u get tired n sweat a lot coz its a 1200 step climb. Click a lot of pics from d view point and the entrance garden. Half way through the climb is the grand lion paw entrance,its really fascinating that this was built thousands of years ago. Once u reach the top,ur blown away by the view. Spend enough time on the top,click loads of pics. Luckily it wasn’t too crowded for us. But ive heard it gets crowded quite often. We started our climb at 9.30, took us an hour to go up,spent an hour on top and then another hour to come back down.

I have visited the rock in several occasions as a local,,most of the time with fellow clients,This time one of a great climb to the rock early in the morning,we needed 2.30 hrs to up and down,with little rest on the top of the rock,foreign ticket price was 30 USD per person,weather was really fine in the day,top view is amazing,landscape,paintings,and the secret irrigation system was eye catching events in the rock,

An employee I will share with you picture, you are alone at a time when you are approaching sex harassment. he starts caressing your wife's, daughter's hands, arms, waist or any other place without saying anything. Watch out for this guy! my statement to the police is attached. you may find yourself under stressing and giving a statement to the police while you are thinking resting on holiday.

A huge rock dominating the surrounding landscape as you approach.  The surrounding grounds are beautifully kept and the ruins are impressive but the highlight is the climb up and the view from the top.  Well worth the effort and a significant historical site. It's best to avoid or refuse assistance from the "helpers" who keep trying to assist you (for a fee) if you can.

Start as early as possible to allow for the humidity and take your time. Expect to find lots and lots of tourists, incredibly popular and busy. The climb to the Lions paws is long, but there are plenty of places to stop and rest. While from here the ascent to the top took about 15 to 20 minutes, we walked slowly, it’s steep and no where to rest, but doable. The view is amazing, especially the remnants of the Palace and old swimming pool

One of the great location and a high tourist attraction , The thing is you have to have a ability and strong enough to climb this mountain and long path to walk as well ( I dont recommend if you are elder / unhealthy or disable)   . For the foreigners  have to buy a 5700 rupees ticket for entrance which is I don't agree about the cost . and the sanitary facilities are little less on the top of sight and there are so many sellers around whom you can be cheated as well .. But the sight is really amazing and the facts of sigiriya make you wonder indeed. There are so many sign board and descriptions enough to get a good idea   .. The top 360 view is amazing ....

The climb up to the top of this ancient castle/fortress was daunting (to a person with fear of heights. (But what a view on top!) And the history of this place - first buddhist temple, then castle and grounds laid out in the 5th century by King Kashyapa, including two moats and the rock citadel. Most memorable: wall paintings half way up of the Cloud maidens!

This attraction isn't for the feint hearted or slightly infirm! There are thousands of steps rising up the rock, mist of which are a good 12-15 inches high so you need to be fit! There are guides who will help you up every step of the way but expect to oay highly for their assistance. I offered 2,500 SR Rupees and got sneered at! I only went halfway up too! The views are spectacular from even halfway but clearly breath taking from the very top, which you access by a metal staircase up the side of this gigantic edifice! Take plenty of water with you and enjoy!

The Sigiriya Rock Fortess is a must do item for every traveller visiting Sri Lanka. This is beautiful emperor built on the rock. The climb is steep but the arrangements using a stairway is very neatly done and well co-ordinated. It is mesmerising feeling once you are at the top. Beware of monkeys on the way and try to climb up with minimal stuff in your hands.
This place was simply amazing. Recommend su rise hike. Views and history well maintained and undisturbed.

Really enjoyed the walk to the top, not a good idea if you don't like heights. Also far to many locals who pretend to be friendly and helpful,  however they are just looking to fleece as much cash out of you as they can. My advice ignore them and do your own research into the historical aspects of the ancient palace grounds. Visit the museum before you climb, you get some useful information. Some historians also believe this was the Palace of Ravana, the epic story of Ram and Sita. Highly recommended if you like history and seeing some fantastic views from the top of Sigiriya.

The ancient city of Sigiriya is an archaeological site whose ruins point to the opulence and architectural wonders of this ancient city. The Rock dominates the area with the ruined fortress on top, a 1247 step climb for the energetic. We wished that we had visited years ago as old legs were unable to obey the spirit. 11 of our group of 34 made it to the top, the remainder were in awe at the photographs that captured snapshots of the ruins and views of the surrounding district. Those of us left at ground level enjoyed the hours viewing the ruins, ramparts, moats, miniature water gardens, fountain garden, octagonal pond and so much more of the area surrounding the base of the Rock before heading to the interesting museum.

Reading the reviews had me worried and nervous for this climb. But actually it was totally fine. I would advise getting there early to avoid the crowds. I got there at 8am and left as the tour buses and queues were building up. The rock entrance opens at 7am and closes at 5.30pm but get there early to avoid the afternoon heat. The climb itself only took 45 mins up - and I took my time. I got to the top and walked around for 30 mins before coming back down. I would say the whole experience took under 3 hours. There are a lot of steps but it's totally manageable if you just take your time and wear sensible shoes. I had my hiking sandals on. Some locals wore flip flops which I personally wouldn't recommend.
A must visit in Sri Lanka . The architecture of the history is amazing. Word cannot explain how beautiful this place is ...

This World Heritage site shows the ancient Sri Lankans' ingenuity in construction, architecture, design and engineering. It took us several thousand steps to get to the top. This place is full of interesting stories of the past ancient king. If not for the history, come for the view. You might think many times if you're afraid of heights but the view from the top is gorgeous and definitely worth it. Bring sun protection because there's very little shade. Wear comfortable clothes and footwear. Bring a cold bottle of water and some trail food if you get hungry easily.

We went with our toddler to Sigiriya. It was quite hard. But we did it! Our toddler enjoyed it! And we did as well! That feeling, when you climb all the way up - amazing! And the view - beautiful. Bring your raincoat in rainy season. We had un umbrella, but it is difficult to manage it. Raincoat would be better choice. And bring some food for the dogs.
The area around the rock and the walk up was beautiful, as was the view. A little too expensive though.

We visited as part of a tour. There are a lot of steps and if you need help, there are some men who will drag you up the steps and give you some info about the site. The negative is that I repeatedly told one of these men I did not need his help and he just kept grabbing my arm, then had the cheek to tell me I must pay 20 dollars for the help, which he said he had negotiated with our tour guide! We did not pay it, so he got in a real strop. The views are pretty amazing, and what remains of the ancient city after so many centuries is intersting. I would recommend a visit, but leave plenty of time as there is a lot to see. I know the helpers have to make a living, but either make it clear what you will pay from the start or send them away. Take a hat and water. There are some facilities about half way up. The climb is about 200 meters of steps.

Climbing this huge massive rock was attached in our Itinerary which we got from our Local Tour Operator and we did not hestitate to skip this because of the Arts. Its highly recommended to climb in the morning as it get heated at afternoon which will be hard and also recommend to take plenty of Water. The panoramic view at the top was amazing. Thank you Kingfisher Tours Sri Lanka and our guide Aswar to take us here. Highly Recommended!

If you suffer from vertigo, then you will need to take a very deep breath before embarking on the climb to the top of Sigiriya, which rises 200 metres straight up out of the surrounding countryside.  The steps up the mountain are universally steep and often hang from the side of the mountain out over the space below and to see the magnificent painted Sigiriya Damsels it is necessary to scale and then descend two winding spiral staircases attached to there rock and with nothing but air below.  While all the steps are quite secure, you sometimes feel as if you are suspended in space! The climb is quite a hard slog and there is little shelter so it is best to go early in the morning.  The remnants of the water gardens and other construction at the base of the mountains, the painted ladies, the extensive remains at the top of the mountain and the spectacular views are well worth the effort.  It seems absolutely amazing that such a construction could have been built with minimal equipment in such difficult terrain 1500 years ago and that the King responsible for the works then rashly decided to leave his impregnable fortress and fight his enemy at ground level only to be defeated and commit suicide.  Such incredible folly!

I went their with my wife. Location was very beautiful. Have lots of thing to capture from your camara. Lots of historical evidence can be seen. Anyone who are visiting Sigiriya or Habarana area must visit to this place.

My first time climbing a rock fortress. I have climbed many mountains, visited dozens of temples and ancient sites to. However this one is awe inspiring and majestic both in its simplicity and 'remote' location. Located a few hundred kilometers (and miles) from Colombo, you can book several tours that will get you there in a few hours from any part of Sri Lanka. It is an island after all. We spent a few hours here after going to Dambulla and I'm glad we did, as this was scenic yet serene. A tour guide is not necessary as the place speaks for itself and large group tours can be rushed to get from A to B. We were in a small group and allowed to take our time. Even though we did this, I could easily have spent more time exploring the place and taking in the setting. Its not an arduous climb, although the spiral metal staircase about halfway to the top can leave one feeling a bit dizzy. However, if you have vertigo you would not be climbing this rock. One of my favorite places in Sri Lanka, which is a beautiful country. Definitely would recommend a visit if in Sri Lanka.

This is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning in the world. Better you get to know the history before you visit. Sigiriya may be the Alakamandava that was built up before 5000 years ago. You may need 2 to 3 hours for visiting.

Our Driver recommended an early start here to beat the heat and we were so grateful for his good advice.  The climb to the top seems much more daunting from the bottom than the actuality of completing the walk up Sigiriya Rock. The history of the Ancient City is fascinating and the scenery is stunning!

A must place to see if ur interested in history and culture of places , located in central province built in 5th century by king kashyap now a world heritage site . Climb is not so difficult , there is places to take a rest and click memories.

We deliberated on whether we would visit and climb the rock as we had a 2.5hr drive from Kandy to Sigiriya and the weather was poor (as it is in October). We made the journey, and we didn’t regret it. It was a good experience, it essentially rained the entire climb which meant just taking it easy to avoid slipping. It is over priced like everyone else has mentioned (but so is stone henge, and that was far more disappointing!). When it isn’t wet, it’s very quickly very hot (so bring water!). On reflection I would consider not climbing the rock when it is wet. It becomes seriously slippery, the stairs become the run off for water and you are exposed to the elements when at height. If something was to go wrong, you’d be in a bit of strife. We went on a Monday at approx 10:30am and it wasn’t busy and we were back in our car by 12:30pm. A guide could be handy next time to give you context on the history (we overheard one guide for a couple and he was very informative). But make sure they are wearing a white guise top

At  USD 25 per person, not a cheap day out for a family  But that is true of most sights in Sri Lanka. There are over 2000 steps, but its not as bad as it sounds as they are quite well spaced out into various sections (2 main ones).  And the view at the top is definitely worth the effort. If you are a little wary of heights watch out for the official looking guides (in matching T shirts) who will rush to help you (or may help even if you don't need it).  In particular they can be found on the last steep section (as you go through the lion paws). Once you are at the top they will demand money for their services!  And not small amounts at 1000 Rps. Luckily we had our own real guide for our tour of Sri Lanka.  And there are a lot of details that he relayed that made our visit all the more interesting.  For example, how did they get water to the top of the rock?  And pointing out  the fountains fed from pools at the top of the rock. If you are lucky you may spot a crocodile in the pools at the base. I highly recommend getting there in the morning before the sun rises over the rock and beats down onto the steps.  We arrived around 0930 and were back down within a couple of hours and were in the shade whilst climbing.

This ancient attraction is just as impressive and awe-inspiring as websites and other reviewers have said. The site is a massive one and other than the rock fortress (for which there is an entry fee), there are other places which visitors can roam for free. As you get down, you will be approached by numerous guides who will try to dissuade you from buying tickets to the rock fortress by mentioning the arduous 1200 step climb and instead offer you a tuk-tuk ride covering the places which are free. They arent aggressive but can be pushy, so you need to firmly tell them off. Foreigners need to but tickets from the museum (entry to which is USD 5 if brought separately and complimentary if you purchase the rock fortress tickets). The museum is a good place to start off your visit. The tickets to the rock fortress are USD 30 for adults and USD 15 for children. SAARC country nationals are entitled to a 50% discount on the adult price but no further discounts for children (so USD 15 for both adults and children). Payment can be made in USD or LKR but change, if any, is returned in LKR. The climb itself is actually quite difficult, especially if you go in the afternoon. The place is also crowded on weekends because of lots of locals coming for a picnic. My suggestion would be to go early morning to beat the heat and the crowds. Carry lots of water and snacks as well, as there werent any outlets selling food or water. The way up is different from the way down, so take pictures as you go up, because you wont get the same view on the way down. A lot of people have suggested the recommended length as being 3-4 hours but from my experience, it takes a lot longer, especially if you have young children and also explore the whole place. So in my opinion, take your time and enjoy the whole place in all its splendour and beauty. Dont try to rush things through and combine this with another attraction (like Dambulla, Anuradhapura etc) because those places too require more than 3-4 hours and it would be better to comprehensively cover both places rather than do a bit of both.
We had a great day climbing up to the ancient ruins. Strenuous but worth the views and sense of accomplishment!
Thanks to Mohamed Elshaer for bringing us around pyramids and Cairo.its good to know about ancient history of Egypt in details.

The staircases attached to sheer walls to reach the top. On the way you'll pass a series of quite remarkable frescoes and a pair of colossal lion's paws carved into the bedrock. The surrounding landscape – lily-pad-covered moats, water gardens and cave shrines – only add to Sigiriya's rock-star appeal.

Sigiriya or Sinhagiri (Lion Rock, සීගිරිය) is an ancient rock fortress located near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. According to the ancient Sri Lankan this site was selected by King Kashyapa (477 – 495 CE) for his new capital. He built his palace on the top of this rock and decorated its sides with colourful frescoes. The capital and the royal palace was abandoned after the king's death. It was used as a Buddhist monastery until the 14th century.Sigiriya today is a UNESCO listed World Heritage Site. It is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning.

It was a tedious climb of 1200 steps to reach the top. Going up was still manageable enough. Climbing down those seriously steep stairs was frightening even if you don’t have acrophobia. They are even steeper than the abandoned Great Wall of China ruined steps. And there were wild dogs on those stairs to distract us. It was then I understood as to why there was the First Aid camp at Lion’s Paw entrance. We had a useless on-site guide who talked rubbish. He was recommended to us by our driver. He did however guide us through the short cuts in the massive site. We were also taken to the ancient caves and shelters occupied by monks as early as 3rd century BCE. The frescoes of the semi-nude ladies with their mysterious smiles and eyes were as hauntingly vivid as they were in the 5th century AD. And those ancient graffiti on the Mirror Wall written in old script dated from 6th to 13th century AD was particularly fascinating to see. Once we went up there, we took pictures by standing on the last few steps left. It was exhilarating. The site is one stunning architectural example of urban planning. All are lost now except for the water gardens, pools, water tanks and wall borders of the Sky Palace. We admired the Lion City from our hotel’s restaurant during breakfast the next morning. I sure feel proud having to make it to the top of the sacred city of Sinhagiri by King Kashyapa.

SIGIRIYA  (THE “LION MOUNTAIN”) Sigiriya is located 175 kilometers north-east of Colombo. 10 kilometers from the highway Ambepussa – Kurunegala – Trincomale. Located between the towns of Dambulla and Habarana. Sigiriya (the “Lion Mountain”) is one of Asia`s major archaeological sites and a World Heritage site declared by UNESCO in 1982. City and Palace are a unique combination of 5th century urban planning, architecture, engineering, hydraulics, garden design, paintings, sculpture and poetry. It has attracted the attention of modern antiquarians and archaeologists since the early 19th century. Area around the main Sigiriya rock was the location of a Buddhist rock-shelter monastery from the last few centuries BC. The present city, Palace and Garden remains from the time of their creator, Kasyapa I (477-495 AC) Often wrongly described as a fortress or castle, Sigiriya is in fact a well-planned royal city and a multi-faceted, multi-period settlement, several square kilometers in extent. The entire Sigiriya archaeological complex consists of following parts. 01.	The central core around the rock and the palace 02.	The western sector – essentially the water gardens 03.	The eastern sector – the inner and outer cities 04.	The Mapagala fortified complex 05.	The Pidurangala monestary 06.	The Ramakale monastery 07.	The Sigiriya lake (Sigiri Mahavava) and canal system The most famous features of the Sigiriya complex are the 5th century paintings (Frescos) found on the rock face more than 100 meters above ground level Ticket Counter: Open at 7.00am Close at 5.00pm Ticket Price: 30US$ (Foreign) Height: About 180 meters (600 Feet / 1250 Steps) Average Time Spent: 2 Hours

UNESCO world heritage site in Sri Lanka, Sigiriya is a wonderful ancient palace built atop a 660 feet tall rock column. Located about 170km northeast of Colombo and 56km west of Polonnaruwa, this wonderful rock castle is a creation of King Kashapa (AD 477- 495). Sigiriya is one of the most attracted historical sites in Sri Lanka and it is most famous for its stunning frescoes. Sigiriya is considered one of the most important urban planning sites of the first millennium, and the site plan is considered very elaborate and imaginative. On the west side of the rock lies a park for the royals, laid out on a proportioned plan; the park contains water-retaining structures, including sophisticated surface-subsurface hydraulic systems, some of which are working even today. The most important aspects of Sigiriya are the gardens and it is among the oldest landscaped gardens in the world. The gardens are divided into three distinct but linked forms: water gardens, cave and boulder gardens, and terraced gardens.

My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Sri Lanka and earlier today we visited the famous Lion Rock at Sigiriya. Although the Rock itself is imposing so is the surrounding complex - which dates back to the 5th Century - of which only 20% has been fully excavated. It is also not a cheap option for foreigners (US$15 & 30 for children and adults respectively) but locals not only pay a fraction of this price but this tends to make the attraction very busy at weekends. Everything is well organised as one sets out to climb the Rock which - through a series of vertical steps (over 2,000 in all!) - should (depending on the volume of visitors!) take the average individual around 30 minutes to reach the Palace/Summit. That proved the case for us but our problem - made worse by the total lack of signage - is that it took almost as long to find the way down! Fortunately - particularly, as a Thunderstorm was fast approaching - the way down is a much shorter route so we were not overly delayed. We also managed to avoid taking on the services of a guide or leave with any local souvenirs which was an achievement in itself! All in all, well worth the effort although this is not a walk in the park and also perfectly safe for anyone having any worries on the Health & Safety front!

Sigiriya is one of the most visited attractions in Sri Lanka and it doesn't disappoint. Visiting the ancient city is totally worth it with awesome views of the surroundings and photo opportunities, although the city itself is in total ruins. The climb up is a little arduous but worth it, recommend climbing it before the sun is fully up. Takes about 2-3 hours to visit. Also recommend visiting nearby Pidurangala rock to catch sunrise/sunset view of the Lion Rock i.e. Sigiriya.
Its quite an adventure to climb up to the top of this rock structure. Stay dehydrated - the heat can be scourging. But it is worth the climb.

Well, what an experience, hardly anyone there. Many many many steps ,to reach the place of the lions feet. What a great view once you catch your breath. What a climb ,but worth the extra effort. Make sure you take enough water.

The Sigiri Lion Rock is a great climb. Lot to see at base too for those who can't climb stairs. External & internal moat & 3 styles of garden  ( now in Ruins ) but you can imagine. The climb has  flat breaks & places of interest so it's not a straight climb

Sigiriya is a rock fortress near the Sri Lankan city of Dambulla. It is very expensive to enter the fortress and foreigners pay US$30 each - remember to bring your passport. When you enter the grounds you walk along a long path over a moat and through water gardens. As you walk along the path the 200 metre high rock fortress juts out in front of you. There are many steps to climb to the top of the fortress. As you climb to the citadel you pass through the fresco with its ancient female paintings, the mirrored wall and the Lion’s Paws - all the while on a rickety metal ladder - the view is amazing. The citadel is in ruins now, but the swimming pool is visible and the view from the citadel is simply awesome and well worth the climb. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a must visit when in Sri Lanka - it certainly provides the wow experience!

Sigiriya is most famous place in Sri Lanka. Beautiful Lion's Rock Fortress is so beautiful place. View from the top of the rock is amazing. This is the 8th wonder of the world. You have to climb 1200 steps to get to top and you can visit Mirror wall, Frescoes and ruins of the palace. you must visit this place

Hundreds of years of history in one rock.  It was the palace and home of King Kashyapa's reign (477 to 495 CE), the son of King Dhatusena.  Sigiriya was developed as a complex city and fortress. Most of the constructions on the rock summit and around it, including defensive structures, palaces, and gardens, date from this period. It has a water system with effective drainage alongside high level pools.  Great day out but be prepared for a fitness test as there is a lot of climbing to be done.  Kings have big visions ad with big visions come great heights.  So to get to the top you need to make sure you have a hearty breakfast!

A must do. Worth the effort. could spend at least a day here to get a good look around. Do early in the morning, take a long break then do safari in the late afternoon. 3 onwards as this is when Elephants come out of the Jungle.
The city is really a place with huge ruins areas preserved and protected. Sigiriya is an area anyone should visit during their tour to Sri Lanka.

Breath taking views. Lots of steps (as opposed to slopes) to walk up. Definitely worth it when at the top but start off early to beat the crowds. We set off around 6.30am and so glad we did as we passed lots more people going up as we were on the way down. Some stalls etc at the bottom for snacks and drinks and souvenirs which are reasonably priced. Plus, the earlier you go, the cooler it is on the top plus whilst walking. Be sure to take plenty of water!

Lion’s rock is worth visiting Sigiriya. 1200 steps to conquer, to see the beautiful 360 degree view. Its preferable to leave early morning at around 7, before the heat hits up. Additionally, proper foot wear and comfortable attire will help, as it be tiring and exhausting to climb. The entrance fee is 35USD, for Indian passport holders, its 10USD. There are guides at the entrance, its better to fix the prices, incase if you are curious about the history of this place. On the way up, there is a cave with ancient paintings which has a connection with Indian mythology “Ramayana” There is a huge wall in the mid, its called “mirror wall” not sure why, no description was mentioned. On top of the rock, there are ruins of the palace of King Kashyap, spread all over. It is amazing to see, at such height, a palace existed in the ancient times. An amazing experience to explore this place.
This is an incredible ancient location and requires climbing 1200 stairs but the view is totally worth it.

This is the first place i visited after landing in Sri Lanka. It will take about 2-3 hours to cover this place. Hire a guide to know more this historic place. View from the top of the hill will amaze you.

Sigiriya is an unique and beautiful place to visit. If we plan to visit there, need to prepare ourselves mentally and physically to climb almost 1200 steps. The entrance fee is USD 30. Luckily, we got a well experienced tour guide who could explain about the place very well. Once you reached the top, we could see the overall view of the city. The best time to visit the place would be either early in the morning during sunrise and in the evening during sunset. We could enjoy the sunset or sunrise. However, in the middle of the day, the sun will be too hot and we can easily feel very tired. Since, we went during the sunset time, the overall weather was nice and its encourage us  to climb in the cool breeze. Overall the experience was good.
Entrance fee is not too small. But in general may be it worth it. If you have a good imagination - in process of walk you will fly to that ancient time when king Kassapa are living there ;)

I and my family went for it on Feb, remarkable ancient remains with great view, good weather and windy over there. Our driver took 5- 6 hrs. from Colombo, acceptable with only 2 lanes road and we had a chance stop at  local village near Sigiriya which we ride a cart to a big pond, take a boat and have local lunch at a home (tour cost is not much).

This historic fortress is an engineering masterpiece. A fort/palace built on top of a rock. Worth the (at times) steep climb to take in the majesty of what was created (now ruins) and the 360 degree view. You will need a reasonable level of fitness to achieve the top but there are a number of interesting sites (rock painting etc) and views to see lower down so don’t be put off. A must see if visiting Sri Lanka

Aim to get there early in the morning, when the park opens, to avoid the heat and the crowds. Lion's Rock is impressive, nice to look at and the view from the top is great. The climb is a great work out.
Be aware that you're in for a pretty stiff stair climb to the top. Well worth the effort! Our guide was excellent and paced the accent to suit our party.

We visited in May 2019 via private car and driver booked through Simply Ceylon Tours (highly recommended, see my separate review).  Most of the visitors were local - it was the Vesak day holiday weekend.  We were some of the only foreigners there.  Security was very good. Be prepared to have your bags searched.  They cut the labels off of your plastic water bottles.  Not sure why, but just go with it...  Definitely recommend going early in the morning when most of the trek is shaded.  Even early, the sun is brutally hot, so take sunscreen and plenty of water.   Restrooms in the foreign tourist carpark were very well kept and clean.  This is a must do when visiting Sri Lanka!
You need a guide to better understand the place. Go in the early morning or late evening. It gets very hot during the day.

Sigiriya like a visiting card of Sri Lanka. Lions rock is past residents of Kassapa kingdom, which is protected by UNESCO. The best time to climb it's early morning or after 4 pm, otherwise it's too hot. It's important to  wear comfortable shoes and clothes. Entrance ticket is a bit expensive 30$, but it's attraction place which "must see". We spend around 2 hours in Sigiriya. First we went through water gardens,     saw old murals, climbed to the place were lions feet and went up to the flat top of hill. Explored archeological ruins. View is really fantastic. We saw many monkeys on the way. It's great attraction place to visit.

Sigiriya is a wonderful destination in Sri Lanka.  You need to be in pretty good shape for all the steps and stairs, and not afraid of heights. At the bottom are subtle remnants of an ancient culture.  As you climb up, be sure to see the colorful wall paintings up the spiral staircase.  The you go around the rock to the lion paws carved from rock and up the steep stairs to the ruins on top, including a pool, and foundations, with a expansive view.  The stairs down to the parking lot level are easy.
It is must watch place in Sri Lanka. It should be preferred only by youngsters since walking is difficult. Should start early in the morning

Another great place to visit if you can tolerate the heights and heat. the rock arts and fortress is one such experience. the climb provides opportunities to grand vistas and glimpse in to liberal arts and sexuality of ancient Sinhalese people( which is quite opposite to today where religious police decides what to wear). here are the negatives, there are hardly any facilities for locals as well as tourists ( drinking water, toilet facilities, medical facilities and shade or restaurant at the site or at the peak, not to mention the hefty fee they charge from foreign visitors. similar facility in Europe or Australia is generally free since there are other means of getting money. disappointed with that aspect.

If you like the outdoors and you have a sense of adventure then this place is for you. If you are unfit and do not like heights and do not fancy walking on tiny metal steps suspended on the side of a rock face then this is not for you. Also if you are allergic to bee/wasp stings then you should also avoid here as there are swarms of them, like thousands at one point. Fortunately we stayed calm and kept quiet and they went away, but I guess you could be less fortunate, there are signs there saying “warning wasps” so you are warned. I thought I would mention the things that may put anyone off first as they are important and I wouldn’t want anyone not to enjoy their trip. But putting that aside “wow” it’s hard not to be impressed by this place, the history of it is fascinating and the views just stunning from every part of the journey up to the top. Obviously seeing the Lions staircase has to be the pinnacle but it is all just beautiful. I don’t know how much it costs to do this, so sorry if you wanted to know, it was all included for us in our package, but I’m sure it’s not expensive and you have to go and visit it if you are in the area, it was certainly a highlight for me on my Sri Lankan trip.

This ancient fortress/city with gardens in Sigiriya before the walk to the top offered different view. Not all people climb to the top but most of them will stop at the foot of the lion where there have place to sit and rest.
This is UNESCO site and an awesome place to climb early in the morning at 6.30am. The place it well maintain and the view from the top is awesome.

This place cost USD 30 for tourists but well maintain and is a must visit place when you're here. It's also UNESCO site. We are here 6.30am when the gate open and the climb is breathtaking. At the top even better to see the view from above and the place with pond etc.

We visit Sigiriya Rock early morning at around 7am when the ticketing office opens. Entrance fee is US$30 each and it was an easy hike up to the top. A great view up there and wasn’t too crowded and hot if you go there early. The crowd starts coming when we descend, but still manageable as tourism was badly affected by the bombing in late April. But it’s worth the trip and security is quite tight here.

SIGIRIYA is an historical city which has a historical value. It is located in the north central province of Srilanka. It is not only a rock but also a fortress used to be protected from invaders. It was re_built by King Kashyapa in Srilanka. And the first owner of this great kingdom was King Rwana..  There's a nice and interesting story was written around that place.. are you curious on it.. then have a look on google "RAWANA''. .. its really mysterious .. I want you to read that story.. Once it was nominated as a world's heritage.. its a bit adventurous and funny.. you will be able to have an amzing feeling while climbing up and looking down.😊 and its extremely unbelievable about its architecture.. have a visit to there definitely..  it takes just 4 - 5 hours to reach Sigiriya area from Bandaranaike international airport if you haven't any stop on the way.. but if You want to visit pinnawala too, then it will take just 5-6 hours.. most preferable thing is to book a personal driver to see the excursions in Srilanka .. its very safe and effective 😊👌..

Went for the third time in May 2019. What a wonderful rock to climb in the evening. Since there weren't much guests those days we were able to climb up within 30 minutes but I heard it usua3take one hour during season. So start your climb with adequate time yo left to view the sunset. If you don't know about its history take a good government approved Guid to learn things and I'm sure with adequate knowledge you will be amazed when you go up. Frescoes will be closed by 6.30pm. So plan your climb accordingly.

Absolutely it's a must see! It's an amazing place, full of history and beauty. It is remnant of a long-extinct and sunken volcano. Located on a relatively flat upland is visible from a distance of many kilometers. Rock has been adapted to the royal palace located at the top, and after that there was buddhist monastery. Now it is archaeological site, you can see there traces of old technology, sculpture and painting. Despite the high ticket price, Sigiriya is recommendable. In my opinion Pidurangala Rock is not alternative to Sigiriya, Pidurangala Rock is fantastic complement of Sigiriya - we are enchanted Sigiriya and we don't regret that bought the tickets and visited it

The Ancient City of Sigiriya is a must visit when in Sri Lanka.  Lion Rock is the towering location of King Kasyapa palace on the top. We arrived about 8am for the hike to the top. You purchase tickets before you get to the screening point (on the right as you approach the rock from the carpark - about $30US). Make sure you take plenty of water for the trip up and wear appropriate shoes. The walk is challenging but there are opportunities to stop at various locations for photos etc. It was not crowded on the day we visited as it was soon after the terrorism incident. The view from the top was magnificent - 360 degree views of the surrounding countryside. The ruins of the palace are interesting to walk around and marvel at how challenging it would have been to construct. I would recommend commencing your walk as early as possible to avoid the heat of the day. A must do when in Sri Lanka

A homogenous blend of Ramayana and Buddhism. That would exactly describe this place and the perfect blend of the two cultures or ideally can be said religion. This is one of the places, where Lord Buddha actually visited. This is a world heritage site. The climb is a must to the top and the view is breathtaking. almost every stone has a story and ensure that you have a good guide to appreciate the relevance to Ramayana. Don't let it detour you. It is worth the climb.!!!

We did it,1202 steps to the top in the heat,we were so proud but it was well worth it. The view is stunning and the ruins worth seeing. There is a circular staircase for a bit which is scary if you don’t like heights.You do go up then down it if you want to see the rock paintings. Most parts you feel quite safe,and do a little training with steps before you go and it really helps.

We arrived about 7.30 am and there were already lots of people there! It is definitely worth getting there early as it is cooler and less crowds. We came down about 9am and it was very hot and very crowded. The climb is up thousands of steps and stairs. Quite a climb but worth it as the views from the top are breathtaking. This was one of the highlights of our trip.

Arrived around 9am with a guide.  Lots of people but did not feel crowded.  The grounds before the actual climb are magnificent and the history is fascinating.  The entire climb around and up to the top is not too difficult.  My husband has bad knees and managed most of the climb missing the last push to the top.  There were people clearly nervous about heights and having to push themselves to the top but it is very achievable.  Yes it was hot but only what we expected and manageable. This magnificent palace is carved out of granite and is truely something you will not want to miss.  A must do.

Sigiriya is the home of Lion Rock, a 200 m high rock and the site of a 5th-century palace and kingdom. Formed out of the magma of an extinct volcano, King Kasyapa chose the rock as a site for his palace and indeed his own kingdom. ﻿﻿The ancient rock palace has some very unique frescoes that are incredibly well-preserved considering they are more than 1,500 years old and at the plateau, you will find the beautiful gardens of Sigiriya, which are among the oldest landscaped gardens in the world. It gets pretty hot by noon, so it's good to get there early and start climbing Sigiriya Rock while it's cool. For really early birds, another tip is to climb nearby Pidurangala Rock and see the sunrise over Sigiriya. The view is breathtaking as the first rays of sun spread over Sigiriya and the surrounding landscape. Tips: Climbing Sigiriya Rock takes about an hour. There are places to stop if you need to take a break. Children can also climb the rock, but I would say a good age is around 8 years and up. Finally, don't forget to pack a hat, drinking water and good walking shoes!

Climbing Sigiriya was probably our favourite activity in Sri Lanka.  The climb is strenuous, but completely do-able. Best to go early in the morning when it’s cooler. The view and sense of accomplishment is worth every step!
There are no words for this place.  Only suggestion is to look at what the palace looked like before so when there you can use your imagination.
Just as well we left at 7am in the morning, the steeps were fairly steep so not for the faint hearted.  Well worth being at the top but exhausting getting there.
This was a great experience and definitely worth doing. The views were spectacular and the history of Sigiriya is so interesting.

We arrived at the museum at 07:00 as it opened to purchase tickets. We then went straight to the complex and started the climb to the summit. It was incredible, but I am scared of heights and it really pushed me. Everything was well coordinated and staffed. After exploring the summit we came back down and explored the rest of the ruins, then went to the museum which was very informative. It is quite a steep climb but definitely manageable. And worthwhile. We had an incredible experience.

At first my wife thought it would be too much, but after our guild Roshan said to give it a go, we both were more than happy to climb. Many steps and a litre of water later we made it to the top. Well worth the climb, and it isn't as scary as it looks.

We managed to do the hike and it took us about 45 minutes to reach the top. Lots of Tourist come here to visit the Sigiriya. There is a fee that needs to be paid at the entrance. We didn't take the tour guides but just followed the trail on the map provided. If you are a person that is afraid of height dont go there.

The ancient city of Sigiriya was top of my list for things to do in Sri Lanka and maybe because of the expectation I was perhaps a little dissapointed by the hoardes of people visting, even first thing in the morning. That said, its still a five star and a must see in Sri Lanka and despite the steep entrance fee. It's recommended to come early and climb the rock before it gets hot, but we could see the rock from our hotel and we saw fewer people on the stairs in the aternoon. We arrived for just after 6.30am and then queued for tickets and then queued to enter. We headed right away to climb the rock and decided to leave the grounds for after. If you come in the afternoon you get the sun on the rock rather than a shadow, so in hindsight an afternoon trip would have been my preference. The climb itself wasn't challenging and I would say fine for anyone with a moderate level of fitness. It's fine for kids too (my friend's 5y old has previously climbed up OK). The ascent is slow because of the number of people. There are a few tricky stairs if you don't like heights and there are men handing around to offer you a helping hand for a fee. Just say no. Once on top there are great views of the surrounding area as well as the ruins of the ancient city itself. Due to the size of the old city, its a less hectic on top and you can easily spend half an hour exploring and recovering from the climb. The grounds themselves are worth exploring before you depart.

This is a beautiful place. If you want to go to the top of this old fortress you have to climb over 1000 stepts.It`s not that hard, but it is very hot outside, so try and go early in the moring of at evening to see the sunset. And also, there are a lot of monkeys up there.

We visited early in the morning to avoid the heat. It's very expensive(30$ to climb a rock), but we liked it very much :) It is recommended to pay in USD, as the exchange rate for USD to LKR is pretty bad and you will end up paying more.

We visited on a hot & humid morning and along with our allocated guide, were soon joined by another guide who offered to help my wife up the stairs. This was appreciated at the time as my wife was struggling with a painful knee. The experience is well worth the effort & the information provided by our guide was valuable in appreciating the site. Once at the top we thanked the second guide & offered him a 500 rupee tip. He said this was not acceptable and demanded a 2000 rupee tip. After returning to the bottom I offered our second guide a 2000 rupee tip but he said 3000 was his price. We never paid this much in tips any where else during our 2 weeks in Sri Lanka & found the guides at the Ancient Rock to be greedy & rude. Be sure to negotiate the tip before your tour starts.

Yes, the view is great, there's a lion paw and some brick walls on the top. You need to try hard to imagine what those buildings could be once. Why is the mirror wall is called mirror??? It is just a yellow painted wall. Overall, it does not worth usd 30. Go to next hill Pidurangala for lkr 500. It's just too expensive for what you get.
Excellent plea wonderful UNESCO died and good view I'm recommend sigrya rook    good people waking buteful images
The best ancient experience how a king has lived inside a Huge Massive Rock with all the Srilankan Paintings inside, Really enjoyed visiting the World Unesco Heritage Site in Srilanka

We climbed Lion Rock in the early morning (7 am) which was a good idea as the heat can be very taxing. I am 75 and have had coronary artery stents 12 months ago. The trail up was reasonably steep with many steps but many rest areas possible. When we reached the staging area for the ladders (the Lion’s paw) I was surprised that we were so close to the summit. The ladders are steep but safe. However if you are scared of heights do not do the final section as there is a shear drop that looks startling. Great views from the top and fascinating ruins.
Amazing history, paintings, architecture, techniques and view. Great place for every travelers who are able to climb. Other can wait down.

As a lot of tour company’s seem to have cancelled their tours, there weren’t many people at Sigiriya when we climbed in the afternoon, maybe 20 people. Make sure you have time to explore the grounds after you climb by following the signs that go to the car park. We found that more interesting than the actual climb. It’s a beautiful area. When we came down there weren’t any tuk tuks around (perhaps a sign of less tourists) so we walked to our nearby hotel (beware of snakes and elephants if you have to do the same).

Being 65 with arthritic knees I found going down to be more difficult that going up. It was 32 degrees with high humidity so that added to the degree of difficulty. However if you take your time and keep your fluids up it is certainly achievable. There are some grand views going up and the view from the top is magnificent. If it is physically possible for you to do the climb then do it.

It was good, the best time to visit Sigiriya is as early as 6.30 am, when the sun is not hot & before the big local crowds come in or in the evening around 3.00 pm when the sin is going down. Take ample amount of water as there are no shops on the rock. The best time to take photographs is from the east side in the evening when the sun is shining on the mirror wall.
Magical place. A very beautiful view from the hill. I recommend going Up. One of many obligatory places on Ceylon.

Everybody tried to put us off climbing to the top. All the advice was that we should do it only in the early morning and when it wasn't so crowded. Needless to say we didn't have any choice as we were there at midday on a public holiday. It was hot, crowded and difficult (I found the first bit up the stone steps much harder than the bit after the Lions Paws where at least there was a handrail), but it was worth all the effort. Magnificent views!! Just don't believe that the local people are going to be polite and queue quietly. They push and shove you all the way and cut you up when they get the chance. They even tread on you to get in front. But there's never any rancour and they do it with a smile - and they don't seem to mind if you push and shove right back. In fact, be wary of anyone who extends a helping hand. They want money!
Must go of Sigiriya! Very hot and very crowdy, you should go early in a morning Dont forget to bring your water to the top Stay away from the cheeky monkies :-)

Lots of beautiful nature. Climbing up is not easy, but I think it is possible to reach the top of every person. The most important thing is not to rush. We are not fast, just a little bit rested. The most important thing is to have water. Beautiful panoramic views can be seen from the top. From the top of the hill we landed down quickly, as it was easy to get down.

I arrived relatively early around 8:30am and purchased a ticket there. There weren’t any queues really which was great. I did this on my own with no guide and really enjoyed it. I do think a guide may have given me a bit more knowledge of the place though. It was busy and the climb was hot! The views are absolutely out of this world. I would highly recommend this experience if you are in srilanka.

Worth getting up early to do this climb both for the heat and for the number of people passing on the staircase going up the side of the rock.  I'd prepared myself for a much longer climb but reached the top quicker than i thought.  We had a guide who told us some interesting information but it's not necessary.  The views in all directions are spectacular.  We left our hotel at 6am and were back having breakfast by 9.30.  Lots of savvy monkeys around so hang on to your valuables!

It is a beautiful site initially approaching the rock through the ponds. You can imagine what it was like when the empire was at its heights. Once you reach the base of the rock its then a easy walk up the the wall of mirrors. Once you reach the Lion's Paw there is a plateau where you get some fantastic views and a good rest stop - then its a vertical stair climb up to the top of the rock. This was the toughest part mainly due to the heat and crowds (it was mid morning) Once you reach the top of the rock you are rewarded with a beautiful view of the surrounding area - well worth the climb up!

Loved the views from the top, well worth the climb but do it early in the day when it is not so hot and it is not too crowded. The history of the place is worth understanding and will make you appreciate the climb. Visit the museum at the base of the rock.
Amazing experience, worth the climb. So much history in this area. Enjoyed the museum tour before to explain the site and its history and significance for Sri Lanka.

In title itself I mentioned both sides of the place. Sigiriya rock or commonly known as Lion rock is one of the two rock climbing points in Sigiriya. A world heritage sight with lots of small caves and ponds signifying the ancient history of the place. History lovers would definitely spend time exploring different section of the premises.I being more on the adventure side wanted to climb up the rock as soon as possible so to breath the fresh air and feel the happiness viewing beautiful view from top. Ticketing counter/ building is not well maintained but lucky enough for us to not visit the place when it was crowded. To my surprise the ticket difference for locals and foreigners is too high which doesn't make any justice to the world travelers who visit to explore and spread the word to fellow travelers. addition to it is some locals who wait on way up to try to make money by guiding tourist in unethical way. This things definitely will spread a wrong message about this beautiful place. You need to climb a lot of steps towards top and as you go closer the steps become steep and more dangerous with respect to the way they are structured as well as on safety aspect. Adventure lovers will love the way as I did but that involves a lot of risk too. some of the patches during travel is too risky for normal tourist and if you are scared of heights then better avoid the place. At the foot of the main rock you can see lion feet carved with a small relaxing place where I did notice some people who did skip climbing the main rock due to higher steepness of the steps. we did go up and believe me though the top plateau looks not well maintained but the view from top is worth every penny which we spend ( this I wrote compare to what I paid for the trip). We felt lovely and spend more than a hour with a breathtaking view from top. Considering heritage place you cannot use drone at this place but clicking pictures for memories is worth. we did click a picture from top with back to Pidurangala rock which was our plan for the next day. I would suggest to visit the place though a bit expensive but avoid locals guides in between which will save you from getting annoyed as well as on extra wasting of money.
Just do it. Get over the height and climb to see one of the great sights. Either the build was genius or folly but either way amazing

I have recently visited sigiriya rock. It was impressive with lots of things to see (gardens, caves etc), however I feel the toughness of the climb gets played down slightly. The steps really are tough, especially the last section. I am great with heights and even I was starting to get a bit wobbly towards the top. When you get to the top the views are worth it. We set off early and got there about 8.15, by the time we got to the top it was 35 degrees and only 9.30 in the morning. I would suggest going as early as possible to avoid the heat and crowds. The crowds were fine at the time we went. One final thing. At the lion feet location, if you decide not to proceed to the top there is an open area with water to wait. This area seemed quite busy (people Not choosing to continue I assume)

The other being the Blue Whale we saw, so this is a high bar! Physically beautiful and historically fascinating must-see.  Recommend visiting very early in the morning - it is worth an early wake-up to get to the top with a handful of people and not have to snake up the steep stairs with an endless crowd in the hot sun.

Our guide did tell us that to climb the rock in the morning is easier but it's busier as more tourists do the morning climb. We climbed it in the afternoon as we had scheduled other sights to see, so it was very hot as the sun shines onto the rock and the access steps which are all on the western side.  If you climb in the morning the sun will be behind the rock.  But with every advantage there is a disadvantage.  In the morning, if there are  more people, then negotiating the steps and then the spiral stair to the frescoes and mirror wall would be busier.  So weigh up what you'd prefer and decide morning or afternoon. It was hot but it was interesting to get the history of the area and then to climb up to see the remaining frescoes.  The spiral staircase up seems the newer one and the down staircase the older one.  So it was good to have that system as I can imagine when it's very crowded how this area would become very congested. But there were only six people in total, in the fresco area when we went up, so it was very.nice to enjoy viewing them without people jostling and having you move along and not just stand and enjoy for a short while. A further few steps and we are at the lions feet staircase to the top  of the fortress.  We chose to just enjoy the views we had from this level, as we didn't think anything further would be accomplished by going to the very top when there was very little left of the palace at the top of the rock. I would say do half the walk, see the frescoes, marvel at the natural rock water tank and enjoy the views from half way up.  If you want to climb the last steel staircase then do so. It's quite a climb in the heat.

Its a must visit place in Sri Lanka. It is also UNESCO's world heritage site. Once you go there you should climb to the top as the views on the way is amazing seeing all beautiful nature and amazing Sri Lanka. Please take water with you and also try to go in the morning.

The rock fortress, Ancient City of Sigiriya, is not only iconic because it is UNESCO heritage, but also because of its beautiful history. If you get a chance do read about King Visthavasa and his empire.  The frescos that adorn the walls and the architecture are still considered a marvel.
One of the best in Sri Lanka. I invite ppls to visit this place if not visited. And also make sure you go early  in the morning  so that sun will not be an issue at all.

We got up early to climb Lion Rock and we're very glad we did! Although we arrived a little late because of an elephant-in-the-road situation!
