My guide was continually telling me to take a break but I had to just change up and didn’t realise until we made it that he was quite tired which is understandable as he was a lot older than me. We spent a bit of time at the top and I was shown all the history and we got a few photos. Again on the decline my eyes were rested firmly down at the steps until we got to the paws. From there i was ok and it is a different route down than up. For most people this is a very doable climb because my fear of heights is massive. I recommend this to everyone as it is unique and for me the guide was invaluable but I don’t think many would require it.

Lion Rock of Sigiriya is one of the most wonderful points of attraction in world. To see the attraction , you need to climb up about 2000 stairs but it worth to see. of course it hot and you will need water. Some where at top of the rock there is a tank of water, but it is a little warm. It had better to take some bottle of water, if you can keep it cold it would be so much better. You will see e very good view at the top of the hill.

Can’t visit the area without climbing to the top! Visited in April which is one of the hottest months. We were one of the first through the gates at 7.30am and made a wise choice as the area is cooking during day. Take plenty of water! All in all it’s a couple of miles of walking and you’ll need a couple of hours to really experience the climb. Do it.

Amazing. Takes your imagination back to the era in which this was built and trying to picture what it must have looked like. Incredible size with the surrounding garden layout and the moat which surrounded the palace. The climb is quite manageable if you don't push it. 1200 steps, take a breather when you need it but be realistic if your not fit or have mobility issues, it is steep, it is hot, it is narrow so don't hurt yourself. Advice: go early before it gets too hot and the tour buses arrive and disgorge their visitors. If youa re physically up to it, you really must do it.

There were lots of locals offering to carry our child but not knowing whether he'd accept being carried by a stranger put us off. Well done to everyone that makes it to the top!

We had a wondeful climb and just being around a a giant boulder was mind blowing. The climb up is really not difficult  and can even be done using flip flops. Do hire a guide so that you see the significance of things.

Lion´s Rock is in itself a breathtaking place. We arrived at 4pm and was a harrowiing experience climbing all those narrow stairs in the afternoon sun. The equivalent to climbing 47 stories I think. Theview from the summit is awesome! Now the less positive aspects I must comment: Why is there a separate parking for foreign tourists? But I think this is a greedy and too quick a way to do this, and I see no visible improvements to tourism as a whole.. I thought 30 dollars per adult was rather pricey, the ticket office only accepts cash, (no credit cards) and I wasn´t given a receipt for my purchase of over 16.000 SL rupees for 3 adults and a teenager. The route after the gardens can pass via the wall paintings or not, this can save you considerable effort and time going up the rock. There were no sign tablets or info giving you these options! Once up there there were many dogs, and four little puppies, skin and bones and full of mange. A very distressing sight. On our way out to the parking lot we (the foreign visitors) are chanelled through an alley of salesmen, all in the name of making a quick buck. So, and all in all, a very historic and interesting visit but many things can be improved.

Absolutely beautiful, not a easy climb to the top but worth it. Getting to the top made me feel like I had entered the Jurassic era, the views looked unchanged throughout the centuries. Climbing to the top took monumental effort, having got to the top, it was worth every second and drop of sweat getting there. Beautiful.

A must see if touring Sri Lanka - really interesting site and great wildlife too in the form of monkeys and land monitors!  We arrived at the entrance at 8am and I think this would be the latest I would recommend going at.  Watch out for the hornet signs, a woman in front of us got stung so pay attention to the notices to be silent.  Take lots of water.  We had a guide as part of our package which was good to get more information but I've also climbed it many years ago without a guide and its still a great experience either way.

Be prepared for a long climb up the rock that is truly worth it! You don't really need a guide to go up the rock, just get the ticket and follow the path to the top. stop along the way to admire the view

Sigiriya is one of the most amazing places I have ever visited, a fortress built on the top of the rock by King Kasyapa (477 – 495 CE) with decorated sides with colorful frescoes and a gateway in the form of an enormous lion. Sigiriya today is the UNESCO listed World Heritage Site.  It is one of the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning.

We were there queuing early before 7am. The hike up was not as tiring as we thought it would be, but the advantage of doing it at this time of the day is that virtually the whole trek is done in the shade. Sections are tiring as the sun heats up. You get a little treat half way as you ascend a set of spiral staircases to view the cave painting which are quite mesmerising. From here you pass the mirrored wall. The walls are not adorned with mirrors but consist of polished plaster which reflects light and are adorned with antique graffiti and some more modern. You then reach one of the most remarkable sights of this trip to the Lions staircase which leads to to the summit. At the foot of these stairs are two huge lion claw carved paws.  Sadly they have been surrounded by protective fencing which makes getting a clear shot of them in context with the stairs difficult, but they really are stunning. From here you have the final 100m ascent and you are at the top ready to explore the ruins of the fortress, palace and ponds that were constructed at the summit  in 495 AD. It’s well worth the climb to have a 360 degree stunning view of the ruins and countryside.

My first site visit in Sri Lanka , that's a great hike to on top of the rock, was quite impressed how they managed to build this on top of this rocks . Very beautiful view from the top of the rocks , the garden on the bottom is very huge and well maintained till now .

We climbed it with our two young kids 4&6 and it was totally worth it. It’s not that hard if you take some breaks and have water with you. The views from the top come as a reward for your effort. Go ahead, take that climb, you’ll never regret it!
The climb is not real easy for those with any mobility issues but the view from the top is worthy of the effort.  The steps are a little scary but safe even if you are fazed by heights.

there are lot of steps to climb. but on the way we can sit and relax there are wall paintings and some historical things to see on the way. tickets are little expensive here its around 4850 in sri lankan rupees.

The hike up to the top requires walking up 1200 steps and its relatively hot but as long as you are able to walk stairs this is worth the time. The views from the summit are impressive and the ruins of the palace are well preserved. A tour guide was provided by the company I booked my entire stay in Sri Lanka with. The guide gave some interesting facts about the area but you do get a map that has the information on too.

Fascinating history with this UNESCO site. Definitely worth going to , if not for the history behind it. It was built and lived in by just one king. There are two moats and the outer one is still there.  Beautifully made.  There are remnants of water gardens , flower gardens, fountains  on the ground level inside the moats. The kind would live there in summer and moved up the to the hilltop during winter. The scenery up at the top is spectacular to see.  But there is not much left of anything at the top. You will see world famous frescoes of nude ladies dancing ( very few left) on the way up . Only a few remain.  Apparently the whole place was adorned with such frescoes but the weather contributed to some loss . but the worst vandalism happened when the king was conquered and the Sigiri rock was turned into a monastery.  The monks didn’t take well to pornography and had all the plasterwork taken out.  Apparently it was too distracting to praying and to celibate men. One word of advice – the climb is long and hard. I think we were told 2000 steps. And Dambulla Caves were only 200 steps.   If you have a heart condition or bad arthritis I would think long and hard about  doing it. Make sure to bring lots of water and take plenty of stops if you can.  No one sells water along the way. Near the top is a tap but not suitable for foreign stomachs who are not used to local water. The young and fit will make it in one short leap, whilst everyone else over 40 will struggle. The fee for getting in is quite expensive  for foreigners I think it was about 4000 LKR each ! . no point paying it if you are not going to do the climb. A lot of the fees goes back to doing more digs, and maintaining Sigirya rock.  Look at it as your contribution to the upkeep of a historical site. Get there early as you can,  as the afternoon crowds is overwhelming.  When you look at the monument from a few hundred meters away.  The visitors look like a trail of tightly packed  ants crawling up this rock in a single file. You will also get no shortage of people wanting to help you get up there ( at a cost of course) . and people wanting to provide guide services.  We were glad for our guide which our tour company ( Genuine Sri Lankan ) had hired and he was good. But don’t be fooled. The helpers  are going to lend a hand , give you a shove here and there. But at the end of it all, you are the one who has to take each and every step.  They won’t be carrying you or pushing you up.  As you climb up , make sure you appreciate how hard it is, because the king was carried up the rock face in some sort of palanquin.  Yep , unbelievable but true ( according to our guide). Unfortunately for all of us , the palanquin services was suspended 2500 years ago. Alas  there are also no cable cars, chair lift or lifts . Enjoy your visit . we did.

This experience should be way cooler than it is, but there's just sooo many people climbing to the top, it's hard to enjoy fully. I would recommend going first thing in the morning to avoid the crowds  - because they get pretty brutal as the day goes on.

I recommend to start the climb as early as possible. The top of the rock have no shelter and it is exhausting to climb during the mid day. Most importantly, when I come down at about 11am, I see long queue waiting to climb up. There are different sections on your way up, so you can always rest a while, drink some water before continue climbing.
Amazing castle on sigiriya lion rock with historical stories. Its better to start your journey earlire. If not you will feel tired with the hot climate.

We had a wonderful trip and walk up the rock. It takes some effort to reach the top (dunno how many stairs, but many. You will make it). The view we enjoyed up there was totally worth it! Wow, that is really something special. And the whole Story of this rock is so fascinating ans shocking at the same time! Visit this place. TWO ESSENTIAL TIPS My first tip, go there right when the park opens. Then you are already on the way up, when the first bus tours arrive and you can enjoy your trip. We did that and on our way down all the people were standing in a big queue all the way up the rock! You dont want to stand in line right? Second, check your condition and fitness. If you are not good by food, in so far that you need help even walking normally, dont go up there. We saw some people, that were already struggling the first 100 steps.. cant be much fun and is dangerous.

Rest assured that there are steps and hand rails over at most parts of the climb.  Climb was manageable but will be better if we start the journey earlier where there will be less crowded. Surprising to discover that the hidden paths of the lion rock - was quite “wow”when some areas actually look like Manchu Picchu.  Overall definitely a plus for the Sri Lanka trip.

As other travellers have mentioned start early - 8.30 am is excellent to arrive prior to the tourist buses!  Take a private tour if you are able.  A lot of the gardens and paintings need to be explained.  Spiral staircase looks difficult - to the paintings - but isn't!  Views are incredible.  Watch where you are walking and all will be fine!  Take your time and you will make it to the top!

As a family with teenagers it’s sometimes hard to keep everyone happy (especially when Mum likes historical temples) so this was a great solution. We arrived around 8am (as per the other reviews...it gets hot and busy so arrive early). I have a bad knee so was worried about the climb but wore walking shoes and this certainly helped. You sweat a lot so take lots of water and take your time. Yes it is worth it and yes you will be happy you did it. One thing I would not recommend is to take food up there. We thought breakfast looking at the view would be special but there are dogs on the top who would be happy to help eat your food so not what we had in mind. We then went to the lower level and a monkey stole my sons sandwich and others were keen on trying to grab the rest. Anyway - go early...with water...and enjoy the view!

We were warned it would be better to get up at the crack of dawn to go on a trip to climb the rock but on our 3rd day of excursions we decided to wait a bit and got there about 10am on a Friday..... so did everyone else though. A sea of school children swarmed over the paths, it seemed every school in Sri Lanka had emptied to visit that same day. The walk towards the rock through the gardens is lovely and peaceful and we would of spent more time there if our guide wasn't pushing us on. Once we were at the start of the steps the queues were pretty impressive and we were doing 5 steps, stop 5 min, 5 steps more. In the heat with packed bodies and not the most stable of legs the higher you got it made for a bit of an unnerving experience. The pace did make it much less of a physical feat however. The detour to see the paintings is well worth a look, understandably no photos and being so busy you were kept moving single file. The caged spiral stair cases up and down to that point were a bit rickety but with no children a bit calmer. At the feet of the lion rock before the final assent you can rest and watch the monkeys dashing about in the trees, there is some shade and with no food stands the place to break out a picnic. The last climb is a bit scary as even for me at 5ft the hand rails are very low and the odd shaking anxiety attack climber you pass on the way doesn't do much to strengthen your resolve. At the top there is little shade but the views amazing, make sure it's a clear day and you can see for miles and to many mauve Buddha statues dotted among the landscape. The decent is much quicker and easier, with compulsory gift shop huts on the way to the car park. Well worth a visit if you enjoy a challenging walk and a bit of nature. Sturdy but not heavy shoes and I don't think appropriate for children that might want carrying. Those saying it's expensive I think need to appreciate that the tourist money is what is funding it's conservation. Is a beautiful area of Sri Lanka.

Extremely humid when I climbed, however, the view made up for it.  Climb is not as daunting as it appears from the bottom and you are able to go at your own pace.  Take plenty of water with you.  Be aware that you will come across monkeys and dogs.  Make sure you bring the mozzie repellent.  Walk up to the start of the climb is just as amazing.   Take your time.  Round trip climb should take between 1.5 - 2 hours.  There are some traders at the car park on your exit that will sell food, drink and souvenirs.

A stunning and interesting historical site which was completely spoilt for us by incredibly in your face people forcibly helping you when you don’t want it.  Repeating the word no countless times had no effect.  Having broken my foot last year admittedly I was being careful but I had the very obvious assistance of my partner.  Partly because of this harassment I decided fairly early on that the climb was not for me so I decided to sit and wait while my partner completed the climb.  I was then followed until I had no option but to retreat to the haven of the coach that we arrived in.  My partner did complete the climb and enjoyed the history and the views.
Worth reading about or getting a guide to talk you through the history. Really enjoyed the garden walk. What a beautiful spot.

We loved our visit and climb up the thousand plus stairs. Cracking views and interesting history. Kids (4,6- girls) both managed with the assistance of some candy bribes. Stairs are quite steep and scary. Completely worth it.

The Sigiriya damsel paintings and the views from the very top are well worth the steep hike. The walk up is actually not too bad until the very last part from the lion's paw platform to the summit. Our four-year-old did it without much help. There are a few viewing areas to stop off at, and the steps level out once or twice. However, if you have a fear of heights, as I do, you will definitely need to steel yourself for the steps up to the Sigiriya damsels and the final set of stairs. The Sigiriya damsels are reached by a circular metal staircase that stretches up the side of the rock. Once you are there, you are on a metal platform jutting out from the side of the rock itself; it has a short railing wall. The damsel paintings are very well-preserved, and worth the extra climb. The final set of stairs was the worst part for me, as you are on a very narrow set of steep stairs bolted to the mountain. We were lucky to be there early, so I could climb at my own pace and not have to worry about passing people on the way up. We reached the summit before 9 am, about 40-45 minutes or so after we started. When we came back down, things were much more crowded, with people standing in line on the stairs to go up. Again, if you fear heights, getting stopped out on this set of very steep, very exposed stairs on the side of a mountain might really bother you. The view is very worth it, though the ruins themselves at the top are nothing to write home about. We found the caves lower down, just above the gardens, to be more interesting. A good guidebook or guide will give you information on the various little chambers and ruins of palace buildings located there. It is not well-signed, but it is fun to wander around and see what you stumble on as you walk through the old terraced gardens.
Really great for the whole family. Take water bottles and fruits for the rest 3/4 of the way up. Make sure you have a good breakfast and wear comfy shoes.
Best time ever, apart from the the heat. Was very hot 🔥 but amazing. Climbed the Rock all the way up to the top. Worth a try and the surrounding was simply pretty and beautiful.
We climbed the rock in the early morning.   I am glad we did.  That said it's surroundings and the stories behind the rock are equally as interesting.

We went first thing in the morning, before breakfast, to beat the heat along with the crowds of bus tours.  We climbed the rock which was stunnin, however. The rock itself and the grounds around it are equally impressive. Along with the stories about the rock.   Walking to the top is not essential.

We arrived around 10am, and it was already packed, so I’d recommend going for sunrise. This would also be smart because it was so dang hot when we went. There were loads of people but it was still ok. There were a bunch of school groups too that held up the walking paths. I’m afraid of heights but I managed ok for this. There’s a mix of stone stairs and steel stairs. The rock is incredible, loaded with history. Worth the hike up. The views from the top are amazing and the top of the rock has a lot of history involved too. Wouldn’t recommend getting a guide as they just add to your costs. There’s a museum you can do at the beginning which will tell u everything, and there’s also google, where you can research! Fun fact: there’s no toilets after the museum, so go then, and take tissues/toilet paper with you. Take lots of water, wear a hat, loads of sunscreen, and wear sunglasses. There isn’t too much shade up the top, and sometimes not much of a breeze.

Try to get here as early as possible. 7am would be good. Temperature can get extremely high and if you get here by 7am, you could be out of the heat by 9.15. There are only 3 trees on the top for shade. After 9am, lots more people arrive. If you want to avoid standing on suspended steel stairways with people in front and behind you, go early! If you suffer from heights, may not be your cup of tea. Coming down is easier than going up as the down stairs come down a different and it feels like an easier route.

great place to visit but avoid climbing if you are afraid of height because the view during the hike can make you dizzy. Well worth visiting while in Sri Lanka. Best to go in the morning, before the crowds!

We climb up here in the late afternoon - a good choice not too many people as all the buses had left for the day.   A bit of a climb for us older citizens but was actually easier that I expected and although narrow it  was very well maintained.  The views for the top were amazing - evening is a good time to go. Using one's imagination it is not difficult to imagine what an amazing place this was at the height of the civilisation.  We did not have any of the issues mentioned by other reviewers eg being hassled, however that may be because of the way we handle it  - around the world this is not an unusual experience.   Would thoroughly recommend this experience unless you are really scared of heights but if possible make the climb.

$30 entrance allows you to walk up hundreds of steps to the top of a rock without any signs.  On the way up my spouse was man-handled by 2 men grabbing her upper arms against her repeated protests. In addition, you will be told you cannot photograph (even without flash) some wall paintings.  My response to this was "for $30 I can enter any major museum in the world and be allowed to take photographs".  At the top there are no signs of where to exit. Save your time, effort, enjoyment, money for other wonderful Sri Lankan sites.  A total Sri Lankan Government rip-off.

Thankfully we set off early as it was so hot and humid. It is not an overly difficult climb but in parts has very steep steps and it's just the heat that gets you. A fascinating history and the expansive view from the top was wonderful. Wall paintings very complete which was surprising. Good there are many levels to take a breather if needed, so if you choose not to climb to the top you can wait for your companions. Amazing to think they built this in such a difficult location complete with a swimming pool. Good to see so many school children visiting this incredible place. Happy to recommend and a must do whilst in Sri Lanka.

it is worth it once if you have a few dollars and time to spare. On the road to Sigriya from Dambulla look out on the left for the board saying 'entrance for foreigners only'. It will take you Entrance cost is USD 30. The climb is very much doable by even a not so fit person. Pick up the site map with numbered landmarks from the information centre near the ticket booth and read the numbered plaques at the site; you will not need a guide. The top is literally ruins or hardly any ruins left, but the view is breathtaking. A great photo opportunity. Be prepared for the heat and queues. To beat both, it is better to do in the early part of the morning. Carry enough water. The museum is like a children's school project, a waste of time. Public conveniences are few and poorly maintained.

Fascinating place steeped in history and an amazing site that just leaves you wondering how on earth they built it and then lived there successfully. We went about 10.00 am and it was a particularly hot (38 degrees) and humid day so we were soaked in sweat as it is quite a climb in such heat. Knowing what I now know, and if I could have added an extra day on to the holiday, I would have split the transfer from Kandy (2 and half hours drive) and visiting the site by organising an overnight stay in either Sigiriya or Dambulla so that we could have climbed at 7 am. We did this earlier time for World's End hike and the temperature earlier is a far nicer experience. If like us though you don't have enough days to split the travel and climb, go for it, the enjoyment outweighs the sweat. One of the more expensive entrances for Sri Lanka but still only 4650 rupees each (£22) and well worth it.

Go early morning as it gets very hot and difficult to climb. Not for young children or those with walking difficulty  very steep steps and loads of them. The views at the top are well worth it. Simply stunning

Wife & 2 kids 10 & 8 commenced the climb at 8.40am & reached the top at 9.10am. There were a few people but never in a queue. It was shaded until 3/4 of the way up but pretty hot. Its not a really tough climb but you do get a sweat up. Yes it is quite pricey but we knew that before we went and glad we did it. The views are absolutely stunning, the history behind it is interesting and just experiencing it was fulfilling. You cant visit Sri Lanka & not visit this place. Highly recommended.

The ancient kingdom of Sigiriya is amazing! Its a UNESCO world heritage site and well worth the visit. Our resort in Habarana organised the trip and recommended we travel in the early morning. It opens at 7am. We travelled by tuk tuk. Some of the climb is single file and it gets hot so try and beat the tour buses. It is a big challenge for those of us who are scared of heights and there some unscrupulous locals who target you. We were approached by a man at lions rock entry (apparently they target anyone not in a tour group with a guide). He flashed a badge saying he was an official but we now know it was fake. He wouldn't leave our side even when we reached the top. We gave him a tip equivalent to $10 Australian which he said wasn't enough. He then demanded more money and in Australian currency. I really don't want to be saying anything negative but people need to be warned. The problem is that locals rightly pay a token fee to get in making it an easy scam for some. Please don't let this warning put you off going to what is otherwise a magnificent site.

Sigiriya is definitely worth the climb but just make sure you go early! There's only one way up, and down, for most parts so steps can get very busy; we timed it so that it was just starting to fill up - a bit too much for our liking - on our descent. I'm scared of heights but was ok for the vast majority of the climb; the worst bit is climbing to the highest point at the end due to the gaps in the steps - don't look down!

We went on this walk in February. We started the walk at 3 p.m. The weather was pleasant about 25 celsius but it was overcast. I prefer the word 'walk' rather than a 'climb' to describe this challenge but of course the walk is elevated. So long as you  are not someone short of breadth or very obese it is very doable if you take your time. Comment has been made on this site about the value of starting the climb early in the day. Well 3-00 p.m. is not early. It was never too hot, never too exhausting and I am 70 years old and someone who has had a heart attack but also someone quite fit for  my age. The disadvantage of starting the walk at 7-00 in the morning is having to get out of bed and perhaps delaying your breakfast until you have completed it. I like my bed. I like my breakfast. It may be that in the hot months an afternoon walk is too hot but in early February it was ok. There is another advantage to a mid-afternoon walk in that the descent it is less frenetic, with less people around. And the top is less crowded to and the stairs are less busy. My experience was that coming down was harder than going up if, like me, you are not keen on heights. Coming down is also quicker than going up because you reach the lower level sooner because the elevation is less severe. Our walk took about 3 hours from start to finish. This is partly explained by the fact we had a guide who shared his knowledge about the sites, history and heritage. We found his contribution added to our experience; not only did we learn a lot from him but his explanations, at different points, provided us with periods of resting. His reassurance that in February that the wasps/hornets would not be active as I am allergic to wasp stings. He knew what to do if the wasps were out and about was also reassuring The monkeys provided a little bit of amusement, that said if you have children and you give them something to eat discourage them from engaging with the monkeys when eating. I saw one little girl (aged 7/8) get a nasty scratch when monkey interpreted her interest in them as an invitation to share her snack. Be prepared for the view at the top being a little disappointing on overcast days. The best views for me were looking up at the citadel as you walk up. However I can imagine that on a clear day you will get great 360 degree views. There are some photographic challenges on this walk. Firstly carrying  a camera around your neck risks the lens hitting the iron work as you climb or descend. Not taking a camera will surely disappoint even more. The best picture I took was that of an indian rat snack which was over 2 metres long. These snakes are  not poisonous and it was in the grassy area when you approach the entrance. I did photograph the monkeys too. The iron work makes for memorable images but with a DSLR you need to have both hands free to get a decent photo which can be a challenge when you get higher up the face of the rock. There are also  better views of the citadel if you approach it from the road if your desire is to take a really great photo. It is amazing to ponder how on earth did people managed to build the palace at the top and how did they get the bricks etc up there. I have wondered how Stonehenge in the UK was erected. This place is probably just as remarkable. I would have liked to have more information on the site itself. I kept wondering was this citadel built by slaves or perhaps built by people in servitude. One wonders how the workforce managed to cultivate, prepare, serve and eat there food; and how  long did it take to complete the project? It is a very remarkable structure. Whether 70, 17 or 7 you do get a satisfaction from getting to the top. I enjoyed my walk very much despite my anxious concerns that I would not be able to make the full ascent because of my fear of heights or that I would be stung to death by hornets or attacked by monkeys. Neither happened and while not a gentle stroll it was a very rewarding and interesting walk. However for me it was not the best experience of my holiday as see elephants in the wild topped it. Hence the score of 4 stars.
Majestic experience! Once in a lifetime chance to experience the Lion Rock and to one of the greatest wonders of Sri Lanka and the World!

There is no place in the world like this, with its human history going back thousands of years and the sophistication of what they managed to achieve is incredible in comparison to most other societies in the world. You must experience it but do so early in the day or it gets too hot

We almost missed this as we were wary of the area because of the recent problems and we were glad we decided to climb the rock. Challenging because of the heat, we nonetheless made the climb and it was well worth the effort. Spectacular views and an interesting look at centuries old relics. That's the Good.... Now the Bad...the sour note was the entry price at $45USD per head. This is just ridiculous compared to the locals price of a few cents. Of course there should be a different price for locals compared to foreigners however a 4500% markup is not justifiable in my opinion. Also the museum is very ho-hum, so this is just about the rock and gardens below. Overall I am glad we did it...but too expensive.
A little over priced but worth doing once at least, Go early morning to miss the queues!
A little over priced but worth doing once at least, Go early morning to miss the queues!

Locals pay 50c, foreigners pay $40AUD. Can understand foreigners paying a little extra but can’t justify such an exorbitant mark up. $80 for two of us to go and see a rock which quite frankly was not worth it. Over crowded, touristy and without a guide you have no idea what’s going on or what it is you are seeing. Our driver told us that a couple of years ago they used to include a map and a CD in the entry price which explained what everything was. Very disappointing. My advice - Skip it and save your money for something more worthwhile. Sri Lanka (as beautiful as it is) is fast turning into a country that charges first world prices for third world service. Wish we had known this before we went up this rock!
Walked up with our two children (4 and 5 yrs). Started 7.30 in the morning. Bring lots of water! Amazing views and lovely surroundings.

If you plan to travel during March - April, bring plenty of water. Because it is very hot during those months. There are two ticket check points. One is at the entrance and the other one just before the Mirror wall and Frescoes, so make sure you have your ticket with you.

We had children (6 & 8) with us and decided to climb in the evening due to jet lag. We set off around 4pm. It was still very hot at the bottom but had cooled down plus there was a bit of a breeze by the time we got up. Kids managed fine, but are used to doing quite a lot of walking. Would have felt a bit nervous with much younger kids on some of the metal staircases, but ours felt big enough. We got down a bit before 6, but didn’t spend ages wandering in the gardens on the way. Bring plenty of water, but beware of snacks with lots of monkeys.

Once you have battled through the queues at the ticket office (for some reason located in the museum - not so for the locals whose office is before this one) you have to part with $30 (adult) $15 (6-12yrs). This is ridiculous, considering Pidurangala Rock (opposite) is only $4 (and much better in my opinion - less crowds, and you actually get to see the rock from a distance). Bearing in mind this climb is only 100m ascent, we saw people fainting, vertigo, dizziness, crying etc. It was hot, but my 4yr old son walked up the steps fine. Mirror wall was not so impressive and the frescos nice but fairly faint/worn/defaced etc. There is nothing of note on the summit, baring the views and packs of mangey/starved dogs (plus tourists nestled under trees for shade). Upon the descent we saw Cobra rock which was good and a few other rock caves and then through the line of street sellers and gift shops to the exit. I would honestly save your money and climb Pidurangala Rock for sunset. It’s beautiful and no crowds.

My partner and I climbed the Rock at about 9.00am and that was too late. You really want to start as early as possible because the heat is insane. There were a lot of people as we were going up so we did have to stop a lot. It is quite expensive at $50usd but the view from the top did make it worthwhile.

Came here with my husband. To be honest, I hate heights so be prepared for a large amount of walking uphill on an edge of the rocks. - Wear comfortable walking shoes with good grip. - it is tough walking in the sun so go early in the morning - We got there around 8am and were back down by 10.30am. - be prepared to get very hot and sweaty. Cover your head from the sun. Take plenty of water. - if you're scared of heights, it is still do-able. I hate heights but managed to avoid looking down. Some of the steps are original rock, so are a bit uneven so take your time. Some of the steps were steel, and there were railings. But on some staircases there's people going up and down on the same staircase which I found to be a bit scary. - if you're not particularly fit your leg muscles will ache for a few days afterwards, so book yourself for a massage ! - when you know the history behind the rock then it does make it interesting

A must see. Incredible part of Sri Lanka. Early morning is the best time to visit before the mid day sun.  Expect a bit of waiting at various stages due to the volume of visitors. Ensure that you wear comfortable shoes and ones that have grip as some steps are worn in places and can be slippery.  Take plenty of water as there isnt any place to purchase inside the site. Fabulous views when you reach the top. A great sense of achievement after climbing to the top only 2 weeks after knee surgery - walking stick in hand!
This is a worth the pain and strain of the climb up hundreds of steps. Take plenty of water and wear good shoes.

A group of us visited Sigiriya The site of the Palace of 'God King' who created this rock citadel and painted his damsels on the rock surface that was the highlight for many scripts on the mirror wall.Started the climb soon after breakfast to avoid  tourist traffic and the sun.The sunset would be the best time for great photos and sun rise from Pidurangala . the unesco site charges a fair price as an entrance fee.The working fountains become spectacular during the rainy season but the climb becomes challenging.To explore the kingdom it takes many hours.To climb and comdown three hours is ample for the not so fit.There are lots of caves,entrances,gardens to see before you enter the Lion paw stair case to see the Frescoes and read the mirror wall scripts.The climb to the top can be a challenge but worth all the effort.to see the spectacular scenery.

Our trip was ruined by the state we found two adult dogs and 5 puppies in at the top. 30 dollars per person and the idiots that run this place can't afford to have these poor dogs removed and taken care of. The puppies have a severe skin problem and are starving to deaf. If you are reading this post and love animals please take dog food and water to help these poor animals. If your are reading this and work for the site get your act together and put some of the the massive amounts of money you are earning towards helping the animals. Review of the actual place.... overcrowded and understaffed. Young people jumping the long que causing problems and no one to stop them. Great views from the top but unfortunately our trip was ruined by the crowds, dieing dogs and a poor baby monkey dead next to path for everyone to see. Once again please take food and water for the dogs at the top Thank you

We went here late morning which was probably too late for the heat of the day. It was a tough walk up the steps but worthwhile to see the views and reflect on how this could have been built so long ago on such a grand scale. Interesting grounds and gardens too. Not cheap to get in but this seems to be approach of government  to make money from tourists.
Expensive and crowded but worth the trouble. Once you are on top it is truly fascinating. Can’t understand why the kings quit using it as a castle retreat and let it go to seed.

The garden around is great, the rock is huge and everyone must go and make a trip there. It is quite expensive attraction in Sri Lanka I would say but not that expensive for what you see and experienced. I loved it.

Yes, it’s the most visited attraction in SL. Yes, it’s worth a visit. However, if you have no other choice then getting there in the middle of the day, be prepared to sweat your life off and wait in line for several minutes in some corner. On the way down, once on the ground level, go to the far left side of the track and you’ll discover some hidden paths less busier (it does lead you to the parking lot).
Entrance cost USD30, but view is nice and worth. Better go early morning or later afternoon, before 7pm closure, otherwise too crowded, especially under hot sun
First class location and interesting thing to do. Good climb but very busy and full of slower moving people. Worth the effort to see one of Sri Lanka’s major cultural sites. You must do it.
The site is really a site where is almost nothing left but the wall footing,but the rock is still a great rock.

Amazing view from the top. The walk/climb not as bad as I thought, except for the last part which is not for the faint hearted. Very persistent tour guides - our chauffeur warned us about them and glad he did.

This is one of my favourite climbs we did! Would definitly recomend doing this earlier in the morning. We started the climb about 8:30 and was at the top by 9:30. There is no shade, so you will feel the full heat of the sun, which is why it's not great to do this early afternoon. It is not a particular hard climb, there is just lots of stairs to go up, so just take your time. The view from the top is amazing. There is also a little museum on site, which is included in your entry fee. Don't miss this as is has amazing photos of the rock over the years. This was a very enjoyable experience!

This is one of my favourite climbs we did! Would definitly recomend doing this earlier in the morning. We started the climb about 8:30 and was at the top by 9:30. There is no shade, so you will feel the full heat of the sun, which is why it's not great to do this early afternoon. It is not a particular hard climb, there is just lots of stairs to go up, so just take your time. The view from the top is amazing. There is also a little museum on site, which is included in your entry fee. Don't miss this as is has amazing photos of the rock over the years. This was a very enjoyable experience!
A steep climb up 1200 steps in the heat, but great views from the top. $30 each to enter, which is a lot for Sri Lanka, but woth it unless on the tightest of budgets.

Sigiriya rock can be seen for miles but the beauty of the gardens and the exquisite archetecture warrant a visit. You need about 2 - 3 hours to do this site justice and a guide is invaluable in describing the various artefacts. Although quite a climb to the top, this can be done in stages and the paths / steps are good. Once the top is reached the full extent of the citadel is evident and the views are fantastic. The lion feet at the base of the final climb are well preserved and the paintings in the rock are still impressive. Sunglasses, hat and water are essential equipment.

Go early morning to beat the crowds and the heat. Lots of steps but there are places to take a rest. Enjoy fabulous views from the top and marvel at the skills needed to build this fortress. Very impressed with the wall paintings.

The museum and rock are well worth a visit. This ancient site is home to some interesting history and a good story to tell. The climb is simple and easy to follow (1600 steps - 660ft). We saw all ages completing it. Best time is early morning, it gets very busy around 10-11 o'clock. It think the photos I've taken speak for themselves. The monkeys were my highlight! People will offer guides for around $20 but we found it perfectly fine reading the pamphlet and going at our own pace (total 3hours with time at the top to take it all in).

We ventured up the rock at 3.30pm yesterday afternoon. I will admit I took a little bit of coaxing as we’d been sat in a car for 4 hours. I was worried that we wouldn’t have enough time to explore and make it up the rock before dark. My worries were unfounded. We had time to first explore the beautiful gardens and then make our way steadily to the top of the rock. We were lucky as it seemed to be relatively quiet at the time we visited so we could make regular stops on the way up. I am quite unfit and carrying plenty of extra weight. At time I was very warm and short of breath but nothing a sip of water and a quick break couldn’t fix! The views from the top are so breathtaking I feel very privileged to have been able to see them and I will remember them always. Sri Lanka is such a beautiful country and walking the steps to the top of this rock offers such a great view point. We are lucky enough to have a driver/guide so he fills us in on the history which is just amazing and so interesting. If you are still undecided on whether to climb we definitely say GO!

We visited Sigiriya Lion Rock as part of our 7 day tour and its a very impressive World Heritage Site. We had a guide to take us to the top and back who had done the climb thousands of times and was very knowledgeable. There are beautiful views both leading up to the rock, the climb and from the top. There are 1202 steps to the very top and some are quite steep so you might struggle if you have any mobility problems. There is also a spiral staircase against the rock face about half way up, which you can climb to see the wall paintings or you can bypass it if you're afraid of heights. We started fairly early before it got too busy and too hot! Make sure you take plenty of water to keep you going. On the way down you might come across a snake charmer which you can take pictures of if you give him some money, you can also have a python around your neck for a fee.

This rock features on most of the tourist brochures for Sri Lanka. The climb is not particularly difficult, but is very hot and slow, because of the numbers wishing to climb. The views are spectacular, and worth the climb

Climbed this rock after much hesitation after reading blogs and reviews to save the money and climb the rock next to it instead which you can see the view of beautiful Lion Rock from top of. Tourist trap - way too crowded. Views nowhere as good as Pidurangula.

This is the best attraction in Sri Lanka according to me. Best stay in the Dambulla City and take the bus to Sigiriya. Easily accessible. Amazing view and one of the best ruins I've seen. It can get hot during the afternoons, so best do it in morning. Also helps beat the ever-growing crowd. If you're from a SAARC nation then you get a 50% discount on the entry ticket. So please carry your passport.

It was luckily a cooler day when we climbed and it was still a hot and hard climb. The views from the top are stunning so well worth the climb. You do need to be steady on your feet and reasonably fit. Museum is interesting and grounds pretty.Go early if you can to avoid crowds.

I did this a couple of days ago and 100% recommend everyone to do it as long as you are physically able! I stayed at a local homestay so that I could get there early and beat the crowds. I was there before 8am and even then there were quite a few people around but when I was walking down around 10am the queues were crazy! I walked around the gardens and museum at the end which were quiet at this time so I enjoyed with some peace. Just some warning, at the beginning the steps are uneven and there are no railings - from previous posts I thought this would only be for maybe the first 1/4 of the steps up but it was more like 3/4 up. Next comes the frescos and then the lions feet, and then the final climb to the summit. Only at the frescos does the metal staircase start. So please don't underestimate the steps if you are unsure if you can do them or not. Sturdy shoes / trainers are a must too!
The first visit we did! It was awesome! Very exciting climb, not too difficult but you might wanna take it slow if you are not used to. The view is breathtaking

One of the stops on the tour of Sri Lanka, very pretty as you walk up to rock and very impressive , it is a very hard walk with lots of steps and loads of people , but the views are worth it , as it was included in our tour l did not realise how expensive it was to get in But you have travelled to Sri Lanka to see this places , beware of boys helping you up the steps they will pounce on you if they see you struggling so beware

Went with our guide in the lower parts and he told us the background and history. The climb we did ourself, we arrived quite early around 9AM and already a lot of people in area. When approaching the rock there where some local guides asking if we needed a guide, we said no and looked bored so they lost interest in us it worked and the the climb started. Finally at the top the view was really spectacular, really worth it. So my tip is to go early to beat the crowds!

This is an 182 meter high mountain as King Kassyapa built a castle on. This is a great trip, 1200 steps. Bring along some water, it's hot, and you need some to cool down. The tickets are a little expensive, buts worth it. My grandson is five year old, and he walked up all by himself. Let the children choose the tempo. A lovely view on the top.

My husband managed to climb up most of the way but was defeated by dozens of school children charging down. I was deterred by the climb itself and the hundreds of tourists pushing upwards. Apparently there were nice paintings of heavenly maidens and the rock itself was impressive but somewhat crumbly. I don't think I missed that much as I saw the rock from the road anyway!

This is well worth the visit, if you have a residency visa for Lanka make sure you take your passport as your pay local fees, visitors from overseas pay substantially more. Take a guide as there is a considerable amount of information that you will miss if you do not take one. The climb is not really challenging however might not be a good idea to do it with bad knees as there are a lot of steps involved. Scenery is truly amazing and in its day this place would have been a serious bachelor pad !!

Lion Rock is a good place to visit for a few hours.  easy hike up the top.  What is annoying is the local kept bothering us that they want to help us up the hike and ask for money.  We told them we don't need help but they kept following us and try to hold our warms etc.  When my husband told them to leave us alone, they started to swearing at us.  was quite annoying and scary.  This really ruin our experience with this place

Amazing view from this site, incredible to think how they built structures around this rock.  Had a great guide who told us the story of this heritage site, so much to learn.  Not the easiest to do especially if you suffer from heights/vertigo 😳 definitely worth visiting & climbing the 1200 steps.

The walk  up to the top is an ordeal but  one worth making. Although we climbed during a rain storm all the way to the top it was still worth the effort. Not  just  the  view when you get to the top but the different views  you get as you ascend this  fantastic monument. Very odd seeing a sign telling you to "Be Quiet" because of a  hornets nest on a near by tree.Ignore all those at the  bottom offering to help you climb as they expect a nice  bung for the effort and you do  not need them. Try to get information about the history of the rock because it is fascinating.Toilets in the ticket office are a disgrace, but would recommend the effort involved getting to the top..

well... you have to clime 1200 steps before you take the way of return... its not easy but its not extrimly difficult. You have to do it. The girls of sigirija and the view from the top of the rock worth it...

Loved my visit to the rock early in the morning. Try and get there before 7am for the climb to beat the crowds and the heat. It is quite spectacular, however the climb is not for the faint-hearted. It is a beautiful setting for the 5th century king and his 500 concubines with well-established water gardens if you are reluctant to make the climb to the top. You may wish to go as far as the Wall of Mirrors. The climb is well worth the effort. One of the highlights of my visit to Sri Lanka.

Fantastic views! This consists of ALOT of steps and isn’t for the faint hearted. It costs 30USD and totally worth it- however I would strongly advise doing Pidurangala (500 r/s) as you get a great view of the rock itself! Lots of moneys and dogs in the area! We got so close as they linger on the stairs on the way up, they won’t bother you if you don’t annoy them! Tip: go early! We arrived at 06.45 and was already a small que of people, it opens at 7am and it took us 40 minutes to climb up! on our way back down around 8.30 there was a lot more people and monks coming up. It’s cooler in the morning too but take water!
Go early to beat the crowds. Lots of stairs with lots of people, but worth it. The museum was so so.

Entry is not cheap at 4650 rupees per person. As you would expect from a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is well-looked after and well-staffed.  There is a small museum near the entrance, which is probably worth a short visit.  There are also “foreigners-only” toilets in this part of the complex, which were just about ok and no more.  The gardens at the foot of the rock are quite peaceful and offer good photo opportunities.  The one-way route up to the summit takes you first to the frescoes and from there up a series of metal stairs to the top. Due to the number of visitors you are only ever walking as fast as the people in front, which can be a little frustrating.  At the top you can wander around the ruins at leisure and enjoy the views of the surrounding countryside (for a more relaxing/less crowded  experience of the same views Pidurangala is a much cheaper and better option).  A few information boards around the site would be helpful.  We went up and down, including visiting the museum, in about 2.5 hours.

Best visited in the early morning, this is a climb worth making.  The first part is the most strenuous up a number of flights of narrow steps.  The frescos are reached by an enclosed iron spiral staircase, with a separate one to come down.  The mirror wall leads to a terrace and from there the Lion Gate and an exterior iron staircase lead to the top.  For me, this was the easiest part of the climb.  Views from the top are stunning and the swimming pool is particularly impressive.  The route down is a mainly separate one and can be taken at a leisurely pace.

Stunning views, great historical interest and a sense of achievement sum up a visit to Sigiriya!  I would completely agree with other reviewers that early morning is the best time to visit.  The gardens are impressive but the rock itself is far more so, imagining what it would have looked like in 4-5AD.  The first part of the climb is up steep narrow steps. The frescos involve a climb up an enclosed spiral staircase and can be bypassed, although I would advise against, as they are worth the additional climb.  The mirror wall is interesting and the terrace provides a welcome rest point, before passing through the Lion Gate up the exterior iron steps to the top.  The architectural remains, the scale of the palace and the views make the effort worthwhile. Gift stalls before the exit are where you can try out your bartering skill!  Pay what things are worth to you!

While we did not make it to the top, the whole area and grandeur of the area has to be taken in and appreciated.  While I was willing to try the climb, other members of our group were not able to do so -- age is one factor and the heat another.  We walked around the grounds and viewed what we could.

We had a wonderful trip to various places in srilanka like...sigiriya, Kendy, Nuwara eliya, Habarana, Waskaduwa, Colombo etc.....we are really thankful to Mr Shanil who arranged our trip in very short duration of time with good luxury vehicle and wonderful driver cum guide Mr Ruchira.....srilanka is beautiful country with many good places for sightseeing and adventure sport's.

Can’t be in this area without this experience. Walked up in the morning, took us 25 minutes with a baby on the back. You should definitely do this early morning as there are less tourists and the sun is not so hot. Great view.
Not so worthy to spend $30, well maintained but views are just if you climb on any mountain, did not like the site

The views from the top are amazing and give a 360 view of the surroundings. Worth the walk and even if busy, people can spread at the top and it does not feel so busy. Spend almost an hour at the top looking around and at the pool and other ruins. Loved it

We climbed this as part of our tour of Sri Lanka. We had our own guide for the tour who pointed the problems with local men trying to appoint themselves as guides or reaching out pretending to help trying to instigate a touch so that can try to extract money. A firm no did the job as instructed. Why they let them there given you have gone through a checkpoint is not clear. Went early morning and it was busy but if you take your time and take water and listen to the guide we made it with minimum of fuss. View from the top are fantastic as it completely dominates the skyline. We took the small diversion to see the paintings, these can be by-passed if you just want to make it to the top
It felt like something out of the Jungle book. Was a great experience. Go wearing proper hiking shoes and take plenty of water
Its really hard to climb with those small foot steps stairs but its really worth when u reach the top of it. Breathtaking view
Great experience - also for kids aged 7 and 10. Great view and safe stairways. Wonderful view over the area

We had visit the Sigiriya Rock. Its a amazing place to visit. Tickets little expensive. taking a side guide is good. because we can have good education. the water garden we canot think how they build in 4-5th century. Highly Recommend this.

If you're there, you must go - for the history, for the beauty and uniqueness of the rock itself and for the sense of achievement. My advice - go when there is almost nobody there. We skipped the morning and the evening hike. We decided to go at 2pm - no queues at the ticket office. ANd yes, it was hot, but I believe it is so much hotter when you walk one step per minute (exaggeration) and expose yourself to the sun much longer. We walked the pace we felt comfortable with. There was almost nobody at the top. It was perfect and I'd definitely do that again :) Admission fee is 30 usd

Few things to keep in mind when you plan to visit this heritage site. 1. you can hire a guide for Srilankan Rs 2000. it is worth it. 2. if you are Indian, carry your passports and you will have to pay only half of the entry fees ($15 against $30 for other foreigners) 3. The site opens at 7am. it's better to go early in the morning.. The weather is nice and climb may be easier 4. it is a steep climb. I saw many people getting back from the first level. 5. The view once you reach on top is worth every drop of sweat and every muscle pain. 6. Carry a small bag which ideally should have water, light snacks, energy bar, goggles and a cap. 7. once you reach on top, enjoy the greenery around. The cool breeze adds to the ambiance and you almost forget that you have to get down. 8. Be steady when you get down...seemed more risky than getting up. 9. Be calm, climb the rock and add a tick to the list

After climbing Bhutan's Tiger Nest, this should be a piece of cake. But we were wrong, it does have its own challenges that we need to deal with. DO NOTE THERE IS AN ENTRANCE FEE. The initial climbs was fairly easy only to be ruined by Touts who "volunteer" to assist you on the climbs and insisting on a fee thereafter. So if anyone want to help you but holding on your waist or pushing you from behind, best to tell the person to stop immediately. After 1/3 point, one have to go up on a Spiral staircase with amazing view, but due to the crowds, it could be quite claustrophobic, same with the hanging metal cage for tourists to view the wall murals. At halfway point, it flat out and there are rest area, one can choose to go further up by climbing more scary steps or just enjoy the view from here, We went all the way up and view is fantastic ! Coming down need to be slow and steady, there are just too many tourists ! Look out for the Foreigners Exit on your way down, there are many tourist shops which the pricing is higher than elsewhere.

Lion Rock is the home of an ancient palace, surrounded by visually-stimulating gardens and rock formations. The climb takes about 30min-1hr, depending on your health. I recommend going with a guide, as he brings the place to life with stories, facts and passion. Absolutely stunning views up top! A must-see if in Sri Lanka.

We didn't like the idea of all the steps to the top and wondered if it was worth going without going up there.  It was!  The gardens are lovely and have plenty of ruins to explore and there's a great view of the huge rock itself.  You can only see the frescoes by going up all the steps - but we decided the frescoes at Dambulla caves made up for not seeing the Sigiriya ones (and were easier to get to!).

We arrived at the site at 0900 and it was already very busy.  Most people seem to visit the site between 0800-1000.  The hike to the top is via steps and these get narrower as you climb, including a spiral staircase at one point.  The width of the steps means that, for the most part, you are in single file and moving at the pace of the slowest person.  When climbing up in the morning, you are in the shade but take plenty of water.  The view from the top is well worth the climb!
Beautiful village didn't climb the lions rock but admired it from below. Saw a wild elephant bathing in the river, a memory that will stay with me forever.
It's a long climb but the wonderful paintings on the way, interesting  ruins and views from the top make it all worth it.
Not only is the Rock an amazing climb,  the surrounding landscaped gardens are lovely. Even if you are unable to do the climb, it is worth a wander around the acres below.

One of the most beautiful places I have ever visited! The museum was fantastic, the cave paintings were breathtaking, and so was the view! So much history and beauty here. I don't want to give away too much, you must see it for yourself. Would happily recommend this place to anyone. Check the weather before you go. You will prefer to see this place on a day it that isn't pouring!

This was my first World heritage site in traveling life and It was amazing experience i never get. As my opinion this site can visit anyone but disables and too old peoples difficult to climb up the rock but they can visit museum which is in ground floor and get idea about the site. Since my first traveling to today the site has no any changes of historical value. Someone feel the ticket price is too high but compare with other countries sites prices are same but the value of site more than the ticket price. You can visit this place over 2 hours and many variety of ancient creations ( Frescoes , Moet, King palace, cobra hood cave, mirror wall and lion paws etc... ) can see. The special thing is great view summit of the rock. Most of peoples loving to experience sun set view at top of the rock , when you in top another special thing is you will see many sites around the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. At first seeing if you feel this site is not worthy to visit after getting the experience you will be satisfy.

A beautiful to visit the old kingdom fortress. It is definitely worth the anxuious climb to the top. Only way to the top is via their scaffold build pathway. That is why the king used to live there. Worth viewing the rock paintings on the way to the top.
I recommend going early in the morning because there will be lots of people and very crowded. The views were amazing and the top had many dogs and puppies that were super kind and fun to pet.

The view is nice, and the ruins also, but everything gets shadowed by the steps you have to climb. Mainly there are some concrete steps, that are really nice, and the ones that are in the shadows of the trees are usually visited by the monkeys. But at some points the stone/concrete steps are not there anymore, and you have to use some metal stairs that don't inspire too much stability (these are found mainly after the lion paws) At first you have to climb on some spiral metal stairs to get to the painted cave - the paintings there are really nice. After that you come back to the stone way. When we visited, earlier this March, it was very crowded, so the stairs seemed a little risky when they had so many visitors, but it all ended well, with some nice pictures!

This iconic rock is a must do for all travellers in Sri Lanka. Aim to start early morning to beat the crowds and the heat. There are steps to the top so it is manageable and safe. Beautiful views of the rock at the beginning and more beautiful views from the top.

Tough climb.. way too far.. but the more you go up the more you will feel the excitement.. nice concept of putting stairs alongside the rock. Too crowdy though and too hot as well. But a must visit heritage place.

The rock towers above the landscape and so getting to the top provides a great view. You buy the tickets at the ticket office and then have to walk to the entrance and then show the ticket to the booth there. I originally went to the entrance thinking I could buy a ticket there only to be directed back, not much of an issue, just something to be aware of. The garden grounds are nice enough and when I was there a couple were having their wedding photographs being taken. First there are some steeps steps, then some winding metal steps to the frescoes. Once you have seen the frescoes (not many there) you then descend winding metal steps parallel to the ones you ascended, which makes it look like the people coming down have already been to the top, but they haven't really you literally just go up the steps and come down. There has been some controversy in the past here, because there is actually a hornets nest somewhere near here, and in the past people have actually been severely stung. There are warnings on show. Then there is the walk along the mirror wall and then more steep steps to the lions paw. Here you can take a breather as in front of you, you see the final set of steps that will give you that sense of vertigo. If you are afraid of heights, this is the part that you will need to steel yourself for. Along the way up, the final set of stairs, you may come across locals who will help you and once at the top will try to stay with you throughout and act as a guide, though of course will expect payment. If you need help then use this service though just be wary of how much you give, you may think you are being nice by giving more but all that does is inflate their expectation for minimal service. I would not advise getting help from one of these people, if you think you will need help or want a guide then organise that yourself before ascending. Some of the stairs make clanging sounds but for the most part are sturdy and there rails all the way up. At the top the view is great and there is quite a bit to see. The descent is easy. I think it is definitely worth visiting for the great views.
Very nice, must see. Walking above from The foot of the Mountain to top, great Overview of the area. Great hike
I'd score this higher if it were accessible to all. It's a massive climb (1000+ steps) and worth it for those who can manage it. those who can't have some pleasant gardens in which to sit and wait

A nice place to visit, lovely views.Very expensive entrance by sri lanka standards though,almost 5000 rupees. We stayed for the sunset and it got pitch black quick, and no lights or staff to help guide you. We had a bit of an adventure to find our way home but it was fun. Something to keep in mind if you do stay for sunset though.

Sigiriya is a popular & significant tourist attraction in Sri Lanka & it is an UNESCO World Heritage site. However it lacks proper signage & information around the site. It is difficult to find the ticketing booth. Why is it tucked in inconvenient area? Also, the signage displaying the prices is confusing. It displays the prices in US$ but they take Sri Lankan rupees? Also, why is it not displaying  the entrance fees for SAARC countries? Unless you ask, you will not be told there is reduced fee for tourists from SAARC countries. It is half the cost of adult ticket (15 US$). You will need to show your passport to get the SAARC discount. You will also need to present your passport at the first checkpoint. The entry fee is ridiculously high for foreign visitor (US$ 30) & you do not even get a brochure or information guide to go with it! You are expected to do your Sigiriya homework beforehand or hire a guide starting from 1500 LKR. Since you do not get any leaflet or information guide, it is good to visit the museum to learn about the history of Sigiriya. Spend bit of time viewing the reproductions of the frescoes, you will not get to take pictures or spend a lot of time at the original frescoes. There are lot of things to look around before you start your rock climb. There are moat, water gardens & fountain gardens, which is worth spending time seeing it. It seems government has spend a lot of effort & resources into ticket checks rather than improve the signage & information guides. There are 3 checkpoints: museum, base of the rock & middle of the rock. The ticket checking process is slow & lengthy. Once you cross the fist checkpoint and start the climb, there is no exit until you reach the lions paw. Once you cross the second checkpoint, if you do not want to view the frescoes, on the right side of the stairs, there is a shortcut to bypass the spiral stairs. You will see few locals, guides waiting there to meet their clients after viewing the frescoes. You can take that shortcut & head straight to mirrored wall & then to lions paws. Once you reach the lions paw, you will see the exit on your left side. Follow this to head straight to the base of the climb, near the tourist car park exit. From the lions paw, you can continue the climb to the top of the rock to view the citadel. The view is amazing. Due to the length of the climb, take a hat for protection against the sun & water for hydration. I wish government did more with the information guides & signage for Sigiriya. It would help us to understand the history & culture better. There should be multiple exit points along the climb. If you are stuck in the climb queue, It makes it difficult to turn back. Combination of long queues, not being able to back out & lack to toilet facilities can make your climb miserable and unenjoyable. Government should abolish the mid rock checkpoint, I do not see the purpose of it, rather makes the queue move slowly. The checkpoint should move toward the base of the exit point., for people who would like to head straight to the lions paw & wants to bypass the frescoes & mirrored wall section. It would also be less strenuous for people who have difficulty. It might be also better option to have the ticket valid for two days, it will get tourists spend more time at the Sigiriya rock, understand the culture & history. It will also aid local tourism industry as tourist will spend more time in Sigiriya. If you like a bit of hike, similar views for fraction of the cost, I would go to Pidurangala Rock. Btw they do give out information brochures there!
It is a marvellous View from the top, and not to hot up there. Quite East to climb as there are god steps all the way. Can be smart to Go up there before it gett to hot during the day.
Pros: great views, well maintained and an enjoyable climb. Cons: stairs get steep so be cautious if you’re nervous with heights.

If you climb Lion Rock wear good shoes and be prepared for aching legs the next day. I wouldn't try it in rain as the stairs would be very slippy. We set off at 6am as it's too hot later in the day. It's a long haul to the top but the reward is a fabulous view of the surrounding jungle. There are ruins of a small kingdom on top of the rock built by a prince who killed his father and was afraid of retribution.

Even if you do not climb to the top (what is highly recommended, please make an effort, it is worth doing it) the whole site is very nice. Paintings in the cave near the top are very beautiful (no photos allowed). Old town is beautiful, make sure you walk all around once you reach the top.

Absolutely fantastic. I love history and heritage places, and this one rates very high on my worldwide list. It is pretty huge complex, and the main attraction is right on the top of the Sigiriya Rock, so keep on climbing these 1200 steps. Beautiful views from many points, and a ruins on the top are also impressive. Top attraction. Try to come as early as possible, to beat the heat and the crowd.

This is a must do visit. I have a prosthesis below my left knee but still managed to do it.  Be wary of the men who are waiting at the steps from ground level to the lions paws entrance. They say they are working there but in reality will expect tip from you of c.1000 rupees for 'assistance' on the way up and down. If you need assistance then you should be open about it and agree a fee beforehand to avoid a misunderstanding later. I had my walking stick and my partner with me and did not need any more. There are handrails in the upper section but not the lower part. Whatever you do - go early and take a small bottle of water with you. Its quite hard work but worth it.  There is a reason this a UNESCO world heritage site.

Ticket counter opens at 7 am. Go early morning or late afternoon. Entry ticket for foreign tourist is $30. For SAARC country citizens 50% discount, for that u need to present original passport (they DO NOT accept photocopy) We started at around 11am & reached the top after 1.30 hrs. There were more school children than tourists. We spent around an hour and started walking downwards. clicked many pics while climbing up. The view is beautiful from the top. Lion claws looks amazing. It's worth climbing the rock! First visit museum, there you will get all information & history about the rock. From Dambulla there are many buses available to Sigiriya. From Sigiriya to Dambulla last bus is at 5pm Don't forget to write your memory on mirror wall at museum!

This is a world famours site seeing to make a life visit to the great archaeological value of king Kasyapa giving it's view to make a remarkeble site to give it's nature to the fortress itself. Great highlight and atmosphere with a greater value yet it's a question how would be the fortress been built and the water supply. Great pleasure to view this heritage site. Had a nice expirience, Great hike, Cool Breeze and Life highlight if I suppose. Good to climb this by morning and to see the beauty it'll take a days delight. Never miss this place when you're at Sri Lanka

We would advise to start very early in the morning. We arrived at the site at 7.30 am to avoid the heat and it took us nearly an hour to climb but we took it easy. We did not return down until near 10 am to discover that there was now a huge queue of people waiting to ascend the steps.  We were so glad to have gone early as it would have taken twice as long to get up. It is a tough enough climb so not to be done in the heat of the day. Also wear very light clothes. We really enjoyed the view and it is amazing to think they could have had such a kingdom in such a place.

Our visit started by seeing that there is a separate ticket booth for “locals” and “foreigners” with the foreigners booth being located a further few hundred metres away from the entrance which was inconvenient. The fee for foreigners is exorbitant by local standards ($30US), this equates to 4650 Sri Lankan Rupees, which is a lot in Sri Lanka. It is sign written in US dollars only which is strange as this is not the local currency. The site seems to be used as a cash cow to extract money out of tourists. With the segregation of “foreigners” here being taken to the extreme. The site is well maintained but lacks signage. We found that doing the hike later in the day (circa 10am meant you could avoid some of the large early morning crowds). The sad part was seeing the poor dogs seemingly stranded on the top of the rock. Some seemed diseased and they were breeding with malnourished pups up there. For a world heritage site I would think they could at least look after the dogs if they are going to have them up there.

Went here as part of a tour. The ticket gets you into the surrounding gardens and access to go up the rock. If it’s a hot day make sure you take plenty of water. Gardens were lovely. The first climb up the stairs takes you to the fresco wall paintings of the ladies. These are in incredible condition. You do have to climb a spiral staircase. If you’re afraid of heights you would definitely find this challenging, although my wife managed it and she isn’t the best at spiral staircases! Once you have come back down from the fresco’s (yes you have to come back down the 50 odd stairs you just went up via another spiral staircase) you go past the mirror wall.  This is only meant to work when the sun is shining on it from a specific angle which we didn’t see. You then continue on up the rock and the climb takes you to the lions paws where you can stop for a break. You then have the final climb to the top. It’s worth noting that you do not have to do this final climb, you can just stop at the lion’s paws. The staircase did get quite crowded at times. The top was a lot bigger than I expected, lots of ruins and some great views. Well worth a visit.

OK this is a real trek and it is not for the faint hearted. It is along slog to the top and it took me (a semi fit 68 year old, 90 minutes to get to the top). Steps are relatively even and ther is a way up and way down sections when things get tight. There are also lots of “rest platforms” on the way up. Half way up at the “ mirror wall” level you  can take a spiral staircase up to see a cave with really nice original paintings ( worth the slight 40 step deviation) At the lions platform you climb thru the remains of a lion ( its paws are still there but the head is long gone) and start the last of the climb - 300 steps, up to the top. There you see the remains if the the upper palace. The views are stunning from the top - if it is not misty! There is a separate set of stairs for the way down ( in places). Note of caution- this site gets very very busy so go early to avoid the crowds. Be there for opening time - trust me when really we were coming down the crowds were awful and as such you get stuck behind the slowest person. We had no problems as we went early and were on the way down before the crowds hit!

Apart from the rock itself, there is quite a lot of other things to see in this site. You will need a reasonable level of fitness . On the way you’ll pass a series of quite remarkable rock drawings and a pair of colossal lion’s paws carved into the bedrock. The surrounding landscape, lillypad covered moats, water gardens and quiet shrines, where you can sit relax and contemplate in the quietness, peace and tranquility that is. The excellent site museum, only adds to the rock star appeal. A late afternoon hike to the top to see the stunningly beautiful sunset is worth the effort if you have the time.
