Not quite sure about the low rated reviews of a site like Sigirya as I am not sure what the reviewers were expecting, especially if they actually read the previous reviews or even a guide book explaining what the citadel was/is. Yes, there are a lot of steps to climb, but not as many as Adam's Peak. Yes, there are some very questionable staircases; but they have been there for years and are still solidly attached to the rock face. Yes, at busy times it is likely to be frustrating, but that is why timing your visit is important; we went in the afternoon and despite the fact that we thought it would be too hot to climb, we were pleasantly surprised as it seemed to us that the crowds had thinned out. We made it to the top late afternoon and descended just before sunset (as we were not too confident about descending the steps in the dark). What's at the top? A stunning view of the surrounding area, yes; but there are also the remains of a palace complex which leaves you to consider not only why it was built but also how they got the raw materials up there in the first place. It was easy to see why. Honestly, if climbing stairs is not your thing, then probably best not to visit, but if visiting historic sites is your ‘cup of tea’, with the added bonus of a fabulous view, then this is well worth the climb. Take it at your pace and you won’t regret it. I have also seen negative comments about the cost of entry for ’foreigners’. Unfortunately, this is a fact of life that tourists will be targeted and I would have to say that in most cases, quite rightly so. A lot of the sites us ‘foreigners’ want to visit are still ‘active’ temples/shrines and the locals still worship at them. Whilst, Sigirya does not have an ‘active temple’ at the top, you will find that it is us foreigners who want to trample all over the site; and in some cases disrespect the ‘no climbing’ signs. Therefore, if I have to pay more than the ’locals’ then so be it. I just wish that this policy was applied in my home country.

It is quite an impressive sight but very overpriced. Especially when you reach the top to see starving dogs. We gave them water because it was so hot and there was nothing around for them. Some looked like they were about to die, very upsetting. Surely with the amount everyone is paying they can afford to feed the dogs. The dogs at the bottom look fed and healthy, I'm not sure why the dogs are on the top and why they aren't being looked after. We spoke to someone when we got down so hopefully something will be done to help. If you go take some water and food up for them.

Enjoyed the view after a long climb to the top.  Visited by monks and locals too.  The guide made it easier to get there and buy our tickets and meet us at the guide parking lot.   Skipped the museum.  Interesting many dogs and puppies live on the top of the Lion Rock,  Monkeys too.  Big pond on top.  Don't lose your ticket or pay twice is what our guide told us.

We arrived here around midday and I believe that every school in Sri Lanka was having a school trip - literally hundreds and hundreds of children! Our guide managed to get them to move to one side to let us pass in some points which seemed to be what all the smaller tourist groups were doing.  The only good thing about it being so busy was it slowed us down so we weren't climbing continually as I think this would have been exhausting.  My husband doesn't like heights but he did make it to the first level (but bypassed the spiral staircase) and the only part he found difficult was the metal stairs immediately before the spiral stairs. I climbed to the top and didn't think the last section was too hard, and I do have a bad knee. There are several friendly but hungry dogs living on the top which was quite upsetting.  Take a little food for them as they do have puppies.  We were told by our guide that the gardeners look after them but there wasn't much evidence of this - they were quite desperate

Many people say this place is overrated and should be skipped, or maybe at best seen from another rock nearby. WRONG. As long as you get there before 09.00am, it's an amazing evidence of the past. The ruins on top are of course the main point, but don't forget to step off the main path every once in a while to see less popular parts of the gardens, caves and terraces. If you arrive too late, you'll end up in an enormous line, waiting to climb the rock in incredible heat and moist - no wonder people hate that. Don't take a guide, as they'll mainly try to push you through the main path as fast as possible and then get the next customer - all that for "only 5000 rupees". We haven't seen a single guide in any of the locations off the central route. Read about Sigiriya beforehand and then explore the area - you'll definitely need 3-4 hours for that

It's a bit of a climb to the top of the rock but once you reach the top, it's totally worth it! The view from there is stunning! We went in the evening and watched the sun set from the top which was beautiful.
Thesis a remarkable place and a must see.  But at all costs get there as it opens and avoid the crowds and queues which build up later.

This program need good knees, because you have to climb up to the 350 m high on steps. There is two place to see- one of them is in the cave - beautiful wall pantings- the mirror wall cannot be touch during the way- years ago people left sign on it but nowadays it is not allowed. Than on the other side of the rock you can climb up to the Citadel- it is heavy and if it’s raining maybe a little slippery too. But on the top you can see a wonderfull view- and a very interesting ruin of the citadel.

First of all, go early, at 7am when they open.  There were very few people when we went and when we were coming down a couple of hours later, the crowds going up were ridiculous. The climb itself isn't all that bad if you are in decent shape.  My wife and I are 59 and 62 and went up in 45 minutes.  We saw a guy with a broken foot and a lot of obese people get up there, too. The climb is great, good staircases and you see cool things on the way up, especially the cave with the Apsara paintings.  It was foggy when we went, but I imagine the views are incredible. Then you get to the gigantic Lion Paws and soon you are on top.  Explore the old castle, look at the views, and wonder how the heck they got this building materials up here.  The way down is quite easy, half of the climb down is along a different route then the one you went up.  Highly recommended!!

I know this is on everyone's must-do list but don't get too excited about the "ruins" you will see because apart from the beautiful paintings of the "ladies" halfway up and a large lion paw there is not much else apart from crumbling wall remains. It's all about the challenge and the view from the top. It is NOT an easy climb. Go as close to opening as possible to avoid the heat and the busloads of tourists. It's ridiculously expensive ( 30 US dollars)
Amazing site! There are some shortcut ways up to the top! Go as early as possible to avoid line! Museum offers great example of artwork and artifacts (which can not be photographed) Not to be missed

One of the world's great monuments never fails to impress. The scale of it absorbs the crowds but given the sheer scale of numbers of visitors it will soon be important to consider how to handle these at the frescoes and other tight points. Visitors should consider an early or late visit to avoid these issues.

Our travel company had us climbing the rock at 7. And that was excellent idea as you had a chance to look around and take time. Was amazed at size of fortress at the top! Cave paintings up spiral steps worth seeing and you can photograph excellent replicas in Museum after. Definitely something you have to do!

The climb up to the top of Sigiriya is not for the faint-hearted. 1200 steps, the lower ones up a winding path and the top section up a metal staircase. On the way you will see the remains of some enchanting cave paintings, sadly far fewer than there once were, of delicate and demure scantily-clad maidens bringing offerings of flowers to the Lord Buddha. This gives you a bit of a breather as well as being a beautiful experience in its own right. When you get to the top of the rock the remains of this ancient civilisation are breathtaking, as is the view. Allow about 50 minutes for the climb, slightly less to get back down, and a good hour at the top. Go early in the morning before the heat is too intense, and be prepared for an experience which wil blow your mind.

It is the best to go early in the morning, as it is a very popular site and the sun can be very strong and too hot for the hike later in the morning (or in the afternoon). Climbing up Lion Rock is very steep and can be bit scary for people who has fear of height, the view is amazing and you will have a beautiful panoramic view of the area. Please be careful when you go to the cave to see the cave painting (top of the spiral staircase). I was taking video of the view going up the spiral staircase with my phone, and stopped recording immediately when I saw the sign of "no picture/video" at the entrance of the cave. I didn't take any picture or video of the painting, however it was too late. The local people who were guarding the painting, they grabbed my phone away, putting it in one of the pocket and didn't return it for about 30 minutes. They told me they would call the police and I had to go to the police station, and pay the penalty. They were quite aggressive and rude. At the end I kept apologizing for taking a video (although I immediately stopped recording), I paid respect for their job and they were happy and returned my phone. (no penalty, no police, but they took my passport number) First of all, please avoid taking picture/video before entering the cave. And 2nd, please do not take out your phone or cameras in the cave, so you will not be in trouble like me :)

A beautiful and iconic place. We went at three in the afternoon and although a bit warm initially, it cooled down nicely as we climbed the rock Apparently this is a quieter time of day to visit Interesting site with some great archeology and brilliant views A must do sight in Sri Lanka

I would hate to have gone to Sri Lanka and not be able to say we visited & climbed Lion Rock. That said - go early to avoid the heat and crowds. Our driver picked us up at 6:30 and we were there at 7 am as soon as the gates opened (we were 3rd car in lot). It is not the hardest of hikes/climbs, but it is probably too much for some. We took our 23 month old with us in our back carrier and he did great. Coming back down the crowds were significantly greater - again, go early!!! We were back to our hotel by about 9:45, so the entire climb up and down probably took 90 minutes or so. Awesome experience and great views...a unique piece of Sri Lankan history indeed!

Great place and definitely worth a visit. Key points -$32 usd or 4600 rupee -GET THERE EARLY!!!! We arrived at 7.30 which was a good time with very little waiting. When coming down the rock there were huge lines of people waiting to go up. It would’ve taken over an hour at least for them to get up probably more.

Visited here as per many other tourists have done with our guide. Arrived about 11am and found it very busy so either go early or late. The queue was unbelievable and many Asian people just pushed in front of us all the time .Couldn’t understand that. Not polite at all . The steps up were easy enough as you couldn’t go fast anyhow. Climbing up the metal spiral staircase was good and there were monkeys all around. Having reached the top we looked around and it  was interesting with great views. Again very busy with tourists. Something not to be missed .

I was ready to back out as it looked pretty difficult from the base.The entry fee was $30us and if you have US$ it’s probably worth paying in that currency.The first few steps are quite difficult but it gets easier.We did the accent in 40 mins to the top stopping for drinks and photos.Dont get sidetracked at the spiral staircase that doesn’t take you to the top but takes you to paintings on the rock walls and you are not allowed to take photos.You then have to walk back down again to get back on the path.Once at the top you have great views and can see all the ruins of the fort that was once there.Really impressive and were very pleased we made it so easily.If you have fitness issues maybe wait at the bottom.We did see some Chinese tourists that obviously found it too hard and they stayed at the bottom.They were totally dressed inappropriately for the hike in platform shoes etc.One of the things in Sri Lankan that I would say is a must do.They recommend doing this in the morning and we were there at 12.45pm.I was very warm.Mornings would be better

We only had time for a fleeting visit to this site. The signposts need to be more detailed for those who visit without a guide. The complex is huge and high. There is a ticket office for Indian Nationals clearly marked but the one for foreigners  is shut, you have to discover the ticket office a couple of hundred yards away inside the museum.

Don't be put off by the reviews suggesting only the fit can make it to the top. Yes it's a fair walk and yes it can get hot during the day but there are a couple of things to consider. You don't need to walk it all at once, take breaks and enjoy the scenery along the way. Get early on and avoid the tours and the worst of the midday sun/ And like anywhere with this type of climate, take plenty of fluids. This isn't much I can cover that hasn't already been discussed on these reviews apart from, think about the bees. There was a section on the ticket we got saying if bees begin to swarm and the top of the rock is closed, there will be no refunds. I didn't think much of it until I was at the steps about to come down. It was then I noticed some people getting agitated and telling other people to be quiet. As I looked round there was a very large swarm of bees hovering over the centre of the rock. We made a swift exit, not knowing whether the attraction was closed after or not. If you can zoom in on the photo I've posted you will be able to see them. Something to be aware of - my advice would be to get there early both to avoid the heat but also better your chances of being able to get up without it being closed.
Steeped in history and intrigue. Its a bit of a climb to the top but the views are worth it. We'd recommend going early in the morning or later in the afternoon as it can get very hot.

A great place to visit. The Gardens as one enters the park are interesting and cool.  The climb is energetic but incredibly worthwhile to see the caves painting and the view from the top. The kings pool on the top of the rock is amazing

You need to be reasonably fit to climb upto the top which is about 2000 steps. Narrow and smooth steps don't help. 1st stop during the climb is a terrace garden which is full of fearless monkeys. Take a seat under a tree and enjoy them entertain you. 2nd stop is after almost 80% climb, full of lovely paintings. Though very few remain now, they are definitely worth the climb. We did not have the strength or inclination to climb the summit, but I am told the top has a beautiful garden and a huge reservoir which supplied water to the palaces down. A visit to dambulla cannot be complete without a visit to this rock fortress

This site has four platforms with plenty of steps. First platform has geometrical gardens, easily accessible to everybody. Second platform requires climbing couple of hundred steps in stairs, some quite steep. If you cannot climb six floors, this is not your place. If you can, you’ll see some nice rocks and craftsmanship. The best platform there. Third platform shows paintings. It requires climbing narrow staircase about 50 meters. If your BMI is over 30 or you are afraid of heights, this is not your place. You cannot take photos of paintings (two years in jail, if you do, so they say, and there are guards). Paintings are beautiful and fresh (must have been restored) but you can see them well in books. Then you come back to second platform and walk to the other end of the rock. There is lion’s mouth, and steps to the fourth platform. If you cannot run for three miles, don’t go. It’s the toughest climb there. Over the top it’s good view and few bricks but not much more. If you are in fit, you should do it. Be there at 7:30 am, or you'll queue for 2 hours.

Those who can't walk can stay down near garden while others can go up. View from down itself is satisfying. Going up is tedious job. Up the rock there is only remains & no palace or nothing. But the view was good. Take water bottles or even little snacks along. One thing is that foreigners please have your passport with you while entry, else you may end up paying more. Indian passport 15USD and for others 30USD.

The Sigiriya Rock is one of those things that you'd have to see to believe. Everything about the place is incredible: The architecture, the ecology, the stunning views from atop the mountain and mural paintings that don the rock face. If you have time to kill, do consider climbing the Pidurangala Rock too, the views of Sigiriya from atop the rock are incredible too. The only downside IMO is the horde of tourists that swarm the place; better to get there early, carry loads of water and douse yourself in sun-screen.

This monument is beautiful. The view from the top of the Lion Rock is amazing. The climbing of steps is a little bit tough for young childrens (our children, 4 and 6 years old, did it). You may see also a lot of monkeys, lezards, birds... Don't miss it!

We went to Sigiriya and was amazed by how beautiful it is. The climb itself is steep at times but incredible views each step of the way and not too difficult as you can pace it. The view is incredible and there is lots of space at the top to take it in. Enjoyed the trip down as well and everything is clear of where you need to go. Highly recommended. Would recommend stopping for food and drinks before as it’s expensive within.

This is expensive but an interesting landscape feature of Sri Lanka and if you are able, it's worth the climb for the views from the top. Be aware though that hand rails are in short supply on very uneven and steep tracks, which is why my husband couldn't face going all the way up. We were warned about locals there who offer to help and seem genuine but then they demand a high price at the end. My husband was fleeced of about £35 by such a man who told me he didn't  want money when I refused his help, giving me the impression when I went to climb higher that he was part of the staff. He was unpleasant when my husband offered about £10 initially for the little help he gave him and made him feel guilty. A pity I was not with him for I'm sure he wouldn't have tried that with two of us. There are monkeys and dogs of course and I was worried when tourists were going up to them quite closely to photograph. A scratch or bite from a these could leave you with rabies, a rush to hospital and a £400 injection to save your life. This happened recently to a young girl so our taxi guide reported - she died.

We had been advised to arrive early and that is my one piece of advice to you...For as we were descending the coach loads were starting and there were queues even at the bottom. However what an experience. My goodness, is it a climb! with some very thin, slippery walk ways along the rock and even a spiral staircase stuck to the outside. I certainly would not advise anyone with small children, or babes in arms to consider this and it might be challenging for the more senior amongst you, or those with mobility concerns. Half way up you enter the area with the Busty Beauties wall paintings. Whatever you do, do not think about getting a photo, do not even take the lens cap off for your camera will be confiscated as happened to the man in front of us. You can even be arrested!!!! But up you continue and at the top, although there is not a lot to see or do, you can mill about the ruins and take in the amazing views. I think it is more about doing the climb than what is up there to attract the crowds. A good half days' activity to get the heart pounding!

This is a must-go for anyone visiting Sigiriya, with its deep history and significance. The climb was not tough (generally ok for anyone with average fitness, even if you are older), however bring decent amounts of water. Do also arrive earlier in the morning as queues form rather quickly to climb the rock, and it gets hot later in the day. The view at the top is decent, but do climb the rock mainly for its significance and history.
A popular tourist attraction in Sri Lanka to witness the skills and the technology of the ancient pedigree. Very famous for paintings on the walls.

The climb to the top of Sigiriya Rock has over 1200 steps. A lot of those steps are uneven, so a little care is needed. But the views from on top are exceptional, and the history and the culture is amazing. Even if you decide not to do the climb, check out the water gardens. Guides are available, and I saw many assisting people who were battling to make it up the last 100 steps (best guess). I hope they tipped them well. But honestly, if you are in decent health, just take a guide book with you, you will get just as much out of the visit. Take $30 usd with you for your ticket. You can pay in LKR equivalent on the day, but there are no credit facilities. There is an ATM near the kiosk, about 100m further towards the rock from the ticketting. The ticketting is on the right as you walk in, at the Museum. Final hint is to arrive early, about 07.30am, and beat the line up at ticketing. Then head straight up the rock. You can wander around the gardens when you get back down. This way you beat the crowd climbing the rock, Buses start unloading about 08.15am.

This area is on the flat, before the very steep climb of the Lion Rock itself. The partly restored pathway takes you past the 4 huge water gardens - two of which are still in good condition. You feel as if you are getting a glimpse of life in the past and a different culture and way of life. Paths are uneven and you need reasonable shoes and a steady tread. If you venture to the sides of the main path there are caves that were inhabited and other structures and areas that most people seemed to ignore - lovely areas to wander through to get a feel for the history and peace of the site. Everywhere there was an army of locals sweeping the paths and grass of the dropped leaves from the previous day - it is very well looked after and well worth a visit.

This is well worth a visit, but you need to be fit to make it up the hundreds of steps to get to the top where the view is stunning. There are crowds here so come as early as possible - that way it will be cooler too. Bring water to drink [there is nowhere to buy it!]. You begin by walking through the ancient water gardens where you marvel at how these were laid out when the only way was to do it by hard physical labour. Be careful of your step - health and safety counts for nothing here! There are groups of monkeys all around and you need to be wary of eating or showing food - a lady near us began eating a banana when it was cleverly snatched from her by a large monkey - not doing her any harm, but giving her a shock. You then begin the climb around the base area. It gets steeper and steeper and there are no hand rails in many areas so you must be firm in your footing. A steel built ladder ascends the rock face - out in the sun, very steep and hundreds of steps. Well worth it when you get to the top and see where they used to live in the palace etc- cant imagine how they got up here - the views are amazing but there is no shelter from the sweltering sun - use good suntan protection. Then you have to descend - a different staircase for the most part. Very interesting.

Challenging climb, save your energy and don’t rush in the longish walk to base of rock. Worth spending 30mins in Museum first to see copies of the rock paintings and artefacts, so when you see the real thing you know what you’re looking at. The climb up is long so take breaks, and can be slightly hair raising in places but hold your nerve, it’s worth it!
This place should be visited while traveling in Sri Lanka. The climbing is not very easy and fast but it is a moment which should be experienced.
We climbed this rock early in the morning (7am) to avoid the crowds and it was really worth it. Although cloudy the day we visited the place is unbelievable

One of the main reasons to visit this area is to climb up the rock fortress and to visit the ancient water gardens.  Early is better as less people on the climb.  I suspect there's not really an absolutely best time, but since you must do it, you must just queue!  Big tip - take some medigloves for holding onto the handrails.  Many thousands of people on the climb, all holding on to the rail and not all the cleanest!! also, it's rusty and if you are unlucky enough for rain (we were) your hands get covered in orange rust - as do your clothes and everything else, so don't wear anything good!

This is a very popular place to visit so it can get crowded. There is only one way up but there is a second way down.  It also can be very hot.  Our guide suggested we get there when they opened for the morning to beat the heat and crowds.  That is the way to do it! We were able to get many photos during our climb and at the summit.  I don't like heights so there were a few places I hugged the rock but it's not bad because the stairs are sturdy.  Worth doing if you visit the site.
Beautiful and impressive lion's rock! Opens at 7 am and I recommend you get there early as from 9 am, crowds start to climb, leaving people one behind the others.

Sigiriya rock fortress is definitely a must visit place in Sri Lanka. Even though the entrance ticket was 30$ , it was worth visiting it. Climbing wasn’t hard at all, instead easier than many other mountains.
We got to the top and we're pleased to have done it. It is amazing to think that they managed to build and live on top of the rock. Not a lot left of their buildings but felt the need to do it.

I'd recommend reading and understanding the history of this amazing rock before you go as we didn't see any information while we were there and it really helped knowing why, what, and most importantly  how they built the fortress on the top! Not recommended if you don't like heights as the metal steps are a little rickety near the top. It is well worth the climb however for the view and to witness this feat of engineering / architecture.

This is an easy one. Allow plenty of time as there is more to this place than straight up the path, up the mountain and back. Go early, we arrived there at 8.30 to join a painful queue to buy a ticket ($30 each). Going up was a bit slow and there is one point just before you go up an enclosed staircase when we had to queue. On the way down the queue going up had got a lot longer, proving the point to go early. I was told to wear trousers which is complete rubbish. Completely a matter of choice but shorts would be fine.

The experience of climbing the rock was thrilling and incredible views from the top of the rock are worth the sweat. And sweat you will, as some parts of the climb may be quite demanding for the unprepared. Be sure to go in early morning if you want to avoid the heat and crowds upon crowds of tourists. Please be advised though that if you suffer from vertigo, you should probably skip this one or brace for serious personal challenge. Some parts of the climb are bound to make your knees weak.

The rock is imposing and beautiful. I can't emphasise enough how much you should GET THERE FOR 7.30AM! We were one of the first 20 people up there and it was a lovely and relaxed walk up. On the way down by about 9am, people were queuing, it was really busy and you don't want to be knocked about on those rickety stairs! It's a lot of steps but totally worth it. Would recommend to everyone going to Sri Lanka!

Quite a  breathtaking view and beautiful countryside with wild elephants.  We did not climb the rock but many did. Instead, we took a walk around the rock which was beautiful.  Most definitely should be on your visit list.

This extraordinary outcrop (with a ruined palace on top) is fascinating.  A visit begins with the Museum, and you then walk through the gardens to the base of the rock and begin to climb.  This is not for the faint-hearted, sufferers from Vertigo or folk with heart and lung problems; there are 1200 steps to the top.  About halfway up is a spiral staircase leading to the famous frescoes, and then you ascent again to a terrace about tw-thirds of the way up.  Thereafter it's up a set of iron steps bolted to the rock.  There are locals who will steady you (tip sensible). Even in the heat haze the view from the top is spectacular.  Of course you then have to come down again...

Spent a morning exploring the gardens before start the serious climb. First to view the ancient frescos and then onward and upward. Through the lions paws to start the climb to the top. The views are amazing and we lived learning about the history of the site. Although it's busy everyone was polite and you can take your time. It was mic to late morning when we went up the rock and it was a beautiful experience. Captured this view from our hotel pool when we returned.
A must-visit site to witness the grandeur of a civilization and the richness of the SriLankan jungle... from above! Totally worth it!

The first challenge of Sigiriya rock was getting here, we arrived in Kandy and started to look at options, reading trip advisor we soon realised this wasn’t going to be an easy trip by public transport, so we opted for a small private car which cost us about £35 for the day. The trip each way was about 3 hrs mainly due to traffic. When you arrive there are guides touting but once inside you really don’t need a guide as everything is clearly marked and laid out. Admission is steep, around £25 each, but we felt better about this when we learned it helps to pay for the infrastructure of many other services such as cheap public transport. You walk through the gardens to get to the rock which are worth exploring. Once you’re getting close to the rock it is quite a steep climb, we arrived around 2.30 in the afternoon and found it very quiet but hot.  Contrary to what we read it gets much busier late afternoon when it’s cooler. If you have vertigo, seeing the cave paintings is quite an experience climbing up a creaking spiral staircase high up. The final metal staircase again can be challenging, especially if you have vertigo with many people looking absolutely terrified on the climb.  once you reach the top it’s well worth it, with absolutely stunning, panoramic views and ruins to explore. This place is totally worth a visit and one of our personal favourite places visited in Sr Lanka so far.
The ruins and gardens you pass on the way to Lion Rock are very attractive and ancient. Some good photo stops to see the rock.

Sigiriya Lion Rock was a must stop for our family. Young boys 6 and 10 made it to the top just fine. The views and cool breeze at the top are wonderful. There are peddlers "assisting" you up the stairs. If you need help please accept it, but be aware they won't leave without a good tip.

What a breath taking view (once you get tot he top) Do visit the lion rock after noon, as the heat might get you in the morning! Although it is a small hike and lots of tourists (it took us roughly 25-40 minutes) to get to the top non stop walking on the marble steps. You won’t regret it after you get to the top! Beautiful views from every angle of Sri Lanka, you could see the tallest Buddha statue in the deep jungle. Cute little monkeys and puppies on the way to the summit. Don’t forget to bring a drink bottle!

It’s an amazing experience but with a 30 usd entrance fee !!! Sri Lanka is still learning about tourism and it’s crazy entry prices to sights putting many people off . You have to pay it in lkr - rupees . We’ve seen a big snake roaming around freely . A little scary. Many many monkeys playing around too . Nice too watch but make sure to come down before dark . The last entry is 5/5.30 pm but once you’re in you’re allowed to stay in until 6.30/7 pm . We’ve watched the mesmerising colours of the sunset but got a little worried coming down , if it gets dark there’s no lighting , very sharp stairs , in our case it started raining when we were descending and we wanted to run to our car since we didn’t want to be left alone with monkeys , stray dogs , snakes in the dark . This is what I mean when I say , 30 usd is too high if in return they give nothing back !!! Litter was everywhere on top , no security except the few guards making sure no photos being taken where the paintings are . This is an amazing place which everyone come to Sri Lanka to visit however I wouldn’t recommend it to families with little kids. I’ve seen a child crying , climbing down the slippery metal stair cases , when monkeys were too close. No escape route . No signs . I’m glad I’ve seen it but if I return to Sri Lanka I wouldn’t rush back to it .  Unbelievable history . Breathtaking views from the top . If you don’t like heights don’t even consider it. As it’s open space . At some parts there’s only one staircase , meaning people going up or down sharing the same one , insane and dangerous!!! We’ve gone late in the afternoon to avoid crowds and the heat , even then there was considerable amount of people there , mostly Chinese tourists because of the Chinese New Year . Happy holidays
The climb to the top is super exhausting but totally worth it! The view from the top and the lion rock is stunning. A must visit UNESCO site in SriLanka.

Okay so this is never going to pass health and safety in the UK but we're not in the UK. Some of the steps are uneven and even a bit loose. There are no toilets once you get past the car park. There is no cable car ride for the less able or less inclined. But the climb is something that really should be done if you can possibly manage it, for both the views, to see the ruins and the mirror wall, and to say you did it. Tip: go early in the morning (7 am) to beat the crowds and to complete the climb before the sun hit the steps.

The rock is not that hard to climb finally - except for the last section that we did not! - with 2 kids (7 and 4 years old). The view from the lion pawn was great. The metallic stairs looked scary and not secure enough, so we took the decision to stop the ascension there and go back.

Yes, it's a dramatic view from the top, or even from the Lion's Paw, where we decided to stop. Not through fatigue or vertigo, we'd just had enough of jostling in a column of sweaty bodies, and the last section was two way and jam packed. This was early to mid morning, the supposed quieter time.

It's a really amazing place and the climb isn't as bad as it looks (if you're relatively fit !).  Go early (it opens at 7 a.m.)  We did and it was relatively quiet but after spending about an hour up there, when we were on our way down we came across masses of people going up. Like all the other heritage sites in Sri Lanka (Polonnoruwa, Dambulla, Pidurangala and Anuradhapura etc), it's really expensive and we hoped that all the income from tourists (a lot) is going to the right place (the maintenance and restoration of these sites) rather than into the wrong pockets - say no more ...

This site just takes your breath away! It is simply stunning in every way: beauty location, views, history, archeology, wildlife, peace and quiet of the grounds - it is all there. Allow plenty of time to explore all of it. Some guide books say you need 3 hours to visit. Definitely more time should be devoted to exploring it  all properly and soaking its unique atmosphere.

World heritage site,  magnificently restored ruins.  Museum for those who dare not climb the hundreds of steps upwards but for those that do, be rewarded with views to die for and beautifully maintained archeological ruins. Gardens wonderful,  monkeys and bird life abound.  Well worth the money.

Quite unique across the world as a site. Be careful to manage though the heat. We went up towards the end of the afternoon which was good, but still a bit hot going up. It was beginning to clear out at the top though.

Too many people even at 8.30 am. Gardeners hard at work sweeping leaves ensured the water gardens etc looked very tidy. Access to the frescoes, mirror wall (now nothing to see), lion paws and the top itself is by a hideous mixture of metal staircases of varying styles. Arriving in the first half of the day ensures you walk up the staircases to the very top in the blazing sun while a visit in the late afternoon would result in being in the shade and jostling with far fewer people. Why this 'attraction' is such an attraction in the first place is puzzling given its $30 per person entrance fee and why its World Heritage Site status hasn't prevented its ruination even more so.

This place was fantastic to visit, we arrived about 7.30am and we were so glad we did, at some parts we were alone on the climb and up top we were able to get some great photos, by the time we came down at 10.30 it was completely different- so busy!! No way I would have bothered then and the sun was scorching. Big tour groups with incredibly old people literally being carried up by sri Lankan guides was ludicrous- so glad we only passed them on our way down! We had an amazing visit, the climb is ok but you are a little out of breathe by the top! just please if you can remember to go early!!
Hard work on the climb, but worth it. Plenty opportunity to rest on the way up. Take water, and enjoy.

Lions Rock is an incredible natural phenomen and has significant Sri Lankian historical value. The climb and view is stunning and beautiful. Now the rating is due to the extreme overprice of 30 USD per person and the fact they don't even accept credit card. Off course we do pay when we are there in SL, but there is absolutely no reason for this price. Pure money machine. Locals pay less than 50 dollar cent (which is fair, but no reason for tourist exploitation). If you are on budget go to Pido mountain, which is just as good.

Lions Rock is an incredible natural phenomen and has significant Sri Lankian historical value. The climb and view is stunning and beautiful. Now the rating is due to the extreme overprice of 30 USD per person and the fact they don't even accept credit card. Off course we do pay when we are there in SL, but there is absolutely no reason for this price. Pure money machine. Locals pay less than 50 dollar cent (which is fair, but no reason for tourist exploitation). If you are on budget go to Pido mountain, which is just as good.

The gardens are great but like most I had come for the challenge. Some parts were harder with steep stone steps but the last part was relatively easy up a metal staircase. Views were disappointing because of the weather and the ruins interesting but not spectacular

Thus is a must if you are visiting Sri Lanka. An astonishing ruined palace on the  top ofthe rock - but be warned, the climb is not suitable for anyone without a head for heights or the stamina to climb the 1200 steps. Don't worry, there's lots to see at the base, including shady royal water gardens.

My husband’s family and I hiked a good portion of Sigiriya, although only my father-in-law, husband and I made it to the top. There are a LOT of tourists, which makes it crowded and tough to take some photos, other areas are off-limits to any kind of photos (the frescos) and the lines are long because there are so many stairs. I still felt it was worth the trip to the top, but some members of our family couldn’t take the pounding on their knees. I’d still recommend this place, but only if you have healthy knees, not much claustrophobia, plenty of water and sunscreen. I’d pay to go back up again, but I enjoy challenging hikes! Don’t go if that’s not you!

should visit the place if you visit Sri Lanka, not for minors and aged for climbing the rock, but if you are planing just to visit the heritage site at ground level every one can do that. the place is peaceful and garden is well maintained. it is bit expensive

the place is nicely maintained and with the stairs it is easy to climb the rock to the top. it is bit scary to look down while climbing but bit difficult to climb with an infant or small kid. Take your own eateries and drink water when you climb. the view from the top is mesmerizing. If you are physically fit it wont take more than 2-3 hrs to complete. but $30 is little high.

Located near Dambulla. Reached from Colombo via AC bus facility. Around 4 and half hour journey duration. Better to start the hike early in the morning before it gets too sunny. There are also multiple lodges located nearby if one intends to stay overnight. The place has been very well maintained and is a UN world heritage site. Entire hike takes around 60-90 minutes depending on ones pace. To reach to the top, one has to climb around 400 stairs. We went for the option of guided tour and it was totally worth it. Tips - For travellers from SAARC countries it is recommended to carry your passports in order to obtain the discounted ticket rates for entry to citadel. - Better to carry water bottles along with you as one might get thirsty and there are no shops present on the way. There are few vendors present once you complete the descent but then we found them overpriced. - Don’t hesitate to bargain for guided tour. Guided are well aware and give you a better picture of the entire place and are highly recommended.

Palace and palace gardens are both stunning. Palace is on top of the rock, climb is long (45-60 min) but worth it. You should climb the rock as early as possible to avoid the heat and the lines. When it is busy take the cobra entrance instead of the main entrance, this way you will enter the queue at the fresco’s. Palace gardens are at the bottom of the rock, you should take a guide to visit the gardens and the rock. Otherwise you will miss a lot of information.

We reached here after much arrangement from kandy.And here when we arrived taken aback by the shear presence of this rock hill.The climb was a steep one.Reaching the top was like your at the top of the world

The view from the top is simply amazing. Infact the whole heritage site and climb is amazing! the only letdown, which is the same at most Sri Lankan tourist attractions, is the price. We climbed the rock just after climbing Pidurangala for sunrise. There weren't to many people climbing then nor was there too many people at the top. After we descended(10:30am) the line up to climb was massive and would definitely take away from the experience.

Having read everything that I could find - we set our stall out to be first in the queue when the ticket office opened at 7am, in fact we were 2nd. Our tuk tuk driver took us to the ticket office then parked up at the exit and waited for us. The timings were ideal because we were able to do the whole walk through the gardens and up rock without a queue of people in front or behind us and before the sun got hot too, there is a temptation to linger in the gardens but in doing so time moves on and you will be soon be climbing in the sun. There are a great many stone steps to climb even before you arrive at the Lions Rock, the final climb is on a combination of metal & stone steps - the handrail is rusty, so take some wipes. We didn’t go up the spiral staircase to look at the fresco - it was suggest by others afterwards that we’d made the right decision. The whole place is kept beautiful, as we walked locals were sweeping all the steps and surrounding ground, picking up leaves and ensuring the areas were tidy - its unfortunate that rubbish is discarded by tourists rather than putting it in the bins that are provided. Having walked down our driver took us back to see the museum which in my opinion is the right way roundly do it,  as it makes more sense that way. There are old photographs but for me the gallery area with the model of the area together with the video was the best. Have a great trip

Tougher than The Great Wall and Machu Picchu ( or maybe I’ve aged a bit). Go early 07.00 to avoid the hoards. VERY tough 1,200 steps to climb but manageable if there aren’t too many people so you can rest regularly on the way up. The views are spectacular (360 degrees). Luckily our guide, Aruna Silva, was a fountain of useful information and the weather was clear and dry.

30 dollars each (thirty dollars!) to climb 1800 steps and see almost nothing? We decided not to pay that indecent amount of money to the srilankian government for one of the biggest scam. This costs more than the Colosseum, Moma museum, Eiffel tower and thousand of Important monuments in the world. Do yourself a favour, go to the near Pindurangala rock where you pay only around 5 dollars, easier climb and better view.
It is a very large site. We started at the garden, went up to the very nice fresco's and the mirrorwal. Then up to the lionsgate and finally after 2000  steps we reached the top. Fantastic view! !!!!

Yes you will be tired and sweaty, yes it is a touch pricey, but you really must climb lions rock at least once in your lifetime! Take your time and the climb will be enjoyable and not too bad. There are lots of people which slows you down-- not necessarily a bad thing. Many shops on the way down for souvenirs but don't let them push you. Just take in the view and the exercise and enjoy!

The way to the top was quite terrifying for someone afraid of heights. Thought I would be tough and do it without any stress, I totally panicked on the rusty spiral stairs above... nothing. So, if you are afraid of heights, consider going with someone who would support you. The view from the top is breathtaking and is really worth the hike in the crowds. Remember to take some extra water and something to sit on at the top! Also, be aware of the monkeys... They were trying to steal our stuff!

Some describe this as the eighth wonder of the world and it's easy to see why. If you have the chance you really must visit this and make the climb. But do yourself a favour and get there early (7am) as it gets really busy and personally I'd hate to experience the massive queues that form later in the day.

Get there very early to avoid the crowds. We had a sunrise viewing from a different area then came straight over. We went straight to the top and by the time we were coming down buses of tourists were starting queues to get up. Really beautiful views from the top. I also recommend reading up on the significance of the site on Wikipedia to give you some background or if you want to pay then get a guide or a tour.

It’s better to take selfie & clicks from down. No benefits to get up that 200 meter rock. Narrow staircase. Ticket cost for outsider is  $30, but don’t forget to carry your passport to get the ticket on $30 otherwise it would be more costly. There’s cafe are also near ticket counter. 2000+ steps need to get on top.

Its near resorts about 500 mtr on walking distance. Go with passport otherwise you’ll have to pay double charges for tickets. From the top you’ll sew adorable view of Lord Budha statue. About 45 minuets takes to reach on the top of the rock. Go carefully and take pictures carefully.

In my opinion this is definitely worth the 30USD entrance fee. We arrived early in the morning to avoid the heat & the crowds and were on the top at just after 9am. Although there are many steps, there are places to stop and enjoy the view and get your breath back. The final set of stairs are very busy but once you are up on the top The views are amazing.
Every person must visit at least once..  Better to bring kids since this is a historical place.. Beautiful Place.. Beautiful View..
The ticket itself is about 4200 rupees and about 30 USD. It is worth to visit it once and thats it. The view on top was stunning but going there around afternoon can be really really hot.
We had a great walk in the park leading to the rock and a small hike towards the top. The view is superb

Great place It’s a great place to go. We skipped the crowds as went early in the morning. The view from the top is absolutely brilliant. The whole area is laid out very well. There are places to rest and thus easy to climb. Our friend who is in her mid 60s with bad knees was able to go right up to the top (she found a branch which she used as a walking stick) The painting in the caves have still maintained the brilliant colors. Definitely a must see/visit.
Sigiriya consists of an ancient citadel built by King Kashyapa during the 5th century . It has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and is one of Sri Lanka’s most popular landmarks.

A really well worthwhile trip. Very well run and clean and tidy toilets. Go early it is exhausting !!! The effort is worth all the stairs and my goodness you climb!!! The route down is easy and quick. The museum is worth the effort too. Don’t go if you don’t like heights it is not the place to have a panic attack. Fantastic

It's an amazing rock fortress from above reveals the incredible engineering that wegnt into construction. The name refers to a site of historical and archaeological significance , King kashyapa build his castle on this enormous rock and decorated wonderfullly. There represent ancient srilankan painting and writings Once you go there you'll get the real experience how ancient srilankan royals spent their lifestyle.  Don't miss your chance to visit there if you are in Sri Lanka.
walking in the area  with  garden, little like, rocks  is really an experience. The the effort to climb over 1000 steps is rewarded by the rock lion's top view! raccomanded
must to see in sri lanka definitely. i can recommend it to you. the entrance ticket is about 30 dollars per person but it is not too much in my opinion. thet view from the top is extremely amazing.

This is an extraordinary place! A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is one of those "must see" places. The rock/citadel is an ancient monument with a fascinating history and it looks spectacular even from a distance. I visited with a friend during a short tour (we were attending a conference). She climbed the rock, but because I have bad knees, I felt I was not up to the climb. It was very steep, and a continuous line of people walking up. Observing the well laid-out, rather beautiful grounds, with statues and lovely trees, I also noticed the continuous flow of huge tourist buses (mostly Chinese). This concerned me; as a World Heritage Site, it might become degraded if this continues; they should probably limit numbers. Instead of climbing, I took a lovely tour of the area via "tuk tuk" (it was raining, on and off) and enjoyed the quiet beauty of the natural surroundings - many birds, a huge lizard and monkeys! My friend said that she really appreciated having her own guide, as she was a little nervous about the climb. She said he was really good but of course she had to tip him extra. Still, this is one of those "must see" places in Sri Lanka. What I loved about it was the amazing views of the rock from different vantage points.

As per the title really! A great visit, I've been twice nice now in the past 20 years. This time around it was *packed*. We had about 5 mins of "freedom" while climbing, then joined a massive queue and slowly walked to the top in single file. All tours of Sri Lanka include this as a stop. Recommendation: go *early*, like be there when it opens at 7am and go up first, then look round the refurbed museum afterwards. We arrived on a weekday at around 09:30 and starting climbing around 10:30 after getting tickets and looking at museum, and wished we hadn't done it in that order, ;-) It is not as steep as people say, if you're of modest fitness, this is an easy enough climb. If you're out of shape, then it will need a few breaks, but it's only a small hill really, so don't think you're climbing Everest!  You're walking up some stairs. Views from the top are worth the climb, definitely. Note: Various locals will offer to help you up the steps - they will expect payment, and it didn't seem cheap from what we observed.

Had a great morning exploring the site. Was great learning about the history of the Citadel of Sigiriya and surrounds Also crocodiles, monkeys and giant lizards wonder the moats and grounds. Magical place.
A must visit place if you are visiting Sri Lanka. Specifically the mirror wall, the caves, the wall paintings, etc.

It's a bit difficult to climb to the top of the rock. But if you can do that it's worth doing it. Excellent place amazing things to learn. Must see are the mirror wall, the caves, the carvings on the wall. A must visit if you are at Sri Lanka.

When buying the tickets, we though the price was rather high. However the site is looked after very well. At no point did I see one piece of litter. It is quite a hike to reach the top. I would advise trainers rather than flip flops. Also take PLENTY of water! There are plenty of places to stop and catch your breath/rest and take in the views. We were here for nearly 3 hours. Very glad we stopped and saw Sigiriya, it’s a must on your bucket list in Sri Lanka 🇱🇰
It is a tiring to make it in one day trip but really worth of doing it, need a good driver to manage this.

enjoyable trip. me and my children were tired but enjoyed the trek upto the fortress. Cons - ticket is expensive. For such an expensive ticket, it would be nice if there was some water at the top of the hill. We did have water with us but a one hour trek meant it finished while we were up there.

This is a wonderful place which was a fortress before during the time of Kings. It's a miracle that the  irrigation system inside the top of this rock and the features while climbing till top . Must visit place in Sri Lanka. I went this place with Arooha tours Sri Lanka, my guide was thaufeek and he was amazing person and took care us well during the tour

We weren't planning to go there, but guide recommended so we went. And I was pleased even the ticket wasn't that cheap. Museum I find uninteresting, nothing special there. Climbing felt like awful first, but when getting higher, the air was cooler and stairs easier. The climbing itself takes about an hour from bottom to up and back, but if you want to take pictures, then reserve more time. We were there 2,5hours and could've spend more in the gardens.

Warm up your calves because you're about to ascend a lot of steps, however the view from the top is completely worth the sweat. This is expensive ($30USD per adult) but as a cultural experience it is a must. Dress light and with good shoes as some steps are narrow.
Don't miss Sigiriya. It is a somewhat steep climb to the top [and a crowded climb in tourist season] but the views from the top are fabulous.
A highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka, worth having a guide to appreciate it fully

This is a must for every tourist. To avoid the crowds it is essential to arrive early - ticket office opens at 0700. Water gardens are delightful and then the walk to the top - 1202 strenuous steps but the sight at the top is spectacular.
Well worth a visit. It is well worth hiring a guide who will show you round and explain the history in great detail.
Nice place, climbing the rock isn't hard. Keep climbing up the stairs, you will get a great view. Enjoy it!

1,200 steps before you reach the UNESCO world heritage site "Sigiriya Rock" or "Lion's Rock." provides you with a breathtaking view. After all the efforts of climbing up, I can tell you that it is worth all the hard work. We spent around 60 minutes admiring the view once we reached the top. If you are from a SAARC (Maldives, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan and Afghanistan) country, make sure to carry the original passport for the special rates. It is advised to stay hydrated and be very careful as at places there are no side railing and could be dangerous especially for kids. Don't forget to keep an umbrella in case of a sudden shower. Also, wear casual clothes I would recommend gym wear. There are several stories around the same and according to one of the stories the top of the rock was used as helipad by Ravana.

This was the physical challenge of our Sri Lankan tour, the climb to the top of Lion Rock.  It is strenuous and not for anyone with any chronic conditions, but the view once you get to the top are stupendous.  The history of the Rock and the reasons for the fortifications are fascinating too. Go as early in the day as you can, as the stairways to the top are two-way and once the first visitors are heading down they will become very cramped. It's cooler too, of course!
Visited here at 7 o'clock in the morning to miss the heat of the day. Climbed to the top up the 1222 steps and worth the effort for the views from the top.

This is one of the best places to visit in Srilanka. Your trip is not complete if you do hit this place. Though you have to climb a lot  it is very doable. Best time to start is 7 am. You can get tickets from the building near the first lake.For elders do it only if you are fit enough. The view from up there is really great. NEVER MISS THIS

Gardens well kept.  Loads of steps to climb before you reach the start of the main climb.  Need to get there early as this really is a tourist trap.  Beware of the hawkers that offer to assist you with the climb and then want to charge you extortionate amount.  Our driver advised us what was a reasonable amount and offered that. They weren’t happy but we told them “ take it or leave it” just be aware !

To me this site rivals the ruins of Machu Picchu. Its amazing how a palace complex was build on a tall sheer granite rock and it served as residence of a king and monks. This fortress complex ruins speak of amazing feat of planning, engineering, art and variety of skills. About 1500 steps take visitors on an amazing journey through boulder gardens, frescoes, mirror wall and lion paws. From the top the views of surrounding area are amazing ! Wear good shoes, bring water and take your time to climb to the top of this amazing rock, try to climb early in the morning to avoid heat. It took us about three hours from start to finish. Little tough but doable and well worth walk ! Do spend some time exploring the museum at the entrance. I also found a interesting souvenirs here, which I didn't see any where else in Sri Lanka. It was "magic box", a carved wooden box with hidden compartments. I paid 2000 slr for it.

We left our hotel the Sigiriya at 7am, to climb the rock before the crowds arrive - and the heat became too much. It paid off. We had a wonderful climb, with hardly anyone else around - and could spend time on the top looking at the views in peace. There were 3 puppies up there when we went a few weeks ago - amazing that they can survive and thrive up there! Wear sensible shoes, as there are many steps to climb, and take a drink up with you. Also beware of the monkeys! (My husband had his backpack side picket picked by one!) It was hilarious - but luckily we didn't lose anything valuable.
Very nice! Beutiful nature, beautiful views, lot of animals. There is possibility of local guide. There are something about 1500 stairs but It’s not that bad as it looks😁

I do not have a head for heights so was unsure if I was going to make it to the top. Lots of relaxing breathing and just concentrating on looking at the shoes of the person ahead of me got me up to the top. It is quite a hike but definitely worth it. Luckily it was a cloudy day so it wasn't too exhausting, but on a very sunny day I would start as early in the morning as possible. At the top there are lots of different areas, the kings pool and throne I was not expecting! And of course the dogs and puppies that seem to live up there?!

We went to Sigiriya early morning and it was already crowded. There were masses of coaches and people. The early morning meant the steps (and there are a lot or them) are very slippery. A local man approach me offering to assist me on the steps. Although I declined he was persistent. I told him again I was ok. Finally I offered him 100 rupee to leave and he said it wasn't enough so gave him 200. Again it was 'not enough' and he got quite aggressive so I gave him 1000 rupee. It would have turned ugly if I didn't turn my back and walk away with my traveling companions. Be warned! It does require a level of fitness to climb this amazing site although I did see people on crutches being pushed and pulled upwards. The history is amazing so make sure you go with a guide. The views also stunning. Definitely a highlight of our trip.
I have to say this one of my highlights in srilanka- amazing view of the site from the photo bottom and epic views from the top Its a must see!!

It is a must go if visiting sigiriya or Dambulla. There is an entry ticket of 30 usd for foreign visitors (15 usd for SAARC nationals). Go early in the morning to avoid the afternoon heat, as you have to climb nearly 500 mtr and walk at lest 1km to reach the starting point of climb. Wear shoes and keep a water bottle along. Do not get bog down by the climb, the view from top of the rock is breath taking and it also makes you wonder, how was it all built in that era.

The Sigiriya World Heritage Site, UNESCO listed, is one of the major tourist attractions in Sri Lanka. It is to be located in the Matale District, near to the town of Dambulla in the Central Province. It is a massive rock, some 200 meters high and is of very important historical and archaeological interest. We strongly advise anyone planning to visit to read up on the history of the rock which legend associates with the ancient Kingdom of the land. One can make the very challenging ascent of the rock up over a thousand steps (which we first did many years ago before the ascent was improved) and guides are available to explain the route and the history associated with it. Aside from the most incredible views, one can enjoy the fantastic historical frescoes and gardens. In the heat of the sun, the climb can be demanding. Water, hat and sunscreen are essential. My latest photo shows the rock from ground level. Other photos to follow. It is an amazing feeling to have done this climb! Over the years tourism has significantly increased here and the route is very busy and you will find many souvenir stalls and drink outlets at the base.
Fabulous trip to the World Heritage site. It was first trip for my son and he really enjoyed the hike.. Lot of steps to get to the top. Beautiful 360 degree view..

Rare ruins on top of the rock and amazing views. The route to the top, is beautiful. You pass by all kinds of ruins (and wildlife). The climb uphill is challenging, even if you are not afraid of heights. But, it is worth it! Magnificent ruins on top, beautiful views of the surrounding area and you feel as you are on top of the world. Bring water and sunscreen. Visit in the morning, the stairs up are in the shade during that time of the day. This will easy up you climb. It can be very busy, so take enough time to visit this location. At the exit, there are all kinds of outlets to get hydrated of buy your souvenirs.
A must see, and a must climb! 1,202 steps. Views are spectacular. The frescoes are most amazing. The history behind this monument is well worth the climb up the mountain.

This is a must must visit site in Sri Lanka. First of all, the rock itself is huge - protruding out of literally nowhere. And I came to know that the rock itself is like millions of years old. It is just remarkable to imagine that they created a whole palace on the rock. The gardens, the fresco painting, the mirror wall and the whole setup on the top of the rocks is worth seeing. It get very hot though. I think they should have some arrangement considering such hot climate.

The most tiring trip in my life. I have done it in 35 degrees and I’m proud of my self. The view was breath taking but prices for tourist’s tickets sooooo expensive comparing with local people tickets.
The climb is steep to the top . Go on a slow pace and request the authorities to provide water bottles on sale.
The wedding anniversary day and climb up was so heavenly.  Would just ask for the authorities to provide water bottles on sale . Climb is steep and the view on the top was breathtakingly beautiful

This is a must see in Sri Lanka. From the moment you walk into the grounds it is breathtaking. The gardens are well cared for and the site itself is magnificent. The climb looks high from the ground but as you ascend it is surprisingly not too hard - it is an enjoyable climb. The spiral stair case is a little scary if you do not like heights as it is on the side of the rock face. Overall this place is as beautiful as you can imagine. The view from the top is green as far as the eye can see. Do not miss this!

I visited on a Thursday arriving at around 14:00. Perfect time as the last people were just leaving and when I left at 15:30 the tour groups started showing up. Tickets had to be bought in the museum (no queue) and I could park my bike right at the entrance. I made my way up the rock. The spiral staircase is pretty creepy but you don’t have to go up there (you’ll miss the wall paintings though). The rest of the path up to the summit is doable but best bring some water and catch your breath from to time. Each of the sites has a little plague with information which I really appreciate (not wanting a guide and all). I arrived on the summit with the palace to gorgeous views of the grounds below. The only downsides were staff begging for cigarettes and the rather high admission price. Still a solid experience.

If you come to srilanka you must visit the sigiriya lion rock. Go well prepared as you have to climb the rock. Go early in the morning as it will become hot later. Prefer wearing shoes and take along with you a water bottle, glasses and a hat. Once you reach the top the view is amazing....

The Sigiriya Rock (also called Lion's Rock) is one of the major highlights in Sri Lanka and one of the most expensive places (30 USD). Anyhow, it's definitely worth going there. As there are many stairs it can take a bit longer when there are many groups with older people around (and I was suprised how many older tourists were trying to climp the rock). Keep in mind that you enter the garden area of Sigiriya from the west. So if you would like to take photos of the rock you will have the sunlight coming from the oposite direction when going there before noon -- not good to take the "classic" pictures of the rock. Should you want to take photos under better light conditions then you will have to go there in the afternoon. However, even if the Rock looks best in the sunset light, it will be difficult to climb the rock when it gets dark. The visit of Sigiriya is designed as a round tour so that you enter through the main entrance and leave the site at the exit near the tourist parking site. So it might be a bit tricky to get back to the garden area after descent.

This was my second visit to Sigiriya, and this time I was determined to get to the top of this rock fortress.  Our guide said we would be starting at 7am when the doors opened for two reasons.  Firstly, it gets very hot later in the day and secondly, the crowds build up from 9am onwards making the climb very slow and tedious.  This was good advice. The climb itself is not difficult but unless you are really fit I would advise taking it at a steady pace - there are no records to be broken and you may do yourself damage in trying to get to the top too quickly.  It is 1500+ steps which are narrow and need careful negotiating, however it gets easier towards the top of the Lion staircase where there are metal handrails.  When you reach the top the views are magnificent and you have a great sense of achievement.  The cost is expensive when you consider you are just walking up a rovk face, but look at it this way - you are helping preserve a World Heritage site. Remember to take plenty of water with you on this climb and start early if possible.

What an amazing place. Well worth a visit but make sure you go early in the day, take plenty of water and wear a hat as there is little shade on the climb to the top. It is best to visit the museum before you go to the rock as it explains what you will see and also has reconstructions of how it looked in its hey day. There are local guides there but we had our own guide. Not sure if you would need a guide if you visited the museum before climbing. Don’t be put off when you see the spiral staircase. You don’t need to go up that if you don’t want to see some of the rock paintings. Allow a half day for the visit.

We thought this to be overly expensive, particularly as my wife also had to pay the full admission price even though she was only going to wait in the gardens at the bottom of the ‘rock’. That said, the climb was worth the effort, with spectacular views to be had from the summit.

Get there early morning and don't be intimidated by the number of steps everyone keeps talking about. The steps are in sections with lots of flat ground in between sections. So you are not climbing 1200+ steps in one go. Take a light sweater with you, it gets very windy up there. Nasty monkeys will try to attack you and take your food.
Fantastic history, nice gardens, scary walk up and down if you have vertigo like me. Still made it to the top and really worth the effort

The climb itself is horrible due to the huge numbers of slow-moving tour groups (allow an hour to get up even if you could do it in half the time given the chance) but you get great views and interesting ruins at the top.  Make sure to explore the ruined gardens at the bottom - there are quite a few areas and they're much quieter and good for relaxing.  There are even paths through the forest that can be good.  Make sure to see the museum as well, since you're paying $30 for the whole site.  There's one cafeteria near the entrance that's actually ok for water and juice and snacks the rest of the restaurants are south on the main road.  I spent over 4 hours on all of it.

It’s a long way up and down on a mixture is stone and metal steps (some of the latter quite narrow Huge fortress grounds and spectacular views at the top However it was a constant line of people going up and down and I felt uncomfortable on the spiral section bit where many of the cage supports are rusted right through and you are very high off the ground Given the weight of people on the steps at any one time it looks to me like an accident in waiting ~ however I am not an engineer!

I got there before 9am and the path was already full with tour groups, many of their members being very out of shape or so wide that they blocked the paths. The heat and smell and noise is amplified by the crowding and the whole ascent was horrible. It took me an hour to get to the top but only because of the crowding as the ascent is pretty easy - 500 stairs to the first big landing, then you can go up and down the circular stairs (about 100) to see the frescoes, then past the mirror wall and it’s another 200 stairs to the main landing and 250 more to the peak of the summit, and the stairs are in decent condition. The ruins on the summit are surprisingly big and interesting, and the views are superb, but there were so many shouting people, barking dogs, screaming children and loud phone calls that it’s like being in the streets of Colombo. It’s all quite spectacular and how often will you be in Sri Lanka but it’s one of those ultra-touristy places that makes you wonder if the hassle and the $30 cost is worth it. Whether or not you go up Sigiriya, nearby Pindurangala is much better for enjoying a climb and views (but not for history and ruins).

Bullet point notes If you cycle there, in the main entrance and you will be directed left, around the moat which is a splendid experience Peak visitors are 1000am, so avoid that time as queues for the frescos. W/E as well when Sri Lankan Nationals visit If it's busy there are 3 staircases to the frescos. The right is peaceful There is a cafeteria where the bikes are parked, good juice bar and inside seating Finally if you do go and reach the top, put the mobile and selfie stick away, look at the wonderful views and appreciate the place

Six of us set off from the bottom. Two dropped out before the mirror wall. Another drops out at the lions feet leaving three to climb the final ladders. It’s tiring but we managed it up in just over an hour. Go early, ie before 11am as it gets horrendously busy and the last stretch you pass people on the way down whilst you go up. Ignore the locals who will try and fleece you for helping you up. Worth it when you get to the top.

We stayed in Habarana for a couple of nights and went to Sigiriya. WOW...dont miss it if you're in this part of Sri Lanka. Be prepared to climb 1,200 steps but even if you are of average fitness its doable. Just take your time. Get there early. No later than 7.30 as it can get very busy with tourist buses around 9.30 to 10am and makes navigating the stairs more chaotic. I promise you the hard work is worth every breathtaking view. An absolute must see.
Lion Rock is truly an amazing experience. Lots of people go and the climb can be daunting but once you get to the top its all worth it.

It was an extremely hard climb up the rock as the railing was very shaky. When you got to the top the view was immaculate. Coming down was even harder as the rails were loose and it was very steep. There were stone paintings in a part of the rock the were very well maintained.

This is a definite visit if you go to Sri Lanka. You will learn a lot about the king that resided in Lion's rock and the way of life back in the days. It was great seeing the Art on the mountain and the way "technology" was administired inside the fortress. The kingdom on top looked very beautiful and just imagining how it must have appeared back in the days will leave you in "awe" and amusement.

We visited early in the morning along with a few hundred others. However the whole site was immaculate with people constantly gardening and sweeping. Very attractive and interesting site steep climb to the top but worth it. I was off put by “helpful” men keep grabbing my arm to try and help me despite being with my husband and our guide.
Expensive for tourists at 30 USD but well worth the climb . If you don't like heights it will test your resolve - Look out for the monkeys , they are very accomplished thieves.

Loads of people claim it's a ripoff but I thought it was ok value. The climb was easy. Cost me 2000 rupees from south side of dambulla to get there with the 2 kids via tutuk  including waiting time and climb up the nearby pidurangala (500rupee adult 250 kids). Book on The street not via the guesthouse. Entrance to sigiriya was around 9300 rupees for me and the 2 kids.  Kids are 6-11. Under 6 free. Better than the sacred city at anuradapurah which was disappointing.

A must for all visors to Sri Lanka.  the cave paintings are incredible and the ruins and view from the top are worth the climb.  It did not seem as arduous as I though it was going to be to climb up.  We visited in the afternoon when it was slightly cooler and less busy.

We were not warned that the climb up this rock castle would be quite a feat for a fit 60 plus couple with a grown up daughter. Anyway without much trouble we managed the hike up but did not attempt the final level where the castle ruins are situated. Wear appropriate foot ware as there is loose gravel on the rocky steps. A very nice climb but make sure you a reasonably fit don't trip and fall as there wasn't any visible first aid assistance anywhere.
You have to climbe 1,000 stairs but than you can apriciate the building project. Exeptional view from the top.worth a visit

The climb is much easier than the Pidurangala Rock. However, recommend going there as early as possible as the climb is much easier and you will have fewer people. By about 9am you will have to wait in line to climb as the many tourist buses make their way. Once up it is amazing view but we really enjoyed the ruins. It makes you go back in time and wonder how the royals may have lived during those days. Our three kids were very creative in each of the areas of the fort. The entrance fees are quite high however we noticed the place is kept clean, there is a first aid office, few staff walking around to help climbers and keeping an eye on everyone. So the fees is put to good use

* Price 30$ for adults and half price for children 6-12 years and less than 6 years free of charge * A must do : this is the most unique thing about Sri Lanka   , you can do other things that is Doable in other countries ( elephant ride, safari, whale watching, beaches) But the lion rock is only is Sri Lanka ... Challenge and ability: We were 26 people, from toddlers to seniors that are 67 years old. We all did it 💪. A life time experience, we enjoyed it.. it was challenging but you can have breaks all the way. In the middle there is a wide nice space that you can sit and enjoy the view before you continue the journey up to the top. The climb itself is enjoyable as you can see very nice view all around you. The weather was very nice.

It's a hell of a walk to the top but 100% worth it. We went on a relatively hot day and enjoyed the grounds around Lion rock before. As you head up prepare for a long walk up and there are less and less breaks as you go up. The view is amazing however it's just as good from the lion feet as it is for the top (and you don't have to que). Definitely visit of your in Sri Lanka, a must see I would strongly recommend you get a drink before heading up as you will need it at the top.
The Sigiriya is very nice and clean place. Hiking is very easy even for older people. However, you should start to hike in the morning because of high temperature.

Absolutely loved my visit here.  Though heavily geared towards the tourist market, the place felt authentic.  I don’t consider myself scared of heights, however, the last flight of stairs up to the summit did put me on edge during my descent. We paid a guide Rs.3000, but to be honest, we didn’t really need him.  Though he was very friendly, I would advise other tourists to skip the guides, and just climb and enjoy. You can easily read up on the history of the place online before or after visiting to consolidate your knowledge. Also, near the summit, there are a handful of monkeys to photograph!

The Sigiriya Rock (also called Lion's Rock) is one of the major highlights in Sri Lanka and one of the most expensive places (30 USD). Anyhow, it's definitely worth going there. Many tour operators offer combined trips going to Pidurangala Rock for sunrise first and then to Sigiriya. It's indeed beautiful to watch the Lion's Rock in the sunrise light, but it can be challenging to go up to Pidurangala and two hours later to Sigiriya. Make sure you slept well the night before to be fit enough. Also keep in mind that you enter the garden area of Sigiriya from the west. So if you would like to take photos of the rock you will have the sunlight coming from the oposite direction when going there before noon -- not good to take the "classic" pictures of the rock.
