As there are many stairs it can take a bit longer when there are many groups with older people around (and I was suprised how many older tourists were trying to climp the rock). The visit of the museum is not worth it, better go directly to the main entrance before it gets too hot.
Clinm up preferably in the evening so that you can witness the sunset from here. Involves a long and uphill climb. Entry ticket is also pretty expensive.
Easy to climb..Great views & beautiful grounds.. can be done without a guide so if your only interested in the hike only, save your money & go solo.. worth a visit

We got there early, bought our tickets and headed straight for the rock, saving the terraces and museum for later in the day. The climb up is quite straightforward and not too challenging, at least when it's quiet. There is a break part way up the first section to detour to the cave paintings of the Apsara/princesses. These are beautiful, although no photos allowed (it is reproduced in the museum and also extracts in the Colombo museum). Then on to the first terrace, before the metal staircase to the top plateau. The museum has a really good CG fly through of how it would have looked. Top is very impressive, with palace ruins, bathing pools and terraces. We spent about an hour at the top wandering around. Not too busy. As we headed down the tour buses had started to arrive, so queues had formed on the climb up. Good time to meander through the gardens and terraces, which were quiet. We took a detour and walked to Pidurangala rock. This was a nice climb up with a scramble section just at the top. Fantastic views and big flattish rock area to sit and watch the crowds on Lion Rock. Not busy at all. Down and walked back to go round the museum. Very good trip and well worth the entrance fee.

Amazing climb and view at the top. Definitely worth it. May be a bit difficult depending on what your exercise tolerance is like but many spots for frequent breaks. We had a guide with us and that made us understand the history a lot better. But regardless it is very picturesque. Would recommend climbing early before it gets too hot!

We had a great time on this very easy hike.  The path is very clearly laid out and there are plenty of tour guides to help you if you would like a guided tour.  It took us about 2 hours to go up and down but we were moving quickly as it was obvious rain was coming and because it had rained the first half of the day there were few people compared to usual.  A must do when in Sri Lanka, the view is breathtaking!

We went here early in the morning with our Tour guide. Mostly due to the heat later in the day but also by the time we were leaving it was getting extremely busy. So worth keeping this in mind, this is also not peak season either. The climb even in the early stages is not for faint hearted. I wouldn’t have a great head for heights and found even the early parts high for my liking. I did climb as far as the claws but didn’t wish to go any higher. Lovely views from the ground and from as far as I went. I was happy I went up as high as I did. Give it go even to that part, as I made it higher on Sigiriya then I did on the great wall of China!
Yes it cost more to see this site, but the history and amazing ruins are worth it.  Not hard at all to climb and yes go early.  We truly enjoyed this Unesco site.

I was so happy to make it to the top, amazing views, we chose to leave early morning and even then it was very hot. We had a lovely sunny clear day,  I'd been ill for two days before, so with dehydration liquid off we went! I had travelled all this way so I was determined to do it. I just took about ten steps at a time had a rest and continued. Hundreds of steps but so worth it. Definitely do it.

Really expansive and well maintained monument. The museum is good, and will give you a nice history of the place. Really interesting. Anyone for 1500 yr old erotic wall art? And its really good! The gardens were beautiful. The monkeys hilarious. And the top; breathtaking. So happy we didn’t just do the cheaper little Lion Rock, as some people advised. We spent 4hrs here. Also don’t bother with Dambulla cave temple. Bit underwhelming after Sigiriya.
Very popular tourist spot! A bit on the expensive side to hike up. Skip if you are on budget and hike up pidurangala rock instead.

The view from the top was absolutely out of this world, so beautiful. But I honestly didn’t feel safe on the way up. There were so many people on the shoddily welded stairways (my partner is a welder) that I did not enjoy the experience as much as I could of, should of. If there were just a few people at a time going up it wouldn’t have been an issue but there were literally hundreds! I would have rather have queued at the bottom for longer, rather than actually queuing on the metal staircase high above the ground. Don’t take food with you unless it’s in a rucksack, I saw monkeys attack a japanese guy as he had a pink plastic bag with food in. It is worth doing it for the views though. Once you’re at the top, it’s magical.

Fairly strenuous walk, part of which is on metal stairways. Start walk by 7.30 am to avoid queues, crowds and heat! The palace is now ruins but would have been extensive in its day. Make sure you walk on the top and see the carved out swimming pool. At US $30 each it is a bit pricey, but That path needs a lot of maintenance , and the whole site is unique.

This is a great place. I can only imagine what it was like when this city was inhabited. Go as early in the morning as you can. The later you go, the hotter it will be, and the more people will be there. We were there during school holidays, and the lines were almost ridiculous. But it's well worth it. The climb itself is really not such a big deal for the reasonably fit. The views are spectacular, and some of the details are quite interesting.

To be honest, it was a bit underwhelming. The climb isn't actually that bad, and I'm very unfit, but the vertigo was a shock, and the views were fairly rubbish (fog/smog? Not clear anyway). That being said, the ruins are cool and using your imagination to comprehend what life was like way up here back in the day is fun. Tips: Stay IN Sigirya. It's a lovely bushy area, and you're going to want to get up early to arrive at the gates by 7am. We stayed near the caves (which btw are completely awesome) and the extra bit of sleep by staying closer would have been nice. Another option, though, is not to worry about the 7am thing, it wasn't that hot (there's a tree or two on top) and it actually looked like the crowds going up when we were going down were having a blast! Lots of laugher and whining and making jokes across all cultures. Slower and crowded-yes- but we thought it might have been fun actually, and a good distraction from the heights. Also this isn't a 'sacred' place. Shorts n singlet/tshirt, and a bit of talking is fine. You have to almost fend off the guys waiting to 'help' on the stairs (who then demand silly money at the top). If you need help, negotiate before. Also, you go out a different way that you come in, which means we didn't get to look around the gardens after. You could get back down there, but you won't feel like going down and then up again to the foreigner car park. If you arrive by bus in Dambulla, you can leave smallish bags at the caves- so go straight there, 200LKR tuk tuk. Then go to your accommodation in Sigirya in the evening, and ask them to arrange dinner in advance. I reckon bicycle would be a bit rough after a big climb. But you don't need a driver to wait for you. We had our tuk tuk, pre-arranged, 2000LKR pick up from Dambulla and drop back at the bus after a no time-limit wait (there's usually a time limit and you will need minimum 3 hours even just going up and back) but I think the shuttle bus would be fine, cheap, and no worrying about time. We didn't know you couldn't easily go back down to the gardens, and has planned on ambling around there after, so bugger the 7am start and look around before you go up. Lastly, I'd suggest do a bit more reading than the guide book so you can get a feel for what you're experiencing or book a quality guide. I'll be doing my reading tonight!

A massive achievement for me to climb this , it was well worth it for the view aswell as the historical aspect. If your nervous with heights or health and safety conscious, this climb probably isn’t for you, but it’s one of the must do’s in Sri Lanka, but not in flip flops.

I'm so glad that we decided to include climbing the Sigiriya Lion Rock to our itinerary to our trip. It's a tough 1200 steps to the top of the rock, especially if you're not used to climbing steps. That said, the experience is absolutely worth it. The ruins and views from the top had us amazed. A definite 'don't miss' of a Lankan adventure, especially if history and ruins are your thing.

Make sure you arrive at 7 am to avoid queues and human traffic jams on the narrow stairs up .The climb itself will be difficult if you are unfit .For me it was about half an hour up and I stayed about half an hour at the summit and 20mins down and then a visit to the museum . But I saw some people really struggling and it was obviously a challenge . Don’t bother with guides . You can get info from the Museum after .Its expensive enough as it is as foreign tourists are expected to pay for the upkeep and keep it a UNESCO site  . Something like 4500 RS each to gain entry as it is . Watch out for the boulders , frescos and of course the glorious early morning views from the top . Take some good shoes and water with you . In my opinion it’s not that difficult to climb but it really depends on your fitness level .Also look out for a great elephant ride when you finally get down and some sweet rotis.

Our original plans in Sri Lanka did not include going here, but a good friend really recommended coming to Sigiriya to go to Lion Rock, so we changed our plans. For us, that was a mistake. We were here in December which is super high season as it is also Sri Lankan holidays. While we enjoyed the view from the top, the journey itself was pretty frustrating as we were literally in a sea of people from the first set of stairs until we got to the top of the steel spiral staircase, and once you commit  it is really hard to turn back. after we got through that part, it was pretty smooth sailing and the way down was super quick. The most frustrating part was during the second part to the summit - my wife is afraid of heights and was having a "moment" when I was ahead with the kids. A kind Sri Lankan man offered to take her hand and help her get to the top as it is one-way traffic only. Once they got to the top, the man promptly asked for money for his "service". After we spent some time at the top, we headed back down and saw the same man in the same place waiting for the next vertigo-stricken tourist. I am all for people looking for ways to make a living, but I would just rather have any conversation about fees upfront.

The ticket includes the vist of Sigiriya rock and the museum. They accept cash only (USD or rupees). Climb the rock first, then enjoy the nice air conditioning in the museum. After reading a lot of comments,  we decided to start early at 7am. To queue up buying tickets then walked to the starting point of the rock took us 30 minutes already. As it's early, the walk was smooth without any stopping. It wasn't too hot at that time. It was actually really nice climbing up the rock. We suggest you to wear hiking shoes as some steps are very slippery with sand on top. They are narrow steps in the beginning then it became metal stairs with handle which is safer. My five year old had no problem climbing up, just taking a bit longer time. When we arrived the top, we enjoyed the view and the ruins very much. We stayed at the top for quite a while then headed down at about 9:30 to 10. We saw long queue going up and not moving already. Great experience! A highlight for us in the whole trip.

There are lots of winding steps (approx. 1200) up to the complex at the top of Sigiriya Rock (visiting the wall paintings on the way) but they are well worth it. The sunset was truly spectacular with 360 degree views of stunning countryside. Recommended times to visit are early morning - for sunrise, and late afternoon for sunset. Also, the legend and history of the rock is fascinating.

My wfe and I recently visited here on a tour of the country. The guide books had warned us about the steep climbs and the drops so we were a little nervous, but it was not that bad really. We visited on a Sunday so there were a lot of locals there too - we had to queue at the bottom for aboyt an hour before we actually started climbing, but when we did things moved pretty quickly. Most of the way up consists of steep steps drilled into the rock - all felt pretty safe. If you get vertigo it may not be for you. The last part from the lions paw was the steepest and busiest but once at the top the views were amazing so I'm so glad we did it. If you are coming to this country, put this on your 'must do' list. Wear good walking shoes, take a hat and lots of water.

We headed up Lion's Rock early in the morning to beat the crowds and I'm glad we did as when we were heading back down there were huge crowds of tourists headed up! The steps and paths are very narrow so it can easily get congested and I imagine it could take you double the amount of time to get up if you were caught up with a tour bus load of people. Once you are at the top you can easily while away an hour looking at the views and exploring the palace ruins, oh, and it's a nice place to watch other tourists doing daft selfies right on the edge of sheer drops! We didn't bother with a guide as you didn't appear to really need one as it's clearly marked out with info points scattered around. The museum isn't the best but does offer you more info about the area and is worth stopping by if you have the time. The price is very steep for Sri Lanka but it is worth it as it's a very special place. If you are on a budget go to the other rock instead as it's only 5 USD! It's also awesome and worth going at Sunset for incredible 360 views of the area.
One visiting Sigiriya must climb the Sigiriya rock which once housed a palace. Climbing is tough but the top view is mesmerising
Completely exhausting climb. 1201 steps, but they are spread out. Well worth it. Wear  proper shoes/trainers. Flip flops won’t cut it. Amazing history. Great views.
Come early when the queues are shorter (still busy) and to avoid the heat. Bring plenty of water. Long climb to the top but lots of opportunity for breaks. View from the top is so worth it

A visit and climb to the Sigiriya rock is definitely worth experiencing. However, there are times when the nasty wasps are around, and if you are scared of them or allergic, you might want to think twice. I was there in Dec and luckily no wasps were seen. Our guide said that when it’s too wet and windy in the rainforest, they come to the rock for cover.
Fascinating history of this place, steep climb up the steps best done in the early morning cool. View at the top unbelievable. Do it.
Marvelous place to visit .i climbed 2 times.i had wonderful journey.everyone should go there.sigiriya was built by king kassapa.

You must go there! The rock is very special and the whole area too. Yes, bring bottle(s) of water and do the climb. The vistas from the top are really phantastic and pay you back the effort you invested before. I did not hire a local guide, but I guess they know more than your guidebook in terms of history and nice stories to tel. But I was pretty happy with just the experience of climbing up and enjoying the views over the surrounding landscape and the sumit in general.
Recommend you do this as a guided tour, the history is quite fascinating and otherwise you simply have no idea of what you're looking at.

Wow - this is really worth a visit. The climb up is a bit challenging, but only if you are really unfit, or can't do heights. The views are truly awesome and the history is quite fascinating. I would recommend a guided tour if you can, just so you understand what you are looking at.
Little bit of a hike. Take a lot of water. Start early in the morning to avoid the crowds. By 10 AM it gets way too crowded.

I visit Sigiriya during Christmas holidays and likely our guide told us to wake up very early so we started at 8.00. It has been hard to jump up to the rock in queue but later when we went down at 10.00 the queue was so long and blocked that some visitors decided turn back, despite having paid the ticket. The top is nice but with so many people little poetry

A must see for anyone visiting Sri Lanka! I recommend a guide that knows the history of this rock. You must have a bottle of water by  person because once you get in there you have no place to buy it. Avoid locals trying to help you climb the stairs because once on the rock they ask for money.

Excellent place to go if you really fancy - teetering on precariously built stairs - while trapped in a heaving mass of thousands of shoving people - surrounded by warning signs about not talking too loudly because you will encourage the plentiful bees / hornets to swarm all over you - while semi-rabid diseased local pooches get crushed underfoot by the crowds. Also. there are no signs or information. At all.

This is a World Heritage Site and has the queues to show for it. However it is also WAY more uncomfortable and dangerous than most other such sites. We arrived at 10:30 in the morning and it took c. 2.5 hours for a 45 minute climb. That is because we had to queue up the entire 1500 steps, moving a step at a time in the scorching sun, most of it without shade, and being pushed and poked by the rest of the crowd. Thankfully we had enough water, but I don’t know what happens to the unprepared - especially as there is no way back or out after c. 30 minutes, the crowds are simply to thick to turn back. The view and remains on top are of course spectacular, but you share them with upwards of 2,000 other visitors, angry bees, and rabid looking dogs (which may be hard to avoid due to the crowds). To sum up: this may be a supposed ‘Must-see’ in Sri Lanka, but I promise you’ll be happier avoiding it and just buying a postcard.
Nice place, visited with family but couldn’t climb to the top coz of too much crown due to local holidays. Museum was good though
Visited with family but couldn’t climb to the top coz of too much crown due to local holidays. View and museum is good though.

I think that a guide is essential for this 5th century citadel & also good walking shoes & lots of water! It is a wonderful sight this 180m rock rising up from beautifully laid out water gardens. Once you have walked through the water gardens then the climbing begins - 1121 steps in all! The boulder gardens, with about 20 rock shelters which were used by the monks since the 3rd century, and then the terrace gardens up to the Lion Platform. Just before the Lion Platform there is a sheltered rock face with frescoes of beautiful women from the 5th century and the Mirror Wall which is covered with rather illegible graffiti dating back to the 7th century where visitors recorded their impressions of Sigiriya. From the Lion Platform there are more stairs up to the remains of the palace at the top of the rock from which there are amazing views of the surrounding countryside.

I need to put a few things right about the Siguriya experience.  Firstly it is not a difficult climb as there are many places to stop along the way.  Secondly there is no real need to heave yourself out of bed at the crack of dawn to be there when the place opens at 7.30 - in fact going a bit later means you miss the bus loads queueing to get in and, in any case, the way up is on the Western side so is in the shade.  Thirdly it doesn't even approach precarious until the last 100m steep climb (on a very safe stairway) up to the summit.  I am no fitness freak but climbed it on my recent 71st birthday without any problem - there were even people going up with walking sticks.  So DO climb it if you are in the area, if you don't you'll be sorry you didn't.

If you are in Sri Lanka you have to visit Sigiriya. It is  must-see. You can spend hours exploring the many pools and rock shelters around the base of the fortress (keep an eye out for the monitor lizards running around). Then climb the stairs up the side of the cliff to see the rock paintings and the ruins at the top.  Really interesting place to visit!

1200 steps to reach the top. You will pass within the garden of the castle, then you will move upward towards the top of the rock. Middle way you will see the paintings for few wives for the king. Then you will reach the lion feet. Final stage is climbing to the top of sigriya (lion rock). The view is as if you are in an airplane, however nothing more than that. Worth visiting once only, since it is one of the main areas u need to visit in srilanka.
I recommend everyone to visit and take the memory of this place when you move home as this is tremendous world heritage.
Hiked to the top of Sigiriya Rock andIt was a really great day. At times, I did feel queasy but it was all worth it once we reached the top. The view from the top is amazing.

Such an amazing experience and well worth the pain of the climb! You could stop at Lion Rock and be very fulfilled or have a rest and power on to the top. The relics are amazing and the views are unparalleled. The reason for my 4 star review and not 5 stars was due to our guide. He was very friendly, great English and knowledgeable but the fact he basically guilted us into paying 5 times the going rate left a bitter taste in our mouth! 1000lk is fair and 3000lk is very generous.
Over priced and no meaningful control on the numbers than can be admitted to a restricted access to the facility. Eg, the gang way to the summit of the rock is one behind the other.
It's amazing what human kind can do :) The pictures on the wall, the surroundings, the view are just amazing

I went with a group of friends and we got a tour guide, I would definitely suggest you get a guide as although the place is still stunning just walking around it there is no information boards so you don't get any history or explanation to the different areas within, there are some very interesting stories. The climb itself was fine, there are 1,202 steps but they are broken out into sections so you don't really notice that much. There are some steps that are quite old and short so be carful! When we reached the top there are actually two more steps just in the middle of the grounds so make sure to get on it so you can stay you reached the top! The views at the top are just stunning and makes for some great pictures, unfortunately it was quite foggy when we climbed it but still enjoyed the views. There are bathrooms just at the entrance but none on the walk up so make sure to go before you start climbing. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes. Also go early in the morning as it gets very busy and it will take you a long time to reach to top with the crowds forming bottlenecks.

This was definitely a highlight of our trip to Kandy and Sri Lanka as a whole. I am not the fittest person and I found this quite easy. Go at your own pace; the stairs are only steep at the very end and the very beginning. Being at the top was wonderful, if not full of people. It is very overpriced but as we paid very little for transport (local bus) it worked out very well. On a side note there are a lot of dogs, including a Mum with pups up the top. I really wish I had food to give them, especially the Mum. So, if you’re an animal lover bring some dog friendly snacks!

We got quite disappointed with the place. I don’t mind the place being expensive since the territory is well kept and looked after. But it was quite unpleasant to see signs like “ticket office for foreigners”, “car park for foreigners”, “toilets for foreigners” and so on. We’re in the 21 century and segregation is still here. The way up took us around 50 min and didn’t seem to be very difficult. But I’d recommend to get there early in the morning before the heat. The view on the top is average, I personally didn’t find it impressive. If you’re a budget traveler, better hike a mountain closeby, the views are the same but you’ll save up a lot.

This is my second time, can spend days walking or relaxing. Breath taking views all around. It’s bit hard to get on but really worth when you reached to the top. Leave plenty of time for this journey (a day)

It was very busy when we got there, we were all standing in a line to climb the rock. Which took us maybe 3 hours, even though it's not a very high climb. But eventually it was worth it! I also recommend to climb the smaller mountain across Sigiriya to get a beautiful view of the lion rock with the lion profile. This is a very challenging climb so be careful!
A straight rock, tough climb, beautiful fresco and the view from the top. Very unique experience and an unique place as well.

Went with a group of friends. We had a local guide, which really added to the experience, as we learnt all about the interesting history of the place. There are so many little stories that we would have missed without a guide The view from the top is quite something and its  well worth climbing all the steps to be able to enjoy it
Had never heard of this before this trip but I’m not sure why. Ruins are spectacular! And a must see for anyone visiting Sri Lanka

Stunning views, interesting history, amazingly built in the past. This is on the UNESCO heritage list for a reason. Go early, preferably when they open a 7 am to avoid the crowd & the heat. Guides might be a bit fussy if you walk alone, but they will leave you if you already hired one. Also, that makes the trip FAR more interesting, and it is not too expensive either.

This is not a climb for the faint hearted. It starts out through the flat water gardens but quickly become a series of steep and often very uneven stone steps. However we managed it with two children aged 4 and 6, both of whom required some encouragement but are very fit and active children. Go all the way to the top for the most spectacular views. It took us 2 1/2 hours all up, including time at the fortress on the top, and we came down as the sun was setting. We ended torches to get down safely as the sun had set while we were on the top. Carry water, torches if you are going late afternoon and wear really sensible shoes.

This busy site was a highlight of our 4 week trip around SL. You have read about it on Lonly Planet no doubt so don't need to repeat here. It is busy in early Jan and a bit on an ant trail. However worth it. If you read up a little, in my view you don't need a guide and can then roam as you please.we climbed first, which is a little challenging for a couple the other side of 50, but very doable. Then we sauntered our way down following the signs to the foreigner's carpark as far as The Cobra cave and then headed to the Museum which is also worth a look.  Good facilities also regarding toilets.
It’s a hike, remember to take plenty of water.  Once at the top it’s well worth it.  The view is breathtaking.

Pending review We lost much time in queque for tickets. It was a very promising walking through the gardens to start of the climb. The steps are very narrow so those with big feet will be stepping sideways. Soon after going under the huge rocks all progress halted. Our group got bored standing around and decided take another route. It turned out to be the exit path and we were stopped further up and had to abandon the clinb.

We lost much time in queque for tickets. It was a very promising walking through the gardens to start of the climb. The steps are very narrow so those with big feet will be stepping sideways. Soon after going under the huge rocks all progress halted. Our group got bored standing around and decided take another route. It turned out to be the exit path and we were stopped further up and had to abandon the clinb.

The ticket prices for this are high for foreigners at just under 5000SLK. We climbed Pidurangala earlier in the day and decided to climb Lion Rock as well since the weather was perfect and there were no queues. The museum is informative. The climb is quite strenuous with stairs all the way to the top. There are amazing frescoes to view along the way. Once you get to the top it looks neglected and could do with some upkeep especially if the entrance fee is that high. However the historical significance is the reason you climb this - you are left with many questions like how did they build this over 2000 years ago and why did they build this. Why were the frescoes painted and what do they mean? There is an element of mystery and awe around achievements of ancient civilisations that you are left with after climbing this.

First the negs. The entrance price (7500 rupees for two) is extortionate for very little. The gardens are nice and quiet but nothing special. We went at 10am and the queue to go up the rock was mental.  Maybe an hour long and so unsafe.  People shoving past on corners with open sides, and really narrow steps.  It needs to be controlled as it's just rubbish. The positive, the view from the top is brilliant.  It's not that busy at the top (where do all these people go???) and the weather was perfect so we stayed up there for an hour. One advice.  There is a spiral black staircase up which takes five minutes up of pretty scary climb to see a mosaic painting that you see for ten seconds, can't photograph and can barely see, before coming down another staircase.  It's definitely not worth it and you can skip it by walking a straight path between the two

With a good tour guide you will discover what a fascinating and advanced society existed at the top of Sigiriya many years ago. The walk to the top is not difficult but a fear of heights appeared to be too much for a few tourists. Expensive yes but worth it.
Visited this site early to avoid the crowds. Long climb to the peak (1200 steps) for spectacular palace ruins and beautiful surrounding views. Well worth the effort.

Visited this site early to avoid crowds. Much to see and interesting climb to the peak for spectacular palace ruins and beautiful surrounding views. Well worth the effort. Needs more facilities and improved signage. Was becoming crowded on our way down about 9am.
Must visit in lanka! Get a tour guide. It’s amazing, the history is very cool. Try and go in the morning as early as possible. Less lines and is cooler.

As others have mentioned, fear of heights should not keep you from this amazing climb.  It's thousands and thousands of steps (over 7000 to the top!) but if you look at the steps, not an issue.  Best advice is to go as early as possible.  We got there around 8 am and it was already getting crowded (but no long queues ) and by the time we walked back down the queue was about 1-2 hour wait! It's amazing to think of the work that was done to create the palace.  This is definitely a must-see stop in Sri Lanka.

It truly is a marvel as to how a castle of that size with swimming pools were built on a solid rock that big! Good to see the steps to the top being done up with handrails and steel steps. Feels much safer now. The view from the top is simply breathtaking! Not to be missed on a trip to Sri Lanka

Sigriya rock is a can't miss destination in Sri Lanka.  The palace at the top of the rock is a wonder in itself and totally worth the hike up to see the ruins and the amazing view of the surrounding jungle.  The sprawling garden complex complete with ancient walls, moats and irrigation systems surrounding the rock is equally as impressive.  It feels similar to Machu Picchu but without the hype.  Go early so you don't have to wait in a long line to climb the stairs - we arrived at 8 am and there were only a few visitors, but by 9 am the site was crowded.

Locals pay 50 rupee foreigners pay 4600 rupee. Please explain where this money is going when thousands of foreign visitors come through the doors daily. This world heritage listed sight is very poor value for money. The whole site is mismanaged and a complete money grab again from the Sri Lankan government. The museum has major maintenance issues. Mould, electrical issues and lack of exhibits to name a few. The rock has very few facilities for the visitors. Toilets, bins and minimal signage for any information. What signage they do have is in very poor condition. The walkways upon the cliff side are not engineered to withstand extreme loads of people upon them at one time. It’s a disaster waiting to happen. I witnessed hundreds of people walking and clambering over the ancient footings and structures of this UNESCO listed site. How can this be? Shouldn’t this ancient and amazing history be preserved and protected for generations to come? Obviously not and a sad state of affairs.

The site is beautiful indeed however be prepared for an awful experience. Imagine a 3-4 hours commute in a London underground train full of sweaty people with absolutely no manners, smelling bad and not worried about pushing you down the stairs. This is Sigiriya! And the funniest part is that you, as a foreigner will pay $30 for it while the locals  pay almost nothing. Not worthy.
It was an amazing experience, we really liked it. But the thing is that people threw carbage. And screaming at shouting,

It seemed like the place to go when visiting SriLanka, but it was not. First of all, all sites in this country are very expensive. You might say for preservation but it is not, if you are local you pay nothing or maybe 20 times less. This system poses a real issue. The fact that it gets so crowded you cannot see or enjoy the site but you pay a lot for it. We went here really early in the morning and we started going up. But we did not get far. There were so many people that it took us 40 minutes to walk about 20 meters. We did not even start to climb the rock. What other rewiews do not say is that in this very long line, everybody is too close to you and too smelly. The locals have no issue to hug, touch or push you down the stairs.

Having read all the comments I did not sleep the night worrying about climbing 1200 steps and my fear of heights. I was wrong. When I arrived there were locals offering their services. Mine was called Chummie. I negotiated with him 10 euros to look after me and how he did. He guided me , supported me advised me and was fantastic. I went up every step to the top did not miss any caves and was down at the bottom in one hour and fifteen minutes. I was delighted by his help. He also carried my water bottle. He was so good that I doubled his money with no regrets. Yes I felt I had climbed Everest with a Sherpa and was proud of the achievement. Not dizzy spells a little apprehension but well worth the effort. A little advice to fellow sufferers look at the steps and internal rock face not below nor the gaps and you will be fine. Take a helper and he guides the best routes the way to go and the climb is over quicker than you thought.

Ignore people moaning about the cost, it's well worth the entry price (which at time of writing was USD30 which is converted to rupees). We went with our 6 year old and he loved it. Make the effort and start the climb at 7am. We left the hotel at 6am (Kandalama Hotel) and were about the 10th people to make it to the top. Earlier means it will be cooler and less crowded, making it much more enjoyable. We didn't rush but were back at the hotel at 9:30 in time for breakfast buffet. My 65 year old in-laws climbed the next day and made it no problem. Climb Sigiriya early for an unforgettable experience.

The whole idea of staying in Sigiriya was the idea of climbing up the  lion rock .Ideally December is the best time as the climate is somewhat better and though there are occasional showers , the heat quotient is low.The climb is a bit arduous but the view is worth it .There is also a mirror wall polished like a mirror with beautiful paintings before you reach the summit Fortunately the descend is a lot easier with a separate pathway so the uneven stairs can be avoided .Worth the view surely

Sigiriya was basically the deciding factor on choosing Sri Lanka as our trip, and i'm saddened to say that crowds completely ruined the experience. We went between Christmas and New Year's, which unfortunately as it turns out is a major week off, in a predominantly Buddhist country. So that was a learning opportunity. We arrived at 9AM and had a 25 minute wait for tickets. We then went directly to the line to the Apsara paintings, where we began what ended up as a 2+ hour line. This would've been bad enough, but Sri Lankan, Chinese andFrench tourists have no interest in waiting in line. The line cutting was absolutely atrocious, and almost resulted in a few fistfights. The Apsaras are interesting, as one would expect 1500+ year old paintings to be. And while they are likely objectively more interesting than the paintings at Tivanka Image House in Polonnaruwa, and certainly more robust than the later paintings at Bagan in Burma, they are in no way 2 hour wait better. Since you have such little time up there to take the experience in, I felt I had the same experience studying the photos in my travel guides. Once we left the Apsaras, it started to pour, which at least lessened the crowds. But climbing up a literal waterfall of a staircase to the top was a little suboptimal. I want to like Sigiriya much more, and I realize our experience was worse than most. But if you do during a busy period, our strongest possible recommendation is arriving the second they open.

We arrived at 7:30am, and despite being ahead of the main crowds this is definitely a tourist trap by definition. The climb is great but does require a moderate level of fitness and a head for heights. We couldn’t help but wonder who was monitoring the numbers on the metal structures hammered in to the rock in places (it seemed like no one). Overall we would absolutely recommend a visit, the paintings are well preserved, the information easily accessible and the view from the top is stunning, but we wished we’d arrived at sunrise to avoid the masses and the souvenir touts!
Very nicely maintained ancient site. Worth the visit and the entrance fee. Great views from the top!

This is not only an attraction for foreign but as well for local Sri Lankan tourist and yes, it is comparatively expensive ($30) but please, all you reviewers, stop complaining. This is money invested into maintaining this spectacular site. To avoid the crowds you want to come early, as early as the opening (which I believe is at 7h). The entire ‘hike’ to the top takes less than 1h and is an attraction in itself. The time we walked down we had a large crowd going up and that was even before 10h.

Interesting place and history, reminds me in some ways of Machu Picchu. During busy times it’s quite packed and due to the way you have to get up you may end up having to wait. Going early is one option, perhaps later in the day as well? Worth a visit.
This is a site really worth visiting if you're in Sri Lanka. It is historically interesting and visually awe-inspiring. You need to be relatively fit to climb all the stairs to the top.

What an experience and what an effort had to be put in on those days to create such a castle upon the rock, as well as the ingenuity that has been pit into, regarding the gardens and surroundings to provide the people living in the complex.

This climb is awesome, as is the rock and the palace complex at the top.  There's lot of information on line indicating a 2 hour climb, and perhaps that is what it takes if the place is extremely busy.  Get there early, avoid the crowds (and the full hear of the day) and it will take nowhere near that long.  Some parts of the climb are challenging, but my wife and two young kids (both under 12) made it up there with no issue in less than 45mins without rushing.

Astounding complex, culminating in a 'a palace in the sky' atop an enormous solitary rock. An intriguing history and a lovely site to wander and explore.  Monkeys abound and apparently there are a few crocs in the moats as well. The climb up the rock is incredible but could be considered strenuous, particularly in hot conditions.  The views alone from the top though are well worth it.  Technically your admittance ticket will allow you to leave the park precinct and re-enter on the same day (so you can sit out the heat of midday or go across the road and grab a cool drink), but we found we had to negotiate at the ticket window to make that happen.
By the time you go up there, you need to get back down.. but worth the view.. Would suggest start by afternoon to view the sunset

Start early before the sun & crowds get in to gear. Take a heap of water. Dont take food - unless you like monkeys on your back. Use reasonable footwear. Can be quite arduous. Rewarding experience (I found the gardens most pleasant).

Quite a challenging climb up many stairs to reach the very top but once up there the views are spectacular. The tourist tickets are now $30USD which is very high compared to the cost of everythibg else, our driver told us even the locals aren’t happy with this price for tourists as it is a lot of money. When you arrive men in the car park will offer to be your tour guide of the area for a price, we opted to just go alone. When you pay there is a museum to go around where you can learn all about the area and rock. Take plenty of water with you, the views at the top will make the climb worth while!

Really enjoyed the climb with a couple of my kids. Hired a guide to make sense of the archaeological side of the site. Glad we did as the guide brought the experience together. Started mid afternoon to avoid the heat of the day. The lower levels were shaded and very attractive with the moat and water pools. The climb isn’t physically challenging however the crowds on the steps up can detract from the experience. Despite the shuffle in to see the frescoes, they were worth seeing. Surprisingly the top wasn’t too crowded. The usual combo of dogs and monkeys were scattered over the rock. No sign of the wasps on the day we were there. Started the descent before sunset which we caught half way down. By the time we were at the bottom it was dark. Not much of a twilight in Sri Lanka!

This is not as difficult a climb as the previous reviews had lead us to believe. The metal staircases are much more structurally secure than some reports state. The ticket office opens at 7am & I would recommend getting there early. Entrance costs 4280LKR which is about £25 each adult. Payment can be made CASH ONLY in LKR or US$ - card payment was NOT accepted.The price includes the gardens, museum and obviously the climbing of the rock. If you get in early, visit the museum first as it is located just to the right of the ticket office. This is air conditioned and gives lots of history and archeological detail regarding this site. There are also clean, flushing toilets. The gardens with their ruins are worth exploring. Recommend that you take plenty of water & make an earlier, cooler ascent as this is easier. There are approximately 1200 steps and some fitness is necessary. Also having a head for heights does help although the climb is perfectly safe even if you just take it slowly. This was our 3rd trip to Sri Lanka and the journey to get to this revered place is certainly worth the effort!

You need to do a lot of stair climbing to reach the top of the rock and it's totally worth the view. Please go either early morning or to catch the sunset. Otherwise it can be too hot. Be mindful that the ticket counter closes at 5pm while you can stay inside till 6.30pm. There is a museum and shopping centre too which is very nice. So budget sole time for that as well on your visit. SAARC countries get discount, so don't forget to bring your passport along. It's about 2325 LKR for a SAARC passport holder.

This is a wonderfully preserved site and a popular tourist destination. Start early, carry drinking water and an energy bar or 2. Not for the very unfit or those with dodgy knees. Very well marked and bounded path with spiral staircase in upward journey. Go all the way to the top for spectacular views. Worth a visit.

Understand the richness in all activities of the ancient Sri Lanka and the heritage of Ceylon and this is a world heritage site too, ancient irrigation systems that pump water to the top and the painting of angles and few things that can confuse you and the top of the rock how they did there pool party
You must visit to see and believe, it's has a great history and marvelous engineering, wonder how all was made possible with very little knowledge and facilities
Excellent mix of nature and history. May be a tough climb for small children and very elderly. Forgotten visors have a separate car park and a demarcated route towards the end of the descent

As we only brought local currency, we ended up paying LKR 4,650 which was slightly higher than today's exchange rates.  However, the USD I kept at home would have gotten me a better deal!  Nevermind, the entrance fees from tourists go towards the upkeep of this incredible site. I hesitated going up the 1,200 steps because I don't like heights.  However, I found that because most steps are solid marble/ limestone/ modern day tiles and flanked on either side by high walls, I couldn't see down below.  Towards the top, it was steel staircase - refer to attached photo - where I could view the sheer drop of the rock face on the side.  That was my cue to steel myself, look up, and practise mental toughness! Thankfully the climb down revealed no gaps in view between the stairs, so I was fine.  Secondly, as there were railings on either side for me to hold, resulting in zero knee problems. Tip #1:  go before 5pm, that's when the ticket counter closes.  You'll be one of the last batches with a very small crowd.  Most helpful when slowly making your descend.  You can then take your time. Tip #2:  sunset in Jan is around 6pm.  So time yourself to reach up before then.. Tip #3:  there are lots of guides around who will help with history of the place, taking photos for you, and (more importantly for me!) an arm to hold onto nearing the bottom of the steps with an absence of railings to hold onto. Note:   our driver said the guide costs USD 20 per person.  When we spoke separately with the guide he charged us only USD10 per person.
at 8 o clock was a long queue at the box office. Next stop and waiting at entrance and from there on is queuing. Its totally overcrowded and overpriced.

if you are the person who enjoys a bit of hiking with historic interest then this place is a must visit. to reach to the top one has to climb around 1300 steps, they are uneven steps, so good grip shoes are mandatory. wear comfortable clothes. after around 500 steps u will reach to a place where all ages old paintings are seen on the wall of these big rocks. all over seilanka has art based on this sigiria paintings which were originally done here on the inside of the walls of these giant rock. at around 800 steps u will reach a plateau from where one can see the view all around. many people do not climb beyond thys as further climbing will only show u higher view from the top of the rock but its worth it. after 800 steps the climbing is only on man made iron stairs and is very crowded with people as its very narrow. once u come down there wud be few toyrists shops down to enjoy the art and culture of sigiria and srilanka... they r very small over priced shops so negotiate hard. me and my family totally enjoyed it more from the hiking perspective and we hired the guide who took has from the different route, dont know if there are many ways to climb up.

Get there early (before 8am), grab a ticket, experience the beauty of the landscape and the ingenuity of man. Yes it's overpriced, yes it can be crowded but the experience far exceeds any negative. Simply a must see in the world.

First of all there is an entrance fee to this visit the park of 4500 LKR for foreigner and 2500 LKR for SAARC national.  There are around 1200 steps to climb.  This may take anywhere from 1-2 hours based on the crowd there.  people who do not want to climb, there are the tuk tuk guys outside the park who charge exorbitant money to take you around the periphery to view the rock from different angle.

Wonderful experience. Get there early (ticket office opens at 7:00) to beat the crowd and the heat and don’t be afraid pf the amount of steps: there are many resting and viewing spots. Even I managed, and I am very unfit! Bring water and your camera. Many chances for nature lovers: banyan trees, giant squirrels, birds of all sorts and monitor lizards

We arrived early in the morning and it was crazy busy even at 7am. The climb to the top is steep and not for the faint hearted. Incredible history and amazing views as well as impressive hydro technology from several centuries ago.

We came when the park opened at 7.30 and the queue for tickets took just 10 minutes. The first part of the climb is on stone steps, some had sand on them. The last part, on the iron steps is quite steep, but there are so many people that is slowing you down so this was hardly strenuous. The view on top is fantastic!

I went at 10am on Christmas weekend and there were thousands of people there. What should have taken 30 minutes took 2.5 hours to get to the top - in the sun.  There were so many people that I would take 1 tiny step, wait 1 minute, take another tiny step, etc. It was a complete traffic jam and it was blazing hot!  That said the frescoes part way up were great and the temple ruins and the view at the top were worth it.  If I ever come again I will get there EARLY in the morning to avoid the heat and the crowds. I will never come at 10am on a holiday weekend again though. Bring a bottle of water as there is nothing available.

This is a place where one needs a guide to explain the history. Great climb for good views and seeing the historic remains. But still do not see the 'Lion' in Lion Rock except those claws at the bottom of the Rock. More needs to be done to preserve the historical monument as too much human interference has wiped out its value. Best view is from the top of the Rock and the Mirror Wall. The relevant authorities should put out warning signs for those who are not fit not to climb because of health reason as it can be very demanding and steep. I have seen visitors wearing high heels climbing the stairs and some elderly stopping frequently for rest. Can't imagine when an emergency arises and how they evacuate from the steep climbs. Otherwise a must visit place to soak in the ruins and treasures.

Definitely recommend getting a tour guide for this climb as they know so much. So incredible to hear about the early engineering of the palaces and see the remaining drawings on the walls. Be prepared to really sweat and get out of breath! Take plenty of water and rest when you can. I was nervous about the stairs and how high it was but it strangely didn’t feel scary. Amazing views once you get to the top. It takes about 2 hours to climb.
Sigiriya rock is one of the most interesting place to visit in Sri Lanka. The art which has made in the cave are stunning. The location & ambiance is brilliant

If you don’t care about the facade DO NOT WAIT in the outrageous line for an hour in the Blazing sun. Take the path to the left and skip that bit and go right to the paws. That will save you 1.5 hrs!! Fantastic view st the top but not worth waiting in 2 hr line to see the wall.
Not so hard as people say although its 1 hour plus up. All stairs and weird metal wrap around. Great views of area.

This rock is amazing, you walk through the water garden first, up to the stairs where you go to see the fresco's in the cave, then you continue up to the top where you have a magnificent view of the surrounding area. Trying to imagine what it must have been like for the king to live there. Go EARLY aka 7am in the morning other wise it will take you hours to get up there, this place gets crowded.

Get a good guide to tell you the story behind the fortress and why it is here before visiting and then get them to accompany you through the site and the whole visit.  A unique place that is unforgettable.  You do need a head for heights and no fear of stone staircases but the experience and view from the top is unlike anywhere else.
Nice view and climb. Be carefull of bees season. Take water with you and prep for sweating. Must see

We visited sigiriya during December holidays of 2017. Sigiriya is generally a green place. We reach the lion rock at 3.30 pm and started our climb around 4 types. There are roughly 600 steps. It was crowded which slowed down our climb. My kids 5 yr and 8 yrs old climbed easily. We carried water and some light snacks with us. You will not get anything on your way. View from top is breathtaking. If you can not do the climb then you can spend your time in the garden and museum. Quite and green place for elders to spend some time.

#1 - start early. We did (begrudgingly, because we like our holiday sleep ins) but we were so glad that we beat the heat and the crowds. We started our climb around 8 am, and even then had sweat pouring off us. #2 - take water and a small snack for the top. Wear comfy shoes and clothing, and a hat is a must. #3 - take your rubbish with you. It’s  world heritage site and it was sad to see the top littered with empty plastic bottles. There were some men employed to pick up but it really is up to each visitor to take their rubbish with them. The only problem was that the Asian tourists kept to the left side of the path, the Europeans went to the right and no one knew which way to go. Some signs to remind our European friends to stay on the left would be much appreciated! It was well worth the trek. It’s not a difficult climb, especially if you take the time to enjoy the stunning views.

Sigiriya refuses to reveal its secrets easily, and you'll have to climb a series of vertiginous staircases attached to sheer walls to reach the top. On the way you'll pass a series of quite remarkable frescoes and a pair of colossal lion's paws carved into the bedrock. The surrounding landscape – lily-pad-covered moats, water gardens and cave shrines – only add to Sigiriya's rock-star appeal.
Make sure you are fit enough to go up 2000+ steep stairs all the way up the rock.or else you might end up cursing for trying.foreigners entrance fee is USD30 adults, kids USD15.

We were very apprehensive about visiting (because we were travelling with two kids - 5 and 2 year old). Our 5 year old climbed the whole way without incident. The 2 year old also climbed 90% on her own. The climb is steep but not as arduous as the reviews make it sound. Great views from the top (especially on a clear day).

Although generally it is quite a nice attraction to visit the amount of self-employed guides who are trying to force you to buy a service from them is too much... We actually did "hire" one but it did not stop from the other guys approaching and approaching us on the stairs as you walk up (especially my spouse - to be frank)... I needed to become more assertive and protective of her to refuse them... This was too rude and too much.. and this is all despite purchasing tickets that are close to 30 USD per person to visit mostly ruins.... This hassle truly ruins the experience you could get from the views and the place...

A rather un-known place for many. But deserves to be at the top league. Interesting (hi-) story and again: we are lucka to experience the work of med Kings/mad persons. A very special place, requiring some travel-planning and support to get there.

We visited the site on a Saturday and it was packed with Chinese groups. If our guide did not show us an alternative way we could have spent hours queuing in the sun. But let’s be honest once you reach the top of the rock you can only be grateful to have waited and climbed that high for such a beautiful view. Just to imagine that the palace was built in the 5th century still amazes me.

As a lot of other reviews have mentioned, this is challenging climb due the scale of the climb, the unevenness/narrowness of the stairs, the lack of shade, the crowds and mostly the heat/humidity.....Go early when its coolest. Take water....lots of it to replace what you sweat out (which will be a lot!!) Take your time and enjoy the climb and take in the spectacular site. Rest often and enjoy your own achievement of getting to the top.
Worth the climb and views but this attraction is very crowded. The rock paintings are great and have never been restored. The climb is worth the effort.

This climb is worth the effort to see the beautiful views of the area. It is 1800 steps but it is not too tough to climb.  The first section before the summit has slippery steps and not many hand rails, so wear suitable foot ware. Once you reach the summit the steps are much better and the climb is not so bad. The crowds make the climb difficult as some people stop on the stairs to rest and it is hard to get around them. Once you have taken photos at the top, be prepared for a long wait to climb back down. It is rewarding to make it to the top.

This is a huge climb with over 1000 steps. It is divided up into three sections and we did manage to make it to the top. After the first third there are excellent wall paintings but no photos allowed.. At the two thirds mark there is the lions gate and at the top you are rewarded with great views. Suggest an early start as it can get very hot. Carry water!
Impressive but slightly spoiled by the poor quality museum and the strong smell of urine half way up

First tip go early in the morning - be there by 7:00am. Second tip don't let anyone help you climb otherwise expect to pay. Third tip you have spent all this money getting here and on accomodation just spend the extra few dollars to get into the sight and climb the rock! Not the cheap rock. Great views and if you get a good guide it will be money well spent.

I would have given this a five star but we arrived during the public holiday and were stuck in the queue getting to the top and going down as well for hours. However do not let that deter you. Once you get to the top the views are amazing. This will give Michu Picchu a run for its money. If you do visit the during the public holidays make sure you get there as early as possible to avoid the queues.

Sigiriya is situated at half hour drive from Dambulla. It takes around 4-5 hr bus journey from Colombo to reach. The place used to be a king’s castle and is in shape of a lion built on a hill. It will involve around 90-120 minute climb to reach to the top. Better to start the ascent early in the morning as the sun 🌞 gets into full action mode later in the day. Also it is recommended to carry your own water bottles for the ascent. Some prefer to stay overnight. We however returned the same day to Colombo due to time constraints. Had a wonderful time visiting the place. Must visit world heritage site!!

Visited Sigiriya on 24th December, first it took more than 30 minuets to find a vacant slot to park the vehicle. After about a 1 km walk from the car park (for locals) (foreigners have a shorter distance to walk) to the entrance over the water lake. Then found the walkway to the top was tightly packed and not moving at all(took about 1/2 hr to move few meters), as we had other plans for the evening decided to turn back before even reaching the mirror wall. Strongly recommend to avoid public holiday long weekends, if you can visit on a week day it will save you a lot of time. Best time to climb will be early morning between 6-9 am and evenings from 3-5 pm when the heat of the sun low. Visiting the museum is a must. A must visit attraction if you are a foreigner who like to learn the engineering knowledge and art of ancient Sri Lankan's.

It's a must do...entry fee is expensive but worth a climb. Was great to see some young children climbing and asking "who made the rock"!! It was an awesome feeling to get to the to.  The grounds are beautiful, very well kept anf tidy.

Although we ended up going to the Lion Rock on a public holiday- when the place was crowd, it was a terrific experience. Whilst the climb was slightly challenging for the young ones, they too loved the adventure. It was by far amongst the best historical sites I have visited in SL. Highly recommend picking a guide for the tour to ensure you do’t miss out on the historical significance of various elements on the site.

Please start early to get the best view. We reached there at 6 in the morning and on our way back the place was completely crowded. A must watch in Sigiriya. Have 2-3 hours to reach to the top. Also, Indians get discount on entry fee, so carry your passport.
The climbing, the art work, ruins of palace atop the rock, the fog, view from the top, all were fantastic. Great fun with the entire stuff was awesome.

What's good The iconic symbol of Sri Lanka is an amazing set of landscape, wall paintings and a somewhat well preserved trek. Sigiriya Lion Rock is a climb that everyone must do if they are visiting Sri Lanka. What's not good The access road is long for walkers going around the moat and they ask you to pay for the museum visit which most are not interested in. What to do Take the climb early morning. Enjoy different levels till you reach the top which itself has different levels. Enjoy the view.

This was by far one of my favourite places to visit during our trip to Sri Lanka, and I think this should be on everyone's list to see if they are in the area/visiting the country. Don't let the size of it fool you. Unlike Table Mountain which is hard to climb on even the easiest of trails, work has been done to make climbing Sigiriya Rock accessible to almost everyone. There are stairs and railings all along the way. It isn't a vertical climb the entire time, and there are rest sites for people to sit and relax if they need a breather. The views from the top are amazing, however as there is almost no shade I would recommend climbing in the early morning to avoid getting too sunburnt or dehydrated during your visit. Also if you go in the morning you avoid the crowds that descend late morning/early afternoon.

What a day!! This is an absolute must do!! Climbing more that 1200 steps to the top of the Sigiriya World heritage site. Very helpful guides, secure and well arranged course up the mountain. One gets the most beautiful views all the way to the top of this site. It is clean, safe and no-one gets rushed. Everybody, young and old, climbs this mountain at their own pace. Highly recommended!!

I see that many people compare Pidurangala and Lion Rock - in my opinion, the only thing they really have in common is that they are both rocks :) People don’t climb the Lion Rock primarily for the magnificent view, but for its historical and cultural importance. The ticket is ridiculously expensive - those reviewers who compare it to Angkor Wat ticket should remember that this is basically a 2-hours thing while you need at least a couple of days to explore everything Angkor Wat has to offer. It seems like at least a part of that money is  well invested as the gardens at the bottom are immaculate, the museum is informative and everything is well maintained. I wish the film they show you in the museum had subtitles as it was impossible to hear anything. I guess they also need the money to pay all the staff - we had three guys checking our tickets on one counter: one to take them and inspect them, the second one to stamp them and the third one to hand them back to us :) The climb wasn’t very difficult for us but we had to watch our steps as it was very windy and it was raining heavily. There were quite a few visitors, despite the very bad weather. I guess that this would be a difficult climb only for old or very unfit people. Kids of all ages should be ok if they don’t mind walking. I would recommend doing it on a clear day in order to enjoy the view but not when it’s very hot as that would make the climb significantly more difficult. If you have fear of heights, this is not a place for you. There are two locations which could make you go back: one is the spiral staircase leading to the famous frescoes and the other one is the long metal staircase from the Lion’s Gate to the top. If you don’t fear the heights, the view is breathtaking, unless it’s cloudy like it was for us. All in all - beautiful but overpriced, which has by now become a mantra for Sri Lankan tourism.

I have visited for the second time this beautiful place which I highly suggest to visit. A huge monolite over which you can visit a very old royal palace (also UNESCO recognised its value and importance).

It is a long way to the top but you get rewarded with an astonishing view. Safety feels ok but it is nothing for the ones afraid of heights as you walk on small metal pathways connected to the rock. We arrived around 9:00 and there was a lot of people but not enough to form a queue. You need cash but there is an ATM outside the museum. Price is expensive for foreigners which initially irritated us as locals go almost for free. A lot of monkeys joins you all the way up. When we came down there was a lot of people and long line to start climbing whe rock. Some people turned around disappointed. So arrive early!

The Citadel of Sigiriya, The entry fee for tourists is about 30$ plus an extra $20 with a guide. The entrance fees are compare to the fees that the locals pay, extremely expensive. (i agree with the concept, that tourist has to pay more but $4 and $30 is a big difference and ridiculous). unfortunately the frescoes and the ruins are not well kept therefore not much to see. What’s left is,the climb and the view (the rock itself and the carvings are interesting), which is nice (if you’re not afraid of heights).

Sigiriya rock was on my bucket list because the 1st time I read about it and saw the photos, I was really amazed by the beauty and manmade effort to have created such a fortress and legacy. Our driver dropped us on the entrance side where we easily found a guide at reasonable price and seemingly good knowledge. I do suggest a guide if you are not very familiar with the history, because otherwise many of the interesting facts hidden in the architecture and rituals might be lost from your full experience. Either way I suggest you read up a little beforehand, which will help to know what to look for and expect. The trip was a complete experience of awe at the sheer effort it must have taken to create Sigirye and the beauty it must have displayed when it was in full use. The climb to the top is relatively easy and there is a good resting opportunity at the lion entrance. You dont need hiking shoes and many people wear only sandals. The view from the top is of course absolutely magnificent and you can simply imagine what it must have been to live up there (even without all the concubines :-)). Definitely my best experience from this 1st short trip to Sri Lanka and a trip I can highly recommend (including the picturesque drive from Colombo).

Theres not much more I could add to the reviews on here. When you factor in the price, you cannot give this place 5 stars. But, it is a place to visit none the less. Your pace around this will depend upon the other people on the steps you are on as some of the staircases are single file. If I could clarify: Many older people visit, and I marvelled at them climbing the stairs to the top but it can your force your pace When it comes to guides- that's up to you. We didn't take one and it didn't ruin our enjoyment - lonely planet was enough. This is one to do and remember - it is more than a tick box exercise.
A really interesting and visually stunning place to visit. Good to have a guide to get the most out of the walk.
Best challenge ever, very high about 350 metter hight and more than 1200 srairs which means 100 floor, and the view from up there is amazing you should try

At first you're gonna balk at the entrance fee. They charge 4,600 rupees (equivalent to 30 USD), which is outrageous considering the fact that locals only pay 60 Rupees. But come to think of it, that's about on par or even cheaper compared to the entrance fees to ancient sites in other countries (for instance, the entrance to Machu Picchu in Peru costs 50 USD, and Angkor Wat is almost 40 USD these days). It only seems really expensive because everything else in Sri Lanka is incredibly cheap! If you want to learn about the country's history and culture, then this site is a must visit. Some parts show a lot of wear and tear, though many areas remain remarkably preserved. Plus the view on top is amazing. It's not that hard to climb all the way up, took me about 30 minutes. And I saw several elderly people having no problem at all. Now you are gonna hear a lot of fellow travelers saying you should climb Pidurangala instead, which is another rock close to Sigiriya. They will say it's the same, only way cheaper (you only pay 500 Rupees). Well if it's the view you're after, then I agree it's quite similar... though I have to say you'd still get better views on top of Lion Rock since this rock obstructs some of the view from Pidurangala. But if you're after history and culture, you won't get much in Pidurangala. There's a reason why the Sri Lankan government doesn't charge much for climbing that other rock, and there's a reason why they charge so much for this one. 30 bucks may seem excessive for a budget traveler, but once you've reached the top you'd realize that it's totally worth spending that amount of money.

Amazing view and so huge, I wonder the  King  must have been one determined and stubborn ruler to climb up this huge rock to build his fortress. It was worth the climb, we climbed in the late evening just before it got dark, we were lucky to have that beautiful view from the top the rocks,, felt like conquered the world once i reached the top

Visiting this citadel is expensive for foreigners, 4650 rupees, but it is a site not to be missed!  An enormous achievement in construction. The Museum at the base gives a background to the site, archival photos and replicas of the frescoes, artifacts, plus a good video. Worth visiting beforehand. The gardens - water, boulder and terraces - are immaculate and make a wonderful approach to the towering rock that dominates the countryside. The steps up are quite a challenge!  But it's worth all the effort!!!  The ruins at the top and the views are simply STUNNING.  An indelible memory of Sri Lanka's heart!

I'm not really all that big on history and can pretty much guarentee that I'll forget whatever I learn or am told within the hour. But for a morning/afternoon surrounded by stunning scenery, ancient monuments, Buddhist monks, glorious sunshine and views to die for, I can't think of many other places  I'd like to have been, so for that reason alone, I loved Sigiriya.

There is a lot of history behind Sigiriya - Lion Rock and it is worth getting a tour guide to give you the the background on how the Lion Rock came to be. The hike up is good for beginners and is doable. People can take their time and have take picture along most of the way. But it is better to arrive early in the morning before 9am as it gets too hot during the day.

The national park service allows (they check tickets) local guides who extort money from mobility impaired tourists for their assistance. This was the worst interpersonal experience we had in SL, which was otherwise wonderful.

The citadel is a remarkable geologic and cultural spot. The fee is higher than most national park fees, but since it is a 'must see' all the foreign tourist (e.g. GF and I) pony up the cash. The walk to the summit is1200+ steps with a staircase on the steepest parts. The rest of the stone steps have no guardrails nor hand holds which was a notable absence on the rainy day we toured there. That's the good news. The bad an inexcusable part is the that the SL national park service allows a large number of yellow shirted locals to prey on vulnerable travelers by offering (forcing) their services to 'assist' on anyone elderly or mobility impaired. I has a recent knee operation and so was moving slow when two guys - Banda and Bishu, a father/son team- attached themselves to me and when I decided to forgo anything past the first set of set and head back to the museum assured me there was an easy path 'just up a ahead' and proceeded to direct me to a circuitous route than led to a large series of wet stone steps around mid-portion of the rock. When we were at a particularly treacherous portion of the path, these two stopped and demanded money to allow me to continue. I said I'd be fine, but they essentially blocked my path saying I owed them for their services rendered. I offered $10/each but they all but grabbed my wallet and kept saying they needed more. Finally when I was worried I might 'accidentially" fall they ended up with $30 each, and even then asked for an extra $10 for 'drinks'.

It was a challenging visit and one should climb sigiriya summit at least once in his life. The technology used to build the castle on this massive rock is unbelievable. It's a challange for us even to climb on to it.

The most famous of the two rocks. Entrance fees are expensive – 5.000 – compared to only 500 at the nearby rock, which is just as interesting and beautiful. You walk up the side of the mountain on a staircase. Go and watch sunset from the top.
Went there on our second day in the region. As others have said, it’s a bit pricy but it’s worth it. It’s quite a hike so remember to bring water. The view from up there is fantastic

Only when you reach here that you realise how seriously Sri Lanka takes it tourism. You find a very well managed Heritage where you can go and enjoy the historical remains of a castle which are a site to see. The climb include around 1200 steps of different size and shape and it is advisable to start the climb early in morning as the the more the sun tougher becomes the climb. Also it is more fun to go with a guide who then explains the architecture on the way. Tickets are around 4700 SL Rupee for foreigners and you get 50% discount if you are from SAARC countries.

The entrance for the rock is 4500rp, which includes the ticket to the attraction and the museum. The climb is not easy, its a little long and steep. For those with height phobias i suggest you thin twice cos some of stairs overlooks the steep slopes. Also there are warnings for wasp attacks and monkey attacks there, so be mindful of your volume and try not to be carrying any food with you during the climb. Sunset from the rock can be seen unless it gets misty (which half the time it is according to the guide) but still worth the view!

Climbing Sigiriya Rock was a highlight of this trip. The climb in the early stages includes ancient rock paintings and amazing views. Then as it becomes more difficult and steep there is a place to rest and ponder the dramatic final part of the climb. Whilst doing this you can take in the wonderful views across this beautiful land and marvel at how this was engineered so many years ago. Our final ascent was all encompassing - taking in the views as well as safely navigating the stairs takes every ounce of concentration. Once we reached the top the scale of the King’s palace became real and you can spend time here soaking it up and taking many photos. Thoroughly recommend visiting this site. Hope you enjoy it as much as we did!
Difficult but worth it! Great feeling when you climb. Be sure to start the climb early in the morning as it gets pretty hot and humid.

We arrived in sigiriya at the village hotel and headed straight to the rock - the village hotel provided a perfect place to start from - either a short walk or tuk tuk ride of Rd 150. The rock was busy but not impossible in the late afternoon - and could only really be improved by some control over the numerous screaming Chinese tourists. The local guides and officials do little to whiten them and they behave worse than the often rowdy Sri Lankan men who did mostly seem to respect the other folk desire to enjoy some tranquility at this beautiful site. Other than that it was a perfect way to spend the afternoon. The climb is not bad - secure well marked stair cases mostly with officials pointing the way and politely showing where and where not photos were allowed

Our first visit to SL so we took the drive up to climb the rock. Arriving mid afternoon we were surprised to find it not that busy. The climb is surprisingly mostly stairs. As others have said you need to be fully mobile and healthy, and not afraid of heights. The climb is hard, but so very worthwhile when you reach the top.  just take your time and check out the view. Entrance fee is US$30/pax. Inc museum within the ticketing compound. Our driver dropped us at one car park and collected us at the other to save the walk back down to the ticket office.

Climbing Sigiriya is something I'd wanted to do for a long time and it was included as part of a tour.  There is a museum and fairly extensive gardens as well as the actual rock citadel.  Unfortunately we were there late afternoon and it was all a bit rushed to get up and down again before it got dark so we didn't really get to look around other than a flying visit to the museum. We had our own guide with us so didn't need to hire one and he was knowledgeable and told us all we needed to know.  The climb is well worth it for the view, although not great if you don't have a head for heights.  There are metal stairs in place but these are up the sheer side of the cliff in places.  The climb isn't actually difficult if you don't mind heights and can cope with the heat and humidity.  If you're not keen on heights, there's nothing too scary until the lions paws so it's worth at least doing that part.  We were at the top for sunset but this meant coming down the last part in the dark (if we'd realised, we would have brought torches with us!). By far the most annoying thing was a group of touts who stuck with us and "helped" us with the climb.  I kept telling them to go away as I didn't need any help but they wouldn't take no for an answer.  There was a sweaty hand in the small of my back pushing me up the spiral staircase to the mirror wall.  They finally got the message when I told them I had no money on me and wasn't giving them a tip!  However another lady in our group told them this countless times and they still stuck to her like limpets.  Eventually she borrowed some money off our tour guide and gave them a tip, so you can see why they keep pestering. Climbing Sigiriya is something you can't do anywhere else and I think it's worth doing, but be firm to the touts, and rude if necessary, to get rid of them.

There are 2 rocks next to each other to climb: Lion rock and Pidurangala rock. The entrance fee for the Lion rock costs 4650 rupees (30 USD), while the other one costs 500 rupees (3 USD). Is this a joke??

Early morning trasfer to Sigiriya, visit the 2500 year old ancient fortress ruins on top oft he Lions Rock. In the afternoon, climb up Pidurangala rock on a little hiking trail. On top enjoy the breathtaking view over the country and at Sigiriya rock
