We've been to a number of UNESCO World Heritage sites over the years, and this one is particularly impressive. The gardens and pathways to and from the main rock path are beautiful and impressive. The rock 'climb' itself is fairly straightforward. It's well maintained and, contrary to other reviews, secure with steel rails or brickwork along the whole route. The spiral staircase is perhaps the most daunting to those suffering from vertigo, but it doesn't go on for too long, and taking is steady, whilst looking UP (rather than down) will see you reach the ancient artwork easily enough. If you really don't fancy the spiral stairs and are willing to miss the artwork, simply walk to the right rather than the left at the point of the staircase. Beyond the spiral staircase (you go up, then down before getting back onto the main path), the route to the Lion's feet is fairly easy. There are some stone steps to climb, but they're well maintained and have a solid brick/stone/cement wall to the sides. From the Lion's feet to the top, there are quite a number of steel steps to climb. They are quite steep, but have steel rails on either both sides, or one side (when walking against the side of the rock). The main problem with the walk is being slowed down by a few people who really shouldn't be walking up the rock. There's not enough space to go round, but they end up holding everyone back. You don't need to be particularly fit to do the walk, but there are well over 2000 steps to climb! Only other thing to watch out for are the pushers/pullers. They're polite enough in wanting to help, but getting on with things yourself is fine, unless you want their help, in which case be prepared to tip generously. A simple "No/No thank you" is enough for them to stop pestering. The view at the top is impressive and the history of how and why the facility was built equally impressive. Thankfully we saw now wasps/hornets, but saw nests. They don't like noise, so avoid climbing with a group of noisy people! Top tip: take water with you, and get there as early as you can as after about 10am the heat is excessive and it's really busy with people! We arrived about 8.15 on a Wednesday and would suggest that's a good time to get there. Earlier if possible though as it was still quite busy at that time.

My Husband and I visited Sigiriya for 3 days as part of honeymoon and decided to climb Lion rock on our first day. We didn't follow other people's advice and get up early, we got to the rock at 11am but were lucky with the heat as it was a cloudy day. We managed to climb up and down within 1hr 20mins, this definitely wasn't easy for me to do so quickly as I tried to keep up with my Husband powering up the stairs. There are ALOT of stairs!! They're narrow steps too and slippery if you're not careful. About half way up you get to a metal spiral staircase which hangs off the side of the rock....half way up this I had a fight with myself deciding whether I wanted to turn back (people behind me so wouldn't have been easy) but kept telling myself to carry on as the realisation that I was hanging off a rock and really high suddenly set in. Something I clearly didn't think about before I started climbing the stairs! Neither me or my Husband are scared of heights but both of us had to tell ourselves to just concentrate on the steps and hang onto the railing on our way back down. Had I known I was climbing up those steps to see paintings on the wall and then climb back down again I might not have bothered but I'm glad I did it to tell the story all the same. Another part I found mentally challenging was the stairs after the lions feet, they too are metal, I decided it was easier coming back down them as I couldn't see the gaps in the steps like I could on my way up. All the while holding on tightly to the railings and telling myself I was nearly there. Even though I was scared most of the time doing this climb, the views are worth it and I'm so glad I did it. I'd definitely recommend it. We also did the Pudurangala rock the next day and have written a separate review on that. In short I would say both are worth a trip but do the Lion rock first and you'll appreciate Pudurangala a lot more like we did!

Our tour guide suggested we visited Sigiriya World Heritage site later in the afternoon and, even though it was a public holiday, the place was not overcrowded. The site is quite big and well worth wandering around. It is helpful to read your guide book in advance to understand the site layout as a certain amount of imagination is needed to visualise this Sri Lankan civilisation over 1,500 years ago and how the the Lions Rock fortress and palace was built. The hike to the top of Lions rock is quite strenuous as there are over 2000 steps on brick and metal staircases - so wear comfortable shoes! You can go at your own pace but there will be people trying to get past you so you need to be prepared. We had a number of school children trying to overtake us to beat each other to the next standing area. You should also be prepared for it to be windy as you ascend. As there are no drinks sellers on the site you will need to take your own water. The first hike takes you up a metal staircase to the frescoes and murals which are very interesting. You walk along the wall to view them and then double back on yourself to descend a spiral metal staircase to continue the journey. As you continue up some of the steps are uneven and steep but all areas are safe to walk on. There are a number of rest areas as you ascend if you need to catch your breath. As you get nearer to the top the stairs do become quite steep so a lot of people do just take it slowly. As you emerge at the top the views all around are fantastic! It is quite a sense of achievement reaching the summit and from her you can slowly walk around the various areas of the ruins of the Citadel. You can take a number of paths to lower levels and you can certainly appreciate the height you have climbed when looking down at the moat and water gardens at the base of the rock. You can descend following a number of different paths which take you to other fortifications, alleyways, canals and gardens to exit the site.

This walk to the very top is so worthwhile.it may seem difficult at first,but is very do-able for those of good fitness.the weather was a little warm then,so make sure you have good water supply and enjoy the flight if stairs along the way to the very top where you can even appreciate the gardens,the pool and summit view..unrecommended for unfit,obese and those needing aids for walking.otherwise a very enjoyable day is guranteed.

It's recommended to climb the rock first, and to do this in the morning. There is some shade on the climb but none at the summit so take a hat. The rest of the gardens are worth a stroll too, if you have time

You need to get up early to do this climb both for the temperature and to avoid the crowds. A total of 1,227 steps to the top but well worth the effort. The climb is not difficult just take it steady and enjoy the views as you climb.Taking an accompanying guide is a good idea to understand the history surrounding the rock fortress and its wall paintings.
Absolutely stunning, amazing and beautiful. Worth the 1332 steep steps to climb to the top! Being sun cream, a hat and a strong set of pins! :) the best!

Being mildly afraid of heights, and not particularly fit, I did not think that I could climb to the top... but I did, and it was totally worth it! The view cannot be described, you have to see it! Just make sure that you go there early morning (it opens at 7am) or late afternoon to avoid the heat and the crowds (even in low season, it was quite a queue on the way down!), make sure you bring plenty of water and you wear 'proper' walking shoes (I saw a lot of people climbing with flip-flops). Take as many breaks as you want/need on the way up and admire the view, I particularly recommend a longer break at the lion's paws: you will be able to catch your breath, take a few pics, and climb the last bit as and when you like it... If like me, you're not too fond of spiral staircases, you can skip the paintings (a bit of a shame, but better than a panic attack!) and go straight through to the mirror wall. Price is steep as well (30$ for foreign tourists) but I guess it's one of those things you can't miss, can you? If you're staying in Sigirya, it's in walking distance from the town and you can skip the tuktuks for once.

We drove from Kandy to Sigiriya (2.5 hours) to climb the Lion Rock. The climb itself was enjoyable and highly recommended. It's suitable for most abilities and is safe. The climb is all within hand railed stairways and platforms. Once at the top the view is terrific. I would advise anyone to take some water along for a break at the top. To give you an idea of time it took our group of 4 roughly 30 minutes to reach the summit and half that time back down however there is no rush so a more leisurely experience can be had. Cost per adult was 35 USD (foreigner price)
A must visit site in Sri Lanka, it's not just the climb that will take your breath away, the scale and beauty of the place and the views from the top are just stunning!

I visited Sigirya (the rock) one day from Colombo, 4 hours ride ( total of 8 both ways) and it was worth the long ride. It is an amazing place to visit as it is full of history and at the same time the view is amazing from the top. I did my tour during the day around 10 am, And I would recommend anyone to do it through sunrise time to avoid the heat and I am sure the view would be amazing. I had to do this as I was going from Colombo.

We visited on a Saturday morning, which was a good decision as the site wasn't too busy.  Its a big site with a bit of walking and over 1000 steps (some steep).  We had a private guide which was good, he worked at our pace and he helped us understand what we were seeing. There are a few facilities;  the toilets were pretty dirty, so avoid if you can.  There is a small cafe before you climb, but we only got some water. Wear good shoes,  perhaps a hat or sunscreen an take some water with you. The climb was hard work but the scenery and views worth the effort.

We took a local bus from bus station for around 200 rupees so significantly cheaper then offered tutk tuk or taxi. Bus has a sign Sigiriya and take about 45 minutes, the driver will tell you were to get off.  The entrance is 30 dollars per person so pretty expensive but the walk up to the rock was amazing and the beautiful veiw really worth all the hassle.

this place has amazing, breathtaking views. the climb was not too difficult. although this is a tourist attraction, the time that I went it was not too flooded with tourists so the human traffic was still bearable. do take note that Sigiriya is a 4hr drive from colombo
Huge expanse of wonderful sculptured grounds. Lots of the archeology still to be discovered but what is unearthed is breathtaking.  How did they do such wonderful architecture?

This place is a pure magic! It has some positive vibe. The stairs are a bit steep but it's worth the walk. And the view from the top of the rock is just amazing. Just go there and you will love it. I am sure.

Sigiriya should be on top of your list if you are visiting Sri Lanka. The views from top of this rock fortress are breathtaking and well worth the daunting hike. Make no mistake the hike is definitely tiring and you need to be reasonably fit to make it to the top. There are spots in between where you can rest to catch a breath and that helps. Best time to visit would be around 4pm so you can catch the gorgeous sunset from up top. The entry fee is definitely steep at $30, nationals of SAARC countries go in at half the price so make sure you carry your passport. Do not miss this one - enjoy the climb and the mesmerizing views!
Absolutely spectacular. Climb early to avoid crowds and also have a bit of peace and quite to minimise the risk of a hornet attack (worrying signs and medical tents about that place!!)

You start from admiration from a long way away as the mountain appears. Once you arrive it is a nice stroll through the grounds to the hill.  Then the fun begins. Is is pretty steep in spots but if you do it in stages it is pretty easy. A word of warning.  There are LOTS of pushers who will help you up by either hauling you or pushing you up the steps.  But nothing is for free!  Beware. Once you arrive at the "base camp", it is a long stretch up to the top but on metal steps with rails.   Pretty exciting.  And then you are at the top.  The view is well worth it
Amazing when you get to the top it's hard work but take your time and make sure that you have some water with you.Watch out of the helpers take a rest stop at the lions gate

This place is every bit as spectacular as photos suggest.  The history of it is fascinating, contemplating its construction awe inspiring and to climb it gives you a sense of achievement.  Before we got there, I had felt like this should have some form of cable car going up to it, but with hindsight it should definitely be conquered by foot. If you're planning to go, definitely go first thing in the morning.  It gets too hot and crowded later in the day.  We arrived at 8 and by the time we made our way down around 9.30 there were long queues to go up. The spiral staircase to the cave with the paintings of the damsels I found most challenging since you are essentially going up the side of a sheer cliffface.  We went with our 2 kids, which are 12 and 9 and they found it easy enough and enjoyed the challenge. The warning signs about the hornets are slightly alarming, but we never saw even one. Would definitely recommend it.
One of the top 5 destinations in Sri Lanka for sure. A must see and an opportunity to learn about the heritage of the country. Worth reading up on the basics before visiting.

Well recommended as one of the top attractions in Sri Lanka. Must be physically able as the climb to the top is a task for everyone. Great day out especially with a guide whom you can arrange at the entry.

our guide had advised us to go there early in the morning and thats what we did. ıt is less crowded and the heat and humidity is more bareable in the early morning hours. took a lot of pictures. İt is wonderful to see the Lion rock. Also the ghardens and pools are awesome.

It is one of the worlds must see historical monument. It is even more breathtaking close-up. Definately worth climbing the whole way up. Climbing the 1200 step stairs is a challenge, especially when your doing it in the hot and humid weather.You definately need water with you.
didn't go the top,but good experience the [pond were very nice,dont do in the mid day very sunny better in the evening or morning

The climb wasn't too challenging for me (30) and my wife (28). The scorching heat gave us second thoughts initially, but it got gradually cooler as we ascended the rock. The view from the top was amazing, I just wish there were fewer people there! Also, the bathroom situation was not so great.

This rock that was a palace is just amazing and well worth the climb along with all the other tourists. Don't be put off by the crowds it moves fast and there is plenty of space. We decided to climb the steep steps to the top of the rock and felt like we had arrived on top of the world. How did they ever get a palace up there. Now ruins it's a stunning place to see and also the views of the Sri Lankan countryside are wonderful. This country has been so welcoming and really been a great holiday with some not to be missed sights.

This was one of my highlights of Sri Lanka. Recommend going early morning to avoid the crowds, and the paintings on the rock are quite interesting. Beautiful views from the top and interesting ruins. Great feeling to accomplish the steps too!
Its a famous tourist spot. You will find tourists riding on the elephants there. The rock and its setting against a beautiful background is a treat to watch.

If you're coming from Kandy, go to the Bus Terminal and ride the bus going to Dambullah (35LKR each), which is a 2hr trip and then take the bus going to Sigiriya (8LKR). Walk from the bus stop to the attraction entrance (around 1km). Pay 30USD entrance fee and off you go to the rock. I dont know why, but when we went there, it was jam-packed. We already paid the entrance fee so no option of backing down. We braved through the sweat of queuing so close to one another. Queue was very long, so many locals visiting. It took us 1.5hrs to go up and 1.5hrs to go down. It was very tiring, and we were like sardines queuing. Some locals were very aggressive at the queue, cutting the line, etc. Will never do this again. We were expecting a better management since the entrance fee was too high. 30 freaking USD and no one bothered to organize the queue. So disappointed with it.

Absolutely loved this place. We went in September and started the climb at 9am, it was hot but easily manageable. It is busy but wasn't too bad. I'd definitely take water with you, you can't get any once you're on the main path heading up. Isn't great for people with a fear of heights as the little metal staircases are crowded and people stop randomly on them. Site itself is amazing and definitely worth it! As a note it is around £25 each to enter.

The hike to the top was fairly challenging but well worth it. Climbers should be cautious though as the rocky/marble steps are somewhat slippery and uneven and most of the climb doesn’t have any handrails. I saw some climbers hire helpers to accompany them to the top. Defintely stop to see the paintings on the way up, which are accessible by an additional wrought iron staircase that would seem a little dangerous if it got very crowded. Paintings are beautifully preserved. We visited in the morning as soon as it opened and we were able to beat the heat and the crowds. We were told the hike becomes much more crowded as it gets later in the day and it would have been a very stressful climb considering the way up and down are the same. The ruins at the top are and interesting site to see and the views from up there seem endless.
An excellent excursion provided you can cope with the 180 metre climb up and down again. It is remarkable that it was all built within 7 years.

There were 9 of us and it was our first trip to Sri Lanka together. Lion Rock climb ... indeed an incredible experience and we made to the top of the last 2 steps. Uncle Murugan, our guide, led us with baby steps. He knew exactly when and where to stop for a short rest during our afternoon climb. Uncle Murugan corrected us ... there were 1202 steps and the last 2 steps, unknown to many, were just a stone throw from the King's Throne. We witnessed the sun set from the last step of the rock. It was indeed a beautiful scene. The temperature began to drop as the sun set. The chilly wind blow-dry each drop of our sweat. No more panting as we were too engrossed with the 360 view. It was worth the climb. It was getting dark. Uncle Murugan insisted that we must leave so he led us down using a different route, again with baby steps. It was very dark when we reached the road. But with Uncle Murugan's guidance he made us felt so accomplished and great. Thank you Uncle Murugan for showing us the beautiful Sri Lanka.

It is a pretty tough climb. Make sure you go early. We got there at 7.30am and it wasn't too busy and the heat wasn't that bad yet. By the time we were almost at the exit at 9.15am, the placed was packed. It looked like about 5 tour buses had just arrived. Cost US$30 per person or equivalent in Rupees. You do not need to wear appropriate clothing, such as covered knees and shoulders, as it's not being enforced. However, culturally, it is the right thing to do. The main toilets are pretty nasty. However, there are some toilet facilities (western toilets) in the museum building (and they are free). The view at the top is good but the other rock, Pidurangala, has a better view and a more rewarding climb. Make sure you follow the noise signs for the wasps. There were a lot of really noisy people around and that brings more wasps.
Nice views and historical importance, but over rated and not good value for money

Unmissable! Need to visit early in the day before it gets hot - and take it slowly up the steps.  Don't miss the wall paintings on the way up.  Don't disturb the hornets! Imagine what it was like when it was lived in as a city - amazing!

An interesting few hours. We went early in the day to avoid the heat. Our driver arranged a local guide who knew the history of the place and the best route, worth the tip at the end - he had earned it for sure. Entry fee was $30 each which we felt was fair given the upkeep and staff looking after the place. Take some water and pace yourself on the climb and you'll be rewarded with a great view and a cooling breeze at the top. Can see monkeys, chipmunks, iguanas and birds on the route.
Incredible experience. Some of the most beautiful views I've ever seen. Don't attempt the climb without water and do it early in the morning.
A must visit for anybody with interest in history or architecture, requires some effort to reach the summit, worth every bit of it.
it is not advise to go above age 45. even is you try to go top of the rock nothing to see other than rocks. all are vanished. only we can imagine from guide explanation..
well worth the climb. also consider small rock. walk early to avoid crowds and heat
Very impressive place to see. Lot of stairs! Don't forget to visit the museum. During the hot season go early.

For me, personally, the experience was just not worth the price ($40USD) + the heat exhaustion and dehydration I experienced. There are signs everywhere to be silent due to wasps (which, yes, commonly attack and land scores of tourists in the hospital...go ahead and Google it) but due to the throngs of people, you have absolutely no control over the volume around you (the volume is loud for the duration of the trip...babies crying, vendors trying to sell water, etc.) Wasp attack is something you just have to be prepared for and accept as part of the experience (when this happens, they evacuate the park and don't give refunds.) We waited in line for over 30 minutes in the baking sun just to get past the entrance to the cave paintings (those people waited even longer to see the paintings...probably 60 minutes or more) all the while getting pushed and prodded as people here don't seem to understand we're all trying to get to the same place. The history of the place is cool and the view is wonderful but I personally could have done without the experience and just learned about it on Google.

Arrive early to climb the vertical stairs of spirits rock otherwise the heat and the tourists will ruin it for you! I myself have vertigo but thanks to some good tips I managed to go to the first view point which is ready really goid. In order to do this when you have vertigo you can avoid the metallic spiral staircase by going at the back - there is a small tunel which you can take. The only thing to bear in mind is that you will miss the mural paintings. After this tunnel the walk is quite easy to the first view point on the side of the rock. My partner went to the top of the rock,sais it was fantastic but definitely not worth 30 dollars!

Lion Rock is a MUST!  Built around 1600 years ago it's an old fort, palace and monastery.  Definitely hire a guide when you get there (about 30,000 rupees) and well worth it. There are 1236 steps to the top but it's not as bad as it looks.  Plenty of places on the way up to rest.  Full of history and awesomeness. There aren't any toilets on the walk so make sure you go before you start the tour. Take water with you and where it says "No photos" it means "No Photos" so please respect that. Highly recommend a visit here.  Go either early in the morning to beat the sun.  We arrived around 3.00pm which gave us plenty of time to do the tour but we could have spent a lot more time there.
Is known as eighth wonder of the world,Best place to visit in sri lanka. The place is bit crowded in the weekend. view from the top is amazing , but to reach their you have to spend time but worthy.

This is the best site to visit for me. The king who murdered his father to become a king, built a palace on a 200 meter high rock, and a city below the rock for the strongest defense. However, he went out to fight his brother anyway and lost, then he commits suicide. So the defense of the rock palace never get used. The rock for the rest of its 2000 years history is mostly used as a monastery for Buddhist monks.

I didn't had the opportunity to claim the mountain but I had the opportunity to check all the places near the mountains like the forest, lake , and discover everything with the help of my Tuk Tuk driver he was kind enough to show me everything and to take pictures.we just loved the place and the weather was wonderful a little bit of rain and sun shining few minutes .
Do not miss. It's a scary hard climb to the caves and then again to the  top but it is a must see sight. Mind blowing to see the art and the ancient ruins not to mention the view.
Fantastic to see such a ancient and historic area that so little is known about in the west. Very interesting.

One of the most amazing sites is Srilanka it introduce you to the ancient history of srilankan civilization. the place was w bit crowded needed too much time to reach the top and the climbing was a bit difficult with too many stairs but the views from the top is totally worth it it is simply amazing. this ancient rock still have some of it's old lion shape form such as the entrance.

This is an interesting and inspiring site. The various zones make for a good day out. The climb was tough enough for me but worth it for the views both of the countryside and the parts of the fort. Dont miss it of you are in Sri Lanka.
It it truly beautiful. The climb is not too challenging even though if you're scared of heights as I am there are bits that are a bit uncomfortable. Totally worth it though.

Of course it is not adequate to pay 30$ for this but we nevertheless enjoyed our visit. The view is stunning and luckily for us there was some rain so people left and we had a good time on the rock. Only two things to complain about. First, there is little information given about the whole area, the murals and so on. That's a pity. Second, the toilets are your worst nightmare. They reek and look like they never get cleaned...its a shame. The least I expected for that price were decent facilities. As usual, dont let any "guide" leech onto you and dont buy overpriced stuff from vendors. Even the beggars here are professional, wielding laminated sheets in perfect English begging for hospital money. Ignore them and dont let them spoil your visit.

If you are visiting Srilanka,it is one place which one  must not miss it...Need lots of energy to walk,climb,Trek around it.....Amazing view at the top.... Best time to visit early morning....bcz sun will be less....

The climb was so it ... view from the top absolutely lovely. The 'mirror wall' was a bit unimpressive ... as were the wall paintings/fresco's. Go as early as you can to avoid crowds and heat. I was once again upset by the condition of the so called 'street dogs' - heartbreaking to see them underfed, mange ridden, on 3 legs where they have had an injury and not been treated, bad eyes and ears. This really needs to be addressed if they want tourists to return...it marred my holiday to Sri Lanka so much that I would not return purely for this reason...too upsetting.

This citadel is simply fantastic but be aware of Sri Lanka public holidays as it gets packed. Plus try to go either early morning or late afternoon, both to avoid the heat and the crowd. We went on a full moon (in Sri Lanka Full Moon day is pretty much public holiday) and took us over 1 hour to go up the step at 1 step per minute because of the huge amount of people visiting... same for the way down.
Were here during mid-day, and it was hot! Very hot! Highly recommended to take a guide, since he will get you past the lines and also explain a lot. 1202 steps up, then down. Bring water!

The crowd climbs up the many iron stairs to reach the top. In this crowd you have all kind of people, including elders and children who slow down the queues, so be patient. Some children throw bottles or garbage from above, so it's not a safe climb, but the whole experience is astonishing.

Must see, the history behind it is amazing and to be there really is special. I had a tour guide approach me I paid him rates are around $2,000 rup, I paid him a bit more as his English was good and the information he covered helped me understand the construction of the fortress.

It hadn't rained in a while, so the grass was on the browner side, and all of the pools were empty or nearly empty, but I would put this in the same category as Ankor Wat in Cambodia.  Walking through the courtyards, and around the moats is peaceful, with not many hawkers to bother you, if your going up to the top, I would recommend getting there early, there was easily a 2 hour queue going up the main stairway, however if you go off to the left(and ignore the people saying they have a secret way for a price, and if you go ahead you will be fined for using the route ALL FALSE) you can go to the right of the main path and take a set of stairs that will get you to the fenced in walkway area.  There are some pretty steep stairs, and there is a line most of the way to the top, and they take parts of your ticket all the way up so don't lose your ticket! The views from the top were amazing, if your a photographer earlier in the morning will give you better pics from the top of the rock looking down, later in the afternoon pics will be better from the gardens and up at the rock. Downside it was pretty expensive and I believe there was a local price and then the tourist price. Exploring the area on bicycle, scooter, motorcycle is the way to go.

This is probably a must-see trip for any visit to Sri Lanka.  The scale and complexity of it is amazing and the frescos are remarkably well-preserved given their age and location and ledge high up the side of the rock.  As others have noted in their reviews, photos are very strictly prohibited of the frescos but there are signs, which should be fairly obvious to most. Getting up the rock means dealing with crowds and a lot of steps, including a couple of spiral staircases, in generally very hot weather, however, it's not the most taxing of climbs and the number of people means it moves at a leisurely pace.  Once you get to the top, the views alone make it worthwhile. Before you start looking around there is a museum next to the ticket booths.  It's worth doing this first to get a bit of insight to the history of the site.  Sri Lanka doesn't seem to be great at museums but this one just about does the job. Another feature worthy of note are the bees!  Once you reach the lions paws just before the final assent, there are impressive bee hives which look amazing when they all move in sync causing a wave across the hive.  However, take heed of the signs to be quiet as they have attacked before causing chaos.

What an amazing experience to finally get to the top. It is a challenge to climb to the top of Lions Rock, and when you think your there, your only half way up. I suggest if your going to do it be there when the gates open and before its to hot. I never thought I would be able to climb 1240 steps but it was worth it.

It is really worth to visit Sigiriya once you are in Sri Lanka. Even if it is definately overprised for tourists - 30$ for a person. While it costs many times less for a local. However, the veiw from the rock is stunning, ancient fresques are amazing, climbing up is not as hard as it might seem. Besides, there is a large place on half way where you can have rest, drink water or even take medical aid. We also saw many monkeys with babies there. You should only avoid people who work there. Even if their main duty is to help tourist and they are official staff members who get salary for their job. But still they expect tips from tourist and can be very annoying sometimes. We had to even shout angrily at them couple of times because guys refused accept our polite ''we don't need help, thank you''.

Ancient kingdom of Sri lanka. 3-4 hours from Colombo. travel with my wife and kids. MY small kid 5 years old and she has climb the rock even without our help. I never imagine. there also paid service can take from local groups. But I didnt took that. This is my second time to there in my life.

I must admit to being a little apprehensive about climbing this magnificent rock but I shouldn't have worried.....there is a series of old water gardens and ancient swimming pools with a secret entrance for the kings harem to enter whilst he watched to see before you reach the steps, around 1000!!! We had a superb guide called Neil who lives in Sigiriya and has been trained as an official guide. He took us a separate way for the first few steps which missed out a bottleneck at the beginning. There are a lot of steps but it is slow going due to the number of people climbing so not really a problem....you are climbing a walkway attached to the side of the rock but it's fine, it's all very safe and sturdy.... the view from the top is amazing.... again Neil brought it to life.... Aim to get there early as it is hot.....

It's about 1200 - 1300 steps and I thought I would never make it but it's sooooo worth at the end.  The view from the top is absolutely impeccable.   Definitely start early or get there by the time they open (I think 7AM) when there are less people (thus you can rest in between climb and enjoy the view) and the path is not unbearable hot.  We bought 2 bottles of water with us and we finished all.  Wear a secure sun-hat cause it's very windy once you get to the top. Wear comfortable shoe (we have hiking boots) and we carried knee brace (your leg would give when coming back down).   By the time we are coming down, the tour groups had started to ascend and I felt for them because one would not have be able to rest coz the path get narrower and one would have nowhere to turn/stop but up.

Sigiria lion rock is a must in Sri Lanka. you'll be amazed at the greatness of this rock and the view above is stunning. the entrance fee is pricey but if you want to pay only for one attraction in Sri Lanka, thats lion rock!

We were there only for a few hours to climb the rock but the place deserves a whole day. The rock is spectacular but there are a lot of other ruins around it worth exploring. Prepare for a lot of stairs i.e. it is not an easy climb. Those with a fear of heights should know that to reach the famous lion claws you must do some climbing i.e. they are half way up the rock. To reach the caves with the frescoes you need to climb to half the rock and just before the caves it is really just metal round staircase drilled into the rock and on your way down the staircase to reach the lion claws you can see right through the stairs down the rock so think hard if you can take this. The final climb to the top of the rock is again metal stairs drilled into the rock but once you reach the top the view is amazing (you can see forests and Buddha statues far away). We had the misfortune that it started to pour rain (monsoon style) when we reached the top and withing minutes we were soaking wet as there is no where to hide from rain on top.
The bad - it's crowded... The good - it's awesome. So even if you don't like crowds, just do it, it's such a nice place to see.

It is a must visit place in Sri Lanka and I heard it was nominated for wonders on earth too. That's true, it is an amazing place to visit. Better if you can arrive there by early in the morning as when in the mid day it would be hot and humid. You can avoid the certain over crowded situation if you avail early morning. Ancient paintings and the kingdom of King Kashyapa are unbelievable.Still the system of water flow to the top of the rock is not revealed.

Sigiriya is an ancient citadel built by King Kashyapa. It's a world heritage and a must see for a tourist. Some tips for tourists * Go early ~7:00/8:00 AM in order to avoid the scorching sunlight. * Bring your own water bottles. Selling water is a big business here. The price of a litre of water sky-rockets once you reach the top! * Watch-out for people trying to sell you over-priced items. * Watch out for monkeys who will snatch any snacks you have.

We reached there at 4 in the afternoon. Even though the place had 50% discount for SAARC countries, we only had copy of our passport so they didnt accept it and charged us full 30$ per person, which is very overpriced. The guides are not needed at all and its all about enjoying the view and climbing 1000 steps. One thing I would highlight is we found so many of fellow travellers being bite by wasps. When people make noise and its too sunny, wasps come out. Luckily, I was able to avoid that. The view at the top and climbing was fun. Be prepared to encounter monkeys as you reach the top.

We arrived early. 7am. I cannot stress enough that this is the right thing for you to do. Cool ish. No queues. Our driver parked easily. And a lovely relaxed climb up. What a beauty of an experience! As we were descending it really became apparent how busy this place gets. It was mobbed! We stayed at the Flower Eco Garden 5 mins round the corner. Fabulous !

We walked up in the morning around 9am which was just about early enough to beat the crowds. Stunning view over the local area once at the top.  Not giving it 5 stars as the 30USD price to climb it is very steep for what it is in my opinion.

My boyfriend and I climbed Sigiriya rock early in the morning (circa 7:45am) and found that there were not any queues on the climb up so would recommend that this would be the time to climb. We had good weather in that it was not raining and the sun was behind the clouds so although by 9am it was hot, the sun was not scorching as well. We wore trainers for the climb up as although it could be done in flip flops, if it was raining, it looks as though the metal staircase that you climb at the top could be quite slippy. Although the views are good from the top, we couldn't see how they could justify the entrance fee of 30usd per person.

Had to pay entrance fees. Its worth visiting the museum first before visiting the heritage site to understand the layout of the heritage site. It would have been helpful to have a write up or map to help the visitors. Instead, there are many touts who were insisting we hire them. Its a beautiful place to visit but avoid going during noon or when its too hot. Please take plenty of water and wear good shoes because its quite a bit of walking.

The paintings , lion rock, ramparts, fountain s etc. are little rewards for every level that is crossed. I guess biggest reward is descending back safely. The view is excellent. Beware of wasps . Written material is less at site and no audio guides are available. Good to take a guide but that can turn expensive unless bargained well. Morning is best time to climb else the heat can drain the strength faster. Carry extra bottles of water. Not recommended to take small children as the last climb and descent is daunting

We did this walk in the evening at about 4.30pm. It was rather hot and the crowds were huge.  As we climbed the sun went down and by the time we reached the top we had an awesome view of the sun setting. The views at the top are breathtaking. The climb is not very difficult but you need to have an average level of fitness at least. Like stated by other reviewers, you must be aware of the touts who try to provide help my holding your hand. Give them a firm "No". You must try to come down quickly before it gets dark. We got carried away taking pictures of the sun setting and later found it a challenge coming down the steps in the dark. Do not be intimidated by the height of the rock. Just do it.

We climbed Sigiriya around 7:30am on a very hot day. Make sure you stay hydrated and wear white/ light clothes. The climb was intense with many steps to the top. You must mildly be in shape to be able to climb. The ruins itself are very impressive and the Lion’s feet at the entrance to the main staircase will really take your breath away. Halfway up after this part of the climb you will be on a narrow/ uneven staircase and see a MASSIVE wasp nest to the left. The sight of seeing swarms of wasps circling the hive completely petrified me at the time. Some Sri Lankan tour guide saw me being afraid and at that point took the opportunity to take my hand and “guide” me up the stairs. Twice I pulled my hand away saying I was fine, but he continued to walk in front of us to the top of the rock. There we said we were okay and did not need him and he stood around until we paid him. We gave him 100 rupees to leave us alone (equivalent of 60 cents US) and he stood around asking for more. We said we didn’t have, but were very annoyed at his opportunistic and aggressive behavior. Our advice is to be alert for these people who prey on tourists and steer clear!

The climb to the top of Sigiriya Rock Fortress has been a highlight of our holiday in Sri Lanka so far. Something like 1,230 steps but absolutely worth the effort. Actually a lot easier than that step count might sound as there are lots of flat bits between the steps. Strongly recommend climbing early in the morning, start by 8am for 2 reasons: firstly the hardest bit is in the shade in the morning and secondly the later you leave it in the morning the busier it gets. Allow a good 2.5 hours to 3 hours to get up, explore the top and to get down. Our tour guide lead us up. Beware the "pushers" though. These are local men that apprear to be obligingly giving unsuspecting people a hand up the steps. They target anyone who looks like they might need some help especially if they have a walking pole or have a stretchy bandage on a knee as several in our group found out. If you do want/need a hand, be prepared to pay the going rate of about 2,000 rupees (less than Australian $20). They will make a fuss and try to get more out of you but we were told this was the going rate. If you do not want help, just walk steadily and say a clear but polite "no, thank you" and they will try the next person. The first part of the walk is flat and through the ruins at the bottom. None of the stairs up in the climb is overly long. There are 2 exit points part way up. The tour buses pick you up at a different point to where they drop you off so if you want to bail out you can walk down to the car park. Do check with your guide though. In lots of places you will see a series of horizontal cuts in the stone. We were told that a lot of the climb was originally canopied and these cuts were the steps to get the canopies up and repaired. The frescoes are part way up and are an extra climb as you then have to come down from them. Access to them is via a steep narrow metal spiral staircase. A separate metal spiral staircase brings you down. The frescoes are worth while. Look for the one that has been over painted by the artist - you can see the painted lady with a little jacket on to hide the fact that a hand across her chest has been painted over but still visible. Once you get to the enormous lion paw you will see a lot of stairs ahead of you. Just take your time because you are getting very close to the top. The views from the top are amazing including towards Dambulla about 20 km away where there is a Buddhist temple carved into the rock. Remember to climb the extra 2 steps going nowhere at the highest point! Coming back down, close to the car park you come across Cobra Rock that looks like a huge stone cobra head. There are stalls at the bottom selling the usual tourist things. The day we went there there was a snake charmer with the usual cobra. The snake charmer also had a large python round his neck that you can put round your neck for a fee. It is heavy but it doesn't feel slimy or unpleasant.

We had a great experience with Sigiriya Lion rock today. There is plenty of nature and views to see in this place. Great looking rocks and fantastic panoramic views from the top. I highly recommend anyone going on a hot day to arrive early in the morning to avoid the noon heat; or if you have to go around noon time, make sure to have a cap/hat/umbrella.
Well worth the Climb to the top - just do it !!! Best bet is to climb late afternoon - just make sure you get back to the car park before it gets dark otherwise you may have a problem !

Get there at 7 am (730 latest) otherwise expect be in the crowd. It is 1200 steps to the top. Take water and a hat. It will be hot and humid. (Windy at top) At 7am it is 90 min round trip. A lot longer if in the crowd. Single file all the way up and back. It's a rip off at $30 USD entry. But like everyone says, a must do. The closest half decent hotel is Sigiriya Village Hotel at $100 USD including breakfast. (Less than 5 min away) Nice pool but the rooms are ordinary. A guide is a good idea as gives the full story of the surrounding area. (500 rupee tip) Dont buy any souvenirs as they are truly overpriced and poor quality.

As a history buff, I was really excited to visit the Sigiriya fortress. Although I really loved the story behind it and the view from the top, the amount of tourists really shocked me. Especially the school trips. Keep in mind that this is not a very easy climb. There are steps though and it is very safe to climb. The view is breathtaking. Try and climb as early as you can since it gets hot. Also if you are a SAARC citizen, you are entitled to a 50% discount if you show your passport.

An early morning start to be handed over to a local guide who took us up the rock. Not as difficult as we expected (but perhaps we are fitter than we thought!). It is a trip not to be missed and the views once at the top are spectacular. There are hornets (huge nests almost at the top) which can become a nuisance in the heat of the day. Another reason to go early in the day, avoid the crowds and the hornets!

WARNING - PUT ALL PHOTOGRAPHIC AND VIDEO EQUIPMENT IN YOUR BAGS UNTIL PAST THE FRESCOS!!  Cameras / phones / GoPros etc There are extremely aggressive guards who are ready to take your cameras and threaten to call the police if you disobey the rule of 'no photography or videos of the frescos'. My 16 year old daughter accidentally knocked her GoPro on.  She was stopped, detained for 45 minutes, the guards demanded her passport, wrote her passport number down and made her sign a statement saying she had filmed the frescos. Our guide spoke to them and eventually they let her go because she was a child.  We had to pay a small donation to Sigiriya Rock. This was a frightening experience and it happens to a lot of people here.  It may be a scam to get your camera or a payment but I have since read and article which states that you could be fined 1 Million Rupees or spend 2 days in prison for this offence. So be warned if you want to enjoy your climb of Sigiriya Rock!!

We had a fantastic time at this UNESCO World Heritage site. The views of the rock from the ground are stunning and the views that you get during the climb and at the top are incredible. The walk up isn't too tough and we saw lots of older and younger people doing it. The little diversion to see the frescos is well worth the trip up the spiral staircase, although my wife found it a bit hairy. Our big tip would be to go early. Both the heat and the crowds increase greatly from 10am onwards, so try and be there before then, preferably when the site opens at 7am. The price is expensive, particularly when you find out what a Sri Lankan pays, but it is a UNESCO World Heritage site for a reason.

We enjoyed climbing to the top of Lion Rock. The views were great. The 1202 stairs (as we were told) were slippery, rocky, and often narrow and small.  This isn't for those with a fear of heights.  We had a blast.

it was 8th wonder of the world – the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. Dating back to the 5th Century A.D, this astounding ‘city’ on the summit of a high outcrop was the royal citadel of King Kassapa for over 18 years. A miraculous feat of artistry and engineering, its unique features and exquisite frescoes continue to amaze all who visit it, even today.

Thousands of people climb the steps of Sigiriya Rock.  We arrived early and moved slowly step by step with the crowd in 30 degrees heat. My teenage daughter had put on her GoPro (camera) which was across her chest. Part way up the climb there are small signs which say no phones and no cameras.  These signs can easily be missed when in the crowd. There are very aggressive guards at an area where there are fresco paintings on the rock wall.  Unfortunately, my teenage daughter had knocked on her GoPro  by accident as she walked. The guards detained her, demanded her passport, made her sign a statement to say she had photographed the frescos.  Yelled at her saying she had disobeyed the Sri Lankan Government. Said she would have to wait until the Police arrived. They detained us for about half an hour.  It was very distressing for us all and especially for my daughter who was distraught.  Our travel guide discussed matters with the guards and they eventually excused us, deleted the GoPro pictures, and let us go on the grounds that our daughter was a child.  We had to give a small donation to Sigiriya Rock as an apology. We have learned since that the aggressive attitude of the guards MAYBE just a scam to either confiscate cameras or exhort money from tourists.  However, we have also read in an article that you can be fined 1 Million Sri Lankan Rupees or spend 2 days in prison for taking photos (but not sure how true this is). We would have enjoyed our day climbing Sigiriya Rock if this incident had not taken place.  It happens to many tourists there and is it not a pleasant experience at all.  Most have their cameras confiscated. SO PLEASE BE WARNED!!   ....put all cameras etc away until you are past the frescos and you will enjoy your day at Sigiriya Rock.

Warning, do NOT attempt this if you are unfit in any way. What a beautiful site and how the hell did the build a fortress at the top of that rock? With views to die for (if you haven't died on the way up) and a glimpse of what it may have been like around 2,000 years ago, this will be remembered for a long time. In a state of ruin, and I do think the locals could take more care of a national treasure, it's well worth a visit.  Had it been standing, I could imagine similarities to Ankar watt. I would not recommend taking young kids up to the top.  It was hard in August and I can only imagine how slippery it would be in rainy season.

This is an incredible place. It is worth getting up early to avoid the crowds and heat of the day. The view from the top is amazing. It has a fascinating history. You can still see grooves etched into the rock where people originally used to climb to the top and the paintings of the Sigiriya damsels are very well preserved. This was one of our highlights of Sri Lanka.
Quite sensational experience, great place. The physical efforts to get on top are manageable for most. Can be quite crowded so better start early. Beware of wasps on the way up!

Yes its better than Pidurangula rock because of the history and ruins, but you can not see the sun rise from here. Get up early to climb Pidurangula (5:00), then continue straight to here to beat the crowd.

The rock itself is amazing! It's defiantly worth the climb to the top! There are around 1200 steps to climb and can be a slow climb due to the number of people! It's best to go early in the morning or late afternoon (less busy and cooler). We went around 4:30/5pm and it was ok!
its a wonderful place specially if you went to the lion rock before the sunrise, climb the rock and watch the birth of the sun from above... it's charming!

The view is breathtaking! It's a must-see place in Sri Lanka. If you are healthy and do not have any cardiovascular disease it will not be difficult to climb the rock. You don't need any special training for it.

It is a world heritage site and clear why. Amazing history of building, but less so the people history. The challenge is the heat if doing during the day; very difficult to explain the size of the site but you need a driver to take you round and even then you are outside in the baking heat for too long. Spend time reading everything in the museum first, or buy a good guide book and read beforehand, and it will make it more worthwhile. 3 stars due to the lack of visitor facilities.
A very good experience. Guide books probably don't do tell the full story, but you need to go as early in the day as you can muster. 6.30 and back for breakfast avoids the crowds and the heat!

In total you will climb 1200 steps but not all at once. There are couple of resting places.  On the way down there is a path with less stairs on the other side of the rock. Half of the stairs are made out of rock and half steel. Only scary part is steel stairs at the lions paw. Because there is only a waist high rail as safety procaution. You go up and down from this stairs. Wall paintings and the view from the top is very nice.
The view from the top is gorgeous and totally worth the climb. Start early and get blown away.... A must see when in Sri Lanka

This is a beautifully maintained attraction and lives up to its billing. The fee is a bit high for foreigners but it is a must see attraction when in Sri Lanka. The climb to the top is exhausting but the view from the top more than makes up for it. You have to start early to really enjoy the climb. The landscaped gardens are an added bonus
You need to climb this rock because the view is really stunning. we got up very early to arrive up at around 9. and we camback per lunch time. I suggest you to do the same

Incredible rock with the ruins of Sky Palace on the summit. We arrived later afternoon but it was still very busy. The queues slowly wind their way up the rock and then back down again! Be warned that not everyone does British queuing and there are a fair few that just push past. The views at the top are incredible though and well worth the climb. This was a fantastic introduction to what Sri Lanka had to offer us.

No need to go right to the top. Just up as far as the Lion's paws is far enough. If you keep going its just the same view of the same countryside but from a bit higher up. The main picture on TripAdvisor is taken from the level where the paws are. You can see in the background the rickety staircase that goes to the top, It's perfectly okay just a bit unnerving when people en masse try and pass going the other way. Really good morning or afternoon out. Go early and be there when it opens as a) it is cooler and b) it is before the coaches tend to get there.

This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Sri Lanka's main attractions. A spectacular pillar of rock whcih is visible from miles away. Sigiriya is a hardened magma plug from an extinct volcano. It's history is disputed between it being a royal fortress under the reign of King Kashyapa (477 - 495 AD) or a Buddhist monastery. There are a lot stairs to climb but they start off pretty easy as you walk through the vast gardens. The main level is about 2/3 of the way up where the 'Lions' paws remain. That is worth going to. If you go right to the top the stairs get pretty rickety and the only reason to go is a slightly higher view.

We arrived later than preferred here so we were climbing in the heat. If you are doing this train a bit before as it is a fair climb. Having said that resilient Sri Lankans do it in flip flops and carrying a baby in their arms:-) it is often very busy but that helps one pace the climb. As always the Sri Lankans also climbing are always super polite, friendly and smiling. If you have a fear of heights this is not for you and if you are a structural engineer dint look too closely at the welds or integrity of the frames or the weight load on each section:-)) If you get too fatigued or are elderly you can hire an assistant for rps 2000 to help you. You can also stop at the base of the lion steps before the final scary assent. Some people were hiring wasp protective suits but I would strongly suggest that you don't as it causes greater hazard and I think it is dangerous. If you or a child have serious allergies to wasp stings....then DONT climb the rock. To do otherwise even with an epipen of adrenalin is an irresponsible as the risk is great. The view from the top is great but usually hazy. The joker who built it was obviously an A/h and never carried a brick himself. It really is a wonder but one that makes you work for its secrets:-)

Best time to get there and do the climb is early morning,be there at 7am you may have to wait to actually start but it's worth it.If you have your own guide do not get 'way laid' by helping hands that the guide cannot stop approaching you.The climb starts easily enough though it does get harder,much harder,you need a head for heights for especially the last leg hanging off a shear cliff but the top is worth it and do not forget the last 2 steps at the top😀

If you love adventure and history then Sigiriya Rock is a brilliant mix of both! I visited with my family and had heard very good reviews of Sigiriya and I was not disappointed. If you are concerned about the climb to the top of the rock, it is not as challenging as it looks however if you suffer from a fear heights you may have moments of feeling uncomfortable. Nevertheless this was a great start to our Sri Lanka holiday and would recommend to any traveller visiting Sri Lanka!

This is a great half day trip but a little over priced. The views from the top are amazing after the 40min walk to the top (could be done in 15mins on a quiet day, as you spend most of time queuing to get up narrow stairs).

Sigiriya is an incredible world heritage site and a must visit when in Sri Lanka. But it is physically accessible for the young and the fit only. Ancillary sites and services could fill the gap but are disappointing. The museum is okay but the museum shops were closed; the cafe and toilets were disgustingly dirty and offered little relief on a hot day. The walk up to the site  - water gardens and pathways were not kept clear of garbage or groomed as they could have been. An incredible place and world treasure.
Amazing world heritage site. Unbelievable water reservation systems, water gardens, fresco and significant mirror wall. When you come to Sri Lanka, Don't forget to visit this wonderful place.
Very steep climb!! If you are unfit you will not get to the top!! Be sure to climb in the cool of the day & take plenty of water. A guide is worthwhile

Highly recommend. We climbed Pidurangala the day before which was great for the view but Sigiriya rock is so much more than just the view and I think people are missing out if they skip this. We arrived at 7am to buy tickets (this is when it opens). Tip- tickets only valid day of purchase (We dropped in the day before to see if we could buy tickets for the next day but couldn't). Only a few people there and we started our walk up the rock. I recommend you walk straight up first and then explore grounds as you come down. Really great to walk up at that time as not too many people plus it is cooler. View from top wonderful but the ruins were incredible to see on the top of the rock and we explored this before climbing down again to the second level and admired the lion paws, then down to the boulder gardens,  terraced gardens and cobra head cave. We descended and explored using paths to the left of the main path (if you had your back to the rock). All the way down there are ruins and baths and remains of paintings (in cobra head cave) etc. It must have been a site to behold in its prime! We spent about 4-5hours at the sight in total. It was getting pretty busy by the time we got down the rock however there were hardly any people in the other parts surrounding the rock. If you have travelled all the way to Sigiriya then don't miss this incredible site.

This is usually missed out because of the high entrance fee it charges foreigners. However the entire park along with the ground level water parks and the citadel on the rock is really beautiful and well worth the visit. Start early to beat the crowds and also the heat. Its quite a climb up all the way to the top of the rock but doable.

The climb up the rock is not very strenuous but yes its quite a climb up. You initially climb uphill quite a bit before you even attempt to do the rock climb. The views from the top  o the rock is amazing. The ruins are also very impressive. Start early to beat the crowds.

This is an incredible sight. It is not without flaws but a must-see for all visitors to Sri Lanka. It can get very busy. We got there at 8am and it was already heaving so get there earlier (or possibly later in the afternoon). The walk up can be tricky, especially for those with a fear of heights. The views from the top, and the various interesting features, such as the frescoes and lions paw, make it completely worth it. We were delayed  from going down because of an outbreak of wasps! We had to wait an hour so make sure you take something that can cover you from stings. Overall though we were buzzing to have made this visit. The museum is worth a little trip too as it shows photos from how the rock has looked over the years. Two people had previously mentioned that they went to the rock next to it rather than pay the entrance fee but this was poor advice- we were very glad we'd paid and witnessed such a unique sight.

It’s quite an expensive attraction, the entrance fee is around 30$ per person (price for foreigners). The remains of king gardens are not interesting as little remains. The rock itself is impressive. The climbing is not an exhaustive one but better have comfortable shoes. Views and landscapes are really nice. There are some frescos preserved in the rock, but the spiral stairways to visit them are literally hanging over the gap, which was impossible for me to climb because of vertigo problems. The Lion paw is attractive and impressive. It’s an attraction worth visit.

When you arrive at the rock you have to walk through the Park with the palace and 3 gardens where the king lived in the dry season. In the wet season he live in his palace on the rock. If you climb up (over 1200 stairsteps) you walk by the fresco's on the rock (very old and impressive). It is busy so you have to wait somethimes but that is oke because you need a rest now and then. When you arrive at the top you see the remains of the palace. It is very impressive if you think what they had to bring to the top off the rock to build it, many ages ago.

It is very helpful if you have a Sri Lankan guide to explain the amazing history & relevance of this special place!  A guidebook or reading any signs will not give you a full appreciation of this place.  Start early in the morning, wear good tennis shoes, and bring water--but don't miss this special place!

This old lady had not realized what a hike this would be and was glad we had chosen to begin early in the day!  Thankfully, I had a wonderful guide to help me watch my steps, take time to drink water, and point out things from the amazing viewpoints and world-class ancient artwork!  It was worth every step!  (Note:  If you are allergic to bee stings, be aware that near the top there are large, active wasp nests.  On the day we went, people were stung and the beekeepers were doing their best to protect people and keep them safe.)  Amazing history of Sri Lanka!

1020 steps. It's busy and at times in the heat and crowd can be quite hard work. I'm 37 and slightly overweight and found it hard work in the 35 deg heat. I will say this, Wear comfortable shoes, take a bottle of cold water, wear a hat to protect yourself from the sun. I did none of those things and paid the price haha. Once you get to the top it's breathtaking and something you won't forget in a hurry. I would also recommend getting a guide although if you can't be bothered then there are placards dotted around the place with some historical facts. I will say one thing, if you suffer from vertigo, then some parts of the climb are a little bit nerve racking but take it easy and you'll be fine. It's just stairs at the end of the day. Oh tip the guide.... oh and don't make too much noise near the hornets nest, they have been known to attack!

Climbing this rock proved a nice challenge, but we were well rewarded by the scenic view from the top. The afternoon sun was strong, but we were encouraged to carry on by the others. Some nice cave art, carvings to marvel at, as well.

We arrived at the rock around 7:30am as our guide said it was good to get there to beat the crowds later on and also it means we weren't doing the majority of the walking in the mid day sun! This was definitely a good tip so I would recommend this. The site itself is so impressive and I am always amazed at how man could build such things  with the tools available at the time. The views from the top are outstanding as you can see for miles and miles. A couple of words of warning, firstly at some of the steps etc, there are men waiting to help you up, if you accept their help they then request money off of you, so unless you really need the help don't accept a hand. Secondly, be prepared to be stuck up the top for a bit if the wasps that are nesting on the cliff face decide to come out! This happened to us and we were stuck for another half hour at the top and ended up having to come down in a net to stop the wasps from getting us. This wasn't so bad though as there are worst places you could have to spend more time! One last thing, be sure to take a couple of bottles of water each.

We went after having breakfast at about 10 am and it was v sunny. This could be seen from a long distance. We decided to climb up and found the tickets to be v expensive for such a steep climb. There was not much rush and queue. The climb with such sun burning down on us was too tiring. They said we should have come early morning. However the view from top was breathtaking. The creation at such height is worth admiring.
Unfortunately when we came to visit the rock, it was under the attack of wasps , so we couldn't go to the very top. But you can imagine the real splendour of this amazing rock fort.
I went there today and was quite impressed. It was a big walk up and very hot and slow as so many people. Get there early. Price of 4620 rupees seems abit steep to me. Nice views at top.

This was the most unforgettable part of our trip to sri Lanka! The water park, the rock and the frescoes are unbelievably amazing! Mesmerized to think such technology existed centuries back!! Breathtaking views from the top of the rock!! You shouldn't miss this place if you visit sri lanka. The experience is beyond explanation!! You just have to come and experience!
Wonderfull place. Should come as early as possible, whent they open it to avoid big asian groups. Great views from the top.

This is a must-visit!  It can be seen from miles and miles away but only when close up to you see what an incredible fortress and grounds this must have been.  Few things to bear in mind: Get there early, the queues up the rock are huge; it is quite expensive  - $30 for adults and $15 for children – so a family of two adults and two children will set you back almost $100; and if you have small children, they might not want to make it all the way up – as ours didn’t!  Still breathtaking however, especially when you see the steps carved into the rock used by the creators!

It is understandable why Sigiriya has been made a heritage site, it really is something magical. Such amazing history, i strongly recommend a guide is taken for the visit, the guides are situated outside the main entrance and they are all official, ensure you visit early morning.

We woke up at 5:30am in Dambulla and hired a tuk tuk for 1,500 LKR to drive us to Lion's Rock and wait for us to walk up and down. We were in line shortly after 7am to buy tickets (4,500 LKR for foreigners) You can visit the museum next to the ticket counter (included in the price) however they don't open until 8am. We decided to start hiking up as we didn't want to hit the crowds of tourists. The rock attracts groups of people from all over the world with different fitness levels and ages from young children, to elderly people, so remember to take your time and be patient if you get stuck behind. We spent in all about 3 hours to walk up around 1600 steep steps, look around at the top and then to walk back down. The views are amazing and its really interesting to see the mirror wall and the views from the top of the rock. Definitely worth the price and time! TIPS 1. take water with you 2. pack some snacks (just be sure to clean up after yourself!) 3. GO EARLY! Be at the ticket counter for 7am, we walked back down around 930am and the line up to go up was HUGE 4. DONT take pictures of the paintings half way up the rock, there are signs everywhere. Unfortunately and Italian couple got busted and they took their passport numbers down (not sure what they did with them but they weren't happy!) 5. Watch out for wasps! there are signs everywhere telling you to be quiet and there can be wasp attacks, but they are prepared for these events. There is a hospital tent just before the summit. Just be smart.

My family and I enjoyed a fantastic experience climbing lions rock-our driver dropped obtained a guide who was very knowledgable of citadel of sigririya and the history - the day of our visit was a full moon so it was very busy even so it was terrific and just added to the experience.  The paths are narrow and the steps are steep but the view at the top is simply unique-an experience never to forget. A must do when visiting Sri Lanka 🇱🇰
easy climb for people who are reasonably fit. weather matters a lot we had a comfortable climb. top view is memorable!

It's a bit of a trek up the rock with some narrow and steep staircases, but it is worth it. Take breaks along the way and admire the view and make sure you get there. We went first thing in the morning and that was more than hot enough.

My wife and I visited Sigiriya in early August and the lion rock was part of our itenary. The initial plan was to go for a jungle safari (Mirisa national park, which is nearby) and then visit the lion rock in the afternoon. We were informed though the best time for the safari would be after 2PM and hence we changed our plan and visited the lion rock in the morning. In hindsight, I would probably like to have gone to the lion rock in the afternoon - the reason is the crowd. The path to click up the rock is narrow and when there is a crowd, the queue can get very long. When we came down we noticed very less crowds and we figured that we could have saved at least a couple of hours waiting in the queue if we started in the afternoon. The entry fee is around LKR 4200 for foreigners; and around LKR 2500 for people from SAARC countries. As we are from India we were eligible for this pricing - One thing you must note is that they require to see your original passport at the ticket counter if you want to avail of this pricing. There are many locals who will offer guide services, but in my view, a guide is not required. There are many information boards along the way to explain the history of the place. You can also spot many monitor lizards along the way during the walks. The climb is basically broken into 2 parts. The first part you get to climb upto a small cave with ancient paintings- They have set of spiral staircases to climb up and down to this cave. Many tourists expect more at the cave - but it is around 20 feet in length and has a few old paintings. They are very strict about not taking pictures at this cave! After the caves, you can rest for a bit at the foot of the lion rock - and take pics near the lions paws carved in stone. This place has many monkeys and if you have a few bananas you can have some fun feeding them to the monkeys. From here there is a steep climb to the top of the rock. If you are in reasonably good shape this should an easy climb. The view from the top is really beautiful and its worth spending some time up there before starting your descent. One thing you must note is the threats of hornets! There are many hornet nests next to the climbing area and they can start attacking. We had just reached back down when the hornets started attacking and they had immediately closed the area and did not allow further tourists to climb. In such cases they also do not refund the ticket amount. Usually tough they are able to resume the climb after some time. Overall, we spend about 4.5 hours and it was a memorable experience. If you visit in the afternoon, i feel you should be able to complete this comfortably in about 3 hours.
This is a must visit when in Sri Lanka, it is a masterpiece of architecture, with a rich history and culture.

We climbed Sigiriya early in the morning and then explored the gardens. The views are beautiful and definitely worth the relatively easy walk. In addition the history and story surrounding the rock are fascinating and it is is a must see. Make sure you get up early and go into the park at 7am. It gets very hot later than 7 and while it is still busy at this time it is no where near the lines and lines of people we saw climbing up at 10am. Definitely do the climb first when it's relatively cool and then take a walk around the watergardens.

Arrived early and glad we did. The queues were getting longer as we left. Well worth the climb. We had a guide/driver who went with us which was good to hear the history. It's a tough climb but well worth it. Views were amazing. Need to allow 2-3 hours. Take plenty of water. Sri Lankan's like to think of it as the Eighth wonder of the world. It certainly is amazing. Enjoy.

The climb was less difficult than expected because it was so crowded. It was impossible to climb with some speed. The climbing and the sun were not an issue (the first part is in the shade of the rock) but the fact that it is so busy is the main obstacle. For me a little bit disappointing, also because there are always people who do not keep the line in the queue. They do not understand that you stop because you cannot move forward. There is a nice view from the top but not spectacular.

It was well worth the effort climbing to the top to see the awesome views that await you. Bring sensible footwear and water. It's also advisable to set off early to avoid the heat of the midday sun. A little pricey but a must-see part of the cultural triangle.

Anuradhapura is a site not to be missed. Expect, however, a long day as the site sprawls over a few acres. You can either spend the whole day on a bicycle to explore the grounds of this ancient monastery, or you can hop from one main site to the other by car and do something else during the half day. Just plan your visit in advance and make sure you have a guide or a good map and book.

This is a must-see. However, come prepared to climb 1,200 steps. Good shoes are advised, as well as a good level of fitness. We saw people huffing and puffing, and even crashing on the stairs. When this happened, traffic come to a halt or a bottleneck, as the staircase is fairly narrow. Best to start early in the day to avoid the hordes of visitors and the heat. You will be rewarded with beautiful sights and a chance to see what a king's whims could lead to centuries ago.
Make sure you take a walk up this world heritage sight. The views from the top are amazing!!! Fantastic.

Worth the effort to climb to the top to see awesome views and amazing work to restore the historical grounds. Every step is well manicured and maintained. Start early to avoid the heat of the day. Highly recommend a visit.

Visiting this site was one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka. Climbing slowly higher & higher , enjoying the magnificent views of the rock & surroundings. The painting halfway are beautiful & very well conserved. When reaching the top , the site is breathtaking with a 360 degrees view of the environment.

There are many hornet nests near the path. They attack, and there are not enough suits for everyone. There is also no announcements regarding what is happening. We had to wait over an hour at the second level of the rock, because the attacks were so strong they blocked the path. Also, no refunds when they close the top level, the hornet attacks are entirely on you. They don't use the steep ticket prices to fund improvements, which is very unfortunate.

place was absolutely breathlessly amazing and will also leave you breathless after reaching its peak. entrance is 4120 rupess (not so sure but its 4000 somethng) before reaching its base. u have to walk and climb a little for like 1km. but it was okay because of the view. be sure to have ur water with you as u will really need it. my knees were shaking and i had a lot of leg cramps that night. but i had fun. i dont think you need. tour guide for this. u can read frst its history so that u will know its story and learn it on your own.

the place was so breathlessly amazing and will also leave u breathless after reaching the peak.  the entrace fee is 4120 rupees (not sure but its 4000 somethng) and before even reaching its base u have to walk and climb like 500meters so it was really tiring. dnt forget to bring ur bottled water. my knees were shaking and i had a leg  cramps all night Ftr this experience. but it was a great great great experience.

Children and the elderly may struggle more. Creeping near to the dangerous bee hives can be nerve wracking but they are harmless unless you agitate them. There is first aid available nearby so don't be put off by this. The views at the top are spectacular and exploring the ruins is extremely interesting. As previously mentioned, spend time around the grounds and learn more about Sigirya Lion Rock. We were met by many more visitors about to climb up and we feel this amount of people would have lessened the experience, especially after having climbed the much quieter and equally rewarding Pidurangala Rock the day before (Also a must).
Such an amazing place, well worth the entry fee. Climbed to the top with our two young kids and everyone loved it. Absolutely amazing place.
Its amazing to see the ruine on top of the mountain. The claws at the beginning of the top are amazing. It is a litte bit crowded but if you are there this is a must.
would recommend all visitors to definitely try and go to the top of the fort as the views are just out of this world. The best time to climb the rock is at 7am as later on it gets hot and busy!
A must, not just for the views, but a feeling of success...Water, sun cream and good shoes a must
