This is a fascinating place to visit, so much history and amazing how it would have been built so many years ago. We got a guide (tip only pay) he was really good, spoke good English. The previous day of our visit they had had issues with wasps, our guide was very good in explaining to us what to do if we got stung (luckily we didn't) It's an interesting walk to the top, but well worth it.

We were very much looking forward to our visit to sigiriya even before we landed in Sri Lanka. I must say that the very tiring climb up did not disappoint us. The details are absolutely stunning and I highly recommend that you listen to details from an expert if you are trying this out. If not this is a yet another ancient rock. So listening to details makes all the difference.

Sigiriya is a little bit of a challenge if you don't like heights, but it's worth the climb.  There's a gentle walk through the grounds to the rock itself, lots of stone stairs to the halfway point, then suspended metal steps up to see the paintings.  Paintings are beautiful, but don't attempt to sneak your camera in for forbidden photos - we watched the guard grab an aggressive and disrespectful tourist and threaten him with 14 days in jail.  The climb through the lion paws and up another set of suspended metal steps is breathtaking, then you are on the top with the remains of the old palace and a view for miles over the countryside.  We got there just as it opened in the morning when it was still cool with a breeze blowing.  The tour buses come in after that and it can get hot and crowded later. My friend and I were told by two different sources not to bother doing Lion Rock. We decided to as the owners of our hostel encouraged us to and we were so glad that we did. The views from the top are breath taking as are the stone work remains. This was the highlight of Sigiriya for us.

Having read the previous reviews concerning the price of Sigiriya, I was skeptical about paying it to climb what looks like a massive rock. However, having done it I am completely amazed and confused as to why people, who have likely spent a lot of money and time to travel to and around Sri Lanka, are so against it. Yes it is USD30. Yes there is a tourist and local price but almost every attraction I've been to in Asia has this tiered pricing system so I'm not sure why people have such an issue with it. I suppose if you don't have a guide then it is just a climb, a great view at the top with some ruins. Sigiriya rock is a Unesco site and the work we saw the local people do, including the man clearing a bin to stop tourists being attacked by wasps, is well worth USD30. Here's my tips for getting the most out of your USD30 ticket: - start climbing before 8am. It took 47 minutes, at a steady pace and queueing to the Fresco, to climb from the water gardens to the top when we started. There were big queues forming on the steps just after 8.30am so go early as I'm sure the climb time will increase dramatically as the day goes on. - allow yourself a good hour at the top to really soak in the atmosphere, incredible view and ruins. The climb down took about 30 minutes so all in all we spent approximately 2.5 hours there. - get a guide. There are people at the bottom of the climb offering their services but they aren't pushy and will stop with some acknowledgment. Ask your hotel to recommend someone. The information I was told about King Kasyapa fortress at the top was beyond anything in a guide book. - wear trainers with good support. I saw old Sri Lankan ladies climbing in flip flops and bare feet but us westerners need a little more support. There are some rocks to clamber over at the top and on the way down. We did see more than one tourist slide down loose soil towards the bottom of the rock which could have been nasty had they just been in sandals. - take plenty of water as there's no where to buy it as you enter the park or on the way up. There's plenty being sold after the climb down but until then there's nothing. - put on suntan lotion. There's barely any shelter on the climb up or at the very top so you will definitely need it. - shorts and vest tops are absolutely acceptable attire for men and women. - whilst watching the sunset from Sigiriya would be amazing, there is no lighting on the way down so if you do plan to do it then you need to take that into account. - wasps: there are a number of nests near the top which you can see as you walk up from the Lions feet. They don't cause a problem normally but do become angered by a lot of noise causing them to swarm. The local people are amazing at isolating the swarm and keeping the tourists safe so please don't worry about it. People do get stung, according to my guide, but if you follow the instructions of the local people you'll be fine. Whilst I'm sure the view of Sigiriya is beautiful from Pidurangala, and you'll get some amazing pictures, I think it would be a travesty to leave Sri Lanka refusing to climb Sigiriya because of USD 30 - a fraction of what it cost to get you there in the first place.

We took an early morning visit here. Stunning location but expensive and so so busy. Queuing was chaotic so come prepared. We arrived at 08.00, might be worth arriving 07.00. Views from the top were fantastic. Not recommended for anyone who struggles with steps or height. 15 minutes in the museum also recommended.
My sons were initially concerned at the cost but the care taken with these grounds explained that perfectly. This was a great experience.
Good place, great climb and nice sights and scenery not to be missed. Worth every single dollar contributed!

Let me keep this short: it's a large rock with lion paws. Nice view from the top. You climb the stairs for 30-45 minutes depending on how crowded the place is. There are a few wasp nests closer to the end of your ascend - these did not look particularly dangerous and everyone including school kids tried to keep quiet while around the nests to avoid making the wasps nervous. Overall, I felt it was an interesting experience. The only downside was the price: USD 30 or the same amount in rupees at the current FX rate for foreigners (see the photo). As nearly always the case with tourist attractions in Sri Lanka, the value for money felt very poor.
Lots of steps in 30 degree heat but the history, building remains and view are stunning. 1000 years older than Macchu Pichu! Well worth it.
Worth the climb but very busy. As a non Sri-Lanka you pay 92 times the rate: 4620 roepi versus 50 roepi for a native.. that's a bit 'over the top'
A little over-crowded, and if you are fearful of heights, avoid. One of those sites you must see whilst in Sri Lanka.

You will be stunned. Make sure you have good shoes to climb. Some basic fitness comes in handy.Also keep in mind that the steps are quite high. If you are afraid of heights, you may not really enjoy some of the steep stairs. The view is fantastic.

the place includes the old water gardens, the fresco's of the aspara's, the lion's citadel and a museum. Near the museum you will find a place to drink and eat a quick bite. Expensive ticket but worth the visit. Take a bottle of water, specially the visit of the citadel takes energy. Watch out for the monkeys near the cafeteria Restrooms are near the cafeteria and in the museum

At 30 dlrs per adult this is probably the most expensive entry fee in Sri Lanka, but it's also a very memorable experience you won't want to miss. A very long climb to the top but with interesting things to see all the way up and a great feeling at the top where you visit the site of the former king's palace and grounds, with huge 360 degree views. Go slowly, ideally not in the hottest part of the day, and enjoy the monkeys. Highly recommended!

The huge climb to the top is energy consuming, specially on hot days but woth the view from the top is specatular on the top you only will find some ruins and the king seat, at the bottom of the stears you will find the 2 paws of the long gone lion. buy water before entering the place because you will not found a place on site!

We climbed the rock in the early morning and were back in our hotel for breakfast. It's hot in Sri Lanka so we made the most of the morning coolness. We had our driver hire a guide for us so we didn't have the hassle of bartering or changing prices on our return. The guide explained everything really well so we were much better informed than if we'd tried to do it on our own. I'm not a fan of heights but with a lovely guide holding my hand on the scary bits I was able to reach the very top. I thought the worst bit was the spiral staircase so everything after that was easy! The views were amazing but what captivated us was the history and the planning of the whole palace! Simply amazing and incredibly well set out. I'm so glad we made this a part of our trip to Sri Lanka. The guide was well worth the $10 we paid.

I went to the Sigiriya Lion Rock after a long drive from Colombo. It was a hot and dry day, so the steps are easy to manage. Hand rail and metal steps are constructed especially at the very steep parts. We went with a guide, and he explains the history of this location. This makes the climb more meaningful. Some parts along the climb was extremely windy. We stopped many times during the climb due to strong wind. Though the climb is tedious and the entrance fee of USD30 is quite high, this place definitely worth a visit. It took us 2 hours to go to the top of the hill and return
You need good shoes and some water with You. But it definitely worth effort.Preferably eary in the morning , view is fantastic.

Steeped in history, largely preserved and an active half day out for any visitor to the area. Probably better with teens who will enjoy the trek up the rock face. If you only visit Sri Lanka once, then this 1st century, iconic site is a must. It is close to other significant cultural sites, so worth staying in the vicinity for a couple of days. Also close to a large elephant sanctuary. We stopped over on our way to the beautiful and tranquil East coast. Lots of reasonably priced guest houses nearby with great curries on offer. Don't take my word for it, go and experience it for yourselves. Picture of a bathing pool at the summit.

My wife and I climbed up lion rock on are first day in Sri Lanka. We did this around 11am witch happens to be the hottest part of the day so if you are going to do it best time is around 7/8 o'clock in the morning. It takes around 40 minutes to get to the top if going at a steady pace. As you go up there are parts where the steps do get tight and narrow. But once you are up there the view is amazing. The history behind it is also interesting. In total it's 1200 steps to the top. If you are unsure weather to do it or not then I 100% say do it as it is one of those unforgettable moments.

There is so much to see at Sigiriya World Heritage Site beyond the amazing Lion Rock.  I would recommend highly to arrive early as it isn't pleasant climbing in the heat.  Also you want to have enough time to really see and enjoy the whole Site as there are historical ruins spread throughout which shouldn't be missed. The paintings were amazing (although you cannot photo them) The actually climb up to Lion Rock and the fortress atop I found more difficult on the way up than the way down (my driver who accompanied me said the opposite for him!) however it's definitely worth it. At the top it was really hot with a cool breeze although in some places it was more of a warm breeze and thus quite uncomfortable. Don't miss this if you have an appreciation for cultural historical and natural sites. Children and various aged people were making the climb - you just take your time. There's only a few places at the very bottom to buy refreshments and water (and souvenirs although they'll be tourist prices!) so make sure to take enough water and snacks.

Sigiriya is another UNESCO World Heritage Site and despite the challenging climb to the top, the experience and view are worth the sweat-inducing hike! I spent close to three hours total walking around, hiking to the top and exploring the site.  It was well worth it for the historical experience and the views. IF YOU ARE AFRAID OF HEIGHTS, this may be challenging.  Even though I am not afraid of heights, I did get squeemish at times, but powered through it.  Going up is much more challenging than coming down, and the trip IS worth it. Be sure to bring WATER with you... it is available for sale AFTER you climb down, but NOT before you enter.

Here are a few tips: if you want to hike on the top of the lion rock, wake up early and be ready before 8am otherwise it will be crowded and you gonna have to queue to reach the top and it might take a while! You can visit the museum afterwards... The hike will take 1 hour on average if it's early!! It's definitely worth it but you should wear sport wear - you gonna sweat that's for sure...! ^^

After climbing Pidurangala rock I met some travelers who chose this climb over Lion's rock. The view was great and it seemed to be enough of the experience. After reading some of the reviews of Lion's rock I was in two minds about climbing - it's expensive and VERY busy! Despite this, we decided to do it and I'm glad we did! It's a completely different experience to "Cheap rock" and the view is breathtaking! The historical element adds a magic that cancels out the annoying moments (of waiting in queues & being surrounded by soooooo many other tourists). We didn't get a guide (we just read the brochure that comes with the ticket) but found the information provided sufficient. Taking away the fact that it costs $30, it was highlight!

You don't have to be the fittest and you can be scare of heights as I am, but you will overcome your fears by concentrating and breathing normally. I would rate this as one of the worlds best climbs with amazing historical significance. It's not that hard to do, just get in line take you time and rest when you need a break. You instantly appreciate the significance of this rock when you reach the top and the how and why it played a huge part of this country's history. The 360 degree view to the surrounding horizon is amazing and should drive anyone to reach the top. It is a pity that the archeological features and areas at the top are not more protected as tourists do damage and should think more of future generations who will want to enjoy it as well.
Do it!  It's scary in places but well worth it and very well thought out. Don't miss the museum first.
The climb is relatively easy since there are decent steps the whole way up. The surroundings and the view from the top is stunning. Pay a guide and learn about the interesting story.
The climb is relatively easy, since there are decent steps the whole way up. The surroundings and the view from the top is stunning. Pay a guide and learn about the interesting story.

Nice place, protected site and could imagine the vision of the king, always wear pants to avoid any embarrassment as we go up wind might blowup our skirts.if you have a small kid, bring water bottle with you

Great views, avoid large hats as you go uphill wind blows your hats off, also avoid wearing loose garments or skirts, wear pants to avoid any embarrassment as we go up wind might blowup our skirts.if you have a small kid, prepare yourself, bring waterbottle with you to quench the thirst.

Unique site that is well worth the visit. The ruins at the top are quite basic, but the view is amazing. The rock as well looks in amazing the the flat landscape. There are a lot of steps, but it is done well and even quite unfit people can definitely make it up. Those scared of heights though, the final ascent and descent was very hard!
Awesome site and well worth the climb up to the top. The scale of the citadel is amazing. We both really enjoyed our visit especially those amazing views!

This definitely exceeded our expectations and the kids were delighted they'd climbed it when we got to the top!  Incredible to see what had been built on top of this rock and wonderful views too - definitely worth doing.

Not for unfit or people scared of heights! Well worth the 1000 plus steps though - amazing views and breeze at the top. Quite a few vendors hassling you at various stages - some trying to assist you up steps! Well worth the walk up though
Lots to see but need to drive between sites - found it was a little too much on a hot day with children but amazing to see

There are A LOT of steps to get to the top - however, it's just fine to climb with flip flops! It's really hot up there, so prefer to climb early in the morning or in the late afternoon. There were lots of locals selling guiding services - we didn't take one, but could have been nice to get even more about the attraction. Cute monkeys on the rest place before the last steps.

Interesting views but it is outrageous that foreigners are charged more than double what local people have to pay.Surely there should be one set figure for a person to enter and the review by Pumpkinny  does not consider this. I would recommend that tourists avoid all places like this where the charges are similar.

The museum at the entrance provides a lot info on Sri Lankan culture and history. Unfortunately, after that it mostly ruins and rubble... The rock itself is interesting as a geological formation, but there is no monument to see at the top. The best feature is the view, which is similar to other high points in the area.

Firstly I have to say I'm not sure why lots of reviews complain about the price. It's a world heritage site  and as you walk around you can see the level of maintenance being applied to maintain it for generations to come. It cost us about £24 each which compared to some National Trust attractions in the UK is a bargain. It's definitely worth getting there early (7.30 -8.00am) to avoid the queues and the heat later in the morning. There are lots of locals hanging around offering to guide you or hold your hand on the stairs. A polite no thanks is all that's needed. Make sure you take some water. After walking through the gardens you start the climb up the c.1200 steps to the top. Looks daunting from the bottom but doable if you take your time. Lots to see on the way up including the remaining frescos which are reached by climbing up the spiral metal staircase and the mirror wall. The final climb after seeing the lions feet is slightly scary but well worth it when you get to the top. The views are just amazing. If you think you may only visit Sri Lanka once don't miss out on this - you can spend as much time as you want to here so definitely worth the entrance fee. It is spectacular in terms of the history and the innovation behind the creation of the many features.

When you visit Sigiriya you will understand why it has a UNESCO world heritage award. This was one of the visits during our trip round Sri Lanka and is well worth the visit. Perhaps not for those suffering with Vertigo but the views are well worth the effort of going up.

My third visit to the rock, this time whilst conducting a food and culture tour of the island. A new addition to the experience is a large contingent of wayside 'helpers', who initiate conversation and will not leave your side and Bingo! you have 'hired' yourself a helper (at an undisclosed cost). The climb although strenuous for someone with average fitness does not call for assistance. If you do need their help, do yourself a favour and negotiate a price prior to accepting their help. Waiting until the end is not advisable. If you do not need them just say a firm 'No' and most of them will leave you alone unlike the 'helpers' at Mihintale Rock who don't seem to understand the word spoken in any language! Having said all of that, this is just an annoyance compared to the magnificence of the overall experience of this place. Do yourselves a favour and climb this rock. Whilst pausing at the 'Lions Gate' look up and to the left for the hornet nests dangling off the rock face. Other standouts of this place are the ancient water fountains, natural showers and of course the frescoes!

Though we were a bit put off by the price at first we were all glad we did this. Amazing views from the top, interesting ruins and the monkeys were cool too. Apparently 4pm is the best time to go as it's a bit cooler and by the time you're up it'll be sunset. We went earlier and it was still great!

Take comfortable walking shoes and plenty of drinks with you. Walking that many steps would be difficult even without the extreme heat and humidity! However the views at the top speak for themselves. The fact that this still stands as an ancient city from 1AD is absolutely incredible! Be warned - go first thing in the morning or in the evening. We did this at midday and it was therefore too hot and too crowded. There were children visiting but due to the number of (sometimes slippy) steps I wouldn't recommend anyone with small children to visit.

This is a UNESCO world heritage site. it was a rock fortress. It is one of the best-preserved examples of ancient urban planning and the masterpiece of architecture in Sri Lanka. King Kashayapa selected this site for his new kingdom (477-495 CE). You can see here Frescoes, Graffiti, Mirror wall, and Garden. The final climbing on the staircase you can see Lion Terrace.

Only discremination is in tickeing bcz for locals it's very cheap & for foreign tourist it's huge. But bilieve me it's worth to pay that money go on the top. The place is huge crowdy, so be mindful about the steps & go upwards.

If you do nothing else while in the cultural triangle you need to take the time to climb Sigiriya rock (Lion rock) the experience was fantastic and the views surreal. If you take your time this rock can be climbed by people with low to medium fitness, and be particularly careful of the helpers who will try to accompany you to the top for a fee.

We visited this as a family (2 adults & 2 kids). Went to the place at around 3 PM. We hold Indian passport, so got tickets at half price. - We did not take a guide. Beware of all the guys who ask you if you need a guide as you climb up. - We took a bottle of water (risky due to monkeys we realized) & wore comfortable shoes & a towel - Preferably wear shorts & short sleeve top to help beat the heat. Free flowing dresses may not be suitable, as it is very windy as you climb up the rock - Do not carry any food. The monkeys on the way are a big menace and scare the hell out of people. They can track the people with food bags, run & chase them. At one point, we saw monkeys on both sides of the ladder & my older son went down half way (he climbed the second half later). A monkey climbed on a lady's back ahead of us and it is very dangerous when you are at such a height. So please give up the food craving for safety reasons. - Beware of wasps on the way - If you are scared of heights, please don't attempt this climb - After all this .. what you see up the rock is just amazing !! Enjoy & soak up in the nice scenery there. Be careful about the heights & especially if you have kids with you.

Unfortunately the main attraction in Sigiriya is with ca. 30 USD overpriced. The park and the walk up is quite nice, but you can get plenty of nice or even better hikes and walks in Sri Lanka for zero money.

This is a fascinating place to visit - be warned if you have a wasp allergy as there are lots of wasp nests on the way up. My partner is scared of heights and still managed this, but make sure you take a guide with you, who will help you if you freeze! It is a long way up so go early to avoid the heat. A must-do in Sigiriya
Loved it! Go early in the morning and take a hat, water and snickers. It is amazing how they could build such royal city in those heights!!
Very beautiful rock, the climb is not hard, you can take your time, it is really worth it! The amazing view is so beautiful! Don't skip this when you are in Sri Lanka!!!
This is beautiful, after this you can climb the Lions rock, it is really worth it! It takes 2-3 hours to walk from the entrance to the top and back to the tuk tuk!

Absolutely great place to see in Sri Lanka. The architecture is phenomenal and the paintings are really great. Just take enough water with you, because the climbing can be quite hard. Note you should really wake-up in the morning to get there and visit the site as soon as it opens. Indeed, you might have many tourists with you if you come later and you will suffer a bit more of the sun and temperature. Only sad point, you cannot take pictures of the famous paintings even without a flash, it was a bit disapointing.
It's a tough climb but worth it.  ABSOLUTELY DO NOT GO WITHOUT BOTTLED WATER!  There is none once you start the climb.

I was really looking forward to this visit. I took a bus from Fort Colombo to Dambulla and then took another bus from Dambulla to the citadel. I think I was the only person taking the bus to and from the citadel as I didn't see any other tourists on the bus. Once I got off, I did notice there are guest house or hostels or hotels close by the entrance of the citadel. I walked in and saw a bunch of monkeys. I stayed away from them as I've read its dangerous to approach them. I bought my ticket for $30, which is the most I've paid for an admissions ticket to a natural wonder. I'm going to ignore paying this price and try to enjoy my day at this historical site. Once I was approaching the citadel, hordes of locals posing to be tour guides approached me. They were very aggressive in trying to persuade me to pay them money for tours. There were also locals in the area was also trying to help me up the stairs. It's very insulting for them to want to help me even though I look young and fit. Also they kept touching me when I was saying "No don't touch me, I don't need your help" repeatedly. They wanted money in return for their poor effort to give service. I was determined not to let this bother me, but there are locals who scanned my body with their eyes to determine if they can steal something from me. Perhaps this happened to me since I was traveling alone. All of these combined made the environment feel unsafe at the bottom of the citadel. The walk up to the top was more enjoyable as there were less locals trying to get money from me. It's an easy walk up. I was often slowed down the the mass of tourists. Today was a cloudy day, so I couldn't watch the sunset. However it was an opportunity to go back down and catch the bus before dark. Ask the guards for bus information if you decide to take the bus back into town. Overall, I didn't think the $30 was justified for my experience. Too many tourists, too many locals trying to coerce me, and the top wasn't as spectacular as I thought it would be. The view was nice, but there were many locals off in the distant burning something because I can see the smoke rising up. The air just doesn't seem as fresh as I saw the 10+ smoke pits. I can now say I checked one thing off my life goal list. This is possibly one of the top 10 wonders of the world, so its good visit. I probably won't go back to Sri Lanka, so its best to take advantage of this opportunity.
This sight should be on your list when visiting Sri Lanka. It is a nice walk up the stairs.. don't be afraid of heights!! The view is really great!
Such a wonderfully well maintained area. Fascinating history, amazing view!! We climbed up with two small boys and they managed well but would suit the fit and night so faint hearted.

We visited this with our family and were overwhelmed with the intriguing story, the structure itself and the views. We hired a local guide for 2.000 rupees, which was really worth it to explain everything you look at. We visited at 4 PM, when the heat was doable. Early in the morning is also good, but around noon I would not recommend to walk the 1200 stairs. If you visit Sri Lanka, you must definitely visit this place.

We visited and got to the grounds around 9.30/10am. The walk leading to the ticket booth around the middle rampath was beautiful. You can see the old moats full of waterlillies and monkeys scurrying around the trees. Tickets are 4500 SLR and there was no queue. Ticket booth is by the cafe and toilet block then you go via another entrance booth. It goes without saying it's very steep and uneven in some places so sensible shoes needed. Would be very slippery in the wet. Take plenty of water as nowhere to purchase once you are in. The floating stairs and spiral staircase to the top are nerve racking. I dont like heights but if you dont look down and go slowly it will be ok. View from the top is beautiful. Easy to spend a long time enjoying the view. Decent is less daunting and tuktuks at the exit if you are too tired to walk back to the  hotel! On exiting at around 1.30pm the queues were no bigger than the morning, if not possibly less as falling in the middle point of half day tours. Really dont think crowds would be an issue. Definitely would recommend. Worth going out your way to see.
Just so interresting to see what old civilisation had bought to the people. Well maintained access. great surounding and view.

This site has to be on everyone's "not to be missed" list of things to do if they visit Sri Lanka.  The site is like a Machu Pichu meets Ayers Rock but with an incredible history and feats of engineering!

An amazing place to visit. Would definitely recommend. Make the climb if you can. You need a basic level of fitness and mobility. Young children or those with health or mobility issues would struggle to make the climb. As would anyone with vertigo issues. However, even if you can't climb, a visit is still worthwhile as the gardens and ruins below are lovely and the view of the rock good. There is a museum and cafe but we did not use either so can't comment. It's very hot so take water and sunscreen. Very windy the day we visited so hats would not stay on unless tied/tight fitting. Wear trainers or similar and carry only a small rucksack, space can be tight in the steps.

Definitely worth a visit while in Sri Lanka. It has such a rich history and a great story behind it. Be prepared physically for it as the climb can be tiring if you're not fit or an outdoor person. The view at the top is fantastic. Definitely worth the climb and glad we did it

We already saw the Sigiriya Rock from the distance but today we actually visited this Unesco Heritage site. After a visit to the museum which really helps to understand the background of Sigiriya we started to climb the rock. It was rather windy but that was fine as the temperature was rising very fast. If you want to visit go there early in the morning. Once on top the view is amazing!! This is an absolute must-see/visit

We have done the tour during the first days of our Sei Lanka tour. We arrived there at 11 am - entry fee was a bit pricy (USD30) but worth it. The area is clean and the wall paintings, the view and the museum are worth the money. It took us around 45 min to climb up, easy walking not so exhausting even for not well trained people. It was a bit windy the day but still impressive to see he landscape. Be careful with taking pictures of the wall painting, it's prohibited and officers are very serious about that and will charge you immediately. Maybe you have a better chance to take a shot at the museum (even if a replica only). It's a must see in Sri Lanka.

If you visit Sri Lanka do visit Sigiriya Rock!!! It is one of the main sights, a really magnificent experience! It is surely recommended that you have a guide to inform you about the history of the monument and describe what you see. Though you have to climb enough stairs to the top, the spectacular view is worth it!

Absolutely awesome archaeological history. Definitely worth a visit if visiting Sigiriya. Allow at least half a day to explore  everything if you have a driver or you can cycle the whole thing which I'm sure takes much longer

There is amazing view from Sigiriya rock and it is well worth the climbing/walking. I thought it wasn't hard and if you can climb stairs and walk well, you should be able to do it. The history behind the lion rock is very interesting, and we had a guide who tolled us all about it. I really recommend getting some background information either by means of a guide or by reading about it beforehand. One of my highlights when visiting Sri Lanka and highly recommended!
Nice Historical Value.. Though only the Remains remain! 50% Discount for SAARC Nationals

This is a great experience not to be missed when visiting Sri Lanka. The climb is very easy, took us around half an hour and we went quite early in the morning to beat the crowds, which were already starting to gather during our descent at around 9am. Stunning views from the top, would recommend to anyone thinking about going.
I am pleased to see it's not just me who was shocked at further hikes in the entrance fee

I first visited in 1992 and have been several times since. To be honest not a great deal has changed in the last 25 years although there has been some restoration work here and there. The one thing that has changed however is the price and frankly $30 is really pushing it beyond what is reasonable. Families with teenage children end up shelling out a very large sum of money and I don't think it's justified when considering the lack of any real activity conservation wide and the minimal input for the benefit of the paying guests. That said Sigirya rock is one of the places to see on the world let alone SL. It's well worth the effort and one marvels at the huge amount of work that must have gone into building this place. Theories about its original purpose seem to have changed over the years and I would very much have enjoyed a look around the museum. However it is situated by the entrance rather than by the exit which I feel would be a much better idea. Over time this place seems to be attracting more and more visitors. The climb though testing should be within the capabilities of most reasonably fit adults though why some insist on dragging young children and even babies up is beyond me. Therefore it's best to avoid the rush which means visiting early or late in the day. It also means you get a somewhat cooler and less sweaty climb. Not to be missed if you can afford it but if the Sri Lankan authorities continue to behave in this way towards tourists then they will tarnish their reputation as a wonderful tourist destination. I would add that here ought to be some obligation for places that are given World Heritage status by UNESCO to moderate entrance fees.
If you have too much money or if you're really interested in old monastries/palaces.

This venue as attested by many others before me is a MUST do however to escape the crowd I can only suggest that you should start early . Am unsure whether it is allowed but I think it would be judicious to be there by 7am. We arrived a little after 0930am, but already the masses were there. Having said that, I still enjoyed this visit. The grounds at the top leave you a dumb founded as to how it was built. The grounds are pristinely clean and the vistas at the top were truly breathtaking. A few notes to share. Getting to the top involves a lot of steps thus for those who have a physical disability  perhaps this may present an issue. As for those who have issues about contending with the fear of heights I can only think that climbing the stairs may  be a little daunting. The winds can get gusty and at times make you question your balance so be sure to give your full attention when you and where you walk around or take the stairs. Last but not least, unless parents are willing to physically carry their toddlers up, this visit is NOT suitable for children who cannot tolerate walking on their own for at least 4 hours continuous walking

A truly unforgettable place from the water gardens and 5' komodo-like lizards and monkeys to the carvings and paintings at the base, to the scary stairs drilled into the rock cliff, to the gorgeous cave paintings to the structures at the top of this cliff, to the forever views up there.  It's remarkable that ancients could build these beautiful memorials all around.  Sigiriya is not to be missed.

Amazing part of Sri Lankan history. Again a 5 min drive from Fresco Water Villa. After buying our expensive tickets, we proceeded to the museum which is neither greatly represented neither potrayed. Climbing the Lions Rock was not going to be easy but we were not going to lie down without a fight. Me and my son counted around 827 steps from the base to the top. There is a stopover near Lions foot where u can rest and terminate and the monkeys give you company or continue to the top. The views from the top are just amazing but not the same from Pidurangala. Secondly climbing down is quite scary as the steps are not in any proper shape. Rightly called Citadel of Sigiriya and a must do if you can. Entrance - LKR 4620 for foreign tourist (Rip off) and LKR 2310 for SAARC countries only if you carry your passport. Notes - we did it noon time so weather was pleasant after 02:00 pm and is great in the evening. Rush is also almost nil. -Carry sunglasses, hat, backpack with water sunscreen and wet tissues and a camera. -Get yourself relieved as no options anywhere in between. -Guides will join you offering help and you will not know they got hired so be careful. Study about the place before climbing and save money.

Lovely experience. We only made it to the lions feet from the bottom as we have two young boys who where sweaty tired and grumpy at that stage haha, but I hope if we return to Sri Lanka they can make it to the top as it is a fair climb. Plus it was very busy packed with school children at that point. Gorgeous vistas, not for those who are scared of heights. Lots of wild life and tourists hahaha! Very well maintained and interesting museum at the beginning o the tour. Highly recommend you visit!!!

I have to echo the sentiment of the majority of reviewers here; the rock is clearly a natural spectacle but the entrance fee ($30) is, for me, just too much. If this much is to be paid then you want to feel that you get value for money and I felt like I didn't here. The site is, however, perfectly accessible and though it is a bit of a climb, this shouldn't phase most hill walkers. Of course the views are stunning and in this regard it is well worth a visit. It is very hot but I was not as exposed to the sun as I thought I would be; the usual sun screen and hat would be advised though. Would recommend but am still grouchy about the price (perhaps I'm just tight though!!).

The rock is the main reason for coming to Sigiriya. The climb isn't too difficult if you're fit and healthy and it  took us 28 mins to climb at 7.30am without the mass onslaught of tourists.  The views from the top are spectacular and the grounds surrounding it are beautiful. We were able to see elephants drinking at a waterhole from the top which was lovely. Would definitely recommend.

I visited on a windy and cloudy day, so heat was not an issue, but I am sure it gets unbearably hot in the sun. The climb is manageable for most levels of fitness as you can break it up and stop briefly in a few places. The remnants of the gardens at the foot of the rock are actually very interesting and picturesque. The 'mirror wall' is a little anticlimactic - don't expect much more than a slightly shiny wall. The remains of the palace on the top of the rock need you to use your imagination - but it is quite easy to imagine how grand the whole complex must have been. There are also some amazing views of the surrounding countryside. I also thought it made for really interesting people-watching. You can see everything from the large extended Sri Lankan family, to the most stereotypical loud and clueless American tour group, to the overly earnest small parties of British backpackers, to the German couples in overly practical footwear, to the Chinese group taking pictures of everything. In short, everyone seems to live up to stereotype as much as possible.

Yes it is expensive at $30 but it's a must do. The museum at the beginning is well laid out and well translated to English. It give you an idea of how incredible this place must have been. The ascent to the top is well marked and is all steps, but very steep! Would recommend going early not only to miss the heat of the day but also to miss the crowds..being in a human traffic jam halfway steepest part of the rock is not fun! The top of the rock has amazing 360 views and also many ruins, including a swimming pool. We also came across many monkeys and, unbelievably 2 dogs. Overall a great experience once you get over the price tag.
Wonderful site ; beyond wonderful, but the staircases are pretty scary if You don't like heights. And watch them monkeys!
Apart from the amazing views there is plenty to see and walk around once you get to the top. The ruins are worth checking out.

Surely one of the highlights of any trip to Sri Lanka. Best to visit Sigiriya as early as possible to avoid the strong heat. A guide helps to bring the place to life. Be warned the climb is quite steep in parts. We had no problems with hornets. A must see in Sri Lanka in my opinion.

First we had a quick visit to the museum, the large scale model and depictions of what the palace looked like was interesting, also the crocodiles in the surrounding ponds was a highlight for our children. As you walk up to the rock you pass through beautiful water gardens, preserved examples of ancient urban planning. The rock climb will test some peoples fitness level, the climb up the rock is hard going but worth it. Make sure you have plenty of water and patience as it can be slow going with the crowds. Breathtaking views from the top, a must see when you visit Sri Lanka. We did the Cave Temples in Dambulla on the same day and found the two sites very manageable on the one day with our two teenage children.

Fantastic experience ! My 60th Birthday was celebrated with a visit to this Rock ! I had researched the Rock on Trip Advisor, and watched numerous U tube Videos.  I count myself as fairly fit, though suffer badly, in recent years, with heights ! We were a party of 6, travelled from our Hotel in Kalutara, with tuk tuk, to catch the 04.30 hrs train to Colombo, another train from Colombo to Habarana, then tuk tuk to the Rock !  8 hours of travelling, and started the climb around 1 pm. My strong will to do this climb and also to enjoy the views and cultural aspects of this world heritage site, ensured that, in spite of the heat, and fear of heights, I made it ! Supported by 5 family members, we climbed it in 45 minutes, spent an hour at the top, and then 45 minutes back down. Unbelievable experience.  Make sure you do it ! Read reports of rickety stairs, etc ......... absolutely rubbish.  I'm an Engineer, and I can assure you that the steel walkways, steps and handrails are absolutely solid, and very reassuring when feeling the exposure. A very satisfying day, followed with an overnight near Dambulla, morning Taxi to Kandy, then brilliant train ride to Colombo and back to our Hotel.  What an adventure, don't miss it !

Absolutely must do. Overpriced as hell, but as they say: when in rome.... You simply have to go here if youre in sri lanka, and the ticket office knows this, so prepare to be robbed of your money for at max, 3 hrs worth of entertainment (unless you get off to museums)...

Basically, you have to go here if you go to sri lanka, but be prepared to overpay for entrance. Feels absolutely horrible when they literally (exactly) make a 92.4 times over markup when comparing local prices to foreigner prices (50 rupee vs 4620) rupee. And if you're a student, you will not get any discounts unless you have some weird green card thing which they conveniently chose albeit im european and we never use that specific card. Also: There are some guys selling hand made puzzle boxes throughout the bottom part of sigiriya, they make absolutely amazing souvenirs but they will try to overcharge you, a few of me and my friends tried to buy some, original price for one was 6800, got him down to 5000, bought one, the next guy we brought down to 4000 and bought it, and kept doing this until we brought one down to 1600. Basic tip: if he asks for 4000, say 1500, pretend to be interested, then walk away. He. Will. Follow. You. And will incrementally bring down the price. Gl xx

This is a must visit. A palace built on top of a 200m high rock. It has to be seen to be believed. The climb up is steep and you must go early to avoid huge queues but once up it is amazing. You can see the remains if the full palace complex including the throne and swimming pool.

Definitely worth going but beware it's a hike! All up hill and not for the faint hearted, infirm, or vertigo suffers out there. Saw a few people getting the jeebs!! However, great views and a very culturally significant destination in the country so if that's what you are after it's a must see. Enjoy but take your time if you must, it's not a race...

Had read reviews and was a bit hesitant but to no avail. Climbed with a 5 year old. Took an hour. Was amazing at the top. We all agree this was a highlight of the trip. That includes my husband and myself plus an 11 yr old a 13yr old and the 5 year old. You don't need a guide unless you want everything pointed out. I would recommend go early beat the crowds and the heat.
A place you gotta go but it's climbing a rock with a good view and not much more than that. Go early. We were there when they opened (7 am) so we avoided the worst heat and the crowds.

Jaw-dropping views, but be prepared for a long climb before you even get to the bottom of lion rock. We didn't think my Mum (age 76) would make it to the top, but she did with help from our trusty guide! Beware guides/touts on the way up who insist they have licenses but will then try to charge you once they've "assisted" you on the way up

Incredible that anyone built a palace on top of a sheer rock 1,500 years ago, how it was done is hard to imagine. It is beautiful. A few tips though, take plenty of water, nothing available inside, I suggest bypassing the spiral staircase as it takes you to some small rock paintings and back down again, no way worth the wait as the stairs will be lined with slow moving people. We went midday, hot but not as many visitors. Be prepared for the (by Sri Lankan standard) very expensive ticket. Do not go to the museum it is a very inappropriate huge ugly concrete mess that resembles a multi story car park. The small collection is lost in the vast ugliness. Anyway still amazing to see it. Sri Lankans are rightly very proud of this heritage.

This is a must visit place in Sri Lanka. SIgrira rock is a hill jutting out of the plains. The top of the hill was a rock fortress with a Palace within it's confines. Though most of it is lost and just the foundations remain. But it still is a reminder to the architectural feat achieved by the people of that era. To begin with, the entry fee is extremely high for foreigners, an equivalent of US$ 30,00 per person. We got to know later that all citizens of SAARC countries could get a hefty discount if they produced their passport at the ticket counter. This information was not given to us either by the travel agent, the driver or at the ticket counter. Before you go to Sigiriya please make sure that you are aware of what you should actually be paying as entry fee. E-tickets are also available, so booking online may be a better option. Once yo have the ticket, you are allowed to three different areas, the museum which is right next to the ticket counter, the ancient gardens and lake and the rock fortress itself. The museum is next to the ticket counter and is interesting for those who want to catch up with the history and layout of Sigiriya. From here it is a long walk through what once were the ancient gardens and lakes. Upon reaching the rock, one starts to climb the steps carved into the rocks. This is the easiest part. As we progress, the steps are take over by narrow passageways made by embedding rods into the sides of the rock and making a platform on it. These passages seem to be suspended from the side of the rock. People with vertigo may have a tough time climbing. The passage then leads to a spiral staircase (again suspended in thin air) which ends in a cave. This cave still has the ancient frescos. Further on and after some more climbing we reach a small table land. a place to rest and recoup. A pair of lion"s feet are carved on either sides of the steps leading further up. Another hairy climb and one reaches the top. The top of the rock is flat where remains and foundations of the ancient palace can be seen here. It's left to one's imagination as to what sort of Palace would have stood atop this hill, in all it's splendor and glory. Hats off to those who achieved this feat. The view from here is spectacular !!! Tough Climb but fully worth the visit. Make sure to climb during a cooler part of the day and carry water with you. You will need it.

We thoroughly enjoyed our hike up Lion Rock, well worth the money and very easy to do (coming from someone scared of heights!). Great views from the top and such interesting history. A must see if you're in Sigiriya (or indeed Sri Lanka!).
50cents for locals and $30 USD for visitors. Not worth the money. Avoid till they realise their mistake
Avoid. If you do go be ware of the horrible scammers selling false items. Do not buy stuff from here.

Don't get a guide, it's easy to find your way. Don't believe anyone who tells you otherwise. The Ticket price for foreigners is severely over priced for a climb up a rock, but if you want a photo I guess it's worth it. I wouldn't go in the heat of the day and especially not in the rain, the staircases were steep and somewhat dangerous.  Impressive what they accomplished though.

The achievement of building the palace on top of this place must have been amazing. We absolutely loved everything about it, and it was a very pleasant ride overall. It is better to climb the rock early in the morning or at the end of the day. Bring plenty of water, but be careful with food because there are some very obnoxious monkeys around.
We took our two little boys to the top of the rock. It wasn't arduous. The history of the place is truly staggering. It's a wonderful climb. Yes it's not cheap but it's unique.

We visited with two friends and were allocated a local guide.  The first thing we notice were young lads helping us up the first few steps then running ahead to do the same again.  We realised that they would be expecting a huge tip at the top so asked them too stop.  Unless you want them to, of course.  We had walking poles with us but they were quite unnecessary.  The paths are very good and there is a 'half way' point where one can take a rest, shade, take water etc. There is also a first aid tent if needed.  There is really no pressure until the last part of the climb which is mainly steps so you have to follow the leader and go as slow or fast as the person in front.  There are passing places but it is not for the faint hearted as the steps appear to be hanging on the side of the rock.  Once at the top the views are spectacular and if you're up to it there is even more walking about exploring the area.  Take plenty of water, much more than you think, good stout shoes and, of course, camera.  We took three hours to explore the whole rock and it normally takes two and at the bottom there are many vendors wanting to sell ice cream, drinks etc.

Extraordinary history and amazing archeology, but - as I've shared elsewhere - the policy of overcharging visitors from some countries very, very high entry fees (done throughout Sri Lanka) left a badly bitter taste. To see wealthy Sri Lankans enter for a reasonable price - and struggling students from developing countries denied entry unless they paid a huge fee - was painful to see. All people -- irrespective of their race, nationality, or national origin -- should be allowed entry on the same terms as everyone else...and the practice of different prices should be ended. Charge everyone the same price -- or charge nobody anything at all... This is the fairest approach. And if one wants to discriminate, one can do so on wealth. Let the rich pay the big fees (including Sri Lankans) - and those of modest means what they can afford... each person can be given the dignity of letting the attendants know which group they fall into. For such a wonderful country in so many ways, these different entry fees are seriously detracting from an otherwise pleasant place. It's saddening and disheartening
Highly interesting heritage, with beautiful views. It is expensive but if they indicated where all the money went, it might justify spending that much on an entry ticket.

This is good to see but be prepared for lots of steps and bring water. It is not for the faint hearted as going up the side of the rock you are going up on a spiral staircase and the rest looks like scaffolding. You need to go as early as possible so as to avoid scores of people which slows down the climb.
Go early! We went at 10am & had a fair wait as we climbed each section. Make sure you take a hat and some sunscreen. Views from the top are breathtaking and lots of monkeys on your walk up.

The Sigiriya Fortress is a must see when in Sri Lanka. It is rumored to be one of the 8th wonders of the ancient world. However the site guides ruin it as they disturb you as you enter and try to charge foreigners very high guiding rates.

My friend and I almost didn't go up wondering if it was perhaps overrated.  We are really glad now we decided to go for it.  Despite the pricey entrance fee it was worth it.  I wouldn't advise it though if you are afraid of heights.
Worth every bit of your energy time n money Pls visit respect the place and the heritage Check my review for rates Start early as u can

A long climb awaits and one you must There's the adrenaline that's going to hit you when you are at the trail end So here's a few tips Its probably cheapest to pay in Srilankan ruppes We were asked for our passports I suppose to verify local or foreigners Wear comfy clothes n shoes We paid $30 though in Srilankan it probably would have been just about 1500 or so Carry water ull need it.. there's 1 or 2 water dispensers around The structure that once existed on this 110 high meter rock would have been remarkable now it's more the ruins The journey you take is over nicely done stairs but in the time you'd see the rock cuttings done n you'd wonder how did they do this It's heavy wind as u walk up n beautiful when u reach up There's many guides should u want one but I'd say read the history n off u go Local tour jeeps will take u to the destination for a mere 2 or 3 thousand srilankan Worth every bit n do it early morning Believe they are up by 7 am to start off the climb

It goes without saying this us a must do. While it's a steep climb it doesn't take as long as expected..we did it in 30 minutes. View is amazing and climbing around side of mtn exhilarating. Recommend doing it late afternoon
One could say 8th wonder of the world. It is an amazing work. One who visit Sri Lanka must see this place. Make sure to spare enough time as there is so much to be seen and explore.

We ummed and ahhed over whether to visit Sigiriya, having read negative comments in regards to the crowds and the price, but we decided that we'd regret it if we missed it. This was very much the right decision. The crowds were not so bad at the time we were there - we were at the toilets at 9:30, so probably started actually climbing about 9:45. There are times when you have to stand still and wait, but you need that rest anyway after so many stairs. I also didn't encounter as many touts as the reviews suggested. The frescoes were probably one let down, mostly as we'd already seen prints of them in the National Museum in Colombo. It is definitely a challenging climb up, but the reward is definitely worth it. The terraces and fortifications are incredible, as are the views. I have absolutely no regrets about climbing Sigiriya Rock and would recommend it to everyone.

The place is appox 2 hrs drive from Kandy. The history of this heritage is worth understanding. I would suggest to hire a Guid to understand the history of this palce. To climb the rock there is a moderate hiking, so its prefered you wear some comfortable cloths and shoes.

Lion Rock is a must see on any visit to Sri Lanka.  Start early, before the heat of the day, as it is quite a climb to the top.  The views are completely worth it-even if you are scared of heights like me and out of shape!  There will be people there who want to guide you, and they will expect payment if you accept their help.  Be clear if you are not interested.

Go early since the steps are steep in the sun. Amazing view and the paintings are magnificent. Be aware if you want to walk the rock first and do the museum afterwards due to avoid walking in noon sun your driver should not park in the foreign park place since it is not possible to get back to it after returning to the museum.

AMAZING! If you like historical places, this is a must-go place that you have to visit. Don't forget to apply sunblock all over your body since the weather was really really hot, I still got sunburn until now LOL For locals, you better bring foreigners so you can park your car nearby :D For foreigners: - You can pay by USD (ticket price USD30, while for locals only LKR50/person if I'm not mistaken) - The wind is really strong, be careful with your hats - If you're afraid of heights, just deal with it, don't look around and go straight to the top by the stairs because the view is really amazing from top there! - The best time to arrive there is in the morning before 9 or 10am, otherwise it will be very hot, the sun will be at its highest position and the lighting for your photography won't be good - Don't bring heavy stuffs as you'll get tired easily when climbing the stairs - It might take about 1-1.5 hours to go to the top but depends on your stamina - When you get down, there might be someone playing flute with cobra snake along the exit way to the car park. If you don't want to pay anything, don't stop, just take a look while you walk and don't take pictures, otherwise he will charge you pretty expensive.

This was a delightful treat. Be careful and respectful of the HUGE wasp nests and the monkeys. Myself and a fellow traveller actually had a female monkey jump on our backpacks to take things out. So be forewarned. Also, LADIES be mindful of the men who constantly want to "escort" you up the rock. They are pests and very annoying and don't take no for an answer. They also touch without invitation. Be prepared to have your guard up. However, once you reach the top all of the hassle of the wasps, monkeys and hecklers was worth it.
If you go to Sri Lanka you have to hike the rock. It was not very difficult even with my fear of heights.  Lovely views!

A little arduous but well worth the effort. The 360 degree view of the surrounding areas is just breathtaking. Definitely recommend trekking as early as possible in the day although the path is shady and somewhat cool.
Sigiriya today is a UNESCO listed World Heritage Site. Really amazing view from the top of the rock! I think every sri lankan need to been there.

We hired a guide called Kumaro at the entrance to take us up this lion rock. We are glad we did as we would not be able to do the climb within two hours if we were on our own. He literally took me by the hand to go up and down the steep staircase. Another young guy helped my husband. This place is filled with history and engineering wonders. Therefore a good guide is worth every dollar (cost is USD20 for a guide) who can explain the complicated history and the uniqueness of this rock. Kumaro did that for us. He explained well and intrigued me. He saved the last punch line till the end. He is very professional and we are happy with him. Had we not been with him, it'd have taken us at least double the time to do this amazing climb!

We did this with 2 kids 6 and 8 and all enjoyed it. Was not too hard and great views. Little one did get a bit scared on some of the higher steps but it was all very safe. Apparently an get attacked by wasps which was a bit of concern but didn't eventuate

I loved this place with its fascinating history. The planning was incredible. Thousands visit every day which makes the climb even more difficult. I was glad to make it to the top and back down in reasonable time.

Well worth the climb - the views of Dambulla, Habarana, etc are outstanding. There were a lot of people and we were left queuing for quite a while on the steps, so it is worth going early to avoid the crowds. We went in low season - I can only imagine how busy it must be during the high season!
Yes, lots of climbing, but the views are superb all the way, and once at the top, provides a 360 degree panorama. Must do activity.

Such an achievement to get to the top, and worth every step. Start early as gets very crowded by mid morning, and most stairways are only just wide enough for passing. It is not just a rock but one of the best-designed palaces from the ancient Sri Lanka
Great place to visit, although not for the faint hearted, quite a tough climb in the heat, but worth the effort .

It is quite hard to get to the top but step by step you realize how hard was for the people to live there and how protected was that place from enemy. The view from the top is amazing, looks like you can see the whole Sri Lanka. I think if you go in Sri lanka it should be in your bucket list!

This is definitely a must visit for all travellers within in Sri Lanka, not only is the site seeped in cultural history but the rock itself is magnificent to view when you first approach it, allowing you to take some excellent photos. As you climb to the top you will be able to see the famous sigiriya rock paintings and eventually end up on top of the rock, where the fortress used to lie- the views from here are beautiful, I recommend, bringing a blanket so you can lay down and soak the panorama, especially if you happen to climb just before sunset. Sri Lankan locals must use the designated car park, beware the tuk tuk drivers who will offer to drive you up to the rock, the distance is a mere 500m and is easily accessible by walking. Tourists have their own car park and pay about 35usd i think. Nevertheless, this is an authentic piece of Sri Lankan history you wouldn't want to miss.

This is definitely a must visit for all travellers within in Sri Lanka, not only is the site seeped in cultural history but the rock itself is magnificent to view when you first approach it, allowing you to take some excellent photos. As you climb to the top you will be able to see the famous sigiriya rock paintings and eventually end up on top of the rock, where the fortress used to lie- the views from here are beautiful, I recommend, bringing a blanket so you can lay down and soak the panorama, especially if you happen to climb just before sunset.
