This is a great resting and deciding point as to if you want to continue to the top or not. Walking through the “mirror wall” hallway is quite the experience.  You can imagine what the people from all those centuries ago must have thought as they ambled up the walkway to continue onto the giant lions paws! Sadly, because of a major “Hillary Step” back up at the frescoes’ I was not able to view them, so cannot comment on this part of site. I am not one that does well with heights. At. All.  We’re talking much past the 3rd rung on a ladder and that’s it.  And, while I wasn’t thrilled about going up all the stairs to the top, I did make it.  (Some older guide books mention that the stairs are “rickety”.  This is now longer the case) The steel metal stair case is designed so that you can’t see through the steps as you climb up as they are overlapped one over the other.  That said, going up you are next to the rock face and there is a (narrow) hand railing.  (I also had a VERY PATIENT and UNDERSTANDING guide!) Depending on the time of day that you ascend, you can also (attempt, at least part way) to come down along the “up” stairwell. However, while everyone races to reach the plateau, I would invite readers to truly enjoy the majestic grounds and use your imagination and awe to envision what the grounds would have looked like centuries ago. Excavation has been done along one side to allow you to visually see the massive gardens which once were.  Quite impressive!  The rock gardens are pretty much the same as they were centuries ago! It’s ashamed that many people just race to the top and race back down again to go onto their next itinerary stop. Try to take some additional time and truly enjoy the area and meet some of the local people.  The Sri Lankans are some of the friendliest people that we have ever met! My husband and I went in the afternoon which was just lovely.  The heat of the day was greatly diminished by the  afternoon breeze that is in the air and the views and beginning sunset from the top are breathtaking. The crowds will be less the later in the day you go.  If your schedule allows, I would suggest and recommend the afternoon.  It will allow you some extra time to linger and really enjoy the area and have it show you its beauty. Step back, breathe in and ENJOY!!!!
We went there on a sunny day and wasn't dissapointed. We hired a local guide, which gave alot of information during the ascend to the top. And the view is astonishing.

At $30 per person we hesitated to visit the Lion Rock. We are not sorry that we did it anyway! Off course you can see it and the line of people making their way up from the next rock over, but making the ascent, seeing the fresco's and wandering around the old palace on top off the rock make it worth you while (and kind of your money)!

We went there in the middle of the day!it was bloody boiling and really hard to pass the stairs,don't forget bottle of water and try to go up slowly because you'll have a hard rough to get the top,it's really worth ,you'll find a very nice panorama view from the top of the Sigiriya and also nice paintings and ancient caves on the way:) try to come back before the weather getting dark there's no light and guide there in the darkness

I was disappointed visiting this location, I thought it was expensive to get in 30us dollars.  The grounds were nice but we were harassed by locals wanting to be our guides, then as we started walking the rock about 10 locals appeared wanting to help us up the stairs I said I didn't need help and that I had no money but they wouldn't take no for an answer in the end we just stopped and walked down the locals then demanded money.

This 1000 year old rock fortress in set in a park like setting - spectacular views.  Approx. 1200 steps to the top - steps uneven heights.  Recommended - good hiking boots or shoes and a water bottle.  A cave partway-up has a number of paintings - with a sign "no photographs in the cave" and they mean it - break the rule and you might loose your camera/phone.

We got to Sigiriya Rock as it opened at 7am, to try and beat the heat. it was definitely a good move on our part, as the climb would be a lot harder in the heat of the day. It's an amazing achievement to have built a citadel on top of a sheer rock, but once at the top, the commanding views of the surrounding country side are amazing, and you can get some sort of understanding as to why it was built there. The climb up has you meander past wall art, and impressive rock formations, so it distracts you (a little) from the fact that you are still climbing.

Though climbing is really difficult, but it's worthy experience. If you are from SAARC countries, please bring your passport with you as entry fee is discounted for SAARC country citizens. If you can't do the summit, please try to reach the lions gate at least, the view of the surroundings is simply amazing!

Bring lots of water and maybe some snacks as it can get very hot in the afternoons. You will definitely be tempted to just find a shady spot at the top to stare at Pidurangala so bring lots of water and snacks so you aren't forced to descend early. On the way up you have the option of going up a narrow spiral staircase to see the frescoes - just thought I should highlight that this is optional as it can be fear inducing for some (when you look down it's a straight drop...) And you won't exactly have the option of turning back as it's really, really narrow.

Visited as part of a Mercury Holidays Tour and did not disappoint.... Highly recommended.  Got some great pics.... you do need a bit of 'get up and go' to get up it..... budget a 7am start and a 3 mile trek over hard going terrain and you will have an idea of what to expect however the experience is amazing... Enjoy it.

This was the best thing we did in our trip to Sri Lanka. We got there early (about 730). Tuk tuk driver waited for us. We paid to get a guide and it was well worth it as it explained so much. Walk up took about an hour. Couple of scary spots (spiral staircases and staircase towards the top) where you are hoping what's holding the stairs up is still working properly. Took about an hour to get to the top and 30 mins to come back down. Take some water with you on the climb as you can't buy any at the top. It was fairly shady in some parts and also fairly breezy so wasn't to hot. Entry was 3850 rupees for foreigners. This is a must see place on your trip to SL.

climbing sigiriya was one of the best things  I have ever done. it was a challenge and at times i wondered what i was doing, but what an achievement. there were parts that made my knees shake but well worth it when you get to the top. i didn't walk around the top very much but the views are breathtaking and well worth wobbly knees. But sigiriya was the highlight for me

Climbed all the way to the top for spectacular views for miles around. Definitely recommend going early in the morning as it's much too hot later and gets pretty crowded with people passing on the stairs. Don't forget to take water with you, Sun hat and  cream also a must. There are plenty of levels to stop to get your breath back. Be aware of the young men who want to assist you up and down. They charge a minimum of 2-3000Rs.

It's a unique place in the world and that's the reason why It worths the really expensive price, around 28€ that, for the standards of the country is a lot. Even you can only see the foundations of the ancient Palace, you can smell what was going on, and the rest, gardens, paintings...are really interesting.

We went around 10am to the Lion Rock and after 1200 steps or so, we were on the top. Enjoy the gardens at the entrance, the views while climbing. Do not take pictures where prohibited, we saw a guy having to pay a fine on the spot. Check out the Cobra head rock at the exit and the souvenir shops.

Walking through the terraces up to the base of the rock was lovely. However, when it came to climbing up the rock to the summit or even the lion terrace was just unthinkable for me. Unfortunately there is no changing your mind part way up if you feel you can't go any further (for whatever reason). Which means you have two choices, you climb all the way or you don't climb at all. Our guide describe the climb to lion terrace where the famous frescoes are as the most difficult part of the climb - steep and scary.

Aim to start at 8.30AM to avoid some crowds but especially the heat. There is no doubt there is a lot of climbing but take it easy and plod on and you will be rewarded. Make sure you have sunscreen, a hat and plenty of water. I was surprised how large the area was at the summit. There are old building foundations to see and wonderful views of the surrounding countryside. Well worth the effort.

Climbing Sigiriya was an awesome experience, quite unlike any other hill/mountain I have climbed before. Quite how the ancient king managed to build a fortress at the top of the rock is beyond me, but it is absolutely worth the visit. Very touristy unfortunately, but as the climb is steep, being held up by people traffic is not too bad. The views from the top are quite impressive and you can get a good sense of what it must have been like in its heydey. Humid Sri Lankan weather makes it a sweaty task, but make you sure experience it.

Sigiriya has to be at the top of any agenda when visiting Sri Lanka, quite simply it is stunning. However, visitors should be under no illusion that the climb to the top is not easy for those not used to physical exertion. There are however plenty of places where you can stop, take a breather and simply enjoy the stunning views of the surroundings no countryside. Before you reach the base of the rock there are extensive gardens and ancient ruins, still being excavated in places, to enjoy. On the climb there are frescos of maidens and the mirror wall with it's ancient graffiti. At the summit is the old royal citadel as well as evidence of royal gardens and a bath complex. However, nothing can take away from the views. The day of our visit it was overcast but still very warm. Whatever the weather ensure you take plenty of water, there is none available on the ascent. Finally, there are numerous local 'guides' on the way up, these are not official and are self employed, in other words they will expect a tip. They normally introduce themselves by offering assistance at the steeper parts or to those who appear to be struggling. Shouldn't distract from the overall experience.

Going up all the stairs is very demanding especially if the temperatures are in the high 30s, but all the way up you have to marvel about what mankind can achieve. Its amazing sight to visit, absolutely worth the labor of going up and quite hefty entrance price (30 usd). But once you are up there its just amazing, and this definitely belongs among the top places to visit in the world.

The stairs aren't for the faint hearted (or the weak hearted).  Even though I suffer from vertigo I made it up there & boy it was worth it. For Goodness sake don't go up after midday, it would be in full sun & boiling hot

This climb is a must during your Sri Lankan travels. Suggest you start early, around 7-8am. Allow for two hours up, at the top and down. Do not follow the crowd up the metal staircase attached to the side of the rock - this is not part of the climb and leads to cave paintings only. You'll feel great once you've reached the top!

Get there around 7am or the line of people is all the way up the rock. It took us 1 hour to climb and we started at 7.15 and we could go at our own pace. I was a little scared on the exposed parts of the stairs but I don't like heights, but so pleased I did it.

Entrance fee to the site is extremely expensive. Having done other climbs in Ella and Horton Plains, Sigiriya was considerably easy. You still get a good view of Dambulla at the top. The climb took about 1.5hours up and down, max 2 hours. The rock gets heated up by late morning, so best to climb it in the morning.

It is a place that you be amazed every time you visit. The construction, waterways, the mirror wall and the rock itself are a pleasure to the eye in every angle. The folklore surrounding the discovery and exploration of the rock in early days are even more astounding! The best time to climb the rock is early morning​ before the sun and before the crowds to enjoy the scenery leisurely. Plenty of hotels and guest housed are located within walking distance of the rock. It is a place that one must include in the itinerary to visit in Sri Lanka!

We slept in Damblla for 2 nights, and went to see the rock early morning. It is a steep climb with more than 100 stairs if you want to go up the palace on the top of the rock. Best done early morning before the sun gets intense. It is also pretty to watch if you decide not to climb.

2400 steps up and down... Every step you take up to the base of the rock is via a marble staircase, very cool. Be sure to take the spiral staircase up to see the painted hall with its beautiful depictions. Before taking the staircase to the top, look to the north and you'll see Elephant Rock! Makes for a great photo. Aim to get to the top for 5.30pm to enjoy the glowing red sun set behind the mountains. A very special scene.
must visit and climb all the way up the mountain for the incredible views and antiquities on top of the giant rock

This seems a bit daunting once you first look at how high you will need to climb but it's totally worth it. Bring water and a protein bar as the trek is long, steep and all uphill. Don't display valuables as there are monkeys around that will steal anything shiny.

I did a day trip from Colombo to Sigiriya. I got picked up at 6am and the journey itself takes around 4 hours by car. I spent most of that sleeping so the journey was not as bad as it sounds. Upon getting to entrance to the park I went around the small museum which gives a history of the rock. There are toilets located here and are the only ones until you get back down so it is worth using before the assent. There are no shops here so bring water with you for the climb. There is a 10-15 minute walk through the gardens before you reach the base of the rock which are a good place to take photos of the whole rock. Once you start climbing the stairs it takes about 15 minutes to get to the fresco paintings. There are plenty of areas to stop and rest on the way and a few viewing areas. There are spiral staircases (enclosed) to get to the frescos which are amazingly well preserved. Note they are very strict about not taking photos of the paintings and there are a couple of police officers and park workers enforcing this. Once descending the stairs you pass the mirrored wall and a few minutes later you are at a small flat area which is the start of the lions stairs. This is not for the faint hearted as there are narrow metal stairs attached to the side of the rock. During busy times this can be slow as you are in single file so there is little opportunity to overtake. Once you get to the top you arrive at the highest point in the rock. As you follow the path down the citadel opens up to give some fantastic views of the surrounding countryside. I was lucky it was a clear sunny day (even if it did make the climb harder!). The decent is partially the same route until you hit signs for tourist car park. There are a few merchants selling souvenirs en route but they were not particularly pushy. When you reach the bottom there is a stall selling cold water and soda which was definitely required! Overall a fantastic and unique trip, but beware from Colombo it is a long day with at least 8 hours travelling.
Sigiriya is definitely a must visit heritage site in sri lanka. Go with a tour guide so they can explain the architecture and some interesting mechanisms that were used in the sigiriya centuries ago!

Go early in the morning to beat the crowd - our host at the guesthouse recommended us to get there 6:30am but we slept in and did not make our way there until 9:30am and there was a huge queue already, took us about 1.5 - 2 hrs to get to the top (a hand fan will be needed while waiting in the heat) * for people who have a fear of heights, the stairs from bottom of the lion paw up to the top is seriously scary, especially when you are heading back down* At the top, the view is simply spectacular (we wished we had brought some food for a light picnic, as we were a little hungry after the long queue to the top) The beautiful view, fascinating history of the rock  and adrenaline experience of getting back down is something I will never forget.

This is probably one of the priciest attractions I've been to for what there is. It was $30 to visit a natural rock with a few frescos and ruins on top. Compare this to prices for attractions anywhere else in the world and you wonder how they came up with the price - I paid about $10 to see Pompeii by comparison. Locals pay a bare fraction of this which is quite insulting.

Its pricey. Amazing thing its how people located it those days.Its a must place to visit.1202 steps is alot for me who dont exercise.Try go in the morning as you got more time to spend there and you can take your own sweet time.We climb about 4pm, thinking we can come down by 6pm but  we took more hours. It was dark and we couldnt find our way back.Our driver had to come and assist us down .Go early .The place closes by 6pm. No toilet on our way up or even at the top.Not easy allthe way its steps .You can rest at the stairs .
this is the most famous tourist attraction place in sri lanka. please try to go there early in the morning because during the day time climate is so hot  ,

The climb to the top can be tough as the last section is in full sun. Highly recommend going as early as possible. The ruins are so interesting and the cave paintings are fascinating. We hired a guide at the bottom (US $20) which was more than adequate. He told lots of interesting tidbits about the people and the king, etc. Definitely worth the effort to get to the top.

This place is called as the Eighth wonder of the world. Its a huge rock and inbetween the structure which looks like the lions legs there are steps leading up the rock. One has to definitely wonder how in those days the material would have been transported and such a work executed at a height. Really it qualifies to be a wonder..
Maybe I have been spoiled by Cambodia but whilst this is worth the visit it did not wow me as much as I thought it would, not great on a hot humid day but worth the walk up to see the views

Lion Rock comes with a hefty entrance fee ($30), but we decided to go up anyway as it would have been a shame to come all this way and not go up.  We started our walk at around 8am, which was perfect as it meant it wasn't too hot on the walk up and it wasn't particularly busy. The views from the top are good, although not as good as from Pidurangala.  The walk up was not too strenuous - steps the whole way with a fair amount of stop off points to take in the view. When we were coming down (around 10am or so) there were long queues up the steps, so I would recommend going up early before the crowds arrive!
Such an achievement to get to the top, and worth every one of the 1202 steps! You can rest at every staircase so not too strenuous. This us a must do on any trip to the area.

Its widely  believed to be the palace complex of King Kasspa and there is school of thought that its the palace of King Ravana ( of Ramayanaya the  indian version of oddesy) There is another school of thought that its the palace of King Kuvera( Kubera) who is the brother of King Ravana according to Hindu mythology.( and some say Ravana nd Kuvera are same person) What ever the history may be the citadel palace is undoubtedly and engineering marvel. with fresco at unbelievable height and locations of the rock, a palace complex in the top with water ponds, how they have ascended to the top is still a mystery. the water garden in the ground level consist of ponds with water fountains activated by the pressure of water at the top of the citadel. during rainy season one can see that water fountains bubbling and guess how the fountains would have worked its in its heyday

Go early in the morning for the best experience.  The 1200 steps were tiring but not as exhausting as we had feared (a couple late 60s / early 70s). Plenty of interesting diversions on the way up. Everyone will tell you about the frescoes which are beautiful and impressive - but what impresses more is the sheer size of the complex, and the history it contains. Easy to spend several hours here if you can do so before it gets too hot and are not in a rush to cram in more of Sri Lanka's fascinating history.

First - Please remember to go as early as possible in the morning before it gets to hot. It is really hard to grasp that such a big site could be established under one king. Our guide could the history but he also took some breaks and we got the feeling we got the quick tour.

Ok let's get the steps issue dealt with first ... there is NO "climb" to get to the top of Sigiriya (Lion Rock). Yes there are a lot of stone steps, and then a lot of metal "fire escape staircase " style steps... but no climbing or scrambling. No safety risk and no exposed places. No ladders. Some reviewers on here suggest you need a head for heights - well not really. The key question is - are you fit enough to walk up many flights for stairs. And does a metal walkway bother you? Sure if you get vertigo stay away but I'd say most healthy people can do this - the biggest worry is the Sri Lankan heat. You can even pay a fit young local man to help you with a steadying hand if needed. Also if you don't fancy the enclosed metal spiral stairs to the murals - you can bypass them .. tho it would be a shame as these are the highlight. The murals are amazing artwork - and sadly will one day be destroyed by nature as they are relatively unprotected. The Lion's paws are about halfway up - if you don't feel up to any more stairs you could stay on the large flat landing here .. but again I'd recommend going to the top because it's a fascinating man made marvel. The huge rock hill itself is a volcanic plug BUT the top is a the remains if a once mammoth fortress and palace - all built in millions of clay bricks. Probably Akin to the pyramids in scale when constructed. A few other tips: 1- start early - as gets very crowded by mid morning, and most stairways are only just wide enough for passing. 2- footwear - you cd do it in flip flops but trainers better. Not heels ! Footing is all solid, no slipping. 3- water - take some ! 4- guide - not essential. 5- wasps - Close to the lions feet gate there are wasp nests on the rock face and warnings of occasional attacks. On the lions paw terrace there is a net shelter just in case . The achievement of building the palace on top of this place must have been amazing and taken huge manpower . Respect! One of Sri Lanka's MUST DO sites.
Me and my wife absolutely loved everything about it, and it was a very pleasant ride overall - the sun is absolutely amazing
An amazing view and a very beautiful visit for tourists. Me and my wife loved it and really enjoyed going up and seeing the amazing landscapes from above

The best time to climb the rock is at 7am as later on it gets hot and busy. Take lots of water. It has beautiful views and is also an archaeological site. Well worth the climb, even if it cost US$30 for the privilege
Really gorgeous morning climbing the Lion Rock.   Its hard work but if you can manage it it is well worth the view!
It is better to climb the rock early in the morning or at the end of the day. Bring plenty of water, but be careful with food because there are some very obnoxious monkeys around.

We kept reading that this was the most visited site in Sri Lanka and when we saw the pics and the videos we immediately put this on our must see places. Let me tell you it was worth it. It's an architectural wonder that one must not miss while in Sri Lanka. I am not a fitness freak hence the climb was exhausting for me but it's not a difficult climb, of course the heat does makes the climb more tiring hence it's advisable to go there early in the morning.   But do climb up to the palace ruins and enjoy the amazing view, it's really really worth the climb.

We visited at Sri Lankan new year, so it was very busy. At this time of year it took 3 hours to climb the Rock and get back down. There are many stairs, which are single file, so can take a while if there is a lot of people. The wall paintings which are a slight detour on your way up are well worth the visit and the colours are amazing.

A world heritage site that shouldn't be missed. An architectural marvel that made me wonder about the lost way of life. It is mind boggling to imagine how the people of yore managed to construct a fully functional fort on top of a cliff that has sheer drops on all sides The fort is accessible through a steep set of stairs, some made of natural rock, some of brick and mortar and some more recent metal stairs. A queue needs to be maintained to go up and come down due to the stair design that allows for only a single file. One of the main attractions in the fort is a wall that has paintings on it, another is a wall dubbed as the mirror wall due to its high shine. Unfortunately, we felt let down by both the aforementioned attractions. The paintings are almost on the verge of disappearing due to exposure to the elements and the glass wall is no longer shining. It is difficult to see anything on that wall. However, would recommend all visitors to definitely try and go to the top of the fort as the views are just out of this world. If weather permits then you get a clear view of the surrounding areas.
Make shore your fit for this one, but worth the early morning for something you will never forget truly amazing

First, this activity is not for the faint at heart. Go early to beat the crowds. One can certainly stroll the ground below while other family members take on the challenge Sigiriya Rock has to offer.  We arrived before the ticket booths were opened and it was getting busy.  My husband and I beat feet up through crowds and it took about 40 minutes up.  The frescoes were fascinating.  If I were to do it again, I would have packed a nice light lunch and enjoyed it at the top - pack trash back out of course.  It was beautiful and we spent about 35 minutes at the top taking photos.  Apparently, we were the the same week Sri Lankans had holiday too; so it seems busier according to our guide.  Take water!

The Sigiriya World heritage site is amazing! Top tips for a climb: get over the fact that as a foreigner you'll have to pay a fair bit of money for entry - then just enjoy! try to get there early to avoid crowds don't accept help unless you really want it for climbing and are willing to fork over more money spend some time looking around at features around the base of the rock think how hard building this castle on top of this rock would have been 1500 years ago

The climb atop this rock is a wonderful experience. We first visited the museum which gave us a glimpse of what we are gonna see. And then we walked through the beautiful gardens which are very well maintained Finally we started climbing. Can say that this is categorised into 3 parts. With a 3 year old, the first part was quite easy.If you want to see the frescos, then you have to climb a spiral stairs.Though it's safe, it's a bit scary. Second section is through the mirror wall which is also quite an easy one an finally we reach the lion's paw.The final leg is completely iron stairs and should say that it's a bit scary. Finally atop the rock is a wonderful view. The icing on the cake is the beautiful pond with chill water. It was worth climbing the rock and should say that we really enjoyed the trek

We had read - don't go in the afternoon, difficult with a young child etc etc. Well, we went after lunch at 3:30 pm in the last week of May. And we went with our 2 year old son. Yes it was hot but as we climbed the breeze that kept getting stronger took a lot of the heat off. A local safely carried our son in his arms all the way to the top and all the way back. So we could manage to carry ourselves. I'd like to mention here that I'm fairly fit but I don't have that kind of stamina. But I made it to the top. So if you push yourself a little you can be sure to do it. I saw 80 year old women in saris climbing up at a pace that pretty much put me to shame. So you climb and you cross places where it really is a good idea to not look down. If you're faint hearted your knees might buckle, but keep going. The views from the top are mesmerising. So we reached the lion's paws where there were arrangements for people to take a breather. A lot of people turn back from there as it's a steep climb from there right up to the top. I'll be lying if I said we didn't consider it. But we thought, we've come all the way to Sri Lanka for this. We'll regret it. Just push a little. And we did. The breeze at the top might have toppled us over if we hadn't held on the ruins maybe! And what ruins. You would have thought firstly. Secondly and more importantly, how did they achieve it?? There were 2 pools where they harvested rain water. One still had some water from last year's rains I suppose. Several levels at the top - stairs, pedestals, other structures. All made of rocks. How did they manage at this height I still wonder. And the views of Sigiriya and beyond from there. And the setting sun. Wow...what beauty! Do go.

Sigiriya is definitely a world heritage. Every person should visit kingdoms like these to understand better about the history and the path of the mankind. I have learned many things as well as my family.

Every traveler who visits Sri Lanka should see Sigiriya. It is not just a rock but one of the best-designed palaces from the ancient Sri Lanka. Most parts of the palace of King Kashshapa is still remaining at the peak of this large rock. The journey to the top is pretty exciting and thrilling. Anyway, the path has been fully repaired recently. So, no need to worry about the safety. Actually, everybody from any age group can climb this amazing rock and enjoy to the fullest. Other than that, there are also other attractions surrounding the Sigiriya fortress. If you need to see Sigiriya properly, allocate at least 3-5 hours. The whole family can enjoy visiting Sigiriya and learn about the historic value of it.

To be honest.... we didn't make it all the way to the top (my mum has a terrible fear of heights!). We did get up to the Lions Paws, which already has some lovely views. I was a bit unnerved by the signs about angry wasps everywhere, but didn't see a single one. Not sure if it's a common problem, but they are posted everywhere. The stairs are steep, and once you get past the Lions Paws from what I could see the stairs became a bit more jarring as they jut out right from the side of the rock. Up until then it's wide walkways and doesn't feel like you are that high. It's expensive (for Sri Lanka) to enter, but it is a world heritage site, and I still think it's worth paying that to visit. Even without the climb, there is lots to explore in the grounds around. Bring a lot of water, as it gets bakingly hot early on!

I recommend you get there as early as possible to beat the crowds and the heat. Bring plenty of water because I do not believe you can buy any once inside the temple area. Also be prepared to climb a lot of steps up to the top which of course you should do. There's a lot of history here and many details could be easily overlooked if you don't know what's what. So I suggest read up extensively or hire  a guide to help you.

The Sigiriya rock fortress rises 600 feet above the surrounding jungle, this monolith is visible from miles away.  It is called "The Lion Rock" because bricks and stucco were originally added to form the shape of a giant lion.  All that remains of this facade is the two enormous clawed, feline feet flanking the 1001 steps to the top.  The steps are very uneven, there is a lot of sand, a few hand rails.  Can be difficult especially if there are a lot of people going up and down.  Be sure to explore the terraced gardens of the fortress, the lush Water Garden and the ancient Boulder Garden.  Climb the spiral staircase to see the Mirror Wall and the colorful frescoes of the sensual Cloud Maidens, whose beauty inspires visitors from long ago to scribble graffiti on the polished lime wall.  The Sigiriya Museum is also interesting..

Must come to see the view at top of the mountain but you need to prepare for 1,200 steps, bring umbrella (it helped a lot at top) and lots of water! put on sneakers and go Best time to go in the morning because the shadow from mountain will hide you from the sun obviously going in the afternoon sound not possible for me....too hot and it was so tired , we saw some people faint before reach to the top but when we reach it worth!!

One cannot help but feel that Sigiriya rock deserves a place amongst the (newer) wonders of the world. To think that 1500 years ago, a King built a series of dramatic gardens (with fountains that activate in the rainy season) around a huge rock which he surrounded by fresco paintings (a few survive today,) and then constructed a three tiered palace on top complete with swimming pool is just astonishing - and after you have completed the near vertical climb to the summit, you will be even more impressed with the feat of the people of that time. Some advice - go as early as you can to avoid the crowds and the heat (the site itself opens early.) Read up before you arrive and be ready to understand the history and the lay out of the place. And don't be put off by the fact that you (as a tourist) will pay a lot more than the locals. I personally think that it is great that Sri Lanka has a two-tiered pricing system which makes it affordable for most of its citizens to visit its attractions. Finally, allow 3 hours for a full visit which will give you a chance to stay a while at the top and take in the views of the surrounding jungles - and then find the coldest beer you can when you get to the bottom!

Breath-taking views atop Lion's Rock or Sigiriya are a given, but the story behind it is just as impressive, we had a guide point out various things along the way that added to the majesty of this ancient rock fortress
Definetley take a trip here and explore the surrounds, its a magical and ancient area going back before christ. The climb up the rock is tough but doable, just bring plenty of water.
Good place to visit. But need to climb the hill,. From the top of the hill you can see the Panoramic view of the area

We didn't go inside, it's ridiculous the price that they asked. We walked around the place and we could spotted what we wanted to see. Is a pleasant walk and I recommend to do it. Btw on the way there near the restaurants is a couple of places for tourists for elephant riding PLEASE DO NOT DO THIS, the animals were incredibly stressed and sad.

What is it with Sri Lanka and the amount they charge to visit their attractions. $100 US to climb is rediculous. I mean if they were pumping money into interpretive signage and keeping the place maintained and litter free maybe but compared to somewhere like Barabudur temple in Indonesia where the entrance fees (much lower) are clearly being invested back into the attraction, Sri Lanka has got a lot to learn.

Well worth the mighty climb to the top, but try to go early in the morning before the heat builds up too much. And take plenty of water. Some very good frescos part way up and lovely gardens at ground level before you start the climb. Some of the "helpers" are a bit annoying and their demands for tips a trifle greedy, but I guess they serve a need and you can always just say No! Have a good look around at the top. You will have deserved it! Journey down can also be a challenge for wobbly legs.
Its a must must must visit . you have to do this and experience the jaw dropping view from the top of the rock .

This is a must do sightseeing attraction.  It is very much like the Machu Picchu in that there is an entire city built on top of the rock. It is great to see and it includes a lot of history of the entire area. It is really important that you go early.  The climb takes a good couple of hours, and the heat is exhausting so the sooner that you can get up there, the better it is. It is terrific to take photos of.  It is so majestic and you can see a terrific area around it.  Well worth it.

If you can you have to see this site. 30$each entrance fee,and I suggest early morning,as later tour buses will make it very crowded for the climb.200m high with 1200+ steps you need to be reasonably fit with the heat.Beware Of The guides at the start,a firm and polite no is required,as they will try To Help you on climb to lions paw,as it gets easier after that stage.The art work on way up is stunning,but the view from the top is fabulous make sure you have 2bottles of water,as heat and cardio workout,you know that it was worth the effort and sweat,because it is amazing😎🙏🌞

You look up with trepidation and think, "I'm never going to make it", but make it you do. Despite the heat and the endless mass of bodies above you on the climb it's fairly mind numbing but once there the effort is worth it. The views are fantastic and you just marvel how the original inhabitants ever managed to construct such an awe inspiring construction. This is an absolute must do in Sri Lanka.

We done this tour today and couldn't wait to review. Our guide recommended we go early in the morning as the heat in the afternoon can be to much. We went from about 7am and finished at about 9:00-30, the heat was was immense even at that time so I would suggest that anyone looking to go to this attraction I would suggest you go early morning time. It was a long walk to the top however you could stop pretty much whenever you want to catch your breath and/or have a quick drink, which we done a few times, at the same time it was a great opportunity to take some photos, when you get round the side of the rock, higher up its all metal stairs with metal railings so there's nothing blocking you from seeing the amazing view. The top was amazing and there was plenty to see with a large open space so you can walk around and get some pictures. It is exactly the same way to get down as it is up so sometimes we found ourselves waiting for the the stairs to clear before we could move anywhere. I will say BEWARE of the guides! Again like every other attraction they try to show you around and expect money afterwards. As soon as we entered the area after buying our tickets we had a gentleman asking us where we were from and started taking to us about the history of the location. We had to say numerous amount of times like we have at every place "no" and eventually we were left alone. However do be careful because you will find that a lot of guides allocate themselves on the stairs and try to help you up if they see you struggling and then will not leave you alone until they get money, my wife had this problem. We also spotted other tourists with guides and they seemed very unaware of the costs of their tour and were surprised when the guides insisted they pay them a ridiculous amount of rps. So if you are looking for a guide or help be clear on their price before you have their assistance because it can become very costly. Other than that we had a great time and would definitely recommend to everyone.

Majestic rock towering above landscape. I think it is the Macha Pichu of Sri Lanka. Nice climb to top of rock but not for people with fear of heights. Especially the winding staircases to the rick drawing.
This was our first stop and it's a great start. So happy we managed to see it, breathtaking! Make sure you get an early start so you beat the heat as it gets very hot. But it's so worth it!
This visit it worth the very hot climb to the top. The sheer amazement of a swimming pool atop the Sigirya Rock! The rock paintings are very special.

Hiked to the top of Sigiriya Rock on the 1st of January with my partner. It was a really hot day, but we were excited to do this. At times, I did feel queasy ( the stairways are quite narrow) but it was all worth it once we reached the top. The view from the top is amazing. Just wish the weather was better though!
Beautiful place! The walk can get heavy in the middle of the day so bring water. It's a must see when in sri Lanka. Entrance fee is around 3500RS
Enjoyed experiencing Sigiriya Rock. But for the cost, I would've rather just done the neighboring Pidurangula. Be sure to get their early as the crowds can get a bit wild.
if you want to know more history about Sri Lanka, this is a must place to go. climb up there for about 1.5 hours, down is about 1 hour. but so beautiful sense!

You must be physically fit to visit this place! You will climb up stairs all the way to the top of the rock! Bring water and something to cover your head with! Go there early in the morning to avoid crowds and hot weather! Definitely a must see!
Sigiriya frescoes and the way it had been design to see the images at the ponds was an amazing architectural fact even the present day Architects may find difficult to fathom.

Warning! If you are not physically fit, this attraction is not for you! Best time to see it is early in the morning, because it is still not as hot and less people. Lots and lots of stairs, steep, narrow and small, sometimes you must share it with people going down as you climbing up. Definitely a challenge! Hot sun, narrow stairs, lots of tourists, BUT a must see! Beautiful view!

Really enjoyed Sigirya.  Got there reasonably early to avoid the heat and the crowds, which worked well.  Hired a guide which was worthwhile as he explained all the history which really brought the place alive.  I think it was around US$15 each, so cheaper than some of the other sites we visited.  Sri Lanka is not a cheap country to visit compared with Thailand and other Asian countries, but it is beautiful and if you are visiting then some things just are worth paying for, and this is one of them.  Climb was much easier than I thought it would be with a good staircase, wide treads and narrow risers which is what I pray for in a staircase.  Great views from the top.  Thought the remaining paintings of the five hundred concubines that weren't destroyed by later monks a glimpse into a very different royal way of life.  No photos of these paintings, but if you go to Colombo visit the National Museum and you can photograph copies there.  Read up beforehand or take a guide - you will appreciate the site so much more if you know something about it.

Note, entry ticket prices are at $25 usd or 4500 LKR. Locals' ticket prices are probably more than 90% cheaper than what we are paying. We walked around the vicinity, looked at the lion's rock from below. Not recommend.

We were at first put off by the price (35 dollars per person) but we decided to go anyway. We got there at 8:00 and there were already many tourists there since the park opens at 7:30. However, it still wasn't too crowded so we could climb the rock with our own pace and take plenty of photos. I recommend going early since later on we noticed a lot more people and also groups of school children. There were many steps so it can be pretty tiring- I wouldn't recommend for small children or people who would struggle with the steps or heights. We are quite athletic and still were out of breath, especially due to the heat. There are no toilets once on the rock so make sure you go near the entrance. Bring plenty of water since there are no shops beyond the entrance. All in all, we were at the site for 3 hours since we took our time at the top enjoying the gorgeous view and marvelling at the ruins on top of the rock. In the end we were really glad we did it since it is quite unique- a kingdom on top of a massive rock.

We did this climb on the first morning of our tour after a very long flight and very long coach drive to our hotel. Climb commenced at 7am!!!  but was well worth the 5:15 alarm call. As you walk closer to the rock you cannot believe how tall it is. Fortunately there are areas along the way that you can stop and get you breath back...... but once at the top (yes we did actually make it all the way to the top) the views are magnificent. I cannot believe that anyone actually lived up here.

We travelled to Sigiriya from Hikkaduwa knowing the day was going to be a long one as the drive was over 5hours there... Unfortunately we didn't have any prior knowledge of the extortionate tourist entry price, which for a family of four (all over 12yrs) amounted to around £100.... (the locals gain entry for equivalent 30pence each). The site was extremely busy on the day we went, as it was the Sri Lankan new year holidays, so a slow and tedious trudge up the many steps was comparable to a busy theme park queue in the UK... If you've never experienced a decent view before, Sigiryia Rock will offer just that... but don't expect much more than that for your money as that is all that the pricey entry entails.... An unfortunate anti climax to a much looked forward to trip...

Loved our visit to sigiriya, read the reviews that pidurangala rock is much better and rock fortress can be skipped if you are short of time. well the views from pidurangala is great and the place is much less crowded and cheap. But if you like history and have ample time on your hand please visit this rock fortress.it is about 4500 rupees and do carry your passport. the climb up tp the top is great. the path is narrow so you have to be slow and follow the people ahead and you get few places where you can overtake. the art work on the walls is amazing, strictly no photographs of the same as the guards may confiscate your camera. Once you reach the top the view and arrangement up is good, worth the climb.

You pass through the citadel before you reach the rock, if you have ample time in your hands you can roam around the citadel and be careful not to step on the old bricks .. lot of employees areat work to keep the place clean. the water bodies are around the rock and arranged in a systematic pattern. do visit the museum first so you can understand the whole area and can appreciate the rock fortress and the citadel.

We got there around 7am and finished by 930am which turned out to be a good timing as we saw a lot of tourist groups and school groups on the way down. We felt the heat even at 8am so I can't imagine doing this at noon. Must wear a cap! Personally I have a slight fear of heights, I felt quite scared going up the steps on the side of the rock as you can see through the gaps in between each step and it felt high. Going down is a tad easier after the amazing views at the top! Definitely worth visiting, and take your time with plenty of water.

Sigiriya rock is as impressive in real life as the pictures suggest and every visit to Sri Lanka should include it. Pay in Sri Lankan rupees to get a better rate than the dollar price and try to get there early to beat the heat and the crowds. If you can arrive by 7.30 it's probably ideal. We arrived at about 8.30 which was a bit late to avoid the crowds and it was like a traffic jam moving up past the mirror wall and up to where the Lions paws are. We didn't linger around the Lions paws too long (as impressive as they are) as they are a magnet for group photos. Views from the top are awesome and you can see great panoramics of the surrounding mountains, temples and Buddha statues poking up above the trees and the lilipad lakes. The remains of the kingdom at the top of the rock are a spectacle in themselves We found the most enjoyable part was wandering around the the gardens below looking up to the rock. Just at the entrance to the gardens you can walk along off to the right hand side of the pathway to a viewpoint which was clear of other people and had some of the best views of the rock. We walked back to this point having climbed up to the summit before. In summary, you can't miss visiting this rock. It attracts crowds for a reason as it is spectacular in nature, the history of it is fascinating and to climb it doesn't require too much effort (you just need to be happy walking up stairs and lots of them). Note: There is another mountain directly north of Sigiriya called Pidurangula Rock that looks well worth the climb. It's smaller than Sigiriya but offers fantastic views directly of Sigiriya Rock and from the looks of things is less crowded. If we had known about this before we'd have probably woken up earlier to climb it before visiting Sigiriya. There's always next time...

A busy tourist spot. Get there early to avoid long delays. Organise a guide who will explain the amazing history and design of the gardens and palace area. Wear sturdy shoes and be prepared to sweat as you climb many many stairs! Well worth the effort though. There is a cost for entry and the guide.

This rock is a miracle! You need 2 hours to climb on the hill and come back. It is better to go early in the morning or at the afternoon for the sunset. I think 30$  is a lot of money but it is worth it 100%. It is one of the monument that every visitor must see. The view from the top is breathless

The views from the bottom, climbing up and more so the top were absolutely amazing. It was unbelievably hot so be prepared. Take water with you and wear cool clothes. Be warned though the climb can be a bit scary if your afraid of heights. My GF didn't make it to the top and waited for me in the middle as she got scared. You have to climb some steep metal steps that can be very crowded

Definitely get yourself a guide. There are no signs or audiotours, and a lot of interesting things you'd miss if you did it yourself. Be ready for a lot of stairs. 2,002 to be precise. Bring water on a hot day. Worth the effort though. Views are stunning throughout.

Amazing  - ancient temple fortress. Must do when visiting Sri Lanka. Totally blown away, breathtaking views from the summit, not a hard climb but hot as there is no shade on the way up. Note: wear a hat & take water and some snacks, then enjoy an hour or two at the top, sensational views. Highly recommended - truly breathtaking :)

it costs you USD30 each... a bit expensive We were so tired after the visit... there are many stairs It's nice up there and it's good for pictures go there after 3pm to avoid sun burn it would be very difficult to walk up there under the sun

I was preparing myself for a tough hike up, even stand at the bottom from a distance it looks huge! Yet it was surprisingly easy (and I don't hike often). There are steps going all the way up, which also made it easier. The views on the way up, as are the ones right on the top, are stunning. Get there early though, as it can get pretty hot and busy.

Our local guide confirmed their are well over 2000 steps to the top. I'd waiger it's closer to 3500 (at least it felt like it). Sigiriya is absolutely breathtaking. The pictures don't do it justice. Your approach will no doubt invoke intimidation, as it seems so much larger from the entranceway. You'll say to yourself, "how on Earth will we get up there?" The grounds are impressive, and so well-preserved. The fortress is like a maze, with so much to see in and around the base of the rock. Bring water, and get there early or towards sunset. They open at 7, and the first two hours are pretty calm. The middle of the day is the worst time to go, as crowds peak during that time. From about 2pm on, the crowds dwindle again. Again, bring water because you'll need it, the journey up can be tiring. Wear comfortable clothing, dry-fit preferably, and don't skip anything. The frescoes are a sight to behold, especially when considering how old they are. As you reach the lion's paws, don't look down during the last ascent. Those stairs can be harrowing for those with phobias, but the summit is well worth it. The 360 degree panoramas of central Sri Lanka are incredible, and you will be glad you decided to do it! Highly recommend piece of UNESCO world heritage history!

Sigiriya rock fortress is the Taj Mahal of Sri Lanka. Must visit whenever you visit Sri Lanka. However it please note that to reach the top you must do a 1.5-2km trekk which includes some stairs as well.

My only shaky moment was looking down while ascending the spiral staircase to view the frescos!  The most difficult steps are at the lower end of the climb.  Even with 2 bad knees, I made it with ease to the top and the glorious views. A must-see on any trip to Sri Lanka

We arrived early in the morning to beat the crowd. You a start by walking a few stairs, then you cross a small "bridge" and then more stairs to see the frescos. Then you walk around the cliff and then you take the stairs to the top.... be fit and don't be afraid of heights..

After my 7 days traveling in Sri Lanka from Colombo, Kandy to Dambulla, I would say this is the best heritage I have seen here. Some famous touristic spots sometimes doesn't look like what they should on the photos. But not in this case. Sigiriya world heritage site is definitely magnificent and fascinating to visit. The entrance fee for foreigners are not cheap about 30 USD per person but it is definitely worth it. The only thing I would like to note is this place may be difficult for old people who are not able to climb up high. The stairs are not very easy to climb up and the central palace located on the top of the stone. But if you are capable of doing this, you should certainly see it since you are in Sri Lanka.

This is an iconic SL must do.  The climb seems daunting but was easier than appearances. Leaving early is vital.  It's cooler.  And less crowded.  It was striking as we came down how the crowds had moved in making moving about as easy as SL street traffic. Signs and help can be lacking.  But don't let one of the "guides" at the base try to walk with you or assist you.  It is just a grab for money scam.  Ask them to leave you alone.

I climbed it on the 13\4\2017. It was great but ... ...it was very tiring. At the top we took photos and had a little break. The view was great. I was quite surprised how they made it. At ancient times it would be very hard to conquer the whole thing. Archers wouldn't work because the archers on the top's arrows could go further than the ones on the bottom, same as catapaults. By Miles Age 8

The view from the bottom and the top are really worth the trip. A great experience. Can go with children if they can walk up stairs (or if you are ready to carry them on your back..but it is a climb).

Be sure to be fit to take this experience on. Start early in the day to avoid the heat. I did the climb by myself and took my time. It was one of the most empowering experiences to make it to the Kingdom at the top of the rock. Wow. Amazing views and tales of a long gone kingdom. Do not miss the amazing rock drawings of the goddesses. Many of which were destroyed by monks. The Kingdom is more than 1,000 years older than Machu Picchu which I found surprising as so few people have ever heard of this amazing place. Do not miss Sigiriya.
Enjoy the view from the bottom and climb Pindurangala rock instead - here you will have an amazing view to the Lion Rock and save a lot of money

I recently visited here as part of our tour. It looks impressive from the bottom, but it is truly amazing at the top. I enjoyed listening to all the history regarding the rock. I found the climb ok, however it was hit so make sure you have plenty of water with you and apply lots of sunscreen. The views at the top are well worth it and you can get some amazing pictures.

one of the UNESCO heritage must see in Sri Lanka. plan enough time to go up, have a look at the cloud girls, go up to the top, breeze the fresh air, imagibne how life must have been there and go down again - without a rush. if you do not need help with the many stairs, tell that clearly to the young guys who want to help you and who want money afterwards for their effort. It is steep up with some stairs! take time and water and sun screen with you! it is worthwhile the effort!
Extortionately high tickets at an unjustifiable USD 30 each. Sunset view was nice but not spectacular as it was foggy. We recommend starting the climb at 4pm.

Start as early as possible to avoid the massive stream of tourist funneling through the narrow staircases. It's a super attraction to visit and you will be impressed with all the history at the Lion Rock, but once the thousands of tourist start to climb, the peace and quiet is gone.

This is a great morning trip, we left our hotel in Habarana at 7am to beat the crowds. Arrived at 730am to walk up the rock. The paintings, views and stories are all fascinating. Our driver acted as our guide and was very knowledgable and interesting. The walk takes some effort as a lot of stairs in the humid weather but once at the top there was a lovely cooling breeze and the view forever.

This place is amazing.  I have vertigo so was pretty scared but I managed it and I am so pleased I conquered my fear.  There are many different levels of gardens and steps.  Although there are around 1200 steps you can take your time so it's not like climbing all that way in one go.  The spiral staircase to the damsels painting was the most challenging for me but I took it easy and steady and wouldn't be rushed.  I would suggest arriving here for the 0700 opening time as it's less crowded and it's cooler.

This place is amazing.  I have vertigo so was pretty scared but I managed it and I am so pleased I conquered my fear.  There are many different levels of gardens and steps.  Although there are around 1200 steps you can take your time so it's not like climbing all that way in one go.  The spiral staircase to the damsels painting was the most challenging for me but I took it easy and steady and wouldn't be rushed.  I would suggest arriving here for the 0700 opening time as it's less crowded and it's cooler.

Went here with ly girlfriend in the early morning. It opens 7 and costs 4320 rupee per person (doubled the price recently) Tryo to come early i would say. Less people and not too hot yet. Except if you want to take pics from the rock. Better in the afternoon as then tve sun is better positioned. Climb itself is ok. But hard due to the heat. take water. They don't sell any. In titel count somewhere inbetween 2-3 hrs

This is a fantastic heritage site. Really interesting frescoes to see on the way up, phenomenal views from the top and really interesting exploration all over the top, too, plus lots of really interesting things to see at the bottom, too (cobra cave, boulder garden etc.). The museum was also quite interesting: the ground and top floors were fairly ordinary and uninformative but the section on the 2nd floor was really, really interesting and definitely added to the experience of our visit here. There is lots of information about the site and the civilization that lived there, plus terracota statues, beads, tools, and all sorts of other things that originated from there and thus helped to develop current understanding about the lives of those who once inhabited this place. We went at about 7:30am, which I would totally recommend. Not too hot yet and not too busy, and the ascent is perfectly manageable if you're in decent fitness. There were plenty of people puffing and panting even at this time though, so beware: if you're not in terribly good shape you're going to find this a challenge, especially if you leave it until the heat's increased... On our way down at about 10am the number of people coming up was INSANE: huge queues and you can only go as fast as the slowest person ahead of you since there is no room to move anywhere. I can only imagine the mayhem at the top as well - it was nice not to have to experience it cheek by jowl with everyone else there! Do yourself a favour and get there early. It is a wonderful place and great to have the time and space to explore it at your leisure.

It was A fun trip! We went quite early and that was A good desicion because when we were about to leave there was A lot of people on The way to climbing The rock. and The temperature was very high. Awesome rock and A great view from The top! I recommend seeing this!

This is definitely not a first day attraction. It's a beautiful rock but as I myself am a teenager and have a 9 year old sister the time difference and temperature change got the better of us. We didn't make it to the top however the view from and of the lions feet is quite incredible! We had a guide who was really good and gave us lots of information but it's very possible to do without one. You will get very hot a sweaty climbing this as there are lots of stairs so bring lots of water and loose clothing!

Our original intention was to climb Sigiriya Rock. However, our guide suggested Pidurangala and it was the right decision. Sigi looked far too busy for us whereas we had a leisurely climb with no crowds. For those on a tight budget it's also a lot cheaper.

This is a truly stunning experience, but as you would expect it is quite hard work climbing all the steps.  However once at the top you are rewarded with an amazing sight, both of the ruins and the surrounding scenery.  On the way up are some amazing things to see such as the mirror wall and the surviving paintings.  However keep in mind that Sri Lanka is a hot place, so take plenty of water and do start early to avoid the heat in the middle of the day and the crowds.

We went early in the morning when it opened to avoid most of the heat. We started our walk at 7:30h and we're already back at our hotel by 9:45h. I recommend going early in the morning since most of the walk up the rock is in shade and you can stop at enough places to catch some of the breeze. Also, at this time, there aren't many people and the stairs aren't crowded at all. On our way down it was packed!! And they were all waiting in the sun. The climb isn't too bad. My boyfriend has just come out of a cast (he broke is foot) and it was so-able since it's mainly stairs :) Definitely a must during your stay in Sigiriya!
Worth it ! Must to visit ! View is fantastic ) We climbed with guide (10$ per person) who was around and he was the best for us ) He explained everything in details , we satisfied with everything !
It is quite a climb to the top of the rock but well worth the effort. Best to visit early in the morning before the hot sun and full tour busses arrive.
It's an amazing adventure. Amaze with the remain architecture.  The entrance ticket  is relatively expensive, but it's worth to go.  Make sure you bring a water as definitely needed while you climb.

I was amazed that I could climb up the Lion staircase, as I suffer from vertigo. It was not as bad as I feared. A great view from the top. Beware of the gentlemen who "wish to help", as they will require payment.

The Paws at the base of the steps are misnamed Lion Rock. They are closer to an Eagle's. But in either case the engineering 1500 years ago to the top of this magnificent fortress/palace/monastery are astonishing. Make sure you're in good shape and not afraid of heights!

This is one of the most amazing fortress/monasteries on earth. A wonder of the world. It is also one of the most expensive. $30. And they don't take credit cards!  :-(  The 1200 step, 200 meter high, steep hike is rewarded by amazing views from the top. Go in the early morning before it gets hot! And don't miss the animated recreation of the palace in the museum. It's mind-boggling. But you need to be in good condition and not afraid of heights!

This place is one of these ones that you have seen in pictures and would love to meet personally. Unfortunately go with young children could be risky for going until summit and we were limited to see it from distance during elephant rides that are offered by locals. But anyway is a misthic place and recommended to include in your travel.

When you come to Sri Lanka you must visit the Sigiriya Rock. Its a must! Leave your hotel early and get there in the morning. Spend 2～3 hrs to climb up and down and also enjoy the view from the top.  Early mornng is better because of the heat and sun. Make sure you bring some water, hat, towel and comfortable shoes. Take your time, enjoy every moment:)

The climb starts with steep stone steps and progresses to the final ladders. The narrow paths create queues. I prefer to climb with a few vacant steps in front of me so it was a stop/start climb. Not all made it past the lion's paws. Such a sense of achievement making it to the top and the site of the Central Palace and see the views.

We travelled with our six year old and we battled through. Start early and leave the gardens till the end when you climb down. Have a lot of water with you and a small towel like a face towel. Most importantly enjoy every level as you ascend and descend.
Go early in the morning and make your way straight up the rock. Then the water gardens after. The views are stunning and not to be missed!

Amazing views from the beginning looking up right to the top. We acquired a tour guide who stopped in numerous locations on the way up  to educate us on the history of the rock.. Would 100% recommend.

1200 steps, 200 metres up, a fortress palace tribute to an ingenious king! We'd been adamant the day before with our driver/guide that we wouldn't do the climb but in the end we did and I have to say we felt particularly virtuous and rewarded by the experience.. The climb can be done in stages and there are slow parts which give you time to get your breath back. The people around us were quite good humoured despite the physical stress and from time to time there was a cooling breeze which was particularly welcomed. All in all a signature expereince.
Our trip to Sigiriya was a hit with all - including our boys aged 7 and 10 who really enjoyed the climb.
Amazing views and not for those with a fear of heights. Entrance fee is a bit heavy but despite this it still gets very crowded. Go early to beat the crowds as well as the heat.

This is something not to be missed. Go there at 7am so that you can be one of the first people up. Do not go up later in a crowd as the climb is demanding, the path narrow and lots of people find it difficult. Only do it if you are reasonably fit. The view from the top is stunning. Take water as you will pour sweat. You don't need a guide.

It was nice seeing the rock fortress and walking around the grounds but I have to say the touts and so called "guides" who pestered us the whole way was very annoying. They grab hold of u and menacingly try to convince you they will guide u and when we actually told them  we didn't need them they swore at us. Not a very nice experience which put us all off climbing the rock. We couldn't wait to get out of there.

A beautiful spot to stop, climb, and wonder. The fortress is explorable without a guide, and though we were told the round trip would take 3 hours, we were up and back in 1.5 hours... a beautiful monument, with breathtaking views. Not for those who don't like heights, but even part way up, the views are spectacular. A must see!

Went on our first day and still tired from flight so weren't as early as intended and ended up climbing in the heat of the day - this is to be avoided- go early or late! Our kids 9&14 found it very challenging in the heat and we only made it to the lion's paws. Not good if you don't like heights. My husband made it to the top - final climb is a challenge. Views are stunning all the way up and the history is incredible. Loved the guide and his insights.
Really impressive site but was quite busy so would recommend an early visit especially as the climbs are quite demanding in the heat.
Long climb all the way to the top of sigiriya well worth it the views are breath taking! Absolutely exhausting though not helped by the heat! When I got down my legs were shaking.

Glad we went early as even the 9am heat is fierce. The walk up was ok, though some steps are slippery so wear good shoes. The lion up to the rock must have been very impressive when the whole lion was there. The views from the top are stunning, especially of the lakes. The museum is often overlooked but it's very informative and architecturally the building has great qualities of natural light and the stream runs through and reflects on to the upper walls.

Very few places I have visited leave a lasting impression with myself but this definatley did. I had seen the photos prior to my visit but seeing the rock in reality is something quite different. I am relatively fit and found the first part of the climb quite enduring and had doubts as to whether I could actually make it to the top! However I soldiered on and am so glad that I did as once at the top the views where spectacular. However it was the remains of the palace, swimming pool, and kings throne which I found simply stunning as I never expected this to be at the top of the rock. The climb down was easier than going up. Only take with you what is necessary, i.e hat, water & camera don't get bogged down with heavy rucksacks!

Sigiriya is 100% worth the climb. We climed both Pigdurangala & Sigirya and I would recommend to do both as they are both completely different. Sigiriya is breath-taking at the top, we didn't expect it to be so beautiful. We could of spent hours up there! The only problem I encountered on the climb, was the metal stairs with gaps in, allowing you to look down! I love climbing and I can climb easily, however when I am faced with steps with gaps in....I am not so good! It took me about half an hour to pluck the courage up to climb them, but I am so glad that I did! There are lots of places to stop along the walk if you need a rest, plus a place to stop just at the bottom of Lions Rock, before the stairs to the top. It does get quite busy, therefore I would recommend heading there quite early to avoid the crowds. We left at 9am and didn't get back until 3pm - We spent lots of time at the top exploring and taking pictures. The views are amazing! Hannah - Travel Through Life

The walk up is tough but completely worth it. Don't bother taking the spiral stairs to the murals, it's really not worth it. You can view the murals online. The view on the top is top notch and one not to miss!

Enjoyed the visit. The palace gardens are impressive as is the trip up to the citadel and Lion's Gate. This involves a lot of walking and climbing stairs but with plenty to see and enough rest stops in shaded areas. The views are magnificent. It's important to take a hat, sun screen and plenty of water. For those who like me, walk with a cane, you need to be careful on the steps especially the granite steps which are covered with loose sand. The steel staircases are easier to negotiate as they have handrails. Allow for rest and water stops and to let the impatient tour groups rush by. Taking a guide is a good idea to get the full benefit of the history. Usually the drivers pay the guides but they may insist on an additional tip. Its good to discuss this up front with your driver. Either way the guides do work hard and as there are 170 guides (I was told) its a hard way to earn a living.

This is a must see if you do not have vertigo.  It is a very significant climb and is best done early in the morning before the sun gets too hot and before the huge crowds gather (at the peak times there can be hour long queues to go up and come down...).  Luckily, not being a religious site, one can wear shoes and hats throughout.  A polarizing filter is useful to mitigate against the haze under some conditions.  I found the whole site fascinating and lover the amazing views.

You will never forget Sigiriya as it is so unique: the scenery, the history, the ruins, the lion paws, the top and most importantly the frescoes! Try to visit in the morning as the heat can be a real problem. Try to make it to the top. It is very steep, but take your time. If you have vertigo, you may want to limit yourself to reaching the frescoes and the lion paws. To best appreciate the site, do your homework and read about its history before getting there. A good guide book with pictures is a must. The web has detailed reviews of the site and how easy or difficult each section is. Watch out for "helpers" who will "volunteer" to help you up. If you want their help, negotiate the price beforehand. There remain only 16 frescoes of the "Apsaras celestial nymphs" out of the original 500. Considering they were painted in the 5th century AD, it is remarkable that they still are in an amazing condition. From the cave where they are you continue to the mirror wall and its very old graffitis and then to the "lion paws". From this esplanade, one can imagine the gigantic size of the lion that guarded the path to the top and the "Royal Palace". The last ascent is quite steep and as you get to the top, monkeys are there watching, ready to steal your water or soda bottles. They have become adept at opening the caps (fun to watch)! While only foundations remain of the Royal palace, one can imagine its grandeur. The views are amazing as you are about 600ft up over the plain. You can still see the "stone throne" the King sat on to watch the sun rise. There is also a beautiful rock-pool, a great photo-op. Going down is pretty straight forward as long as you try to ignore how high you are.

The grounds around the famous Sigiriya Lion Rock are fascinating and if you go to Sigiriya then you should spend some time here as well. There are several interesting areas that take you back in time and force you to imagine what life was like in this place many centuries ago. The site is very well-preserved and well-maintained and we even saw people carefully working on the maintenance and upkeep of some areas. The Lion Rock is the main attraction here but we spent a little over an hour exploring the other areas and we still weren't able to see everything. There were even more such areas along the return path. There's also a museum that I recommend visiting, especially if you want full value out of your ticket.

Interesting history and archeology but not the amazing view I thought I would find. Hot and tiring, no cold water will be available. The more water you bring with you the heavier you will be and hence the more thirst you will have. Paradoxical

The best time to arrive at the ticket counter is really at 6.30 in the morning, otherwise you'll be waiting in a long line just to buy the entrance tickets (Yes, this means there will be a lot of tourist). We arrived there very early and had to wait until the ticket counter is opened and we were one of the first ones to enter, so we really had no problem with the climbing at all- no queue. I would say it is quite tough to climb up the rock- it is a lot of steps! So do bring enough water and if you plan to go to other places on that very some day, I suggest you to bring extra clothes because you are surely going to sweat a lot climbing this one. Make sure you wear comfortable hiking shoes too, although I saw some people were fine with just sandals. Absolutely worth all the efforts and sweats! It's really beautiful up there.

One of the most challenging experiences of my life. Visiting Sri Lanka with good friends, I was a victim of testosterone poisoning and decided that I was going to make the summit no matter what. There are very helpful guides that help you up and help you down. Challenging climb with uneven steps and questionable handrails but a great feeling at the top coupled with a great view. Be sure to have proper footwear and be ready for the climb.Those with questionable orthopedic problems will decide to stop at some point but you still face the down trip.
You will have to climb through stairs along the cliff to see the great drawings on the wall of the cliff. The view from the top is great. Be careful withe bees while you are at the summit!
We take tuk tuk from Dambula and back for 2000 R .Amazing view from top. Walk thru water gardens is beatiful. Turtle in river monkeys on threes. Amazing trip. :)

We were initially going to climb Pidurangala Rock - Sigiriya's neighbour after reading the reviews on trip advisor. However last minute we decided to go for Sigiriya. We really enjoyed the experience and exploring the grounds and the views were exceptional. However the price was high at $30 p/p as with all the other tourist traps in Sri Lanka and you do slightly begrudge feeling like you've been ripped off. Definitely climb Sigiriya either early in the morning or late afternoon as we made an error in doing it just before noon and it was extremely hot. The climb is okay for anyone of relative fitness only made difficult by the heat.

Actually we did not climb the rock - no head for heights however did talk to other tourists who did and said on the top was amazing and worth the climb but it was really hard both going up and coming down.

Just because you're climbing the Rock, don't overlook the story about the whole site.  A good local guide helps make it come to life.  Take care with the monkeys as they can be spiteful and will snatch anything that looks like food or water.

Most people visit early in the morning at around 7.30 am because it's cooler but it's also very busy.  Don't go late morning or early afternoon as it is seriously hot and there are a lot of places on the climb with no shade.  We went at 4pm and it was still too hot for the first part. Get a local professional guide as they have great knowledge and aren't expensive.  Ours was amazing and spoke several languages really well. I found the climb to the lions claws hard as the steps were uneven and quite slippery/smooth but once there the climb up the metal staircase to the top is easy and there's a lovely breeze.  The views were unbelievable and although the guide warned us what to do if the hornets swarmed, we didn't see any.  Plenty of monkeys and, more entertainingly, dogs trotting up the stairs to the very top!  No idea why as there's nothing there for them but they weren't causing a problem. Coming down was very easy compared to going up.  We are not young but we managed it so go ahead and do it, you'll be thrilled that you did.

Climb up and up the somewhat rickety appearing stairs to the top to view the crumbling ruins and the spectacular views. Yes it's crowded, and you will sweat buckets, but it is fun and very worthwhile. Take a moment to contemplate what the climb may have been like for the earliest residents!

My wife and I visited Sigiriya during our recent 3 week holiday to Sri Lanka. The climb up the 1200 steps to the top is not for the faint-hearted, but the view is spectacular once you get there. The remaining frescoes are amazingly well preserved considering they are reported to have been painted approximately 1600 years ago. What remains of the royal palace or monastery (some dispute apparently over what actually existed at the top of the rock), gives you an idea of the scale of the buildings. The hydraulic engineering system build to supply water to the palace/monastery defies belief for its age. The weather was perfect the day we visited, with spectacularly clear views from the top across the surrounding area. A visit to the Sigiriya Fortress, or The Lion Rock as it is also known, is a must if you are planning to visit Sri Lanka.

This is a magnificent site but very busy even though we arrived quite early in the morning!
