It was fantastic to see the old paintings and the views from the top. It is definitely a world wonder. You have to visit it. It shows so much culture and Sri Lankan history. You just have to experience it yourselves. Definitely, definitely visit.

Do visit this place if you are looking to taste some bit of Sri Lankan folklore..lot of stories around the kings who built this monument and beautiful surroundings. Loved the historical water bodies and how people would have lived in such height. Say that it was well planned for those times as well
Facing my fear of heights ! I can safely say this hike was well worth the reward - Go as early in the morning to avoid the deluge of tourist buses later in the day .

I'm currently in Sri Lanka on holiday and a must see whilst here is Sigiriya. I was very concerned about my fitness to be able to go up the 1,300 steps. I am 115kg heavy and have high blood pressure. I decided to give it a go and this is my experience. I was with a group of younger people, far more fit than I am. They were very fast and in a matter of just over half an hour we had climbed the 900 steps leading up to Lion Fortress. I managed this far but I got very tired since I had to catch up with them. So I stopped at the Lion gate and they carried on the last 350 steps that where left. Had i been with a group who did not rush so much, i could have easily done it in my own time to the very top. So if you're planning to visit Sigiriya make sure that you are traveling with a group that will allow you to do it in your own time without having to rush after them.......

We all really enjoyed this! We realized going down that our early start of the day really boosted our experience as a whole since the crowds arrived around 9-9.30 and by then we were already on our way back down. Get there early and bring water!

If you like ancient sites this is the place to be. Simply a marvel of buildingcraft and engineering. What you need to think about is to be there early because most of the big busses Come there around 09:00. So its less People there before and the walking up to the top will not be as stressfull and crowded. Also early means less warm and sweaty.

A must do visit for any visitor to Sri Lanka, incredible place but, be warned, there are lots of steps (1,200+), some precarious, to get to the top - but oh so worth it when you get there. Take a guide with you as they have so much knowledge to share regarding the history of the site

Quite unique in many ways. The geography of the area is amazing and the view from the top is worth the trip alone. Historically fascinating with fresco's and ruins quite well preserved so that you can imagine its heyday as a kings palace. Impressive too the feats of engineering to build the fortress, irrigation works and water gardens. Go early to avoid the heat and do the hardest climb in the shade. Not a problem for the reasonably fit but some struggle. No sign of the $30 entrance fee being invested in the site. Facilities poor, rotten cafe and museum depressingly run down (new in 2009 apparently). Clearly the tourist board know what a cash cow they have and intend to milk it.
Very nice scenery from the top, but expect a lot of people both locals and tourists, which means you will have to stand in line a couple of times. But it's worth it. Was there in 2013.
Fascinating place from a historical, cultural and scenic perspective. It’s a long way to the top of the rock, but we all made it and are in awe of the people who built a monastery there.

Me and my wife where in Kandy and chose to go to Sigiriya for a day trip. It is very easy to get to by oublic bus and takes about 3 hours from Kandy. 30$ is a bit too much to pay, but after walking around the gardens and climbing the Rock, you will feel like getting yours money worth. Make sure to pack lots of water and some snacks and Sun screen! The hike is easy and takes about 1 hour, including photo breaks. The views from the top are stunning!

This site is fantastic, the views from the top are great. If you are scared of heights, there areas where you can stop for a while, but I would suggest trying to get to the top. Just bear in mind 2 things, first a guide is good to have but not required and expect to pay around 2000 rupee's. There are also helpers which again aren't needed. The steps can be a bit slippy and there are monkeys there so don't bring food or they will try and get it from you.
nice view but hot to go up. we went as close as required to get a good photo and decided to return another time to climb up

Those not fond of heights or hornets might do well to keep away, but the trip up the rock is OK for all but the  most height phobic, and the view from the top is spectacular... Go early in the morning to avoid queuing on the steps, and if anybody suggests you go up the spiral staircase and you aren't keen, just ignore as there are only a few paintings on the rock and it's the most unnerving bit of staircase for very little reward... pass it by!

It's really high, so a got a bit scared but it is safe because it always have somewhere to place your hands or bars. A bit expensive (over 4000 LKR). You climb for 30 min through stairs and the view it's really like a jungle, far but no to far, perfect.

Wasnt awe inspired but carving of lion feet good and various terraces interesting...good view over the area too to take photos of what the king could have seen...not sure if any army would have much energy after climbing it as we were exhausted and we thought we were ok in fitness terms...not for those who struggle with stairs

Went here in morning before too hot...but v packed and lots of queues going up metal staircase so in end didnt go to top as saw queues and could be bothered as could see nice views from the lions feet. Lovely water gardens but shame no water in them which apparently there is when wet...dont forget water as nowhere to get some whilst climbing up. Is quite stenuous but if u take slowly ok. Thought it was ok but not awe inspiring..painting on wall of half naked ladies ok but nothing to write home about as not original and have been touched up. Wouldnt go again and quite expensive for what there is.

Make sure you visit to enjoy the sunrise / sunsets of this world heritage site. Get your driver to take you before the bus loads of tourists arrive. The park is a lovely to walk around and if you trust the stairs and walkways, you will be rewarded with spectacular views from the top of the rock. The actual citadel is largely ruins now. If you are elderly or not good with heights / sheer drops, don't attempt to climb. Avoid the gentlemen hanging around offering guide services, they can be persistent. USD 30 entrance fee applies to foreigners.
Amazing place. Breath taking views, ancient arts and ruins. 8th wonder of the world... A must go place in Dambulla!

I made it to the top with the help of my guide I was 70 this year if I can do it anyone can. It was Well worth the climb the views were fantastic and I was amazed at how so long ago they built Palace so high up. My legs were a little sore for a couple of days after but soon recovered.

This is a master piece in early civisation 5th century A.D. how they managed to build the palace on the top of the mountain is just amazing. The carvings in the rock are just fantastic, you would have to think that construction techniques must have been influenced by the Romans or Grecians but they weren't. It's very well worth climbing the 12290 steps ( that's the amount our guide told us there were) to the top, fantastic views for miles and miles. A must see attraction in Sri Lanka.

This is one of those places that you simply must do in Sri Lanka if you're physically up to it. It is a longish climb but a steady pace should make it accessible for most. Heat is potentially the bigger enemy so go well supplied with water. The cave frescoes, half-way up are a revelation and would be worth doing just for these alone. A word of warning - nowhere on the climb are you exposed to falling but for some with vertigo tendencies even the steepness of the steps and the open aspect might spook them. Funnily enough the spiral (fully enclosed) metal staircase to access the frescoes which is built into the side of the rock was, I thought, the potentially worst part and I witnessed one guy have a slight vertigo "wobble" there. Check with your guide whether you can avoid this (if you want to) and still go to the top of the rock - it was my impression that you couldn't because of the one-way system they operate but I may be wrong. If you're thinking of taking very young children also consider it carefully. Wonderful piece of history in a beautiful location. Try and do it if you can.

Before you go, would be good to read something about this site's background. Also take some time to look museum and gardens before going up. Climbing up is not so bad as you think. Even ticket price is quite high, recommend to visit.

This is a very interesting historical site that is worth the visit. As mentioned by others, you need to climb up a lot of stairs to reach the top of the hill where you can see remnants of citadel & drawings. I however think that it is a bit pricy (USD 40 for foreigners if not mistaken) This place is a bit far from Colombo It took me about 4 hours to reach this site from Colombo. So that is easily a day trip. However you can enjoy the view of along the way - small towns, villages or stop for fresh mangoes or coconut drink. You should also aim to arrive early in the morning when it is not so hot or crowded.

On the day we climbed sigiriya we had torrential rain to battle, despite this there was a constant stream of people climbing the treacherous steps. Not a climb for those afraid of heights but so worth it once at the top. It was beautiful up there with old ruins and the cloud cleared enough to get a view out across the country. Would highly recommend.
Bring good shoes and enough water. But all the steps (over 1000) are worth it! Great view and interesting site.

I must say we were a little apprehensive when thinking about climbing this rock especially in the Sir Lankan heat and not feeling that fit. However as our guide was 69 years old we thought we had better give it a try. The hardest part is when you get to the lion's paws and you make the final climb to the top. However I urge you to persevere as the view is spectacular and you feel so exhilarated when getting to the top. It is amazing to think this King built a fortress on the top of this rock and even more unbelievable to think how in heaven's name did they do it. Fascinating story attached to the site too. Top marks, it was amongst the best things we did in Sri Lanka.

This site is truly awesome & I cannot believe it's not as famous as machu pichu or Chechen itsa.  Get there early, (i.e. 6.45 am when cooler & uncrowded) get a good guide (not one of the layabouts lounging on site), climb the 1200 steps in the rock face slowly then prepare to be speechless at the summit!! One of the best ancient sites I have ever visited
On the next level from the murals is the lions rock All that is left of the statue is a large lions paw
At age 75 I found the steep climb heat and high humidity a bit exhausting Murals worth the climb Amazing that a wooden village was once on top of this rock

We visited Sigiriya on a Monday of October 2016. The gardens place is very nice to walk through. The frescoes on the middle of the rock are really well kept. And that's all!. We payed 30 dollars per person to climb up a rock that has almost nothing to see on the top! The employees were indifference and some of them rude and bored! I have visited monuments in all over Europe and New York and the fee in Sigiriya is ridiculously high. Please stop going there so they can low the price at list on the half.

Must do activity in Sigiriya area. A world heritage location having ancient history. Bit difficult steps to climb but feels worth to do it when you go on top of the Rock. Amazing view of the forest from top.

Visited Sigiriya and the challenge to climb 1202 steps was excerpted. We had a local tour guide who charged Rs.2800/- and walked with us until the end. One the way we found a person selling wood craft items he simply charged double the price. The journey to reach the top was tiring and luckily had a bottle of water with us. It took us 50 min approx to reach the top. And 700+ steps to come down in total took 1hr 30min for this memorable experience. Do your research before you go to the place so that you have a better understanding of things. Highly recommended for a life experience.
The climb of lion rock is a very long climb and is worth the view from the top. you can see the large landscape of the area
Climb to the top of the hill is all worth it. takes about 45 min and better to visit early morning to avoid the heat. good place for photography in the evening
Interesting site but entrance fee is very high. From the next hill you have the same view with only small entrance fee. I would have gone to that one if I had known better.

This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and quitr rightly so. 2,000 years ago the Sri Lankan King decided to build a palace on top of this enormous rock. A completely insane idea as it was totally inaccessible with sheer Granite faces. But 4 years later and probably with the help of thousands of men he achieved it. If you have stamina you must go and climb it, amazing to think they carried all the building materials to the  top on their back.
Amaizing vewe after we climbe up abaut 1200 staers all the rode up was not eazy but we are recomended to do this
The walk up the rock is not as daunting as we thought it would be. Best to do it in the morning as it gets pretty hot after 10ish. Amazing views and the surrounding gardens are pretty amazing too.

The place is mainly just ruins now- you don't see any bit of the structure but the whole cliumb, the view and the imagination of what this could have been is fascinating. Make sure you get a guide, else it's just a plain hill
We went very early in the morning when it was cooler. I only got half way up to the top as I am not good with heights but the other half made it to the top. Lovely gardens with lots of monkeys.

This was the most expensive entrance fee of them all.  Not quite sure what they are doing with the all the money. Unlike  Machu Picchu very little that I could see is being done for preservation or to enhance the experience with the daily fleecing of the tourists, although I admit I did not go the museum and am unaware if there is an additional charge. Upon arrival you are immediately surrounded by local helpers or guides or pushers or by anyone that wants money. I was not even into the tour and I already felt like an ATM. So up you go.  Unfortunately, as there are so  many other world travelers, there is limited time to stop and take a photo or rest, as you will be blocking those behind you on the trail, so you move forward.  If you are slow a "pusher" will come up behind you, crab you by the butt, and push you up to the next flat space and will become you best friend until you return down and their tip is paid. You reach some spiral stairs, thinking you are making good progress to the top, to look at a wall that is supposed to have something on it that I could not see, only to go back down the spiral stairs to where you started.  Good exercise but sort of a waste of time and energy. The final assent is sort of cool.  If you are afraid of heights, this narrow steel stairway may bother you.  It's just attached to the side of the mountain. Finally at the top you see different levels of historical rock foundations outlying where buildings once stood, and can imagine what it must have looked like.  I'm sure it was quite the place to be in its time.  You also get to stand on some rocks that are said to be the last and highest for a photo op. The pusher will wait patiently for you there. I must admit the view on the day I was there was pretty impressive, but I've always liked the view from a mountain top.  As I can now say I've been there and done that I need to now re-read the history of the place so I get the overall feel for it. It is listed as a moderate hike for those in shape.  If you don't fit the category, you may want to pass and look at the pictures.

- the whole experience is magical - I recommend you start early in the morning, I started at 7:30 and was the third on the top, it was an easy walk on the stairs, since I was alone; later larger groups started to come up and the stairs were crowded - the museum is well designed and very informative

I visited Sigiriya in April this year and it was truly an amazing experience. you can see this big rock from a far and when you are walking thru the entrance, I was totally amazed by the symmetrical water garden. As you walk closer to the rock itself, I started to wonder what an incredible job was done. The climb is mostly staircase, it's quite a walk, but in the middle of it you will get to a corridor with ancient paintings and that was a good small break before reaching the top. View on top of Sigiriya is really amazing with the endless forest around the area. One suggestion that i would have is to take a look at Duran Duran's video of the song "save a prayer", that surely will give you an idea of what you will see in Sigiriya.

The site itself is simply awesome and a must visit. Don't miss climbing to the top either. Take your time about it - stop, rest, hydrate, but get there. :) The downside however, the place while well maintained, needs a lot more tlc. They don't have any audio guides, so you are forced to rely on the guides to understand the history, structures etc. In lieu of the Audi guide, a good thing would be to mark the sites with a bit of write up, so travellers who'd rather be self sufficient have that. And for the fee they charge, they really could afford better upkeep of the museum as well! But let none of this deter your visit, it's definitely worth one. :) Pro-tip: passport holders from SAARC countries get 50℅ off on the $30 entry. So carry your passport or a soft copy of your e-visa to avail that.

One of the best sites in Sri Lanka to explore ancient culture of the country.. Ancient technology used by the ancestors is very advanced... Unfortunately the facilities for visitors are not that much... I wonder foreigners have the value for their money.. But the enormity of the place will outweighed all the obstacles in my opinion..
the site is an old fort complex of the king , neatly maintained , foreigners have to cough out a lot of money but its worth

Allready when you enter the bottom of the area it is magnificent. We took the local turist guide who guided us to the top. He told as history of the lion rock ( good listening, interesting). Climb is quite hard if the day is hot. Better prepare water. On the top there is a view that will impress you. Must see.

Lion Rock in Sigiriya needs a lot of energy to climb. It's better going it in the morning to avoid the heat. It takes you around 1 hour to arrive to the summit; but once you arrive you forget all the pain when you see all the magnificient nature & surrounding.

A must visit place if you are in Sri Lanka. Truly a world heritage site which definitely needs to be explored. The trek to the top is challenging and takes 2 hours. But the reward of the climb is to be seen than to be explained. You can only see miles and miles of green cover all around you. Recommended time to visit this place either early morning or late afternoon. If you are visiting this place towards evening, make sure you start getting down immediately after sunset. Gets dark pretty soon, and gets very difficult to get down in darkness and dangerous considering this is in the forest.

This Rock Fortress is a "must see" for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. It is unimaginable how the palace, pools, steps and possibly gardens were constructed at the top of the rock. It is a strenuous climb to the top of the rock by steep stairs but well worth it. The famous painted frescoes of maidens is something that should be seen as well as the Mirror Wall and the massive lions paws that guard the last climb to the top of the rock. This was supposedly constructed around 500 AD (1,600 years ago) with a moat, 3 tiers of gardens, ponds and other places carved from the rock. It is best to visit as soon as the gates open in the morning as that is the coolest time of the day and also because the rock hasn't warmed up.

We did it in the heat and it took under an hour I think set off early and it would be easier. It does give you a good work out but the views are well worth it. It wasn't cheap though I think about £25 pp

We set off for our hike early in the morning before the blazing midday sun. The hike is gentle if you're fit. If you have knee problems don't go - there is no shortcut down! The eroded steps up have been largely reconstructed. As you get steeper the steps turn into metal steps that have been scaffolded onto the side of the rock. There are two stopping points; one is halfway and the other is about 80% of the way up where the Lion Paws were engraved into the rock. If you are scared of heights like me, be prepared for the very steep steps leading up from the Lion's paws to the top. But ... it is SO worth it. What greeted us at the top was absolutely breathtaking. I knew we were in for a treat with the view but I did not expect to see the ruins of an ancient city. I wish I had read up beforehand! It is beautiful, and makes you wonder how the old civilisations lived. Don't wear flip flops and pack a bottle of water. Some ladies were going up in glamorous maxis and sandals; what did they think they were doing - going to the beach!!?!

We travelled to Sri Lanka with our 3 children aged  22 months, 6 and 7 years old and this was one of the highlights for us. And what felt like a good achievement with all the kids in track. Recommend you go as early as possible, before the crowds and before it gets hot. Take lots of water and hats and a small snack for the kids at the top. It was a little tiring but worth it and everyone was pleased with their achievements after. We paid for a tour guide to come up with us, he explain the history to us which was worth it, he also helped with the kids. You can easily find someone below to come up. We saw the beautiful paintings in the cave which where amazing to see, the kids also loved to see this and hear about the history and the technique that was used to paint these. The views are breath taking. I Especially loved the views of the 2 Buddhas in the distance. We Saw a snake up the top (not poisonous) which again the kids loved. At one point on the way down we had to to sit quietly until the hornets settled (at which part I was really glad we had our driver and tour guide with us as this was just extra piece of mind with 3 kids). Heard that one of the tour guides that went up previously to us had been stung once. So do be careful. We didn't wear long sleeves but where aware they where there so ensured we where quiet when needed to be. On the way down we saw Lots of monkeys and giant squirrels which the kids loved taking photos of. Highly recommend to do if you can....

This was definitely the highlight of my trip to Sri Lanka, try to go up first thing, where it's quieter and not unbearably hot. Quite pricey in comparison to other attractions but we'll worth it the views alone. Would definitely take my time to explore as it is breath taking.

On aerial photos and marketing imagery this place looks sensational, in reality it's a bit underwhelming. From viewpoint it looks like what it is, a large rock. From the top the view is nice enough but not special. It's hard to appreciate it for what it is - it's also very hard work in a hot day! The cave paintings half way up are very mediocre, they looked rather fake to us. The temple complex on the top is hard to appreciate as it's little more than ruined walls, some more information or visualisation of what it looked like in its heyday might be better. It also may be better in a season when the top is more vegetated.
Nice places. We were here two times, in winter in the morning and in summer in the afternoon. In afternoon before sunset it was great :) Very nice view. We were here about at 4 pm. I recommended

Arrived early with our driver - as we pulled up we were approached by a supposed guide. Who after speaking to our driver assumed we wished his services. I politely told my driver ' We wish to walk alone and at our own pace'. The guide was very unhappy with this and despite being repeatedly being told would not leave us alone. He continued to harass our driver, who I could see was somewhat distressed, offering the driver a share of the fee ect. Given the choice I would not go again. What could of been a reasonable morning out was spoilt by constant harassment. Top tip - take plenty of water and be prepared to stand your ground. There is only one toilet ( if you dare ). Considering the cost the amenities are very poor.
a beutifull place worth geting there and climbing all the stairs to the very top. the sites from the top of the cliff are wonderfull.

It is recognized as a world heritage sight. The entry fee is little on the expensive side. It is a tiring climb up the rock. But all through you have stairs and hand rails and hence it is perfectly safe. The view from the top is amazing and massively windy. Better to go early in the morning.
Impressive monument and well maintained by Unesco since it is recognized as a heritage sight. A hard climb to the top but worth the effort.

Spent the first 3 days of our holiday in North Sri Lanka ( Sigiriya ) Our driver during this period arranged for a tour guide around the museum & acient city, he was very knowledgeable and spoke excellent english, we paid 2000 SLR for this + tip ( at your own discretion ). Day 2 - Lion Rock, got up early, as can be very busy and of course very hot. What should of been an enjoyable climb, was spoiled by constant hassle from supposed tour guides, helpers & hawkers - they don't leave you alone. A polite 'No Thank you' would not suffice. It's very hot, very expensive, very busy, be prepared for the hassle & take lots of water.

Sigiriya world heritage site never ceases to amaze me. There is so much history behind how this rock citadel came to be. The King who created this monument out of the rock did so to find a secure place to hide after killing his father and knowing his brother would be seeking revenge. The history is not peaceful and it is difficult to reconcile the brutality of the king's heart with his appreciation of beauty and his creativity. Reading up on the history before going or hiring a guide is highly recommended.  Sigiriya is a must-see in Sri lanka.

Sigiriya is one of the greatest historical places to visit in Sri lanka. It is highly recommended that you read up on the history of this fantastic creation before you go or hire a guide to get the full benefit of the visit. I have visited the rock several times and the best view has been in the evening toward sunset when the view was clear.During the day, it could be pretty hot. Sigiriya never ceases to amaze me. Luckily on this visit there were no wasps. We were told that just last week some loud crowds were stung. Apparently these wasps abandon the nests during some periods, but nobody seemed to be giving a very clear explanation. It is a bit of a climb, but with frequent breaks, good shoes, plenty of water and determination, most people can do it. Our guide even said that there were people who would carry you for a fee. This, however, was not independently verified. The entry fee for foreigners is much higher than the local tourists. But, this amazing citadel is well worth the entry fee.
Get a guide, bring water, camera, tp for restrooms.  Took about 2.5 hours with many stops

We made a route deviation from Kandy to Colombo with a single aim to visit Sigiriya and Dambula, and have no regret for this. Our expectations were completely overpassed. We climbed to the rock top. Views over there are absolutely fascinating and deserve an effort.

Great way to spend a morning learning a bit of history, getting a bit of exercise and seeing an awesome 360 degree view. We hired a guide which would definitely recommend as was reasonable value and worth it to hear the history. Climb was fine if you are reasonably fit, although wear sensible shoes, at least trainers I reckon. View was fantastic at the top.  Take enough water with you too as was hot work even though we did it earlyish in the morning.

I have visited the Sigiriya site couple of times and I am amazed with its beauty. It is one of the best tourist attractions in Sri Lanka. This time we climbed to the top and enjoyed really well. I would recommend this place to everyone who visits Sri Lanka.

This is a breathtaking site!! The larger layout with gardens and watchtower-kind rocks is already fascinating, but highlights are the rock graffiti including the "cloud girls" and the climb up the rock to see the remains of the old fortress. Climbing is on steep metal or rock-cut steps, it takes some effort. Older people or people who are afraid of height are helped up by locals. Just don't look back.... Up there stunning views, remaing thrones and brick structures, lots of chamaleons and brisk winds. Get up early to avoid the crowds. The site opens at 7 am. Count your change when buying tickets, officials tried to cheat 1000 SR from me and locals told me that this happens offen. I asked for correct change (the lady even had a calculator) and the got it...  It is easy to spend lots of hours here as there is much to see on the way back, too - like the Cobra rock e.g. This is a stunning world heritage that stands up to the Pyramids or Angkor Wat temples and is an absolute must-see when visiting Sri Lanka!

With the art work and the situation of the palace, this site is pretty amazing and deserves being a tourist attraction for 1 1/2 millennia.  The murals, the graffiti, the palace. All pretty spectacular. it does get crowded so either come when it opens or late in the day (with enough light to see everything).

Simply stunning and spectacular.  This place has some much to offer and surpasses all expectations in what there is to be seen. Unfortunately it is also popular and not suitable for the volume of visitors. Try to get there really early or later in the day when hopefully all the groups are gone.  It is not pleasant when crowded.
Fabulous. Lots of stairs (1204). Go as early in the day as possible. Allow several hours to explore all around. An amazing World Heritage Site.

It is Sri Lanka landmark, so guess its something everybody goes to see, which also reflects on the pricing to get in. Yes its an old rock and fortress, so if that is your interest for sure go for it. That being said if you miss to see it then you will probably also survive.

Is a nice place to visit. Nice Buddhist paintings. although there are almost no remainings of the fortress. Lion paws still welcome the visitor when climbing to the top, where there are beautiful views. No need for guides. If you are equiped with a guide book or search on the Internet, you´ll probably get better information, and won´t need to pay additional "tips". We expected more of both the place and the guide. Bring water, as it may be hot. There are sellers around, although I guess they can charge two or three times more. Better go early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid heat peak.

This is one of the best places that I experienced in Sri Lanka. It is truly spectacular if you have the stamina to climb to the top and a lack of acrophobia.  There are places to rest along the way if you need to but there is no getting around the height.  Halfway up are the caves with beautiful paintings. Even though the climb was quite vigorous, there was a beautiful breeze that was most welcome and much of our climb, which started in the morning, was in the shade. Even so I would say that that you should bring water and a hat that you can keep on your head in the breeze. I also always travel with electrolyte tablets that I pop into my water bottle when needed. There were people climbing this with no shoes on and no water bottles visible but they were probably people used to living and working in a hot and humid environment. At the bottom we saw lots of macaque monkeys, one or two langur monkeys, giant squirrels and other local fauna.

If you wish to visit there I recommend you to climbe the rock as early as you can.becouse the climate is very hot at the day time on the top of the rock. It's better to have a guide or someone who knows about it bcos there are very interesting stories behind this heritage . Price is a bit high for the foreign visitors...

The place is amazing..View from the summit is wonderful. but management poor.. ticket charge for foreigners is very high... huge difference from the locals.. no additional benefits were provided to the foreigner in spite of the high charge.. Guides charged extra..

Superb archaeological site definitely worth visiting. The climb along the steep iron stairs can be problematic if you suffer from vertigo but holding on to the handrail becomes feasible. It 'a UNESCO heritage site and one of the major attractions of the country. Became famous in the fifth century when it becomes fortified town subsequently it became a Buddhist monastery remained in use until the fourteenth century. This user mutation has transformed the appearance because the monks have removed much of the beautiful frescos in the palace. The Port of Leonl, called "The Llon Rock" or the input port used by real and giving access through what remains of the open jaws of a lion carved in the rock; the secondary palace with its moats, the cavities richly decorated with frescoes and beautiful gardens that stretch for hundreds of meters over the edge of the rock.

1. Go to the museum first. If you leave it until last they won't let you back in to get to the exit car park which is in a different place to where you will be dropped off. 2. YOU DO NOT NEED A GUIDE. Especially if you have a Lonely Planet book. You will be approached by various men who will walk alongside you offering advice and support. One even got hold of my elbow and tried to help me up the steps and I had to ask him to stop it. In total we were approached by 11 of these men. The last one walked with us for five minutes because we couldn't shake him off and even though we said "no guide" he still asked for money. If hadn't been for these irritants I would have scored this trip review a 5 rather than 4. Despite all this though it was pretty amazing and I am glad we went.

It wasn't until we were on our way to Sigiriya rock, that our guide told us about the hornets! there are many nests a long the walk, and there have been many hornet attacks on tourists! Funny how we never heard of this before. You can lessen the risk by going first thing in the morning, before it gets too hot or too busy. Apparently attacks mostly happen around dusk, and when its too noisy. There are a lot of signs a long the path that warn you and tell you be quiet. However not all tourist seem to pay attention to these signs! But otherwise, was a great morning. We learnt some history about the fort, and climbed up to the second highest point. I am too scared of heights to go to the very top, as the only way up is on a narrow metal staircase, and it was full of tourists. Lovely view from were we were, didn't feel we missed out by not going any higher! Worth it to note some parts of quite steep, and there are a lot of steps. Not suitable for people who maybe elderly or injured.

One of the nicest location we visited during our trip to Sri Lanka. The site is well presented. Be ready, as in many places in Sri Lanka for steps but the view at the top is great. Good history lesson as well for for a civilization totally absent from our history books.

Came here, really liked what I saw but have to say Usd30 is a lot to pay for an attraction site, understand this covers the museum entry also but when I realize the locals are paying 40rupees, 20x less than me, I felt like foreigners were milked like a cow! I come from a third world country where we have the local/foreigner price difference and that's 3x fold, but 20x fold in Sri Lanka, I personally do not think this is right. Again, the usual constant harassment from locals offering guide service, some times saying no politely and asserting with a smile don't seem to work anymore as I got abused and followed.

30 USD each to get in, on the pricey side.  But probably still worth it - gardens are beautiful and the walk up to the top is pretty spectacular. Try to get there as early as possible to avoid mid day sun climbing! One word of warning: there are hornets nests attached to the side of the rock that you have to walk past (and signs telling you to stay silent). They swarmed while we were there and it was pretty scary! Wouldn't recommend with kids...
when visiting the cheaper rock you realize this is way to expensive to pay and see. sigiriya offers so much more than this

This place is spectacular, I want to say "must see". Clean nature around. You must be carefull in few things : 1. 1200 steps on the top (in 35°C very painful :-) ) 2. Helpers - never accept help on stairs, after that, they want money. 3. Stairs from lion foots to up looks dangerous, not for people, which are scared of heights. 4. Very expensive entrance for foreighners - 30€ 5. Don´t take a pictures of paintings - very big penalties (but don´t worry, you will be noticed many times

It's is the grandeur, beauty and tragedy unparalleled story in Sri Lankan history. Also it is located just 20 minutes from the town of Dambulla, Central Provence (Google Maps will help you). Make a challenge with your companion and ready to walk nearly 1800 steps to the top. Fair entrance fees for all local and foreign visitors. Vehicle parking available. Many accommodation facilities around Dambulla according to your requirements. Don't forget to take a camera ( DSLR :) ), wear a hat and anti-slip shoes. Just walk like a pro climber. Best place to show your fitness to everyone. Keep in mind that this is a UNESCO world heritage area and reflection of the proud people of Sri Lanka. Love #nature #photography #driving #music @shashikasign

“Sigiriya Rock”, this is a very important place to visit, a "MUST". The History, the ancient art, the view from the top, absolutely amazing. Go early to miss the crowds. Take a hat & water with, you will need it.

I recently visited Lion Rock with my family.  Firstly it is amazing.  The history, the climb, the views, the experience.  However, along with many attractions in this part of Sri Lanka (cultural centre), I found the entrance fee to be extortionate - way out of line with anything else in Asia, Europe, Australia I have ever visited.  I thought I might be missing something, but alas could not find it.  I suppose it is one of the main attractions in the country and you "have' to visit so they have a bit of a captive audience.  Needless to say, we paid the fee (about A$150) and went on our way.  It's definitely something not to miss in Sri lanka but at a price!

I visited Sigiriya Rock in mid September. my tour guide recommended me to visit first thing in the morning to avoid heat and crowd. I arrived a little past 7am. The weather was very nice, cool wind. No lines and took me about 30-40minutes to the top. I'm scared of heights but was not so scary as i thought. The view from the top was amazing. i had my breakfast under a tree, after minutes of climbing it tasted great and relaxing.  If you're planning to go during daytime, I highly recommend going there first thing in the morning. Cool and smooth. It would be amazing to see the sunset from the top, but thinking about the crowds and hotness visiting early in the morning was the right choice. By the time I was climbing down, it was hot and crowded. Sigiriya Rock is a must visit!
view from the top of the rock is just amazing. :) We saw everything, museum included in like 3 hours so it´s not for a whole day but definitely worth the visit while in Sri Lanka :).

Takes around 30-40 minutes to climb but well worth it. Some fantastic views from the top so worth the effort of the hot climb. Wear good shoes and take plenty of water for this as anyone with mobility issues might find this a struggle.

We came late saturday morning, but there were so many people we couldn't really go up unless you want to stuck closely with other people for hours. During dry period, the gardens are not so great looking and definitely don't go on weekends or holidays. For tourists it's horribly overpriced, more than 3000Rps. Shame, I really wanted to climb up, but chose an exceptionally bad time to visit. You can go around the crowd by staircases on the right, but still was jam packed.

Maybe the most important place in the country. Ready to walk 1200 steps to the top??? Have water and camera with you!!! You stay astonished to see the rock by far. But it gets more important to go above . The rock itself is very interesting but the view from above is breathtaking.

This magnificent  ancient rock fortress provides spectacular views and photo opportunities from even half way up the rock. Ancient markings are to be seen as you climb. The steps and track are well maintained and many of the steps as you climb higher have a railing to assist. Even if you go only halfway it is worth the trip. This is a unesco world heritage area and the people of Sri Lanka site it as one of their major tourist attractions.

We spent a couple of hours visiting this exceptional historical place. The climb to the top of the rock takes about 30 minutes and it is advised to take some water on the way up. The frescoes of the ladies are absolutely beautiful and in a great state of conservation. Definitely worth seeing ! We had a guide for our visit and this was helpful to understand the history of this site.

We come here from Colombo. The roads were lousy and bumpy, and took more than six hours to get here. We arrived at around 3pm. The stairs were not so steep than I thought but sometimes shaky and scary. You should carry plenty of water and wear proper shoes. On the TOP of the rocks, the view was breathtaking. Definitely worth a visit.
It's very well worth the climb. Go as early as possible (opens at 0730) to beat the heat and the crowds. Take plenty of water. The top provides amazing views of the surrounding countryside.

Sadly, didn't manage the climb past the lower stone steps which are very steep, narrow and with no hand rail. Further up are many more steps including metal spiral staircases. Beware the locals offering you a hand up the steps, as the will demand 100 rupees and hound you relentlessly. Nice grounds to wander round below. No doubt the review would have been different if I'd made it to the top and other members of our party thought it was amazing.
Of touristic importance! Nice place and we had a very good time after driving all the way from Colombo to Sigiriya.
This was unreal and I'd go again! Take good shoes, go early and take plenty of water. Crowds are large but once you're up top - it doesn't matter at all...
Second visit to this amazing place. If weather is very warm try and make your climb early in the morning before the midday sun. Carry water and be sure to get a photo on step 1200, the very top

This was one of the best experiences during the whole trip. It was not part of our iternary but we are glad we did it. Whole thing worked out expensive as we had to shell out big money for the cab and the entrance to this place is very expensive. SAARC nationals get a 50% off though. One should plan to get here in the early hours to beat the harsh sun. The walk from the ticket counter to the rock looks long but there are many caves with stories to tell through out the path. The ancient structure is very attractive and for those with an eye for architecture this can be a great experience. The climb up the rock is adventurous and the way they have built the walkway on the edge of the rock is thrilling. The rocks are home to wasps and there are warning boards that suggest a wasp attack. Once on top the views are breathtaking. on one side you get the view of the massive national park,if lucky yu could see wildlife activities. The ruler had bil his swimming pool and entertainment centre atop the monolith. Another must see in Sri Lanka.Its advisible to bundle this with wildlife activities.

Listen, you have to go, this place is out of this word, definitely worth the money (little over 4000Rp) and worth the steps. On a sunny day, it´s quite a hike but it´s doable, don´t doubt yourself. The view is so stunning, you won´t regret getting little sweaty, trust me.

Me and my husband were unsure whether to come here and we thought $30 was a bit expensive but we are so glad we did it now! The views are amazing and the Rock is so beautiful! The climb is also very enjoyable and not too challenging as most of it is in the shade. This is definitely a must.

Was a good hike,  not for those who are afraid of heights.  Plus be wary of locals who try and help you up the stairs.. They end up following you and demanding money... Shame this is the case with all locals I've met on my trip.  Once people start talking to you on the street,  expect that they are doing it for money..

Loved this place. Go early to beat the heat & crowds. Lots of steps but well set up. View is spectacular and the ruins on top were great to walk around. Not a lot of shade on top & was windy when we went. Grounds & museum were good to look around after the climb. You go up 1 way & back down partly another way the way down is much easier. You are suppose to exit via a different car park but as we did the museum last we just got our driver to pick us up in the drop off car park and missed the hawkers. Take water however there is a kiosk with food & cold drinks.

The whole complex at ground level and up on the rock is actually quite interesting. The climb to the top is strenuous, but most of it is at least on even, metal staircases which helps a bit. I was there on a Sunday morning before it got too hot. Top of the rock is very windy. All in all, this is the reason to visit the area

Overhyped and overpriced. After visiting other magnificent ancient sites in Asia (Ankor Wat=incredible) this came as a thorough disappointment. I did not expect it to meet those standards, however what really disappointed me was the exploitation of tourists. The difference in price for Sri Lankans vs tourists was exorbitant!The relevant council must surely do something about this, as I was definitely not alone in thinking this.
Very nice half a day trip. A lot of monkeys running around, which was great! Fantastic view from the top. It may be challenging for people with acrophobia.
Amazing wonder of ancient Sri Lanka. Visit hear and learn about ancient history and how the rock fortress was built. It is pretty amazing to thing what ancient people in Sri Lanka created.
His was a hot and epic half day experience. Take loads of water with you and good walking shoes... At the top are the most amazing ruins with an incredible view of the land 😍

Yes ... it's ridiculously expensive for what it is and Yes ... you are sharing your experience with a lot of other hot and sweaty people but it is so worth it! We started at 4pm which was still very warm and had some big tour groups there at the time. Pack water then double it ... we went through 2litres each... the climb is possible in thongs/flip flops but so much more comfortable in proper shoes....no need to cover up as there are in the temples , I took a sarong and ended up with it over my shoulders to keep the sun off ... be as rude as you need to with the every helpful guides if you don't want one to 'help'... we were soon left alone. Overall a great afternoon

I have just written a review and more concise view on Sigirya and how on a hot and humid day this is not a great attraction for unfit or elderly people as it is a shame as the place is magical,mysterious and a wonderful place to come to. Take plenty of water with you and try to visit around early morning before it gets too busy with pilgrims and tourists. Be prepared for steep climbs and steps that are not tourist friendly,so wear suitable footware which is a must. But if you are on a tour to Sri Lanka then you must have this a High priority place to come too.

After a long drive and little sleep from the night before we arrived at the very impressive Sigiriya world heritage site and we were blown away with the mystery and wonder of the place. Very busy and very hot The place was packed with pilgrims and tourists,but not as many as had been told so try to visit early on in the day. The ruins and gardens are amazing and we could have wandered around for hours,but it was so hot and humid ( take plenty of water with you ) Our guide had wonderful knowledge of the place and was very informative. Not sure on admission as pre paid The museum was a slight waste of time but a cool place to get out of the heat,showed the history of Sigirya and artifacts found. Walked up to the Lions rock and climbed some of the way,but refused to go to the top as very high up,and asked our guide how long to get up and down,he said about 3 hours,and as it was getting around mid afternoon we would have had to climb down in the dark,and after a long hot day did'nt fancy that at all. He got quite cross with us,but as we were paying him for his service,,tough. It looked a long and hard climb too the top,and we are not that old and fairly active and fit,I can't see elderly or disabled people will be able to go up to the top as all climbing. All in all a magical place,but if not very fit,people may struggle on this visit.

The view was great, but 30$ is way too expensive! We even had a residence visa because we live and work in this country, but they would not give us the local price like at any other place. They offered us to go to Colombo to get half back. This policy is not acceptable.

Well we went there around Noon and it was as hot as it gets in Sri Lanka i am guessing, it was over crowded with people and even though the view is pretty cool from the top I guess its not worth the money, they charge you 4.260 SLR for it which is more expensive then any entrances around the globe, its better to go to Pidurangala Rock which is just 500 SLR and the view is 100 times better and no crowd and its worth it.. especially for the sunset.. keep lots of water while climbing these Rocks....

Another place that I've been that has made me marvel at the determination and innovation of ancient people. It is simply mind blowing to imagine people climbing up and building on this enormous rock. The views from the top are truly breathtaking and almost prehistoric. I was initially quite apprehensive about doing the climb with our 18 month old son, but it was do-able with him in a carrier. Don't be put off if you have kids: you can do it!

This was an amazing experience and definitely something everyone visiting Sri Lanka should do. Can't quite remember the exact price to get up, around 2000 rupees, but definitely worth it. There are guys wandering around that will act as a tour guide for you, but we opted to just go up alone. Amazing views with really cool history. Expect lots of stairs!
The rich Heritage of the ancient Kingdom a castle/ Fortress build on a rock surrounded by the water and rock gardens and the beautiful  paintings on the rock and the murals on the wall.

Two hours drive from the capital, roads are great. There is a fee to enter the UNESCO world heritage site, approximately 2000 LKR. There is a discount for SARCC countries, upon passports being presented. There is a museum that explains the specialty of the fort on the rock. Its well explained and can be completed in 1 hour. Even has replicas of the paintings for those who can not make it till the point. Suggested to now ascend the fort. We did not take a guide as we were told it is very expensive. The walk is long till the top. Carry water bottles. Also best time to get to the top is during sunset. Around 5pm in September. Makes for great photographs. It is very windy on the top. Tie down all caps and clothes. The monkeys in the fort are wild. The animals do not care as they scratch and grab food. Advised not to feed. Local dogs however are milder and ask for food, seen at the base and top. Once back at the bottom, the cafeteria only has a few items but there was a evening entertainment program at 1830hrs. We didn't get to see it as we had to travel further till our next stop.

Two hours drive from the capital, roads are great. There is a fee to enter the UNESCO world heritage site, approximately 2000 LKR. There is a discount for SARCC countries, upon passports being presented. There is a museum that explains the specialty of the fort on the rock. Its well explained and can be completed in 1 hour. Even has replicas of the paintings for those who can not make it till the point. Suggested to now ascend the fort. We did not take a guide as we were told it is very expensive. The walk is long till the top. Carry water bottles. Also best time to get to the top is during sunset. Around 5pm in September. Makes for great photographs. It is very windy on the top. Tie down all caps and clothes. The monkeys in the fort are wild. The animals do not care as they scratch and grab food. Advised not to feed. Local dogs however are milder and ask for food, seen at the base and top. Once back at the bottom, the cafeteria only has a few items but there was a evening entertainment program at 1830hrs. We didn't get to see it as we had to travel further till our next stop.

I can't believe I did it !!! - Words at the top.. Sigiriya when you see it from afar is something you definitely want to climb..as recommended by the people of Sri Lanka. So my husband and I did it. Recommended to wear sneakers, sunscreen and a hat.. and oh yes...take a water bottle...you will need it. You could make use of the guides (but better to take a registered guide other than people hanging around the place asking you if you need a guide). We did not take one as we were more interested in just the climb and the view and they give you a pamphlet wih information as well as they are placards over the place.. this felt sufficient for us. Although we did see a group in front of us with a Sri Lankan guide explaining in German...so I guess they offer guides who speak different languages. When I reached half way, I almost gave up. But once you get going again, there's nothing that can stop you. There is a cave with pre historic paintings ..so beautiful.. and you also see lion claws...carved out of rock.. The view at the top is simply breathtaking.. And you can see a statue of Buddha afar. Lovely experience. The way down is another route and alot quicker. You honestly don't feel it at all. There are people selling wooden artifacts and paintings.. it's entirely upto you to make a purchase. There is a bathroom (male female separate) when you finish your walk at the bottom where the cars are parked. Clean and well maintained. The place is well maintained by the Cultural Heritage department. Worth the climb !

So the grounds are amazing, so beautiful that it is almost too much to take in all at once. Massive area. We had one of the guides on site and he was absolutely amazing, he knew every intricate detail of the grounds, the history and the whole area. Started climbing the rock and you don't realize at first the amount of stairs, by the time I got only 1 third of the way up I was already huffing and puffing, no need to mention the state of me by the time I eventually got up the more than 1200 stairs!! Legs like jelly, calves aching but a great experience and would highly recommend to anyone willing

We visited Sigiriya Rock on a day trip whilst staying at Kandy, which was an hour or so group taxi ride away, organised through our hostel. This made up for the price of the entry fee for tourists, so we'd still recommend going. It's advised to visit in the morning, to avoid the midday sun, however, due to lack of communication from our driver, we ended up arriving later in the day. It was indeed VERY hot and a sweaty climb with lots of others and there is not much shade at the top, but this didn't bother us. The views take your breath away. Take lots of water, snacks, and a hat/scarf for shade! (We then visited the Dambulla Cave Temple on the way backto Kandy which worked out really well)

Although I didn't make it to the top as I have a knee problem I did get to see the frescos which I really wanted to do.  The spiral staircase part wasn't easy for me for I was pleased I did it, though coming down was harder.  There is plenty to see on the lower parts and it is a site worth visiting.

A must visit place if you go to Sri Lanka..this is an awesome place..the paintings have withstood the elements for hundreds of years. The remains of the ancient settlement is a true wonder of the world..you should climb to the top well within.25

We went Sigiriya just for Lion's Rock - there really isnt much else to do here. The tickets are expensive at 4150LKR per adult, but the view from the top is really not too bad, and the climb is very steep and tiring but short (compared to World's End, which is like a 9km hike). Do go to the museum at the entrance - ask where it is as its easy to miss - going there lets you see a replica of the frescoes (wall paintings) as well a mini model of the place - it gives you an understanding of where you are going, what you are looking at, and also a history of the place. Do take pictures of the replica, as you will not be allowed to take any at the real site.

Great place to visit. Views from the top were great but you get just as good views (if not better) from Pidurangala rock. The only downside to it was the price. Far too expensive. Would have been happy paying 2000 rupees per person but not nearly 5000 per person

Go early, this is not a site to climb with lots of people and you miss the heat. Try about 7 am when the site opens and the climb can be undertaken at your own pace. The climb requires a degree of fitness but one of our number was recovering from a serious accident and managed all but the last section with his walking stick. The painting gallery is lovely, ancient figurative frescoes, still looking fresh. You can't take photos here but the figures are in most reputable art history books. When you get to the Lion Platform you are nearly there. While you are climbing the stairs look for the large wasp nests clinging to the clif face. The ruins are beautiful and extensive and amazing to contemplate how it was constructed. From the many vantage points you San see the parks and gardens stretching out for miles. The entry cost is approximately $25 and worth every penny

The grounds were really lovely with some spots to take photos of the rock.  The foundations of the ponds are interesting and the grandeur of the whole site is breathtaking.  The steps are steep but ok. I was too scared once I saw the suspended spiral staircase after checkpoint two to go any further. You get bothered by the guys offering their 'help' and telling stories about tourists being rushed to hospital with broken ankles from falling down steps ( maybe it's true so be careful). Also there are lots of men selling stuff so if you haven't stocked up on wooden elephants or magic boxes, it's perfect. The price? Well yeah, it's comparatively expensive especially if you decide not to climb! Lol.

Unfortunately, Sri Lanka is not improving on its reputation for gouging tourists. My fiance & I visited on a day where hundreds of locals were also in attendance. Some were holding small children and, we were squashed against the young & the old making the slow ascent up Lion Rock. One would woop it up as part of the experience were it not for the excessive difference in pricing for "foreign" versus local ticket prices. Were our opinion of value, we would say that USD$20, not $30, though still high, would at least be received with less gall. The ticket also only allows you to enter the Museum & certain sections of the rock once. Because the crowds made manoeuvring difficult, we had to cut short our museum visit to make sure we could actually explore Lion Rock before close. Ideally, we would have liked to return after coming down but, we lost that option. Coming from a country that boasts its own rock attractions, Sigiriya was still an exception because of its unique history and, though now only a ruin, the palatial remains that sit at the very top of Lion Rock. The Rock itself is a shock of colours and, it provides ample vantage points to take in beautiful panoramic views. Some may recommend the additional investment of a local guide. The guides themselves mill around the ticket booth and impose heavily on "foreign" tourists to engage their services. I wouldn't bother in my opinion but, you may have a bigger wad of american dollars to part with than I & my partner!

Sigiriya - is a huge rock, on top of the rock there is ruins of a temple built by a King. the whole experience to climb the rock (well they have stairs), before you climb the very top theres a place to enjoy the views. to climb the top the steps are narrower nut not an issue, once got up loved it every bit . and you try to picture the whole palace. Note: queue to climb so better to try as early as possible as you could be in 1 hour queue on the middle of the climb too. must to do. after the climb we went to a near by massage place very very relaxing.

The gardens around the rock were lovely and a great place to watch monkeys! Tourists have to pay $30 each to climb 2000 steps! If you are interested in visting the museum, do it before the climb - the tourist car park is in a different place to the drop off area and takes you through an area of small stalls selling drinks and 'handmade' souvenirs. The climb itself is a very hot, hard, convivial slog, but there are lovely rewarding views and a welcome breeze on the top.

This place is high. You'll have to climb it, so bring plenty of water. Entrance fee is around 4200 per person. You'll have to walk up the stairs all the way and some of them will test you, if you are challenged with heights. However, it is very nice once you make it up. Bring a guide book to learn more .. or get a guide, if this is more your thing.

Sigiriya is and archaeological site which contains ruins of our ancient palace. 1200 steps to climb but don't worry there are several platforms to rest. About half way of the rock a spiral stairway will take you to famous Sigiriya paintings. Wow ! There no similar figures among them. Make sure to take plenty of water, hat, good shoes and of course your camera. Do it early morning to beat the heat & the crowd. Well worth the climb. Stunning views from the top , will be amazed !!.

Don't approach this if you are not fighting fit or don't like heights. If you meet these criteria what are you waiting for. It's a long way 1200 steps. It's hot. Might be better early or later although we did it in mid day. You might need a change of clothes. Locals for this barefoot so no excuse really. Fantastic view from the top

The rock and the idea that there used to be a monastery and a fortress there is really impressive. The view from the rock is spectacular. But it is definitely too expensive. There are many sites in the world as impressive but for less then 30$ per person. Not sure it's worth that money...
We went on a hot day so always make sure you have water. We did have to queue for a while to get up but so worth it when you get to the top. A must

Myself and my fiancé visited Sigiriya Rock only yesterday and it was very good to climb. It's not too hard to climb (elderly and children were hiking it) but it is a good work out! Big negative - the price. We understand it's important to pay to maintain these sites but they charge foreigners 4200 LKR ($30) each! And locals go up for 40 LKR. Now maybe westerns have more money, but most of the locals were trekking up in better clothes and better phones and cameras than me! A lot of forum activity is always very angry at Sri Lankas attitude to foreigners and entry prices. Our thought was that we paid the money to get from London to SL and then to Sigiriya. So we paid it. Tips: / Ask about bees and wasps on the rock. If you get up and they shut it for bees you don't get your money back and you can't climb - Whatttt! / Take some water and watch out for your hats, lots of hats were flying off when we were walking and one gentleman lost a very special hat and seemed quite down from the strong wind / Watch out for monkeys! They are confident around humans and one tried to steal our drinks on the way to the rock / watch out for guides. Our tuktuk driver said that the guides will teach you about the rock but it's better to take a guide book. They are usually reluctant to talk all that much and you will generally pay $30 - $40 for one. Overall it was kind of cool but not worth $60 for two people in my opinion. At $10 each it would seem more in line with the experience. You will have to judge if it's worth it. My advice, skip the rock - see the elephants for the same price if you can only do one. The national parks are far better than the rock in my opinion.

This is truely amazing! If you are going to or staying in Sri Lanka this is an absolute must! It is a bit of a hike to get to the top but it is so worth it!! Such beautiful views and great photo opportunities as there are still quite a few ruins in the top! The view of the surrounding area is amazing! Try to do t earlier in the day as it does get quiet hot around lunch although we had a strong breeze (wind) while we were climbing! Just watch out for guys trying to help you up the rock!

I decided to do the gardens and rock climb while friends went Zen with yoga session. First, it is exy 35 USD. You can only enter once, can't see gardens separately, and probably not worth entry fee to just see gardens. Rock is spectacular as you approach from western side. The climb is in sections so not tough at all. It is shaded and there was a strong cooling zephyr. There is a helical spiral stair upto the wall paintings which are amazing. Sadly you have to descend down another staircase before ascending to lions paw steps. There was a tank of drinking water here for all and sundry. I drank and survived. The ascent to the top is not difficult via some 2 way stairs. Note the massive fungi on L side of cliff as ascending. The top affords great views. There is alot of reconstruction work going on, and the workers want to engage the tourists. There are about 4 trees up there and their shadows disappear after 11 am so try and get there early if want to loiter. Otherwise 20-30 mins at top is enuf. I went up around 830 am. Don't know what it would be like on pm.

One of the amazing touristic site in Sri Lanka. Quite high and risky to climb because the the law level of safety system. But the ancient kingdom and the architecture just amazing. Its a must to see those cave paintings. Try to avoid visiting on weekends because crowed.

A 2 hour trip that you'll talk out forever. The ancient history of Sigiriya makes it an intriguing place to visit, and the views from the top and seeing the lily ponds and old constructions are truly breathtaking. There are no vendors en route so my advice would be to have 1l of water on you.
No one can imagine what they are going to see there. Just avoid to see any detailed pictures of the place before going there. Doing that is like to see a movie spoiler.

This is iconic rocky structure in Sri Lanka and I was wonder struck with the first sight. It's on Dambula- Habarana main highway. An amazing creation from 5th Century served as military and royal purpose for King Kassapa. Some archeologisits hold a view that it's not a royal palace but a Buddhist monastery connected with deep religious functions. Whatever the debate, it's the most imposing and dramatic struture in Sri Lanka.Declared as  World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1982, Sigiriya is not a place to missed by anyone travelling in this country. It's better to start climbing vertiginous and circular staircase, sometimes with help of railings as early as possibly in the morning to avoid fierce heat. There is a ticket for all  and for those from South Asia(they must carry the passport) to get ticket at concessional rate. On the way I was thrilled to see expansive landscape, remarkable frescoes and thick vegetation around including waterbodies and artificial terrrace gardens. It's a must to wear a hat and also a bottle of water and also apply sun screen lotion. Those with heart problems or any serious health issues should avoid the climb or consult their Physician well in advance. At the entrance before reaching the summit on a large platform one has to begin real ascent through two Lion's Paws( there used to be gigantic brick Lion but it no longer exist). There are mysterious ruins at the summit and also offer astonishing  365 degree view from the top. The Mirror Wall on the way contain unusual graffiti,inscriptions and erotic poems. While coming down one can see ancient caves like Cobra cave, Gardens and sculptured structures. After coming down it's a must to visit the Museum that provide excellent and reliable overview of life and times of ancient Sigiriya( same ticket is valid). There is also souvenir shop in the Museum also selling few well researched publications. There will be lots of guides hanging around but it can be avoided or better negotiate clear price before engaging such guides. There are good public toilets and a teashop at exit point for parking place for vehicles of foreign travellers.

Its a must do but its not easy. No health and safety here!! Narrow stone steps that climb forever and high winds.. Its a matter of one foot in front of the other until you reach summit. Take your time,  water , comfy shoe's and a hat. Its worth it.

Quite a physical and psychological challenge. Although there were some elderly people climbing the steps in flips flops I recommend a decent pair of trainers as a minimum. It can get congested at times and therefore become annoying when progress is slowed by slower people and then you get bumped and jostled by a large group of school kids pushing there way through.... in some parts this climb is I would say on the "unsafe" side and it would not be allowed in most countries due to the complete lack of any health and safety.... However once at the top the views are absolutely outstanding. The ruins on the top leave you in awe of the task itself to build the Citadel.... mind boggling
We could see the rock from our hotel. While lying in its pool, the rock appeared to be huge. In fact it isn't. Our friends tried climbing it but I didn't I think taking photos are enough.

This amazing rock with such historical significance looked intimidating at first.  We went in the middle of the day!! on a local public holiday so very busy and a slow queue up.  That was just the time we arrived from Kandy. On the up side it was nice to be surrounded by locals rather than tourists.  I am nervous of heights but found it manageable by focusing on where I was (each step sometimes) and only looking down when I felt able.  I stopped before the last summit as feared heat stroke and my companion went to the top and highly recommends that.  Waiting a level down was entertaining with the local monkeys.  I think locals should be able to visit for next to nothing, it's their heritage and they are proud of that.  Don't miss it!

Awesome site to visit. Separate enterance for foreigners (I did not like this as I was with local friends) and price was very highly for me only. The heritage site was awesome , grounds clean and kept and guide was very informative . Guided walk for 1500 rupees and it was worth is. The stairs was a killer but worth the view

The entry fees is 30$ but tourists from Saarc countries have to pay 15$ per person. The climb on stone steps are a little tedious.But overall climbing up was not so difficult as there was slow moving crowd! You can rest at lion's paw and then climb further! The museum there is also good.The  water gardens were good too!
4260 Rs entry but worth it, arrive early and get up the hill (no water on the way,1h up). Great views at top, then museum is good!

Worth the climb for the spectacular views from the top.  It's not a hard climb if you're relatively fit. We set off about 7.30 and by the time we descended about 8.45 there was a continuous queue coming up. Meeting so many at the top would have spoiled the atmosphere and made photography much harder.
Very beautiful water garden and painting Be careful from local guides there are trying to charge about 20$ it is very high

I would recommend to try and get as early as possible to avoid the people and the heat, preferably before 8 o'clock. Once you have climbed all those steps you are offered amazing views of the surrounding area.

For any visitor to Sri Lanka climbing to the summit of this rock is a must do.  The whole site is fascinating, even if you cannot manage the 2,000 steps to the top.  However, those who make the effort will have a great experience and enjoy fabulous views. Take note that the locals have very little idea of the concept of queueing!  Take plenty of water.  Be firm to turn down unwanted offers of help from local men.  Anyone without a head for heights should note that there are some suspended metal stairs.

This is well known for its cave paintings and mirror wall. Perfect example for the  Irrigation system srilankan had in the past. Once you get to the top the views are amazing. Better to avoid long week ends/week ends as  it will be crowded. Not wise to climb if you are afraid of height. Best time of the day to visit is morning.

A very well-preserved archialogical site with very well preserved gardens. The climb up the rock was easier than I expected,  although I strongly recommend you take water with you as there is nowhere to buy anything once you leave the base.

This is a historical place worth visiting. In around AD400 a King has built a rock fortress on the rock with near vertical faces. Even today the climb is hectic and is not for the fearful or the weak. But if you can muster the courage,  the time spent visiting and climbing is well worth while. The surrounding area and the villages are also very fine place for the photographers especially the bird photographers. There are several very fine hotels nearby to relax after the hectic climb.

Bit of disgrace this attraction the cost is astronomical, 4300 Sri Lankan which equates to around £ 21.50 is a lot for one person to walk up a rock ! Yes it's interesting but once you've read the guide book and know the history etc there's not a lot else to it.  Even in the quiet season, I was there today it is crammed with people, it's got to be the worst experience I've had in Sri Lanka I'd really advise you not to bother, visit a temple instead at puja and see real life at no cost and gain something from the experience. The appalling thing with this is that we as westerners we pay the huge inflated cost and if you have a Sri Lankan passport the cost is 50 rupee, that is 86 times the cost for us !!! Imagine if we done that in the uk charging foreigners more ? I've no problem paying to see a sight in order to pay for its protection and upkeep but this is unfortunately Sri Lankan corruption at its best.

It's usd 30 which is expensive but it's worth going. There's a reason why it's a world heritage site. Make sure you have enough water, proper shoes and a good condition because it is a heavy climb. You'll get a map at the entrance so you know where to go and what you're looking at. Don't miss out the wall paintings, that's what I loved the most

Travelled with another family and 6 of 8 climbed to the top for the amazing views.  Wasp nests half way up were a tad disconcerting but no need for alarm. Recommend going early as gets hot at the top.

My wife and I visited the site. We started up at 10 and that worked perfect. We were in the shade most of the time.  The hike is not difficult--just go at your own pace. Round trip takes ~3 hours. It is an impressive archeological site--although no buildings are intact.  The most impressive parts of the site are the frescoes of young women--and the lion paws! A guide is recommended

We can totally recommend a trip to the Lion Mountain (Lions Rock!) It is absolutly worth the money and the time it takes to go on the top! Take a big bottle of whater and a cap/hat with you, it'll make it easier! Once on top: Enjoy! =) It's also clever to go early in the morning, because of the heat and because there won't be so many people. Have fun! =)

This is one of the must see sights in Sri Lanka and is an iconic view. It lives up to its hype and is well worth the hike to the top. Its relatively expensive (thats a whole different story though that gets covered in more detail on the forums) but its still well worth it. The grounds leading to the rock are beautifully kept bounded by man made lakes covered in lotus plants. We went early in the morning (the ticket office opens at 7:00) which meant that we were in shade on the way up. The stone steps lead to iron spiral staircases that take you to the top via some beautiful rock paintings but its not at all dangerous though still quite a nervy climb in places (at least for me!). We passed the much talked about hornet nests but we saw no evidence of them flying around which was a relief. At the top the 360 degree view is magnificent  of the surrounding countryside dotted with lakes, distant mountains, temples and buddha statues. The ruins of the palace are not great to be fair and it would be useful if there was some more information on display though this didn't detract from a memorable visit.

We climbed Lion Rock on a hot day, but it was worth it. The climb took 1.5 hours return. Going up was a bit of hard work in the hot sun, with many people also doing the climb, it got a bit busy on those stairs. The view and the history at the top of the climb was worth it. Don't forget to wear comfy shoes and take water.

Well we went in 2009 when I believe it was very cheap to enter. The place is just amazing even the lovely hornets make it a bit more exiting, especially running down the rickety stairs to get away from them. Would love to be able to be there alone and maybe camp in the grounds A must see if you are near the place.

This truely was an amazing experience for us (we are not young chooks anymore)as it was a real challenge climbing up all 1202 steps to the top. We engaged the services of a tour guide, which would not have been necessary if the caretakers have printed material that could guide us through the site and also give us a brief on the history,etc,etc.  With proper written material, it would surely attract much more foreign tourists than the site does at present. This probably is one of the better managed historical sites in the country and hope it continues to be so. A wonderful experience!!!

The $30 entrance is not cheap. The stairs now better maintained and the final climb now includes safety rails and stairs bolted to the Rock face. The climb is not extremely long, it takes about 1 hour to get to the top at a leisurely pace if you are fit. You really need to be fit and not afraid of heights.
