Avoid offers of help or if you take a guide make sure it is one of the accredited and approved guides. About half way up just before the Mirror Wall you can go up a fairly rickety very high spiral staircase to see the famous Rock Paintings of Sigiriya. If you are not afraid of heights you need to do this. Well worth the trip even if the entrance fee is overpriced. Definitely a World Heritage Site.

We climbed this around 8 in the morning. It took us total 2 and half hours to complete this.. The climb may be little scary for few people but no much climbing or hiking skills required as the total climb is on stairs and slopes. While we climbed we saw kids and older aged ppl climbing too so nothing much to fear. The view is amazing both from beneath and from the summit.. The cost is 4250 Rs for the climb which is too pricey and they have a 50% discount for SAARC citizens. Would recommend if you are here in sigiriya. A day well spent.

Sigiriya is one of the World heritage site in Sri Lanka. Sigiriya rock fortress is one of the  great archaeological site in Asia. If you know to great Sri Lankan proud, Sigiriya is the best place for that. Because Sigiriya is unique combination of Hydraulic management, gardening, Urban planning, architecture, art, sculpture, engineering & poetry. Sigiriya history we can divided in to 3 different eras. 01. Pre- Kashyapa era 02. Kashyapa era 03. Post- Kashyapa era Among those periods Kashyapa era was golden period of Sigiriya. (477 - 495 AD). That 18 period King Kashyapa rule this Sigiriya rock fortress. * To conserve or enhance the environment * To maintain symmetrical presentation are two main concepts followed by the Sigiriya builders. Sigiriya pleasure garden we can divided in to three, * Water garden * Boulder garden * Terrace garden Sigiriya water garden can be considered as one of the oldest in the World which is still functioning. Other most important parts are * Sigiriya frescoes * Grafifiti * Mirror wall Sigiriya frescoes have been a wonderful gallery of paintings. Now only few paintings are remaining.  The technique used is called fresco bueno which means to paint the wet plaster. Entrance ticket for foreigners US $ 30.00 or SLR 4260.00. After the ticket firstly you visit Sigiriya Museum. Then you can good knowledge about Sigiriya rock fortress. Always keep you tickets with you. Because Museum, close to  Water moat and before the frescoes check the ticket. Warmly welcome to visit Sigiriya and share Sri Lankan experience.

built on top of a rock , i need not go into detail as every traveler who looks up about the lion rock will get familiar with this famous story about this fortress build for betrayal. Things to note if you are not traveling with a local guide is , how the ponds at the top of a rock still have water to date, the carved rocks and other ruins still standing with the water fountains around this run down world heritage site will amaze the more inquisitive traveler. On top of the rock you get a breath taking 360 degree view of the surrounding. The Best time to climb is early in the morning or at around 3 in the afternoon, avoid a being on the top at mid day. Its not a long climb ( less than 1 hour) but take time to see the surrounding structures at the base of the mountain. the cost for foreigners is USD 30, its worth it i suppose. (local i think less than 1 USD)

This place is really amazing. We were here early in the morning so it was not too hot to climb up. I advise take a guide, you can find in parking area. They are very helpful and tell you a lot of history and interests. You can pay him around 2000- 3000 Rps
Very nice place to see and to learn about it's history, but very big difference between price for locals (less than a dollar) to what western foreigners are being charged ($30)

Sigiriya, was always on my bucket list, ever since I got to know about this place on the famous TV programme - Ancient Aliens...!! My mind had continously debated with itself, on how could man achieve such a magnificent feat of building a palace on top of a natural rock mountain of over 500 feet..... Finally, I got the opportunity to visit this UNESCO world heritage site, which is the most visited place in Sri Lanka as per statistics... I was expecting good, but the experience was simply amazing....  This massive rock structure towers above you as far as your sight goes.... Not to mention, every stone, every step tells a story.... Be it the "Boulder gardens",  "Cobra caves", "Mirror wall", Fresco paintings, The Lion paw entrance,  Citadel on the top..... Everything is like a leaf from a fairy tale book... Lankan history attributes the credit of building this citadel to the kings of Kasyapaa dynasty,  yet the intriguing folk-lores of King Ravana, extra - terrestrial beings and outer world beings intervention adds to the mystery of this place.... One might never be able to ascertain what actually is true, yet what remains and can be seen gives glimpses of an illustrious past.... For my fellow visitors, do visit once, but with an open mind... Read the history, but do look beyond it.... An interesting incident -  I saw and heard the guides explaining about the fresco paintings to one Spanish tourist couple,and while pointing out to a fresco painting he said, he will show errors that the painter made while making them.... Like 6 fingers on one of the maidens, and 3 nipples, or half body missing in the cloud.... ( to the un-initiated,  I will say,  our ancestors were smart and I would never, even in my dreams would doubt their intelligence that they would do such a silly thing.. Lol) Maybe, they knew much more about the concept of extra-terrestial, mutation or even more than what we presently know... But, the paintings are a true work of art and been preserved for soo long is intriguing in itself. So,  I feel, that this amazing place gives you an introspection of what we know is nothing as compared to the knowledge of what is not know.... Enjoy the special view from the top.. Best time to visit is early morning, while is sun is not at its peak... Carry lots of water... You can reach sigiriya either by road thru car or bus, or by train. I chose the train journey for the sheer joy of it..  Train leaves Colombo at 6 am and reaches Habarana at around 11.30.  From there a tri Shaw ride costs approx 100lkr. There are separate pricing for the entry ticket for tourists and for locals. All in all, I'm happy to Complete one of the places off my bucket list... Would definitely recommend this to all Travellers....

I have travelled many countries, have visited many UNESCO sites and my experience in Sigiriya was the worst in my 15 years of travelling... 1. entrance fee 30usd, the locals pay 80x less... 2. we stayed more than one hour in a queue to reach the mirror wall, than we repeated this procedure to climb last streetch 3. for the entrance fee you don`t get anything, no guide, no material- simply nothing Overall that we payed 80x more than locals (and getting nothing for that) is simply unacceptable.... Marko

The entrance to the site was around 40USD which is worth paying. The park before the Lion's rock is very nice with monkeys wondering around, but the main attraction is the Lion's rock with it's citadel. The climb to the top for some people can be a little scary but I enjoyed it a lot. Once up, the view is beautiful and it simply makes you wonder how could somebody build a citadel on this rock.

Travelled to Sigiriya on September 12th (11:00 hours) after visiting Dambulla Cave temples. Beautifully maintained historic site, clean and well presented. I wrote a review of this but it seems to have disappeared into the ether. So I will do my best to recreate that review from memory. This is a must-do, but if you are not fit or have young children or are afraid of heights (some of the climb is on dodgy looking metal stair cases set into the rock), I would reconsider. Sri Lankans seem to do it regardless of physical condition or children - I saw a mother and child being pulled up the stairs (not out of any malice, but as assistance). I will come to the central focus of the location in a little bit. The whole area is of interest. Surrounding the unmissable rock are areas of archeological interest, ruins of water gardens and other structures, caves, original plaster behind a poorly presented glass or Perspex protective casing which makes it so hard to see the plaster and other areas. A good map or guide would help in hitting the highlights apart from the rock. There is a second mound in the same area, quite visible from Sigiriya. We did not climb it but could see others had done so. I imagine it provides an unparalleled view of Sigiriya (unless you wanted to chance a helicopter or light aeroplane flight). As far as I can tell, tickets are for the day. Which means that, if you want to do everything within the region, it is a whole day affair and you will need to deal with the heat in the middle of the day. Also be aware that they do shut down the summit due to wasps - so check before you buy your tickets. We started our ascent to Sigiriya shortly before 4pm at the ticket counter. There is a lot of climbing! Funnily enough, the Sri Lankans seem in a hurry to get to the top and will push past. You get funnelled into single file any way, so not sure what all of this achieves. If your objective is the summit, veer right immediately after the ticket check at the base of the rock. Here, you will see people queuing up to go left and up a vertical circular staircase - this just leads to a small cave with some rock art. Impressive as it is, you simply get funnelled back down the staircase and onto the the other path. If you veer right instead of joining the queue, you go straight past the staircase, past the mirror wall and up to the Lion's Paws and then the final ascent to the summit. The summit is covered in archeological ruins. It must have been a glorious sight once, but is now nothing more than the base of the walls and foundations. The photos on postcards are somewhat misleading - they are taken after days of rains when water pools within the foundations. On this hot, dry day, there was only one location with water. It is an impressive sight, as are the surrounding mountains and region, which can be seen clearly from the summit. The climb down is much the same as the climb up, albeit faster - exercise more care. This is not a rainy day event - I expect the metal staircases will be slippery. Also, if you follow the signs to the international guests car park, make sure your driver knows to look for you there - it is not at the same location as the ticket counter and you may be faced with an even longer walk back if you haven't discussed this with your driver. Not all drivers know of this car park (and I am speaking from personal experience, having walked two sides of the base of Sigiriya as a result)!

We visited Lions Rock with a pre-arranged guide who was very good and gave us lots of information, history and stories about this site. It can get a bit windy and the last part is on a narrow fairly exposed pathway with reinforced metal railing so not ideal for those with vertigo. Once at the top however you are rewarded with the ruins of a fairly large palace including swimming pool and its hard to believe that people carried all the necessary materials up and down the rock to build this complex. There is a nice yet hazy (at least the day we went) view from the top of the surrounding area. You can see for miles. The grounds around the main rock are also interesting to visit and restoration work is continually ongoing and more parts of the whole complex are being restored and uncovered. There are toilets just after the entrance but not in the grounds or once you reach the top of the rock. There are also some fairly large hornets nests present but the staff are ready for any attack and there is even a metal cage for visitors to run into to be protected just before the last part of the climb in the event the hornets let loose! There are also signs asking people to keep the noise down so as not to provoke an attack. In total we were there for about 3 hours and felt like we had a very good unrushed visit.

The climb is supported with stairs so it's not a very tiring journey. The views are amazing. Go early in the day to avoid crowds and have the place for yourself. Carry lots of water

The place is breathtaking..no question about it! Yet -- the entrance fee is way more of a rip off when the service inside is not tourist friendly. There is no proper signage where to go next, this place is huge so it needs proper signage. it only takes to see a rock and climb it for an hour -- yet we spent 2hours looking for our friends to get back to our car -- all they answer --- WE GOT LOST! -- climbing up is not safe at all, when we went 2 kids fall from the stairs and rolled over. ( not safe at all ) -- not advisable for kids to climb up Go and be there early in the morning as it will be really too hot when its high noon.

Truly amazing views from the top and very interesting to walk though the fortress and see what would have been all the individual rooms, baths, etc. I was amazed to see that other people writing reviews were all complaining about the price. While $30 may be expensive for something in Sri Lanka I would happily have paid more for a once in a lifetime experience. Besides if you go up The Shard in London it costs more and no one seems to quibble the price then. It just seems expensive after only paying $3 dollars to get a taxi there and 20c for a bottle of water, etc. While some people have complained about the hornets I can imagine it would be an extremely rare occurrence to even see one let alone get stung. If you are planning a trip to Sri Lanka make sure you don't miss out by not visiting.  Make sure to go as early as possible in the morning or late evening if you want the quietest times and less heat.

The main attraction in this is the history part. From the moment you enter the area you get the feeling that this is BIG The ground level and the remains of the empire leaves an impact that was unexpected Climbing up the rock itself there were additional attractions such as the frescos and the mirror wall On the top you realize that even if we today can build skyscrapers and complex structures, the buildings on the top are truly impressive - and one wishes that you could experience this in realtime... Not a thin to do twice - but I would not miss it..
What a place! What a view! Get there very early to miss the crowds and wear good shoes, bring loads of water and some snacks.

This rock fortress is `One of a Kind' and the climb up there is part of the excitement. ..if you are lucky you will catch a wedding party  on their photo shoot...as we did. But you must do this jump on top..to capture this Top of The world feeling !!!

Absolutely worth it. The climb isn't too bad. The guide books say it takes 2.5 hours but it really doesn't. We're not particularly fit and it took us 30 minutes. Definitely get there for 7am when the rock opens to avoid the heat. Once at the top, you'll have breathtaking views. Also on the way up, there's signs about hornets but we didn't have any trouble.

Sane with all these sites foreigners pay extortionately more than locals and expensive in sri Lankan terms.  But it is a must see. Get there early for opening time 7am so you walk up in the cool and avoiding the crowds. Looked like the mirror wall half way up got very congested layer on in the day. Only took 45 mins to walk up, first bit is hardest. Not much shade on top so take lots of water with you. Explore the ruins and the views. The gardens are worth wandering around on way down, lots of hidden gems if you avoid the main paths. Also museum at start is with visiting at the end even if just for some of air con areas.
Words cannot begin to explain how great this place is. Excitement from the climb... wonder at the building achievement.... overwhelmed by the view. Makes the pyramids look dull!!!!

Climbing Sigiriya Rock is something one must do if you visit Sri Lanka. The place is amazing with fantastic views. Be aware that the climb is treacherous. There are about 2500 steps, mostly along metal staircases, whcih are bolted into the rock. In some instances it looks a little wobbly. There are many people trying to pass you and in some spots its a bit treacherous, but hold your ground. When you get to the top the view is worth it. Beware of monkeys who try and grab anything they can get a hold of. Make sure you start the climb before 3PM or you will be stuck in the dark. Wear lots of sun screen and take a hat.

Sigiriya is amazing - King Kasyapa's fortress atop a huge massive rock, with lovely frescoes on the walls.  The view from the top is well worth the climb - which is not very difficult but yes, it leaves you gasping. The lion's foot, carved on the rock, halfway through the climb, is a great photographic point..  The water gardens and well kept water ways leave you marvelling at the highly evolved scientific planning that happened centuries ago!   Our 9 year old kids could climb to the top but better to carry a bottle of water - we were all left feeling thirsty.

Very hot in late morning August and big crowds with usual approach to queueing.  Climb is steep but not rapid so easily do-able for most people.  Rock carvings and views exceptional.  This is very much a 'one-off do not miss' site. Museum also v good

Fabulous experience and as long as you take your time and are reasonably fit you will be fine. The effort is well worth it. Suggest you go early to avoid the heat and crowds. A must do for the Sri Lanka trip

Beautiful surrounding park and view from the rock. The fresco's are Worth visiting although it may take some time waiting there so try to avoid weekend days and local holidays. The walk to the top is very easy and Well worth trying!
Go up and visualize that you are the King Kasiappa , beyond words. A bit of a challenge to get the tickets after that enjoy.

I visited the ruins off season, so I didn't have to handle the big crowds that other people mention. It is true that the price of the tickets is absurd and I was lucky that my partner is local and was not paying. The Sri Lankan authorities should check if their disproportion prices are good for the turist industry. The place as such is very spiritual and magic. As you climb up, you discover gradually the vastness of the place and once reached the summit, the view is incredible. If you are lucky to travel off season, you basically have the place for yourself and feel the deep energy of that sacred place. The visit is a must to any trip to Sri Lanka

We hiked up Sigiriya Rock and were advised to do so in the morning which was a great choice as it wasn't too busy and the sun wasn't hitting us on the way up. The walk itself took us 1 hr - 1 hr 15 minutes and water is a must! Awesome view from the top. Such a unique feature this rock is when you look around and see the other landforms around.

I didn't climb up the rock although one from our party did, who made it up and down within an hour (30 minutes both ways). I did take a tuk-tuk ride around the rock though, which cost 1200 rupees total (2 persons) with a fun young driver who gave us some history behind the rock (albeit in broken English that was a bit hard to understand) and took us around so that we could see Sigiriya from different angles - he was funny and we had a good time - more of a thing to do if you're say, waiting for someone who's climbing Sigiriya than a must-see thing - we enjoyed it because we like random things.

Sigiriya or Simhagiri is an ancient rock fortress located in the central Matale District. The top of Sigiriya rock, Kassyapa's Palace was built. The Ajanta- ( India ) frescoes similar paintings have been painted.

Get there early and I would advise to make a bee line to the top and explore the surrounding areas afterwards. The stairs up are all solid enough but the last section is a little precarious. Amazing that something like this could have been built so high up, the walk up must have been hair raising. Great views from the top. Gets pretty busy unsurprisingly and I think its a bit over priced but there is only one Sigiriya and the place is really well kept.

Go early - avoid the crowds and get up there before it is too hot and hazy. Also keep quiet, you do not want to disturb the hornets nests! It is absolutely amazing and breathtaking to imagine how they built it!

Probably No.1 Activity in Sri Lanka. If you go to Sri Lanka and don't do this ... you have lost a great opportunity. There are 1200 steps to the top. The process was great from the start. Climbing up and up. But we ran into bit of bad luck; near lions paw we had to stop because there was Wasp/Hornet attack was on going. Just before our visit a week earlier there had been attack and 50 people got hospitalized. Protective clothing are provided at Lions Paw but they are strictly for adults. Recommendation: Get Good Trekking Shoes Carry Small Back pack with Water Bottles in it Do Carry Camera for images YOU DON'T NEED A GUIDE for this. He will charge 1500 which you don't need to do. Signs are helpful enough

Beautiful place. It's a good idea to set off first thing in the morning so that you are not climbing in the heat. There are guides who can take you up at very reasonable cost and explain the place to you which is worth the money. You are advised to avoid all other 'helping hands' on the way up as they expect a tip. Take your time and enjoy the views. It was the highlight of my trip.
Such a peaceful and awe inspiring place. The climb up might be tough for some but boy is the view worth it when you get there! A day that will long live in our memories. Stunning place.

Sigiriya is a UNESCO world heritage site. The rock fortress is adorned with many fountains of which some are actually in operation even today. Its windy at the top. There are beautiful frescoes to look at.

Must visit place in Srilanka. Ideal time to go there in the morning. Should be there sharp by 7 am. this is the time they open and issue tickets. and start climbing the rock. Ones you start in the morning you don't fell the heat of the sun, can climb the rock easily.

A must as its such a iconic place to visit. The views at the top are spectacular. The climb is not as bad as you think it may be be as there are loads of other people so you do get to take things slowly. Don't be alarmed by the hornets. Indeed there are huge nests but they are fascinating....... Lion's rock was not the only place in Sri Lanka where we saw the hornets either.#Worth the effort. When you get to the top make sure you climb the last few stones...

We got there early which I can highly recommend, so started the climb at 8:30. I'm not fit but managed it ok, taking it steady. Beautiful site and very interesting! As we left at about 10:40, it was crowded and lots of standing around waiting to climb with huge groups of people.

I found it a amazing natural wonder on earth, climbing over 1200 Steps on this mammoth rock was very refreshing , thank god the wasp attack was did not occurred . One could climb the 1200 Steps - it was not easy but was the WONDER ROCK was very inviting and encouraging .... So completed at last. Must visit place in Sri Lanka

As you approach Sigiriya Rock, it's hard not to be awed by the climb ahead of you. The rock rises up, seeming almost sheer. The "climb" is a succession of of stone steps, walkways and metal stairs. As you climb ever higher, particularly on the final metal staircase, it's hard not to think about the age of the metal work, the sheer number of people on it, and the height! Summiting provides spectacular views in every direction, and the quantity of walls and stairs is stunning. It gets very busy, and you should take water. Trainers or walking boots are recommended.
Probably is more charming from below than from the top. The way up is interesting and you see nice drawings and architectures. From the top the view is nice but way overpriced!

The highlight of our 3 week trip. We made it to the top but go early as it is quite hard work. I get vertigo and it is a bit tough on the way down but go as early as you can and is it the best thing I've done.

A must visit place. Take plenty of water as its a stiff claim to the top. Sensible shoes are advised although some wore flip flops! The whole site is magnificent and steeped in history and a 3-4 hour visit should be expected. Watch out for sellers who over charge and better buys can be made elsewhere. The views along with the murals are spectacular. One of us dislikes heights but still managed almost all the way to the top. A memorable day and a highlight of our stay in Sri Lanka
You can not miss this place! Beautiful, well designed and well explained historical site. If you are afraid of heights, think twice. It was pretty scary at some places.

This is a great place to see and the hike is not as bad as it looks. Nice and easy stairs the whole way up make it accessible for any able bodied person. Climb early in the morning to beat the crowds and the heat. The only downside is the ticket price. At $30USD a person it is a pricey excursion, especially for Sri Lanka.

Lion rock : unique place in the world! Its a giant rock of 200m height at least. The best esperience It's to climb it and get to the top. Surrounded by monkeys. The way up its very steep and a little scary because of the instable steps in some parts. but if you do not look down you can actually make it and I really recommend it because when you get to the top you'll be speechless.

Amazing that people could build a fortress on this hill so many centuries ago with the technology of the day. Start with the moat at the bottom of the hill and the garden. The only (large) negatives are that you have to climb so high (1,000 steps) in high heat and humidity with no provision for assistance for older or handicapped people. In fact, our young guide, supposed to go everywhere with us, didn't come and just said he'd meet us in the car park on the other side. Also, beware of the warnings of wasps along the way.

One of the wonderful place . I have ever seen with 👌Superb room & friendly service . One hand  i felt the Seen of Sigiriya Rock & the other hand the beauty of the Nature . I got a nice Sleep & spent a marvellous night with Comfortable Matters in impressive room . With my family Well Done . Keep it up 👊

What a fantastic adventure. Our awesome guide created a wonderful experience for us. Learning about this world heritage site at each of its levels from the summer palace through the various gardens and up to the palace at the top of lion rock was one of the best educational days of our trip. Connecting the ancient history of Sri Lanka to events that involved the citadel was a wonderful way to relate to and retain what we were leaning. The children loved it! You need to wear good shoes, take plenty of water and make sure you wear sunscreen and a hat. The climb is reasonable without being too demanding.

Must see must climb must go But...in luxury stay at Aliya resort check in noon have a swim then head out at around 3pm to avoid the strong sun, bring a warm jacket as the climb up gets windy. Grab your photos right at the entrance way before you reach the base cos thats the best shot, honestly the view up there is stunning but no one can tell where u are. Download a photo of the original palace that was at the top of the rock and sit there reminiscing...head back to Aliya resort for a swim w infinity view and sleep out in one of Aliya's luxurious tents.
This is a must visit, and if you can, climb it too. I did it and so did my mom - proud to have accomplished climbing the 1002 steps to the top.

A very nice and beautiful place, full of history. You just want to seat and keep silent, to enjoy the view. The stairs are a little bit stiff but it worth it ! It's better to climb early in the morning, around 7 am, because it's not so hot yet and it's not too crowded too. A must do in sigirya !

Even if it is expensive ( 30.  $), the fortress is really a must. First the 3 garden With rocks and baths (better TO see After climbing), next the climbing . I recommand TO Go at 7 in the morning So You have less Tourists and a Fresh air. After it cans be over crowded and take Time. The fortress is Well restaured but if You want TO understand how it was before, Go TO the muséum where You have a 3D presentation on computer and alSo terracotta statues and a Copy of the paintings ( You CAN take pictures). Don t Forget a lot of water ... No bar on the roof !

We arrived at Sigiriya early around 9am and were met by a local guide.  He was a 69 year old former history teacher and his knowledge of the rock was invaluable. He told us that we will be walking to the top of the rock, which appeared daunting, and actually was! There is a lot of history surrounding the rock, but without a guide the trip would be meaningless.  The climb was on steps, some narrow, some slippery but it was a steady climb and when you reach the top the view was impressive, especially when you realise that this was the seat of the monarchs, who were then carried up and down the rock by the servants - poor servants I say. The whole trip took around 2 hours and was a must see place in Sri Lanka. If you are taken around by a guide, they expect a tip - so be ready!

We got there around 9am, there were a bit queue at ticket office.  We hired a local guide who is very helpful.    There was roughly 20 minutes queue time to see the cave paintings.   Going up the top, you also need to wait patiently on the narrow stairs and slowly move up.  The view at the top is worth it.  Good chance to learn about the history. The idea time is to start even earlier if you can to avoid the crowds.

We arrived quite early (8am) on the advice of our driver/guide, as Sigiriya is popular with tourists & locals alike - even more so with the Sri Lankan school holidays beginning the day before.  Like many 'official' attractions in Sri Lanka, if you want a guide you must hire a specialist associated with that particular place - ours cost 4,000lkr (+ tip!).  The gardens leading up to the rock itself are very picturesque & the guide explained how the ancient gravity fed water system still created fountains in the rainy season.  There are 1,202 steps to the top, but it's a fairly gentle (if hot) climb.  The hardest part is the section that uses metal spiral staircases.  Our guide told us how various parts of the palace had been constructed & the Lion Gate is magnificent.  There is a fabulous view from the top across the plain & jungle.  You must go if you are anywhere near.

This is well worth the visit. Try and get there as early as you can to avoid the coach tours and the midday sun. It is a long hard climb but worth every step, the wall paintings half way up are beautiful and the view from the top is amazing. You will need to be reasonably fit and healthy as theer isn't really anywhere to sit and rest, the steps are quite narrow and open to the elements, definitely take water with you!! Enjoy the gardens on your way to the foot of the rock, as its easy to over look them in your eagerness to start climbing.

Start your climb first thing in the morning before the heat of the day. You will enjoy and appreciate this amazing area a lot more if you take my advice! The steps during the climb are steep and at times uneven, but the effort is worth it. There are plenty of opportunities for photos, and amazing views when you reach the top.We did not use a guide, but their services are available as you start the climb. Take your own water, wear a hat and enjoy the exercise.

We were on the fence about going as we didn't know much about the place. SO glad we went in the end. It is a great spot to visit. Really spectacular, the climb isn't too challenging (even for those scared of heights like myself). There are warnings about wasp attacks, we saw no wasps during our visit. The museum is pretty good and worth a quick look, it is included in the price of the ticket. Views from the top are awesome. Bring plenty of water on a hot day!

No doubt it is very scenic and beautiful place but surely not worth the ticket cost ( 30 USD for foreigners, 15 USD for SAARC). The ticket cost for locals is just Rs 60. I am from India and I feel in India we have places better than this which we can visit free of cost. Otherwise it provide beautiful view from top. Lot of stairs to climb and people who are afraid of height will find it difficult to climb as stairs near top provides drop down view of valley with heavy winds blowing whole day. Place is not friendly to old people and they should avoid it. Dont plan to visit in noon time as it will be very hot. Lot of shops are there near parking lot where you can purchase Lankan souvenirs.

I arrived at 8am. Minimal queue for tickets (maybe 4 people in front of me). Tickets 4250lkr or $30. I wasn't looking to run up the thing so the number of people I didn't find inhibitive at all. It maintained a nice, steady pace. Everyone was polite to each other and smiling and understanding of breaks needed. The walk up the rock isn't demanding, just a bit long. There are points/terraces to stop at and take photos, sit, rest, or drink water at fairly regular intervals. The steps are also quite even, with none being particularly steep (I'm only 5'3" and had no issues). If you can climb stairs with minimal issue you will do this absolutely fine. (If you've ever done the Tiger caves in Thailand or Great Wall in China this is MUCH easier and more accessible). If you struggle with stairs/steps due to hip/knee issues you will struggle on the rock. HOWEVER the first section of the site is FLAT. I tried to find this out before I went but couldn't get clear info. My mum has a bad knee and hip so she stayed behind at the hotel while I did this solo. She could have come and looked around the ancient gardens and terraces though, walked around the moat and watched the monkeys play. It's a pricey stroll but very accessible. I've put up a map of the site in the pictures. Only points 13 and 14 are high up. The rest is flat. You can also come down quite easily if you do struggle. The site is more than just the Lion Rock!

I arrived at 8am. Minimal queue for tickets (maybe 4 people in front of me). Tickets 4250lkr or $30. I wasn't looking to run up the thing so the number of people I didn't find inhibitive at all. It maintained a nice, steady pace. Everyone was polite to each other and smiling and understanding of breaks needed. The walk up isn't demanding, just a bit long. There are points/terraces to stop at and take photos, sit, rest, or drink water at fairly regular intervals. The steps are also quite even, with none being particularly steep (I'm only 5'3" and had no issues). If you can climb stairs with minimal issue you will do this absolutely fine. If you struggle with stairs/steps due to hip/knee issues you will struggle here.

From a distance, Lion Rock is amazingly breathtaking. However, once we started climbing it was far from it. There was huge amounts of crowds and we could barely move as we walking up the stairs. We were moving at such a snails pace. The view from the top was great, but again you have to wait in a 30 min queue to even reach the steps down!! If you are not bothered about the history, climb Pidurangala Rock (next to it). It's much cheaper (400lkr instead of 4000lkr), no crowds and you get a great view of the Lion's Rock.
Even though I'm not extremely fit, the climb to the top of the rock was really do-able. Stunning view from the top! Try to go early, cause it can get crowded.

Entrence ticket is 4000 rupee in compare to 50 rupee for locals. There is same rock just 200m from it and absolutely free of charge. You can google it 'pidurangala'. We go there by taxi from Kandy (full day taxi 8000 but you can easily find for 6-7000, we just prefer that guy, who was very helpful and helped us save those 4000 per person). The climbing is easy (after Adam's rock). It will take 30-45 min. The view is amazing but little bit scary because of strong wind and no safety at all :) Unlike paid rock, there are no queues or limitations. The only difference is that paid rock has statue of lion and that years ago it was city center. However, it's very short and keep you busy for 2-3 hours. If you think go there or Adam's peak (same distance from Kandy) I would definitely suggest Adam's peak.

If you are going to Sri Lanka your path will leid you to Sigiriya Rock sooner or later - and that for a reason. Sigiriya Rock is probably the most impressiv sightseeing stop to visit in the country. You usually have terrific view and can marvel at the remains of the rock fortress. Since it's so popular among foreigners and locals you can expect a large crowd an the entrance and a high entrance fee (around 4500 Rs, 30€). If you want to enjoy the view and are not willing to pay that much or wait up to 2 1/2 hours to get to the top I recommend climbing up Pidurangala Rock next to it, which is usually frequented much less by visitors. You can also get a good look an Sigiriya itself from there (entrance fee 500 Rs).

Go early, best just after opening at 7 am. Without the crowds its magical! Takes about 3,5hours + 20mins for museum (not that great). Price is 30 USD at this time. Tip: We stayed near Habarana and hired a tuk tuk for the day and managed to do Sigiriya, Dambulla caves and afternoon Minneriya safari in one day. Its a full day but not really tiring (I am 30).

Go there as soon as possible in the morning in order to avoid the queues but mainly the temperature Go first through the beautiful gardens. Then start the climbing There are 2000 steps so take your time in order to achieve your goal: seeing the 360 views Bring water with you and your camera It's incredible the fortress that was billed so long ago at this high

Just a quick review as I don't normally review attractions. A word of encouragement. If you can, definitely go at opening time - 7am. It is definitely worth going to the very top. Take your time, get your breathe back and keep going. When you get to the Lion's Paw the last push is not too bad at all. Just take a brief break (a quick paw shot) and keep going as the view from the top and the experience is spectacular. I have to use a walking stick due to balance problems, am not terribly fit and made it to the top in about 45 mins (I found it harder coming down). For those worried about making it, as I was, find a flight of stairs and try doing a bit of stair training a week or two before you leave home. Worked a treat for me :) Good climbing and enjoy!

Start early before it gets too hot! - Be prepared to climb over 2000 steps and you will be rewarded with an amazing view and a ruined palace with so much history behind this palace. The wall paintings are beautiful and dont forget to visit the mirror wall.  'Prior to the climb, take a quick tour to their museum.

Although 4200 rupees is the cost to climb this rock, the views at the top are most definitely worth it. I think the cost is a shame and may put some people off. I would have liked to have seen more information for such a historical site, luckily the day before we climbed we had a history lesson from our b & b owner. We were not attacked by hornets however you can see the nests quite clearly at the lions paw. We were told they do not allow you to go beyond the lions paw if the hornets are swarming. Tips: - arrive for 7.30am to avoid the crowds and endless queues - If you have a south Asian passport take it with you as you will get 50% off the price

Hired a guide to escort us up the rock. He was essential both in terms of affording us his extensive knowledge of the site's history, but also in getting us access to the frescos that we would not have seen otherwise. Also, he helped my wife and daughter during the ascent and descent--which can be challenging at points.

Impressive climb to the top of the rock. Beautiful views. Not for those who are afraid of heights. But much better than 35 years ago when you had to climb up over wooden stairs with rope railings and steps cut out in the rock. Some of the old stairs are still visible! Beware of the wasps.

Took a taxi here from our hotel in Dambulla (30 mins drive away). We left early to get there so it was less busy (we did well as when we were making our descent plenty more people were coming up and we were glad we had done it already)! Quite a lot of money per person but it is worth it I would say as there isn't much else to see and do in Sri Lanka as good. It is quite steep up but there is railings all the way or a wall so you have always got something to hold onto to help you get up. Took us about 45 mins to walk up. The only slow people that get in the way when you walk up and makes it difficult to walk up is the old ladies, we were shocked to see so many old people going up with flip flops on!? don't get that bit. Wear trainers and shorts as it is very hot. There is no Exit sign when you are at the top so we took about 15 mins to find the way down! They need a sign! Glad we did it and it was a good day. Good view when you are up there. So big up there that you can get a photo with no one else in the background easily enough. A total of 2-3 hours I think I will put down as which includes the walk up and down.

The history of this place is very impressive. And even though the climb can be very tough, especially in hot weather, it is really worth it. If you manage to get to the lion's claws, you should definitely go beyond and take the steps towards the citadel. Breathtaking views
interesting site with historic highlights in a beautiful natural setting. the rock is worth the climb for sure!

This place is astounding. The structures, the boulders, the water systems - all of it surpasses it's time. We had an excellent guide who shared stories with a passion. The walk was intense, though it started off easy. This is not for the weak of heart. Steps are steep and it goes up extremely high. The top of the mountain isn't much to rave about but I guess it would be something you need to tick off your list at least. I definitely suggest a guide as this is what makes a difference in understanding this UNESCO heritage site.

This place is fantastic. Very picturesque, great history and so unique. The climb up to the top is not too bad. I had recently had knee surgery and had no problems. Make sure you don't try to sneak photos of the paintings on the rock as there are guards and they get quite upset. One person in our group found out first hand. The top of the rock is so large and great for taking photos. Make sure you take water with you. I can see why it is one of the most popular tourist sites in Sri Lanka. Not to be missed.

I was frankly disappointed on my return trip to Sigiriya.  It is a very important historical site yet little has been done to open up much of the very large area to sensible tourism.  I would like to see some of the entrance fees spent on archaeology as I am sure there is a lot more to know about this place.  Crowds stream up the rock.  There is too much rubbish lying around and my view is that numbers need to be limited to restore some sort of dignity to the site.  Clearly a cash cow for the government but something needs to be put back

I can see why some people rather climb Pidurangala Rock (way cheaper, less tourists), still I wouldn't wanna miss the experience. Pidurangala is all about the view (at Sigiriya rock of course), Sigiriya has so much more to offer: the gardens, the mirrir wall, the paintings, the lion paws and the ruins. The climb is totally doable. Make sure to visit the great museum afterwards too.

We started at 7:00 and it was quite busy then - when we were returning there was a huge line of people waiting to climb it. Everyone moved in a slow pace, one by one. I really enjoyed it, the climb is not very hard (30 minutes of stairs) but can be quite challenging if  you are afraid of heights. While climbing you can se some beautiful paintings on the wall. The top offers gorgeous views and a nice walk around the ruins.

We are in our late 60s and have climbed Machu Pichu but these steps finished us before half way. Twice as  high as normal steps and constant. You do have options to bale out at 3  places and of 18 in our party, only 4 made it beyond the frescos to the Lions Claw and the foot of the 75 vertical steps to the top. The constant badgering and hands on of the guys looking for money to assist you on the way up became a terrible nuisance.

This site was selected by King Kasyapa (477 – 495) after he had killed his father, the then king, to obtain his wealth.  Obviously he had lots of enemies, including his brother, so set about building his kingdom on the top of the Sigiriya rock... The full story brings alive this wonderful piece of nature and the man made community on top... including swimming pool with shallow and deep end!!  477AD!! There are one of two step climbs that would hamper those with vertigo and of course the wasps!  You are reminded to keep quiet as underneath the stair passageways are numerous giant wasps nests... and we had to wait to descend as they were swarming. Wonderful views from the top.  Simply a must do experience.  Our guide brought it alive with the Kings story.... I won't spoil it in case you visit.... but its not a happy ending :-)

Breathtaking site, naturally recommended in all travel guides of the island. As it has already been mentioned, don't forget to take some water and be ready to climb a lot of steps! However, my main piece of advice is to HIRE A GUIDE in order not to miss any of the hidden secrets of such wonderful spot. Personally, I was very lucky to have Suresh by my side - a local guide that accompanied me throughout my 3-weeks trip in Sri Lanka. I had read a couple of reviews about his driving & guide services before my trip and I am absolutely delighted after it!! Highly recommended, experienced and modest guide ready to drive kilometers to please his clients. If you want to discover the authentic Sri Lankan landscapes and culture through the eyes of a local, do not hesitate to contact Suresh. Hereby his website, with contact details, rates, testimonials and photos of various clients: http://www.srilankanchauffeurguide.com/index.html Enjoy your stay in the magical island of Sri Lanka!

Crazy king who made it but impressive to visit. Loved the museum which explains well and short the history of the site (and as such no need for a guide). Next wandering gardens, straight towards rock. Long traffic jam at the stairs to get up and to see the wonderful ladies (ie fresco-wise) and climbing to get a superb view and luckely a lot of wind to cool down. Spend around 3 hours visiting it.

This was our favorite Sri Lankan trip, a huge rock jutting out of the forest just waiting to be climbed! You start through gardens and then begin to climb the steps. Some are pretty steep especially near the top and this would not appeal to those with vertigo. Note: get there early before the crowds build up, we started to climb around 8am and by 930 the stairs were very busy. The other tip is avoid the loos which were horrible and if you can't avoid them......take loo paper!!!

First of all, be ready to climb 1200 steps! Our guide was really good, he knew everything about everything. Take some water with you because the climb is tiring! If you don't like heights then its not worth going because the best bit is when you reach the top and see the amazing views! There's an area with paintings where you can't take photographs or videos so its not worth the risk as one woman was caught and interrogated by the staff and had to delete everything she had. The place itself is amazing and would recommend everyone to go and climb!

We arrived at 8am so that we could climb Lion Rock before the sun too hot, even at this time it was very warm and very busy but definitely worth it. The view is outstanding and seeing the ruins and lion's paws is really interesting. The gardens are quite large and the boulder gardens especially where impressive. The museum gives a good background and history of the place and is worth visiting. Make sure you have a decent look at the gardens on the way to the summit as when you come down the path ushers you out of the gardens back to the museum, though you can go the other way and get back to the gardens. It's was $30 to get in which seems quite steep but it was well worth it. Also if you enjoy a climb don't miss Pidurangala which is just a short distance from here, the views there are even more spectacular.

You attain a sense of euphoria on the top of this magnificient trophy of an attraction. You need transport to do the cultural triangle properly but its worth every cent! Best time to do the rock is either early morning or late afternoon given the sun exposure, its crowded and getting more popular every minute but it is easily up there with both borobadur and Angkor what. The most beautiful part of the attraction is undoubtedly the cave frenscos half way up their beautiful and complex, of a greater standard that what you will see at Dambulla. The view from the top is simply majestic a great place to reflect on the morning!

Myself and my girlfriend took some advise given further down and went very early for opening time this was the best thing to do. You miss the crowds ish and the heat won't be as harsh for the climb. Yes the ticket does cost 4000lkr ($30) for foreigners, this is not just for this site, this is tax on tourist handed out by the Sri Lankan government I believe. But it is worth the money as its not every day you get to see the sites there! I will say though that you have to be reasonably fit to do the climb as it's not a easy assent, especially in a tropical climate. We did see a large man and woman who were not in the best state half way up. There is a first aid tent just before the summit but you'd have to make it there first. Overall this is a place you can't miss on you travels in Sri Lanka and is a good way to spend 3 hours out of a hotel or hostel.

We visited Sigiriya on August 5th - a truly wonderful place. 1200 steps up to the top - but it was really not very tiresome - no problem to walk up for "normal" people. But I recommend that you use good waking shoes or sneakers. Very nice wall paintings on the way up, and a spectacular view from the top.

We didn't went to Lion Rock because we went to Pidurangala Rock (some recommendation). At the end, you only need to pay a donation of 3€ and the views are the some and with less people. I really recommend you not go to Lion Rock and going to Pidurangala Rock

We visited Sigriya Rock whilst on honeymoon and would highly recommend it. The centuries old decorated plaster on the way up is incredible and there's also quite a few locals willing to help out on the way up for a few $. (although my wife wasn't really comfortable with them hassling us) It's a fair trek up in the heat so remember to pack plenty of water.
Ealy morning rock and stairs climbing worth every penny when reached the top! Amazing views of Sri Lanka! Highly recommend visiting the Lion rock.

A very special world heritage site. Worth the climb to see cave psintings ans mirror wall with graffiti.  Very windy on summit so wear sensible hiking shoes & watch hats. Grwat giew. Beware cost is steep for foreigners..  around $USA 36.. exch a nge r a te of the day is used.. still worth it. Dont mis the myseum.. v good. Takes about 1 hr to climb rock. We stayed at Lal Homestay whuch was excellent and walking distance to the rock. Down town roadside restaurants r wrstern and touristy. Better to let yr home stay family cook yr dinner for traditional Sri Lankan food at a local price. Bus to Danbulla cave temple stops just outside Lal Homestay.
We went not knowing that the ticket price for non-locals is 4000 rupees, which came as a shock! I would still say it is worth climbing though, but be prepared for the high price

Visit in the morning to avoid the heat. The place is beautiful and is worth the expensive entrance fee. There is not much left but the ruins still show well how complex was the infrastructure of the palace and how advance they were in terms of water drainage. Such a shame the city fell.
Amazing complex of ruins. Some walls still have centuries-old plaster. Shame some idiots feel the need to scrawl their names on them. Views from the top of the rock are fantastic.
Amazing, if crowded, climb up the rock. Views from the top are amazing. Incredible complex of ruins on the summit - lovely place to live! Go early to beat the crowds.

We went to Sigiriya in March. I was very reluctant to climb up there but I'm so glad I did. This wasn't supposed to be the highlight of my trip as my focus was on Polonnaruwa, but it turned out to be the best part. It's crowded, but that's OK. It's a must-see. There are people there who for a few dollars will help you climb up the steps if you are leary of it, and they are very nice and helpful. There's the occasional person who will "help" when you don't want it and ask for money, too, so just be aware of that.

The entrance fee is expensive but it is totally worth. we went there at 8 am , it wasn't so difficult to climb to the top, even though it is more than 1,000 steps. When you reach to the top it is amazing. It took us around 4 hours to visit all the area: rock climbing, museum, garden... Do not leaving Sri Lanka without climbing the Lion Rock! it was a great adventure. don't forget to take with you water and some snacks.

Lots of steps to the top and a large queue.  It's worth the climb.  Amazing place. Note: the wasps do swarm.  The notice is not for fun.  We were trapped at the top for  15 mins when the path was closed.

Sigiriya is definitely a "must see" despite the cost - 30 USD!! When you are a family of four that adds up. Furthermore we decided for a guide, but he was worth the pay of 15 USD. The walk up wasn't as bad as it looks and the view from the to is amazing. We spent around two hours in total.

It's HARD work getting to the top, you need to be fit and without fear of heights. Don't forget water. Very interesting site with a great view. Leave time for shady gardens at base & visit museum to see how it would've looked all those years ago. We downloaded history / info to take with us which made visit more interesting.

It's HARD work to get to the top, you need to be fit & without fear of heights. But so worth it. A very interesting site with a great view. Leave time for shady gardens at the base & visit the museum to see how it would've looked all those years ago. We downloaded history / info to take with us. Don't forget water.

The entrance fee is expensive but it is worth it. We went there at the opening at 7am and there were already a few other people climbing the rock with us. There were much more people on the way back so I would advise to go there early if you want to enjoy the view in peace and it is also less hot. The hike is very easy and we spent a good half hour on the top which is bigger than we expected.

Well worth a morning trip to climb the Lion Rock and learn about the palace that once stood there.  It can get very hot and they warn about swarms of bees later in the day so best to go when it is opening about 0730.  We hired a guide ($15) who was able to tell us the whole story of the rock.  The final part of the climb may be a bit daunting for those not keen on heights so again go early to avoid the crowds.

As I love historical and cultural tour really loved this place. As this fort is on a high mountain one need to be careful climbing. The Lion paw gate, painting inside the cave and terrace garden is amazing and breathtaking. Only suggestion there should not be so much difference in Entry Charge between Srilankan and Foreign. You need to pay LKR 4250/- per head as entry fee where a Srilankan pay only LKR 50. All in all worth visiting if you are in Dambula
In the beginning i was not sure it's a good idea but when I tried specially with kids I and they really enjoy the traditional life in this village

Climbing the mountain is not so difficult . But during windy seasons (June, July and August ) it is difficult to climb. At the foot step of lion lot of hives of wasps. So we need to keep silence. Before getting dark we need go out  ,as wild elephants may attack.

The trek is long and tiring and it wasn't easy to find reasonably priced hotels in the area but it's a must do. The views from around the rock and on top of the rock are amazing and it's amazing to see how the rock was carved to make a castle

Climbed to the top of the rock in August 2016.  Very very very hot! Take loads of water with you.  Once you get up there it is very interesting to see the ruins.  No guide is needed but it does help to have a little explanation of what you are looking at from eg a guide book. Museum slightly interesting but as with many foreign museums, there is little explanation in English. Entrance fee was US$30 (children 6-12 US$15) payable in LKR in cash only.  This is by far the most expensive attraction we have found in Sri Lanka. Toilets are ok! Advice: set out really early - we started our climb at about 8am and it took almost 2 hours to get up to the top due to the crowds and how long it is.  On our way back down it was much much hotter and the crowds were even busier and so it would have taken longer still.
We climmed the Lion Rock. Our driver Nuwan Sameera stayed at the parking place. The view up the rock was marvelous.

This was one of the most powerful experiences of my life. I have vertigo and was apprehensive but I was blown away by the scale and enormity of the structure. You must see and experience this place if you come to Sri Lanka. You could spend all day here - start early to get the most out of it.

This is definitely the most important thing to see if you are in Sri Lanka. It is best to go in the early morning, when the sun is not right in your face going up the steps (because it is a very long way to go). Be aware that there are giant hornet nests! You have to be in complete silence going up the rock so that they are not alarmed and don't come out. I have a phobia of them and had no idea this was a risk. Better for older people, does not seem like the safest tourist attraction for kids!

What beauty!! What unspoiled beauty!! This is a truly special place and is worth the fairly steep climb to the top. Access from the car park is a combination of paths and some very steep stairs - this is not a climb for the faint hearted - however the views all the way up and especially the top are breathtaking. Like many attractions in this part of the world, you're free to roam about unchecked at the top but thankfully this does not seem to have spoiled the attraction: there's no graffiti, there's no obviously worn away pathways and no litter either. You're just free to roam about and take in the majesty of Sri Lanka. It's expensive relative to most attractions in Sri Lanka, but you can spend as long as you like roaming around the vast expanse of land marvelling at the ingenuity of the ancient civilsations who lived here. One tip: if you're just going to stroll your way to the top and then stroll your way back down, don't bother with a guide. You are given a map when you pay and even then there are plenty of information boards around too. And you're free to do that at your leisure.

$30USD is expensive just for a walk up a hill but there are spectacular views of the surrounding areas. It makes for a good walk and gets the heart pumping. Excellent views on the way up and also 360 degrees at the top. There is nothing else to do in Sigiriya.

A must-see place on any trip to the area, with very interesting grounds and a wonderful view from your ascent up the rock. There's a number of places to stop and admire the view on the way up but be aware of some steep steps and the spiral staircase to the cave half way up - this was particularly busy and perhaps not for those who have a fear of heights. If you are wary of heights, bypass the spiral staircase (by going underneath) and you continue to the area with the lion's paw. Don't be put off as it is worth it. Outstanding views from the top and plenty to see up there with the ruins. Great photo opportunities. Try to go early-ish because there's no shade at the very top and it's exposed.

I spent two years wanting to visit this place - it was the main reason for my second visit to Sri Lanka, as I missed out the first time - and it didn't disappoint! It's so different to anything i've been to before, being a rock and not a mountain. And the views were fantastic. We took a guide, which I was hesitant to do at first, but he told us all of the royal history that I wouldn't have known, and he knew a few shortcuts to avoid the queues. The stairs are quite open and steep - I managed to do the whole thing in flip flops, but did get a few funny looks from everyone in trainers. I wouldn't want to walk those steps in the rain! We arrived at 9am which was perfect - any later and it would have been very hot (and even busier). We were up and back down in just short of two hours - although it did feel a bit rushed, but we needed to get on the road to Colombo. If you like nature and walking then this place is worth the hype!

Sigiriya is listed as one of the "must see" things in Sri Lanka and I have to agree it's very cool. Do be aware though that the entrance fee is $30 /4260 sri Lankan rupees!! So dear!!! As with all tourist locations in Sri Lanka, it is far more expensive for "foreigners" than Sri Lankans. Despite the cost, we felt we had to see it. We had a guide included with our tour company Loris Vacations and he was excellent. He gave us enough information for it to be interesting but not too much to be boring. We were travelling with our parents in their 60s and he was very good to them both taking his time walking up and making sure that the "push you up the hill for a price guys" didn't intervene or annoy them. There are guys along the way who will try to help older people for a charge but they can be pushy. A firm "no" kept them away no problem!! The walk up wasn't as bad as it looks and we spent about 2 hours in total. The frescos are at the mid way point and are interesting to see. Then there is a 3/4 way point which is just before where the hornets nests are. We had no issues with hornets but did see the nests alright. The view from the top is fantastic and there is lots to see up there. Very interesting hearing about the king and his 500 women!! The walk back down was quick and not hard. Overall, I definitely enjoyed it and I know you can go to the rock beside Sigiriya for $3.50 or something but I still would recommend this one unless your budget just absolutely doesn't allow for it. You will still get lovely views too I'm sure.

Expensive but taken with the climb and as a package it is great. The site is amazing with great archeology that is well explained by signage. We skipped a guide but be wary only use accredited guides, talk to them first to check their proficiency in your language and do not take the first price offered. We were told it was 2800rupees flat rate by the first guy who approached. The second said 2000. A third shouted 1500 at us... we were happy without but there is no harm if you'd prefer one just don't get ripped off. The gardens are amazing and you get a real feel for what they were like. Viewed from above the site is stunning.

The climb looks daunting from below and it certainly isn't easy but it isn't as bad as it appears. You haul yourself up from the gardens up hideous stone stairs. Then you've got metal stairs to the gate. Up a spiral staircase, into a cave. Down a spiral staircase. Along the wall... up stone stair cases... and you think you are done. You've only just reached the lion paw gate. Nasty rickety metal stairs ahead and you've made it. Take your time. Take breaks. Totally worth it. 1) the views. Unbroken jungle on many sides. The gardens on another. 2) the ruins. Simply amazing and you really are left with a sense of admiration for the builders of the place and the engineering of the gardens below. 3) the views... worth mentioning twice. There is a lot more here to explore than you first think. It is very tiring but totally worth it.

We were very amazed that they could build a palace on top on a freaking big rock 150m straight up in the air. And this was hundreds of years ago they managed this. And they say we are smarter nowadays? Definately worth a visit! And while you are in Sri Lanka I can recommend our driver "Sagara" who is one of the best and most honest guides/drivers in the country. He drove us around the entire island and helped us with everything from finding the best restaurant and guest house within our budget, and even helped us with lowering the prices on hotels so that we could afford it. And they say we are smarter nowadays? Definately worth a visit! And while you are in Sri Lanka I can recommend our driver "Sagara" who is one of the best and most honest guides/drivers in the country. Yes a very busy area, we were driven by our tour guide. but saw many people walk a fair way to the start.?? we went inside to the museum while we waited for the men to do the hard yards up the rock. we walked around this Citadel all flat ground, kept looking for crocodiles in here but didn't see any. very good view of the rock in some spots and nice trees to get some shade from while waiting also some local monkeys around near the Museum yards. well worth the visit and if you have time climb the rock . the men said it was great and not that hard to do.

Very nice walk to the top and your are rewarded with the best view you can imagine. I am afraid of hights but did ok. There are stairs all the way op and it is very safe. A bit expensive to get in (30 USD pr. person). Make sure to get an early start to avoid the crowds.
no doubt the 8th wonder of the world . super experience but slr 60 for locals & slr 4500 to foreigners is absurd. foreigners should boycott  until price is around slr 1000.

It is one of the Wonders of the World. highest stone in Sri Lanka. there are many steps you should walk and go up but be careful from bee. the bee there very dangerous. we had a beautiful day but bees stop me to go up.

I imagine that how busy the area is completely dictates the quality of the visit. It is also quite pricey. It took us three hours to get to the top because it was so busy that you were all completely sardine packed on the stairs on the way up. At times it was very stressful as we were actually pushed over and had to scramble back up. There was also a lot of signs up saying to be silent because of all the hornet nests yet no one was obeying them ... so I feel we were lucky in that regard. However the lion rock is still very impressive, especially considering when it was built, and the views from the top are stunning. I wouldn't recommend it to someone who suffers from vertigo though as my partner nearly didn't make it all the way to the top due to the very narrow mental staircases that are just bolted to the side of the rock-face when you get closer to the top.

Some advisors suggest saving your money and climbing the neighbouring rock rather than this rock fortress. Do this only if your sole interest is the view. The rich anthropological story of this site is simply stunning! It may cost $US 35 per person - but is value for money. Make sure you have cash, no card payment. It's quite a climb - but take things slowly and it's entirely achievable. The view from the top and the citadel ruins at the top are spectacular! Save some time to visit the museum on site after you climb the rock - the entry is included in your ticket.

We were amazed by the rock and the surroundings at the bottom. It's a little pricey (USD 35) but well worth it. I suffer from virtigo and my smallest child was a little scared to climb up, so the two of us stayed down below whilst my husband and older children made the climb. My husband doesn't have problems with heights but admitted that even he was a little nervous, especially on the way down. He said the views from the top were just breath taking! My youngest son and I had more than enough attractions walking about the ruins and grounds below for the hour - hour and a half that the others were gone. Be careful of the "guides" who do their best to grab you at every occassion and are difficult to get rid of. Despite a firm "no thank you" we had trouble getting rid of one of these and then got angry that we didn't give him any money. At the top of the rock my husband did take advantage of a guide (also because he couldn't get rid of him) but said that actually it turned out to be useful as the guy did tell them some really interesting things and helped leading the children down at the end. This is certainly a "must see" in Sri Lanka and I thoroughly recommend.
Beautiful place to visit and an incredible walk.  Only problem is that it gets slightly busy and is quite pricey.  It is however worth the money and we had a lovely day there.
Beautiful place to visit and an incredible walk.  Only problem is that it gets slightly busy and is quite pricey.  It is however worth the money and we had a lovely day there.
take your time for the visit and get on top of the rock, interesting museum and the DVD you get with the ticket

You need "good legs" to go up there but the view then is great, I don't suggest it to overweight people or anyone suffering of vertigoes. Note: take a little umbrella with you, if the weather changes you'll get completely wet before getting down, as it happened to me! :))

Great experience, very nice climb (approx. 2hrs). Allows you to take very nice photos on the way up and on the top. Relatively expensive compared to other tourist attractions (entry fee is 30$) but worth it!

First off, Sigiriya is impressive. It's also not as much of a difficult climb as some people have made out. My parents (56 and 61) managed it with rests on the way up. We were in two minds as to whether to visit or not because of the price. Bear in mind that locals pay 50rupees and foreigners pay just over 4000. Also, this money doesn't go to maintaining the site, but gets swallowed up by the government. That notwithstanding, we were all really pleased that we made the effort and the expenditure - the views are astonishing and the whole experience was great. It's definitely manageable if you're older or if you have kids - there were loads of people of different ages doing the climb. Watch out for hornets - at the Lion's Paws there are massive hornets' nests hanging from the rock. A Canadian woman wee met said that when she was there, some tourists had been attacked whilst she was there.

We did enjoyed our morning climb of this rock and the view on top was spectacular.  But visiting this place gave us a sad feeling after seeing so many stray dogs there. We have read a comment by a fellow tripadvisor urging people to bring food for these dogs.  We decided to bring some dog food for them.  We carried the dog food in our back packs.  We saw many many dogs.  Most were skinny and hungry. Some of them limping. The dogs were mostly friendly. They followed us for a long distance begging for food. There were even dogs on top of the rock.  Luckily we have enough food to feed them. For people who loves animals, please  bring food to feed these helpless animals. Don't be deter by these dogs, this place is still worth visiting.
This is a place not just for history lovers. The natural beauty is awesome. The scenery from the top of the rock is one of a lifetime experience.

I was challenged by my friends to climb sigiriya or lion rock of Sri lanka. We went there by car, start 2am early morning from Colombo to avoid traffic and reached about 7am. Sigiriya open at 7.30am. Just perfect time to start, otherwise you will get burn once u reach the top. Carried water, snack or bread (u can choose one), don't bring unnecessary things otherwise u get tired easily. From the top u can enjoy your achievements by the amazing view

Climbing the rock is best done in the early part of the day before it gets too hot. You get a real sense of achievement as you make the climb. What you find at the top is amazing. You can't come to Sri Lanka without doing this!
Be sure to pack a good supply of drinking water. The climb isn't too bad but the heat and humidity can be a challenge. But it is worth it in the end for the view from the top.

The story here is incredible and it is a real privilege to be able to see this.   I would recommend climbing in the morning when it is cooler and not so crowded.   There was a nice Breeze so I didn't get as hot as I thought I might but it is still a strenuous climb and not recommended if you don't have a reasonable level of fitness.

Almost 100 steps to the top but managebale. A few points to stop and rest if needed. Get a good guide who will explain the relevance of the rock and its rich history. Take plenty of water and start the climb early morning as it does get very hot from 11am onwards. Take time to enjoy the view while climbing. A good camera always worthwhile. Pack a sandwich and enjoy the rooftop view. Gets very windy.

One of my favourite activities in Sri Lanka. It is a bit of a climb and on a hot day is hard work but the views at the top are stunning and you can spend a good hour at the top exploring and enjoying the views (excellent photo opportunities!)

The surrounding are is basically a forest as far as the eye can see so it's interesting to hear about the history of the rock. The citadel is nice but I would definitely recommend climbing the stairs for a great view of Sigiriya, the steps could be a bit demanding for people that are not regularly active under the hot sun so it's nice to have a hat but it's not hard to climb. Every level has different structures so the goal shouldn't be to get to the top asap but rather spend time on each one to learn more about the history.

At the age of 1500 years the citadel is very well maintained. Obviously the main attraction is the rock but the surroundings are also interesting. There's a lot of back story to the place so it may not be as flashy without a guide but there are books available to tell the tale. If you focus on the rock and don't allocate enough time it may be a miss in terms of the sights.
The heritage site is big and well taken. During week ends can be crowd due to lot to of local visitors. The view on the top is fantastic.

Great view, but a little crowd due to a big popularity of this place. The way up took about 40 minutes and was really hot. Best to go there earlier in the morning when the sun is not so high up. On the top of it is surprisingly not-so-hot..

1,200 steps don't seem too much, try walking them up a rock. A lot of the steps are man made, then you go a wrought iron staircase. I am 51 and made it, not without a few stops along the way. Sensational views, ancient art on the rock and the lions paws are worth the effort, this is about 2/3 of the way up. The final 1/3 will get you to the top of the rock, there the King decided to build his castle so that he could see if anyone was coming to get him. The ruins left are the King's throne, swimming pool and the base of the castles. This took us about 2 hours up and down. It is well worth it.

First off its not a difficult walk unless you're in incredibly bad shape. 45 minutes or so to get up, no issues going in thongs. Good view at the top and interesting history. Yes it's expensive so if you're a backpacker you might want to go the cheaper option.

We really enjoyed the walk up to the top of the Rock which at 50 flights of stairs is moderately challenging. The view from the top is more than worth it & it was great to learn some of the history from our guide & then back at the museum - where we particularly liked the CGI video of how the palace would have looked

Wow, what a walk to the top, but when you get up there you will get an amazing view. It really is breathtaking, so would highly recommend making the effort to go up there.  Go early and beat the crowds because it gets too hot mid to late morning.

Early start important if you want to get up and down before the heat becomes unbearable. You need a bit of a head for heights - some seemed troubled by the exposure on spiral iron staircases. Worth it all for the famous frescos and the stupendous views from the top. Feels like you can see all of Sri Lanka from there. The 'idea' of the wild bees in the hives on the face of the rock below the frescos is more frightening than was the reality. They are there, of course, and in some number. Our second visit to Sigirya. The first was 30 years ago. Does anyone else remember things in 'negative'? It all felt the other way round this time. Time can do strange things.  Perhaps they have changed the way you go up. The size of the lion's feet at the foot of the face still impress though,  and it must have been a mightily formidable sight when Sigirya was in its pomp.

This place is definitely worth a visit. We didn't realise how majestic it was until we were walking towards the rock. Must say we were freaking out a lot about the hornets as we heard about the attacks in the past, but as long as you go early in the morning (we got there around around 8:30 but it opens at 7 or 7:30) you should be fine. Just keep your distance from other groups especially if they are loud. If you are cautious and don't hang around the middle bit (about half way) than I really don't think it's too much to worry about. It does get really crowded later on during the day though so the hornets may be more irritated by then. They looked pretty calm when we walked past.

This ancient monument/palace is worth climbing up to on very precarious steps (1200). It is worth walking up in early part of the day as it can get very hot. Foreigners are expected to fork out higher sums but this is affordable and the services offered make up for this. The top of the rock offers unsurpassed views.

What a wonderful visit !! The paintings are just superb, the view on the top of the rock is breathtaking. Don't forget the museum which is really interesting, and built with a surprising  architecture. After the visit we have climbed the Pidurangala located 2 km away. It offers a wonderful view on Lion Rock

To be honest, when we arrived in Sigiriya the afternoon before, with one teenage son a vertigo sufferer, and me balking at paying out another $100 for the three remaining family members to climb a flippin' rock (we have a lot of these back home) I wasn't sure I'd even bother to get up early to do it. But the day dawned, and I decided what the hell, and arriving just after seven o'clock with the early morning sun shining white behind the rock, it started to look pretty cool. There were already other early birds but the climb was fine for us - we are reasonably active and used to hiking etc - and it took us maybe 40 mins to get to the top. Once there, the views were pretty beautiful, and the best bit is the far end where the pool is, and lovely views across lakes to mountains. We sat up there for a while, eating sugar buns for breakfast (if you're not keen on the stray dogs following you around, maybe avoid this bit!) before descending.
