If you don't like heights, that bit is probably the worst - the first section of metal stairway as you get a sense of the distance below - but it's quickly over and the rest is actually very easy, much of the descent on path in fact. Getting to the bottom around 8.30am it was a shock to walk back through the gardens facing throngs of visitors. It had been pretty peaceful up there, and we wouldn't have liked doing this at all if we'd had to follow queues and queues of people. That, I suppose, is the advantage of travelling independently so maybe think carefully about tours. It also gets hot quite quickly. And a little grand finale for us was our teenage son laughing at the 'keep out of the water, it's very dangerous' signs only to spot a baby crocodile basking on a wall between two pools. The wasps and hornets you're warned about are an issue, but just walk past their nests quietly. We didn't encounter any problems, but there is a first aid hut at the Lion's Paw so they clearly are a 'thing'.

The rock looks great from and majestic from near! When one starts climbing the rock it does look daunting - over 1000 steps and about 200 metres of climb ! But it not difficult to do the climb if you are reasonably fit - it took us about 40 minutes, a motley crowd of 10, average age 55 ! Number of places to stop and catch breath. Remember to carry some water. Te water garden (the channels were  dry as we went before the rains, one can see the thought behind the distribution of channels, executed so long back... I want to climb the rock once more. and see the garden when the channels are filled with water!

the temple ruins and the rock climb are amazing!  its so interesting to see how much people were able to create so long ago.  it gets crowded fast so go first thing in the morning before the big tour groups and school kids.  if you're in good shape you can get up and down in about an hour and a half. but you can go at your own pace.  the views are impeccable.

Its an hours  trek. but once you at the top its breath taking. The cost is 1500 LKR per person. Theres a discount for Indians but it always better to cross check while paying.Carry water and essentials.There are myths about the place, its more interesting if you read about the place and go. There are quite a bit of documentaries on it too

Sigiriya is a worl heritage site and many things to see around if you are a history holic. Famous for it's  fresco paintings ,water management and landscaping. We were there early morning and did fantastic climb before sun gets hard.view of the top was amazing. One of the best place to see and learn Sri Lankan History, but you need a guide to understand it's history. Show your student ID if you are a student. You'll get a special price for entrance. Worth to visit museum.IF you have a ticket for Rock fortress, museum is free.else you have to pay 5usd.

While climbing the rock at Sigriya may not be everybody's cup of tea , the garden is also worth a visit especially if the group is a mix of young and old . There is a museum which also depicts the area and the rock before modern times . There are a lot of pools and architectural elements which throws light on the town planning and life of the people living here before . There is plenty of space for people to sit and laze around for those who don't wan to make the climb . also there are some shops on the way out who will try to sell you local products though they are expensive .

Don't miss this amazing sight. The views from the top are spectacular after a strenuous climb. There are interesting cave paintings, gardens etc along the way. Probably best to climb early in the morning or mid-afternoon.

We both enjoyed our trip to Sigiriya and even the climb to the top. My husband isn't good with heights but we managed ok - although the staircases are a bit harrowing! We weren't aware of the wasp risk before we went but I now know that there are special outfits available to borrow for free - def worth looking into this if you are travelling in a high activity season.

Really nice scenery and a lot to see. Takes 1200 steps to the top. Beautiful view on the top. You can take a look at the cloud pricesses or women or whatever which wasn't really necessary for me as I don't really understand what they mean to them but still more or less beautiful. Beware not to make too much noise as there are bees or hornets or wasps i don't know what exactly but there are signs everywhere and you can see the nests of them.

Quite an expensive tourist attraction...priced at $30 per person. Was very busy when we went- thousands of people. This made the experience a little less enjoyable- so many people pushed and shoved on the way up. Great views of the country. Didn't make it all the way to the top, was quite tiring and very hot weather. Went mid way and then a swarm of Hornets came so I made my way back down. Quite a funny moment I must say. Defo worth a visit!

Ok firstly we loved this place but you need a guide to understand the history. I am not a history person but did enjoy the history. Yes as I read in one critical review the guides have strong accents but be patient or stay at home, I didn't understand everything but his English was way better that my knowledge of his language. Don't you just hate tourists at times. I mean there wasn't a Mc Donald's and Starbucks there how 3rd world. Rant over back to review. Take this history in. Basically a mad King who was a very dirty boy who loved ladies with big bobbies built an incredible fortress down the bottom of the Rock and winter place up top. 30,000 men and 7 years to build. See i listened to the guide. My wife was laughing because the guide was very into showing every example of proof that the King loved ladies with the big bobbies! Ok some caution. It is a tough climb, not impossible but tough. Bit of uneven stone but a lot of steep metal steps. Take breaks and bring water. We took 3 teenage kids up who moaned a bit but loved having got up there. There is a danger from hornets 1/2 way up so keep noise down. One review complained that the view from the top was just a view. Again I assume they wanted a KFC at the top? The view from the top is just extraordinary and if you have a brain then you can see the madness of having built a palace at the top. Breathtaking. They created a bamboo lift to get the King up. We can only assume that he kept his energy for the ladies with the big bobbies. Top bloke.

It is amazing to see this 200 meter high rock outcropping rise from the surrounding plains. The walk is strenuous, but not difficult because of the steps and railings. The views from the top are magnificent.

We started climbing quite early. There was a good crowd of tourists from all nations climbing the rock. If good footing and easy going is a requirement,this is not for you. The steps, stairs, handrails and spiral staircases are varied in their design and age. We took our time and stopped for many breathes along the way on the climb. As you climb, the full extent of the magnificent view of the surrounding plains becomes apparent. Half way up, you will be warned to be quiet so as not to disturb local wasps, whose nests are nearby. It's part of the fun. They did not attack us. Once on top, the ruins of the ancient palace are there to see. The trip down is much quicker and easier. A great excursion.
Its great to see a structure which remains in Sri Lanka for a quit a long time and being one of the best attraction and every body likes to go

Really worth visit ! The rock mountain was amazing and the way they built was unbelievable. And the park just around was wonderful. It's good to start climbing the rock before sun comes up. Bottom part of the rock is easy to climb, but the top part of the rock was not that much easier ! really worth visiting this place !

A fantastic climb to the top of this very incredible place, the climb in 35 degrees Celsius made it a little tough but it was worth it. The entrance fee was 30 USD per person, a little expensive but again it was worth it. A need to see.

Highly recommend to start the climb early in the morning before the heat kicks in. Don't be intimidated by the height of the rock, it's not difficult to complete the climb. It took us less than 30mins to stroll up. It is actually a little intimidating for people with vertigo phobia as the staircases are pretty steep. Wear comfortable shoes (no flip flops!). After a short hike, you will get to enjoy a birds eye view of Sigiriya. You will understand why the king wants to live there (but it brings into question how in touch he is with his subjects perched on a rock!). The most interesting find is to see a king throne on high ground overlooking the pool. Guess the King likes an eagle view of his ladies taking their showers. Very enlightened ruler indeed! Lastly, do be aware that hornets attack are common. Try not to follow any tour groups to reduce the chances of being attacked. Hornets are provoked by loud noises. Sadly, we didn't have the chance to see the museum as we ran out of time. Message me if it's worth a look!

All world heritage and UNESCO sites are overpriced in Sri Lanka: something has to be done about this. Foreign tourists are considered as cash cows every where and get very little service in return. Excavation and restoration works seem to be inexistent at Sigiriya: it is a shame because the site is exceptional.

This place hosted a royal palace and a monastery in different points in history. It s a beautiful climb with incredible views of the royal gardens and the forest. Notice: This visit involves a 1200 step climb. Use comfortable shoes and take some water with you.

It is one of the most spectacular place I have seen in my life. The mountain is impressive and the park around is just wonderful. The price is a bit high but the park is very well preserved so it's definetely worth the visit.

An experience you won't forget. Advise you get to the rock as early as possible and take a local guide avoiding the heat. Good walking shoes and a hat as the climb is tough but oh is it worth it. Our guide gave a very informative history on the way up and gave us plenty of rest stops ( intentional I am sure). The whole experience and the triumph of getting to the top with the views was incredible and one i won't forget.History of the how is one I will now read up on. Take your time and enjoy..
Worth the very steep entry fee, but the view is better and its much quieter climbing pidurangala. No sarongs needed. Climb not too hard and a nice breeze

This has to be the best heritage site in Sri Lanka and i would only rate it behind  the great wall of china in asia. Its a tough climb to get to the top but when you get there a see what they built on top of this rock its quite something, not to mention the views!
Great experience, can be very hot during the climb around 11 - 1Pm, recommend either to start the journey around 9-10 or after 3Pm

Located about 25 kilometers away from dambulla.located 300meters above the sea level.rock itself high about 200Meters. You will see water garden,Bolder garden and  Terrace garden on your way to rock. Those are best examples of Sri Lankan ancient time engineers and water irrigation and managment systems. Paintings, mirror wall and graffiti will make you more happy. Trust me.Finally when you reach top.You will say thank you to yourself.

It is well worth either reading extensively or having a good guide to fully appreciate the history. The rock itself is spectacular but the history of the people that built it is both sad and fascinating. The fountains still work when it rains, even after 2000 years. That puts London's sewage system to shame!
Both the ruins of the former royal palace and the views from the top of the rock make this a must-see sight. Price is a little steep (for foreigners at least) but still worth it.

We had a great time. The views were lovely and the breeze at the top very welcome. We set off around 8 so it wasn't too hot or at all crowded. Had we been half an hour later I'm not sure I would have enjoyed the congestion on the steps. Certainly worth going early! We went here as part of our 4 day tour and the price was included so for us it didn't make any difference that it was expensive as we had in effect already paid. I understand completely there is a 2 tier system and locals pay less. There are negatives but I found that they were outweighed by the view at the top. We did not spend much time looking at the ruins - just sat in the shade and looked around enjoying the breeze. Take water. There are rubbish bins at the top but It's was a tough walk for me but not impossible. I'm not very fit, in my 40's and overweight but I made it. I did have to tell a constant stream of people who appeared to be after tips that just because I was catching my breath that I did not need to be helped up! Everyone else was fine. It took around 45 minutes to walk up. Heights- not the best if you are afraid of heights but as long as someone is there for you I think most people would be fine. The alfresco paintings were up a spiral staircase (one up one down) - I wish for my daughter 's sake we hadn't bothered as she was petrified - but the rest she was better with. It's an option halfway up. Apparently there are wasps/hornets - warning signs ask you to be quiet in certain areas and this was fine for us. Watch your hats - it gets windy!

We thought quite expensive for what you get. Lots of people there today resulting in a big backlog and a long wait to see the frescos. The gardens and rock themselves are very impressive though and worth seeing. We didn't chose to have a guide and it was fine to find our way around (we read up about the history beforehand so had an understanding of the place). Not suitable for those with a serious fear of height as some of the staircases are quite exposed! Also, would not recommend if not able bodied as a big climb (though this is steps) to the top.

Wow! A man made wonder in ancient times on a natural wonder. Explore by employing a guide when you get there to appreciate the history and achievement. Shame the government is price gouging but unmissable anyway.

The Lion Rock is the mighty rock with so much to see and observe. Very well maintained and throwing challenge to one na dall to climb to the top. It has 1202 steps and its not easy to climb to teh top. Great place if you have interest in archaeology. Great frescoes at the midway is another great attraction to see and observe. At teh top one can soak the sweat and can cool off . Should take a guide to enjoy the place to the fullest.
Enjoyed our visit here. Go early in the morning before the heat and crowds. Wonderful history. The views from the top are amazing.

It is realy an unbelievable creation of human being.its entrance price is very high.area is huge.but the most attractive thing is to climb on top of it.it is nearly 1000 ft high with a man made staircase.on top of the hill all the kings palace are destroyed bt the arts on the wall is excellent.it is forbidden to take the photo of that art,which is unfortunate.if anybody climb to the top he can see a comanding view of whole sigiriya & kandalama area.a cable car is highly needed so that tourist can enjoy it easily.

The entrance fee is a little expensive but it is worth it. I recommend starting early in the morning to avoid climbing in the heat. The climb itself is fun unless you have vertigo! Once on the top the 360 view of Sigiriya and its forests is breathtaking. It was super windy when I got to the top so be weary of that. The top is just nice to sit and observe the surrounding. Definitely wear comfortable shoes. Put sunscreen. Take lots of water. Take insect repellent and something for wasp stings as its quite common. Don't forget your camera. Take snacks and food as there is not much option at the cafe at the base. After finishing the climb there are plenty of walks to do at the base. Lookout for the grey monkeys, there are plenty of them. I did not take a guide as I did not feel the need. But you can get guides at the entrance.  I enjoyed every bit of it.
i enjoy this place . very beautiful and very valuable . you can see sunset in the rock . and you can enjoy

Not so high but the view on the top is absolutely awesome!! We went there when it was raining season. So there is a big pond on the top when we reach. After so tired and a long time climbing, many people come to the pond for a natural foot massage. It was so nice! We really enjoy it. This is a place u must visit in Sri Lanka.

So prior to visiting Sri Lanka the Lion Rock stood out as a must see. We set out very early to try to avoid the crowds and also the heat. We arrived at 7am for opening and would advise this as a tip. It is quite a difficult climb. If you are fit and able bodied then it shouldn't be a problem but plenty of my older relatives would have struggled going up the 1202 steps. So may be worth baring in mind. Whats more as you get towards the top, the path becomes a metal stairway that is drilling into the side of the rock. Seemed perfectly safe to me but my girlfriend was less convinced and was a bit uneasy on the ascent. Again just worth baring in mind. Overall the experience of climbing up isn't not one I would describe as fund and when you get to the top it is a bit underwhelming. Just a few brick ruins however the views are simply stunning, and for that alone if you can do I'd advise it.

Very nice location to enjoy the ancient ruins. There are several walking trails and you can take your time and see what interest you the most. There are locals that stand by the entrance that will offer you guided tours. I'm not sure of the charge because I just chose to see the sites own my own. I would really recommend coming here if your in the area.

This is the highlight of my Sri Lanka tour but you do need to be in decent shape to tackle the 1200+ steps all the way to the top. All the steps are well maintained and even though there are sections where the wind can be quite strong at times, there are hand rails throughout the climb if you feel unsteady or need to rest for a moment. It will be rather hot during the climb and at the top but the wind does help cool things off a bit. Of course, the view at the top was magnificent and feel free to take as many pictures as you want. There is some shade under a few trees at the top as well. As usual, there are guides who are more than happy to accompany you up and give you more details about the history of the place but I choose not to use them. The USD30 entry fee seems a little steep but it is a rather unique attraction in Sri Lanka.

Amazing journey into the past. Quite a hard walk up the rock and not for the faint of heart; some of the paths have high vertical drops. The views from the top are stunning. You need a guide to understand how important this place is and how luxurious it was. Recommended for all visitors to Sri Lanka.

This activity was worth 10/10 from the minute it started till the last minute. We hired a guide; which is highly recommended. It is a place where one of the rulers had built a palace and had 50 wives about 1600 years ago and takes about 1202 steps to reach the highest place; 1200 steps to get at top and then there are another 2 steps. Beautiful scenery and how it was managed (the fountains, the different gardens ant different levels and 3 different entrances). This is a must visit place. Don't miss it

Entry to this place is very costly and I would say is not upto the mark for what was paid since not guiding map and what are the thing to see. SASRC national entry is LKR 2130 and other foreigner is 4600 LKR including entrance to the Museum. Opening time is 7am and closing time is 18:30 but ticket counter will close by 17:00.Approx it would take 3 hours to visit this place and you have walk more inside so pack up with some snacks and water. You need to take a long walk(~3 km) to reach the ticket counter from main road, if not okay to walk take a tuk tuk(auto) they charge LKR 150 only.only few hotels available around this place and resorts are limited for stay, nearest main town is Dambulla around 12kms and buses are available for every 30 mins. After 7pm you will feel like in middle of the forest, no street lights and shops will be closed by 9 pm.overall this place should be visited as a part of half day visit and remote location. Hope this helps!! let me know for any further details about this place, happy to share my more experience. Bon Voyage :).

Our kids 14 and 11 were nervous but excited about the challenging adventure. Our tour guide Pio Mendis had organised a knowledgeable   certified local guide to accompany us up and down the climb. This was a great idea as we learnt about this site's great heritage and history. The climb is not for the faint hearted but we saw several older people journing up and down ably assisted by 'helpers' that you can hire for a fee. It's well worth the experience. The kids were extatic at having done what I had the privilege of doing a few times as a kid.

Our climb of the rock took place in the late afternoon as it was cooler however other reviewers recommend climbing in the morning. We had a paid guide (Rs. 2000 nett) who took us up in about 1.5-2 hours. As you'll be climbing many steps and staircases, best to wear comfortable covered shoes. Pros: - Well maintained historical site with interesting stories about the origins of the rock and surrounding areas - Availability of multilingual guides - Sturdy ladders and staircases leading up to top of Sigiriya - Good exercise, the elevation is about 200m - Remember a camera because the views are worth capturing Cons: - Wasp nests hanging near the top of the rock - At the end of the tour, our guide said 'if you feel my service was good, please pay a MINIMUM of 2,000 rupees'... needless to say we gave him the minimum. The guide also didn't go to the top with us because of the wasps (which didn't pose a threat) and offered to bring us jackets if we got stung. As another reviewer mentioned, there were a number of Chinese tourists who were also there and they were generally well behaved so that was pleasant to see.

Its totally worth visiting this site and i suggest a morning visit.  Good time to start would be around 8 AM.  There will be guides pestering you, in case you are a history buff, take a government approved guide.  Else guide not needed. The stair climb is a bit tough if you are not in good shape, but, after reaching the top, the view is worth it. The stair case is on the western side, hence it is shielded by a shadow and winds. There are some reviews that state that the near by Pidurangala Rock offers better views, pay no heed, both are different places of visit,
1 hour hike and you"ll witness some breathtaking views. Know as the ancient fortress of king Kashyapa.

Gardens approaching the site more impressive than I imagined. Got a tour guide who was informative, inexpensive and saved us from lots of pestering on the way up. Wasps do swarm half way up - 30 people hospitalised on the day we visited! Climb not too hard but heights can bother some. I suffer from mild vertigo and it was not a problem for me. If you do have vertigo or claustrophobia avoid the spiral staircase to the murals, which honestly aren't worth it anyway. Amazing at the top and walk down easy.

We were looking forward  to see this place after reading about it in the internet and decided to take a break in Dumbulla on our way to Trincomalee from Kandy. Our driver however cautioned us that the trip to Sigiriya could be arduous  for me and wife who were in our mid seventies. After collating  bits and pieces of information from the various website on Sigiriya it was quite clear this trip would have been great for us some ten years earlier. The hazards of a visit  - more a trek - to Sigiriya is seldom mentioned in sites that extol the tourist value of Sigiriya. We had to scuttle the tour but we did pass by it and wondered what we had missed. Tips for intending visitors. Read as much as you can on Sigiriya and decide whether you can make it before going for this trip.

The chance to climb Lion Rock was what inspired me to travel to Sri Lanka. The 1202 steps to the highest point are worth every hot and puffing moment. Along the climb there are little gems to see such as the caves temple and the massive hornets nests and the giant lions paws after which the Rock is named so there are plenty of chances to take a breather. A guide is not really necessary are there are plenty of signs along the way pointing out and explaining the features. Take plenty of water along with you - it is cool at the top but on the way up you will need it. The views at the top are truly awesome. The lovely Bodhi tree - which must be the highest in the country - is a great place under which to just sit and 'be'. I don't think you could say you have been to Sri Lanka unless you have been here.

Lovely location, wonderfully kept, quiet, quite busy with tourists.  There are lots of steps so if you struggle with stairs then this is not for you.  The climb can be quite hairy in places, I would recommend seeing the freezes half way up but it can feel claustrophobic so you can skip this if needed.  Definitely go up to the top however be careful as some parts of the year there are hornets nets!

not many such big rock in this world. more amazingly, a palace was built on top about 2 centuries ago. such historical site is definitely worth visiting. it is better to visit early in the morning as there is not much crowd and need not to face the hot sun as the staircase is located on western side of the rock.

It was nice visiting this place and easy to climb. Total trip takes 2,5 hours. Better start around 8.30...not too late. But anyway you need to get around many many chinese tourists. But still worth it!
A wonderful ancient city. Steeped in history and an amazing design and structure. A really long walk to the top with 1000 steps but a beautiful view and well worth the effort. Very glad we went.

The climb itself was not as tiring but the heat and dehydration can bring you down. So make sure you have atleast a litre of water. Enjoyed the ground views and the rocks and the gardens. And once on top i was awed by the view of the forest. Worth it! You are not allowed to take pictures in the caves. I wish all tourists would respect that.

We reached the place with a lot of excitement, luckily got a tour guide from the entrance who briefed us stage by stage. The initial climb crossing the different gardens was casual. As the ascent begun the excitement was getting intense, the higher we went, the steeper the climb was. Felt for a moment will drop it & go down but we went all out & reach the top. It was worth the climb, the view & the breeze was just serene & lovely. It was an amazing moment & we captured many memories as we climbed & whilst we descended to our car park...
It is quite a climb. Very tiring. But it's doable. The view from the top is beautiful. Try and do this before the sun gets too harsh - it will be easier then. Coming down is anyway easy.

Citadel of Sigiriya presents you two things-the 8th wonder of the world to see, learn about, and also a physical and mental challenge to summit. Sigiriya is very well maintained. If you have the imagination, the gardens, the settings can immediately take you back to the ancient ages. Surrounded by unspoiled greenery, wildlife, Sigiriya is a 3-4 hour activity, although it can be cut short a bit more if you are fitter and not engrossed with taking snaps. The climb is moderately challenging-almost anyone can attempt-the difficulty is more psychological than physical. The scenery from the top is sth you ll remember all your life-simply breathtaking, gorgeous. One cant help wonder how astute these ancient kings must have been fortifying themselves in such a difficulty terrain, the line of sight enabled them to see any approaching enemy from probably hundreds of miles. You are also awestruck to see the water/bathing pool right at the top-it perplexes you how these kings were able to transfer water up so high. If you are a selfie/photography fan you ll probably end up with a massive album of pictures following Sigiriya. If you are simple a nature lover or history buff-you ll absolutely love it. Heck if you just want to relax you will not get purer, cooler, stronger winds anywhere else in Sri Lanka. Even in the mid day intense sun the strong winds keep you cool and relaxed. Sigiriya is an absolute must. Probably the number 1 destination for tourists in Sri Lanka. Dont miss it, you ll remember this for a long long time, if not all your life. And this is probably a place you ll be telling your grand children about

The climb is about a 2 mile round trip, but with a pretty good elevation gain (along with the heat) will get a sweat going. But it is well worth the work. The view is stunning and the ruins are remarkable.
Kind of an adventures tour and full of exercise.No Flash light photos allowed on wall paintings .I think there should be good water source near the lion's head .
The best views from the top! Pretty pricey but worth it! Don't get tempted to do the smaller rock next door which is cheaper it doesn't have very good views in comparison

This is the truly remarkable ancient ruins of a palace or monastery. The climb is not for the fainthearted as some of the steps are suspended in the air with a long drop below. There is also a problem with stinging bees. You can see the massive nests suspended from the rock face and if disturbed attack viciously. Panic on these stairs in dangerous and when we spoke to the on site first aid team they made it clear this was an issue. To avoid the problems of heat. crowds and bees I would recommend an early start - the gates are open at 7. Apparently the bees are only active later in the afternoon.

The climb up the steep rickety steps up the cliff may give you adrenaline rush but the view that you'll get up this ancient citadel and palace is so rewarding, it worth all the effort and courage climbing up those steep steps!
great place, amazing views worth the climb. there is also a museum with some information and artefacts worth having a look in. suggest early morning to miss the big crowds.

An amazing experience. Just remember to pack water with you before starting the climb. Its quite strenuous to climb up so be prepared to get stuck behind unfit people, children and tour groups. Well worth the climb. The views are amazing and the history is compelling.
A delightful place to visit. The rock garden of Sigiriya mirrors that of Palais de Versailles in France. Take water. (A bottle per person). Loose clothes and  good pair of sneakers.

We climbed the rock first thing in the morning and it was still quite busy. We were on a tour organised by Genuine Sri Lankans, but we used a local guide for our visit which cost us 1500 rupees. Much cheaper than the entrance fee of 4000 rupees per person. It was well worth it as he gave us a good commentary on how the Rock was used by the King and his concubines. The climb took about 2 hours, the last part being up a metal stair case. My fear of heights worked well for me as I was so focused on that I was less worried about the feeling of tiredness of climbing 1250 steps in 32 degrees.
Great place for history buffs and archeological enthusiasts. Harsh if climb done around noon. Morning and evening are good. Take halts and climb to the top

It was a great hike to the Lion Rock. Nice view. However, the entrance fee to the whole Sigiriya, which includes the museum, the heritage site and the lion rock, is way to high for tourist. I think we paid about 30usd.
enjoyable and interesting trip, great for all the family even older children, i would definitely recommend it to others

Walked to the top with our 7, 5 and 2 year old. 2 year old in backpack, the other two walked the whole way. It is a must do, the view is awesome and you get a great appreciation of how hard it would have been to build! Took us about an hour and a half to get up and down and the kids really enjoyed it. A great sense of adventure and plenty of monkeys to see.

We hired a guide to explain all the history that of the rock, well worth it! The guide had lots of information, but didn't quite know enough english to answer our questions. My mother is scared of heights so it took us extra long to climb up the rock, our guide was very patient. It wasn't a physically difficult hike, there were lots of stairs though. Bring water and your camera!!! This is a must do in Sri Lanka

My second visit in three years required that I make the most out of this amazing site.  6 of us having hired a mobile home off airbnb called Kandy adventure bus, we were able to park it getting a majestic view of the setting son hitting the palace rock!  Its truly worth to enjoy the gardens below and us being in the locality allowed us to take things at our pace.
I never be amazed from anything else like this. such a wonderful creation of great king Rawana. Must see place in sri lanka. the climb to summit is totally worth.
The site shows the engineering expertise of 3rd century B.C. Sri Lankans. A must see place. Dusty and hot during dry season. Be prepared for that.
Magnificent site. Amazing how advanced the 3rd century B.C. Sri Lankans were. Make sure you bring a bottle of water, a hat, sun screen and sun glasses when visiting.

We climbed this with our driver guide, though tat didn't stop other guides trying to step in! Its almost unbelievable that this was built so long ago, its a struggle to get up even now with its uneven steps, hornets, and sticky heat. Well worth it when you get to the top though, not only for the amazing view, but to see the extent of this city in the sky.

If you are visiting the Sigiriya Rock during summer then make sure you carry a bottle of water to keep yourself hydrated and please carry minimum luggage so that the climbing won't get difficult. There are around 1200-1300 steps to climb which gets exhausting due to the heat. The entry charges were around 2200 Srilankan Rupees per person. There will be local guides inside who will keep pestering you to show you the place and explain the history, it is best to avoid them as there are boards which explain the historical details of the place. The climb after the Lion's foot are bit scary as it is very windy up there. People having vertigo or any giddiness problems must avoid it.

My Dad, wife , 2 children and myself climbed the rock 2 weeks back. I must say that this was the most exciting moment during my whole Srilankan trip. Initially I was very doubtful of my dad wife and children were able to climb up to the top. So we thought of giving a try and climb only a portion of the rock. But when we started climbing we were so excited that none of us felt tiered. In an hour we reached the top of the rock without much fatigue We missed the sunset from the rock top as we were late by 10 to 15 minutes. But the view from the rock was fabulous We stated descent after  spending 30 minutes there We enjoyed the climb thoroughly

Jutting out from the flat plains , Sigriya Rock is perhaps one of the most iconic sights in Sri Lanka offering panoramic views of greenery in so many hues that one can only imagine . But Sigriya is like a mysterious maiden - revealing its beauty little by little as you pursue it and teasing you . One has to brave through 1500 precipitous and barely there stairs to reach the summit and then submit your eyes to be awash with nature - a climb i would make a 100 times over to be amidst so much verdure !!!

I know people complained about the extraordinarily high fee to get in this heritage site for foreigners, it was worth every penny in my opinion. Beautiful surroundings, interesting caves and boulders. I would recommend to get a local guide who knows this place. Ours explained everything very well and it gave us a sense of history and certainly gave us a picture of how everything looked like 1600 years ago. A few steps to climb (1202) and it could get really windy on the way down. Make sure to bring plenty of water, and perhaps some shades. Although breezes will keep you quite cool... Highly recommended without a doubt. Perhaps most interesting attraction we had during our trip so far!

This is a must for any visit to Sri Lanka, however, it isn't cheap(actually very expensive) and quite hair raising. You start by buying a ticket note it is cash only in either Sri Lankan Rupees or US dollars so get money out before you arrive. You may be approached by guides we didn't take one but if you do agree a price upfront. You wander through the moats and start to climb gently and easily at first, it is also enclosed by rocks early on. Things start to get interesting when you reach the spiral metal staircase bolted onto the rock to see the frescoes. Don't look down or sideways if you don't like heights also it can be busy so you are in a queue.  The staircase is in a cage so you can't fall out. The frescoes are interesting but the best ones are at the beginning so don't rush past. After this is the mirror wall which isn't so impressive but watch out for the graffiti. You then come on to the wide area of the lions paws guarding the final ascent to the top. Great views from here but also you can see the final staircase to the top. It is literally a metal staircase attached to the sheer cliff face. This is where if you have issues with heights you will may not go the whole way Great views all of the way up. You will be offered help to get up but remember the help isn't free money will be asked for. The top views are stunning and how the palace was ever built up there is a major engineering feat. Coming down is a different route from the lions paws and much easier The only other thing to mention is the huge wasps nests on the cliff face and if disturbed the rock will be closed to visitors
Lovely water pools and combined with the tour leaders explanation of the site enhanced this visit. Make sure you take a water bottle
Beautiful rock art which requires a climb up steps. Best to go early in the morning before the crowds. The views from the top are superb
so interesting. really worse the trip and the climb to the top. do this early in the day though as its a long way up and very warm

Lovely day out! If you get a good guide then you can skip the long queues! Very interesting however you must be mobile to climb the thousands of steps. Beautiful view of the country from the top. Not too expensive, would recommend getting a guide to explain the site.

I cannot understand why this Sigiriya place is so famous. Sigiriya, pay 30$ to climb a rock with nice views and some ruins... , Pidurangala, the same but for 3,5$ but people... this is Sri Lanka! You can find hundreds of mountains with better views that you can climb for free! Must visit if you are the tipical checklist tourist, otherwise please avoid Sigiriya in general and let Sri Lankan people think about their foreing visitor explotation policy. A place like this, loses the magic when you pay 30$ to follow a line of noisy tourists under a heavy sun. Cannot understand this as number 1 atraction in Sri Lanka.

Sigiriya - it's hot, there are 1,200 stairs to confront before you reach the top, it's vertigo inducing (my friend who suffers from vertigo was in panic mode!), it's steep and it's compelling..... Once you reach the top it's a little disappointing, in terms of the historic remanants but the surrounding view is terrific. The experience is in the climb and the wonderment of how it was originally conspired then built ! It's amazing. The mirror wall was not reflecting the sun whem we visited mid-morning. Go in the afternoon for that.... but it'll be even hotter then. The spiral staircase to see the frescos is interesting, yet tedious. Historic and wonderful but only a few to see and admire. Try to go mid-week. Seems that it's a popular local "hangout" on Saturday's and Sunday's. The locals walk slow and want to have conversations with each other, spread out and take up all the stairs.... because they can. It costs a bomb for the privilege of climbing the stairs! 4200 SL Rupees, approx SGD$42 (Singaporean dollars) or $30+ US dollars per person !!! Its an amazing site and archaeological achievement. Go see it! Reasonably ho-hum at the summit but we'll worth the sweat and effort of you dare ....

Well worth the trek to the summit of the rock for the most breath-taking view. It felt like we were in Africa! We went in the afternoon and it was soooo hot! This means while on the single file steps heading up...its highly likely youll be smelling some strangers sweat - this can't be helped but a morning trip may prove more comfortable. TAKE A HAT and a bottle of water for each person. There is very little shade! The steel steps that go up along the rock look questionable. Although nothing seemed loose....I couldnt help but feel it could have been safer - perhaps staff to limit the number of people using the steps at any given time.

We were a bit unsure if a trip to a big rock and ancient ruins would be appropriate for our two boys aged 2years and 4years and worth our time and money. I'm happy to report we had a really enjoyable time. We had a guide, which I highly recommend. He gave us a much bigger insight into the site. My 4 year old was fascinated with the story of the kingdom and my husband was intrigued with the engineering from 1600 years ago. We didn't climb to the very top but went to the lions feet, I believe we saw most of the important parts of the site. Even to get here we still climbed lots of stairs but the views were worth it. My two year old was in a hiking pack. I'm not sure we could have managed without it. Some steps are very steep and narrow.

An absolute must see place in Sri Lanka. The lower gardens are interesting, but the real gem is up top. I highly recommend getting there as early as possible, this way you encounter less heat and less crowds, because the climb up is no joke. Once you conquer the climb up though, you are rewarded with some fascinating ruins and an amazing view.

A must if your in the area. The price to get in was 30.00usd or 4260lk for foreigners but I think it's worth it. If you arrive by tour bus the parking lot puts you near the first steps but don't forget that a lot of ruins before you every get to the first stairs. The climb can difficult for some as the steps are short and narrow. At the top you'll get amazing view of the entire area. One the way down from the top there is side path with no steps if you choose to go that way.

Went to Sigirya Lions rock, and it was great. There is a bit of a climb, but should not be an issue unless you are doing it in the scorching heat. Views for the citadel are great and overall great place with great ancient stucture

We visited Sigiriya early in the morning because of the heat forecasted during the day, and really vere glad we did so. But even if would come there during the hottest time of day - the trip and views are worth all climbing. Amazing place. Trip starts at the Sigiriya gardens, which are quite nice, but are walked quite quickly, as all the time you see main atraction in front of you, and want to go there as soon as possible. The ascend is of two parts - one in the shade (if you come in the morning) - it is quite steep, but with breathtaking views and wall paintigs. Approximatelly in the middle of climb there is quite big open area with drinking water tap. Here those of you who are too tired can wait for the strongest and bravest (you will need this) - you will the climb to the top on steel stairs with open space on one side, and rock on another. My phone showed, that we climbed 54 floors to the top, but the view atop is simply breathtaking, speaking at least. The feeling of warrior sets into you. Amazing. Worth every drop of sweath!
I would recommend all those visiting Sri Lanka to climb Sigiriya and enjoy that spectacular view! We are so glad we did!

We climbed up 650feet and the views were simply amazing. Its a tough climb and best done early in the morning however worth every drop of sweat once you get up. However you need to be cautious of the staff and locals who have free entrance. A guy approached me to me and asked if i wanted some water and i bought a small bottle of water from him. He charged me double the price for the bottle. I had a large note with no change and he said he'll go get some change however never turned up.
This iconic heritage site is one of the must see when you visit Sri Lanka. The hike up is a little challenging but not difficult and is well worth the effort.
Can’t believe how they have build this impressing artistic site. Stile the water fountens in working in order. How- nobody knows.

While the rock itself and the view from the top are breathtaking, lines can be fairly long as the path is narrow.  As a result you may be standing in the sun for extended periods of time with little reprieve, so ensuring adequate water and a hat are packed is a must as there is no opportunity to purchase any once the ascent is started.

Although the museum doesn't look great from the outside, it's well worth the visit inside....very interesting and informative. We then walked through the water gardens up to the rock then up the rock itself. It's not for the faint hearted but take it slow and steady and plenty of water. It's frightening to think that centuries ago people used the steps carved into the rock sides. The last leg to the palace is a lot easier and the views were amazing. Our guide looked after us very well, worth every penny!
If you are on a tour to Sri Lanka it's a must visit and there is a cost of 30$ per person . I am sure you will enjoy .

Visited 07:00 on a Saturday. Large party of Sri Lankans soon passed and had a very pleasant trip up the rock. It was a little humid and was a challenge for more elderly travelers but is ok if you take it on in bite size chunks, take regular rest breaks and don't push too hard at the start. Well worth the effort.

Before climbing Sigirya we climbed neighbouring Piduranagala rock to watch the sunrise over Sigirya and surrounds. Got to the base of Pidurangala by 455am, up top after an easy scramble by 5.20am, had the rock to ourselves and the sunrise over sigiriya was stunning. Paid 500rupees each. All stairs lead up to the top of the rock to the reclining buddah then follow the red arrows to the top. We climbed down the rock, took some time with the lying Buddah then drove to Sigiriya, were there by open at 7am. Hired a guide (chose the man in the matching sarong and shirt, has been taking people up Sigiriya for 30+ years) and had a tour up the rock which we had mostly to ourselves. By the time we climbed down at about 9am the car park was full with sightseers. Paid about 4000 rupees each and 1000 each for the guide  (we gave a big tip as he was a fantastic guide). Highly recommend the early start, to escape the heat and too many crowds.

This rock fort is worth a visit. A world heritage site. You climb 1200 steps. Stunning views from there. It is clean and they have maintained it well. My only gripe is the entry fee. Foreigners are charged in USD. The local people pay 100 LKR and we paid 4260 LKR per person (42 times that as locals). The ticket is different and it says 'Thanks for the generous contribution which allows them to maintain this site). No doubt, the foreigners are paying to maintain this site.

this is a amazing historical place. entry fees  $30 US  per foreign. It's very bad i think.  The view from the top is worth the climb and the sense of accomplishment in having survived is decidedly memorable.

Impressive piece of Sri Lankan history. The rock dominates the region. The citadel would have been an impressive and marvellous building. The white stone pathways that must shine in the dark are just one testimony.  The paintings are another. The climb is steep and one does not feel very secure on the steep steps. We did it when it was fairly quiet, so that was okay. To better understand the history around the citadel it is important to also visit the museum.

This is a wonderful space to explore at leisure. There are three distinct garden spaces and it is possible to wander around for hours. It's best to leave this area till after you have climbed The Rock... a nice place for a picnic. There are many signs asking visitors not to take plastic (bags) to the site, and you need to be aware that the monkeys are happy to be over-familiar.

At $30 US entry per foreign person I was a little taken aback by the cost... but the ticket thanks us for our generous contribution to the maintainence of the site, so I guess that's some recompense. The view from the top is worth the climb and the sense of accomplishment in having survived is decidedly memorable. Wear sneakers rather than jandals/sandals because the steps are of an uneven space and rise and some places are tricky.

The Lions Rock or Rock Fortress in Sigiriya was a pretty amazing site and absolutely crazy climb. I like to think I'm in shape, but the climb up was crazy hard, however it is definitely a must. You HAVE to climb to the top, especially with how amazing the views were from up there, its an amazing experience. There were ruins leading up to the Rock fortress (i had a personal guide explaining the history to me) and then we climbed up the fortress to get to the Lions Rock, it was all pretty amazing and i've never seen so many stairs in my life. Had to take a few breaks (definitely bring water!! i had a camel pack with me). There were also macaques running around here and there through the ruins. I=The climb down was equally as beautiful, we went down through a different way. There were old caves where monks used to pray, and wall painting that were still visible, it was all so cool to see. Definitely recommend.
Optimum time to visit would be sunrise or sunset. We went during sunset and didnt have to deal with large crowds, or even any people. Keep in mind if you are doing that bring a head lamp!

Went there with a sri lankan relative. Got myself a locals ticket (cos i look like a sri lankan :DD) which is 50 rupees and my girlfriend had to take the turist ticket which was over 4000 rupees. This is the nasty thing in sri lanka. They are robbing tourists like this. I highly recommend sigiriya though! It was worth every penny!

A ‘MUST VISIT’!!  Sigiriya and Dambula have been nominated as UNESCO World Heritage sites, and is rich in history.   It is most famously known for its Rock Fortress structure from 5th century BC.  Though the ancient rock fortress is an archaeological marvel, it is simple and rustic, and therein lies its beauty.  Folklore has it that it was once kingdom to Kashyappa the God King [some considered him a Tyrant] who murdered his father.  The fortress was nominated  as the 8th wonder of the old world.  The 1200-steps climb to the top is a hair-raising experience, with gusty winds and steep stairs on the cliffs, but worth the effort – brilliant view from the top.  600 steps upto the Lions paws is half-way.    There are gardens, caves, frescoes, stone inscriptions and ancient structures.  Sigiriya is the most central point in the cultural triangle and   The surrounding attractions are in the areas of Kandalama, Habarana, Minneriya, Polonnaruwa and Anuradhapura.  Go at the crack of dawn to beat the heat.  Wear comfortable walking shoes and clothing and take water. Watch out for the monkeys.

We climbed up to the top of the citadel and spent a couple of hours there. It is a centuries old Royal fort which is now in ruins, but one can imagine its magnificence in its hey days. I particularly like the water pond near the top. It is amazing how engineers of that era designed it so that it can function without the need of a water pump. The Lion's paw just before the final ascent to the Fort is another very impressive thing. One can only wonder how the full lion would have looked like. On the negative side, the queue management leaves much to be desired. It took us three hours to climb because of the massive queue and there was much shoving and pushing in the queue. I understand it was an unusually busy day because of a Buddhist festival and it normally takes less than an hour. The authorities should warn the tourists of the day of such festivals so that it can be avoided. Alternatively, I observed the main bottleneck is the spiral staircase to the rock paintings. An alternative route should be given from the bottom of the rock itself, rather than just before the spiral staircase as we had already spent over 2 hours 45 minutes in the queue by the time we reached the staircase.
It's impressive. And you need faith in the engineers who screwed the ladders to the rock face! If you are Chinese you will see lots of your countrymen. Climbing to the very top is a nice achievement.

Sigiriya is amazing and definitely a wonder.  But foreigners are charged Rs. 4,200 while locals only Rs. 50.  The entrance staff had no PR skills, they were unfriendly and unpleasant.  No cues for ticket issuing. No services given for foreigners even though they are charged a high amount.  As a local who invited my friend from England to see Sri Lanka, i was disgusted with the services provided at many touristy places and the ridiculous fees charged from them. The hassle and bad entry experiences are not worth the visit.
I was amazed by my 7 year old girl, how brave she is to have such a hair-rising climbing, both by the gust of wind and cliff walking.

The site is much bigger than you expect and is worth a visit even if you don't do the climb. If you do the climb the view from the top is brilliant. This is a must see in Sri Lanka. Tip: Don't go at weekends. Tip: If you can afford it (1000-1500 LKR) hire an official guide (though the guide books cover a lot of what there is to view. Having someone to point out different things gives you more. Tip: Only pay the guide what you agree up front unless they have been super special.

Must visit place. Though u need to walk a lot to climb up to top of rock ,it's worth the bird eyes views u get from there of total of surroundings on all directions. Keep small water bottle and a juice bottle of ur choice handy to catch up with your dried throat. Carry cut fruits like water melon,pineapple to get proper quenching hydrating food portion.worth carrying n taking break at foothill area .( Use dustbins for trash) Take small breaks sit relax n continue to keep good pace between ur climbing up. Try not to wear loose skirts,tops n lungis as it ll b difficult to  walk n control ur clothes with high speed of wind.wear shorts or capri's to walk with ease .and strapped sandals n crocs will help u walk freely without worrying of ur slippers free falling from top.

It is very good, I would rate it a must see in Sri Lanka...have not been to Machu Pichu, but some of my friends who seen it said it's like a mini Machu Pichu. It is a very nice place, spend some time hanging around to take in the views and breeze. The downside, the entrance fee is very steep at USD30 per pax.

An experience not to be missed! While walking through the gardens at the bottom of the rock you can see a lot of monkeys doing their monkey business, beautiful butterflies and birds. As you start to climb the stairs up to the fortress, you will definitely feel the grind, but it is so worth it! Go early to beat the heat. Climbing 1,200 steep steps is not easy but doable even if you are not fit. Most steps are narrow and steep, and it gets windy near the top so better wear appropriate footwear with a good grip and comfortable clothing.

This is a stunning place to visit and a must see if you come to Sri Lanka. It is essential to get there as early as possible (opens at 7am) and our driver drove us down quickly from Anuradhapura leaving at 6:30 and getting there for about 8am. We made the mistake of going there on a bank holiday weekend, and apart from the usual foreign tourists there were huge numbers of locals and because of the bank holiday lots of school trips. This made our tour of the site take about 3 hours. I have posted pictures of the queues. It is a good idea to use an official guide if you can afford it (~1500 LKR) although a lot of information about the site is in the guide books. Unfortunately our guide was getting a little agitated about the time it was taking because of course the turnaround dictates how many sets of tourists he can take up. He did take us on some short cuts to get around the queues and he also missed out some things to see, actually we didn't mind missing these minor things as it was very hot by 11am and an ice cream and a lime juice were the order of the day. The climb is hard work and there are some steep drops that you walk by, so be aware if you are scared of heights. My wife is scared of heights but battled on to the plateau immediately after the wall paintings but too much time standing with steep drops meant she could not face the final two sets of steps. The top gives magnificent panoramic views and the pool at the top which you at first think is natural but on examination is too regular is impressive as it must of been carved out of the rock but if you can carve lions paws I guess a bathing pool is not too difficult. The guide told us that there is always water in this pool even in the driest dry season. Last tip it is a great place to visit but pay the guide what you agreed at the beginning, unless they have been very special.

The walk up the Sigiriya Rock is really tough. We have to climb about 1200 steep steps. The site is well maintained and well indicated also. We climbed 600 steps upto the Lion's paws which is just halfway. It was exhilarating and the Breeze was tremendous
This place must be seen! We were there at a very busy moment,  but worth visiting this place! Take your time  to climb the 2200 steps to reach the top and see the beautiful surrounding.
You need more energy to cover this place. You need to climb above the rock to see the beauty of the place and surronding.

The most exciting things we did in Sri Lanka. Well worth the time and energy spent walking up the 1202 steps. The final two steps are the cutest! Although it seems alot, the walk was pleasant with plenty rest stops, our guide was amazing, explained all the details throughout the walk. Would've been a very different experience without Sampha. The view from above is breathtaking, the winds literally blow you away!! Take water. Wear comfy shoes. Hire a guide. We paid 1500LKR.

This is something you must visit in your life time and would never forget ..! Frescoes were great and well protected. Museum gives a 3D animated video supported information which you will imagine how it was during King's time.another great effort..!
A long hike up to see a rock fortress from 1500 years ago.  I am amazed that they had crops on the top.  There are some cave paintings that obviously have been touched up but look great.
The climb takes a while but it is totally worth it. The view from the top is totally beautiful. The stairs aren't in great condition thought.

The lion rock is a must see in Sri Lanka. The view on the way up and on the top is fantastic. We have been there in the late afternoon and the light was very good for photographing. However, with 30 usd entrance fee it is not the cheapest attraction. Next to sigiriya is a smaller hill which you can also hike up and probably you have a very nice view on the lions rock. But I still wouldn't want to miss the way up to sigiriya!

We went to the top with our two small kids of 2 and 5 years old. And we all enjoyed it. I am a bit afraid of heights and was a bit scared going up to the cave paintings, which is up a set of winding stairs half way up. You can go to the top without going to the paintings.

The views from the top of Sigiriya are beautiful. If there is one thing you must do when is visiting Sri Lanka - it is visit Sigiriya. Be careful of the tourist touts/"guides" on the way up - they are unnecessary.

We almost didn't go to Sigiriya, but decided to at the last minute because we thought it might be something we'd regret not doing, and I'm very glad we did! It's quite an expensive attraction at just over $40 AUD per person, but by this stage we were used to inflated costs for tourists. I'll admit to being a bit concerned that my fitness wasn't up to scratch for the many, many stairs to the top, and although it did take the stuffing out of me, I got there, and the view was amazing. I highly recommend getting to the rock at 7am when it opens so the weather is a little cooler and the crowds less. We did this, and saw a huge amount of people either starting or being mid way through the climb while we were already on our way back down. Take plenty of water, it's a hot climb!
Sigiriya is a rock fortress build by king Kasepha. It is a amazing place. We cant still understand how water was supplied to the rock top . It has water gardens, ancient arts and a mirror wall
A must visit. And not as hard to climb as you think. Don't bottle out. It's worth it; great views, history is incredible.
UNESCO listed World Heritage Site & the best preserved examples of ancient urban planning......

Superb experience. You need a good guide to enjoy this place we luckily got one who has been here for 30 years and his son's also work here. Do carry your passports though our guide helped us a lot to get "India" discount. Have uploaded his ID card details since he knows a lot about this place and will keep u engaged

Its a must see place when you visit Srilanka because it a unique place and view. This is the most expensive tourist ticket in the country, you pay 4000 SR per person. Do some plan a head cuz this place is nit pleasant if it crowded!! It took my 2 hrs to go up in a crowded day :( Take with you water and a light snack, you need at least 2 hrs to enjoy the place and the view. Included in the ticket a visit to the museum too.

A definite must to visit if you're in the area. Make sure you go early, 1) to avoid the heat - it's a decent climb, and 2) to avoid the crowds. We visited from 8.30 and were leaving by the time the crowds started arriving. At the top you will have fantastic views of the countryside around. We were fortunate to take a driver/guide with us who was very knowledgable about the attraction and the area. You will be pestered quite a lot by locals trying to sell you their wares, it takes slightly more than a polite 'No' to deter them!! Don't let this put you off tho. This is a stunning place

There's no use writing a review about how awesome this world heritage site is - you simply MUST go there. I'm not going to go on about all its amazingness, but give you a list of what to do: Do go as early as possible to beat the heat and the crowds. Do take water with you. Do have a guide so you can appreciate what you're seeing. Do wear sensible shoes and clothing. Be prepared for lots of steps, dust, dogs, monkeys, and a course, locals trying to scam money in the guise of helpers. Do take time to take it all in. Do take lots of photos, if that's your thing. Be prepared to be amazed by the genius and creativity of the creators of the site. You'll probably only go there once, so do it thoroughly. A most important: Do enjoy - I certainly did!

Sigiriya, touted as the most visited historical site in Sri Lanka as it is an excellent example of ancient urban planning, was certainly worth a day's visit. Just be prepared for a good workout as there were at least 1200 steps to climb and I couldn't have made it to the top wearing a dress without the assistance of two guides (at a tipping cost of 2000rp each guide)! That almost doubled the cost of the entrance fees which was 4260rp. And I bought a wooden "secret box" carving at 3500rp which you could probably bargain down to 2500rp if you had better bargaining skills. I spent about USD100 for my day trip there but you could easily spend half the amount, without the guides and the shopping. The views at top are splendid and pretty breathtaking. It's totally worth the climb. Do it while you still have the stamina and fitness! Enjoy the climb, the breeze and views!

Sigiriya rock is a must vist tourist attraction in Srilanka.We can still experience one of the best irrigation system built centuries ago. The kings garden is amazingly beautiful and people can enjoy some bird watching too. Climbing the rock can be little tiring but it's woth the climb.The frescoes are still preserved carefully. The View from the top of the rock was breath taking.Overall it was worth visiting and i recommended this place for fellow travellers .
Every step to history and climb it to view. A must do activity who can climb and have thrill to get the touch of near sky.

I went to Sigiriya Rock around 8am and started the walk. I didn't know that there was so many ruins there and was positively surprised. Then the 4260Rs ($30) made sense for me. It is expensive to climb a rock, but this is a site more than 1500 years old and if you look around you will see many people who is cleaning, taking rubbish and maintaining the area, I was told that more than 300 people works there. And then I happy want to pay the money! It might have explained more to me with a guide, but that's expensive as well. And I was very lucky to meet one of the cleaners on top who explained me everything! I was so happy when I went down from the rock, and so glad I did the whole thing! Absolutely a must thing in Sri Lanka!
One of the absolute highlights of my trip, a must do for sure! the climb is an adventure in itself and the views are just incredible and so worth it

I travelled here on a tour and of the 2 weeks I was in Sri Lanka this was by far my favourite activity! Even though it was pouring rain most of the time we were here it was still a highhlight, an absolute must do! the climb itself is so incredible and the views are just breathtaking!

This place has the title, Eighth wonder of the world! O M G!! Absolutely worth a visit scenery and views from the top of Sigiriya Rock are stunning, on the rock it's self there are paintings, which unfortunately you cannot photograph due to the fact they need to be preserved, look out for the Hornets nests on the rock also, if you are going to climb the rock wear sensible footwear as its a fair climb! We cannot even imagine how beautiful it would have been at the top had the buildings  been in situ, remarkable to think there were buildings up on top of that huge rock!

Well worth the climb. Very interesting to see the paintings half way up and the view from thew top is breathtaking. It cost 4250 lkr pp to visit but was worth it. Try going early morning as you will melt at midday and careful of hornets.

I climbed here 7th June. Started 8.30am. The climb itself is manageable, it was quiet enough, which is help as it is narrow in spots. Views are amazing. There is a medic just before the final part of the climb which I thought is a comfort for some. Scenery is amazing. When I got down from the rock and making decent a local guided me a more direct way, I took his advise and then he was looking for moment for this and had guides me through stalls where they were eager for you to buy.

Sigiriya fort was one of the items of the trail. The king who built this was supposed to have taken King Ravana's (a leading villainous character of the grand Indian epic Ramayana) original Lanka City as the model for his city. The Fort is a on a large rock that is over 100 mts in height and having sheer vertical sides. The king built his flourishing city around the rock. The physical remnants of the city are a few pools and broken walls at the ground level. To reach the top, we climbed 1200 steps. The steps are in good condition, but the heat and exposure could be the difficult factors. Wind was buffeting us in some of the directions while we were on top. The structures on top also are in a fully damaged condition and weather worn. There is a large natural pool with clean cool water on top. About two thirds of the way to the top, there is a special enclosure with original frescoes of beautiful damsels. Here photography is not allowed. The entrance fee for foreigners of SAARC countries is at a discounted price of 15 USD or equivalent Srilankan Rupees. People have to show their original passports to avail this discount. For all other Foreigners the entrance fee is USD 30. The vehicles are allowed to drop off visitors at the main entrance point and then go to the exit and park. There is a separate Exit for Foreigners and ample parking space also there. Please note that Vehicles with people in them are not allowed to the Foreigners Exit parking point. The shopping area for souvenirs and memorabilia are in the Foreigner's Exit route. There is a small medical kiosk at the top of the rock. The climb is arduous, hence the climbers need to be prepared with drinking water etc. Shops selling short eats and beverages are available at the entrance and exit points.

Getting the most out of visiting Sigirya involves an incremental climb up approx 1000 steps. However you stop at different levels to see much of the ancient palace and can manage the climb according to your own fitness level - there's no rush!! I would definitely recommend visiting - it was incredible how much is still preserved.
When you are in Sri Lanka, you have to visit this site.. Too bad it's so expensive and polluted with plastic bottles etc.

There are 1200 steps to the top of lions head but worth the climb for the view! We went during off season, so for us it was no problem to stop and take breaks as needed, although I've heard during peak season it can be quite packed. I think there are only 3 actual resting spots along the way. The steps are very steep, and uneven at times without anything to hold onto. My friend did it in flip flops but I'd recommend good walking shoes. I think the climb takes about an hour to get to the top. Be prepared to sweat, it's very hot, so bring lots of water. The fee is $30US or about 4300R

The view from the beginning was amazing, I imagined the scene of one of the movies of Jackie Chan...or something like that. However, be prepared to climb in this 770ft fortress as the steps are narrow and slippery and there is no drinking water available until you reached the middle part of the fort and with heat its exhausting to climb without water. The entrance fee is quite expensive but I can understand it because maintaining it is not easy for sure. There are beehives around and it looks scary but they are hidden so you wont see it unless you really look for it. The paintings of Harem women are amazing and the view from the top were mesmerizing but its not for people who has fear with heights.

This is a great landmark from afar & even better as you get closer, it is certainly a must see & go for it and do the climb, it is so worthwhile, amazing views, although it was quite windy when we went & certainly a bit scary but it is safe if you are careful. Then wow!

Very attractive ancient site built by King Kaashyapa. Mesmerizing irrigation systems, water fountains which are still working, The Sigiriya fortresses is amazing to see. The frescoes are the main attraction at Sigiriya. In addition Mirror wall and so many amazing things done in ancient era. A Place not to miss in any case...

We visited as part of a small group, so don't know about the price. I did NOT climb to the top (at over 65, the number and steepness of the steps, many without adequate hand rails and of uneven depth, was a bit much for me, so only went to the first level). However the rock is certainly spectacular and the climb is very popular. A few observations: 1. Do it in the morning, it gets very hot as the day progresses and a lot of the stairs are in direct sunlight. 2. Wear good footwear. 3. Take water, you'll sweat a lot on the climb. 4. If you wear glasses, remember the steps are uneven in places and can be difficult. 5. Steps can be very crowded (see some of the pictures on the Trip Advisor site), so early is good. 6. Remember - going up is only half the journey. 7. Have a good look at some of the visitor pics on Trip Advisor again - it's as steep as it looks, so if you're an older person.... I rate it at Very Good, and it is, so don't miss seeing it, even if only close up from the bottom. Even if you only go to the turn-off to the cobra head rock then spend time looking at the gardens and surrounds, it's worth it.

Cost was about 30 usd each for rock and musuem entrance. It's quite a bit of walking up stair cases most of which are uneven, high steps or spiral stairs. Very windy at the top but satisfying once you've reached there. Very good views of the area

Entrance fee is steep as mentioned by others,but I'm glad to pay it to ensure the site is looked after. When you go up and down the welded steel staircases you will be glad they are not skimping on maintenance. The view from the top of the lion rock is spectacular and thinking back to what had to be done to built this is humbling

This stand alone rock in the middle of no where served as a residential place for the wannabe king.  The climb is exhausting but the view from top is exhilarating enough to forget about the aches and pains to follow :-) It is worth visiting if you are interested in seeing how resilient humans were compared to the current couch potatoes. Oh yes...watch out for the bees and wasps.

Beautiful views from the top of the rock fortress provided u take the pains to climb 1252 steps !! Its peace at the top. Wonder how they built this. Pls note that u need to climb before they shut the gates at around 5 pm and u need to surely climb down back to ur parking area as there are no lights at the fort or the surroundings, which is surprising and a downside to this visit.

This looks like hard work, and it is! However it's worth it. Try to get there early in the morning to reduce the heat and the crowds, as you are in a long line of people; it's lots of steps, but you can pause on the way up. And a great sense of achievement if you aren't super fit.

The view is quite superb and worth the considerable effort although,like most places in the Cultural Triangle,every last penny (and more) is charged.Be prepared to be labelled "foreigner" and beware the freelance guides lurking around the entrance.It is an imprisonable offence to masquerade as a guide if you arnt one!Wall paintings are also worth seeing even if photography is prohibited but the man supervising made clear he was amenable to a backhander .Local bars for a beer after the climb can be unusually expensive or so it seems if you don't look at a price list first!Its a great sight but beware the potential for "extras"

SIGIRIYA ROCK This Lion Rock popularly called Sigiriya is located in the Central Province of Sri Lanka, about 20 km from Dambulla. (Dambulla is about 150 km north of capital Colombo). The Sigiriya Rock is about 200 meter high and contains ruins of a complex of ancient structures, buildings, garden, and water tank, reportedly built by usurper King Kashyapa (477–495 AD) who shifted his capital from Anuradhapura to Sigiriya for fear of attack from the rightful heir to the throne, Moggallana. After the defeat of Kashyapa in 495, the capital was moved back to Anuradhapura and Sigiriya became just a Buddhist monastery for next few centuries. Now there are ruins of palace and few religious monuments only for the adventurous tourists and dedicated Buddh pilgrims. There are about 1200 stone and steel stairs upto the top of the rock. The adventure is magnificent and surroundings are breath-taking beautiful. As usual with Sri Lankan tourism, the ticket is abnormally high i.e. 35 US$. It is an expensive day trip but worth the money provided you can easily climb 1200 stairs. (Eiffel Tower has about 600 stairs upto second level). Sigiriya is 650 feet high rock having ruins of a palace, pond, temple and a garden of ancient times. It is 20 km from Dambulla, inviting adventurous tourists and dedicated pilgrims for a panoramic view of mesmerizing forests spread around.

We payed 4260rs while sri lankan people pay 220rs. This is way out of balance, but what can we do.... We didn't want to skip the place because it's really worth seeing. (You can enter for free if you enter from the side, but beaware that you can not visit the museum or climb to the top of the rock.) We visited the place early in the morning when it is not too hot and did the climb first. Bring water (and some cookies) because you can not buy anything inside. We recommend doing the climb first, then the visit the lower parts (as it gets hotter) and visit the museum last. In the museum you can read about the history and see a reconstruction of how it must have been like. You can skip the parts where they show a reconstruction of the fresco's (because you have seen the real ones on the rock already).

wonderful place to visit, Sigiriya -Lion Rock , pronounced see-gi-ri-yə is an ancient rock fortress located in the central Matale District near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. The name refers to a site of historical and archaeological significance that is dominated by a massive column of rock nearly 200 metres (660 ft) high, when you climbed the rock you can see The Gardens of the Sigiriya city are one of the most important aspects of the site, as it is among the oldest landscaped gardens in the world. The gardens are divided into three distinct but linked forms: water gardens, cave and boulder gardens, and terraced gardens.

We drove from Kandy leaving around 8:30 and getting there about 10:30.  Late May on a Monday is not crowded and there were few people.  We were a little shocked at the price - we should have checked - US$36 and no credit cards. Be clear whether you want a guide or not and establish a price. About 2,000 rupees is the minimum. To be honest the guide told us little that was not on the signs and couldn't answer any more detailed questions.  (which may have been because the answer doesn't exist) All that notwithstanding it is a fabulous place and understandably a world heritage site.  Like Macchu Pichu "lost" for centuries and still only partially excavated.  I wondered about the labor for such massive works and how it was "paid" for.  But there are no answers. Some other trip advisor reviews were dismissive of the paintings on the cliff face.  When you think that these date to the time the Romans left Britain, that they still exist and are so delicate and lovely we thought was a wonder. Stiff climb to the top but not too difficult and well worth it. Sunscreen and hats essential

Highly recommended. This is a part of the UNESCO site. famous among the locals and all the tourists, avoid a Sunday or Saturday as it gets flooded with locals. Also start early (before 10am) to have a crowd free climb and some own time !

The long 1200 odd step climb to the top is breathtaking and totally wort have. The remains of the castle on the top and the view from up there is totally worth it. Don't give up on the climb as from the top of the climb, you'll redeem all the effort.

After reading many reviews of this place, we decided to start early in the morning. Special prices to citizens of SAARC countries for entry tickets - Take your passport to claim discount. Overall a 3 to 4 hour engagement. Fitness needed as climb is steep but an average healthy individual can make it without issues. Highlights for me were the paintings which are beautiful and the views from top. Recommended !
