I set out to Sigiriya from my hotel in Negombo. It is quite a ride so you may want to stay closer if you don't want a long drive to start the day. Because of the long drive, it was noon by the time I reached Sigiriya. This meant that the climb to the top would be in the heat of the day. Before starting the climb, I visited the museum which was surprisingly nice. The grounds leading to the rock are also nice in their own right as well. The climb is actually quite strenuous as it required stopping several times to complete. It is a unique, adventurous climb but it is physical. The rock has been largely undisturbed so you are walking literally on steps attached to the exterior of the rock. You are not walking on steps caved into the rock. There are great views along the way and at the top. While it is exhilarating to reach the top, it would be nice if there were some sort of guidance once you reach the top. I would do this again but early in the morning or in the afternoon.

Very nearly didn't come here as it is pretty expensive, but totally worth it! You pay a huge amount to see Machu Picchu, Taj Mahal etc and this place is on par and the best thing about it is that it's empty. Phenomenal views from the top and lovely walking round the ramparts and gardens. New price is in photo I've uploaded - $30 or 4260 rupees. Don't let it out you off though!

The climb is not for the feint hearted, although if you avoid the spiral staircase to the less than impressive paintings, you can cut out some of the problem. The steps are steep but manageable, even to those of us nearing seventy years of age. Take your time if you can but there is sure to be a lot of people about. We went mid-afternoon and it was extremely warm. Take plenty of water, sunscreen your self and go at your own pace, its not a race. Great views of the plains from the top and the gardens below.

Some effort needed to climb up the circa 2000 steps but once at the peak the views are really magnificent. Also, awe-inspiring was how the kingdom was built at that period and preserved up till today.

What ever the weather climb the Lion Rock Sigiriya. It is a fantastic experience. We took to stairs in poring rain. Umbrellas were useless but when you get to the top and saw the foundations of what once stood there including a large swimming pool for the king carved out of the rock that still holds  water you wont be disappointed.Then turn around and look down and over the Land.The Kings gardens perfectly forming the entrance way to the Citadel.Beyond lay the fertile lands and jungle. Don,t forget a water bottle and climb SLOWLY. If you don't like hight's don't attempt the spiral stairs to the frescos, the rest of the stairs are steep but all with good handrails of some sorts. Enjoy, you can do this even if you are close to 70 years old. Esther

My parents and I visited Sigiriya World Heritage Site during our tour to Sri Lanka, and I was amazed by the staircases winding up. Near the lion's paw, we say many wasp nests, which freaked me out. I can't wait to go back.

Sigiriya Rock is a great attraction with spectacular views at the top. Be careful if you are afraid of heights as some of the staircases are a bit scary! Also, you can walk all the way around the rock which is a lovely nature path and, according to the locals, about 7 kms. It's relatively flat and shaded, making it perfect to do in the afternoon heat. (Just take a left or right along the moat before you go through the ticket gate - after where you buy tickets.)

This was one of the spots in Sri Lanka I wanted to see. I was worried about the steps but it wasn't as bad as I thought. It was single file and there was a lot of people (it was a public holiday) so we were going at a steady pace. The view at the top was worth it. Yes it was hot so make sure you have plenty of water with you. It is pricey but I don't mind if the money goes towards the up keep of the site. A fantastic spot.

We went first thing in the morning and the heat was still somewhat unbearable! That being said, the rock is beautiful. It was a little challenging to make it up, not going to lie, but I think the heat had a lot to do with that. Be sure to bring plenty of water. There are signs explaining what you're looking at while you're on the ground, but once you climb there isn't many. We were stubborn and didn't want to hire a guide, so that's probably our own fault. The view from the top is amazing. Although, due to the lack of signage and the fact that we were some of the first up that day, we couldn't figure out how to get down! We walked all over the top, would find stairs/rocks and start descending, only to discover said stairs just ended. It was quite frustrating as we were baking in the sun. Hint: you go down from the summit the same way you go up! D'oh! Overall, it was a good experience and really beautiful. It's pretty expensive compared to many things in Sri Lanka but was worth it. We're glad we went!

Unmissable, just unmissable. Go very early in the morning before the crowds gather (don't want to be waiting in line half way up the cliff) and before the heat kicks in. See the museum at the end. Bring sensible shoes and water. Absolutely a 100% worth seeing!

The strategic mistake we made is that we stayed overnight in Kandy and therefore arrived at Sigiriya at around 11:30am - it was already baking hot. If I'd visit Sigiriya again, I will make sure I stay overnight nearby and be at the rock when the park opens (7am). Tickets are expensive and if you are not local, you have to pay equivalent of $30 (credit cards NOT accepted), which is highway robbery and yet another sign how government of Sri Lanka "loves" tourists. It took me about 30 minutes to ascend and 30 minutes to descend. All in all I spent about 2 hours at the rock - high factor sunblock, hat and plenty of water is essential. Great views from the top. Food options are very limited so you probably need to time your visit with he view to eat elsewhere. Museum is very basic and not worth spending more than 15 minutes in.

4260 entrant NRP / 30USD / Throughout Sri Lanka, this is the most expensive ticket! Go in and come out of the gates can be individually that they are farther apart. Arriving just go sideways admission ticket !!! Other Images are not allowed to enter. Top of the Rock mid-tempo one hour by road. On top of ancient ruins are found. All the way down until you reach the cliffs NO !!!!! Drink shop. A minimum of 0.5 liters of liquid take with you, because it will be a hard journey! Stairs are exposed, but who used to miss more dizzy! In the evening, head lamp to be with you !!!!

Okay, this tourist’s spot is only for people who don’t suffer from vertigo and physical fitness is highly appreciated. I got up the rock and all the steps are worth it for the stunning view you’ve got from the top. When you once started to go up, it is really difficult to stop or to go back. First of all there are so many tourists that you walk and climb the stairs in single file. The other reason is that there are sometimes other ways down than up and you don’t reach the way down without going the whole path. This tourist’s spot is run by the government and because of this the fee is quite expensive in comparison to local attractions and I hope the money will really be spent for the rock

We visited Sigiriya on our last visit to Sri Lanka and it was phenomenal. If you have the chance to visit, please go here. It is amazing. We enlisted the services of a guide and I'm so glad that we did, otherwise I think there would have been whole sections I would have walked passed and not taken any notice of. There aren't really any signposts for points of interest so the guide really did bring it to life. It is such a beautiful place and if you can make it up the 1502 steps then the views are well worthwhile. We went in the heat of the day which was crazy so I would recommend an early morning or evening visit. And remember, as with everything in Sri Lanka, there is one price for the locals and then you can pay four or five times as much as a tourist. Well worth seeing though and I'm so glad that we went. It was the highlight of my holiday.

A truly fabulous, breathtaking wonder of the ancient world this predates the pyramids,  this is should not be missed when visiting Sri Lanka, I dream of one day returning and spending more time there looking at the well preserved ancient paintings in the caves would love to see what else future excavations uncover, as only a quarter of the area has been excavated so much more to learn and discover.  Please visit your mind will be blown away.

I absolutely love the place, it is like a palace on a huge rock. Make sure you go in the morning because it gets too hot in the afternoon, carry water with you. You can see the beautiful scenery when you reach the top of the lion rock. The ticket is definitely overpriced for foreigners and they only take cash, so make sure you have like 5000 local money with you.
This is a fascinating place and worth battling the multitude of tour buses to visit.  The "guides" are persistent and annoying but could be helpful to explain the layout.
This is not to be missed as it is truely an amazing piece of natural and man made attraction.  The US$30 entry fee is a bit much but the place is unique.

start early in the morning to climb the rock , as after 10 it is extremely hot to climb the hundreds of stairs, a viewpoint to the surrounding valleys , do not expect amazing gardens there, there have been some 12 centuries ago, now there are just the foundations nothing left and a legend too.
This place seems to be reviewed twice on the site.  Briefly; it's amazing.  If you're within 2-3 hours you must go there.  Straight out of Uncharted.  About £20 entrance unless you're a local!

This place was amazing. Ancient palace set in the Jungle laid out over 100 acres of land and with the palace itself built high above on a rock.  Straight out of Indiana Jones or Uncharted!  Walk amongst ancient ruins still being restored. Just like the photos.  This place made my holiday. Very high and with a steep climb to the top would not suit those who do not like heights or are not good with steep climbs.  The views are however fantastic. Entrance is about £20 each.  Get there early as it gets very hot getting up those steps! Watch out for the monkeys!

We climbed the mountain mid morning. Temperature was not yet extremely high. Climbing seems challenging sometimes but at the end is pretty simple. When you get to the top the view is fantastic as well as the sense of achievement experiencing the feeling of being over the top. It's a little bit expensive but still recommended (not between 12 and 15 pm). Great memories from that really amazing place.
Really nice ( and easy) walk, beautiful ! It took us about and hour to go up and down the rock. I would suggest you take water with and maybe a snack as the cafeteria is closed down! Enjoy!

What a great place!! It is incredible how this site was developed and the history that lies beyond. The views from the top are breathtaking but be aware: go as early as possible because the heat is "important". You can not leave the country without visiting Sigiriya.

It is expensive, very expensive (30 dollars for foreigners) but the views are just amazing. Don't go between 12:00 and 14:00 because it can be too warm, of course bring at least a big bottle of water. There's almost no shadow at the top. There is a museum that you can visit as well after the rock, useful if you really want to know the history and is not as crowded as the rock itself.
An amazing site that is worth the big climb. Grab a guide to get the most out of your visit. The views from the top are amazing .

One of the things to be conscious of when visiting heritage sites in Sri Lanka is the cost. There is a charge of about $25 per head per site, unlike the archeological sites in Myanmar which was a once off fee payable at the airport in Bagan. So these entrance fees can add up very quickly depending on your plans. In addition if you hire a guide there will be a fee and often there is an expectation of a tip if you are "happy with the service" and various people trying to sell you souvenirs along the way. So you need to be careful what you commit to and a firm "no thanks" is clearly understood. Leaving that aside, the walk / climb up Lion Rock is amazing, scary in places, exhausting in others, will temp you to give up at certain stages but don't - it is really worth all the effort when you reach the summit and take in the view - stunning! The morning we completed the climb was in searing heat & the crowds were very big. There are a couple of places on the journey where you are walking on a metal overhang and I couldn't help thinking the crowds on the day had the potential for something to go wrong. But it didn't and while exhausted at the end it was an enjoyable experience but it is not for the faint hearted. I think it took us a little over three hours to go up and get back down. You need to go at your own pace even if it is busy or the guide is pushing you, bring plenty of water, light clothing and a hat for the sun. Don't forget your camera! So I would certainly recommend this attraction, but do your research so you go prepared.
Worth visiting - it's a significant walk so best done early in the morning before the heat. The views are stunning and the cooler weather on top a relief

In Srilanka  my ambition was to see and climb the Lion rock a world heritage monument. Start early in the morning,wear comfortable shoes ,take a bottle of water and polo mint.Must have cash becoz when i was there  credit card swiping machine was not working Stairs are not bad to climb .Before lions paw do see frescoes. Till there it is not that difficult but when you climb the spiral stairs its little scary.When you reach the top all your efforts are rewarded .What a view from top Coming down is from another route and you can see serpentine rock.
it's best visit in the early morning or late afternoon. very nice experience. Lion paw was amazing. views are very nice.

We did a daytrip from Kandy to Sigiriya, Dambulla and back. We were with 4 and the driver cost us R8000 for the whole day. We left at 7:30 am in Kandy and arrived in Sigiriya at 10am. As it was in May, it was not too hot to do the climb and we enjoyed a cool breeze on top of the rock. There are warnings everywhere for hornets, bumble bees and wasps. They have huge nests at the rock. We did not have sny issue with it. On the way back to Kandy we stopped for lunch, at the Dambulla rock temple, a spice garden and a Hindu temple near Matale. We were back in Kandy around 6:30pm. For us it was a good and affordable daytrip.
It is not easy to get to the top if it is 35 degrees so do not forget water and keep a steady pace. Do not miss the paintings about a 1/3 up the way as they are more then beautiful.

This lion rock was amazing to see. Views are spectacular and makes you wonder how they were able to carve a lion out of rock all those centuries ago. There are alot of steps to climb which are narrow and although it was dry when we went, I could see that it would be slippery when wet, so wear sensible shoes. My advice would be to go early as the rock is extremely hot to climb in the day time and you will sweat an awful lot, so take plenty of water with you. Definitely worth the steep climb and be aware of the wasp nests. Do not make a lot of noise as this provokes them to sting.
! I’m not so strong enough for climbing but by a suggestion from my friend said it is better ealier. I did hike until the top and not so crowded. It was quite sweat though.

This was my fave part of Dambulla and I was dreading the 1,400 steps to get to the top but in the end it really was worth it as cliched as it sounds.  I would recommend you go early as the later it gets the hotter it is and climbing the steps that weave around upwards to the top is NOT for the faint hearted.  My husband and I saw people from all age groups and all levels of fitness including children, ladies in sandals and saris, elderly and overweight. I am probably of average fitness but don't particularly enjoy physical exertions in 30 plus degrees direct sunlight / heat and I must admit although being in my 30s I struggled.  I saw several people huffing and puffing also but there are plenty parts and ledges where if you go early you can pause without facing too much traffic and causing congestion. At the top its a great view but if you want you can get to the top, look around and literally turn back the way you came, but the trail so to speak makes you walk all the way around to look at ruins that are visible from a distance and can be skipped.  It is crafted such that if you are already tired and don't know you will end up walking around on the top and circling back anyways to the way you came. It is however really lovely to take in the views under a shady tree and congratulate yourself for working up the courage to scale 1,400 steps!!  Would definitely recommend a visit to this site with some comfy shoes and a hat to block out the heat.  Also carry water as there is nowhere on the route to pick up any on the way up and no water tip you are back down and heading to the exit.  The stairs and climb are very safe with railings so I would recommend it for all ages providing younger or elder are supervised and sturdy It took us (average fit with about a half hour pause at the top) approx 90 min to get all the way up and then down again.  Fabulous workout!

As someone who is afraid of heights this wasn't too bad. There are railings to hold on to during the steep bits. Go slow and take your time. The stairs on the summit had a railing the entire way up as well as metal caging on the outer ledge. There are lots of places to stop to let people go by if you are worried about crowding. Tips: go early in the morning to avoid the heat and the hagglers. Try to do it on a weekday if possible. I climbed at about 7am and it was a good temperature and hardly any other people there. Don't worry too much about fitness unless you have a heart condition  etc. I was surprised how fast you reach the summit. There is no rush. Not as hard as I expected (p.s I am not incredibly fit) Once you reach the Lions paw it's so worth going that extra little way up!

we traveled from Bentota  to climb the rock, so we stayed over at Kandy so we were nearer you need to be as early as possible as the heat will stop you in your tracks if you are there mid day. It was a hard climb but well worth it, the views from halfway then the top was amazing, make sure you have a guide so you get the history of the King on your climb, but beware of people trying to help up the stairs as they will expect payment !

I believe that if you are in Sri Lanka it is a good opportunity to visit the Sigiriya Rock. It is not that this is a lifetime experience but the rock offers some nice, thrilling views. Visit as early in the morning as possible because the heat is extreme when the sun is up.

Lots of steps, but it all felt quite safe, even when the traffic was two way. I have a problem with heights, but this was fine,  so long as you don't look down when the drop is straight below! Starting early with plenty of water is good advice and don't forget to look out for the frescoes of the beautiful ladies on the way up!  We were impressed to see a first aid post at the lion's feet, but fortunately we didn't have cause to use it, so could not comment on it's efficiency. The museum is also worth a visit, if you have the energy, but leave it till after the climb, or you'll lose the cool of the early morning.

The place is really beautiful and the view from the top is awesome!! Just be sure to bring enough water with you, good shoes and a hat. Avoid talking with anyone offering to explain and try to be quite so that you won't disturb the hornets there (and we all know why!)

it is a unique place,i think that you could no where find a similar site in the world. this remaining fortress is near Habarana town, when you take a look at the rock it looks not so high but it is actually 200 meters height and has 1200 steps to get to the top, but those steps are not continues there are several platforms where you can have a rest. Don't hesitate to go up it is a real adventure and from the top it has beautiful view, But you should go there either early morning or in the afternoon and to wear sport shoes and light cloths and don't forget a bottle of water, if someone has acrophobia then it is not recommended to climb and it is certainly not recommended for children less than young adults. It will not take less than 3 hours all the way up and down.  the entry fee is 30 US $. Enjoy this adventure and you will never forget it.

Beautiful place. The climb takes about 1 hour. Tickets are 30$ per adult. Make sure to bring plenty of water. If you start at 7:00, when the ticket office opens, the whole climb will be in the shade of the rock. There are a few trees at the top where you can get a shade to rest. On the way down signs point towards a 'tourist' exit, where your cab get juice and souvenirs. Sigiriya is a rocky plateau towering 370 meters above the sea level and is about 170 meters above the surrounding plain, in the heart of the island of Sri Lanka. In the last quarter of the V century BC., king Kasapa over build a fortress on a rock into his palace, around which canals filled with water were laid. Endless gardens were planted around the rocks in which perhaps the first fountains in the world were streaming. On top of the plateau, a monumental Lion Gate is lead. Prior to, and after, Kasapa’s reign existed in a rock cave a Buddhist monastery. Of the existence of the fortress the Europeans became aware only in 1907, when the British explorer John Steele, described it as "a huge art gallery”. Sigiriya - "probably the largest painting in the world." He was referring to the hall mirror before porcelain was lined with numerous frescos, that extended to 140 meters in length and 40 meters in height. A favorite motif of the Sigiriya frescoes are naked female concubines. Unfortunately, at present time only a few images are present. And from the last year, it is forbidden to photograph them. From the giant lion figure, which was carved into the rock and once served as the entrance of the palace, only its paws survived, on which curious verse inscriptions are left from Sigiriya’s visitors since the VIII century. At the top, one will discover the carved remains of the palace buildings and swimming pools. And certainly some breathtaking views of the island will open!

However, some parts of the climb consist of simple metal stairs bolted to the rock, so may not be suitable for anyone with a fear of heights. The hike up to the top of Sigiriya was just as draining in 37 degree heat as we expected it to be.  Then again, we are out of shape.  Still, lots of other tourists walking alongside you, and lots of sweating, so it’s not a trivial undertaking for anyone.  Walking slowly helps a lot.  The entire trip took us about 3 hours, including bottom to top, exploring the top, and getting back down.  There is almost zero shade at the top and we went through almost 2 liters of water per person.  I think one of our group was close to heat exhaustion (not heat stroke) upon reaching the top, so we rested, drank, and consumed bananas.  I recommend starting the hike as early as possible in the morning, when heat is low, when most of the hike is on the shaded side of the rock, and when crowds are thin.  We went up at 8am and I wish we’d gone up 1-2 hours earlier.  Also, it’s easy and convenient to break up the walk into sections, which is nice. Anyway, the walk up is well worth it.  There are ruins at the bottom, caves/art/ruins/views/terraces on the way up, and ruins and a hell of a view at the very top.  Sigiriya’s occupation dates back to almost 500 BCE, so it’s 2 millennia older than Machu Picchu, 1.6 millennia older than Angkor Wat, 1 millennium older than Chichen Itza, 600 years older than Hadrian’s Wall and the Roman Colosseum, 300 years older than the famous parts of the Great Wall of China,  and 50 years older than the Parthenon and Acropolis.  Sigiriya is approximately contemporaneous with the earliest of Peru’s Nasca Lines.  What’s older than Sigiriya?  The earliest parts of the Great Wall, the various Egpytian pyramids, Stonehenge, and a certain bristlecone pine.  Color me impressed.

Upon arrival there was chaos in the car park, with vehicles parked all over the place and local guides touting for buisness, we were with our own guide. The entry is quite steep $30 for what you see. Going in there are some ruined water gardens - the outer and the inner moats are there and then you face a steep climb. It is not for the fainthearted as the climb is steep with uneven steps. People come up and down the same stairs so watch out. It is very dusty so do not wear anything white as it will get ruined. The view from the top is nice, but it is a long climb. I personally think the rock looks better from a distance. Watch out for the amusing signs - keep calm in case of wasp attack for example. Go in the morning when it opens otherwise you'll bake.

I climbed the citadel of Sigiriya in 1969 and it was very much harder then. Hardly a soul about - now it is a constant stream of tourists taking a much easier route. Not so sure whether the changes are for the better.
Fantastic place. Good feeling about the place. Only downer is the dozens of guides that pester you from start to finish.

This place deserves to be a World Heritage site. Beautiful Fresco paintings on the wall, that huge lion gate, archaeological remains on the top of the hill narrating story of a wealthy kings that once rules that region, remains ageing back to 10000 BC...its just amazing. You can spend full day here. Its extremely amazing. Entry fees for Indians is ~2500 INR but its totally worth it.

Driver got us in good time of 9AM before the buildup of the day heat - which helped climb 1400 steps to reach the submit - very scenic view but nothing more to see on top the Rock - perhaps satisfaction

The ascent can be challenging during the day. Try to go early so it's not that hot. Bring lots of water. Very rewarding experience! Once you get to the top, the ruins of the citadel are amazing and the view is unbelievable! That's a must do!

A wonderful climb of 1200 stairs to the most amazing views of Sri Lanka.  Not for the faint hearted as the last few hundred stairs are on the outside of the rock.  Well worth the climb.  Very busy and hot.  Don't make too much noise for fear of disturbing the hornets nests.

Sigiriya - unesco world heritage site,endowed with centuries old frescoes with large unexplored hidden sites is a must visit site for anyone visiting Srilanka .Its the ruins of a palace of king kashyapa ,who has made this dream of his, a reality.For a traveller there is art, mysticism ,history,the grandiosity of the past and much more. We started our climb on sigiriya early ,it starts at 7 am .entry tickets can be directly purchased at the gates.they give discounted prices for people from saarc countries.Hiring a guide is real useful here, no matter how much u read. Travelling along the three gardens we climbed through centuries old trail leading on to the frescoes, then the mirror wall, lions foot leading up to the palace now in ruins. At the top , the view is amazing ,imagining men could do such things ..... Travel tips : start early ,climbs after 10 will be tedious ,tired and really hot. climbing up and down for a fit person is 3 hrs.dont buy anything that's sold on the way ,at the museum u ll get same things at a cheaper price.water bottles and chocolates are handy.hire a guide and immerse yourself in history.guides charge 1500 lkr.for saarc people get your passport.

We are a family of 4 inc 2 boys 8 & 9. We took a guided tour to the top of the rock. We climbed early at about 9am but it was still 28 deg. The 1200 steps wasn't too taxing but final climb up the metal stairs was tough for a vertigo sufferer like myself although the odd hornets nest on route offered a distraction! The view from the top was breathtaking and the history of this ancient fortified playboys palace was fascinating. A must do when touring Sri Lanka.

A very impressive achievement for such a long time ago. The climb is not for the faint hearted, overweight, pregnant, heart conditions or seriously unfit. It is exhaustive,  incredibly hot and straight up with 1200 narrow steps. If you can manage it then you will be rewarded. Be wary of the boys that will try to help you up stairs, they touch without asking and if you accept their help you are stick with them and you will be asked to pay.

An early start to avoid the heat of the day is recommended for a visit to Sigiriya.  Join the masses as you ascend the approach to the rock.  There are many guides vying for your business, but we chose to go it alone. The lower reaches are climbed by rocky steps initially, then metal staircases and the handrails get hot. There's a good resting place with trees for shelter before you make the final climb to the top. The ruins at the top would benefit from information boards as it's impossible to tell what things are without a guide book.  Amazing views and a refreshing breeze at the top. The descent is remarkably quick compared with the climb and separate up/down stairs make the trickier areas easier to navigate. An expensive visit, but on balance worth the money.

We were due to do this early in the morning - but went the previous afternoon around 3pm instead, good move, the temperature rose to 40 degrees next day!  This is definitely an early afternoon / late afternoon excursion. The steps and staircases are all perfectly stable and manageable, the heat is by far tougher than the climb.  Take advantage of the shaded areas en route though and it's fine, the views from the top are great - as is the satisfaction! I had a half a banana grabbed from my hand by a hungry macaque - so do take the warnings about monkeys stealing possessions seriously!

Arrived at 7am when they open, small queue, but no problem, and up to the top. Most of the walk is in the early part, it can be hard work just getting to the base, but if you take your time, its easy enough. Time we got to the lions feet, I thought it was meant to be half way, but in fact I would say that you are two thirds of the way, and it's really not that far, its just slightly harder going. Worth going to the top, excellent views, and much easier coming down. Not hassled at all, enjoyed the morning, but do it early, we were done by 9am, and it was starting to get hot!

This is definitely something you must see, if travelling around Sri Lanka. I think only very few places can compare to the beauty of this one, in the whole world (Ayutthaya and Machu Picchu are among these). Bear in mind the ticket won't be so cheap, and the area itself is very hot and wet... but apart from this, what could I say? This is a well preserved archaeological site of a rock fortress built 1500 years ago. Terraced gardens, ancient buildings, stairs, narrow passes, huge water pools: there's so much to tell about, you have to really see this amazing place with your own eyes. The only thing: beware of the stray dogs and the monkeys around the area.

It's absolutely essential to visit this fortress and when you get to the top you'll see why. It's disguised at ground level, although aerial photos give it away - try to avoid looking at these photos  before going. Top tip - go very early in the morning before the crowds arrive and before it gets too hot
Lovely layout which archeologists are still working on uncovering.  Not as grand as many other heritage sites but works is proceeding.

Not for the faint hearted.  It's a long hard walk to the top.  The museum is cooler and nicely done.  It is very expensive.  It is crowded with school children and other tourists.  There is the smaller rock a short distance away which is only 500 Rs and has great views of the archeological site but without all the tourists and a much easier climb.  Watch out for the tut tut drivers as they rip you off.  The distance from the bus stop to the entrance point is only 1 km and you can easily walk it.

If you are not physically fit please avoid this place as you have to climb around 2500+ steps and refrain from climbing in between 11:00 AM -3:30PM under scorching sun in between end of March-July. What a place.It's worth visiting.
It is a wonderful climb to the top of the rock! The feeling was very similiar to visiting Hampi which was also a heritage site!

The grounds of Sigiriya are lush and beautiful. Climbing up to the fortress was a challenge -and one that is worth the effort. I didn't not go all the way to the top. I stopped at the Lion's paws while my husband and friends continued to the top. The views out over the countryside are breath taking. Wear comfortable shoes and bring your cameras!

From Marawila we went to Sigiriya 3 hours. We climbed more than 1000 stairs up to the rock. It's really worth seeing when visiting Lanka for the first time but due to very high temperatures you can feel rather tired. Climbing up takes you about one hour.

If you are in Sigiriya, you have to visit this place. It has stunning view. Its very easy to reach the top, its not necessary to take a guide along. The entry fee is really expensive.  I had paid around 4000 LKR for two of us, so see that you make good use of the time, click as many pictures as you can, visit all 3 locations, museum, cave and top of the Rock. The passes will have entrance coupon. Carry water along, there are many steps to climb.

we went to visit the rock fortress i was not looking forward to it as we were told the climb was very hard but no it was not bad. i enjoyed looking at the different rocks on the way up to the fresco. to get to the fresco's you need to climb a spiral staircase and come down a spiral staircase but the pictures are worth seeing the colours are still very vibrant it is very well preserved. the mirror wall which i was told used to be so shiny the king could see himself when he walked past. the next climb was up to the lions paw (which was another entrance ) you can walk round and see the views it is amazing and well worth the climb they also have a first aid tent but it is for wild bee stings although we did not see any bees. there is another climb up metal stairs to get to the very top my husband went up but i stayed and enjoyed the scenery my husband said he enjoyed the view from the very top and he would recommend it if you go, overall it was a great day out.

We went to Sigiriya and Dambulla on the 1st day of a two day cruise port stopover (Mar 9, 2016) in Colombo.  The tour company we used was Kanota Tours.  Expect a 12-14 hour round trip depending on road construction.  At Sigiriya there is a separate foreigners entrance.  Entry fee is $30 USD. After entry, you will meet "tour guides" who we resisted at first, but later found that the ones we used were helpful and informative and at times assisted negotiating the narrow treadle stone steps. These "tour guides" can be at the entry or along the route. A tip is expected and for us, these guides were value added.   Dambulla is a Buddhist temple consisting of four natural caves. Shoes are not worn, so you might consider bringing shoe covers.  For us, the 12 hour trip to Sigiriya and Dambulla was worth it.
Start before 7.30 AM, before the Russian bus or for the sunset. The worst time is 8AM-10.30AM. But to be honest if you go to the top only to take a selfie it's a bit expensive....

Main attraction in this area and one of the most popular in Sri lanka. It's one of the best places I ever go. An awesome rock at the middle of forest with amazing historical structures and great nature around. After passing Lion's gate and going up through stairs , you can sea a excellent view on top of the rock. I strongly recommend here.

It was wonderful to be in the grounds. Just by seeing pictures you know it's going to be beautiful. But a few tips. Leave early. Leave wherever you are staying as early as you can. It can take some time to get to the park. If you leave it too late the heat of the day comes out and makes it 10 times harder to climb to the top. Carry light. Taking snacks and water might be high on your list but it is a vertical climb at some points in direct sun. A hat, sarong or light scarf to keep the some off you is great. You can buy water there so don't think you need to bring everything at once. Take it slow. There is SO much to see. Take it slow on the walk through. It's not going anywhere. Lovely shaded caves and gardens all the way up to the rock. Don't get a guide. They are not official/necessary. Everything can be explained along the way with stone information plaques. Vertigo. Steps are slotted and see though so if you do suffer from vertigo, be careful. Made worse with the Sri Lankan sun on top of you.

After visiting all the greatest places in Sri Lanka with a view (including Adam's Peak, Horton Plains, and many beautiful stops high in the mountains), I have decided that the most beautiful view is from the top of the Sigiriya rock. The ascent is not bad although the heat is challenging and everyone is dripping sweat along the way. So not very pleasant but all well rewarded once you reach the summit. Unlike the crowded summit of Adam's Peak, the top of the Sigiriya rock feels more isolated more zen more tranquil. And the views are breathtakingly magical.
The Sigiriya Rock offers very well preserved examples of ancient urban planning. Very elaborate and imaginative. Easier climb than it looks at first. Lovely scenery and views throughout.

Making a visit here was one of the main reasons for booking a holiday to Sri Lanka as the photos of this place had me mesmerized.  The rock is somehow smaller than you imagine though and the climb only takes a short time.  The grounds around the rock are worth spending a lot of time exploring though and this was something I hadn't expected.

If you are in Kandy, do spare one full day for this excursion.  Suggest that people who are fascinated by trekking must not miss this attraction.  However be selective with your family members who are elderly and children.  This may be too much of a climb for them.  However the entire rock climbing is an amazing experience.  The entire way is nicely done up to minimize and risk.  There are proper stairs with reeling so no risk of any fall.  Ample opportunities for taking pictures.  It takes about 1.5 hours to reach the top.  its an entire rock city.  Once you reach the top, the view is amazing.  Though there is nothing much at the top.  its just a flat surface.  Even the journey back is also exciting.  Entry tickets for foreigners is pretty high around USD 15.  Carry good stock of water, sun glasses, cap/umbrella  and nice pair of sports shoes for this trek and enjoy.  Preferrably do it in the morning.
This trip was so enjoyable. When climbing the rock I saw many things. On the top of the rock there is a old broken  palace.

Sigiriya is an archeological site in Central Sri Lanka. It is essetntially the ruins of an ancient palace / fortress complex, built during the reign of King Kasyapa (477 – 495 AD). It is one of the seven World Heritage Sites in Sri Lanka and is one of its most popular tourist destinations. The climb to the top - via the famed cave paintings is not for the faint hearted as the second part of the ascent is up narrow metal stairs (a bit like a fire escape) that are bolted to the rock face. To climb here was one of the best thing I have ever did! just be careful the bees!

thanks to a local's recommendation I went there very early, meaning starting to climb at 7:30. If you go later it gets really hot and very crowded. the 30USD entrance fee is in my opinion not justified, but I was able to share the transport costs and from there also go to Dambulla which has no longer entrance fee, so the day was rescued :-)

Great views but go early in the morning to avoid heat while climbing the rock. Take some time to wander thru the garden area before climbing the rock - parking is in a different direction - so you would not pass the garden again.

The most expensive tourists attraction ever, 30$ in my opinion are not worth the visit. But once on the top, you will enjoy a beautiful panorama. Avoid the hottest hour of the day, because there are a lot of stairs.
I would recommend this to people who have some time left to spare, as this involves a bit of walking.

I hate heights, tourists and exercise on holiday! We had a great guide and even though it nearly killed me it is worth it. When you are on the very top, jump up and get someone take a pic crouching down, comes out amazing! Take lots of water and the juice bar at the bottom is welcoming
This place was a huge rook which has a legendary regarding the ancient kings of Sri Lanka.we climb the rock with out guide and saw the drownings , pond and some ancient important feature of the place
Historical site, with a stairway to the top.  Best to get a guide so you can hear about the original inhabitants of the castle rock - go in the morning before it gets too hot.

If you go to Sri Lanka and miss this you are crazy it is awe inspiring the climb to the top is hard no point saying otherwise but when you reach the top and see the beauty and lush country below it blows you away and the story and history of this rock is again awe inspiring All I can recommend is take your time and drink it all in. Busy site. After lunch we were taken to the cave temples again awesome beautiful and so worth a visit Lots of monkeys on the way up

Very spectacular historic sight. Nice garden to walk through to get to where you start the climb and café with facilities. Note the climb up is mainly all stairs and its a long climb. You also come back a different way to the way you go up. If you can't manage the whole climb its easy to get halfway look at the vies and come down the same way. You normally get off you transport at one place and pick it up at another. Worth it if you take you time and do it in stages.
A beautiful site and a must if you can. Do the climb (not easy for young and old). We got stuck in the rain at the top which added to the adventure!

To me this place is in the group of world monuments worth travelling to see if you can -  but not at the same level with Tikal, Machu Pichu and Petra, etc. Great history and great scenery. It would be criminal not to visit whilst in Sri Lanka.

This really is an amazing place. I went with my 6, 8 and 10 year olds and they all made it to the top. It gets very hot so go early or late afternoon but with a good guide who can bring the site to life it is worthwhile even with small kids.

As nothing was planned ahead, everyone kept recommending to visit this site, and we did, the driver with an airconditioned car charges 15-17k and the trip takes around 5 hours driving. The guide is recommended but not essential, especially if you get someone who can give you good information, and you can bargain the price, 2-4k is reasonable, check their English or language first as it makes a difference. The attraction entry fee is fixed and it is 30$ per person. The grounds are clean and looked after, although the steps are not that comfortable as they are short, a point to consider if you have long feets, but shouldn't be an issue to stop you from climbing. 1200 steps to go up, and it is worth it, but need to be moderately fit, many stops can be taken to rest. The preservation process and the damage due to time stopped me from ranking it with 5!!

As nothing was planned ahead, everyone kept recommending to visit this site, and we did, the driver with an airconditioned car charges 15-17k and the trip takes around 5 hours driving. The guide is recommended but not essential, especially if you get someone who can give you good information, and you can bargain the price, 2-4k is reasonable, check their English or language first as it makes a difference. The attraction entry fee is fixed and it is 30$ per person. The grounds are clean and looked after, although the steps are not that comfortable as they are short, a point to consider if you have long feets, but shouldn't be an issue to stop you from climbing. 1200 steps to go up, and it is worth it, but need to be moderately fit, many stops can be taken to rest. The preservation process and the damage due to time stopped me from ranking it with 5!!

Sigiriya is a world heritage site with a lot of things to see and discover around the citadel. Access roads are not maintained well. Foreign visitors should be careful with some local people who offers to help with climbing, that is of course, for money!  Authorities should make proper arrangements to keep them out of the citadel as the image of the country is at stake with those kind of people. Apart from that it's a very good attraction.

High cliff and beautiful. Beautiful natural scenery and unique. But a long way to go to reach the top of the cliff. As well as its rising value. Unfortunately responsible for selling tickets and guides are not in a good place. And collection management was very poor.
Wonderful place take plenty of water as the climb is difficult in the heat. Was very busy when we were there , wall art interesting views spectacular

Fantastic site, only recently excavated moats (1982) and a lot more to be done. Incredible that they could build something like this more than 1500 years ago. Really worth visiting. Wear good walking shoes and go early (0700 or 0800) die to heat and crowds. Take water, they charge double in the cafe. Museum ticket included in entry price and was actually quite good. Truly fascinating high culture achieved this UNESCO Heritage site and sone very strong young men.
Steep and should be reasonable fit. Need to take water and there is no toilet once you start the climb. Ensure your camera is fully charge as the view is worth it.

Climbed the rock with my wife and two children aged 5 and 6 at 10am. It was very hot so please bring plenty of water and wear a hat, you don't want sunstroke here like a lady we came across. Is a hugely rewarding climb to the top, although quite steep and if you don't like heights some parts see you walking through steps with a sheer drop a long way down so best not to look!! Our children made it up and down unassisted and were the youngest there. Having to carry them would have been very awkward so I would suggest taking this onboard before climbing with young children. It's an incredible place even looking from the bottom to top. We didn't get hassled by the locals offering to guide us and was hugely rewarding.

Wow - and to think this site and its buildings and grounds  date from 477 AD. the size and  complexity of the layout and gardens make you realise just how skilled our forefathers were. The irrigation of the various gardens as well as the marrying of the natural rock into the building of the palace put their skills on par with those of ancient Egypt. One could spend many hours on this site but be aware there are some very steep stairs to negotiate if you want to reach the top of the rock. That said there is plenty to see without having to be that strenuous. Truly an inspiring site.
Worth the stairs to see the view of the area... Read your guidebook or hire a guide for the full story

This is the same place where Duran Duran shot their music video: Save A Prayer in the 90s. And I found the place exactly as it was 20 years ago, as I found it in the video. Although I was exhausted, I enjoyed every step climbing up there. The view from the top is fabulous. It's worth the high entrance ticket every tourist pays. Apart from the palace, one can also marvel at the fresco on  way to the top. The paintings tells a lot about the King's lifestyle back then. I would recommend going early in the morning as the place gets crowded as the day progresses. I also advise to watch your step as you climb the final steps to the top.

This was one of the destinations on our tour of Sri Lanka. I knew it was a big rock and an iconic tourist spot, but had done no research about Sigiriya whatsoever! First of all you enter along a central path through old and beautifully kept landscaped gardens at the foot of the rock.  We arrived just after 8am and I was very daunted at the sight of what we were about to climb.  We had plenty of rests and the only bit I really didn't like was the spiral staircase hanging on the side of the rock face. You can avoid this if you don't want to see the cave mural drawings. When we got to the platform almost at the top, my heart sank when I realised there was still a precipice to undergo.  At this point it's wrought ironwork steps with handrails on the rock edge, at an almost ladder-like angle all the way.  I am a bit of a wuss when it comes to heights and exerting myself!  With support from my husband I managed the climb, and was so proud of myself that I had achieved it - because otherwise I would have missed out on all the interesting bits, all the ruins of the palace at the top.  Of course having a guide was a great advantage as we had a commentary on the history. The panoramic view at the top was the reward. All in all it took us a couple of hours or so. Coming down was much quicker as you would imagine.  I must be fitter than I thought as I didn't ache at all the next day.  Steel yourself and do it, you will be glad that you did.

Worth the walk to the top, truly magical experience. Worth the $30 US to get in (this includes the gardens, the Rock and museum) This attraction is very popular and a decent physical quest. A must see if you visit Sri Lanka!

A very busy tourist site but worth the hot climb (start early in the day). Don't miss the Gallery of the Maidens on the way up. There is a cooler breeze when you reach the top and some exploring of the different areas to do. The water gardens at the base of the rock are being renovated and it should look wonderful when it is finished.

The Lion Rock fortress has much to offer travellers in experiencing the ancient Sri Lankan engineering to beautiful art work and amazing scenery.  The climb to the top of the rock in the heat and humidity is definitely worth the views!
For a bit climbing up the hill using stairs you will be rewarded with amazing view. Due to hot sun and higher temperature I do recommend to go there very early morning.

This fortress is on a huge and tall rock. You have to climb a lot of steps. We being pretty old decided not to climb this rock. We saw it from a distance. But our guide explained everything to us. This is a World Heritage site.A lot of Foreigners visit this place There is an  art and culture monument up there.You have to go through a gigantic Lion Paws which is overlooking the symmetrical garden below. How the king made the water to be mannually pumped up there at that time is really wonderful.

Our guide took us to the road from where we could see the Fortress. But we did not want to climb the up because of our age. Our Guide explained to us about the engineering Marvel of the King Kasyapa and urban planning and also one of the finest monument of art and culture. This is a 5th century Rock Citadel and a World Heritage site too.From the front side, there are two gigantic lion paws and you you have to step through through these paws, over looking the garden. The guide also told us how this this king got the water to be pumped mannually at that time. Pumpimg it to 3-4 heights again and again and finally to the top. Simply marvelous.

Had a good climb to the Sigiriya rock early in the morning. The citadel opens at 7:00 AM but you can collect the tickets from 6.30. Try to finish it early as the heat will be just too much after 8:30. The views of the garden is superb at the top of the rock. The crowd is more compared to the Pidurangala. Take good amount of water as well! Cheers!

I spent four days visiting the Cultural Triangle in Sri Lanka with a group of friends. It was very hot and sticky, made much worse by having to remove shoes and hats and cover knees everywhere, resulting in very sore feet and being uncomfortably hot. Entrance fees for foreigners cost us a total of 13,000 rupees (about US$90). Some of the archaeological sites are not much more than piles of old bricks. There are many steps to negotiate - some of these are very steep, badly spaced (admittedly built over 1,000 years ago) and slippery. English speaking guides have accents so thick that you only get every third word. Crowded with thousands of tourists and local schoolchildren, especially Sigiriya where you have to negotiate narrow suspended walkways and steps. Photography is prohibited in some places including the famous Sigiriya frescoes. Many mangy stray dogs and mischievous monkeys roam around, both of which have rabies. Hawkers selling trinkets pester you everywhere like flies. Beggars (cripples) hang around car parks pleading. Narrow roads are shared by huge white coaches with enormous wing mirrors. If you can put up with all this then you will probably enjoy the Cultural Triangle. On balance, we did!

This is a must for anyone interested in ancient history or wonderful panoramic view. Stare out at a landscape barely untouched in thousands of years. Arriving early is the key to avoid blazing sun and hoards of people and bring plenty of water! Having one of the many guides available is also recommended as otherwise you don't really know what you are looking at. You may see them as pests when you arrive in the carpark, but they know their stuff and you won't be sorry!

Don't panic about the number of steps you have to climb just go for it. From the symmetrical gardens to the frescoes, the wobbly staircase to the gorgeous views from the summit this is one place you have to visit while in Sri Lanka. Take a hat, water and lots of sun cream and enjoy, you will be disappointed if you don't attempt it.
Ask your guide to take you up late afternoon and stay until sunset - but take a torch for the descent!

A wonderful experience and whilst there are quite a few steps to the top it isn't that hard if you tackle it early in the day to avoid the heat.  The summit and old palace area are wonderful with incredible views and the Damsels pictures on the cave walls are well worth visiting.  You'll not be disappointed and it is well worth the climbing.

A must visit on the itinerary to understand the culture & history. Avoid the place on Sri Lankan public holidays as it gets unbelievably busy. I'd say arrive for 7am & go to climb the rock as it will be much less busy and the heat more bearable, we climbed at 10.30am and therefore faced a queue waiting to go up. Take water & plenty of protection from the sun with you & be prepared to be accommodating of others who will push past you. If you have young kids, still do it but be prepared for the 1200 steps up to 200 metres. It took us roughly 2 hours to climb due to the sheer amount of people but it was very much worth the effort. It was a clear day & the views from the top was spectacular. The information on the substantial history was limited & we were grateful our guide came up with us. There are drinks to buy at the car park at the end as well as plenty of local stalls selling an array of gifts for you to take home. The water gardens as you walked in were beautiful also. Well worth a visit 😊

We went to Sigiriya during our tour of Sri Lanka, we were accompanied by a guide who had also been driving the two of us around. The guide was very well informed about the history of the place and as such really added to it. The climb to the citadel whilst not heavy going in one sense (there are well defined steps) will be challenging if you have no head for heights or if you struggle more generally you may want to consider carefully whether to go up. On our attendance we saw a number of individuals start to struggle in part due to the heat, and due to the crowds it was difficult for them to abandon the climb once committed. We did however see families climb but you are very exposed to the elements so sun hats, water, and creme are a must if you are fair or burn easily.  The route down is in our view much easier going as you miss out the gallery and spiral staircase. The views are second to none and we were fortunate to have a particularly clear day.  The history of the site and how it came to be the site of a palace was fascinating and the ruins well preserved.  There is relatively little explanation relating to the history of the site in comparison to some and so we would recommend doing your own research in advance if you want to get the most out of the history side of it.

We went to Sigiriya during our tour of Sri Lanka, we were accompanied by a guide who had also been driving the two of us around.  The guide was very well informed about the history of the place and as such really added to it.  I would recommend looking it up in advance though as the initial museum is not as comprehensive as it could be on the history.  In any event even if you're not interested in history or archeological sites there is a great deal to keep your attention. On arrival there is a musuem and some information about the history but this could have been a little more comprehensive in our view, especially given how much there is to the story of the location. There are then the remains of the water gardens which are both pretty and boasted some great photo opportunities.  The climb begins in earnest from here and whilst not heavy going in one sense (there are well defined steps) if you have no head for heights or struggle more generally you may want to consider carefully whether to go up.  On our attendance we saw a number of individuals start to struggle in part due to the heat, and due to the crowds it was difficult for them to abandon the climb once committed.  We did however see families climb but you are very exposed to the elements so sun hats, water, and creme are a must if you are fair. Approximately half way up is a gallery and at the top both the remains and views are incredible, they certainly made the climb worthwhile.  The route down is much easier going not least as you miss out the spiral staircase to the gallery. As foreigners you pay a little more on entry (which seemed fair enough to us, but at an equivalent of £25 GBP it isn't a cheap day trip, although concessions are available for children) but in terms of value we thought it well worth it to see this incredible archeological site and the views from the top. Also of note is that we went on full moon day, something we were ignorant of before coming to Sri Lanka.  In short there is a public holiday for many on the full moon and as such was very busy which may be worth considering when planning your visit particularly if you have young children as you will have to wait when climbing if it is busy.

Yip this is definitely a highlight of the area and if you are in and around it you should definitely go and see it . This place seems to divide people. The price goes up almost every month - in March 2016 it was already up to 4260 LKR per person (approx 28.40 €) and if all you're after is the view you may be better going to the other rock a few km away that's only 500 LKR. However at Sigirya there is more than just the view. You begin with a walk through extensive gardens and ruins at the foot of the rock, and then begin climbing the steps. There are ample opportunities to stop and rest, take pictures etc. About one third (guessing) of the way up there is a spiral metal staircase up to a cave with beautiful paintings (no photos allowed) and another spiral staircase back down again. You cannot avoid doing these staircases, and for me they were one of the toughest parts as there is no way of stopping so you have to do the whole thing in one go to avoid holding everyone up. After this there are a few more flights of steps and you get to the Lion's Feet - a large area with benches and shade that is (guessing) about two-thirds of the way up. From there it's up a series of steps and metal staircases to the top. Not easy to pause from there up, but there are two staircases, one up and one down, and it is possible for folks to squeeze past if you need a breather. When the metal staircase ends and you're back to brick and stone you're only about 30 steps from the top. The top is astounding. Not only are the views absolutely breathtaking, but the ruins on the top are so extensive you wonder how on earth they ever got all the building materials needed up there, in the days before the metal staircases were built and they were just using footholds hacked into the rock. Do make sure you explore the ruins - there is a huge stone throne bench (facing leftwards from the direction in which you arrive up the stairs) which is worth seeing. You descend using the same route (but a separate staircase) as far as the Lion's Feet, and then two flights of steps below that you deviate off and take a different path to those coming up. How hard is it? Not as hard as I expected given some of the reviews on here. We arrived at 7 a.m. when they opened, to try to ascend before the day got too hot. Not only was it a shade cooler, but there were about 20 people at the top when we got up there, and by the time we were back at the bottom I'd guess there were several hundred at the top. I'm over 40, 22 stone, unfit, asthmatic and have a dodgy ankle, and from the gardens at ground level (i.e. the bottom of the first actual 'staircase') to the very top took me about 45 minutes. I stopped for about 6 or 8 brief breathers, including a 5 minute stop at the Lion's Feet. You will sweat ridiculously - even the fit ones were drenched - so take a towel in your bag, along with sun cream and lots of water. The metal staircases up from the Lion's Feet to the top seemed to be causing a bit of concern to those with serious vertigo, but it's possible to get up without having to look at the drop, because if you look straight down all you see is rock, not 'thin air'. If I had to give one tip it would be to start at 7 a.m. - it was getting so busy by the time we started our descent that you would have no chance of going at your own pace, you'd be stuck behind hordes of tourists, whereas at 7 we could pace ourselves and do it how we wanted.

If you are not reasonably fit you will need to stop often at the various landings, and take plenty of water.  If you are old or infirm this is probably not for you. You need to start early, around 8am, to reach the top before the worst of the blistering sun - and to avoid the crowds who later in the morning make the last section a slow procession in the heat of the sun. It is quite expensive, but take my advice and that of other reviewers - just do it.

John Still in 1907 suggested, "The whole face of the hill appears to have been a gigantic picture gallery... the largest picture in the world perhaps And he was not wrong. My experience with Sigiriya has been a bewitching one. When I crossed the moat, there lay a vast plan of an ancient garden and fortress. They have excavated the northern part only, the southern part has been kept for future studies. After crossing many lawns, the main ascent to the rock plateau begins. There is the Cobra-hooded cave, the water garden, the boulder garden, and the terraced garden in between. After climbing almost 1400 stairs, the frescoes on the wall make you forget all the fatigue. Though you are not allowed to take photos of the frescoes, they remained etched permanently in one's memory. There are further stairs to reach the top of the plateau. Looking down from the top gives a sense of satisfaction of testing your physical stamina.
