Citadel of Sigiriya - Lion Rock, Dambula cave temples and Matale Hindu temple may all be visited on a day tour from Kandy. The entrance tickets for the sites cost 4100, 1500 and 400 Rupees respectively. Don't forget to pay a visit to the museum before visiting the frescoes and the Lion's Gate in Sigiriya.

We had a great day out at the Sigiriya Site. Even though is poured with rain for most of the day we persevered and it was well worth it to do so. The climb is a bit of a challenge but not impossible. The cave paintings are stunning and the view from all the stopping points along the way are gorgeous. Make sure to wear good walking shoes with good grip, plenty of water and a hat. Make sure to take a tour guide with you to explain all the points of interest along the way. Try avoid the guys alone the way who will try to help you up the stairs and then as you come down bother you for a tip. Well worth it!

Great site and well worth it, even in the wet. As everyone says, go as early as possible to avoid the queues and crowds. Which become a problem on the narrow shared up/down staircase. However. Pretty poor form from the people running this place. The signs are becoming unreadable. You get no map or any information. For Rs 4,200 per person (USD30) you expect a lot more. It would take very little to make this attraction really excellent, but they couldn't be bothered.

We had a very enjoyable couple of hours when we visited Lions rock. It is not for the faint hearted though with some of the steps to the top being very steep. Having said that, the view at the top is very rewarding. You can see for miles in all directions and you really appreciate the extraordinary level of work that went in to building this place. We arrived around 4pm which was ideal as it wasn't quite as hot as earlier in the day and we got to see the sun setting on our way down. Tip: take plenty of water with you as very hot work!

Sigriya  Rockfortress: Sigriya rock fortress is one of the must visited place in Sri Lanka.  History telling king Kasyapa was made his palace in Sigriya.  He chooses the 600ft high rock to build a palace over it to protect himself and family from enemies.    There are about 1200 steps to climb to reach the top of the rock fortress. The stairs made up of rocky steps at the lower part and narrow iron stairs to the top.  The debris of the Palace is wonderful.  There are signs of multi story buildings, swimming pools, gardens, open terrace etc: The Panoramic view from the top is awesome.  The view of a vast area of Matale district with surplus greenery, water pools, lakes and Elephant rock are really mind blowing. This rock fortress and surrounding gardens are well preserved area and it is listed in UNESCO’s world heritage site.
Its worth the visit. The fort on top was amazing. Better to go early morning before it gets too hot.

Views are spectacular but the experience of getting up to the top was absolutely horrendous and the place is totally mismanaged. Massive queues of people trying to get up the stairs made worse by tourists who've paid guides pushing in at the front. Security should stop this happening but have most likely been paid by the guides. Then to make matters worse you have elderly people and very small children who can't manage the stairs and hold everything up. I'm sure it would be amazing with less people around but I would avoid at all costs during the high season.
The sigiriya frescoes and the hike to the top of the rock was an amazing experience. One of the historic city in Sri Lanka and the rock really looks like a lion..

This is an amazing place to experience. A very well planned urban city since the 475 CE .... amazing planning. Water bodies, gardens, boulder gardens, fountains... As you start the climb to the rock - Sigiriya, the adventure becomes thrilling. You come across various caves, where frescoes done by the Buddhist monks 1500 years ago are visible. The COBRA HOOD cave is just awesome. A cobra hood cut out of the single rock gives one a big surprise. The climb to Sigiriya has been made quite easy with spiral stairs leading upto the LION FACED rock (about 3000 steps).... As you enter the cave cut out within the HUGE rock, one is awestruck by the colourful frescoes 1600 years old .... such vivid colours with so great attention to detail. As one comes out of the cave, you come to the magnificient LIONS PAW cut out from the rock. An experience worth remembering the lifetime.
But try not to visit when there's a holiday as the crowds were quite huge. But, crowd or no crowd, worth the time and energy spent climbing to the top.

This is a fort built on top of a rock with its own water hydro system dating back to ancient times with many caves with historic drawings inside. Don't be put off by the climb, its not as hard as it seems or as the tour agents make you believe it is. Once you reach the top you will be rewarded by the amazing views of the whole area from the top. Well worth the climb! Things to be aware of: - Men will be offering to help pull you up the steps, or try to give you guidance, just ignore them - Others will be trying to sell you souvenirs or umbrellas, again, ignore them, cheaper souvenirs of the same type and quality are available in the major towns and cities - As the climate can change easily, wear something light but durable under the rain. Make sure you wear comfortable shoes for the climb especially that some of the steps are very narrow and slanted and get slippery after the rain. - Bring a hat, put on sunscreen and wear shades just in case. - Buy the entrance tickets at the designated area and not from the men standing around.

We had limited time but please start with the visit to the museum as then can know the real history and when you see the real structure can relate to the history, very scary climb down for persons with altitude sickness, but when at the top it all seems to be worth it, beautiful old gardens and clean all around.

The path to the top includes some vertigo inducing stairs. Try to get over it... And you'll be glancing at amazing wall paintings and you'll be overlooking the jungle from the top. Truly a rewarding experience. Be sure to start the climb at 7.00 to beat the crowd.

Amazing history behind this place, and lots of beautiful gardens surround it. If you are strong and fit enough then go up the Sigiriya mountain rock for the view (you can see from the skyline a couple statues of Buddha)
Amazing views and worth the many steps to and walking to get to the top. We went early in the morning and that made it much more pleasant.

A must-visit site in Sri Lanka. Steep climb but thrilling. We stopped every now and then to soak in the view of the lush green forest and a giant Buddha statue while on the way up. It can get very hot and sunny at the summit during mid day, suggest to apply sun screen if you don't want to get sun burned

Between the cave paintings, water gardens, and amazing lion claw palace this site was incredible.  As a rock climber, its impressive that I was scared ascending the many stairs and very impressed when imagining the king climbing this back in the day.  I do wish our guide had given us more information however, there was nothing to read that I could find either.

Don't be put off by the price ($30 US) or the climb ... The climb looks harder than it is. The worst bit is the crowds. Go early to miss the worst of it. We went at 8.30 and probably should have gone 30 minutes earlier. It was already busy. The are some bottle necks in places getting up to see the frescos (don't miss this... It is fabulous - amazing that they are still there in this tropical weather! Some are less preserved, but there are a few that are stunning). There are enough places along the way to rest and catch your breath. There are some steep bits where if you a scared of heights it might be a bit scarey, but persist because the views from the top are worth it all. There are ruins up top and a large pool area. Makes for great photos. We went up on a rainy day nut views were still good. Lastly ... Go to toilet before you start .... There are some near the ticket office ... There are none on the walk ... It may take some time to get to top. Also take water. .. No stalls until you get to bottom.
Amazing view and the environment.  The heritage and the ancient technology and architecture is impressive. Promising enjoyable times if your a history and a nature lover.

A brilliant place to visit, lots of steps so some level of fitness is required but worth the climb. Would recommend you hire a guide to get the best out of the place as they will point out bits you would otherwise miss and give you all the history of the place.
This is a very interesting heritage place! The children loved the climb and the view was spectacular! It was worth every steps!

Entry was 4200 LKR and my guide was 3000 LKR. Get the guide - they bring you on the express queue and the sites would otherwise be place cards to read. He was kind enough to show me the flora and fauna around the grounds like the oleander tree and the crocodile and iguanas. I would definitely make it a point to visit to understand the lavishness of the King's habits and for the views of the surrounding area. Make sure you have good shoes and strong knees. Fear of heights? If only there was a pill for that.

It is a 1-1.5 hr walk but we end up spending around 4 hours. Part of the time is spent on waiting -  we went on a national holiday thus hundreds of local Sri Lankans are joining us for the hike. Another part is spent to enjoy the sunset on the rock summit - we managed to catch the last 5 minutes of the beautiful sunset. Back to the walk, it's actually a leisure hike where most of it are paved steps walking up to the top. There are two routes: one that get to see cave images, another one that skip the cave images and directly get to the top. The cave images are some Buddhist paintings in a relatively small space (2 mins walk at most). You can consider skipping if getting to the top is your top priority.
A hard climb but worth the effort.  I'm 71 but made it to the top with the help of a guide.  It's in 3 stages so time for a breather.
Great view from the top, but before you need to climb a few steps, nice paintings as well to see, not for people having vertigo!

Expensive ($30 pp) but truly amazing view. Go around 7:30 in the morning for less crowds. We heard that you can also climb the rock next to it (probably less expensive or free) and have good views of Lions Rock from there.

On our Cultural Triangle trip we of course made a stop in Sigiriya as well. The rock is the reason why you come here so we had to go up. Our driver told us it would be best to visit early early morning. Since we are not early birds we started the climb at 1100. It was a bit busy but this was not annoying. The climb is actually a piece of cake. Some 1,000 steps up easy and safe stairs. During the first half of the climb you can see the famous paintings. They are beautiful and make you wanna by the king back in these days ;-). Half way there is a plateau where you can have a rest before you take the second set of stairs which take you up to the top. On this plateau you once had the lion gate which was the entrance two the stairs. Now only the lion's feet are still there at both sides of the stairs. Once you claimed the second set of stairs you find the palace layout and get a clear impression on how the place must have looked like. The views from the rock are obviously stunning. Also the gardens downstairs leading up to the first set of stairs are beautiful. Maybe this is the most beautiful sight to visit in the Cultural Triangle.

We arrived at the park entrance 12 pm. When we arrived at the foot of the rock we discovered there was one long barely moving queue all the way to the top. a round trip reportedly would take 6 hours. No warnings were given when we puchased the $30 per person tickets and $15 for kids (50 times what Sri Lankans pay) and no refunds where given either when we after standing in line for 30 minutes while barely moving returned. Turned out this was a long holiday weekend. Park opens at 7 am which is the best time to get in if you want to avoid the queues.
Make sure to get up early to avoid the large crowds. This site contains beautiful ancient frescoes and some of the oldest gardens in Asia.
Wonderful place, you need to come early to avoid the crowds, especially on Sri Lankan public holidays,

I have visited this site many times over the past 20 years and have advised friends that it is a wonderful place to see. It remains a wonderful place and the maintenance of the grounds are excellent. BUT As a Sri Lankan resident I usually get a local price to attractions throughout the island as we are always taking our visitors to them. However here I had to pay full price of 4,200 Sri Lankan Rupees. There were 3 of us, so that worked out at 12,600 rupees (£63) But I have to say that the whole place is well worth that! However a guide accompanied us (3 ladies) and whilst he was excellent demanded that 2 of the ladies pay him 3,000 rupees each for his services.. Unfortunately I have cataracts and could not complete the climb and was accompanied by 2 young men to help me up the very first part. I decided to return to the car park and offered them 200 rupees each. They wanted 1,000 rupees each!! This meant that the total for about a 2 hour excursion was 20,600 rupees or £103.00 (at an exchange rate of 200 rupees to the £. So visitors beware. It is worth the initial entrance fee...But if you ask, and I had to ask, for a leaflet about the site, you have most of the information you require.

Amazing views on the climb and at the summit. Go early in the morning - it opens at 7, as your walk up will be shaded, and there won't be many people. Even at 9:30 on our way back down we saw crowds of people and queues to climb the stairs going back up. As others have said, it costs 4,200 rupees or $30USD but it's worth it. Take water with you as there is no where to buy it, and no toilets. We saw young families and more elderly people doing the climb so it is quite accessible, lots of places to stop and rest. Easy climb down. Thoroughly enjoyed it and relished the amazing view at the top, you can even see the white Buddha statue as you climb. Highly recommend a visit.

The entrance fee is a little steep and there are lots of guides offering their services (also at steep prices). There is a museum right at the beginning that explains the general history of the place. The climb is interesting with lots of murals and architecture. The views at the top are amazing. It's interesting how an entire fortress was cut out of sheer solid rock without use of the tools and techniques we have today.

This is a fantastic heritage site and a must visit in Sri Lanka. Our family commenced the climb at about 800 am only as it was raining until then. We would consider ourselves unlucky as drizzle turned to very heavy rain during our main climb; which meant less photos as well. Since we had come prepared with umbrellas and rain cover for our bags & camera bag, we kept going up slowly. The climb was less enjoyable for the fear of slipping & falling down. The view from the spiral iron ladder to the the cave with the frescoes offered some stunning views of Sigiriya and the route that we just covered while coming up. The frescoes were awesome and our guide told that they were drawings of different types of asian women; we could notice subtle differences in their facial features only then. The next phase was a walk towards the Lion Rock. However, relentless drizzle & rain meant more risk climbing up and also getting our professional camera kits drenched. We had to give it a miss unwillingly and regret that we were unlucky with the weather. Be well prepared for rain with umbrellas, ponchos/rainwear and additional protection for your camera gear. On a normal day, this site would need a good 2 to 3 hours to enjoy the different spots @ Sigiriya. Not recommended for young children that need to be carried/taken in a stroller, people with knee/leg pain, arthritis and older people that cannot climb up.

The Price is very high, it's crowded, it takes long to go up because there is a lot of people. Better not to go there if you have vértigo. In my opinión going to Pidurangala is better, you have the same view, you have a very good view from Sigiya from there ans it's only 500Rp. Hope it helps!

Like many others have said, tourists are charged a premium of $30 US but this seems to be stopping no one as it was packed. For this you get a very interesting museum at the entrance which helps explain what you are about to climb. Suggest doing this as don't expect any map, guide leaflet....nothing. Lots of guides offering their services but we were tired of haggling over everything and paying marked up tourist prices. The walk up is an hour maximum with great views and history all around. Don't miss the flat topped audience rock or cobra cave on the way down. The snake charmer is also worth the 500 rupees. A must see but if it was cheaper we would have 'shared the love' with the guides and shop owners on way out.
As for me nothing super special about the place. Nice rock paintings, nice view, super cool monkeys, but as for me not worth of 30 USD entrance tickets. Dambulla temple is much more interesting.

Sigiriya is a great site. The ground are well maintained, and the cave paintings are nice. However, at $35 it's way overpriced. There are a few plaques around explaining details, but not enough to really learn about the place. The museum is is a interesting building, but the displays are ordinary, poorly preserving the artifacts and many lights are out. And while the views are nice on a clear day, it seems the rock is often cloudy. I'm glad i did it. I would not do it again.

Lonely pLanet says this place opens at 8:30am but it actually opens at 7am, we arrived a little after 9 am and the place was very very busy already. By the time we got down again at around 11:30 the queues were starting to get silly. Its best to get there as early as possible. It is quiet a steep climb in some places but I think most people would manage it quite easily. I saw people who were American fat at the top so if you have a pair of legs you should be fine. There are pleanty of places on the way to take a little breather. Make sure you have water with you because once you enter the park there are no,places to buy it, atleast we did not see any. When you get the top there is a nice breeze to cool you down a bit, before enjoying the views of the surrounding area. Definately worth the climb and you can get an icecream when you get to the bottom.

I have so many words to describe this place! I will keep it short though: stunning, amazing and simple beautiful! a tip: start climbing before 7:30 to avoid tourists crowds and waiting for a long time on the way up! Its not that easy to go up but is definitely worth it! Watch gardens after the rock as there will be nearly no tourists!

I found that this place was extremely beautiful, the jungle surrounding it was dense and inhabited by many animal species, I even saw a wild elephant walking on a small road near the site. However the entry ticket for foreigners was unreasonably priced and far too expensive for the typical budget traveller

This is a must visit and well worth our 4.30am call time. Our driver picked us up at 5am, at our hotel. It is about a 2 hour drive from Kandy. We got there around 7am, just as the ticket office was opening. That's the tip, get there by 7am. So you miss the tourists crowd. We saw the crowd when we came down 2.5 hours later, and it was a lot of people, we were really glad we went early. The view on the top is great, but it is a bit of a climb, so whilst you don't have to be super fit, you need to be able to climb stairs for about an 1 hour with a few stops here and there. Bring water, wear covered shoes, shorts or pants is fine. It is not hot when you do a early morning climb, that's around 7am. But it got warm by 9am. It is December so we got caught in a bit of rain, but we came prepared with our umbrellas and windbreakers, check the weather before you go so you bring the right stuff. We didn't have a guide though others had. It is up to you. There is also a museum at the location which we didn't go to as we knew a bit of the history. The ticket for tourist is 4200 LKR. Definitely worth it, you must visit it. The view was beautiful.

The climb of the rock at Sigiriya is obviously the main attraction of this site. However, there is more to this World Heritage Site than just the summit. On our way down from the top we took a few detours to explore for example the 'Cobra Hood Cave' and the 'Boulder Gardens'. At the 'Octangle Pool' we were lucky enough to see a small Mugger Crocodile sunning itself on a rock. The forest around Sigiriya is very good for birdwatchers and we holds Fork-tailed Drongo-cuckoo, Indian Cuckoo, Orange-headed Thrush, Sri Lankan Green-pigeon, Sri Lankan Woodshrike, Jerdon's Nightjar and Jungle Owlet, mostly around the western and northern boundaries. We also saw Purple-faced Leaf-monkey and the ubiquitous Toque Macaque. Sigiriya is more than just a climb. It combines culture and nature beautifully.

Fantastic - the view is spectacular and the climb is very exhilarating (NOTE - if you're afraid of heights this might not be for you). Go to the museum second - we went to it first but it felt out of context without having seen the site.  Also the rock got crowded at the end...

Not the best sign posted place to visit but a must if you're in the area. The walk up to it gives some great views of the Lions Rocks and the old buildings which once sat around it. It as a warm but dry day when we walked up it and I wish we had more water with us (no places to buy food or water after leaving the payment/entrance). Before arriving we did get told about Asian bees attacking people but none of us saw even one (maybe it depends on time of the year and weather). The view from the top is breath taking I wouldn't like to say how many miles to can see but it's a lot! We didn't have to queue at any point which I'm glad because the walk ways aren't very wide.

We arrived at Sigiriya for 7.00 when the ticket office first opened and after wincing at the 4,200 SLR entry fee per person we enjoyed a shady cimb to the top which at this time of day was free from would-be guides and hawkers. By the time we were walking back through the gardens at 9.00 the crowds heading towards the rock were huge and we feel that if we'd been with them it would have been a less enjoyable experience. There is one small cafe within the grounds, near to the entrance gate, which appears to cater for local people. However,     if you're desperate for a bottled drink, yoghurt or samosa (and can ignore the army of ants) then it's worth trying. As we're keen walkers, we then walked through the grounds towards Pidurangala and scaled that too - a very different experience - we've done a separate review on it. Overall, climbing Sigiriya early in the morning was excellent but it is marred by the excessive entry fee. If you are fit and confident at scrambling over boulders at full stretch then pay 500 SLR and climb Pidurangala for stunning views of Sigiriya.

I am not ashamed to admit, I almost gave up after some 300 steps climb.. it is a very tough climb. But my tour guide made me believe in myself and with the encouragement of others in my group I made up to the top.. The feeling is awesome once u reach till the top. V made the climb on a day which was drizzling, so it was not to hot. But on a sunny day better to do this climb early in the morning, with plently of time in ur hand, so that u can take rest in the middle if needed.. it took me total 2hrs for both going up and coming down.. Wear proper shoes, sunglasses, cap/hat, plenty of water must.. dnt carry unnecessary items, which not required for the climb. Atlast the view at the top makes the climb worth it
Key Up early before the sun gets to work. It's a bit of a climb and not for the infirm. Nice views from the top.
We were here early morning, so not so many poeple and it was amazing. Step by step up to the lion rock. Unbelievable how people in past could built such a breathtaking place.

Quite amazed by the irrigation infrastructure which still exists till this day.  And of course, one will admire the Sigiriya Rock which served the Emperor well at that time as both his palace and fortress.

We got there just after 7am shortly after it opened its door. The climbing wasn't super easy as we thought but nothing to be concerned. You will enjoy panoramic view of Sigiriya as you are climbing up. It could get hot as you walk and at the top so get there early!

We couldn't get up to the top of the Rock as it was too dangerous due to heavy rain making access too slippery. I am sure the views would have been stunning. Another site which charges locals about £3.50 to enter and tourists £15. Does grate with me but suppose understandable due to the economic differences. Still worth the visit. Watch out for the mega-wasps at the top!!!

All the tourist sites that we visited are quoted in USD and this was the most expensive. We did not take a guide and found reading up on the site most helpful. You need 3-4 hours and it is a 60-90 minute climb. About 1200 steps to the top. Toilets at main entrance/exit only. Open 7am - 5.30pm, last entry at 5pm. Best time to climb is early morning or late afternoon. Not for you if you are afraid of heights, its a long, hot uphill climb, but it is safe. If you time it well you can watch the sun go down, but then you descend in the dark so take a headlamp and torch. You need a hat, sunblock, good walking shoes, water and do not take anything unnecessary as it is an uphill climb. You can do it at your leisure but in certain areas you will hold up the masses if you stop. Young and old, fit and unfit - I noticed everyone determined enough can get to the top. One of our group has a hip replacement and made it without training and a few rest stops on the way. The climb is worth the view, but it can get windy on the last section. You do need both hands (vertigo) however some children skipped up on there own and ran down the stairs...! It starts off with the long walk to the rock face from the car park, followed by narrow metal spiral staircases (which can make you a little "dizzy". The Sigiriya Frescoes painted over 1600 years ago are in a small sheltered depression 100 metres above the ground. Then a walk along the side of the rock face to a landing and the Lion's Staircase, situated half-way up Sigiriya Rock, the gatehouse which protected the entry to the Sky Palace on the summit where you can stop if you do not want to go any further. Followed by fire escape type staircases to the top, this can be daunting if you are afraid of heights (just do not look down). The view from the top is worth the climb, but remember you need to come down. The palace complex built by King Kasyapa in 480AD, 200 metres above the surrounding plains has wonderful panoramic views.The complex divides into three distinct sections: the Upper Palace area, occupying the high northwestern section; the Lower Palace area, occupying the lower northeastern part of the summit; and the Gardens to the south. The three sectors converged on a large rock-cut pool. A walkway paved with marble runs down the center of the complex. Limestone and quartz blocks were used for paving the stairways and passages throughout.

Come on Sri Lanka, haven't the tourists been ripped off enough. As usual the hefty price of $30 for tourists while locals play pennies. This is a very special must go place and it should be affordable for everyone not just tourists with money. This kind of charges takes away from the beautiful places. The Rock is awesome with stunning views, history and beauty. Beware of people who are waiting to help and then want money for th service. The climb is not as scary as it looks and good fun. Go early in the morning to avoid getting overheated and note that there is no drinks and eats available. The litter lets the place down a bit.

beautiful spot, well worth a visit. LOTS of hot steep climbing though, so not for all.We though it was very expensive, by far the most expensive thing we did in Sri Lanka. well maintained. Lots of people trying to sell you stuff, and wanting to be guides. You don't need one.
This is a must. You will feel liberated and in complete awe of this creation. Bring water. Lots of water. And cash, this is not free.

This Place is must visit for anybody traveling to Sri Lanka! Its fun to climb the steps and reach the top. Spectacular views from the top and is worth every step you climb. Do not rely on the cafe and restaurants nearby and do carry water, candies etc. while climbing. It s good to start early morning as later it gets very hot. Wear comfortable shoes while climbing as the steps are narrow. There are many hawkers selling wooden items while climbing. We were able to climb this place in 45-50 minutes. I would definitely recommend this place.

We climbed to the top and amazing view. good tip get there early or as we did stay the night before. You avoid all the masses that get bused in as we were coming back down he queue was very big.  Not much in the way of food around the area if staying though the restaurants that were there were very friendly. If you can climb the sister rock as this is a fraction of the price cost around £2.50 as the view were as stunning and when we went around 1pm and met three other couples....if you are not good a climbing rocks give a miss as you will not be able to scale the last bit to get on the top.

the most expensive and breathtaking 1200 steps of my life. we were not prepared for that but we did it, with a one year old baby an nothing for carry her. NEVER MORE. going up was ok, after the effort you really enjoy the fantastic view even if it's always windy and rainy. going down was a nightmare at the beginning, baby was crying like hell, amd moving like a fish in my arms (we were both wearing k-ways). i was afraid that she colud slip off so i was holding her so tight that probably i hurted her. when we reached the lions feet finally i relaxed and she fell asleep. than i could enjoy the way down to car park. don't go there with babies unless you have one of those baby backpack. don't accept the guide... useless... they will tell basic about king palace (which eventually is not evenn true) mirror wall and paintings . you can find those information wherever.

This is the first thing we did in Sri Lanka. We are a young couple and found the climb fairly easy. The view at the top was brilliant, we were lucky we had good weather. Definitely worth doing. We didn't bother with a guide, there are a lot of information plaques on the walk that tell you what you need to know. Entrance fee is $30 USD per person which isn't cheap but then that's about right for Sri Lanka.

It was a great experience. I visited Sigiriya almost after 24 years. This rock fortress is world famous and it gives great pride to explore its wonders. Mesmerizing sight and a wonder which has yet many secrets to be revealed. Pride of Sri Lanka

Awesome experience climbing this huge rock! A bit daunting if you are afraid of heights but it is very safe. The old remains at the top are so impressive given the height and difficulty getting to the top! And the gardens around the rock are pretty. A must do in Sri-Lanka!
Great view, we did not have the time to treck the rock but great sight and lots of history to read about it.
just train well to take steps then go there, be prepared well for the 1200 steps, but once your up there, you will forget all the steps you climbed :)

Great experience bar the strenuous climb up. Never quite made it to the top! The view and surroundings are extraordinary and well worth the trip. Even if you don't quite get to the summit - you can turn back after the galleries at the mid point - the on- site museum offers a good alternative on what you may have missed. The nearby Cafe is really miserable...a pity as it could be a nice place to rest.

It was a nice place to visit with lots of history behind it. The climb was safe and reasonable to manage. What left us a bit of sour experience was the so called "staff member" or "helpers". The helper we had came out of nowhere and decided to hold our hand when we were going upstairs. Our guide wasn't too helpful either (local guide at the mountain) and whispered under his breath after 5mins that we have to pay this "helper" at the end of the trip. We had to clarify exactly what the "helper" does. When we asked about price, he said to discuss it after the trip, this is very dangerous as I read in other reviews (after my trip) they can ask a ridiculous price. My partner was smart enough to ask the price when we realised what was happening. We initially decided not to use him, but felt sort of sorry for him, so asked him to carry a bit stuff for us and decided on $10 (he asked even more initially). He tried to gain our sympathy during the trip which was clearly with the intention to get more money. To put things into perspective, a tea picker in Sri Lanka work the entire day and gets paid about $4. We felt that $10 may not mean too much to us but may mean a lot to the lovely person in Sri Lanka that we have encountered so far. Next time we think we will be less polite and just say no. The $10 would be better off going to the kids we met than someone who try to rip tourists off.

This is worth visiting for the 2,000 year-old cave paintings alone, and the heart-stopping climb up the rusty iron staircase bolted to the outside of the rock to the ancient palace grounds on the summit is an ad entire unto itself... but really, the $42 CAD price tag compared to the peanuts locals pay really makes you feel like you've been robbed blind. Not sure why Sri Lanka is like this but either the tourism minister should be fired or the industry needs to re-set as I felt fleeced by "tourist prices" and rip-offs and scams everywhere I went.

Sri Lanka s 1st Kingdom is Anuradhapura . In 5th century AD patricide king Kashyapa scared to rule Sri Lanka from Anuradhapura because he scared about his brother who fled away to india . He realised that one day his brother will revenge him for the murder of his father . Therefore King Kashyapa decided to shift the kingdom to Sigiriya . Sigiriya is a castle which surrounded by water moat . It has Water Garden , Boulder Garden and Terraced Garden . You can see beautifully arranged royal palace on the top of the rock . Don't forget to see Frescoes and Mirror Wall . PLEASE BE CAREFUL FROM UNAUTHORISED GUIDES . THEY WILL COME TO HELP YOU IN FRIENDLY WAY BUT IN THE TOP OF THE ROCK THEY WILL ASK FOR UNFAIR AMOUNT OF MONEY . IF YOU WANT TO TAKE SERVICE OF GUIDES YOU CAN SEARCH IN " VIATOR " OR " WITH LOCALS" .

In our tour of Sri Lanka in early Dec 2015 we came across the maximum number of tourists at Sigiriya. As it is touted as a great attraction, we too followed the crowd to climb the steps to reach the top of the 200 metre high monolithic rock, hoping to see something of high archaeological value . The steps were narrow, 8 inches; so one does not get a proper foothold; often one had to climb sideways in order to get a proper foothold. At the age of 79 one found the climbing daunting and half way one was tempted to abandon. But the hope of seeing something unique and also the spirit of endurance kept us going. However, on reaching the top there was nothing to see except 360 degree view of the terrain from a height of 200 metres. The palace is all gone; no statues either ; only the foundation of the palace where the king who lived there two millennium ago. The climbing took one and a half hours and down trip one hour with intermittent rests. Those who attempt to climb should do so for the fun of climbing and not with the expectation of seeing anything of archaeological importance or otherwise.

If you're ok with climbing stairs on the outside of a rock then go and visit Sigiriya. We fortunately went when the heavens opened and as a result has the steps, frescos, & summit views all to ourselves ! I would recommend the way back down through the boulders on the left to eventually find the cobra rock.

This is site where you have to walk and climb the steps (nearly 900-1000) if you go to top.  This sight is having Ajant Ellora Style paintings.  You can have nice scenic view if you climb to the topmost point.

As a Sri lankan I was always ashamed for not been here. But Finally had the chance of being there. An excellent landscape. Sigiriya paintings and the view from the top was my favorites. But always you have to good enough to climb to the top. Don't forget to take some water, otherwise will suffer with dehydration. Drinking water provided in the site is not that good (Too much chlorine taste). But bit disappointing to see lot of local tour guides who were making bit of disturbance for the foreigners. There are lot of good hotels around where you can pick, so accommodation is not a problem

We went to Sri Lanka for our honeymoon and it was amazing. This is a small country with so much to see and do. Sigiriya was my favorite part of our two week stay in Sri Lanka. It is quite a climb but so worth it when you get to the top. Take plenty of water and snacks. Go early in morning when the sun is being blocked by the rock itself.

The heritage site is well maintained, but a long walk from the parking lot through the gardens (which weren't well maintained) but you could even see the snakes and their holes). The structure itself is worth climbing the stairs for but if you're expecting a lot of paintings at the top, then you'll be disappointed as there are only 3 or 4 on the walls. However views from the top are lovely.

This trek is very steep at times; in fact, so of the steepest part is at the highest altitude.  Glad my wife had a guide to steady her at times.  Some of paintings of the wasp-waist women halfway up were beautiful.  The ancient villa at the top was ok, but not as inspiring as the view.

Worth seeing but you can't help feel a little indignant about the price. With a guide it was about 4200 rupees each plus 3000 for guide. However amazing views (if good day) and interesting history. Easy climb, doable in 40mins, slower if lots of older wobbly kneed people ahead of you. Wouldn't go if you are going on a budget, much much better to go to Pindurangala Rock (much more fun, intrepid and 1/10 price)

The lions rock was one of my favorite place in Sri Lanka. It's pretty easy climb, around 1 hour. The views from there are really awesome. Only be careful of "guides". They will follow you and help you with climbing and wanting to take photos, and then asks a lot of money. Really dont need any guide, its very easy way to walk.
Although seems a high entrance fee a must see on your Sri Lanka travels A good idea to get ther by 8am to miss crowds A good 3-4 hour morning

we have been mainly to Dambulla and Kandy area, where we have visited fantastic temples, Buddhas, nature... highlights were: Sigiriya -lion rock, jeep safari in the jungle, ride on an elefant, elephant orphanage, cave temple, tea plantages. The roundtrip was organized by Samantha very well and our driver Keith drove us with his van (perfect view) from highlight to highlight. hotels were very good! we have even had a dinner at his home with his family

Used to be a rock climber but its been a long while since I last used my carabiners. So when came in front of sigiriya was taken back to memory lane for some time. A world UNESCO heritage site the history it laid out was nothing less than amazing. The history of the gardens, caves, the kings courtyard, the frescoes, the lion gate, the mirror wall were just enthralling. And our guide a very sweet guy called hemanta was always on hand to explain everything. He not only helped with the guidance but also helped us with the pictures. So do check him out when exploring sigiriya. When we reached the fortress at the top the archeological and the architectural significance were not the only things that one stopped in awe of. The view was astounding. I was at peace with nature. Sri Lanka truly is endowed with a calming natural beauty.

Walking through the gardens and across the moat towards the rock, you can see just how impressive this defensive fort and palace would have been in it’s time. The sheer rock face would have been hard to climb and there are even huge rockfalls balanced on pegs still in place to crush invaders. It took an hour to reach the top, mostly at a leisurely pace as visitors are forced into a single queue for most of the way. People with vertigo might have problems in some parts and bare in mind that once you join the queue, it’s not possible to turn back. Halfway up, there is a cave with some colourful frecoes and a “mirror” wall which has become less reflective over the centuries. After 1,200 steps, you reach the top and will be rewarded with a great panorama of the surrounding countryside. The only remains of the ancient palace are some low walls and pools but it would have looked impressive perched atop this magnificent rock. There are no means to get water or food until you come back down, so go prepared. A guide can be useful if you want all the details and stories but it’s perfectly possible without one as well. Some have said the fees are expensive but Sigiriya is clearly the most iconic site in the area and it would be sad to miss it.

the views, climb was spectacular from above, but the price you for that 30$ for foreigners is WAY too much for it. if you pay that much for something, you expect to have signs on the way up or down because there are several of them and sometimes you might get lost. and the area on the top is messy, dirty and things are just lying on the ground. if you pay 42x more than the locals, i could only say you got robbed + you pay for Tuk-Tuk some 4-5K to get around which is also surely overpriced like 2-3 times because they see they can easily get money from travelers and if you are there for one time, you will pay anyway. in country like Sri Lanka where a lot of things are REALLY cheap and you see hotels and other touristic places so overpriced it sickens you to ever go back there. even in Europe you don't pay 100 EUR for simple room in hotel...here you do, in country that is really cheap..had a feeling that everyone everywhere is gaining on this BIG time.
It's quite a marvellous climb... a little steep but much worth it. Lovely scenery and panoramic views from the top. Overlooks all the greenlands of Sigiriya.
It's a long climb up but worth all your trouble. The view from the top of the rock made me feel like a conqueror.

Pros: It's quite a long/challenging walk depending on your fitness, be sure to bring water. Fantastic rock formation and the view at the top is magnificent. Couple of monkeys are there :) Cons: A bit pricey! USD 30 for foreigners, LKR 100 for Locals.
It's best to go very early and to take plenty of water. But it's an extraordinary site with amazing views. Don't miss the beautiful frescoes on the way down

It is very expensive (30 $), but climbing the lion Rock is something you have to do when you are in Sri Lanka.  I’m very glad that I did it.  The frescoes halfway up and the view from the top are magnificent.  The steps and stairs are in excellent condition and have handrails and such to keep you from tumbling down. Just go as early as possible. You will be at the top before the crowds and the heat.  I was there at 7am when the ticket office opens, and had the way up to myself.  I had a rest and took pictures whenever I wanted to, without holding up other people.  Don’t forget to bring water with you.

We came from Colombo to Habarana specifically to visit Sigiriya. From Habarana we arranged a tuk-tuk to take us to Sigiriya, wait there for us (4 hours in total) and take us back - this cost us 2000LKR which we thought to be pretty fair as the wait time was so long. We did the climb at around 9:00am so it was already pretty busy, but as it was an overcast day we were told it wasn't as busy as it could be. The climb up Sigiriya itself is actually pretty easy. It took us about an hour to get to the top, but we stopped a lot to take photos and enjoy the view. The only major killer is how hot and humid it gets so make sure to take lots of water! On the climb there is a lot of interesting things to look out for such as the wall of mirrors, the lion paws and of course the view. At the top are the foundations of the ruins of the peak and we spent another hour walking around as well as sitting down and enjoying the sights. There are also quite a few monkeys running around the top! As part of your entry ticket you get to visit the museum which definitely warrants a visit (maybe even BEFORE the climb so you get a firmer idea of the history of the site). The only very annoying thing for me is that I am a resident of Sri Lanka and have a residency visa which allows me, usually, to get the local price rather than the tourist. The local price being only 50LKR (50c) compared to the foreigner price 4200LKR ($42AUD), I was very annoyed that they wouldn't accept it while everywhere else I've been to had. (Best times to do early morning 8:30 onward or late afternoon to avoid the massive crowds; bring lots of water; entry ticket 4200LKR per foreigner; tuk-tuks available in parking lot in case you need one.)

It's a walk, but so worth it. Carry your own water and do the climb slowly, the way up is as beautiful as the top. It was raining when we went and though that helped with the temperature the humidity was sky high. I also felt that the summer sun would have brought out the quartzite and feldspar in the rock face. I didn't take a guide up with me, and even though I went through the museum, I missed someone pointing out the sites to me. Main palace fine, but the details of layout, the bath area etc etc. Reading up on the place a bit more would have helped immensely.
A togh climb to the summit and not for the faint hearted, especially in the heat. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen!
Best go at 7 in the morning as the walk to the top is quite exhausing and the air in the morning is cool and refreshing Also there aren't too many others.

Despite a long, hot and sometimes scary climb up an uncountable number of stairs our family of four (children 9 and 12 years) agreed that this was one of the best experiences in Sri Lanka. A guide makes all the difference and ensure to bring plenty of water and comfortable shoes. They did not accept credit cards at our visit, only cash.

The place's USP is the view from atop. The citadel used to house the palace of the exiled king. The entrance to this attraction was by far the most expensive one. As part of the SAARC nation citizens, we were charged LKR 2100. For visitors from the rest of the world, the entrance fee was LKR 4200. Be prepared to climb a lot. There are steps leading all the way to the top, but this is not an easy climb given that the steps are very small in size.

The climb was quite easy and not as difficult as it looked. It was well worth the effort and the steep charges to experience the stunning views from the top. A tip for SAARC country tourist. Please carry your passport in original to get a discounted rate. Photocopy or any other form of identification wont do. Would suggest taking the services of a guide as it makes the entire experience more meaningful
One of the obvious must see and dos in Sri Lanka. Easy access unless you're handicapped. Not hard. Can be busy tho. Go early or when it's a bit rainy. Beware the monkeys at the top.
Stunning views from the top, well worth the climb.  No real need to pay for a guide - a visit to the museum first will provide all the information you need
Sigiriya is the places to live ind natura and adventure,, its made beautifully and architecture is 16 th century,  nice place

It was an amazing tourist site to visit.  It didn't have a touristy feel.  There was somethings tranquil about the place even with the large crowd visiting the place.  The view from the top, breathtaking and amazing.  The Lion rock itself is a work of art, not to talk about the man made art and structures built on it. You have to be prepared for a long walk up several steps, not for people with fear of heights please!!! Some vantage points are in fact frightening. The guide with my team and I was very good.  He was quite knowledgeable about the Rock and its history. His spoken English was impeccable and he also had a wiled sense of humour.
An amazing site to see, really impressive and a must visit if you are ever in Sri Lanka! Get's incredibly hot in the middle of the day so try and go up early or in the afternoon for the sunset

The walk up to the top is not as daunting as it sounds. However, if you can't make it early morning (7AM), then it can become very hot at the top. Just get the essentials... cap, sunscreen, water. The entry fee is different for locals, SAARC and other countries. We had our passports with us and had to pay less being from India. This applies to almost all paid entries in Sri Lanka. You can take the main steps while going up and skip the steps on the side which anyway you can visit while descending. We wasted a bit of time trying to explore everything at each level. There were people selling hand crafted merchandise on our way out. But they are pricey and targeted solely at tourists. But thankfully Sri Lankans are not as pestering unlike their Indian counterparts and left us at peace.
This is a beautiful place. The climb is not too difficult and the view from the summit is breathtaking. The entry fee is surprisingly high (4200 Rupees per person) but worthwhile nonetheless.

Sigiriya is beautiful place. Started the climb in the morning to avoid the heat but turned out to be a cool and rainy day. A king murdered his dad by plastering him in a wall..after that he fled to Sigiriya and made his fortress. . Back in the day the rock was made in a way where it would look like a white cloud and had reflecting mirror on the rocks and beautiful ponds and wildlife..later on this king committed suicide
Hike up only took us about 20 mins (not including the photo stops). Really amazing views, frescos and ruins. The area of sigiriya is worth the drive, but don't got to Kandy. The roads are crazy.

Sigiriya is beautiful and really interesting. One of the best sites we visited and the fact it wasn't primarily a religious site made a nice change. The museum is the best we have been to - well maintained, a wealth of information presented clearly - make sure to go if you visit sigiriya, we wnt before we climbed which made the site more interesting for us. The only issue is the price of the ticket which is quite high - 4200 rupees when we visited. Easy to reach by bus from Dambulla and a few local places to eat on the main road just outside the site.

Wow, what an amazing attraction. It is a hard walk to the top but well worth the effort. You definitely need a guide but try and steer clear of the guys who push and pull you and expect a tip. The history of the place is outstanding and when you take in that the work carried out to build 2 palaces over 7 years over 500 years ago is unbelievable. The wall paintings half way up the cliff face are truly amazing and the views from the summit are breathtaking. Probably needs some signs in place to warn older and unfit persons that this is indeed a strenuous walk.

There's actually very little to see except for the remaining frescos and the Lion Steps. Otherwise, it's just a long walk followed by a long climb. The palace remains are at the top and these are underwhelming mainly because there's nothing but the outlines of the buildings. The views from the top are impressive (that's pretty normal from 200m up right?). Definitely not worth the 4200LKR. Far better to climb the little rock at 500LKR, then you can at least get a birds eye view of everything on the big rock. The museum has a re-production of the fresco,, so you can see all the paintings in one view.

We hadorganized trip from Kandy to Sigiriya - some 2,5 hours by car with a bit annoying rush hour on the way back. Sirigiya itself is an rock you must climb in order to see a great view on the surrounding nature. Informations about the site you can find on the internet, and what you should know is that climbing up is a quite exausting - some 1.000 steep, sometimes narrow and slippery steps. On the second halfyou should be quiet because you don't want to awake hornets - one huge swarm started to fly all over me at the very top and it was quite scary. If it happens to you don't run, just stand still or go slowly to the cover until they fly away.

I climbed the rock now for the 4th time. In three occasions I took a guide. This I would recommend for all visitors. Climb early in the morning and be there at the entrance when they open at 7am. Take water with you and proper walking shoes (guides wear flip flops, but you won't be able to manage with that). The climb is nice, whether you go from the elephant or the cobra entrance. Take the staircase up to the famous paintings of the ladies and enjoy the view from the stairs to the country side. When you have reached the lion paws you are nearly there. Just a few steps on the metal stairs and then you made it ( don't forget the last two steps on the top of the rock - your guide will know) The view is amazing and the story behind all that is interesting. When you come down visit the museum as well and learn something more. A good guide will accompany you and explain further. Also you can't take pictures inside the museum it is worth visiting it.

No wonder it is nominates as the 8th wonder of the world. It is amazing how such a rock with difficult access was turned into a palace with beautiful water gardens, rock gardens, boulder gardens, frescoes, the mirror wall and fountains. Some of the water fountains are still functioning after nearly 1500 years .......
After a short climb you will discover an incredible view and an impressive place at the top of this huge rock.
This is a great location to visit, but everyone else thinks so to.  Get there really early before the bus loads of tourists arrive - and you will beat the heat also
Can't imagine visiting Sri Lanka without a visit to Sigiriya.  So glad I was able to visit and climb this incredibly historic and culturally important rock.

Possibly the one thing on my travels in Sri Lanka I HAD to do.  I was not disappointed.  Not a difficult climb compared to others in Sri Lanka but oh my the view from the top.  Wow!  This history of this fortress is mind blowing.
great experience. can be lots of tourists and is not cheap in terms of sri lanka money but if you visit sigiriya is a mu

We took 45 minutes to climb up. The view is wow. On reaching the top we had rain and fog, please take an umbrella or jacket. You can easily spend 45 mins on the top. We started climbing at around 08:00 and came down at abt 10:15 hrs. Better go early morning that in the afternoon.

We visited Sigiriya at about 10am to avoid the heat of the day - you need a ticket for the attraction which grants you access into the mirror wall, museum and another cave. The walk is quite tiring but more than anything on a couple of stretches you're on a metal staircase adjacent to the rock which can be quite unnerving if you're not good with heights. Some locals wait on these stairs and offer you help up for a fee of course. One guy helped me up just by holding my hand which actually did calm me a little, he demanded 1000rupees which was just ridiculous but once I was up there I was so out of breath and exhausted I gave in because I couldn't find anything smaller!! The views from the top are truly incredible it is the most beautiful place I have seen and massive once you're up there. It is totally worth the stress of getting up (and you can see ancient cave paintings on the way up if you're prepared to queue within a caged in staircase). I could have looked at that view all day, a lake, paddy fields, forest/jungle, mountains Incredible

Although this isn't quite "off the beaten track", I had an incredible experience climbing to the top of Lions Rock and would recommend it! The view is incredible from the top and the climb up is exhilarating.
Very impressive to visit but unfortunately way too expensive (4200 rupees p.P.!)... Besides the historical aspect the site offers nice view over the surrounding area as well.

t is a vast archeological site build on the center of a huge rock. Take plenty of water because it's a hard climb and no where to get water on the way up. Also beware if you have any food especially fruit, the monkeys can get very aggressive and will attackThis place is simply amazing it's a must visit when you go to Sri Lanka! I'm not an athletic person but i enjoyed every bit of my climb all the way to the top to be blown away with the incredible view and refreshing wind from up there!amazing and wonderful place. sri lanka has a great history and this is an evident for thatThe craftsmanship still visible in the remains of the former entertainment areas is impressive, even to this day.It was packed but still a great experience in the gardens and on top of the rock.best thing is to go as early as possible. the view is amazing. we had loads of fun there.Amazing world heritage site.

The title of this review says it all. As early as possible. Depending on your fitness level you may end up spending a lot of time waiting to climb the stairs behind people who have bitten off more than they can chew. It is a decent amount of stairs on a hot day. All part of the experience though. The view from the top is amazing, and completely worth it in my opinion. The 4000rupee (37CAD/27USD/26EUR) entry fee for tourists is absolutely absurd though considering what you really get for that and that locals get in for free.

You will be constantly hassled by young men helpers, many will block the steps, will walk beside you grabbing your arm, and are a nuisance and hindrance.Do NOT pay them off, it redoubles their attention. Shout "no" loudly!
The obvious place to see in Sri Lanka but it's well worth the climb, not just for the views but the refined frescoes. No problems with hornets when we were there.

Not an easy climb for someone suffering from vertigo but worth it in the end.  No problems with the hornets .  I loved looking at the other rocks around and their carvings, the top was slightly reminiscent of some S.American temples.  To think that people had to climb up and down the rock to serve the king and its court who I guess didn't ;-) . T he mind boggles!

This is complicated to review, as the history of the site is fascinating, the view at the top lovely, but it requires a lot of stamina and patience with humanity and the pushy people trying to "help" you up the stairs, annoyingly. I found that the ruins on the top of the rock were mostly underwhelming, but the rock paintings were worth seeing in person. Be sure to bring plenty of water for the climb, you will need it. We got a reasonably early start but as everyone states, the earlier the better, both for the heat and the crowds. While expensive by Sri Lankan standards, at $28 or so the entrance fee seems fair for the maintenance and continuing restoration of this World Heritage Site.

This is a spectacular place to visit, but not for the disabled. I knew that I would not be able to do the climb but wanted to experience what I could. The museum was interesting and easily accessible, as were much of the lower area. Well worth a visit and you can share others photos online of the higher reaches.

When first seen it seems climbing to the top must require rock climbing skills but in fact a series of stone steps and metal stairways means anyone with a reasonable level of fitness can do it. There are well preserved rock paintings to enjoy and some vertiginous sections also so beware if you don't have a head for heights. The view from the top is spectacular.

I booked this for me and my husband and then read some of the reviews and freaked out, I'm not good with heights or metal see-through staircases. We started the climb around 730am and it was a lovely morning. Not many people. I got part way up and the wind was blowing a gale, I told my husband to carry on and said I'd wait.  As I stood there an old man came by, said my husband would exit around the corner and grabbed my arm and we edged around the rock. We got to the foot of the metal staircase and after another freeze, my husband came down. I was persuaded to carry on. The stairs aren't hard from a fitness perspective, for me it's the height. Anyway I did it and so happy. Well worth the tears!  We did not go on the spiral stairs. Encountered no hornets or monkeys!   Did see one dog, one crocodile and lots of lizards.
The sigriya heritage site is over 4000 lkr and definitely not worth the steep price. After all you have to climb the rock yourself. I recommend coming the other rock which is only 500lkr
Whilst the fort and the rock climb is amazing the price is not. Over $30 entrance for foreigners (90%) higher than for locals  and you climb the rock yourself.

Pricey and check the exchange rate when you pay, was cheaper for us to pay in LKR than USD.  Get there for when the gates open and you'll miss the bus loads of crowds that clog the stairs later in the day.  Take plenty of water since it's twice the price here, nearly 200LKR.  People will offer to help you up the stairs and then ask for 500LKR when you get to the top, repeatedly tell them no thankyou as they can be pushy. Amazing views.

1K + steps to climb to reach top. The view from top is worth it. Nice natural paintings on the way. my 3 yrs old kid loved going on steps & felt sense of achievement when he reached on top. Discount on entry fee for citizens from SAARC countries so carry your passport if applicable. Nice juice centre on exit.

I personally feel that the entry fees for foreigners can be priced lower. However it is one of the best heritage site to visit in SL which combines little bit of all..sheer size, historical importance, cultural heritage, physical activity of climbing a vertical rock, a magnificent view of the surrounding landscape from the summit,  etc.

Even my friend's sister who is 70 years old made it to the top. But keep your voice down on certain part of the climb...It might disturb the hornets along the side of the Rock.. Especially, the Chinese tourist from CHINA.They are loud. So tell them to shut up or speak softly.
Only problem is that you will be itching to get up the Rock and by the time you come down all you will want to do is collapse and drink about 5 ltrs of water.

However only one of several in the cultural triangle.  Definitely the most arduous.  On the day we went to the Rock I was the very 1st tourist through the admission gate - I was not the 1st to ascend the summit.  You'll find it much easier and quicker coming down largely due to the way up leading through the mirror wall and the frescoes.  Once on top of the rock the views are truly breathtaking and you can see very clearly the beautiful grounds you walked through some hours earlier a 7 am.
This was my first stop..... climbing all the way up while learning the history of this palace was amazing.
Dont forget to bring water (bottle) and wear a pair comfort shoes, you will pass a thousands steps in this place, and from the top you will see a nice place and the view is amazing from there.

I rate this as excellent because it is amazing, esp if you make it to the top of the lion rock. The views are amazing. It is quite  a climb and we went during the afternoon (not a good idea). I would suggest go early morning or evening when the sun is not as hot, it ll make the climb easier. There are 1200 steps I think. However, I was not happy with the Rs. 4,200 entrance fee. I think it was more worth it if it was half the price. Anyways, it was still one of those, you should visit once in a lifetime things.

Beginning from the landscaped gardens and water tanks you ascend slowly towards the gigantic and impressive boulder that is Lion's Rock. The most important tips for climbing towards the top according to me are: 1. Timing: Make sure you go as early as you can (tickets are available from around 7.30am). Otherwise you will end up sweating and losing energy in the sweltering heat during the steep climb 2. Clothing: Wear comfortable and loose clothing like sweatpants and t-shirts that absorb sweat and keep you cool 3. Water: There are no shops or posts anywhere on the climb and once you reach the top you will have to partake of a few drops from a questionable tank with a tap. So carrying a small bottle of liquids to quench your thirst is highly recommended 4. Take time to enjoy the stops: There are some places to rest at during regular intervals in the climb and enjoying the view from each of these helps to catch your breath and carry on Overall, if you are lucky to visit at a time when the hornets are not disturbed at the rock, then you can ascend at your pace and once you reach the top, the view is simply brilliant. The paintings on the mountainside are gorgeous and intricately detailed. It is definitely a MUST to visit this place and behold the majesty that is Lion's Rock.
A must see citadel. The history of it is amazing and the entire construction of the site is unbelievable.

It is definitely worth climbing the 1200 steps to the top of Sigiriya both for the exercise as well as for the incredible view of the grounds from above.  Sigiriya is a must see if you are in the Dambulla area as it is from approximately 477 to 495 AD and was built by King Kassapa I as a rock fortress city.  By all accounts it is one of the oldest and best preserved ruins in the area.  It is quite spectacular.
a valuable historical place to visit. public transportation's are available. very beautiful and elegant place in sri lanka.

Highlight of the visit so far the Lion Rock is amazing. Spectacular views all the way up to top, don't give up, you will find the summit views truly wonderful and there is an amazing swimming pool. Word or warning don't get help with the climb from any of the many locals that are all along the path/route, they are not doing it out of kindness, they will want paying.

It is a shame that Sigiriya is not a world wonder yet, it surely is one. The amazing huge rock with fascinating shapes and colours is enough of an attraction but to visit the remains of a kingdom on the top and see the beautiful paintings on the walls is next to unbelievable. The breathtaking view from the top is a must see - we had never seen so much green, it is a vast area of forests! Compliments for maintaining the site too, the climbing constructions are excellent and the site is very well kept. Beautiful!
It's hard work but the murals on the way up and the view from the top is worth it!! Take time to explore the rock formations.

This is a must do in Sri Lanka.....the climb is not difficult at all, roughly around 1200 steps. It gets a little steep after the Lion's paw - i.e. the entrance to the ancient palace ruins, which is roughly after a 40 minute climb but not at all dangerous. Start climbing as early as 7:00 a.m or a little later after this so as to beat the heat. The climb will roughly take 2 hours. It is not a difficult climb for elderly people who are healthy and children after age 6. If you are a SAARC country member, you get a discount of USD 15 per passport. If you are traveling as a family / group, you need to carry the individual passports for discounts, not copies - original passport otherwise you will not get the discount. Wear comfortable clothes and a good sturdy pair of shoes, don't carry anything expensive loosely since there is a chance of it falling off during the climb especially after the Lion's Paw stretch. Carry a bottle of water, a small towel and wear a hat / cap. View from the top is breath-taking!!! and simply beautiful. Guide is not required if you do your research.....The climb is not very tiring if you are fit and exercise regularly. There is nothing spectacular on top except for the view since there are hardly any ruins left over to see. There are some ruins on the way which is very interesting. There are many monkeys around and they are pretty fearless, so take care of your belongings....the monkey's don't attack though, they are just on the lookout for food. Wasps were not at all an issue since we did not encounter any.

Expensive entry - so be sure you can do the climb as it is worth it! In some of the parts of the climb, you will near a good head for heights as you feel quite exposed.  Go early in the morning as the climb is tough and it's very hot.

This was the best historic site we saw in Sri Lanka and what of best around the world. The ancient complex is huge. You can spot lot's of monkeys. We went there early in the morning and it was really hot. So don't do it in the middle of the day becouse heat will kill you:) Bring water and snack for about 2h.
One amazing experience, worth every step, with a stunning landscape, and very special energy. Worth the trip.
Truly unique and special place, stairs and stairs until the top, worth every step, not just because the amazing view, also because of the journey, should be in everybody's bucket list.
The entrance fee is overpriced compared with the other sights in Sri Lanka. But the view is breathtaking. It is worth asking the helpers, how much they charge to avoid misunderstanding later.

An anazing historical site with beautful gardens and ancient pools. A long climb to the top of the Mountain. Watch out for slippery steps. I stopped at the Lions Paw plateau which was a great area for relaxing and enjoying the spectacular view.
These is an wonderful place where we have to climb 1,200 steps to reach the top of the rock. Amazing view while climbing. Overall a must visit place.

To start off with , SAARC country members get a 50 % discount. Amazing climb and what a sight once up there.  Do not miss the museum to the left of the ticket counter. It's a replica of what lies ahead . Stay away from Guides. Food etc is not available up there , so be prepared and carry enough liquid. Also no washroom up there .. Great place for Photography ....and yes post the sightseeing , we havd great lunch of rice and curry at a very reasonable priced restaurant,  to the the right on the main road. ( wijaisiri family restaurant ) Nonveg also available

Climb the 1,200 steps leading you to the top of the rock is exciting. I recommend the experience. Some will rise faster than others but the ascension is possible for almost all types of people. The views from the top are spectacular. The best place in Sri Lanka for nature lovers.

It was amazing experience i had. Prepare to bring face towel n drink because it will make u thirst and sweat when climb the rocks. There were lots of dogs there but dont worry they are keepers.it wont disturb u except there were also monkeys and dont show foods or plastics or else it will approach u. I went there frm kandy. U can take bus no 41 or 42 to dambulla. It takes abt 2 hrs to reach dambulla. Bus fare abt 94 rupee.frm there just wait another bus to sigiriy which takes abt 1 hr to reach sigiriya. Bus fare is 32 rupee..the bus only come every 1 hr so be patient. Or u can take tuk tuk 2000 rupee. Last bus to dambulla is 7pm. But u must govack before 6pm because after 6pm is getting dark. Also bring rait.coat.or.umbrella it will get.rainy easily. The view was amazing and u can see buddha srstue frm for and mountainous view. Entrance fee is 4200 rupee which i think too expensive. Toilet is clean and there also has first aid house. The restaurant serve nice milk tea but bit dirty and food is cold.
I would not go again. 4200 rupees for one adult is ridiculous. Nice view but there's not much ruins left...

This is one experience that you shouldn't miss in Sri Lanka. The climb seems difficult but it is not! To understand it better, I'm a BMI30 person who works out an average of 50 minutes everyday and I was able to climb it with ease along with my 7kg dslr bag! I saw several elderly people climbing the rock using their walking canes. I even saw one person climb wearing 3" wedges! Having said that, please be aware that if you have a severe knee problem, you'd be better off not climbing it as the steps are too narrow and going down could prove to be very painful. If you have a heart condition, you should try the climb at your own risk since there is no provisions for medical emergencies. The view from the top is brilliant. You can see the entire area around you, which is lush green and brilliant. You can easily spend an hour up there marvelling at the landscape. Recommendations -bottle of water....or two -hat, sunscreen, some food (sometimes you have to wait in line to get to the cave paintings, so it might take longer even if you are a fast climber) -go early in the morning as the late morning sun can be really harsh. I was drenched by the time I reached the top -beware of the wasps! I almost walked into one which was hovering about at the top -careful of the monkeys! -respect nature. Please bring down all your trash with you -if you're a SAARC nation passport holder, you pay Rs.2100 (U$15) instead of Rs.4200

The entrance fee is overpriced for foreigners (4000Rs against 500Rs for locals!). The property is not handled with care (garbage everywhere, a lot of dogs, people running on walls,…).  And if the entrance fee isn’t expensive enough, you also need to be prepared to fight off “guides” that want to charge you a lot of money (around 2000 rupees!) for helping you up and telling you information that you don’t know if it’s accurate or true to actual history. I found the site itself very interesting. I’m still impressed by how people of that time could achieve what they build on this rock! It’s amazing. The climb to the top is very intensive but totally worth the effort!  On your way to the top, you have to walk on a narrow spiral iron staircase to see the beautiful frescoes. After you pass the lion paws, you need to walk on a small iron stair that’s attaches to the rock. This stair, sometimes gives me a scary feeling but when you’re at the top you have amazing views around the rock and you see the ruin of the palace. The view to the garden is wonderful. TIP: go up early. In the early morning, there are not many people so you don’t have traffic jams of people on the stairs. Take a bottle of water with you.

Truly a wonderful site, built in 447AD it amazes you at the sheer scale. Swimming pools, lots of them, as symmetrical as if built today, are part of the winter and summer palaces - a must see. The steps are steep and in places a bit vertigo inducing. Not possible for those with mobility difficulties. Visit early to avoid the heat. Local guides available but use registered ones at site.
One of top thing to do in Sigiriya. It was amazing. It is a good exercise also. I s better if you can get a guide for there. Then you can learn lot of things about there.

The Srigriya Fortress is a place not to be missed. It is not for the fainthearted as you have to climb 2000+ steps to reach the top. However the effort is worth what you get. That such a construction could have been done in the ancient times is mind bogling. A fortress on the top of a sheer rock with palaces and gardens laid out. Swimming pools and Baths for the royalty! In it's hey days it must have been one of the wonders of the world. The view from the top is breathtaking.The layout of the gardens, moats, ponds, halls etc on the way are also beautiful. You can see for miles around. And the icing on the cake being the beautiful paintings that are similar to Ajanta in artistry and antiquity. A place not to be missed. However please carry an umbrella with you for the rain or the sun, We were caught in a heavy downpour with no protection. However we trudged on getting drenched but have no regrets. Also carry some water and light refreshments as nothing is available once you cross the gates.

This rock is just beautiful. Is a little bit hard to get to the top in this heat so at entrance buy water and if you are smart enough go early in the morning. Because after 9-10 in the morning there are so many tourists and the whole.experience can turn in something not so positive. Check for the guide because its a good thing to have one. Some guides have licence some are just young boys who cant tell you alot and you will just waste rupees.

It's mostly about nature and culture, so may not seem very exciting for everyone, however I liked it. Just one thing is that water should be bought before you enter the site!!!!!! It was burning hot and no single water stall... It's a bit tiring journey but worthy to go. Monkeys there are really naughty but easy to photograph))

Went very early in morning with a guide who explained all the heritage and sites as we went. we climbed to the very top, was a little hazy but the view was still amazing. The vast area of the site starts out with a beautiful and impressive park area with water installations all around. The craftsmanship still visible in the remains of the former entertainment areas is impressive, even to this day. The property is very well maintained and inviting. The actual climb, first to the wall paintings half way up the rock and then all the way up to the top of the rock, is not for the faint hearted. A total of 1830 steps are to be overcome, all the way up and then again all the way down. While the initial stone steps are easy to maneouvre (provided you have the basic fitness to do so), the metal staircase up to the wall paintings is rather tricky. A narrow winding staircase busy with pilgrims leading up to a metal platform and into the cave - but it is worth it as the paintings are strikingly beautiful and sensual in its appearance. Hard to believe that we are looking at art work thousands of years old! Back on the intermediate platform, the steps up to the next platform are easy and solid stone. The last flight of steps up to the final platform are a challenge for all those with vertigo! Free swinging metal steps built along the vertical rock surface! All the way up you will find more ruins of former palace and outbuildings. The views from up there are impressive, but could also be had from other sites in the area. Please be aware of young men offering their help to you on the way up the first flight of stairs. They will want money for their help and are, unfortunately, very persistent. Please ask your guide for help if you cannot rid yourself of their unwarranted assistance. The place is very busy at any time of the year. A good time to visit is early in the morning or late afternoon.

Sigiriya Rock has its charm. Standing all alone surrounded by greenery , it seems to beckon one towards it. One first crosses the moat which runs around the rock and then comes to the sprawling garden which consists of ruins from bygone days.
