Mornings & evenings are recommended for climbing Sigiriya. Sigiriya This is a UNESCO world heritage site & also known as the eighth wonder of the world. The rock in another way is a palace and a museum of arts, culture, royalty and architecture. The unique town planning and irrigation system still remain a mystery even to the modern technologists. It will take about 2 1/2 hours for you to get on to the top. As the temperature goes high by the noon the suitable clothing is recommended. According to the ancient chronicles, this site was once the capital of King Kashyapa (477 – 495 AD). Some say that the great king Ravana was the one to convert this rock in to a palace and the story goes on as there is a hidden chamber of Ravana inside the rock which can be accessed only by the original possessor of it.

It is the most valuable heritage site of Sri Lanka. If you are a foreigner visiting this site you must have a good guide to explain this to you. I highly recommend you first having a look at the Museum and then climbing the rock because the Museum has a lot of information regarding the kingdom presented attractively - which will truly amaze you. Clothes to wear; Wear something comfortable because you have to climb 1200 steps to reach to the top. Most stairs are slippery and small in size - So avoid wearing skirts of large shoes when travelling. Best time to climb; Mornings are ideal for rock climbing as otherwise the rock gets heaty and you will easily get tired. Climbing; There are several entrances you can reach to the top. You won't get lost but will definitely get tired. It is the best if you can relax at places - and climb taking your own time. Also, there could be times you experience heavy winds - at that time take care of your kids and team or family because the wind is heavy as it can push you. Time taken; Most probably 1 and 1/2 hours or more to climb without any pain or strain. Age; Eventhough age is not limited. Be careful when taking older parents and kids to the top. Be a good traveler! -  It is indeed the most precious site for Sri Lankans, do not use camera flashes when exploring the paintings at caves. Avoid sitting on the rock walls as they decay if you step or sit on them. Enjoy the marvel of the Indian ocean - be safe!

Sigiriya and Habarana I had the opportunity of visiting Sigiriya few days back after my last visit two years back. May be, it is time to make few comment about the new development around the location, night stop if needed and few areas which need to be concentrated, specially for a first timer who I interested to climb the great rock fortress or you could call it  the “kingdom on a rock”. The history runs back to the 2nd century where the base of the rock and its surrounding caves had been used as monasteries by monks. During the 467AD, Kind Kassapa had taken over power forcefully from his father, where the controversies between his brothers as well as clergy, had compelled him to shift his palace to a more secure place. This is where the rock castle comes in to the scene, where the king had stated to build his empire, the castle over the Sigiriya rock. Kind Kassapa had reigned for a period of 18 years, up to 495 AD and during this period he had build this amazing castle along with an inner and an outer city with two ramparts, baring unauthorized entry in to his rookie kingdom. Before ascending the rock to reach the summit, one has to pass three beautiful gardens called water garden, terrace garden and boulder garden. There had been over 200 ponds full or water where, around 90 ponds are still full of water during the rainy season. The supply of water to some of the ponds from the nearby Sigiriya tank which is few kilometers away is an engineering marvel, compared to the facilities, technology and knowledge which were available at that time. The ascend commence from the great lion’s paws, where you have to first watch the world famous Sigiri frescoes. There are 18 to 21 frescoes to watch and thereafter you will have to go through the mirror wall to reach the lion’s paws. The mirror wall, which had been contracted in-between 467 and 495AD had been so reflective and polished that, the king’s image had been clearly observed on it. It had been used to write graffiti from those days. When the ascend begins” you need to be careful for a hornet’s hives attached to the edge of the rock face as there are large hornets hives by the side of the rock. By any change if an attach originate, you need to be motionless. The best time to start the climb is soon after 07.30 am where the sun is still not strongly set. When the sun is up, the rock get warmer and the temperature will increase. As there are a lots of thing to observe on top of the summit such as the palace foundation and ponds within an area of approximately 3.5 acres of land you need to carefully move from one to another location. Also it is assumed that water had been pumped to the palace as well as for ponds through wind power or wind mill technology. Also it is assumed that there would have been an elevator through the large lion’s stature to a point where king had reached this point and carried by his men to the summit. The engineering marvel used of all these is amazing and unimaginable. While descending, there are many places such as caves, terrace garden, the conference hall and the octagonal pond to watch. It would be a wise thing to tell your guide to take you through all the above areas before reaching the car park. Now that you have completed you tour of Sigiriya, it would be beneficial to take a tour to Minneriya and /Kaudulla national parks to watch elephants. From Sigiiya it is only about 15 minutes drive to Habarana. There are plenty of places to have a night stop in Habarana to fit your budget such as tree houses, Home stay, guest houses and luxury hotels with air conditioned comfort, where you can complete a safari and stay the night in Habarana to start you journey in the following morning. It is also to be noted that the temperature may rise up to 35 degrees centigrade where it may be unbearable for some of you who are coming from colder climates. Habarana I o central that if you need to proceed to Trincomale or the historic city of Pollonnaruwa, it would be ideal to have a night top and commence your trip the following morning  from this location after doing a safari to watch elephants and birds.
Good to go in the morning to avoid the scorching sun. We have a good walk and enjoy the magnificent place. Be prepared to perspire and wear a good pairs of walking shoes. We took lots of photos

As Sri Lanka's wonder of the world, Sigiriya is definitely worth a visit. The walk up is for the reasonably fit and choosing either the morning or later in the afternoon is probably best as you are out in the sun. There is a cave with engravings around half way up and then two thirds up a place to stop and rest before reaching the top. There are a few trees where you can get some rest from the sun. Take plenty of water and possibly some food for energy, although watch the monkeys as they will steal it. The views from the top and the remaining layout are quite something.

I have been to Sri Lanka twice previously and never visited sigiriya, but boy do I regret that now. The towering rock is beautiful at its base as well as on its peak. The only improvement may be more guards that spoke English to explain historical elements.

I suppose it just happens to be one of those places you have to visit when you travel to Sri Lanka. We ended up getting dropped off by our tour guide then made the trek up the stairs. The whole process took almost three hours primarily because of the mandatory trip next to the "mirror wall" and the quick jaunt through the cave paintings. The mirror wall was pretty disappointing and obviously had not been polished in some time. Perhaps a better name would just be "a wall." The best thing to do here is take a left and avoid the trip to the cave paintings and go straight to the top. It will save you an hour and a half of waiting around with your 20,000 closest friends and let you get on with the rest of your trip.

We were keen to visit this attraction on our recent trip to Sri Lanka however as you are approaching it, it looks as though it would be impossible to climb to the top. As you get closer the natural and then metal steps become more obvious. We had a Sri Lankan with us who was telling us the history and pointing out things such as the mistakes on the frescoes which was interesting and gave us an excuse for a breather! He also pointed out the wild monkeys and iguanas nearer the bottom. Although we are quite keen walkers we found this quite strenuous, especially in the heat of the day. Sensible shoes and plenty of water are essential. Once at the top the views all around are spectacular, although there is limited evidence of the kingdom which once existed there.
We went in the morning, you walk up in the shadow stay on top in the sun with an amazing view. Well kept heritage, beautiful!!

The term World Heritage site is enough to make you visit there. The place is really good and involves a climb to the top (approx 1200 steps) the views are spell bound and worth the climb definitely. Its something that will make you have fun.
I would like to say the place is really amazing and that one should definitely visit it once in Srilanka. The place is marked with great beauty. The scenes are amazing and worth taking pictures.
What seemed like a daunting task turned out to be a challenging climb up to the top of the rock. Breath-taking views.

The highlight of our tour!  You need to buy tickets to enter which are more prices for foreigners than locals.  Take plenty of water because it's a hard climb and no where to get water on the way up.  Also beware if you have any food especially fruit, the monkeys can get very aggressive and will attack if they smell it.  The views from the top are truly amazing, well worth the climb!  It can be a bit nerve racking as the steps higher up are quite open and metal with metal railings so you can see how high you are climbing.  There is also the museum to wander around and the beautiful grounds.  There is another beautiful rock to climb not so far away but we only found out on the day we left, it is not advertised as it's free and not commercialised but has awesome views too!
Go in the morning when there's less crowd and less sunny. Its an okay place to see. Although the climb to the rock is very energising. Very good for fitness freaks.

Climbed up the rock from early in the morning to avoid climbing in the heat of the midday sun. It takes a good couple of hours but the view from the top is amazing. I'd recommend using a local guide as the history is interesting but do make sure you take plenty of water to drink - you'll need it! Don't miss the wall carvings on the way up. Glad I've done it but wouldn't attempt it again - been there got the tee shirt!

Yes its costs a lot. But the paintings and lion feet are quite spectacular, the views are great, and its got a great history. Even if you are going to climb Pidurangala Rock I would still say this was worth it despite the price. You are only there once, and you can always make more money.
Long moats and some nice scenery to stroll or pedal around. It's something worth doing after the main site, or while cycling to Pidurangala Rock.
You must visit ones you are in Sri Lanka this is one of the best landmark in Sri lanka.It's a wonderful creation.

The splendour of this site is beyond description. Truly amazing. A place one must visit. Have a guide because the history is an incredible tale, and the magnificent view from the top will leave you breathless as might the climb to the top. Don't miss!

Sigiriya Lion Rock citadel, also called Simha-giri (Sinhala: Lion Mountain) built by King Kasyapa (Kassapa) (479-497 A.D), grand nephew of Buddhist scholar monk illustrious Thera Mahanama, the first of the authors of Mahawamsa the great historical chronicle of Sri Lanka, is a fortified-walled and moated-royal city with living manifestations of glorious Sinhalese civilization: it's a unique combination of 5th century urban planning, architecture, engineering, hydraulic engineering, garden landscape designing, sculpture, art, painting and poetry.Sigiriya,a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is of immense archeological significance: it is one of the best preserved and most elaborate surviving urban sites in the South Asia from the first millennium A.D.

You can use any part of it that you like. Shafith has been a wonderful guide for our two trips to Sri Lanka.He is very knowledgeable and considerate, going out of his way to make sure we had a good experience.We toured the ancient cities of Anuradhapura and Pollonaruwa, were astounded by the art in the Dambulla caves, climbed to the top of Sigiria and Mihintali, and saw the amazing elephant parade at the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy. Last year we enjoyed a new experience, an exciting tour of the wild animal park. If you are interested in any site shafith is an expert. You can see the living Bodhi Tree, brought from India by King Asoka's daughter just 200 years after the Buddha's death, the Aluvihara rock caves where the Pali canon was first written down on palm leaves, the huge stone trough used to feed the monks at Anuradhapura, many huge stupas and ancient Buddha statues, the original Abayaghiri Monastery, and many other heart-warming Buddhist historical sites. Shafith is a great guide and trust worthy companion for anyone's trip to the beautiful  country of Sri Lanka. Jenny berri USA thecloth@usa.com
We spent 9 days in Sri Lanka and this was definitely one of the best sites. I recommend you get a local guide because the history of the place is really fascinating.

visiting the palace grounds and climbing to the top of the rock where kings palace was situated. the way up is beautiful. very very hard climb ...not suitable for handicaps. 1322 stairs  if i remember correctly. watch out - on the way you will have srilankan young guys try to assist you with the climb. if you allow them to do so you are oblged to pay them for this service. unfortunately we found out that they request alot more than what you were thinking to give. if you want to use their hlp make sure you finalize price upfront

well me and my friends visited Sigiria by a van. it costs us 15 dollars per person because our country is a south asian country. so if you belong to a south asian country you are lucky. my advice is take plenty of water, and some short eats since it took us about one and half hour to reach the top. best thing is to go as early as possible. the view is amazing. we had loads of fun there.    it was just one day we didnt stay nearby we came back to colombo the same day.

The Lion's Rock, Sigiriya, is an imposing rock outcrop rising 200m. About 1500 years ago, a king turned it into his royal domain. This in itself defies my imagination: how a palace with swimming pool, water systems etc could be built up there is mind-boggling -- or was it all say-so? I had to see! The stepped climb was -- for me personally -- challenging but I am so very glad I made it to the top to see the relics, the panorama and the fresco cave paintings midway. A couple of warnings. Some locals will doggedly follow and offer you a 'hand up' steep steps. If you accept their help, they'll expect payment and follow you to the top. Also the 'first' landing is only that -- the first landing! It's not the top!!

The ascent is quite steep, but worth it. En route to the top are some amazing,quite amusing, wall paintings. Also the lion entrance, but be careful of the hornets. At the top are the atmospheric remains of the ancient citadel, with superb views all around. Great for photos. Take a small bottle of water and some form of head cover. Avoid"guides" at various points who offer to help you up the path by holding your arm then ask for money. Be polite but firm.
Climb high from land to see top of the rack but nothing there. When I walk through the highest point make me feel a bit scare cos its so high!!!! On top have plane land and big pool.

it is recognised by the UNESCO as the 8th wonder of the world, it is truly a wonder that should be seen. it is a heavy climb but very doable as you can have rest and take pictures from time to time. from the above you can see almost the whole country and the Buddha status, get some water before you start the climb, you'll certainly need it and you may not find it in the top. mind your steps as the stairs sometimes are so small and slippy good luck

The rock is amazing, the climb can be pretty scary, rusty scaffolding up the outside of the rock but do climb it. Go and look at the fresco's and the oldest mirror on record. When you finally reach the top you are stunned into silence, the King's chair, the pools and the view and amazing. The cost isn't cheap but if you are only going to Sri Lanka once then do it

Amazing world heritage site.  The view is worth the hike, but beware, there were numerous people that we passed that were not up to the challenge.  The pathways have been developed well and you can get away with flip flops although training shoes would be better.  Look out for the guys at the lower levels trying to 'help' you by offering their hand or arm to assist you, they expect payment.  Once you get passed the mid level though where you have to present your ticket they disappear. its hot work so make sure you take a bottle of water.  The view is spectacular and has you asking yourself how on earth they managed to build this amazing structure 200metres up!

So basically this involves a little hike up a hill that has steps carved out for you. The hike is enjoyable off season as during the winter months you will many tourists all making their way uphill in a disorderly fashion. Once up, the view is breathtaking.

Very busy with a lot of tourists, so I would suggest getting there early if you can. We were climbing at 10am, and it was quite slow, but luckily, at this time of year (Oct) most of the climb is in the shade. At 4200rs each, it is not cheap, but still a must if you are in the area.

We are backpackers travelling round Sri Lanka so money is always going to be a consideration for us. We reached the foreigners entrance (yes, there's separate entrances!) and were told that entrance is 4100 rupees... Far too expensive so we went to Pidurangala Rock instead. Fully recommended as not only is it cheaper but you also get a fantastic view of the Lion Rock for an eighth of the price! We had a good climb, took some fantastic photos, watched a stunning sunrise and felt like we were on top of the world...! No complaints whatsoever.

Firstly Sigariya itself is great but ripping off tourists is not. Having lived here for 4 years i get plenty of feedback from tourists every year complaining about the constant price hikes for all tourist sights, national parks, entry visas ( it used to be free but has gone up every year since it was introduced ). I have paid the full price twice before to climb Sigariya and last year a resident/ local rate, i visited again today only to be told that residents now have to apply for their tickets from Colombo beforehand, there is nothing on the Sigariya tourism website telling you this so this time i refused and stayed at the bottom while the rest of my  party climbed. Sri Lanka tourism needs to realize that although at the moment  SL is very popular there will always be some new destination for tourists.

We have travelled all round Sri Lanka and Sigiriya is in a class of its own. It combines ancient ruins, ancient rock art, climbing a big rock, and amazing views. And monkeys. Climb the rock in the morning and most of the climb will be in shade. It's actually not that strenuous and the steps, railings and walls mean it's not that scary. Our 10yo managed it with ease. Sigiriya is expensive to get in (4,200 LKR for an adult) and a guide will probably cost another 2,000 LKR. But this will be about the best money you spend in Sri Lanka - Sigirya is the very soul of the nation and by hook or by crook, you have to go there.

We climbed Lion Rock in a thunderstorm and it was a truly memorable experience. The climb is not as hard as it looks (just take it easy) and the view is amazing in fine weather. We are happy we did it, despite the weather!

We visited Sigiriya in late September in early morning. This is a must as it gets very hot and the crowds arrive later on. I am 67 with heart trouble and found the steep climb very hard. There are very few areas where you walk on the flat as most of it is climbed by endless flights of steep steps. This is a sheer rock face and those with any mobility problems would find it a real struggle The cave paintings are about half way up and are accessed by a spiral staircase which must then be descended. A plateau is reached and this is where the impressive Lion staircase is. Many more steps lead to the summit with sheer drops beneath them. If you don't like heights bear this in mind. One of our party bailed out here. The fort at the top is basically rows of stomes about 2 foot high not unlike any Roman remains you find in the UK. ie Houseteads in Northumberland. I was rather underwhelmed by it and although the view is decent it is no better than any 650 foot viewpoint. The attraction for me was the cave paintings and the Lion staircase which don't require going to the top. Go to the top just to say you have been but don't expect the wow factor

We were there in 7am and that was recommendation from our host. And I am glad that we do it in 7am because after 10 is very hot and there was a lot of people when we finished. We packed our brekfast and ate it on the top of the Rock and it was great. It's not that hard to climb. I saw a few people over 60 and 70 years old and all of them were on the top. The view is really great.
set off early morning to climb the rock before the sun and the tourists,it was windy though. kids loved it

Great experience. We didn't linger too much at the sites leading up to the rock itself. But the ascent up the rock itself is pretty special and the peak was among the most memorable places ever visited. The views are amazing. The ruins are primitive, but feel quite intimate. And the whole thing leaves you with this sense of overlooking history from a perch. We spent a while just soaking it in (and taking great photos, of course.) Advice to go early is worth heeding. It was hot!
The walk is easy and if you get there in the earl morning its a stunning view. The Entry is not cheap but its was a must see place for us in Sri Lanka
Sigiriya was a great morning activity (before the weather was too hot). It's a bit of a hike up the stairs, but seeing the ruins and the surrounding area make it well worth the trip.
If you visit Ceylon, do not miss the climbing of Lion Rock. The view and the historical atmosphere is amazing! If you can do it, rent a bike in a nearby hotel and visit a village near the rock.
Entrance fee is USD $15 or SL rupees 1950. One of the more expensive attractions in Sri Lanka, but totally worth it. Wear comfortable clothing & sports shoes, as there is a bit of a climb.

Sigiriya was created in the 5th century embracing a 200 meter rock outcrop and its natural surroundings. Unesco declared it a world heritage site in 1982. Avoid visiting on weekends & Public holidays as it gets very crowded
Nice view from top maybe after an hour of climbing. Easy for all ages. On the side notes.. Desperate Sri Lankan males will try to take advantage of your partner during narrow paths. And. Hornets

yesterday I visited Sigiriya for the 3rd time after 15 years. Lots has been changed, but it was a amazingly nice trip. I could see so many foreigners have visited sigiriya and there was a special function for them because of Worlds Tourist day. It was bit hard to reach the top due to heavy crowd today and it took three hours to climb. Most of the year sigiriya has dry and hot weather. Always try to take a water bottle. There are two water taps are there on halfway to take drinking water, but it is advisable to take a small water bottle.

It's 1200 steps up. 1202 steps if you climb the two remaining steps of the building on top. It's quite a climb so better be in shape or you'll lose your breath. Entrance fee is 3960rupees per person. It's a nice climb and better if you have a guide that explains everything along the way. Just be sure not to get ripped off. Go there prepared with light clothes, better not those that might get snagged along the uneven rocky areas or stairs. Bring water, umbrella and sunscreen.

I loved the climb and the whole World Heritage site. Wall frescoes well preserved, lion's paws at the bottom of the Sigiriya rock just before the final climb. Stunning views all around. Be ready to pay as all tourist attractions are quite expensive for foreigners in Sri Lanka and costs sum up if you wanna do a lot of sightseeing during your stay. But that 's what we did and we loved it, there is so many places to see especially around the cultural triangle area... The Sigiriya entry fee was 8400rs for 2ppl - the most expensive one to be honest. Have fun.

Amazing views from the top if you are able to climb over 1000 steps.  Take a hand towel and a bottle of water and wear comfortable footwear.  Use the toilets before heading up the mountain.  It takes at least 1.5 to 2 hours to climb up and back down.

The entrance fee is very expensive for a tourist attraction at USD30. Hard work begins after paying the expensive fee. There is a need to climb the rock, there's no elevators going up or coming down. Some parts are very steep and windy. One slip on a step, you will be in ICU. I did not see any emergency kits on the route up or down - so proceed with caution. Need to be very fit and have sufficient stamina for this. There is also a need to carry your own water for the climb. However, once you are at the top, the view is very beautiful and we spend a good 20 minutes or so at the top enjoying the view. Winds can be strong along the climb and at the top. I did it once and will not do it again a second time - it's painful to pay so much money to torture myself.

Best approach is to arrive early in the morning before the sun is up and make the climb to the various fresco areas up before the crowds arrive. Get a good guide beforehand and avoid the so called 'helpers' who happen to be there to assist you up as they are only after money and sometimes your possessions (they are not licensed) vs. your own personal safety. Your own guide would be the best approach to explain to you the attractions and walk with you the whole route with will take about 1.5hrs u and down. Wear good trekking shoes and avoid this place when it rains as it gets very slippery.

Not for faint hearted, a lot of steps and then brilliant views from the very top. often a lot of people around. Surrounding gardens lovely, lots of monkeys about too! When we went it started to rain, a welcome relief to the heat! we didn't mind getting wet, made the steps a little slippy though. When we got to the top the storm came in, was great but scary being that high up with lightning around you!

This isn't for anyone with knee problems, but take your time and you'll be rewarded by spectacular views from the top.   If you can, try and go early before it gets too hot - we didn't and it makes it hard going with the sun beating down on your back.   Having said that, the higher you go, the more breeze there is so its not all bad. If you can't make it all the way to the top, at least try to get to the halfway point after the mirror wall and the paintings as the view is worth even going that far. Look out for the water channels cut into the Rock near the top as well as what look like previous 'steps' and be thankful for the metal staircase. On a busy day, the pace is slow, but that does make it more manageable with plenty of pauses giving you time to catch your breath,  just take water with you and leave anything else at the bottom.

We climbed the rock in the later afternoon. I'm glad we didn't do it any earlier as the temperature was hot enough! I did struggle, but then I am fairly unfit. I am so glad I pushed myself to get to the top. The views are incredible. Take plenty of water and a bag of sweets to keep your sugar levels up. There are a lot of wasp and horrnet nests near the top. They have been known to attack so if you are allergic to stings maybe reconsider.

This is one of my best adventure climbing I would say! More than 200m heights and almost 1000+ steps to reach the top of this rock is not easy as it seems. Its not for the faint hearted. The view from the top is outstanding and definitely a must visit place in Sri Lanka. Please go with a tour guide to understand the details and history of this place. If you are going with a kid/infant get prepared to muscle up and carry him all the way like i did!.

not worth the climb..highly priced for foriegners..1200 steps ,very narrow and steep.very tiring,,you have kids ..big problem.no wash rooms in the vicinity. no stalls for drinks..u need to carry yr water.

The Sigiriya Citadel is amazing.  The surrounding gardens are striking.  The climb up the citadel is best done in the morning when it is cooler and there are fewer people.  The ticket office, however, does not  opens until seven.  The climb up is strenuous and much of the time there are no railings.  So a walking stick is recommended for older climbers.  A hat and a bottle of water are recommended as well.  The view from the top is spectacular!
The climb was exhausting in the heat but well worth the effort. The rock paintings are amazing and the views stunning. It was extremely busy but it's a must see.

Wow......Brilliant view from the top but not for the faint hearted. The climb from the entrance is very steep in parts although a reasonably mobile person can scale the dizzy heights if they take their time. on the downside, there are rather annoying young men who keep grabbing peoples arms with offers to assist them to climb the steps for payment, they need to be firmly told assistance is not required. they only operate at the lower levels where the steps are reasonable and are nowhere in sight when the going gets a little harder higher up. This notwithstanding it is a spectacular 360 degree view from the top but can get very busy. Carry plenty of water on your climb.

We went to the Lions Rock at 6:30 to avoid the heat and tourist masses. The entry fee was absolutly overpriced. We had to pay 4200rs/person. We didn't wanted to get a guide which would has caused another payment. So we went there our own. It's nice to see the ancient ruins and climb the rock, but there's not really much informations about what you see. As we climbed up the stairs there were already a lot of other tourists which caused "traffic jams" on our way up. We went down at ~10.00 and there were a huge mass of tourists. Luckily we went there that early. The day before we went to the 1.5km located Pidurangala Rock which entry fee was just 500rs/person. The view from Pidurangala and the Lions rock were totally stunning. Also the way up on Pidurangala was total fun as you have to literally climb the rock. If you have kids I would recommend to not go there. But if you would climb the Lions Rock for the view, don't waste your money and go there to Pidurangala around 5pm to be up there for the sunset. Mindblowing!

Buses in Dambulla can be taken from the main bus stop where the clock tower is (just search for "Dambulla Bus Station" on Google Maps). I am not 100% sure but buses should run from around 6 am. Tuk tuk Dambulla-Sigiriya (about 18 km): - I paid: 800rs. - Time: 30mins Entrance fee to Sigiriya: 3960rs Opening time: 7am We travelled by tuk tuk in the very early morning to be in Sigiriya at 7am (we could have done it with the bus but for several reasons we choose to take the bus only on our way back). Forget about the remains at the base of the rock, you can visit them when you climb down. For the attraction itself, nothing to add to the many reviews here on TA. Perfect plan.

This is a beautiful place and one of the best things we have done in Sri Lanka. It took less than one hour to climb in what turns out to be adventurous and fun activity. And then, when you reach the top you see an amazing view.

Half way up the rock after viewing the wall frescoes you are confronted with a steep set of stairs going up and up and up. But it must be done. My wife gave up at this point but I trekked onward and upward. Not quite Machu Pichu but magnificent all the same. Make sure you view the gardens below

The place at its own is wonderful!! Just amazing on every square meter. BUT jou just feel ripped of at the beginning! 4000 Rupees the entrance for a foreiner and 100 (!) For a local. WHAT THE HELL SRI LANKAN GOVERMENT? It should be the other way because locals throws garbage everywhere!! They are very rude, not accepting ques and walking at the walls and ingraving their names in the old monks caves?????!!! Just great.

We climbed Sigiriya in August when it was still quite hot and humid but there was a really lovely breeze the higher you got, even getting quite strong at the top. There was a fee for tourists only (understandable as they need to maintain stairs, staff for safety etc) it was about $US 30. There is a water tap at the top but I didn't really trust it (some water pipes were damaged during civil war in Sri Lanka so there is always threat of cholera) so just make sure you bring extra water if you don't either. It was an easy climb, there was a well maintained path through 1600 year old ruins, only a few steep steps and then you get to the base of Lion Rock itself. The stairs there are secured well to the side of the rock so quite safe, but also offer amazing outlooks over the whole area. The first stop through Lion Rock takes you to see some amazing 1600 year old frescoes painted on the rock face. The next stop is the base of the lions paws- the beginning of the ascent to the old palace. An easy climb, the main worry is the many hornets nests buzzing next to the stairs. You must be very quiet so as not to disturb them- apparently on occasions they have had to close the attraction because of this. The view from the top and walking through the ruins of a 1600 year old palace is breathtaking. Definitely well worth a visit. There is little shade along the route so make sure you wear sunscreen etc. Cannot say just how amazing this was, definitely the highlight of our trip.

I read different reviews about this heritage site. Some of them was good some of them was bad. Of course its individual way how you gonna rate this one.... for me - worth to go ! we went there in the morning (around 7 am we start climbe up) and we were down by 10 am. I would say its the best time to go (warm but still not to bad). Take a bootle of water with you put some sunscreen on and foreget flipflops (steps sometimes are small and slippery). View from the top - priceless :) if i good remember its over 1200 steps up so be prepare for that We were travelling with one of the travel office so entrasnce was in price already. But if you travelling alone you need to pay around $40 pp.

From the bottom it doesn't look that high but you do need to have a reasonable level of fitness to get to the top. That said it is absolutely worth the effort ! The rock paintings on the way up are beautiful and the view from the top is amazing. There are quite extensive ruins on the top and it is incredible to think how they could have built this more than 1,500 years ago.

Journey time 4 hours & ticket fare 150 to 200 LKR 2. You can travel from Kandy to Dambulla & from Dambulla you can travel to Sigiriya. Journey time 30 to 45 minutes & ticket fare less than 100 LKR 3. If you are at Polonnaruwa, you will get direct bus from Polonnaruwa bus stand. Journey time 60 minutes to 90 minutes & ticket fare less than 150 LKR. 4. If you are at Anuradhpura, you will get direct bus from Anuradhpura bus stand. Journey time 60 minutes to 90 minutes & ticket fare less than 150 LKR. One should have original passport with him to get discount on the ticket. With discount the price for me was 2850 LKR. I was a little apprehensive about this from seeing the pics and understanding the heat involved and height to climb. Probably the truly "must see" place to go to when touring the Cultural Triangle area of Sri Lanka. Last here 16 years ago and its fair to say its become much more professionally organised since our last trip - not least the metal steps up to the very top of the rock are in a rather better state of repair! There's lots to see both at ground level in the remains of the gardens at ground level as well as the various terrace areas on the way up to the steps to the rock. The residual rock paintings on the way up to the Lions feet area half way up are vibrantly coloured (but I suspect have been "improved" since our last visit as I don't recall them being as clearly defined before). The Lions Feet are is as far as a lot of people go when they see the steep metal steps up to the top - its very much worth the climb though as the views from the top are spectacular and the residual ruins worth a good look see. The way down now takes a separate route from the Lions Feet which as well as aiding the human flow allows you to see some of the other terrace features of the site. Its worth getting up early to be there at as near as possible to 07.00 (or alternatively late afternoon) to miss the crowds. Otherwise be prepared for some extremely long queues in hot, humid conditions as the site's fame has spread around the world meaning everyone on the island would seem to be there at the same time as you

Avoid some old men you meet at the last section who pretend to want to help you as they end up demanding for money in exchange. Also be careful with some guides who after the successful clim will want to bully you into paying more than agreed on the pretext that they have done a splendid job. On the whole, not much to worry about, just a bit of common sense and you will have a thrilling experience. Do not over dress, keep it simple. Carry a bottle of water if you may.

Providing you're not terrified of heights, Sigiriya is definitely worth an early  morning (or late afternoon) of anyone's time - but avoid going in the heat of the day, as it's quite a climb and you'll suffer as a result. The remains of what must have been an astonishing palace, the fact that anyone was able to build their HQ  on this giant rock is reason enough to climb it - but the stories surrounding its inception, and the workmanship that remains are truly fascinating. There are enough gruesome facts to engage a younger audience - a king that killed his dad and deposed his brother, moats full of crocodiles, sentry posts placed at points that would ensure that any soldier nodding off fell to his death - but I would strongly caution against taking very young children up here as there are some massive drops! It's also not one for anyone suffering from vertigo: we saw people quite literally frozen to the spot with fear. That said, provided you are of average fitness, the climb isn't as bad as it looks - and the gobsmacking views that greet you at the top are well worth the **** steps. (Sorry, can't tell you - you'll have to do them to find out.) Take plenty of water and wear decent shoes. This is not a great place for flip-flops.

Parts of this magnificent palace complex were built on top of a steep rock over a period of some 11 years, most likely with great human sacrifice. Built for King Kashyapa exclusively, it was occupied only for about 8 years before being abandoned and the lower palace being donated to the monks. It is probably best to climb to the top as early in the morning as possible, the site opens at 7 am. That way, you avoid the big crowds as well as the most intense heat. There are a couple of hairy sections (especially on the way down), above the Lion’s Gate, but in general the climb is quite safe if rather demanding. So, take your time and do wear trainers! The views from the top are spectacular and you’ll be able to appreciate the whole vast site from there. A guide is probably not worth the money (about 2,000 rupees = $20) though for the less energetic climbers there are plenty of helpful hands to lean on, for hire, with the going tipping rate at around 500 rupees ($5). Watch out for the fine red dust everywhere. Probably best to wear darker clothes. Definitely a must in Sri Lanka.
