Definitely worth a visit - allow 2/3 hours as sometimes big queues. Very impressive monument and very interesting to imagine what it would have been like. Gardens are pretty too. They give you a free DVD on the way in.

It is an amazing construction when you consider the when it was built. Lots to see when climbing to the top. The preservation of the colours in the paintings is wonderful . Climbing the spiral staircase to see the mirrored wall is worth the effort and finally when you reach the top there is a panoramic view of the area.

This attraction is quite famous for several reasons.  Firstly, it is spectacularly stunning in the way it stands higher than everything else.  Secondly, the remaining wall paintings have been very well preserved and are quite accessible.  Thirdly, the walk up is broken into several parts, with attractions at each level and thus a bit easier to complete.  The remains of what was the edifice at the top is quite superb and there is enough there to appreciate the grandeur that once was there.  It is still a challenge because of the heat and humidity, and anyone with a fear of heights would have an issue, but it really is well worth the effort.

a great climb with breathtaking views from the top. Have water & a towel with you especially if you are climbing during the day. The climb takes roughly 30 min to 1 hour especially if you stop for photos

I am stunned that this place is not as well known as Angkor Wat in Cambodia. It has 1,002 steps up steep rockface stairs to a summit which then overlooks a 460 AD pleasure palace. If UNESCO and the SL government ever decided to rebuild some small part of the ruined palace or harem it would be beyond stunning!

Sigiriya World Heritage Site is on pretty much every tourist itinerary when visiting Sri Lanka and it is easy to see why. The site is stunning and has plenty of wonderful things to explore around every nook and cranny. During the hot season, it is quite an arduous climb however so expect to get a good work out. The views from the top are absolutely out of this world. It almost felt like looking back to a prehistoric era. Those who suffer from vertigo may not feel too comfortable with some stages of the climb. The downsides of this attraction were the high entrance fee ($30) which kind of felt pricey considering there was a lot of rubbish everywhere. Also, beware of locals who want to "help" you climb. They pretty much just try to hold your hand in exchange for money. Furthermore, please don't feed the macaques - it is not good for them.

You ve got to visit this place. Word of warning - Slightly challenging for people afraid of heights or suffer with vertigo.  But we really loved the views and  this tour. Go early and avoid the slow movers in your way. Beautiful paintings on the wall and a mind baffling man made swimming pool at the top. Avoid those hornets!

The rock was a great experience. We had a guide. We could easily have done it without since much of what he explained was written on signs along the climb. The rest was stated in the Sri Lanka guide book. We came very early in the morning. I am pleased about that. Already at 9am it starts to get warm - and the busses with tourists arrive. We were the first to arrive that morning and that was great. When we were walking back visitors were already queueing up all the way from the bottom to the top of the rock. We were there during the buddhist new year and that might explain some of the crowds. The view from the top is fantastic. We had our 4-year-old doing the climb. He was fine.

What a climb, but what a view. It's a long, hard climb to get to Lion Rock but it's so worth the effort. The fresco paintings are beautiful and lovely. They are also a nice way to catch your breath before you go on climbing. Don't stop half way at the Lion's Rock but take the stairs up to the citadel as the view is your biggest reward. You can see for miles and miles as far as the eye can see. What a amazing sight.

Some things in this rock fortress is still a mystery...well...i love mysterious stuff. And this was built by a sri lankan king named Kashyapa.It is hundreds of years old but still...the fountains there are working when it rains. The Sigiri frescoes and the mirror wall are somethings that needs definite attention...

The climbing of this rock is not too difficult, all stairs all the way to the top. We did it early morning (7.45 AM) and that was great because it was not too warm yet. We were on the top within the hour, and we had a 4 yo with us who we had to carry parts of the way. By 10 AM we were back in the pool at our hotel. It was much easier than we expected. Beautiful views from the top and a great sense of accomplishment :). Not to miss!

If u are staying in this hotel it is a must to explore ancient sigiriya,the world heritage. the view from the top the sigiriya rock is amazing. for a tourist it will cost approximately 30 USD for the entrance.

The Lion Rock of Sigiriya is a UNESCO listed World Heritage Site. A MUST visit for all tourists to Sri Lanka. This citadel is 1,500 years old and it's only rediscovered in 1853. Best time to visit the citadel is early morning about 8am or 9am (Opening time is 7am to 5.30pm) otherwise it gets extremely hot. The entrance fee is USD$30 per adult. Expect to climb approximately 1,500 steps to the submit (although it felt more like 2,000 steps!). The stone steps are rather well maintained and certain areas have metal stairs to replace the worn out stone steps. The climb to the submit maybe a bit challenging to the elderly or young children and definitely not recommended for wheelchairs or strollers. But if you succeeded in climbing to the submit, the scenery at the top is breath-taking. On the way up, look out for the paintings of 23 damsels and the mirror wall. It's incredible that these paintings are well preserved after 1,500 years. Wear comfortable shoes and hat and carry a bottle of water with you. There are trees with wasp nests around the compound so walk carefully and avoid disturbing the nests.

We hear so many different things about this place. The narrow steps and the long climb. All in all it wasn't as bad as we expected. The climb it self starts through the water gardens that leads through boulders and steps up the mountain. There are plenty of points to take a break and soak up the view. The ancient frescos are worth a peek when you realise the scale of the paintings in their original state. The climb up and down can get busy with coach load of tourists being drafted. When you get to the top the view is stunning! What really made this trip for us was our guide who also worked at the museum. Like all guides it's 50/50 on the quality of information you get but having someone who is experienced in the history and archeology of the site brought the visit alive. I was in awe at the complex irrigation systems build for it's time. Also the history of King Kashyapa and the building of Sigiriya is truly fascinating! Take lots of water, wear comfortable walking shoes and cover up from the direct sun is my advice. Also take some snacks to boost your energy it will really help on the climb as the heat tends to take it out of you. Cereal bars and bananas was our fix.

The rock itself is placed after the museum, which we didn't visit due to time constraints. The climb is well kept - better than my boyfriend's last visit. There is a spiral stair up to the Damsels Gallery and a second stair added on the final climb to the summit. The site itself was also well kept and pretty tidy. I can't believe that people visit a World Heritage site and drop litter around the place but they do. The climb down was easier than the climb up! The price seems quite steep (pardon the pun) at $30 but overall, given the cost of upkeep, development and probably research behind the scenes it was well worth the price.

A place that definitely have to visit. The climb has an average degree of difficulty, but it is worth contemplating the landscapes we are going to reach the top. I recommend just go at 7am because of the scorching heat it feels like to climb, to bring water and a small towel and of course the camera. is also good to have an extra tee in the vehicle to change after the climb. What I did not like is that there is a price for tourists and one for locals.

Its incredible to imagine how the this place once was or even how it was constructed on top pof this hiuge boulder. The climb to the top isn't hard since there are steps leading all the way. On the way up you will see some fresco paintings. The frescos are very good shape considering the time they were painted. Once on top the view is outstanding. The gardens are a nice stroll around the premises as well. In all, one must use their imagination to wonder how this sacred place once looked like. One thing is suggested- go early to beat the crowds because t I if its crowded, the climb up can take some time. Bring sunblock and water.

It's amazing - but if you have any mobility or health problems, then don't attempt the climb up the staircases. Same applies if you don't like heights. My travelling companion had an asthma attack on reaching the top!

The Wandering Yank here again.  This place is spectacular!!!  The climb is not easy, but it was well worth it for many reasons.  The view, the ruins, and especially the fresco gallery.  The gallery about halfway up alone made the visit worthwhile, so if you're not quite up to making the entire climb, at least see the frescoes. Try to go early if possible to beat the heat, and take plenty of water.  Wear appropriate shoes as well. The museum was an excellent introduction to what we would see, so see that first if you can.

First up Sigiriya Citadel is an overhyped and overpriced attraction in Sri Lanka. It's like Stone mountain park in Atlanta. A big rock with a bit of a view. You have to climb 1200 odd steps and it takes the life out of you to climb the steep rock and the view that you get is crap. Some greenery all around that's it. I would suggest that people with kids avoid this place completely. To add to it there is nothing left of the citadel per say. All u get to know is there was a fort here. There was something else there Spend your $30 elsewhere. You'll be glad you did. Wonder why this is a heritage site

This was our main focus for our Sri Lanka trip and it didn’t disappoint.  The entrance fee is relatively expensive (US$30 each) but it is a must do.  We arrived shortly after opening at 7am and this was a good option for two reasons – we beat both the heat and the crowds.  The grounds of the temple are very well kept and there is limited commercialisation of the site which is quite refreshing for a UNESCO site.  The climb up through the boulder garden was quite tough even early in the morning  but the views were very good. The frescoes accessed via the spiral staircase were well preserved - if you haven’t seen other frescoes it is worth seeing.  After the frescoes you go past the mirror wall (now roped off to prevent vandalism) and then onto the Lion Terrace.  The feet of the lion are pretty spectacular and you can rest here under the shade of the trees before the final ascent to the top of the rock itself.  This is via a series of steel staircases – if you have trouble with heights, you will find this a bit scary (coming down is worse).  Once you are on top of the rock, the views are spectacular and the ruins themselves are extensive and very interesting.  Make sure you bring water, a hat and sunblock as there is very little shade on top. After descending, you can exit via the cobra rock and see various snake charmers and souvenir sellers.  By the time we returned to the boulder garden (9.30am), the queue to view the frescoes was backed up to the boulder garden. (2 to 3 hour wait)  If you are arriving at this time, I would recommend skipping the frescoes and taking the path to the left (instead of going up the stairs).  This way you can go straight to the lions feet platform and save yourself some time.

The newly installed museum is built around the existing environment and the architecture of the building, in itself, is very interesting. There was a lot of great exhibits to teach people about the history of Sigiriya and the significance of the rock. It was great for my children to learn about their cultural heritage and I felt they truly enjoyed the experience. There was even a guide to inform you about an interactive exhibit which my children really enjoyed. The entrance fee is waivered if you purchase a ticket to climb Sigiriya rock. Definitely worth a visit!
I liked this new museam which is included in the tciketyou pay for climbing the rock. It's a nice and informative one and can get more information and the history behind the Sigiriya

You need to climb very early or very late. Ignore all offers of help from locals, unless you have no choice or you choose to. Read in advance about the place, will open your eyes more to the beauty and history of the place. Seems quite an effort to climb, but we met several very old turists, the older was a german man of 82 years of age!!! Take water and cover for your head with you.
The way this kingdom has built is unbelievable and the advanced technologies used here are still  hidden. A real WONDER!

We stayed at Lakmini Lodge just down the road from the rock, and I'd really recommend it - choosing accommodation nearby means you can get there before the tour buses arrive. We arrived at 7am which is when the ticket office opens. This was the best decision we could have made, because we could take a leisurely climb, before the crowds and the sun's baking heat caught up with us. Once we reached the top we were one of the first few tourists up there and the view was even more breath-taking because of this. We got chatting to a guide on the way up and decided to let him show us around, which you can refuse, but his english was excellent and he had some great knowledge. He was called Desmond I believe, and is a short, slim guy with medium length hair in a bright shirt. If you spot him, we'd recommend hiring him for 30 mins or so. He's pretty funny! We paid him 800 LKR. On the way down we were met with hundreds of tourists shuffling up the rock and we felt quite smug to have missed the crowds. Set your alarm clock early!

The only reason I planned a trip to Sri Lanka was to explore Sigiriya and climb the Lion Rock. It was truly an amazing experience and simply breathtaking. I hired a private car (about USD90) to pick me up at the train station so I can go immediately to Sigiriya from Kandy. I wasted no time head off but arrived quite late about past 2pm with an overcast almost about to rain. But guess what? It was a perfect timing - less tourists and no sunburns. Shoes and sandals could be essential but I used my flipflops as I was more comfortable with it going up and down the stairs and rocks. Check out the frescoes paintings as the girls' eyes may change directions. If travelling solo a single guide and a selfie stick may work well. Otherwise read online advance notes. There was a secret passage to climb up ask your guide that was supposed to be the passage of the consorts of the King. Take time to fully embrace the beauty of Lion Rock surrounded by vast forest area. Again simply breathtaking!

We based ourselves in Cinamon Ladge, Habaranna for 4 nights. We went to Sygariya Rock and Dambulla caves and  were able to make an early start  as they are reasonably close. Good idea to go early as possible as it gets crowded and hot as the day goes on. Our wonderful driver climbed half way with us and was great as a guide. We would not have got as much out of either attraction without his knowledge of their history. I would really recommend that you go to the top, it's quite a climb but really worth it. Take plenty of water though and sensible footwear!

This was our third visit to Sri Lanka and this time I was determined to see and climb Sigiriya. My husband and I stayed in Dambulla at a hotel 45 minutes away. We took a tuk tuk all the way to Sigiriya. I was intimidated when I first saw it but as I began to climb I realized it wasn't as hard as I thought. I am quite physically fit but not as much as I would like to be, my husband struggled a little more towards the end, especially because it was a rather hot day. Sigiriya was easy to climb because you can keep stopping and enjoy the view and take photos along the way. The frescos were gorgeous and in good condition. There are a lot of scam artists wanting to "help" you climb Sigiriya and then harass you for lots of money - we witnessed this a few times. Once at the top it was very peaceful and a great sense of satisfaction was achieved. The spirally staircases leading to the frescoes gave my head a bit of a spin but generally it was fine. All in all we must have taken 2 hours to go up and come down and only because we were slow and taking our time. I would imagine you could climb it in 30-45 minutes one way and 1.5 hours in total. Definitely a site worth visiting!
Not as hard work to climb as I thought. Very interesting frescoes on the way up. Use the restrooms at the start

Went early morning at 8:00, with a knowledgeable guide we spent approximately 2 hours at the site. No issues with crowds , wasps or monkeys. A true wonder of the world. The site is vast and the views from the top are stunning. Tip, good walking shoes, water and a head for heights.

Its a bit of a climb to the top especially in the heat but its worth it! You get some great views and see some carvings/drawings on a wall in a little cave! Bare in mind we had a guide with us who was really really really good!

Very interesting site but lots of steps! There are a few places on the way up where you can wait but the view from the top is worth the hard slog!  Just beware if you need help the locals may charge a lot of money for their assistance as one of our party found to her cost!

It is hard to give this a bad review but after doing other attractions in Sri Lanka, I tell people to pass on this. First, it is expensive. Second, there are major traffic jams of people on the path that majorly slowed the hike down. Third, I spent an entire day traveling there just for this attraction, like 8 hours on a bus. With all that said, the views are really nice at the top. The paintings and village/ruins are interesting. It sort of looks like Manchu Picchu. However, there are people everywhere at the top. One recommendation is to start the hike before the tour groups start in the morning. I think you can enter 30 minutes before the tour groups are allowed to start. Look it up. You won't have to get stuck behind huge traffic jams of people on the climb up and you will be able to take photos with way less tourist around. If I did that, I imagine my experience would have been quite different and better.

great place to visit for all ages who are able to climb about 700 steps (with breaks..). amazing view. the site's museum is not very impressive but still can add some layer of knoweldge. be sure to carry lots of water as you will lose a lot in prespiration.
The Rock, and its surroundings, are stunning and absolutely worth a visit.  But plan it to off season and off hours or you end up queuing up and down.  A guide is worth getting.

A great way to spend 1/2 a day. The climb up is not for the unfit although we passed many people who took rests along the way although note that one can't stop in some spots. The view from the top is amazing and it was fantastic to imagine how this royal fortress must have functioned during it's heyday. From pools sculptured naturally from rock to the paintings, this ancient site was one of the highlights of our Sri Lankan visit.
Worried about doing this. I am 59 with a dodgy knee. Took my time and was so pleased to reach the top. The frescoes are a real highlight

A really exciting climb up. The modern stairs are really safe, we can only imagine how it was climbing this on bamboo sticks 1 600 years ago. Magnificent view from the top. The extra climb up to the frescoes are a must!

Sigiriya Rock even surpasses the hype. We also spent some time and explored the gardens at the lower parts, a good way to relax after the steep climb. Our guide had a lot of information, most of which we could read in the TripAdvisor book.

Stunning architecture! The hike is not difficult. You can see ancient wall paintings and different landscape on the way up. This ancient palace is magnificent. But somehow is not over crowded compare to other ancient palace around south east asia. You can easily found a private space to enjoy some peace and enjoy the view. Simply bring a guidebook and follow the apparent roads to head up to the palace. You don't need a tour guide to visit this site. Take it slow and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere in this "lost empire". A must go in Sri Lanka

Stunning and memorable experience. As much for e experience of doing the climb than the site. Probably overpriced but would still do it again every time. Definitely go early when it is cooler, the site could benefit from a water stall halfway up.

We did this "little" hike, and trust me comparing to Adam's peak this is a little hike. It was a very pleasant hike with a lot of beautiful views. We left later to be able to enjoy the sunset. And what a sunset that was. Absolutely worth it. There is also a lot of friendly monkeys on the top :)

Of all the places my wife and I visited in Sri Lanka - this Rock Fortress and the Ancient city of Polonarawa were the best.  Bring good hiking shoes and water.  If you are afraid of heights as my wife is - this can be a daunting trip.  The entrance fees was about 3600 rupees per person plus another 2500 for a guide.  The guide was adequate but not great.  Was it worth about $75 for two people?  Yes, but as we found across Sri Lanka - the tourists are "soaked" while the locals pay next to nothing.  We told our guide that some of these attractions really aren't worth the cost and much higher than what is typically charged in the US or Europe... a lot of the stuff in Europe is free. It took about 2 hours walking and going up a lot of precarious steps made out of marble.  If you have small feet, no problem - however at 6'8" (2 meters), I had to walk in a switch-back pattern with my feet at 45 degree angles to the steps.  I guess the Sri Lankans back then had small feet.  The temperature was about 90F when we visited, so it was a hot, sweaty experience - but again well worth it. Again the only issue was the guide - his English was fair at best.  He gave me an overview of some of the history, but it was brief, and I only understood about 40% due to his accent.  We had a driver from Blue Lankan whose English was very good, and he told us a lot about the history of the Rock Fortress before-hand.  But a lot of these attractions only allow their own "certified" guides... I think just a way to make more money off the tourists.  I would recommend talking to the guide for a few minutes first before committing to make sure you can understand them well.  I probably would have passed on the $18 (2500 rupees) we spent on the guide and bought a book to read afterwards.
Go early in the morning before it gets hot and crowded. the climb is not too arduous, but better with a good shoes, a hat and water.

Visiting Sigiriya was a huge highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. The climb was long and very hot but so so worth it. The views were incredible and the site incredibly peaceful and untouched. I'd do it again if I had the change, fantastic!

Just loved this it was the best trip that we did on our holiday in Sri Lanka. 1200 steps to climb up the rock and the same coming back down. It is exhausting climbing up in such heat and it took us over two hours plus to climb up and down and to see other things. We went after 4pm when it was getting cooler so it was a little better. Coming back down your knees just tremble. The steps are very narrow and there is a spiral staircase on the outside which some people may struggle with but bear with it because once you get up there it is totaly exhilarating such a view. I don't believe I have had many of these feelings if any as I had when we arrived on the top of what felt like the world. The welcome breeze at the top is your second reward for the climb but the first is defiantly the view from the top Get a tour guide to tell you all the history in why it was built and who lived there and the 18 naked ladies that are left on this atraction as this is true part of Sri Lanka Tale plenty of water with you and sensible shoes are a must

Amazing rock & stone art. Very unique world heritage site which i've visited. Entree fee is killer. LKR 3,900 (US$30) per person. You need at least 3-4 hours to cover it. How to reach sigiriya from dambulla : From dambulla there are direct bus to sigiriya. Ticket cost LKR 40. Bus stops at cross road which goes to sigiriya world heritage site (check the cross road snap posted with this review) From cross road to site you can hire tuk-tuk but i've walked to the site which was around 2-3km away. Come back same way & you will get bus back to dambulla within 5-10 minutes. Total tour time from dambulla will be around 2-4 hours. Pictures tells a story. I have added many pictures with this review. check them.

We loved coming here! The grounds were interesting, with some signage around the place to explain what you were seeing (we didn't take a guide with us). The climb to the top was worth it all, the view was incredible! We didn't find the climb too hard - however we did see some very dramatic climbers on the way up! Just take your time and enjoy the views and experience! I would definitely recommend visiting early as it can get very hot there! We arrived at 8am, and by the time we were leaving it was getting very hot.

Go really early in the morning...as soon as it opens.  You'll appreciate the view, peace and the lack of visitors.  When we came down from the rock we headed past streams of visitors pouring in and it would have spoilt our experience.  Its quite scary using some of the staircase/walkways, don't reccommend it if you dont like heights!
Very nice place. Try to go early in the morning to avoide big queues, the heat and enjoy it the most.

Even if you are not interested in the history or the archaeological site, we would recommend climbing to the top as the views are spectacular. Our advice would be to go first thing in the morning (they open at 6.30am usually, 7am if it's poya) to avoid the crowds and the heat.

Beautiful palace(s) on the top of the massive rock, built 16 centuries ago. Those brave ones who dare to climb to the top (I'm not one of those, due to the mild fear of heights) will be awarded by having opportunity to see beautiful frescoes (originally, there were 500 of frescoes, only 18 remained). I did not climb to the top but I enjoyed the site, and would highly recommend it.

Lions Rock at the entrance to the royal palace in the Fort , comes when we almost finishing major part of the Fort and while beginning to enter the last part comprising the royal palace .Good spot to relax for a while.

Fifth century Fortress in the sky is a world Heritage site . its known as LIONS ROCK, AS there was a huge Lion that used to stand at the entrance to the 600 foot high rock, says my guide MR. RANJIT BHANDARA.

ARCHITECTUAL MARVEL.NOT to be missed.It has 1202 steps . Watr garden,fountain, rock garden and caves should NOT be missed.It has three gates elephant, Lion and Cobra. Frescoes of 18 damsels with natural mineral colours by artists are marvelous..1200 old mirror walk is another attraction. Steps in the fortress are topped with marble which reflect in the moonlight.we can see the entire area from the top which is WORTH TRYING. I really enjoyed a visit and climbed to the top. always remember SIMHA GIRI the ancient name of this place which is now SIGIRIYA.

An amazing natural wonder paired with outstanding history, architecture and culture. It was a very hot day when we were at the rock fortress so make sure you take plenty of water so you can take your time and enjoy the experience. The wasp attack warnings, the monkeys, the lizards and the view of the rock make for a very exciting start to the adventure! The steps and stairs up to the top of the rock will test your fitness and nerve as some sections are just bolted to the side of the rock. Once you are at the top take the time to take in the incredible 360 degree view of the country and surrounds, and make sure you take note of the interpretation panels that are situated around the site, these will help you appreciate the incredible design of the palace and the surrounding area.
World Heritage is a must anywhere. And in Srilanka it is heaven on earth. Loved visiting it. A must see site and very enjoyable
Loved the way it is amazingly sculptured by nature. Very very breath. Highly recommended to visit whilst in the area.

it is a magnificent castle.... bit of a tiring climb up... but a must if you want to see the mirror wall....when climbing with small children you must be extra careful... also keep in mind about the hornets.....dont make loud noice.... Sigiriya (Lion Rock ) is an ancient palace located in the central Matale District near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. The name refers to a site of historical and archaeological significance that is dominated by a massive column of rock nearly 200 metres  high. According to the ancient Sri Lankan chronicle the Culavamsa, this site was selected by King Kasyapa (477 – 495 CE) for his new capital. He built his palace on the top of this rock and decorated its sides with colourful frescoes. On a small plateau about halfway up the side of this rock he built a gateway in the form of an enormous lion.

This posed a bit of a challenge, but one we wanted to beat.  The thought of climbing a rock some 200 meters high and up 1200 steps (this figure seems to change depending what you read) was a little daunting.  Our guide was very keen for us to get to the top and said we would take it slowly.  There are plenty of places to stop and take in the scenery and have a rest - so don't rush. In our mid to late 60's and both with back problems we did it!  The view at the top is amazing. Take water, a hat and your camera.  Don't carry anything you don't need.  Try and avoid the men trying to help you up.  They grab your elbows when they can and then stick with you wanting payment at the end.  Fine if you need a bit of extra help and they did give up when I said I was with my husband.

We climbed the rock right after our flight to srilanka .it was a hard climb but definitely worthed. The museum is a waste of time but the   fortess itself is majestic. Do the climb in the early morning to avoid the heat and dont forget water. The views are breathtaking.  The cave paintings are also interesting and detailed
Superb and well worth the climb. Yes it was busy (arrived about 10:00) and we had to queue to get to the paintings but after that it was my lack of fitness that limited our speed of climb.
Over 1250 steps, but the ruins at the top made it so worthwhile. Great views from the top. This is a must for any trip to Sri Lanka.

We were told not to miss the strenuous climb to the top of this rock fortress even though we are a little fearful of heights. By persevering and gritting our teeth, we managed to reach the summit. The queues were a bit daunting, and I suppose it was that which helped ensure that we completed the climb. Once at the top, we were rewarded with breathtaking views all around. On the way up, you get to see some very old cave paintings - these are really beautiful (and viewing them gives you a break from the climb). We had ensured that we acquired a guidebook for this site since - as others have noted - there is limited information around. Some have complained about the disparity between foreigners' entrance fee and that of the locals. This should not be considered an issue. How about comparing the wages of the foreigners with those of the locals? You may then see that it is not at all unfair. This really is a "must-see".

This place is fascinating, get a guide as the history is worth knowing, although ours was so keen to get us up there we missed the museum.  Half the gardens are being restored, the other half yet to be done, so a good example of before and after. The climb is hard in the heat, but welll worth it when you get there and plenty of places to stop and rest on the way.  Highly recommended.  Our kids are 7 & 11 and made it up no problem

With no doubt it was my favorite place during my trip around Sri Lanka. You can climb there to enjoy the amazing views from the top, there are around 1200 steps but it sounds worst that it really is, because you enjoy all the climb to the top. There is also an amazing wall paints in the middle of the climb. You must be aware of the hornets, they could be dangerous.
This is a well presented museum with many Buddist artefacts. It describes the history of the Sigiriya Rock Fortress. A Must.

Okay folks. This a massive rock with a settlement at the very top just like Machu Picchu. Fantastic rock paintings.It is best to go early in the morning before it gets too hot. However a warning to the unfit, this is a major climb with about 1500 steps. There are a number of buddist temples

This is easily the most breathtaking (literally and figuratively!) activity we did while in Sri Lanka. I cannot recommend it enough! When you make it to the top, the views are absolutely stunning and well worth the effort getting there.  If you have a panorama function on your camera, this is the place you will want to use it. The timing of when you go can really influence your experience.  We were there around 11:00 AM when the sun was really starting to get hot and very direct.  Earlier in the morning would most certainly be best.  Also, there are not many food or water options there so it is best to bring what you need with you and be prepared. If you have a major allergy to wasps, this may not be the best outing for you.  Several parts of the trail require you to pass by large nests and some people have been stung.  Just make sure to travel with your EpiPen or other medicine. Finally, from the look of the rock along with comments from other travelers, I thought this hike would be prohibitively difficult.  While it does require some level of physical fitness, the hike is not as difficult as it looks from the ground.  When you make it to the paw, the most difficult is behind you.  Hang in there, the top is amazing!
If you are interested in a castle built on a rock, an ancient mirror wall and beautiful fresco, this is something you do not want to miss!

There are ladders and metal skeleton frames that help tourist get up the rock column but the place is well-kept and it's not as crowded as other places where structures are placed to transform it to a tourist destination. The top of the rock is well preserved and I couldn't see any modern man made stuff there which is great so you get to see the ruins at its perfection. I wish I stayed longer and explored the gardens as well.

Sigiriya is one of the best sightseeing in Sri Lanka, you have to climb more then 2,000 Steps which is tiring and a lot of people give up, but once you reach the top you will experience the best view. I wished i had my go pro/DJI phantom at the top. Don't give up and insist to reach the top of the Rock

The Sigiriya rock is an imposing structure, and climbing it all the way was certainly an intimidating thought.  The ideal time to attempt the climb is early in the morning – it opens at 7 am – before the rock heats up.  There are about 1200 steps  – which is not impossible to do if done at a slow and steady pace.  The best part are the frescoes about half way up – if anyone has issues climbing all the way, suffice it to know that the frescoes are the best part of the rock.  I was not overly inspired by the next stop -Lion’s Gate - and did not attempt the last 400 steps to the top, from where, I understand, you have a spectacular 360 degree view.

It's a long walk to get to the rock itself, most of the time whilst being pestered by folks trying to "help" you (for a tip) who tell you that you won't make it and "you will fall!" once you tell them to stop pawing and pestering you. The climb itself starts as quite steep, goes to vertical to get to the curtain wall (up metal fire escape type steps) and just when you think you have got to the top there are more, even more precarious, steps to climb. From and H&S point of view they are not the safest but if you want to get to the stunning view from the top what else can you do. Take plenty of water, facilities are few and far between and no refreshments until you get back to the bottom.

This is a very impressive site which well deserves to be a World Heritage Site and, possibly, the eighth wonder of the world - as our guide suggested! Unfortunately if, like me, you are terrified of heights - or not exactly the heights but the means of getting to them (scary stairs) - you need to be aware. I found the first half of the climb fine as it was on stone stairs cut into the rock. However when you get to the see through metal stairway hanging off the rockface I'm afraid I couldn't hack it - and I wasn't the only one! Parts of the stairway are fairly steep and, as I say, open in all directions. Our guide told me the stairs were fairly new, and if only they'd had the foresight to cage them in, as they have with the spiral stairs lower down, I'm sure I could have done it. It's a shame as I know I would have found the top fascinating and not had a problem with that. My husband carried on and reported that the top was, indeed, well worth the climb. I wish I could have made it. If, like me, you can't manage the scary bit it is still worth doing the first half - you get some fabulous views, interesting mirror wall, and there's a large area where you can rest in the shade while the braver ones in your party carry on up.

Too good to miss. Impressive rock, ruins and gardens. The climb is challenging, about two thousand steps and would recommend early start to avoid crowds and the heat. Take water and food although you can get some food when you come down. Wear sensible trainers/ walking shoes and sun lotion plus hat

Breathtaking views, rich in history and culture. I was amazed by it! Quite a sporty walk but worth every step! We had a guide, and we enjoyed his company and him sharing bits and pieces of his knowledge and we got to chat with him(for more historical info, check online or your guides) Not to be missed!

Sigiriya Rock has virtually everything that you could want in a touring holiday attraction.  It is a strikingly impressive 200m high geological phenomenon rising almost vertically out of the forest, the history surrounding it is very interesting, the ruins themselves are remarkable and the 360* view from the summit is stunning.  Be warned, though, the climb is not of the easiest and for those who may be faint of heart or suffer from vertigo, the spiral staircase up to the frescoes can be a trial - but they are definitely worth the effort, even if the famed Mirror Wall is a bit of a disappointment.

It's a nice walk up to the fortress ruins. Kinda long, but if you're in decent shape, it's a breeze. Don't be put off by the height of it - it is actually not as taxing as it seems. The gardens surrounding the rock are beautiful - time for some thoughtful contemplation? The top of the rock is mostly ruins, but has a nice vibe to it. Sit around, enjoy the cool breeze and reflect on stuff.

We arrived at the entrance about 8am in order to climb before it got too hot. Before travelling to Sri Lanka we had read about wild hornets on the rock face. A guide told us they can be disturbed by noise.  Seeing plenty of  Chinese and school children climbing out of the coaches we quickly made our way through the gardens to the bottom of the steps to try and avoid them.  The steps at the start were quite deep and broken in places with no hand rails. There were several ‘guides’ trying to grab our arms and offering to help us to the top but we declined their help preferring to go at our own pace. We were both 70 and reasonably fit but live in a flat so we were not at all used to stairs.   Fortunately it was not too busy so we had the opportunity to rest at the top of each flight if we wanted to and let large groups pass us.  Hornets were soon forgotten in our desire to get to the top. Halfway up, at the Lion’s feet, we discovered a large flat area. We took the opportunity to rest for a while in the shade of trees.    The stairs from now on were mainly metal fire-escape type stairs which we had thought would be the worst part of the climb. We paused only briefly to admire the painted murals on the wall as it was very claustrophobic at that point.We slowly started the final climb.  Surprisingly we discovered that this part was easier than the stone steps providing you don't have any fear of heights.  People were moving very slowly so we had chance to climb at our own pace.  Finally we made the top! We felt quite proud of ourselves as people far younger had dropped out at the halfway stage. We sat for a time under the shade of a tree admiring the 360 degree view.  Our hotel, on the opposite side of Kandalama reservoir, was so camouflaged it was difficult to see it.   After walking round the ruins we made our way back down to the car park. Here we were grateful to find much needed ice cold drinks for sale.

The climb to the top takes about an hour and a half at a medium pace. We went with my parents and siblings. It's a bit tiring for old people. My parents stopped half way. We forgot to take water, which was really a bad idea since it was burning hot. We're lucky to now have steps and protective railings to climb the fortress. The people of ancient times climbed the rocks, which just had tiny foot ledges hewn out of them. They must have been really nimble footed. But the views from the fortress are stunning. You can see the remains of what once were perfectly landscaped gardens and pools at the bottom still looking beautiful. The frescoes and the "mirror wall" are interesting. The view from the top is amazing. It was a bit crowded when we got there around mid morning, so it would probably have been better to go there earlier in the morning.

Must do in Sri Lanka if you are in this area. I'm not usually scared of heights but did find the steps attached to the side of the rock slightly terrifying! View from the top was well worth it though.

The view from the top is worth a trip to Sri Lanka for itself ! It is a long climb, and all steps, but it is perfectly possible to take your time and stop along the way. It's not just the fabulous view across lakes and mountains from such a height - the palace, gardens and frescos are well worth a visit. If staying for sunset, which is beautiful, do not delay your trip down again.

As we approached the Sigiriya Rock Fortress from the parking lot, we were welcomed by gangs of monkeys. The approach had gardens all along upto the base of the Rock's gradual climb which also had a river which we had to cross. The river was filled with schools of fish and also had turtles in them. We also spotted a few monitor lizards and chameleons. The climb from the base of the river to the top which is carved out of red stone is an architectural wonder and a mind boggling experience, going back to the time it was constructed when there were no metallic rods available which was now used for safety and protection measures along the climb ladders, fabricated to make the climb less tiring. Your mind tells you that the people of those days were really 'Hanumanic'. After reaching half way up there are beautiful frescos hand painted on the walls. At the top there is a tank that some people drank water from. The return journey was a slightly different but equally enthralling route upto the base water gardens and our parking area.

Unmissable.  The views from the top are extraordinary, and the fortress/palce/temples on the summit utterly awe-inspiring in terms of the the effort and engineering skill it must have taken - it's quite hard enough walking up to the top on a well-prepared staircase, I can't imagine what it would have been like to try and carry rocks and building materials up there. It's strongly advised to get there in time to go in immediately on opening at 0800 - -we didn't and regretted it, both because it gets very hot very quickly and because it gets very crowded, since it's one of the top attractions in the whole of Sri Lanka. The Buddhist temples are very impressive but it's a bit like the Moscow metro at rush hour, the crowds are sufficiently dense to make it difficult to appreciate, and the murals and frescos are beginning to suffer real deterioration due to the moisture from all the tourists and pilgrims. The climb to the top took us around an hour, but we could have made it in 40 minutes without the crowds and queues.  It's around 1200 steps to the top, so given the heat you need to be moderately fit but taking it steady even comparative couch potatos should be able to make it, and the arrival at the summit makes it all worth it, both for the views and the constructions on the top, and the sense of achievement.  Take water (there are places to buy water and soft drinks at the base but not the summit)  and be sure to wear insect repellent.

Start as soon as possible with the climb of Sigiriya Rock. We started around 8.30 and this was even a bit to late. It was really crowded and it was getting hot fast. The climb is really nice and the view from the top is stunning. Watch out for guys who pretent to be working there and telling you a lot of things about the rock. They demand a high payment afterwards.

This is definitely an attraction worth visiting in the area.  The place is beautiful and the views are stunning on the way up and at the top.  Be ready to climb a lot of stairs.  Give yourself about 3 hours to go up and back down. Not only due to the stairs but also due to the line of people.  It is sunny and hot in February so take hat, sunglasses, and some water for the way. We saw large lizards on the grounds and met up with friendly monkeys.  Beware of people trying to lure you to a short cut on your return down.  They will ask for money if you follow them.  There are a few souvenir shops at the entrance/exit. All in all a memorable experience.

An amazing place. Make the effort and climb to the top. Don't give in half way. You can stop at the lions feet but don't. I'm retired and have a dodgy ankle but I did it. Over 1000 steps but you can take your time. Coming down is a bit more precarious and you can slip in wet weather so definitely check the weather if you have a choice. The paintings are amazing and the view from the top is stunning.you need good shoes and water and an umbrella for rain or hot sun. You will be offered help and if you are at all uncertain take it. 1000 rp to the top and back but don't pay til the end. It's a hard climb but worth the effort

Although there was a lot of elderly people making this trip, they required some assistance from the staff, and I would personally not reccomend it as it requires some physical abilities. But for everyone in normally good shape, this will be a very pleasant and beautiful trip. You should definately start early in the morning as the rock gets very hot later in the day. We started the climb at 8 am and it was perfect. Also it gets very crowded from around 10/11 am. Remember to bring good footwear (no flip-flops) and lots of water. Almost at the top there is a tank with water for you to fill up your bottles, but I am not sure if that water is completely safe to drink, we didn't risk it as we had brought enough. It was a bit expensive (3900 rupies per person), but in the end, we had no regrets about spending that money. The atmosphere, the view and the slight physical challenge made for a very special experience alltogether.

The visit requires also physical effort but it is nice and I wonder the only place in the world with the same structure: a palace built above a huge mountain rock. The view is outstanding and the structure interesting. I recommend to visit the museum before start the climbing.

It was great experience for witness the great history of ancient Sri Lanka. Still its seems miserable. No clue about the transportation method used to clime his rock castle in the past. If you travel his place at rainy season you can see the ancient fountains which are still working. Its amazing

We climbed the rock in the early afternoon, the hike to the top was good with amazing views to the surrounding countryside below. However, come sunset a hoard if people descended on rock with lots of big groups of young school children. We were glad to be leaving when we saw this! The old fortress is incredible to see and I'm glad that old historical sites are being taken care of in Sri Lanka, but I don't think that this is worth the huge expense to get into. As a couple travelling and backpacking, $60 is a massive amount of money and probably the most expensive 'attraction' we've ever paid to see. We also didn't think the museum was that great, despite the hyped reviews.

this is amazing place, be prepared for about 2000 steps to go to get on the top, but after that you will see beautifull views. This is one of must see if you are in Sri Lanka. O ecrecommendation go there early in the morning ( start latest on 7 am) to avoid heat and also lot of tourists. It is worth to visit, if you traveling with small kids it is possible to make it with them. We have made it with 2,5 and 6 years old kids.

The ruins around the site are impressive. Also, the view from Sigiriya is very nice as are the cave paintings. However, on the descent down the mountain there are not clear signs indicating the path to the foreign tourist parking lot. This parking lot is in a completely different location from the arrival area. Since the parking lot is not visible from the path we had to ask for directions. Multiple local people directed us in the wrong direction. Then at the parking lot's restroom there are attendants looking for tips.

At the outset I want to say how expensive the entrance fees are for this. We paid 3000 rupees each. Also there was no water for sale nearby so stock up before. The climb was fine. 30 mins. Steps all the way. We climbed in the late afternoon and saw the sunset. Just magical.

Lovely place but seems to be on every visitors list of essential Sri Lanka making it a very busy place. You need to be reasonably fit to make it to the top but the effort is worth it for the views alone. Watch out for the young locals who try to help you up the steep bits, they are not being friendly, just offering a service for money!

Yes, this is an expensive site ($30) and requires a lot of physical effort to climb the 1200+ steps. However it is worth it. Passing through the gardens as you approach the rock, you can see fountains that still work hundreds of years later! The grounds are impressive and it's even more awe-inspiring to think how the top of the rock hosted the king and his 'guests'. Along the ascent you see the frescoes and mirror wall and can see garnet seams in the rock. The steps get steep near the top. Heights and me do not get along well so I stopped at the lion's paw but my boyfriend trekked up to the top himself. His panoramic photos are spectacular so it's worth the time and effort to continue up if at all possible. I saw many families with children and seniors coming down so it isn't as much strenuous as steep! Take water to drink and be silent to avoid the wasps. This is the best site to see in Sri Lanka, in our opinion!

The Sigirya Rock Fortress is accessed via 1200 steps ranging from large steps to a circular stair case. This is a fairly strenous climb that takes place in three stages.  The first part of the climb consists of stones steps (quite high). If you go up the steps in the middle there are no hand rails.  It's best to use the steps off to the right which do have hand rails. At the top of the steps you get a great view with the Buddha emerging from the trees in the distance below. The middle part of the climb involves climbing come iron steps followed by a circular staircase that leads to paintings of well endowed sri-lankan women that are very old on the side of the rock. The top part of the climb takes you up some more steps leading to the fortress entrance protected by lions (only the feet now remain). When we visited in March 2015 there was an infestation of hornet wasps which had formed their nests.  People were offered protective clothing if they wished to make the final asceent (which we declined).
Views from top are wonderful. Climb is fine, just take your time. Well worth doing the spiral bit half way up to see the rock paintings. Go early to avoid crowds.
Expensive, but well worth it. Come early to avoid crowd. The climbing is nice, but the atmosphere at the top is what I enjoyed most.

This was an excellent find in Sri Lanka,  absolutely amazing this lost city with it's water system built around 12BC it still functions today. The cave paintings are still very clear and colorful.  The entire construction is an amazing project that used elephants,  and many thousands of people.  The cost is $ us 30.00 per adult. It's a great climb.
Loved it here worth the hike up to the top , beautiful views & amazing to see it , we took a bag of bricks up to help with the restoration a must see if in Sri Lanka
head off in the morning to avoid crowds and the heat. The entrance fee is $30. It's a pretty long way up but it's worth climbing !

I climbed lion rock this week. I thought the views and the frescos amazing. The people were helpful and friendly. The only downside was being asked for money by the some helpers. One in particular latched on to me as I travel solo. He continued asking for money, even dollars at one stage

Beautifully laid out this is well worth a visit. There a 200 metre climb to the top of the rock via steps. Part of the site is at normal ground level and paintings on the wall are reached by steps (on the way up to the first level of the rock). You can marvel at the rock from afar and visit some of the site without climbing to the top. Remember to take water with you if you intend to climb to the top, where there are superb views and more of the ruins

Our No.1 tip is to Check the weather forecast first. The climb is strenuous.  It would be such a pity to reach the top of the Rock and not get the well deserved view.                                             Take an umbrella for either heat or rain, carry water and wear comfortable clothes and shoes as it is a long climb to the top.      Before you embark on your climb please go to the toilet as there are none on the rock.          Try not to give up 2/3 of the way up as there is a summit where you can rest before the final climb of the remaining stairs which are steep but safe .         Along the way up or down you will be offered help if you accept a hand up payment is expected so do take small change to avoid unnecessary conflict.          The view from the top is spectacular. There are also ruins of a bygone Royal presence such as swimming pool or bathing area, thrones and remnants of courts.                      The whole area around the base of the rock and leading up to it is scaped. The scenery is typically jungle teaming with trees flowers and wildlife such as birds and monkeys. It's a wonderful place to charge your batteries. Sigiriya Rock and climb is a must when visiting StiLanka

Absolutely spectacular! Though the stairs are not so easy to climb, my retired parents made it to the top, and it was definitely worth it. The rock with its surrealistic colours amazes you when you approach and then completely blows your mind up when you get to the top of it - the view is breathtaking, it makes you feel something really special when you look down the valley. It’s unbelievable humans created such a masterpiece on a steep rock and even painted some frescoes on it. Make sure you don’t miss the meditation caves on the way.

Having climbed this 12 years ago, when I was younger and fitter (and less afflicted by asthma and COPD), I approached this with a little trepidation! We arrived a little later (about 8.30am) than our guide initially wanted us to, as he wanted to beat the crowds, but that played to my advantage as I was able to get a few breaks on the climb up. It was quite crowded in places, particularly just before the paintings, and it would have been nice if some nationalities hadn't tried to queue jump, but after 90 minutes of very sweaty climbing we made it to the top, where the views over the countryside are spectacular, even if the ruins aren't much to see when you are up there. Fortunately, our holiday company guide was very knowledgeable and able to tell us plenty of interest. The descent is, as you would expect, a lot easier! This is a must see for any visitor to Sri Lanka and, if you aren't too fit, just take your time and no-one will mind. Make sure you start early(ish) morning though or you will spend a whole lot longer queuing than sightseeing.

The Sigirya Rock Palace has been referred to as a "Must Visit" attraction in Sri Lanka and even the "Eighth Wonder of the World".  For the historical significance of the palace and its grand water gardens, the site is certainly well worth making the trip, but I wouldn't put it in the same league as the monuments of Angkor Watt in Cambodia and Petra in Jordan. The elegant water gardens leading to the Rock Palace are splendidly laid out with well preserved ponds, fountains and pavilions. The huge rock in the centre on which the palace and fortress were built is awesome, but the strenuous effort required for climbing up the 700 odd steps up to the top (though less challenging than climbing up the hill to the monastery in Petra) is certainly not for the faint-hearted and those lacking stamina.  On reaching the top, one can find little left of the palace and fortress but the panoramic view from the citadel of the water gardens and the surrounding country is breathtaking and rewarding. This is indeed a sight in Sri Lanka not to be missed, even for the exorbitant price charged for foreign tourists.

Our driver instructed us to check the museum before heading for the mountain. It helps you understand what you will see. It is not an easy climb on a warm day. And not cheap at US$30. The frescos are minimal and the runs at the top are only so-so. Nice view though on a clear day. You can either go right to the top or enjoy the numerous sites and caves along the way. They are all numbered but not clear what the number correspond to.

However if you are there of course you are going go. It is $30 USD pp for entrance. If you can somehow figure out how to avoid the crowds, perhaps in the afternoon this could be a lovely experience. In the mornings though it is you and hundreds of other people all trying to queue up to reach the top...god forbid it is sunny or rainy all the morons have their umbrellas up for protection from the elements however you're likely to loose an eye with this nonsense. Views are great of course but with a place so busy it looses so much of it's appeal. Still something unique to see and the climb is entertaining.

No one could dispute that this ancient rock is to Sri Lanka what the Grand Canyon and Ayers Rock respectively are to the USA and Australia respectively with its art and archaeological features complemented by 360 degree views.  One wonders how the original residents obtained access. One has to be careful of the steps in wet weather as they largely lack a standard rise.  The way back to the car park is not properly signposted. However the only way we could avoid the crowds was to be there by 0700 for the opening of the ticket office.  By 0820 there were large numbers of mainland Chinese and French tourists streaming in. The Lion's Head is worth seeing, the Mirror Wall marginally so. There was total disorganisation in the car park with private cars on tour making it hard for coaches to reverse. The admission price of R3900 for foreigners is another example of Sri Lanka milking the golden cow as locals get in for a fraction of the price. The car park is unsealed and the 2009 opened museum already decaying. One has to ask what happens to all the money collected from foreigners in admission fees?

ARRIVE EARLY - and be ready to mount those steep steps and climb up the elevated terrain.  It is very manageable, even for the unfit if you pace yourself.  It is DEFINITELY worth visiting and go to the Museum too, as this paints a further picture of the resplendent Palace that existed in the 5th Century.  The views are breathtaking, as well as the climb (truly).  You miss the queues and the hordes of people by going early, at 7am and can appreciate the highest level, with a few people around.  The Entrance Fee also takes your breath away, at USD35 per person.

This is an amazing place. I am a reasonably fitm60 year old but I have to say this was quite a climb to get to the top. It was however absolutely worth it. The views are amazing and the way you get there is also quite different with spiral staircases, hard rock steps and metal gantries. For me one of the key attractions of Sri Lanka
We enjoyed the experience and we had a great guide, it was very hot and we did not realise that it was such a steep climb to the top. Not great for older people

This is a must see in Sri Lanka, you can see why it's on the UNESCO list. It's a steep climb up with scaffolding stairs but well worth it. Half way up you reach the cove hood caves with the paintings that are beautifully preserved, what's left of them. Then further up you reach the lion gate, and that climb is slightly harrowing, the view up the top is breathtaking. The sun setting something else up there, tranquil and peaceful looking out to the land, this is must do!

This is a must see in Sri Lanka, you can see why it's on the UNESCO list. It's a steep climb up with scaffolding stairs but well worth it. Half way up you reach the cove hood caves with the paintings that are beautifully preserved, what's left of them. Then further up you reach the lion gate, and that climb is slightly harrowing, the view up the top is breathtaking. The sun setting something else up there, tranquil and peaceful looking out to the land, this is must do!

Can't imagine how someone built this place. This filled with mysteries which I think will never get revealed in future even. There are lot to see which you won't find anywhere in Sri Lanka. Journey is bit tired but won't regret that at the end of the day.
Amazing sight and a fantastic experience - the walk to the top is not that bad eventhough I'm a little afraid of heights.

When I saw that some had given this attraction a poor review, I had to see why because I couldn't imagine anyone saying that!  Most of those reviews were submitted by folks who had been stung by wasps.  Let address this first.  If the wasps are active, our guide said, we would not be able to go all the way to the top.  There a large nests on the side of the rock and apparently nothing can be done about them.  They are out of reach of extermination.  Just be aware.  Luckily for our group, we had no trouble. NOTE: It's a strenuous climb with lots of winding metal staircases.  If you aren't in very good shape or if you are very afraid of heights, consider heading to the museum and skip the climb On to the good stuff.  Sigiriya is really an old city, which one can easily imagine in all its grandeur judging from what has been excavated and left for us to see.  I highly recommend hiring an official guide, who will tell you all about it as you go, who climbs with you the entire way start to finish and who, at least in our case, was able to bypass some of the long lines of others slowly working their way to the top. NOTE: There will be many many unofficial guides, men who will help you up every little stair step by taking your arm and walking with you and chatting in the hopes of you hiring them to make the climb with you.  They expect to be paid $20 for their efforts.  If you want a guide, engage them.  Otherwise, continue to firmly refuse their help and don't even make eye contact or return their friendly banter.  They will eventually leave you alone.  If they do not and you've already hired a guide, ask your guide to tell them you don't want their help. Now, enjoy!  It's a pretty amazing thing to see, along the lines of Machu Picchu.  Don't skip the museum at the bottom, but please know it's not air conditioned and you might find it a bit hot inside some of the exhibits. .
The view from the top is manificient. Its not that bad of a climb and once your up the top you can relax and take your time and soak up the views and the history.

This is an amazing place to visit.  I recommend going during November to February as the rains will fill all the ponds making it a spectacular place to visit.  Also the climb to the top won't be so hot.  The view from the top is stunning.  You should get a guide to explore the area and to learn some history.  Also the museum is good to visit.  If you have the time the area around the rock should be explored as there are many entrances.  This is one of my favorite places to visit.  I have been here over 30 times and I plan to go there another 30 times.

Was in two minds given the price but am glad I went. Expensive yes at SLR 3900. Have struggled more getting up a 500 step temple - steps all the way and a rail most of it. The crowd actually works in your favour as it slows down the climb and there are many places to catch your breath before moving on. Great views from the top and you really need to get to the summit to appreciate it all - lots of ancient ruins give it a great atmosphere. Read a few reviews about the other free rock and whilst that is an option I think it misses the point of what you get when you get to the summit of Sigiriya as they really are chalk and cheese.

I knew very little about this rock before the trip but it is certainly one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka. We visited early morning to avoid the heat as it is a challenging walk although not as daunting as it looks. Our guide was very informative and it certainly is a fascinating story  and a marvel for its early urban planning , organization ,gardening and art .The view from the top is well worth the effort.

This was a really interesting and enjoyable sight, especially as we had a really informative and friendly guide who explained a lot of background history. It's incredible to imagine how it must have looked and the work and ingenuity involved. The view from the top is stunning. We started at 4pm, so it was starting to cool down as we climbed. Also meant we got to see a stunning sunset from the top. The climb is not overly strenuous, it's definitely the heat that saps the strength (take plenty of water) so the higher you go the cooler it gets and easier the climb.

We were thrilled to change our route and drive to the North of Sri Lanka together with our friendly driver Some from Nadee Lanka tours. Despite the price for this visit is a rip off (we paid 52 EUR for 2 entrance tickets in February 2015!), we enjoyed the amazing 360 views after going up hundreds and hundreds of steps. For us the best time to go up was about 4:30pm - it was already not so hot and we managed to see the Mirror Wall when there were no tourists at all plus a breathtaking sunset just for 2 of us...not counting the monkeys :) Normally everyone goes to the right first and visits the Mirror Wall, but we actually chose a pass which led us to the left and then passed by the Mirror Wall on the way down to come back to the parking spot. It is not so well indicated when you come there, but no matter what - you will not get lost ;) Take the most comfortable shoes you've got and some water, it does take some energy to go up, despite it is quite well organised with the stairs most of the time. We met some people on the way who was climbing earlier and told us it is a nightmare in the sun, really tiring experience.

Its a must visit. We were completely in awe with this rock fortress which is a world heritage site. The paintings are amazing and also the view from the top and the final climb from the lion's foot. The water management of the site is just amazing as its still functional.

Went to the rock fortress with my wife, whom at first glance was put off the prospect of climbing all those steps for what she thought was nothing - however two recommendations I have for my fellow travellers - one - walk up the steps at a pace that that gets you slightly out of breath but not panting this will get you to the top without any trouble - if you pant your are travelling too fast, two - go to the top, it is a fantastic view and worth every effort. :)

The site is amazingly impressive. Hard to imagine how artisans and labourers were able to climb to the top of the massive rock  hundreds of years ago to create the outstanding buildings, statues and artworks. Watch out for the hornets nests and make sure you are fit enough to attempt the climb.

Expensive entry fee. The actual site was amazing however the guides and helpers don't take no for an answer and then rip you off at the end insisting on equivalent of £10 each before they let you out. Be warned

To climb up to the Rock Fortress you first walk along a long path, take some steps, walk flat again, take some steps again, until the normal road ends and you have to walk on an iron construction along the side of the mountain. It's not that it looks dangerous, but as I have a terrible fear of heights, my legs started trembling there already. From the iron pathway, you can go up a spiral staircase to see the frescos or walk straight through along the Mirror Wall (a wall that used to be so shiny you could see yourself in it) to the Lion Gate. You'll already have gotten some nice views by then but, of course, the ultimate view is to be had from on top of the rock. At least that's what they told me, because I have to admit I was too scared to climb up the steps to the top of the rock. Lots of people did it though, so if you're not terrified of heights, definitely go for it. A few tips: 1. There are a lot of Sri Lankans near the rock trying to sell their services of a guide. Be prepared to turn them down. 2. Take your camera, you'll see amazing views and a couple of monkeys as well 3. Don't ignore the warning signs for hornets. There are huge hornet nests hanging from the side of the rock and the hornets respond to noice. When it's really crowded, they can attack or swarm out and when they do you simply have to squat down and make yourself small.
I was dubious of this climb, but it's not that bad and it is worth it when you get to the top.. Take plenty of water with you if it's hot.

Ticket cost is 30 USD per head. Very crowded almost all the time. Best time to climb is before 8.30 in the morning. Rock fortress is about 200M high. Lots of steps. Make sure to carry few water bottles and towels with you.  Breathtaking views from the top.  Worth a visit if you love ancient architecture.
I have a heart condition and it looks really intimidating when you see it but there are fantastic views when you get to the top.  Top tip though, go early before it gets too hot

An effort to get to the top +1000 steps but well worth it. I was travelling solo and took a guide, which was helpful. Do not accept the assistance of the guys "helping" rather pathetically people to climb up- they simply want cash and apparently up to $20! As with all the cultural sites, entrance costs are steeper than one might imagine but this was worth it and if choosing between Dambulla and here, this would be my preference.

The climb is absolutely wonderful. Lovely scenery everywhere you look and a nice cool breeze blows as you get towards the top of the rock.  The 360 degree view from the top is well worth the effort it takes to get up there, seeing for kilometres in every direction! While the cost is a little high for what it is, (3900 lkr, or about $40 Australian), the climb is not that difficult and should be a 'must do' if you are visiting Kandy or northern Sri Lanka. Make sure you wear a hat and take lots of water as it is very hot and humid.

While initially hesitant to climb Lion Rock due to the most inaccurate reviews about its difficulty, it quickly became obvious that this is a very manageable ascent/descent.  Take your time, walk slowly, stop often, and relishes original fresco painting and the fabulous view. A Definite Must!

This was at the top of our TO DO list on our recent and first trip to Sri Lanka. Go prepared...water, good footwear and just take your time. It is a truly spectacular hike to the top and it is not for the faint hearted or those scared of heights, but if you can overcome your fears you will be truly rewarded when you reach the remains of the palace on the top. The area where the original frescoes remain on the wall - about two thirds of the way up are accessed via a steep spiral staircase which then leads to a small steel balcony that hangs over the side of the rock - its solid, but a bit shaky when there are a lot of people on it - just be prepared if you are of a slightly nervous disposition. The views are breathtaking - you can see for kilomteres and it is worth just sitting down and trying to imagine the grandeur when it was a palace. The whole site is vast - you could easily spend the best part of a day here if you wanted to really explore and enjoy the gardens too. As we made our descent from the top we were met by the monkeys making their way up, just inches away. It was an incredible experience, especially at 400ft in the air on a narrow metal staircase - hold your nerve - they won't hurt you, but they will not budge either...it is very much their territory so respect them and they'll just walk on by so you can continue your descent. We were fortunate enough in that we had our own driver / official tourist guide - it meant we were not harrased by any of the so called unofficial 'guides' who are inside the grounds and will try to get you to acquire their services. Our only complaint was about some of the other tourists there who who had aboslutely appalling manners and no respect for other visitors. Shouting, obnoxious and no manners - telling other people to move so they could have photos without anybody else in them. Not a good advert for Far East visitors I'm afraid! Other than that a truly fantastic experience.
We took one look at the crowds at Sigiria and decided that for th eprice this was not for us. It was heaving with too many people. If you dont mind that good luck to you and it is expensive too

This world heritage site is definitely worth a visit.  It is full of history which is worth reading up if you don't go with a guide. It is a slog up the rock and the rate is determined by the slowest person as a lot if it is single file up vertical spiral staircases etc.  It takes time! About half way up are the spectacular frescoes in remarkable condition and even if you go no further these are definitely worth seeing.  A little further on about half way up is the lion gate with the massive lions paws cut into the Rock.  They are quite amazing.  The view from the top is spectacular although it was quite hazy when we were there.  The fortress ruins on top are interesting and particularly considering how everything must have been carried up there to construct such an extensive complex. Best allow 2 to 3 hours for a visit.  In the morning at least the climb up is mainly in the shade of the rock.

To climb on this mountain is a little bit challenging especially when you go there not in the morning or afternoon - really hot, no wind! But when you are on the top, you forget all these inconveniences - amazing view around and lot of monkeys :-)

I have been there in february and there was a lot of people. After the frescoes (really beautiful and conservative well) the Sigiriya team have blocked me (and all the other people): there was a wasps attack in act. I waited for 3 hours with the other people and a monkeys family, in this time the staff has evacuated the rock's top. was not pssibile find out whether they would have reopened on the top and big part of the visitors has decided to go away. after 3 hours I decided to try to go up. in front of the the beginning of the stair there was a small group of visitors and the staff. the team told us to stay in silence (the noise provoke wasps attack), they gave us the waterproof jacket and we decided to try to go up! was really amazing! only 15 persons on the top and a really wonderful view. thanks to the wasps we visited the rock in only few people and we had the opportunity to enjoy it in all the splendor! the only fault was the price: 30 dollars per person and inside is not as clean as you would expect compared to the price.
Both the city, the rock and the nature around it is incredible. This is definitely a place to visit!

While I loved climbing on the Sigriya rock, there are many things that need to be done to preserve this site and also to help tourists actually enjoy the trip. Too much crowd. Imagine kids of an entire school going up on the stairs along with hundreds of tourists and locals. Very tricky. Perhaps school days could be fixed to avoid any accidents and extra traffic on such a tricky climb. The entrance fee is exorbitantly high but I managed to get it for half because of a SAARC passport (they don't cut the prices at Dambulla for some reason). You could try to get to Pidurangala instead as it only costs around lkr500 and see the rock without any extreme human traffic too.

Definitely not one of the fittest and took me a few short breaks but it was worth it. You can take a rest for half an hour or so near the paws as there's a water tank and spaces to sit and relax to help you finish the last leg of the climb. Don't miss this one at any cost! Tip: keep a couple bottles of water with you; one side of the rock faces sun directly so it's quite hot. Also, wear comfortable, minimal clothes to help you conquer this fortress.
An Engineering Marvel. A must visit in Sri Lanka!!I f you are into Sri Lankan history. this is a good place to visit.

Can't imagine its 1500 years old. Frescos are the marvel. Mirror wall is on the way to frescos and having Graffiti written by ancient visitors. Ruins on the top of the rock is unbelievable. Water fountains in the garden are still working. This is called as 8th wonder of the world. Make sure to notice gardening structure.
Start early (we were there at 7,30) and bring lots of water. Not only is it much hotter later in the day but the queues are terrible.

The climb to the top is not as hard as it looks.  The reward for your effort is worth every step.  The ruins are amazing and very interesting.  The views from the top in all directions are incredibly beautiful.

Really incredible place! Its quite effort to get on top but if you have two legs you should handle it. On your way on the rock wall you will see some old beutiful paintings. When you will almost reach the top be aware of the bees  nest sticked to the rocks. On the top the view is really breathtaking. When we walked down not the main Road we found a guy with cobra Snake and some Python. For some money we could make some movies and photos with them.
