It is a nice challenge climbing the maze of stairs leading to the highest part of the rock. A true world heritage - not to be missed

First off - don't make the mistake we did and start your climb right around noon!  It was incredibly hot and the sun was killer...especially for this redhead! :)   Even though we picked a bad time to climb, it was worth every drop of sweat and the following sunburn.  Do know that it is quite a hike up a LOT of stairs; I can't remember the exact number, though. The locals that offer to "help" you are doing it for a fee - if you don't intend to pay them, tell them up front that you aren't interested, otherwise they will stick to you like glue and then at the end ask for money. Enjoy the views from the top and all of the monkeys hanging around.  It is a truly incredible view, and it's amazing to sit and think about how they were able to build things on top of the rock so long ago.  The professor that took us on the trip is originally from Sri Lanka and was telling us how he remembers scaling up the side of the rock before all of the stairs were in place.  Amazing!  (and pretty scary!) The "mirror wall" and lion are both great things to see on the way to the top!  :)

This is one place that should not be missed during a visit to Sri Lanka. Though it is a very daunting task to climb 1200+ steps, standing atop the Rock (supposedly King's throne!) and turning head in all the directions gives great sense of achievement! The Fresco paintings from 5th century that you see here is a matter of national identity (one of many) and could be seen in various paintings, wood carvings all over the country! I was truly awe'd by the fact that these paintings have been preserved for so many centuries for all of us to see and relish!! Thanks to UNESCO!! Seniors (50+ years) may want to plan the trip in such a way to ensure atleast 90 minutes to climb the rock. "Guides" to help aged or physically challenged people are available as soon as you enter the main gate. These "guides" appear from nowhere and ask for $25! Being from India, I was used to these "helps" and settled for a price of Indian Rupees of 500 ($10 apporx..hope it was a good deal). The guide was very helpful and helped my mother climb all the way till the Lion's claw and also helped her to climb down the fort - very impressed! I did not have enough time to visit the museum but learnt that I did not miss anything that important!

If you have health problems don't do this climb - it is steps - up the face of the rock - at certain levels there were caves with ancient paintings on the walls and statues of budha etc.   The view when you reach the top is panoramic - how they built places up that height is unreal.   Well worth the effort when you do get to the top - and then you have to come all the way down again!!!!
Just the beauty and the amazing feat of building and paintings of the rock of Lion.

Interesting and amazing site.  Take a bottle of water.  Do the climb early in the morning say 730am to avoid the heat and crowds.  It's fairly straight forward and you can go up to the top and back down 2.5 hours.  Plenty of steep steps though and could get slow going if stuck behind slower people.

Place is wonderful! Awesome piece of history. It's impressive how they built a palace on top of a rock. Few things useful to know before you get there, based on my experience: 1. Tickets cost $30 per person. It includes "free" DVD with a 10-minute film, which I could see on youtube for fee anyway. 2. Start your climb early in the morning, before the sun didn't start burning. Up on the top there is almost no shade, so you'll anyway end up standing under direct sun. The earlier you start, the less you'll get burnt. 3. Politely (as much as your patience allows), ask the "so-called" guides to leave, if you don't want to pay them for few introductory sentences and following you all the way up to the end. We were annoyed by a guy who just stuck to us like a gum. I told him, we don't need a guide, because I'd read all I needed to know in Wikipedia before leaving for Lanka. He insisted he wasn't a tour guide, but was introducing us to the place out of his sole interest and as hobby. In the end of the tour he asked 1000 rupees for his "hobby". If you anyway chose to be accompanied by one of these guys, pay them as much as you feel it worth. Do not be cheated by urges, and examples of "good people pay me 2000". I can understand the need of people to earn money, so had he shot his price right from the beginning, I'd agree. But cheating? No way. 3. Make sure you take a bottle of water with you. We thought we'd buy one on the way, but couldn't see anyone selling anything all the way until we were down the rock and heading back to the car.

The Rock fortress is the best place in Sri lanka !!! Although u need to travel a lot to reach up there so u must plan up you visit so as to see the places in between like Dambulla, Anuragpura, KAndy .... so u must pan up south to north as accordingly !!!

Sri Lanka is a little country but it an unexpectedly wide range of ancient monuments, some of them amongst the best in the Hindu-Buddhist world. Apart from its two marvellous ancient capitals, it also boasts the sumptuous rock fortress of Sigiriya, which sits high on an outcrop above the surrounding plains. Boasting some erotic art in the rock shelters, some magnificent stone dams and staircases, a giant stone lion's paw and mighty rock walls, it is one of the finest military structures we have ever seen. Add to that the amazing views and you will have one of your best days in Sri Lanka here.

Sigiriya is One of the best site in Sri lanka, This is an awesome place, so much history here.Views of the jungle when standing atop a very interesting course and there is a fresco of the world-famous beauty, rugged mountains to climb after the palace is the best that is made to a steep rocky mountain.

Sri Lanka is an extremely hot country - you will be soaking wet from sweat 99% of the time BUT don't let that deter you from visiting one of the most incredible places in the country, Sigiriya.  You won't need a guide or a "pusher" (young SL men offer to push and pull you up the mountain/rock), just take your time and enjoy.  Get there first thing in the morning and read all of the information at the stations along the way.  The climb is very, very strenuous, but do it anyway - your sense of accomplishment will be high.  There is a lot to admire and look at all the way from the entrance booth - this is not a 20 minute stop.  We were there several hours.  The "toilet" facilities are appalling, but they are like that in most of the public areas in the entire country.  Make sure you have 20 rupees to pay the attendant at the toilet.

I was in Srilanka for Paramotor training. The training  field is close to Dambulla  (Sigiriya). In the day time we can't train because is too windy and too hot then we have some time to do some thing nice. Than our friends drive us to Sigiriya and when i was there i just say " WOW " that is high rock  !!!  And our friend told to us " you have to climp up there " then  i said " let's go " That is long walk and climing. On the way up you will see nice drawing of the queen and that drawing is 500 years old still beautiful. And on top of the mountian you can see beautiful forest around the mountain. Is very beautiful. I was there for about 30 minutes because the last point is a bit difficle to climp but i made it YEAH !!!

After reading previous reviews I wasn't convinced I could make the climb but I did and if I can do it the majority of others can! I'm not at all fit but by visiting as soon as the site opened at 7am, taking our time with rests between flights of steps and drinking lots of water we made it - my husband did take it slowly on account of me! Up and down in just under 2 hours with time at the top to take photos and rest a while. It was much quieter at this time and was starting to get busier by the time we left which would make the climb slower. If you do not want a helper just politely say "no" and keep walking, they weren't too persistent. The cave paintings were lovely and surprisingly still vibrant - and a nice break to view part way up. The views from the top are wonderful.
The guides tend to be in a hurry - more people, more money (remember they only get paid if they have punters, so don't be mean). But the site is awesome.

This really is one of the wonderful things to see in the world.  Minor quibbles about pushy "guides" and initial entry cost aside, the view from the top is outstanding, and the history of the "fortress" is very evocative.

The entry ticket for foreign tourists  seems to be daylight robbery -- but c'est la vie.  And as with any government org, morose employees. Keep in mind that there are unlicensed, uninvited "helpers" lurking around who will "help" you for some monetary considerations, be your guide etc -- 100% fraud.  They may be very aggressive.  Gotta push back heavily.

Sigiriya is a large stone and ancient rock fortress in Matale, Sri Lanka. The climb to the top is steep but very worth the effort. You will be rewarded by 360 degree views that are unsurpassed. It is interesting to walk around the palace ruins at the top. The ancient frescoes and the gardens are amazing. This is a popular tourist destination and was one of the highlights of our holiday. Do not miss this unbelievable experience.

This was one of the first sights I visited whilst on a ten day tour of Sri Lanka. I approached it with trepidation as I am not a lover of heights. My 2 teenage kids wife and  I arrived at about 9.30 and it wasn't too busy or overly hot. My only disappointment was that I was unable to buy a cultural triangle ticket from the ticket office which would have included this sight and others at a reduced rate as they do not acept cerdit/debit cards.. CASH only, I barely had enough to cover the entrance to this sight alone. Be mindful that tourists are exploited and that you will pay the same sort of prices you would to enter attractions in the UK and USA. The locals will pay a much reduced fee. For example a tea picker only earns about 400-500 rupees a day ($5/ £3)and will therefore only be expected to pay about 200 rupees to enter a sight or temple. You will be charged to use the toilet facilities but at least you will be provided with paper. Wear sensible shoes, although I saw people do it barefoot and in flipflops and take some water. A couple of hours should be enough if you are reasonably fit. There were groups of school kids 7-9 yr old shimmying up it with no problem. There are touts who will go away if you are firm, just don't show an interest in anything they are trying to sell or let them take your photo. I made it half way before giving in to my fear of heights. My daughter made it to the top and made the mistake of having her photo taken. She was hounded all the way down the stairs but the tout soon disappeared when confronted by me. This should be an enjoyable experience which on the whole it was. I got chatting to a group of older schoolgirls who were surrepticiously photographing my blue eyed blond haired son and we all had a good laugh.

On our trip to Sri Lanka, I was told about the Lion Rock and though meh what's so special about it, but once you reach there and look up from the base... it is breathtaking.  The 2000+ steps to get to the top is quite a workout and there is a lot to see on your way up, from the thousand year old paintings, to the remains of the lion himself.  My only complaint from this whole experience was the cost to enter, which compared to other world heritage sites, seemed a little steep at $35USD pp, but in the end it was something I am glad I did at least once in my life.
Great visit and local guide, spent at least 2plus hours there and enjoyed it the climb taken steadily was fine

The view from the top was brilliant! On the way up a local man took hold of my arm and tried 'assisting' me up the steps - they do this so you tip them at the top. However, i removed his hand a couple of times and told him i was fine to do it on my own. Just be clear with them and they leave you alone.

The best time to climb is in the early morning. It is still hot but the occassional breeze is a big help. The frescoes are amazing and they alone are worth the climb but the view from the top is fabulous. Our guide was very knowledgeable but did expect a large tip, at least 1000 rupees. This can get a little annoying as we were on an all-inclusive guided tour. However, he was worth it and it is still a small price to pay for a terrific experience.

It was amazing to see the two moats surrounding the fortress with a warning about crocodiles!! IF you have time, take a walk in the gardens at the foot of the hill. Just when you wonder if you should give up, there is a resting place halfway, where the giant front paws of lion guards the entrance to the top. And of course you are rewarded by the 360 degree view when you get to the top. The bathing pool at the top must have been an amazing luxury. On the way down, we took a different route, and were rewarded by meditation spots, under rock-overhangs in which either the king or monks must have used.
A must if you are visiting Sri Lanka. Not as daunting as it looks. Worth the 1200 steps. Would go back tomorrow.

Pros: + great park, well kept grounds + great view from the top + good museum + fun entrance ticket with CD Cons - touts. - expensive park entrance fee ($30) - a bit out of the way (not a problem if you are on a tour) - fair amount of litter - groundskeepers use the cistern as their personal bath, which is strange, to say the least I arrived early in the morning and was actually the first one up the rock that morning.  Before even purchasing my ticket I was hounded by a tout who wanted to serve as a tour guide.  I had to politely tell him off several times that I simply was not interested:  there wasn't much he could tell me in his limited English that the museum, provided CD, numerous signs, or guidebooks couldn't.  Soon enough, I was being tailed during my ascent by a groundskeeper who wanted to take my photo, and wanted a fee for it.  I had to tell him thanks, but not thanks, several times, before almost being rude to him.  Rather than enjoy time along at the top of this great rock, I had this guy jabbering in my ear, telling me where to go, and asking, then demanding to take my photo.  They're called timers and they're built in cameras for a reason...Paying someone 100 rupees to take photos of you would defeat the point of buying a camera with one of those things...  At the top, a couple of stray dogs and groundskeepers bathing in the cistern were a strange, but interesting sight.  Upon leaving, I was accosted yet again, this time for a fee to use the bathroom.  Doesn't the $30 entrance fee cover that?  I guess not. All in all, what should be a great 5-star attraction, but I pegged it down 2 notches for the expensive entrance fee (compare, for example with $20 to enter Cambodia's impressive Angkor Wat complex), and for having to fight my way through touts or groundskeepers demanding "tips" for simply breathing the same air I was.

One of the most stunning places on earth! Sigirya Rock Fortress has to be a must see item for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. The views from the various stopping points on your way to the top are breathtaking and the 360 degree panoramic views from the top are incredible! Although 1200+ steps this is by no means a hard climb, start early and you will manage in comfort. We were lucky enough to have our driver / guide Koshala Rathnayake as well as a specific Sigiriya guide who knew all the history and culture of this incredible site. The initial  climb is stepped and longer than that for example to the Dambulla Temple. The second part is on caged stairs, which while safe is not for those who are claustrophobic. Though it's one of the more pricey attractions (US $30 per person), and although it is a very strenuous climb to the top, the ancient rock fortress of Sigiriya is well worth it! Upon arrival, be prepared to be approached by numerous guides offering their services to take you to the top. The 1st time we went, I used such a guide and it was well worth it. They are friendly and are very knowledgeable about the fortress, the surrounding areas and its history. 1st make sure you set a price in advance! They will tell you "let let me take you around, I'll give you a great tour and then you can tell me what you think it's worth at the end" SET the price 1st or be prepared to have them tell you it's 2500 rupees (around $25). We paid $10. Also, if you decide to forgo a guide, you will be approached probably several times (at least) by guides that will point out facts about the area you are standing in - they will then 'join' you and unless you tell them "no, you're on your on" they will stay with you and expect some payment (this is what happened on our 2nd visit). But beyond the slight hassle of 'guides', you will find yourself quickly overwhelmed by the physical enormity of this place and the beautiful attributes that abound here. From the pools that King Kassapa built for his concubines (supposedly he had around 500) to the giant Lion paws, remnants of a once massive statue that you pass through as you make your way up the many steps to the top, there are wondrous things to see everywhere. Sigiriya is especially well known for its ancient frescoes painted high up within indentations in the cliff faces - absolutely amazing to think that these were done around the fifth century AD and with nothing more than ropes and bamboo ladders to get up there. Also, be sure to ask your guide about the defense mechanism that King Kassapa employed to protect the stronghold (you can see it - a massive boulder on staged, smaller rocks - these rocks could be hammered away allowing the giant boulder to crash down the hillside into attackers below). Despite the arduous climb, there are numerous stopping points all along the way and yo can certainly (and should) time your rests accordingly. (one important point - BRING water - there are no facilities and no water for sale). From the outset of your journey, you will find spectacular views but nothing compares to the top where you have a truly amazing 360 degree view of the lands all around. To the south you will see the mountains that house Kandy - to the Northwest you can see virtually all of the way to Anuadhapura and to the Northeast, the jungles of Minneriya and the lake that sits next to the ancient city of Polonnaruwa is visible. It is simply breathtaking. Good news on the trek down too - you don't go back the way you came. There's a shortcut and although you do come down part of the same way, the trip down is much shorter.

From the moment you arrive by the 'crocodile moat' you know you're in for something special. We were a family of 4 (2 x teenagers) & as you walk through the water gardens and look up the impressive rock - you do wonder how you will get up there! I suggest getting there early, you can take your time, not feel pressured and if you are nervous of heights you can take it in your stride. It really is a quite unbelievable experience. The walk to the base of the rock whilst tiring is by no means arduous. What follows next is walking up essentially a spiral caged stairwell and entering caves to see the various paintings / images. It is a fabulous vantage point to look around before you enter the cave. You then leave by way of another caged stairwell descending to the marble wall. I think this is the hardest part of the trip, it just seems more exposed and because there may be lots of people you may feel rushed.the trick again is to just take your time & you'll thoroughly enjoy it. From there you climb to the Lion Paws courtyard and through the entrance up the steps to the top of the fortress. The views are stunning & assuming it's a clear day it's worth taking in the views and absorbing the surrounds. We all really enjoyed this, it's a must see attraction if you are visiting Sri Lanka.

We were feeling a bit undecided about visiting Sigirya – we were worried about the climb (I’m really unfit), plus from what I had read before we left, I couldn’t work out why a big rock could really be that interesting. In the end, it was one of the highlights of our fortnight’s holiday. The climb is done in lots of chunks, with places to stop in between and interesting things to look at, so I didn’t find it hard at all (although I skipped the very last bit after the lion's paws, which is the only bit that's on narrow metal stairs rather than wide stone staircases - it didn't look like I was missing much!). The place itself is just amazing. Walking up through the remains of the water gardens towards this huge lump of rock sticking straight up out of the jungle gives you such a sense of how ostentatious and intimidating the place must originally have been – especially painted all over with thousands of naked ladies! Then you begin the climb, past huge boulders, caves with bits of surviving paintings, the ‘Assembly Hall’ with its throne and so on, and the view gets more wonderful the higher up you get – it was raining when we went, and the fog in the air made the whole thing even more gobsmacking. The painted ladies in the one cave where they’ve survived are just absolutely beautiful and serene – somehow not salacious at all. And the lion’s paws are crazy – the idea of a king making his servants climb through the throat of a lion to get to his palace really hits you when you see them. We found the drive to the rock from Habarana really lovely, too, as our driver took us down an alternative route on a poorly finished road that’s known for great wildlife sightings – we saw about 20 species of birds, plus land monitors, grey langurs and a mongoose. There’s supposed to be lots of wildlife around Sigirya itself, but we didn’t see much, perhaps because it was pouring with rain. We visited in late afternoon – about 3.30, I think – and I’d recommend that as an option. It’s not so hot, the light hitting the rock is beautiful, and we managed the impressive timing of being the last people to be allowed inside the painted cave.

We visited the citadel of Sigiriya on a sunny Christmas Day in December 2011, and therefore did not experience climbing under the rain. Indeed this is the best cultural visit we did in Sri-Lanka: 3 hours to enjoy this wonderful site (but 6 hours would be better for a detailed visit). The 360º view on the top of the rock is just amazing and is the best reward for climbing. The lower parts building, pools and fountains remains are truly interesting as they give a nice hint on former dwellers lifestyle and religious customs. The ruins upstairs are well preserved. We took the time to visit all citadel corners and it is worth spending 30mn to do it. Half way to the top of the citadel, a rusty spiral iron staircase brought us safely to the well-preserved frescoes / painting on the rocks: a moving piece of ancient art. We took a short break on the platform before lions feet and final climb, being careful that monkeys/macaques did not jump on us to taste our cookies. The final staircases steps are small and require some attention to avoid incidents. We arrived around 11am and crowd was quite dense, obliging us to queue before every stairs. Some tips: - Make sure your driver is using the “Foreign visitors” Car Pak right next to the site main gate (the “Local visitors” is almost 1 Mile away). - Make sure the local tour guide offering his services is speaking a decent English, otherwise you may be disappointed (we gave him five hundred Rupees). A good guide book would certainly be a good alternative. - Do not forget to bring good shoes (no high heels!) and 1-2 liters of water per person. - The granite steps are slippery with a coat of dust; therefore be careful of potential hazards caused by other visitors falling down. - Even if you are suffering from vertigo, just do it anyway and you won’t regret it. - We spotted “wasp attack” warnings but did not see any (may be Christmas break for them as well). - The Sri-Lankan authorities’ decision to discriminate between “Foreign visitors” and “Local visitors” is disappointing: entrance fee for foreigners is quite high (30 USD).

Before visiting Sri Lanka In knew very little of Sigiriya, it mentioned it in tour books, but we just so happened to have booked in at a nearby hotel and for this reason visited the fortress, and now having visited I can not believe this place does not have more of an international reputation - it is easily one of the most incredible places I have visited. Yes, it is a bit of a walk to the top, but its very manageable, particularly if you want to take your time, there are lots of spots to stop on the way. And once you reach the top, you will instantly be so glad you did. The rock is a fascinating piece of history and I particularly enjoy the idea of a mad monarch deciding to build his fortress in the most inaccessible place possible, just because he could. As well as the rock, the grounds around are extremely impressive, including a water fountain garden that, despite being thousands of years old, still spurts out fountains when it rains. I think what made it such an incredible experience for us was that we made the effort to go as early as possible. I would say this is the best piece of advice I could possibly give. Not only do you avoid the heat for the climb, but you also maximise your chance of getting the place to yourself. We were lucky to be totally alone for large parts of our visit and this afforded the whole place such an air of mystery and in many senses made you feel like you were right back in time. And to reach the top and be on your own is simply one of the best experiences you will have. All around you are surrounded by wonderful ancient ruins, and then looking out into the forest of Sri Lanka and the perfect skies and sun. Get up early, if you don't, you'll wish you had! As other reviews have alluded to, there are many guides who will try to insist on taking you to the top. But just be polite and assertive if you don't want any help. Finally worth mentioning that you buy the tickets from a small little hotel nearby - we thought this seemed a little bit dodgy (perhaps as it was the same tuk-tuk driver who was trying to sell us bootleg arrack!) and thought maybe we were being taken for a ride, but it proved to be the way to buy the tickets. Don't miss these place if you are in Sri Lanka. And I would also very much recommend the nearby Hotel Sigiriya if you are looking for somewhere nearby to stay. Its on tripadvisor with very favourable reviews, to which I am just about to add another!

Surely with the entrance money collected they can afford a decent toilet for visitors. The view from the top was stunning:-)

30US per person and who wants a CD! However unfortunately like most things in the world, you have travelled all this way and you just have to suck it up, because to be honest it is pretty impressive, After reading the lonely planet ( I did have a chuckle) i was in two minds on whether getting a guide. well in the end proberbly should have given it a miss, he told us nothing more than what was written in the "book of lies", it is a nice place to wonder around and have a good look and the view from the top is impressive. I would rate it up there with one of the best attractions in Sri lanka, that we did anyway. Go see for yourself

There is nothing to dislike other than the price! :) 30 USD including a CD, well, it's once in a lifetime, right? Place is gorgeous, sorrounded by nature in all shapes, colours and smells, old grass-covered staircases bount with roots of ancient trees and the views from the top are just to die for. The climb up is not that hard just slightly breathtaking for vertigo sufferers at some points. I really recommend to be there at very first time in the morning to get the best picture with no one else on the background it really makes the difference, trust me! Not to be missed! Enjoy your time in Sri Lanka!

A site not to be missed, but not for the elderly or faint-hearted.  We climbed the 1292  steps at 8a.m - too late (it was too hot).  But what a sense of achievement when we got to the top.  Spectacular views, a fascinating history and countless photo opportunities.  However, despite the $30 entrance fee per person (almost as steep as the rock) you will still need a good registered guide (1500 rupees), or at least a good guide book.  Beware the 'helpers' who try to assist you up the steps - there's one at every turn and they all want rewarding.  Make sure your heart and lungs are up to it - there's nothing in the way of medical assistance on the way up.
This was a nice half-day trip. It's a little reminiscent of Angkor Wat - not as grand, but elevated with great jungle views. The stair climb is very well equipped so no issues for anyone there.

The view from the top of the rock is magnificent. The gardens look lush and green. The winded stairs can take a toll on you, so I would suggest carrying a bottle of water along with you. It takes around an hour to get to the top, so it would be best to start a bit early so you miss the afternoon sun.
Climbing high stairs in really not for everybody  but still worth of, you may believe! And that vew from the top of the Rock, unbeliveable!

On the road from Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa there is a place called Lions Rock, 200 m high. Seldom conglomeration of  craftsmanship specimens of town-planning, architecture, landscape architecture, horticulture,  engineering, hydraulics but also art  from V century. One of Sri Lanka's  marvels.

This is one of the most amazing sites in the world.  Don't miss the climb to the top. As you climb  the rock you see several amazing sites including fantastic paintings. The children also loved the climb.
make sure you leave early to climb before the sun hots up too much, worth the effort though

Pleased to be there at 08.30 because it wasn't too hot and more importantly there were fewer tourists, which meant we could walk at our own pace and not be hindered during the climb. By the time we were coming down, around 09.30 there were lots of visitors. We were there on a Saturday, so obviously a lot more families at the weekend.

Little did we know that we'd be in for a workout as we set out to visit the Lion's Rock!! It is a rather steep climb and some parts are almost vertical. The first pitsop on the way is a cave which has paintings dating back to the earliest centuries. It was truly a wonder to find such artistry in a place as treacherous. We then continued our climb to the top. Enroute is a passage with a mirror wall. When the sun's rays fall on this wall, the surface glistens like a mirror! Its a long way up, but we trodded on and we reached the top of the rock. And what a sight it was!No wonder this place was declared as the 8th wonder of the world! If you are planning a trip to Sri Lanka, then Sigriya is definitely worth a visit! Tip 1 - If you are interested in heritage sites in Sri Lanka, a round trip pass for Sigriya, Polanaruwa and Anuradhapura is available at the ticket counter for 25 USD for citizens of SAARC countries and 50 USD for other foreign nationals. Tip 2 - If you are interested in Hot air ballooning to the top of the Lion's rock, there is an operator who organizes a 4 hour excursion that begins at 6 am. Most hotels in Sigriya would be able to provide the details. (We were unable to do this due to bad weather). This requires booking in advance!

Really good, best time to go is early in morning or late afternoon to avoid heat and queues. We went late afternoon and saw the sun set over a magnificent vista of the Sri Lankan jungles and plains. Watch out of guides touting their services at various places in and around the site. Some places this can be a good thing to do to get the most out of the visit, but not here. A decent guide book will be more than enough. Give yourself at least 3 hours to get up and down and be able to explore the site properly.
Awesome! Very cool climb with a scary part rewarded with an espansive park from which to enjoy the view

The view, the cave paintings all beautiful. Not as hard a climb as I though, and plenty of rest stops along the way if you need them. Make sure you climb early in the morning or late in the afternoon as it gets really hot and really crowded in the middle of the day

Yes, you look up from the base and wonder if you can do it, but it's a question of taking it slowly and steadily, drinking plenty and resting when you feel like it. This is an interesting place, with lots to see and a truly magnificent view from the top. My friend has a pin in her leg and was worried, but she did it, even the spiral staircase. Don't miss it!
A unique experience, but still hard to justify the entrance fee of USD 30 or SL rupees 3750, charged to tourist/foreigners.

Even if you have very limited time in Sri Lanka, visiting Sigiriya is a must. This huge citadel is truly one of its kind in this world, if nothing else. The frescoes of the beautiful maidens that adorns a section of the wall is still in good condition, the body or authority looking after this place is doing a good job of trying to maintain it as it is. The climb up the steps, from the lions paw up to the top on the steel steps and bolted to the side of the rock, gives us a wonderful view of the surrounding landscapes, we could see other attractions from here, such as Dambulla caves, Aukana Buddha. Take the climb at your own pace, there is no rush. At the very top, i dont have the words to describe the feeling, as words would not do any justice to what we can see and feel from the very top.

This beautiful rock formation is incredibly gorgeous and worth it. The hike up isn't bad, just take your time and go slowly and rest when you need to. The view at the top is worth it, as is learning about all the different rock formations. This was the best part of my trip.

If you can imagine how this fortress would have looked and felt so long ago, then you will have an excellent visit.  From the ambition of a king to the protection of Buddhist monks, this place must have looked stunning in its day. Flowing water through the gardens, paintings on plaster more enduring than that of Victorian London, and swimming pools 200m above the surrounding jungle.  And the view of a relatively unspoilt jungle carpet alone makes this worth a visit.

Do it! Even if you are scared of heights (as i am) you can make it to the top and enjoy some incredible views. Make sure to take a guide (cost around 2000 rupees) and make sure to take water and good footwear as some steps are quite narrow.

A fascinating climb up the huge Lion Rock, though not good for vertigo sufferers.  You start going up steep stone staircases, and then proceed to metal walkways which are literally bolted onto the side of the rock, connected by spiral staircases hanging over the void.  Worth doing, but a mite scary if you don't like heights.

The Sigiriya Rock climb could easily be the highlight of my trip! The  climb up is well worth the effort as the views are amazing, enroute one gets to see well preserved frescoes cave paintings. The symmetrical gardens and the surrounding moats are beautifully maintained. It well worth getting one of the certified guides. A good guide would go a long way to get the most from your visit.

This is a fantastic place to visit and see the remains of an ancient palace in the sky.  The view from all sides of the rock is spectacular and you discover the man-made resovoir and what was once a thriving royal community - amazing

In October 2011,  I had the priviledge of visiting Sigiriya for the 2nd time.  Wearrived after 4:00 and realizing that the site closes around 5:30, we wandered through the rock gardens and started to ascend the rock.  The spiral staircase takes you to the mirror wall, which affords great vistas of the surrounding area, as well as allowing you to get close up and personal with the ancient frescoes.  Then you descend via another spiral staircase before following the walkway up to the paws of the lion, after which the rock is named.  This is still, for me the most impressive part of the visit.  The huge lion paws can only ibnite the imagination as to what the actual carved statue of the lion used to look like...and of course access to the rock platform is still through those paws. The final ascent is on metal walkways.  It takes a bit of energy to ascend, and is not necessarily for those with a fear of heights, but it is really not too demanding and once at the top, the views are wonderful.   In our case we were there close to sunset and the shadows provided wonderful photographic opportunities.  The monkeys, are amusing, although one still needs to exercise a bit of caution in their presence and a firm grasp of your hat, glasses, purse, camera case etc is needed to prevent monkey-thefts. We did wait for the sun to set before heading down, and again, the vistas were wonderful.  By the time we returned to our bus, it was actually dark. Sigiriya is one of those magical places.  Hint:  Read up on the history before you visit so you can appreciate the various myths and legends surrounding the origins of the site--and don't be afraid to let your imagination run wild as you explore this unique UNESCO site.

We stayed at a hotel miles away but could still see the mammoth rock.  When we got to the site there was a couple of 'guides' touting for business, they claim the signs and information about the rock and area aren't in English...they are and it's not like you need a guide to tell you where the rock is! I did hear one guide telling some tourists what I am sure are untruths about the site, about the paintings in the cave (which are beautiful) and the reason and usage of the top of the rock.  As we climbed the last set of steps a man began pointing out bits of land you could see, we just smiled to be polite, but as we reached the top and sat down the man sat down with us, we explained we didn't need a guide but he asked for money - he didn't get any (I'm sure this is a rare accurance, as everyone is really nice, however, very poor). Take lots of water and a trusty guide book, we climbed the rock in 37 degree heat and was wet with sweat on the first set of steps, but as you reach the top it is well worth the view (also the wind cools you down!).

The rock is a must climb - 1200 steps is not as bad as it sounds.  The view from the top is amazing and the cave drawings amazingly well preserved.  In December it may rain but if it is light a hat is sufficient.  It does get windy at the top.

The rock is a good historical place to visit. It is helpful to gt a licensed guide. The going rate is 1,500 Sri Lankan rupees. Carry your passport - rates are based on nationality. There is a tiny place that sells water, fo those who are about to climb and have run out. The place can get crowded, especially on holidays. The steel stairway going up the face of the cliff was a little scary for the kids. We had our 20 month old in an Ergo on our back.

First of all you would be surprised by the level of civilization the was there many years ago. The most important tip is to find a good guide - as there are many interesting facts that he can share with you. Take some water with you as you will have a long way up under the sun. On your way downstairs there will be many people trying to sell you unique souvenirs from Sigiriya which is a RIP OFF. You can find all that stuff in the city several times cheaper!

One of the highlights of Sri Lanka. The frescoes are worth seeing if nothing else, but the whole complex is really interesting. If you are able, get a guide to take you up, as they can impart a lot of knowledge about the sight. We had a guide called Alfred who was brilliant.

Had been loking forward to seeing the rock for 40 years and we still haven't seen it as it was hidden in the clouds.  Even from the village and Danbulla we could not see the rock.  Ho-hum, that's the joy of travelling. I am still pleased that we went there and had the place to ourselves in the warm but torrential rain. Good luck for your trip

Its Massive , is huge, with a lot of history and culture , you can go there, take pictures , but do not climb the rock , its massive and tiring , with monkeys around , instead if you go to Heritance Kandalama you can get a better view of Dambulla and Sigiriya

Great history. Its a steep climb of 1200 steps..but worth it. Pls do take a guide who will explain the history of the place. They normally charge 1500-2000 SLR. The climb up the rock and back takes 2 hours. Then the museum will take an hour. For the climb up the rock, there are persons available to carry infants and children. Very clean and well maintained historical site. Sigiriya Rock has been the higlight of our 8 day long Sri Lanka trip.

unfotunatly it is really expensive (35dollars) and rather difficult to get to. But if you are in Sri Lanka you should go and check it out. The whole area is nicely kept and very nicely restored. They also start to value the importance and look after the place. People are not allowed to touch the drawings and walls anymore to preserve them. In the beginning there are a lot of guides that offer there services. But the descriptions are more than enough to explain everything. When you get to the top, which is work, you have an amazing view over the whole area on a good day. I am happy that I took the time.

We were foolish (or uninformed) enough to go on a full moon festival day when the place becomes incredibly busy.  Despite this, and the queuing, the view from the top was fantastic and worth every step. The climb, though seemingly impossible from the base, is actually very manageable and broken up into stages which really help.  There are a number of sights on the way up which are interesting and again help split the experience up.  When we got to the first cave it seemed to end there, but do not be disheartened - you do get to the top, just keep on going. As the climb is all steps and staircases, what shoes you wear are not such a concern, but make sure you take water and a camera.

It's best to go early in the morning, before the hordes of visitors descend, or I should say, ascend on Sigiriya. It pays to get a guide as well, as they are very knowledgeable and will explain everything, every detail to you. The only down side to the guides is that they work with the 'pushers', the young men who help you climb up and down. It's not that difficult and having just the guide wil be more than enough, so do not let any of the pushers latch on to you.  Wear comfortable shoes that you can slip on and off, as whenever you enter a sacred area in Sri Lanka you are requested to take your shoes off. The climb up the rock is what I would classify as very good exercise. If you are reasonably healthy you can do it. There is plenty to see on the way up, so there will be a few brakes along the way. The view from the top is as breathtaking as it gets. The price of admission is included in the cultural triangle ticket, and you can combine a visit here with a visit to Dambulla and the Golden Temple and temple caves. But whatever you do, if you have time for just one attraction, make it Sigiriya. You will not be disappointed.

very beautiful place. I was a little bit scared to climb on the top but it worth to do

This was my third visit to sigiriya rock ,and i enjoy it every time (even it involves climbing steps in the hot sun ),this place has a big history behind it .place is famous as the castle of king kashyapa .some say this belongs to  king ravana who lived many centuries back . Overall the architecture is magnificent (the view from the top to the paintings ) the land  expands up to more than 50 archers I think  as mentioned by other traveler it’s advisable to take you’re drinking water and if you’re traveling with little children it’s better not to take them cause it might be too tiring for them . On your way from sigiriya  take few minutes to go to the sigiriya museum which is near by .the place is well equip with state of the art technology and they will show in 3D image what sirigiya structure was at that time (The ticket you buy includes this aslo)

it was an amazing experience to climb up so many steps ! I  was concerned before doing it  but did not find it difficult at all . one suggestion,  do it either first thing in the morning around 7 O' clock or after 3 O' clock in the afternoon to avoid hot sun. We started after 3; 30 in the afternoon and  enjoyed the cool breeze up there  . The sunset was brilliant and the view  too . do keep in mind there are no toilet facilities or food and water  available for purchase once you start the climb.   Worth the climb  despite the fact that all you find up there is-- ruins! Don't miss it . Do read about the history of the citadel --- a king's fear and what a human achievement at that time.

A photo of Sigiriya was what made us plan a holiday to Sri Lanka, and this majestic place lived up to all the hype that it had built up for us. The gardens, the caves are simply marvellous. They make you marvel the architectural & civil prowess of a civilization hundreds of years old. The Sigiriya damsels are one of the best paintings, and when I learnt that the 21 surviving damsels are just a few of the original 500+ paintings, it got me completely dumbfounded. Imagine a canvas as big as dozens of football fields, strewn with beautiful pictures of women ;) The climb to the top, and finally the view was very refreshing and we enjoyed every minute of it

My husband and I visited the Citadel as part of our honeymoon trip to Sri Lanka. We stayed at the incredibly beautiful Jetwing Vil Uyana which is pretty close to the Rock. We had been advised to visit in the morning or late afternoon and were very pleased that we had taken this advice and gone fairly early in the day. The climb up the 1200 (or so) steps to the top was breathtaking but extremely hot. Make sure that you take PLENTY of water with you. I was very grateful to be able to get back to our hotel quickly and make use of the pool. I personally did not feel like travelling on to another attraction immediately afterwards! The Fortress itself is well worth the long, hot and tiring climb. It is definitely worth taking a guide as they fill you in on all the extra detail that the usual guidebooks miss out. We had experienced some questionable guides in Kandy but the guy that our driver recommended was absolutely fantastic. He made our visit more enjoyable and was keen to show us lots of spots for photos which he delighted in taking! The climb up to the Sigiriya damsels (up two spiral metal staircases which are attached to the side of the Rock) is a little hair-raising but the paintings are beautiful and not to be missed. The immense swimming pool structures at the top of the Rock are also incredible, as is the stunning view. The story behind the structure is amazing and it is well represented at the very modern museum at the base of the Rock, make sure you don't miss this as many guides are keen to start the climb immediately. In short, this is a fabulous place. Both my husband and I were enchanted by it and he even commented that it was the most unbelievable place that he had ever visited! It's not somewhere for children though, the climb is long and hot and there are some very steep drops!

Visited Sigiriya in March this year. Arrived in the afternoon after lunch en route from Polonanaruwa. If one was staying nearby (we stayed at the Cinnamon), Sigiriya is definitely doable together with Polonnaruwa in one day with ample time to take a slow walk and soak it all in. Most tours would have had a local guide waiting for you at the entrance but even if you don't, one should consider getting one. Ours was very knowledgeable and the commentary he gave was fantastic. Things which we would missed out even armed with a good travle book was pointed out to us. This place is fantastic right from the entrance (long walk), through the gardens to the base of the rock. To see what remains of fountains made 1,500 years ago and yet still functioning (ok, well just about) is...Wow! What the books say about visitng in the afternoon/evening is true - the direction of the sun makes it light up in an orange-ochre colour. Good for photography. Half way up the rock is a diversion up a flight of spiral iron staircases leading up a steel platform which overhangs (my other half got a bit scared going up this bit) the rock. Here, one can see the lovely frescoes on the wall. I would recommend anyone to bring a spare t-shirt as you are bound to be drenched in sweat by the time you are finished. The final flight of stairs to the top is also a flight of steel staircases. Once you are on the top, the magnificent thing is, it doesn't feel or seem as if you have just spent the last 1/2 coming up this block of seemingly unscalable rock - it is very flat. Photos which we took up here did not show the scale of the rock and its physical aspect.  You must be there to experience it - to see it from far, then walking towards it and going up it. Give yourself a good 3 hours or more. This UNESCO heritage site is definitely one of the top draws of Sri Lanka. A must visit if you like.

This was the only thing we visited in Sigiriya and it was well worth it. The climb is tedious especially in the heat, so bring a hat, lots of sunscreeen, and a few bottles of water because there are no places selling beverages or food once you start the climb. Definitely take a tour guide, otherwise you may pass by a lot of things and not understand their significance. We really enjoyed our guide and he did a great job taking pics of us throughout the climb. He made our experience a lot more fun i would say. If you have kids, I do not recommend you bring them along unless you are extremely fit and can carry them all the way up the 200 steps!

For a person who's not in great shape, this was a long, hard climb where I had to stop to catch my breath after every flight of stairs. But the good thing is that you can rest at any point and enjoy the great view. A couple of bottles of water are essential to carry with you in case of dehydration. I went up the citadel with my tour guide who stopped at all the right places and relayed the stories behind the citadel. The frescos in the caves are amazing. But the best part for me, was reaching the summit and taking in the exhilarating view. Totally worth the climb! What mortified me was that I saw a number of  families of locals climbing with their little children and infants in their arms! I think the climb is safe enough for adults but the authorities should consider putting an age limit or recommending that children should be carefully supervised. Also a good idea to have medical care close at hand, just in case!

A must for anybody that is touring Sri Lanka.We started out early in the morning to miss the later heat.Climb up was not to bad but you need some element of fitness to get to the top.Wall paintings on the way up were beautiful.The views from the top were spectacular and the ruins of the citadel very interesting.A must do.

Great place. Beautiful frescos. Appreciate the beauty of the place once you recover from the effort of climbing the sheer rocks. View from the top is beautiful. Climate needs to be good to facilitate mid day climb. Recommend either early morning or in the evening at around 4 pm. Very much felt the need for shops/kiosks selling water and food mid way or at the parking place. Lots of butterfies and wasps as well but they seem to have got used to the pious and not so pious over centuries and do not disturb anybody. Strong perfumes could be avoided. One of the highlights of  our Sri Lanka visit.

it was a hot day and we were late. we started climbing at 9am. we bought the tickets at half price!we didnt know it is half for SAARC country. so we gladly hired a guide. he climbed the rock with us and describe in detail the history of king Kaashyap. at first when he told us that we have to climb 1270 steps, we thought its not so bad. but we were wrong. its very exhausting. i was really panting. when i was at lion's paw i thought i couldnt climb any more. but i did at last. it took 1 and 1/2 hour to climb up and only 1/2 hour to get down. and i was very happy to. i was disappointed to see the bare top.( i dnt know what i expected but it was disappointing). the view of surrounding is very nice but we could not stay long as i was burning under sun (literally). but overall it was nice to see all the water garden, bolder garden, swimming pool, dancing floor and all the gates. its really amazing how they built this thing and climb this every day at that time! this think gives me goosebumps till now.

Sigiriya which owes its glory to the vision of King Kashyapa. The monarch erected this ‘Palace in the Sky’ in the 5th century AD. On the top of the Sigiriya rock (meaning the ‘Lion Rock’) are the remnants of a large palace, which is the earliest surviving royal building in Sri Lanka. The palace has several chambers and a bathing pond. In a pocket of the giant rock are the celebrated paintings of 5th century. The Mirror Wall, which had been exposed to elements for more than fifteen centuries still, has some of the original sheen. This archaeological site has been declared a World Heritage Site.

visiting sigiriya, walking the gardens & surrounds, not just climbing the rock, is a truly worthwhile experience. you may be given a guide, or you may choose one yourself; ours for the last two visits was Siri, a softly spoken guy, who really knew about the rock and it's history. it's hot & humid, take water, say two litres, and take a face washer / towel ; sunscreen is a v good idea too, as there is little shade. take your time, it's not a race, and BE RESPECTFUL to the place, don't touch the walls / paintings / etc!!!

the lion rock is definately one of the highlight in SL. however do take note it is NOT a easy climb, mostly you are climbing up stairs and steep steps!! Bring water and towel for the sweat.....a change of clothes would can be consider if you are going directly to other places from here.. we decide to go back to hotel to change since we stay at hotel sigiriya, Ignore the touts and so called local guides unless you really feel comfortable about it, meet one who told me his service is free with the entrance ticket!! that is a new one! ha ha Do explore both side of the base before ascending. Go early morning 7 am is already very bright and by the time reach the top. dont rush down, spent some time to enjoy the place, admire the cascading levels with the water catchment pond! One of the best spot for photo is to turn left from the top to the lower section, and then take pics from the edge looking back at the top, so the pond is on your right... coming down is so much easier but take your time to avoid injuring your knee!! ha ha. A must if you can stand the climb. Do purchase the multiple entry ticket which covers the cultural Triangle. (ticket booth is 5 min walk at the left of the road, the entrance is right side)
It can be daunting the hour climb - but there are the wall paintings and lions paws to see on the way - and you can turn back at a number of points. Great view from the top - very interesting history

We really enjoyed the climb, wasn't to difficult or scary! Loved the history, the view and the remnants of the Kings existence. Named the 8th wonder of the world.... We could see why. The wanna be guides at ground level aren't persistent, once you have said no. Tip, visit the loo before you climb and take plenty of water. We went in the mid day sun, it was quiet and didn't take anymore than about 30 mins to go up.
Be prepared to walk a lot, is not easy either if u r afraid of heights. As all Sri Lanka, better to explore in a group tour or wih a guide.

worth the visit and the climb - a great view once there! that someone chose to go so high up and build a palace says so much about the culture and the times. the monks and their caves, the swimming pool and the assembly hall could be missed on the way down or up, ensure you catch it!

this is one of the historic places of srilanka.. story goes- King ruled Sri lanka for 18 years from the fort. The story goes that King Kasiappa killed his father and after declaring himself as the king came to this fort in Sigiriya. After 18 years his younger brother built his own army and declared war at King Kasiappa. King Kasiappa while on way to the war groung in Anuradhapuram met a marshy land. His elephant got stuck and king had to withdraw his steps. Seeing this his soldiers ran away. And as tradition says that no king is to retrace his steps in war,King Kasiappa committed Suicide by slicing his throat.

It's an ancient and World Heritage site but more than that it has breathtaking view of the Rock from the bottom and the surroundings from the top of the Citadel. We also loved the Mirror Wall, wondering how could ascetic monks do such things at such height without much technological help to speak of. Highly recommended!

We went on a day trip from Kandy to see the Lion rock. This was a 2 and half hour journey in a car but it was absolutely worth it! It is quite a walk up all the steps, but when you get to the top the 360 degree view of the surrounding area is simply breath taking. The weather was fantastic as well. Remember to pack sun cream though, and take some water, it was very hot on the top!
Great views and atmosphere. Try to avoid visiting during the warmer hours because it can get pretty hot, but do not miss it.

If you only do one trip while in Sri Lanka,this has to be it,yes it can be a tough walk in the heat and for $30 its a bit pricey,but when you get to the top and see the view you will not be disapointed.Would recommend that you get a local guide as its more than a lump of rock and do it early,armed with plenty of water
Gives you an insight into how kings of yesteryears lived.  Great climb and fantastic view all along.   Frescos, though limited (unlike Ajanta, in India) are very well done.

We visited Sigiriya on a very hot and sunny day but the climb was was well worth it! The views are amazing. It amazes me how anybody could build anything so high up. Well worth visit and a place not to be missed whilst visiting Sri Lanka!

Beautiful scenery when you near the Rock and a bit terrifying looking up when you are beneath at the stairs. After a fantastic climb you see beautiful rockpaintings and the views at the top are just awsome. Our guide sam explained about the Fortress and the history. Just GREAT!!

So many rush to the top, and if its your first visit this is the obvious thing to do.  Since I had climbed the top before, spent two hours enjoying various pleasure gardens with water features, ancient assembly halls, caves etc.  The museum too is probably one of the best in Sri Lanka and well worth a visit before the climb.

Did the climb early morning, to beat the heat & the tourist buses, & glad we did. Glad they have now put in a new path as i wouldn't fancy the old way. Amazing views from all angles, The frescoes in unbelievably good condition.

Very interesting. Go during a cooler time of day. The climb requires physical fitness, and is not for you if you are afraid of heights. The view from the top is spectacular. Could use additional signage on the descent to indicate the location of the car park.

I had originally read about this place in Arthur C Clarke's novel 'The fountains of paradise' and wanted to visit it ever since. it did not disappoint. Stunning views, the water gardens (that must be the oldest formal gardens on the planet) the awesome 'Lion entrance' well worth the trip. Tip 1 - go early -there are over 1000 steps and you want to get there before it gets too hot Tip 2 - decline all offers of 'helpers' to get you up there - or negotiate a price before you start Tip 3 - read the book I mentioned - it will bring the place alive

I won't repeat what has been said about the beautiful views, but here is some useful info: cost 3030 SLRp ($30 ish), easy to get to by local buses from the nearby conurbations (run every 20mins, conductor will point you in the right directions), toilet facilities available, usual vendors and overpriced water, guides available at entrance (variable English speaking ability, negotiable cost), open from 7am till around 6pm. Need at least 1h30m to have a good nose around. The Sigiriya citadel is an interesting archaeological site and is currently undergoing large amount of rebuilding. This may affect the quality of your experience, if you are a history buff. There is some signage to explain what is around but it is very limited. Some of the caves adjacent to the ancient climbing route are not marked out and can be easily missed. Unfortunately, much of the 'graffiti' has deteriorated and is difficult to see. However, the famous ladies of sigiriya have been well preserved. It was sad to see the mirror wall covered in inane, juvenile slogans. The climb up the rock is not very arduous- it is broken up in to a couple of stages and there are opportunities to rest on the way. The stairs can be narrow and can feel rickety in places. On the rock there are very few sheltered areas and this can mean exposure to intense sun. Take water. The view is, as many have pointed out, beautiful. I would suggest that weekday, early morning or late afternoon visits are best- you avoid the weekenders and the large number of tour groups which arrive en masse. All in all, if you are there just for the views then you should spend your money in the highlands. The citadel is a magnificent spectacle but the level of disrepair is disappointing. I would also point out that the $30 entrance fee doesn't feel justifiable.

I would recommend the Sigirya Rock to every visitor of Sri Lanka. Nestled far away the hubdub of the towns this hillock/ rock gives you the perfect getaway to relax and enjoy SriLanka's history. Though in ruins , with a bit of imagination you can picture the sadistic king and the impregnable fortess he had built . There is an elephant rock, Snake rock and a lion rock (figuratively) guarding this palace of his :) and when you enter the final king's chamber , its designed to give you a feeling that you're walking into the lion's mouth !!! eerie but effective . Its a 1202 step climb and will take you a mimimum of 2.5 hours atleast. Make sure you set aside the time to enjoy the 4000 year old rock paintings painstickingly preserved.

It looks daunting. A great boulder rising over a thousand feet and a vertiginous stair clinging to the rock. But it is worth the effort as the climb itself takes you through a marvellous gallery of erotic rock paintings and when you reach the top the whole of Sri Lanka seems to be spread out below. Allow an hour for the ascent, take a bottle of water, stop frequently and you will be fine.

I loved this place. I got to climb some stairs to see some amazing views of Sigiriya. The luscious green trees and plants made the slight trek enjoyable. I would highly suggest that you arrive early because you could be stuck in line waiting to get to the top of Sigirya. Along the way up the rock, we saw some paintings inside the caves. Afterwards, we went to the top of the "Lion's Head." The hike itself was easy. Just bring lots of water since it could be humid. I thought the price to visit this attraction was expensive, around $30 a person. But at least I can say that I visited this place.

After the entry to the site, there are the remains of the water gardens, now completely dry, then another garden and terrace gardens. Finish the different types of garden begins the climb. It is not difficult, in less than an hour you get to the top. You can also easily climb in late afternoon, the only thing, for those interested, that the museum closes at 17:00. Now very little remains of the ancient palace. The view from the top is still very beautiful. What I do not understand is why do not perform routine maintenance of the site. The stairs, especially spiral are rusty and battered. The price of admission has increased, now costs $ 30.

Have a good guide to provide all of the information on this site.  If you take breaks along the way to discuss the historical features the innumerable steps become surmountable.  Take water with you.  In the end the view is fabulous.

Sigiriya is simply amazing think back 1500 years the roman empire had just collapsed and in Sri Lanka they were building this amazing place. surrounded by two large moats 900x800 metres and walled fortifications then the water gardens only part of which have been excavated , the pool where the elephants cooled down then the climb to the palace on the top 200 metres above the plain. Its a good idea to get there early the crowds and heat later in the day, bring lots of water the climb can be done in 3 or 4 stages but the reward at the top is amazing the views are stunning and the palace itself if you can picture it 1500 years ago wow, its been nominated for 8th wonder of the world and it has my vote. If your in Sri Lanka pay and go.

There are two hypotheses about this place. One that king Kassapa(ad477) murdered his father and run away ti this place and built here a palace. The theory that the place served for the buddhist monk as a place for meditation. No matter what you want to believe, the pkace is exceptional beautifull. You need to work hard to get there. To climb about 5000 steeps, but the place deserve the effort.

There's a reason UNESCO ranks Sigiriya as the 8th Wonder of the World and once you see it you'll completely understanding.  Sigiriya is a stunning ruins of a castle build atop a tall rock mountain.  An engineering marvel, water was piped from the pools at the base of the rock mountain, all the way up to the castle.  It was the rock fortress of a king who killed his father, usurped the throne from his older brother and hid out upon this high lookout to await his brother's attack to regain the kingdom.  Everything in Sri Lanka is beautiful and Sigiriya is among the top.  Read up on the history and technological marvel.  Remember, it's not an easy climb but their are refreshment stands at the base of the stairs that mark the final ascent to the top of the fortress rock.  Be ready to be amazed!

As others have mentioned the $30 entrance is a little steep, and for this the Cultural Triangle of Sri Lanka (Government Agency managing these sites) could and should make the facilities and historical information a little better and more exhaustive. All of the times the climb seemed to get easier and easier, with the stairs now better maintained and the final climb now includes safety rails and stairs bolted to the Rock face. On my earlier trips the steps were carved (about 6 inches wide and 2 deep) into the rock face and you passed people coming down on this as well. Not for the faint of heart. But I digress. The scenery in the surrounding Royal Gardens is now much better maintained and you can now start to get an idea of what this Palace and Grounds must have been like when in working and livable order. The climb is not extremely long, it takes about 1 hour to get to the top at a leisurely pace if you are fit. I would advise getting there early to avoid both the sun and the tour groups. The last time we went we arrived at the site about 8:30AM. The sun is not so high then and by the time you climb up it's still not too bad. As others have said avoid offers of help and if you take a guide make sure it is one of the accredited and approved guides as they have been tested for their knowledge of History. About half way up just before the Mirror Wall you can go up a fairly rickety very high spiral staircase to see the famous Rock Paintings of Sigiriya. If you are not afraid of heights you need to do this. There's also a museum near the main entrance which I heard was worth seeing, however I did not have a chance to visit this yet on my many trips. Perhaps another visitor has something to add about the Museum? Well worth the trip even if the entrance fee is overpriced. Definitely a World Heritage Site.

Amazing....!   Bring water! And only go up in you are in good health, it is little hot, and steep. Lots of climbing. not only climbing water garden and nice surrounding lot of travelers miss this. need to find very good guide who know about history. otherwise you will miss lot of impotent legends. i visited Sri Lanka two time i used Asian Exotica Excellent service. worth paying them www.asianexotica.org

I would highly recommend climbing this rock when in Sri Lanka. Make time to visit this attraction - the only downer are the fees which are a steep US30. Other than that, wear comfortable clothing - bring a cap and a bottle of water and maybe a handtowel to wipe off all that sweat. Don't forget your camera of course and wear sandals instead of power shoes as they are cooler.

Sigiriya is trying to position it self as the most iconic monument of Sri Lanka with every travel brochure to Sri Lanka featuring the fortress as the 8th wonder of the world. It is truly a magical place with ancient architecture frescoes and water gardens. But rather overrated when you look at the exuberant entrance fees tourist have to pay to enter the site.
Very beautiful!  Don't let anybody help you up, unless you are willing to pay!  Bring water!  And only go up in you are in good health, it is very hot, and steep.  Lots of climbing.

The Sigiriya Rock is phenomenal. You walk past the water garden, boulder garden and terrace gardens, the mirror walls, Fresco paintings  It is  a very pretty steep walk as long as you are physically fit.  From top you have a awesome  view  where you can view  the mountains and on a sunny day you even can see until Kandy. It is highly recommend that one visit this place if you touring Sri Lanka.

We hired a tour guide to take us up, while a bit pricey, it was worth it. He gave us loads on info and was very helpful and polite. The views as you go up and truely breathtaking and leave you with a real sense of history. That the king had his servants carry him to the top and manually fill the pools at the top of the rock is impressive when you finally haul yourself to the top in the burning heat of mid summer! If you do go in the summer months, do take drinks with you, there is nothing on the way up and you will feel the heat. Great bit of history, great views, well worth it.

As usual I'll start negative as thats what people want to be aware of! 1. Approach Roads - Don't even pass as roads! Beware if you're driving. I recommend a local guide via a hotel. Ok so thats about it. I read a load of warnings about being ripped off but personally I did a tour as a package through Kuoni for £300 that included many sights in Kandy, Dambula, Sygiria etc. It was excellent value for money and I got an incredible driver with local knowledge who was worth the money for the 5am day 1 pickup through to the 11pm 2nd night drop off. The tour had a sleepover in Kandy (Tree of Life hotel which was adequate). I think if you are strong willed then you can dismiss the penny pinchers and tip beggars. If you have a local guide as well then he should be helping you to dismiss these people and warn them not to bother. The Sigiriya Rock is worth to see. There is an entrance fee USD 25. With that you can see the rock, the water garden, boulder garden and terrace gardens, the mirror wall and the museum. It’s a pretty steep walk but it’s easy to manage because there is a lot to see and you can do some breaks. Sigiriya is a "must see". Though the climb is a little tiring. Its definitely worth the climb
Sigiriya sure is worth a visit! What a mountain! The climb is mostly interesting and once you're up there, It offers a great view around. Don't miss it!

One of the most exciting sites I've ever been to... Mesmerizing views of nature and monkeys while climbing till the very highest top. Citadel of Sigiriya was like living a unique experience at a place that makes you proud to have seen and have experienced living it in person!!!!!!!!! SIGIRIYA IS THE PLACE TO BE IN SRI LANKA! :D

We managed to visit the Lion Rock at the start of June which meant it was during the transition of monsoon seasons so it was pretty much empty. Having seen the photos of people queing to climb the rock, I might have thought of it differently if it had been really busy. The gardens at the bottom are very pretty but its the climb up and the views from the top that make this place so special. The climb up would never pass health & safety in the UK but thats what makes it so amazing (especially when you realise that the fortress at the top was built without the steps up that I used!!). The voews from the top are amazing as the majority of the area is flat aorund the rock. This also means you can see the rock from miles away, our room in the hotel (Heritance Kandalama in Dambulla - very good by the way!) looked out towards the rock. This is a fabulous day out to see a world heritage site in the heart of Sri Lanka's cultural triangle. Sigiriya or Lion Rock as it is known houses ancient gardens and a mountain top fortress, as well as amazing cave paintings. The climb up the is incredible via Moonstone steps and a rather heath robinson metal staircase, but well worth it when you reach the top and see the amazing views across jungle to the enormous stone Buddha to the hills surounding Kandy. If you are not on an official tour with your own guide be alert when you arrive as there are alot of guides around and they will try it on in terms of price. Also if you start off with a guide and you notice a couple of hangers on then make sure you stop and say you only want the one guide to come with you, otherwise you will be stung for additional charges for 'helpers'!

Look around the museum first, to, get an idea of the layout. It's far too big to do that on the ground. There are a lot of steps involved and it's not a good place to go if you don't like heights. You can leave out the final climb up to the top of the rock but the spiral staircase up to the frescoes is pretty hairy as well. The entry fee is a bit pricey, so if you intend to visit other Cultural Triangle attractions it's worth getting a Cultural Triangle ticket that includes Sigiriya and several other sites. It makes the whole thing much better value. Overall it's an amazing place and well worth a visit. Allow about half a day.

I can't believe that when the kind had his palace at the top he had guys carrying him up there, what strapping chaps they must have been. I (stupidly) took his hand and smiled a thank you. He then grabbed hold of my wrist and wouldnt let go of it until we got to the top. One merchant followed us to the car with this elephant gift insisting prices and we just was not interested. As long as you give a firm "no" its fine, but I can imagine it being very annoying for some who are tired and just want to get back. The whole experience was well worth it however, especially if you can't be bothered to do something as exausting as Adams Peak but you still want to do something of relevance in the same nature. Well worth the climb, enjoy x

Sigiriya is well worth going to, as it's very interesting. The view from the top is absolutely breathtaking (as is the climb up there... ) and you pass several interesting gardens, a moat, and some interesting rock writing on the way up.  It is a bit of a demanding climb though, and you're well advised to bring plenty of drinking water. We stayed in Dambulla, and from there you can go to Sigiriya in a tuk-tuk for 400-500 rupees. Be prepared to bargain hard though, - if you look like a tourist, the asking price is 2000 or more.  Going by pubic bus is 20 rupees a person. As in many places in Sri Lanka, there's a double princing system in work. Sri Lankans can enten Sigiriya for 20 rupees, tourists are (infuriatingly) charged 2250 rupees.  (or around 5500 if you want a joint ticket to see some of the other attractions in the area.) If you're on a desperate budget, there's a moat you can swim across to dodge the fee.... Also there is one checkpoint in a gallery on the cliffface, but the path forks out before that. If you take the left path (which is a bit shorter), you wil bypass the checkpoint and end up the same place anyway.

So, i'll be going to be honest here. Sigiriya was amazing. It was really nice and an interesting place to visit. But, it's a rip-off. The money that they are charging to tourists who are visiting the place is too much. Beware of the guides. Our guy.. we gave him 20$ and he declined.. This people are dreaming. It was a nice place but the people in there Ruined it.

we too had to push off 'guides' and people wanting to carry our daughter (we dont look ancient but we aren't fitness freaks either.
